suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Acer Router Log Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' Initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to acer_cgi.log on Acer Wave 7 routers (192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com). Alert on 200/206 responses returning log file content without prior authentication (no active session token or failed login immediately preceding request).

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credential Harvesting from Router Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' Credential extraction from acer_cgi.log is the privilege escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate log file access (acer_cgi.log requests) with subsequent suspicious authentication attempts using credentials that match patterns in logs. Detect exfiltration of files containing password=, login=, or telnet keywords. Flag large log downloads or repeated log requests from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Key-based Backup Decryption and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-49201: 'The upload.cgi binary...contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor upload.cgi requests for backup file submissions. Detect anomalous backup lifecycle: backup downloads followed immediately by re-uploads (decrypt-modify-encrypt cycle), backup uploads from non-administrative IPs, or uploads outside approved maintenance windows. Cross-reference backup file hashes against known-good versions.

suggestion.title: Router Firmware Version Enumeration (Acer Wave 7)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable versions as 'T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier.' Identifying vulnerable firmware is discovery step enabling exploitation targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query or monitor for Acer Wave 7 firmware version strings matching T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or below via management interface access patterns or device telemetry. Flag vulnerable devices for prioritized patching. Correlate with inbound connections to admin interface (indication of external reconnaissance).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article advises 'disable remote management' as mitigation, indicating 192.168.76.1/acerconnect.com remote access is the exploit delivery channel. Both CVEs require web interface access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) connections to router management endpoints (192.168.76.1:80/443, acerconnect.com) from external/untrusted networks. Alert on successful authentication without corresponding VPN context. Flag repeated failed login attempts (1+ per minute) followed by success within 5 minutes (credential spray). Detect admin interface access from IPs without prior legitimate user context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Extracted Router Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article notes compromised credentials are 'for web and Telnet,' enabling network access. Attacker pivots from router to internal systems using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Telnet or SSH login attempts using credentials extracted from Acer router logs. Cross-reference known-compromised credential pairs (web user/pass from acer_cgi.log) against internal authentication logs. Flag Telnet sessions originating from router IP (192.168.76.1 or router-associated CIDR). Monitor for credential reuse across internal systems within hours of router compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking – InprocServer32 Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' This is the primary persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 and HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\*\InprocServer32. Flag writes where the InprocServer32 Default value points to unusual paths or newly created DLLs, especially from user profile or temp directories. Correlate with game installation directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL Import Chain – FFmpeg to natives2_blob
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a modified FFmpeg DLL...that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin. Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Classic DLL sideloading/proxy pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ffmpeg.dll loads that occur from game installation directories (outside Program Files). Cross-reference with presence of natives2_blob.bin in the same directory or parent. Flag if the DLL's imports include GetClassObject pointing to unusual paths.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Script Execution from DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' This chains DLL execution to obfuscated script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe spawned from unusual parents (game executables, explorer, rundll32). Look for -EncodedCommand, -Command with Base64 content, or suspiciously short command lines. Correlate DLL load events from games with PowerShell process creation within 1–2 seconds.

suggestion.title: Controlled Environment / Sandbox Detection in PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article states Stage1 PowerShell script 'performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Defensive evasion pattern common in RATs to avoid analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell scripts for artifacts of VM/sandbox detection: WMI queries (e.g., Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BaseBoard, Win32_BIOS), registry checks (VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V keys), or execution of analysis tools (tasklist, wmic). Flag when these are queried before network or file operations.

suggestion.title: Game Distribution via File-Sharing / Torrent Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'These links redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service' and 'trojanized games have also been distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena.' Targets niche communities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of executable game archives (RPG Maker, RenPy) from PixelDrain and torrent trackers. Monitor user agents and referrers from adult game aggregator sites. Correlate with subsequent suspicious DLL loads or PowerShell execution within hours of download.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Downloader Execution – PowerShell Stage1 to Trojan
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' Delayed execution indicates C2-coordinated download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts that perform HTTP/HTTPS downloads to unusual domains, especially with delays (scheduled tasks, sleep loops). Correlate with persistence mechanisms (COM hijacking, scheduled tasks). Look for DownloadString, DownloadFile, or Invoke-WebRequest in process arguments or script blocks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Exploitation Attempts Against Redis
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names the vulnerability. Pipeline generated zero use cases covering exploitation of this RCE flaw despite it being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network traffic to Redis ports (6379, 6380, 26379) containing known CVE-2026-23479 exploit payloads, Lua script injection, or malformed protocol commands. Alert on shell spawning (bash, cmd, powershell) with redis-server as parent process.

suggestion.title: Redis Vulnerability Scanning and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain begins with discovery; article context 'autonomous AI tool finds' implies scanning activity. No initial-access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify port scans targeting Redis services, version probing via INFO or COMMAND commands, and authentication bypass attempts. Flag rapid-fire connections to 6379 from single source.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from Redis Instances
suggestion.rationale: RCE enables attacker code execution and data access. Article describes impact but pipeline ignored collection/exfiltration phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DUMP, BGSAVE, SYNC, or bulk export commands from Redis followed by large data transfers to external IPs. Detect unusual egress patterns from Redis server (port >1024 to non-standard destinations).

suggestion.title: Privileged Code Execution via Redis RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE necessarily results in arbitrary command execution on the host. Article context implies impact to underlying system; pipeline skipped process-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any child process spawned by redis-server process, especially interactive shells, interpreters, or network utilities (curl, wget, nc). Correlate with Redis service network activity.

suggestion.title: RomulusLoader Process Hollowing Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes RomulusLoader downloading 'payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' Process hollowing is a named, specific technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of VirtualAllocEx→WriteProcessMemory→SetThreadContext targeting non-child processes from loader parents. Alert on legitimate system processes with anomalous child launches or unsigned code execution in memory regions.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'shellcode injection' as RomulusLoader deployment mechanism, core execution evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API call sequences (OpenProcess→VirtualAllocEx→WriteProcessMemory→CreateRemoteThread) initiated by suspicious loader processes. Flag injection into system binaries (svchost, lsass, explorer).

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox Registry Enumeration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Atlas RAT performs 'anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the CExecSvc service, and OS UUID.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious processes querying HKLM for 'CExecSvc' registry key or Defender Application Guard config keys, or enumerating OS UUID via WMI/registry. Correlate multiple evasion checks in single process execution.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential Harvesting by SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes SilentRunLoader stealing 'Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data' from UK and Southeast Asia targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access to Chrome Local State, Login Data, or Cookies files by Python processes or unexpected parent processes. Alert on file compression, encryption, or exfiltration of %APPDATA%\Google\Chrome artifacts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Remote Tool Deployment (AnyDesk/SyncFuture)
suggestion.rationale: Article states RomulusLoader 'was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture,' with explicit note that SyncFuture is 'popular in China' yet used in German attacks—signals unusual tooling for financially-motivated group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of AnyDesk or SyncFuture spawned from loader processes, non-standard paths, or without user interaction. Correlate launch with outbound C2 connections or process memory indicators of malware.

suggestion.title: Webcam and Audio Recording via Atlas RAT
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Atlas RAT capabilities as 'Audio and webcam recording,' explicitly flagged as surveillance potential sold to espionage groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malware process (Atlas RAT, Winos4.0, ValleyRAT) accessing audio/video driver interfaces or Windows.Media.* APIs. Alert on unsigned process loading mmsys.cpl, accessing camera GUID, or requesting microphone/webcam permissions after malware execution.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alert: CVE-2026-45247 Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited in the wild.' Pipeline must instantiate baseline vulnerability detection for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results reporting CVE-2026-45247 on Mirasvit installations. Prioritize public-facing instances. Flag patch lag against federal due date 2026-06-06.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CacheWarmer Cookie Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' This cookie name is the direct delivery mechanism for RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing 'CacheWarmer' cookie with PHP serialized object patterns (strings starting with 'O:', 'a:', or base64-encoded variants). Correlate with vulnerable Mirasvit versions.

suggestion.title: PHP Unserialize Gadget Chain Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability... remote code execution.' Exploitation requires PHP unserialize() processing attacker-controlled objects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP logs for unserialize() warnings, class instantiation from cookie data, or gadget chain indicators. Alert on unexpected function calls during cookie processing.

suggestion.title: Command Execution from Web Service Context Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RCE outcome: 'remote code execution by supplying a crafted serialized PHP object.' Successful exploitation enables arbitrary command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning with parent PHP-FPM, httpd, or nginx from web root. Flag shell commands executed via PHP execution contexts or suspicious child processes from cache warmer.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Placement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article's RCE outcome implies attacker capability to write files. Standard post-exploitation pattern involves web shell persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected .php, .phtml files written to Mirasvit cache directories or web root. Correlate with CacheWarmer cookie activity and suspicious file permissions.

suggestion.title: Android Integer Overflow Exploitation – CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2025-48595 is a 'high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework' affecting Android 14–16, requires 'no user interaction to exploit,' and 'may be under limited targeted exploitation in the wild.' Pipeline generated zero detections for this active attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android 14–16 devices for unexpected privilege escalation or system-level capability grants without user-initiated actions. Flag processes gaining elevated privileges through framework integer overflow patterns, particularly in system_server or framework processes handling integer operations on untrusted input.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel cgroups v1 Privilege Escalation and Container Escape – CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article details CVE-2022-0492 in 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' enabling attackers to 'bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' Pipeline generated zero detections despite explicit container escape scenario and active exploitation context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cgroup_release_agent_write system calls from unprivileged or containerized processes. Correlate cgroup manipulation attempts with unexpected privilege escalation to UID 0. Flag processes running in container namespaces that subsequently access host-level resources (cross-namespace PID/mount/network access) or spawn root processes.

suggestion.title: Container Namespace Isolation Bypass – cgroups v1 Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CVE-2022-0492 'primarily impacts containerized environments' and is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' No use case captures the container-to-host escape sequence or namespace boundary violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes running in container namespaces (identified via cgroup membership or container orchestration metadata) that escalate to UID 0 via cgroup subsystem manipulation. Alert on containers writing to /sys/fs/cgroup or /proc/*/cgroup_release_agent. Correlate cgroup_release_agent write attempts with subsequent root process creation from container context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Linux Kernel Inventory – CVE-2022-0492 Unfixed Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit vulnerable kernel ranges ('2.6 through 4.20' and '5.5 through 5.17') and patched versions ('4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, 4.19.229+, 5.4.177+, 5.10.97+, 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+'). No inventory or alerting use case to identify systems still vulnerable after June 5, 2026 CISA remediation deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Linux systems running kernel versions in ranges 2.6–4.20 (excluding patched versions 4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, 4.19.229+) or 5.5–5.17 (excluding patched versions 5.4.177+, 5.10.97+, 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+). Flag unpatched systems as CVE-2022-0492-vulnerable after CISA June 5, 2026 deadline.

suggestion.title: Android Security Patch Compliance – CVE-2025-48595 Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2025-48595 fixed in 'June 2026 security patches (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 security patch levels).' Pipeline generated no use case to detect unpatched Android 14–16 devices or enforce patch-level compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android 14–16 device fleet for security patch levels older than 2026-06-05. Flag devices with patch level earlier than required CVE-2025-48595 fix as vulnerable to active exploitation. Correlate unpatched device population with incident timelines and active exploitation reports.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cgroup Subsystem Access from Containerized Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes CVE-2022-0492 exploitation via 'insufficient authentication checks' in cgroup_release_agent_write(). Pipeline generated no detection for suspicious cgroup I/O or access control violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any attempt by containerized or non-root processes to write to cgroup release-agent properties or cgroup subsystem files. Monitor audit denials on cgroup operations. Flag child processes of cgroup manipulation attempts that execute with elevated privileges or in different namespaces.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_UID/GID in body
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value' — direct detection of exploit attempt at API endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoint with body parameters KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID set to 0 or other prohibited values. Correlate with source IP and user agent for clustering.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway service account creates kernel pod as root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass outcome: 'launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID' materializing in pod creation — detection of successful privilege escalation via pod with UID/GID=0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when enterprise-gateway service account creates pods with spec.securityContext.runAsUser=0 or runAsGroup=0, or when containers specify runAsUser/runAsGroup=0.

suggestion.title: Kernel pod with hostPath volume mount by enterprise-gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1611 'Escape to Host' paired with pod creation indicates lateral movement via host filesystem. Kernel pods with hostPath volumes enable container escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when enterprise-gateway service account creates pods with hostPath volumes mounting sensitive directories (/, /etc, /var/lib, /sys, /proc, /root).

suggestion.title: Cron/persistence file written from container runtime context
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1053.003 'Scheduled Task/Job: Cron' indicates persistence/install phase. Detection focuses on cron file modification by container runtimes (runc, containerd-shim) as UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation/modification of /etc/cron*, /etc/crontab, /var/spool/cron files when initiating process is container runtime binary (runc, containerd-shim, containerd-shim-runc-v2) running as UID 0.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway vulnerable to CVE-2026-44180
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-44180 in IOC section. Standard vulnerability matching hunt for exposed/vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory and vulnerability scanner results for Jupyter Enterprise Gateway instances with CVE-2026-44180. Identify exposed /api/kernels endpoints.

suggestion.title: KERNEL_* environment variable injection with YAML-special characters
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'environment variables used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest allow YAML injection.' Pipeline does not detect the attack at the injection point—detecting malformed or special-character-laden KERNEL_* values in POST body before manifest rendering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to /api/kernels with KERNEL_* query/body parameters containing YAML structural characters (---, ..., |, &, *, !, >, <) or securityContext key names. High fidelity if source is external or unusual user agent.

suggestion.title: Multi-document YAML pod injection via securityContext rewrite
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject multi-document YAML to create additional unintended Kubernetes resources' and 'overwrite existing keys like securityContext.' UC_1_3 detects pod creation post-facto; this detects the actual manifest rendering anomaly—pods with mutated securityContext differing from user request.
log_sources: Pod spec diffs from ConfigMap/Secret changes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pods created by EG service account where the requestObject.spec.securityContext differs in significant ways (privileged=true, runAsUser=0, runAsGroup=0, hostNetwork/PID=true, hostPath mounts) from what the user would reasonably request via /api/kernels. Requires baseline of legitimate EG pod specs.

suggestion.title: Unsecured environment variable exfiltration in Jupyter Enterprise Gateway logs
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'environment variables used during the rendering...' attack relies on KERNEL_* env vars being passed unsafely. Operators may log these variables for debugging; detection hunt for any logs disclosing KERNEL_* values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search logs for 'KERNEL_' environment variable assignments or expansions being written to logs, especially if those logs are world-readable or shipped to external systems. Indicates debug mode that amplifies injection risk.

suggestion.title: Enumeration / fingerprinting of Jupyter Enterprise Gateway endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a public-facing application (T1190). Reconnaissance phase missing: attackers must first discover EG is present and /api/kernels is exposed. No detection for port scanning, endpoint fuzzing, or version discovery attempts.
log_sources: Web access logs (404s, OPTIONS, HEAD to /api/kernels*)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of requests to /api/kernels with unsuccessful status codes (404, 405) followed by successful POST, or multiple different User-Agents probing /api/kernels in a short time window, suggesting scanning/fingerprinting.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'DesckVB RAT' delivery; any RAT implant establishes command-and-control. Detection of outbound connections to known/suspicious DesckVB infrastructure is fundamental.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from user processes to rare, high-reputation-risk ASNs and domains not in approved C2 allowlist. Alert on process execution of DesckVB loader/RAT variants contacting non-standard ports or known malware C2 sinkhole domains.

suggestion.title: Malspam with Malicious Link Click Leading to RAT Download
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Malspam Campaign'—phishing link in email body leading to artifact download is the initial-access vector; should detect email delivery + click telemetry + subsequent download of RAT payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email with malicious/suspicious URL to click events from same user, followed within minutes by download of executable from attacker-controlled or compromised CDN. Flag if click bypasses sandboxing or if URL redirects through Google DoubleClick endpoint.

suggestion.title: Google DoubleClick Redirect Chain to Malicious Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Google DoubleClick Abused'—DoubleClick ad network is being used as intermediary redirect to RAT payload. Should detect abnormal redirect chains from legitimate ad endpoints to attacker C2 or payload host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP redirects originating from doubleclick.net or *.doubleclick.net that terminate at non-advertising domains or IPs with malware reputation. Flag when DoubleClick redirect payload is executable (EXE, DLL, MSI, OCX).

suggestion.title: DesckVB Process Injection and Memory Artifact
suggestion.rationale: RAT implies process injection and persistence tactics; DesckVB in particular uses injection into legitimate processes. Should detect injection patterns and in-memory shellcode execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process hollowing (parent process terminated, child inherits memory), unusual DLL injection into explorer.exe/svchost.exe, or API hooking patterns consistent with RAT families. Correlate with unsigned/invalid-signature binaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Downloaded via Email Link
suggestion.rationale: Malspam campaign delivery chain: email → link click → download. Article states RAT is 'delivered' via campaign; need detection of file execution immediately after suspicious email click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads to user temp/downloads folder from internet zone, executed within 2-5 min of user click, with parent process = browser. Flag parent-child execution chains (explorer → cmd → powershell → executable).

suggestion.title: Malware-as-a-Service Infrastructure: DesckVB Loader Beacon
suggestion.rationale: DesckVB RAT delivery suggests staged attack: initial stager/loader beacons to C2 for payload. Should detect first-contact beacons before full RAT capability is loaded.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for beaconing patterns: regular outbound connections on interval, DNS queries for suspicious domains, HTTP User-Agent spoofing as legitimate software, or binary protocol handshakes to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Business Document Phishing Attachment Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'disguises itself as an everyday business document — a purchase order, a quote, or a request for proposal. Once an unsuspecting employee opens' — this is phishing with user execution of malware. No T1566.002/T1204.002 detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) spawning wscript.exe or cscript.exe with parent in user Downloads or Temp directory. Monitor for .js/.vbs file execution with Office parent process. Establish baseline of legitimate Office macros vs. script interpreter spawning.

suggestion.title: JavaScript RAT Process and Network Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Malware explicitly named 'JS.MonoGlyphRAT'—JavaScript-based RAT. Article provides C2 domains (aryamint.com, scan.aryamint.com). Need detection for script interpreter establishing network connections to adversary infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: cscript.exe or wscript.exe initiating outbound connections or DNS queries to aryamint.com, scan.aryamint.com, or similar suspicious domains. Flag cases where script interpreter connects to IPs 158.94.211.76 or 91.92.243.79. Establish baseline of legitimate script process network activity.

suggestion.title: Evasive Script-based C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'stealthy' and 'most traditional security tools are completely missing it'—indicates obfuscation/evasion. RATs beacon to C2 over standard protocols; T1071 alone insufficient without executable context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Persistent or periodic outbound connections from script-interpreter processes to aryamint.com/scan.aryamint.com or IPs 158.94.211.76/91.92.243.79. Look for DNS queries that fail before successful connection (DNS evasion test), or encrypted payloads in HTTP/HTTPS headers suggesting custom protocol wrapper.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence from JavaScript Process
suggestion.rationale: RATs establish persistence; JS.MonoGlyphRAT targeting 'US Enterprises' suggests campaign expecting sustained presence. No T1112 or persistence techniques detected despite malware classification as RAT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Script interpreter (cscript.exe, wscript.exe) writing to HKEY_CURRENT_USER or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE Run/RunOnce registry keys, or modifying AppInit_DLLs. Flag write activity to Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* paths from script parents. Cross-correlate with initial Office spawn.

suggestion.title: Discovery and Enumeration by RAT Process Chain
suggestion.rationale: RATs perform host and environment discovery (T1083, T1033, T1057). Article names malware as RAT; no discovery techniques detected despite this being standard RAT behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Script interpreter spawning child processes for command execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) followed by enumeration commands: dir, tasklist, wmic process list, whoami, ipconfig. Monitor script process children with arguments containing 'system32', 'drivers', 'temp', 'appdata'. Flag rapid-fire process creation from single script parent.

suggestion.title: Office to Script to Network Attack Chain Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Full kill-chain correlation across three phases. Pipeline detected zero kill-chain phases despite article describing complete attack narrative from document delivery through C2 establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Multi-event correlation: (1) Office process (winword.exe, excel.exe, outlookexec) in user's Downloads/Temp, (2) child script interpreter spawned within 5 seconds, (3) script interpreter initiating DNS or network connection to aryamint.com/scan.aryamint.com within 60 seconds. Single alert on completion of chain; tuning threshold per baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Active Directory Enumeration Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'automate Active Directory discovery'—direct discovery-phase TTP. Pipeline failed to extract T1087.002 despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume LDAP queries, dsquery.exe invocation, or bulk directory enumeration from user endpoints. Alert on rapid sequential queries targeting domain objects (users, computers, OUs, service accounts) especially from non-standard client processes.

suggestion.title: EDR Tool Disablement or Modification Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actor 'test endpoint detection and response (EDR) evasion techniques'—explicit defense-evasion activity. Pipeline failed to map to T1562.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable, modify, or unload EDR drivers; monitor for registry modifications affecting Defender, third-party antivirus, or EDR exclusion policies. Alert on service stop/disable operations targeting security-related services.

suggestion.title: Payload Staging in User-Writable Directory Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'suspicious endpoint triggered alerts tied to payloads stored in a user directory'—indicates staging-to-execution pattern. No use case generated for this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable or script file creation in user-controlled paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Desktop, Downloads) followed by process launch from that location. Flag unusual parent-child relationships; correlate with network anomalies.

suggestion.title: Automated AD and EDR Reconnaissance Framework Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'AI-assisted tools' and 'post-exploitation frameworks' indicating scripted reconnaissance and evasion testing. No use case suggested for this emerging attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential enumeration and evasion-testing commands executed in automated fashion (e.g., multiple reconnaissance commands within seconds). Monitor for execution of known AD/EDR testing tools or suspicious PowerShell/cmd.exe invocation chains consistent with frameworks.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to AWS Lambda URL domain pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws as C2 infrastructure and states threat actors 'hide inside one of the world's most trusted platforms, Amazon Web Services'. This specific AWS abuse vector has no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound TCP/UDP to *.lambda-url.*.on.aws from non-browser processes. AWS Lambda URLs are rarely used in legitimate enterprise communication. Correlate with process reputation and file hash to surface HazyBeacon samples.

suggestion.title: DNS queries to AWS Lambda URL domain patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) technique. Defanged domain in IOCs suggests DNS-based communication path. Separate DNS detection catches reconnaissance and fallback communication distinct from HTTPS beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS A/AAAA lookups for *.lambda-url.*.on.aws from non-browser processes. Lambda URLs are typically accessed directly; DNS resolution suggests staging or domain validation attempts.

suggestion.title: HazyBeacon malware hash detection and execution hunting
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline completely failed to extract the seven SHA256 IOCs. Article lists them as 'high-fidelity only' samples but generated zero file-based detection. Early payload execution is critical before C2 beaconing initiates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert rule for exact SHA256 match of all seven HazyBeacon hashes. Correlate execution with parent processes indicating phishing delivery (Office, browsers, email clients) and subsequent AWS Lambda URL outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated executables with C2 callback to trusted cloud services
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) but no detection for this dual-evasion pattern. Article states actors 'turn trusted cloud infrastructure against organizations'—combining obfuscation + legitimate-looking infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect packed/high-entropy executables that unpack or inject code to connect to AWS infrastructure. Use behavioral indicators: process hollowing, CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory followed by outbound to *.lambda-url.* domains.

suggestion.title: Southeast Asia government network targeting context enrichment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'targets government networks across Southeast Asia'. IOC-driven detections lack geographic + sector context. Threat-specific alerting reduces FP noise and increases analyst confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Tag Southeast Asia government sector in asset inventory. Increase priority and reduce suppression thresholds for IOCs (domain, hash, IP) when matched against this population. Apply lower alert thresholds than commercial or US-based detections.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 HPACK Amplification Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'inserting a header into the HPACK dynamic table and referencing it repeatedly via compact indexed representation' yielding '5,700:1 and 4,000:1 amplification ratios' on Envoy and Apache. No detection for this compression exploitation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 streams for single-byte header references followed by rapid decoded header expansion. Trigger when decoded header size exceeds expected ratio (>100:1) or when header allocation scales faster than actual request count from single source IP.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow-Control Window Stalling DoS
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'prevents memory from being freed once the request completes' by 'advertising a zero-byte flow-control window' and sending 'tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames to avoid timeouts.' No detection for held incomplete connections was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 connections with zero flow-control windows held open for >30 seconds without data transmission. Correlate with repeated WINDOW_UPDATE frames that fail to increase window size, indicating indefinite request hold pattern.

suggestion.title: Memory Exhaustion from Single HTTP/2 Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a single client on a 100Mbps connection can exhaust tens of gigabytes of RAM within seconds' and specific results: 'Envoy 1.37.2 exhausted 32 GB RAM in about 10 seconds.' No resource-consumption detection keyed to HTTP/2 client count was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline server memory usage per HTTP/2 connection; alert when single source IP triggers memory growth >500MB or total server memory >80% with <10 concurrent HTTP/2 streams from single IP. Investigate if memory fails to release after connection close.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Web Server Version Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies explicitly vulnerable software versions: 'Envoy 1.37.2 exhausted 32 GB RAM in about 10 seconds,' 'Apache httpd 2.4.67,' 'nginx 1.29.7,' and 'IIS (Windows Server 2025).' Patched versions mentioned: nginx 1.29.8, Apache httpd mod_http2 2.0.41. No inventory or version-detection use case produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag web server processes matching vulnerable versions: Envoy 1.37.2, Apache httpd 2.4.67, nginx <1.29.8, IIS on Windows Server 2025. Cross-check against CVE-2026-49975. Recommend inventory query and patch-readiness scan.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Decoded Header Size Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'bypasses existing defenses such as limits on the total decoded header size, as the header values used in the attack are tiny, and amplification comes from internal per-header bookkeeping.' No detection for amplified internal allocation vs. transmitted header size was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish ratio of transmitted HTTP/2 header bytes to decoded header allocation per request. Alert when ratio inverts (allocation >> transmission) or when request count stays low but allocation grows monotonically, indicating compression amplification loop.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Server Restart Correlation with DoS Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes complete server exhaustion forcing crashes within 10–45 seconds depending on platform. No detection linking restart events to unusual HTTP/2 traffic patterns or DoS precursors was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate server restart/crash events with preceding 60-second windows of HTTP/2 traffic. Flag restarts preceded by memory spikes, single-source connection floods, or anomalous flow-control patterns. Alert on repeated restart cycles indicating attack replay.

suggestion.title: Preinstall/Postinstall Script Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states the malicious code 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines' during npm installation. No detection use case exists for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/npm processes spawning during package installation that access credential stores (.ssh, .aws, .kube, git config, browser profile directories). Flag process execution from node_modules or npm cache with child processes accessing HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Credential Manager or Linux secretstorage APIs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—indicating malicious re-upload of legitimate package versions to npm registry. No detection for republish anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry activity for republishing of existing package versions by new/unexpected maintainers. Flag rapid version increments within same major.minor range. Alert on package uploads from IPs/ASNs misaligned with historical publisher geography or during off-hours for that maintainer.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from npm Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'silently infecting CI/CD environments and developer systems.' No detection use case for exfiltration of stolen credentials post-collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections from node.exe/npm child processes to non-CDN, non-npm-registry domains, especially with POST payloads. Flag connection to attacker infrastructure from CI/CD agent machines shortly after npm install. Correlate with credential-access indicators (time delta, same process tree).

suggestion.title: GitHub/Cloud Provider Credential Access from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'GitHub, cloud platforms' as credential targets. Specific detection for API key/token theft from these services during npm execution missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for env var reads (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET) or file access to ~/.ssh/known_hosts, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config during npm install context. Alert if processes spawned from node_modules read these credential sources within <30 seconds of package install completion.

suggestion.title: Persistent Reinfection via Supply-Chain Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'persistence' mechanism: malicious packages republish themselves, creating a recursive infection of downstream consumers. No detection for this persistence loop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install of a package that itself triggers an npm install of the same (or sibling) package to a different target repository. Flag if package.json scripts contain npm install, npm publish, or git push to npm registry. Alert on repeated infection patterns across organization (same packages installed → credentials stolen → re-published).

suggestion.title: Process Execution from node_modules with Elevated Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CI/CD environments and developer systems.' Attack likely runs postinstall scripts with unexpected privilege escalation. No detection for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution from node_modules or npm cache directory where the process runs at higher privilege than the npm install caller (e.g., npm install as user, but postinstall script runs as admin/root). Correlate with parent process being npm and with credential-access child events.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Command Execution Violating Freeze/Safety Constraints
suggestion.rationale: Article directly describes: 'A real-world example is the coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This is proof of concept for agents executing high-impact destructive actions despite explicit safety boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when service accounts tied to AI agent frameworks execute destructive commands (DELETE, DROP, rm -rf patterns) against production databases or critical files. Correlate with agent workflow logs showing safety constraint instructions preceding the command. Flag accounts with historical patterns of constraint-respecting behavior executing out-of-profile destructive actions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized MCP Server or Malicious Skill Runtime Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'often selected and invoked at runtime, with no review' and cites Snyk research: '76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984 analyzed.' Article explicitly identifies lack of visibility into agent tool selection as the control gap: 'If you don't know what agents are using, you can't know what risk is entering the development workflow.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a baseline of approved MCP servers and skills per agent, derived from static manifests. Alert on runtime invocations of tools not in the baseline. Cross-reference invoked tool identifiers (name, version, registry) against threat intelligence feeds for known-malicious or exploitable components. Flag dynamic tool selection that deviates from declared dependencies.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Leading to Unintended Agent Action
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'prompt injection inside development workflows' as a key risk vector enabled by agents acting 'faster than human review can intervene.' This is the attack surface enabling constraint bypass (the database deletion example).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM prompt inputs for injection markers ('ignore', 'pretend', adversarial suffixes, role-play requests). Correlate unusual prompt content with unexpected downstream agent behaviors (tool calls, constraint violations, unsafe commands). Alert on prompts containing instructions that conflict with the agent's declared safety guidelines or operational constraints.

suggestion.title: Agent-Generated Code Bypassing Repository Review Gates
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'generate production-ready code' and 'This doesn't replace the SDLC; rather, it overlays and accelerates it.' Agents bypass human checkpoints by completing full workflows 'in a single uninterrupted sequence' without waiting for approval gates designed for human-authored code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits/merges authored by agent service accounts that skip required code-review approvals or merge-request gates. Prioritize changes that introduce dependencies, modify permissions, or affect high-risk systems. Cross-reference commit content (dependency additions, privilege escalations, secrets injection) against agent's declared authorization scope.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Dependency or Skill Addition by Agent Without Manifest Declaration
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'These inputs can become part of your software supply chain even though they were never declared as traditional dependencies. Additionally, they're often selected and invoked at runtime, with no review.' Agents may add transitive dependencies or tools without updating manifest files, breaking supply-chain visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare runtime dependency resolution (observed via import logs, package manager calls) against declared manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, etc.). Alert on runtime-only dependencies not declared upstream. Flag agents adding packages from repositories outside the organization's approved registry. Cross-reference new packages against CVE databases and supply-chain threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Data Access or Exfiltration Through Unapproved Tool Invocations
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'data exposure through tool calls' as a core risk. Agents invoke APIs and query systems with permissions they inherit, potentially accessing sensitive data (credentials, PII, internal configs) that would require explicit approval if requested by a human.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-agent baselines of data-access APIs and query patterns. Alert on agents accessing sensitive tables/APIs (secrets, identity stores, customer data) outside their declared operational scope. Flag high-volume queries from agent service accounts or queries returning large result sets. Monitor for tool invocations that expose credentials or internal system configuration.

suggestion.title: Access Attempts to OFAC-Sanctioned Crypto Exchanges
suggestion.rationale: Article designates Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex as sanctioned entities. States: 'Nobitex is believed to have helped evade economic sanctions and also facilitated transactions linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).' Detection should flag internal users or systems attempting to interact with these platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex domains/IPs. Alert on any internal user or system accessing these exchanges, particularly from finance, crypto-trading, or high-value employee accounts.

suggestion.title: IRGC-Affiliated Ransomware Ransom Payment Flows
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'wallets associated with ransomware threat actors related to the IRGC.' Establishes a direct link between IRGC-affiliated groups and ransomware payment infrastructure. Should detect when internal ransom demands are being routed through Iranian exchanges or IRGC-linked wallets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ransomware attack indicators (encryption artifacts, ransom notes, C2 communications) with evidence of crypto-exchange login or API calls to known IRGC-linked addresses or Iranian exchange platforms. Flag ransom notes mentioning Iranian exchanges or IRGC-affiliated groups.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Stablecoin Movements to Iranian Central Bank
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Nobitex also helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins used to prop up the plummeting value of the Iranian rial.' Massive stablecoin inflows are a detectable sanctions-evasion pattern with financial impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for USDT/USDC/DAI flows to known Central Bank of Iran addresses and Iranian exchange wallets. Alert on transaction volumes exceeding 3σ of historical mean or transfers >$10M in a 24-hour window to these entities.

suggestion.title: Designated Individual Nobitex Executive Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article names four OFAC-designated Nobitex executives: 'Amir Hossein Rad' (chairman), 'Seyed Ali Khoee' (CEO), 'Seyed Mohammad Ali Aghamir Mohammad Ali' (co-founder), and blockchain lead (unnamed). Detect any post-designation activity by these individuals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crypto exchanges, banking platforms, and blockchain analytics for account activity matching names, known email addresses, passport numbers, or phone numbers of the four designated individuals. Alert on any login, transfer, or trade activity after June 2026 designation date.

suggestion.title: Predatory Sparrow Breach Activity & Stolen Asset Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'In June 2025, the pro-Israel "Predatory Sparrow" hacking group claimed to have breached Nobitex, stealing digital assets worth roughly $90 million.' Specific actor, victim, and ~$90M in stolen cryptocurrency should be monitored for downstream movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for known Predatory Sparrow TTPs (exploit kits, malware families, C2 infrastructure if published). Cross-reference blockchain intelligence for movement of the ~$90M in assets stolen from Nobitex in June 2025. Alert on detection of Predatory Sparrow malware or known attacker IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: IRGC Dominance in Iranian Crypto Ecosystem (Baseline Shift)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Chainalysis: 'addresses associated with the IRGC accounted for over 50% of the value received by the Iranian crypto ecosystem in Q4 2025' vs. historical lower baseline. A >50% shift in ecosystem share is anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish monthly IRGC-linked address clusters via blockchain intelligence. Track IRGC inflow share of total Iranian crypto ecosystem. Alert when share exceeds historical 3-month baseline by >20 percentage points or enters >50% territory, indicating coordinated large-value movement.

suggestion.title: Malicious Windows Search URI Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability'—attack delivery is a crafted URI triggering forced authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for invocation of Windows Search processes (SearchIndexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) with suspicious URI arguments containing file:// or search:// schemes embedding SMB, HTTP, or attacker-controlled hosts. Flag attempts to open search queries referencing external IP addresses or non-trusted domains.

suggestion.title: Forced NTLM Authentication from Windows Search Process
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'Steal NTLMv2 Hashes'—vulnerability triggers Windows to initiate NTLM auth to attacker-controlled or monitored host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication requests (type-3 messages, Sign-and-Seal failures, 4625/4768 auth events) originating from Windows Search service context to unexpected external IPs or non-DC hosts. Correlate SearchIndexer.exe process execution with outbound port 445/139/3389 connections.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Windows Search Service Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Windows Search components do not normally initiate outbound network connections; any external network I/O from search processes is a strong indicator of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: Windows Search processes should not connect outbound. Alert on SearchIndexer.exe or SearchProtocolHost.exe initiating connections to non-RFC1918 addresses, SMB ports (445/139), or ports associated with credential relaying (3389, 5985). Exclude internal domain controllers and known indexing services.

suggestion.title: NTLM Relay Attack Following Hash Capture
suggestion.rationale: Once NTLMv2 hash is intercepted, attacker can relay it for lateral movement or impersonation. Implied by 'Steal' language in threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NTLM relay signatures: rapid NTLM authentication to multiple hosts from single source within short time window, successful auth following sign-and-seal negotiation failures, or NTLM auth originating from non-domain-joined machines. Cross-correlate with Windows Search process events to identify source.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'install an extension that extracts the GitHub OAuth token' — requires detection of extension source anomalies and post-install credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory for unsigned or non-marketplace-sourced extensions. Alert on extension process spawning with tokens in environment or arguments. Track extension installation events from unusual sources (github.dev URLs, non-standard package managers).

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev' — requires detection of credential access patterns in development tool contexts and browser storage queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing browser localStorage/sessionStorage for 'github.com' or 'github.dev' tokens. Monitor for network egress of valid GitHub OAuth tokens. Track credential variable expansion (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN) by unexpected child processes of VS Code.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Enumeration via Compromised Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PoC that 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access' — requires API-level detection of high-volume or unusual enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls (api.github.com/user/repos, /user/installations) from single token within short time window with high repository count or cross-organization scope. Correlate with token creation time and legitimate developer activity baseline.

suggestion.title: Webview Message Passing Exploitation in VS Code
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers abuse 'VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system' and run 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses' — requires detection of webview IPC manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code process for webview postMessage/onMessage event handlers with suspicious payloads. Alert on synthetic input events (KeyEvent, MouseEvent) originating from webview context. Track modification of VS Code settings or extension configuration JSON from browser-based code.

suggestion.title: Keystroke Injection via WebView in Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly 'simulate[s] keypresses in the main editor' to automate extension installation — requires detection of synthetic input injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VS Code processes receiving keystroke events from webview context without user interaction telemetry. Monitor for programmatic UI automation (accessibility APIs, SendInput, xdotool) spawned by VS Code child processes or webview scripts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious github.dev Cookie/Auth Flow Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation is 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev' and describes 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev' — requires detection of abnormal auth flow manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to github.com containing Authorization headers destined for github.dev redirects. Monitor for rapid cookie deletion on github.dev followed by re-authentication. Detect Bearer token strings in HTTP request bodies or unusual OAuth callback parameters.

suggestion.title: Minecraft-related process spawning shells or system tools
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users' — direct attack vector. Pipeline should detect Minecraft launcher or java.exe (from game directory) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Minecraft-related parent process (javaw.exe, minecraft-launcher.exe with game-directory ancestry) executing command shell or scripting interpreter. Alert on first occurrence per endpoint.

suggestion.title: Pirated archive extraction to execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' — archives (ISO, ZIP, RAR) are delivery mechanism. Correlate extraction events to suspicious binary execution from same directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Archive extraction from Downloads/AppData/Temp (WinRAR, 7-Zip, or built-in) followed within 2 minutes by execution of unsigned/high-entropy binary from extraction target directory.

suggestion.title: CountLoader command-and-control beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CountLoader Hits 86K' — named malware family with published IOCs. Pipeline should identify C2 domains and detect beacon-like traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodic HTTP/DNS requests to known CountLoader C2 infrastructure (should be extracted from article references or threat feeds) at regular intervals with low payload bytes. Low false-positive if source is user-context process from temp directory.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer behavioral detection via resource hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies miners as outcome: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' High-fidelity detection: sustained CPU utilization >85%, memory patterns consistent with SHA/AES operations, mining-pool network communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process with sustained CPU >85% for >5 consecutive minutes AND outbound connections to known mining pools (monero, cryptonight, etc.) OR process from Temp spawned with zero parent process visible. Correlate with memory allocation patterns.

suggestion.title: Pirated software site access preceding suspicious archive download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Spread via pirated content' — supply chain compromise. Detect access to piracy sites/CDNs (TPB mirrors, Rarbg, RARBG proxies, etc.) followed by archive or executable landing in Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Browser or download manager connecting to known piracy domain or RARBG-associated CDN, followed by large archive file (>100MB) or executable in Downloads folder within 10 minutes. Escalate if followed by extraction.

suggestion.title: Bulk Tenant/Subscriber ID Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution' — attackers iterate through sequential IDs to extract records from all institutions. Pipeline missed detection for parameter manipulation and resource enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency sequential API requests with incrementing or enumerating resource IDs (tenant_id, subscriber_id, org_id) to the same endpoint within short time windows. Alert on burst patterns where request count and parameter variance exceed baseline for unauthenticated or low-privilege API consumers.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Exposing PII/Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states the endpoint 'required no authentication and no session of any kind' yet 'contained named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles'. Detection should flag APIs returning identity/credential data without auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API responses containing PII patterns (full names, phone numbers, email addresses, internal identifiers) when the request originated from an unauthenticated or sessionless caller. Cross-reference response size and field count against known schema for sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin API Requests Exfiltrating Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Detection should catch CORS misconfiguration abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API requests with Origin headers pointing to external/untrusted domains targeting sensitive endpoints. Flag responses containing organizational records, PII, or internal codes when request source lacks authentication context. Use CORS policy audit logs as baseline.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Transaction Submission Using Harvested Internal Codes
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name' — this is impact via credential abuse. Detection should catch submissions using internally-harvested codes from non-officer sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on loan application submissions where the internal personnel code (extracted from API) maps to an officer different from the authenticated user submitting the form. Cross-reference submission source IP/device against historical patterns for that personnel code.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Vendor Portal Asset Discovery via DNS/Certificate Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the asset 'entered the bank's external footprint when the vendor onboarded the bank to the platform' but remained undetected for 345 days because annual scopes missed it. Detection should catch new vendor-hosted assets appearing on bank subdomains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new subdomains registered or appearing in certificate transparency logs under the bank's domain that match third-party vendor naming patterns. Alert on subdomains pointing to out-of-band infrastructure (vendor IP ranges, CDNs, SaaS platforms) not previously inventoried.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality'—direct T1055 indicator with forensic artifacts in Documents folders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process spawning legitimate Windows executables (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, regsvcs.exe, rundll32.exe) with suspicious parent-child relationships. Alert on memory injection patterns or legitimate executables loaded with unsigned DLLs immediately after Python writes to user Documents directory.

suggestion.title: Telegram API-Based Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure'—non-standard C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS traffic to api.telegram.org from non-browser processes. Monitor for Telegram bot token patterns in network traffic and process arguments. Alert on rapid sequential Telegram API calls indicating command polling.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Traffic Masquerading as Legitimate
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests'—evasion of network detection via legitimate-looking surface indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike beacons via fixed-size HTTP response patterns, unusual request intervals, or legitimate User-Agent strings originating from non-browser processes. Alert on rundll32.exe/regsvcs.exe with outbound HTTPS at consistent intervals.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel...delegated to remote agents, with results being reassessed'—programmatic reconnaissance at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential LDAP queries from single source within minutes. Detect execution of net.exe, dsquery.exe, or ldifde.exe in automated patterns. Flag queries targeting user objects, group membership, or organizational unit structures in high-frequency loops.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker Proxy for C2 Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server'—legitimate infrastructure weaponized as C2 proxy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag persistent traffic from non-standard processes to Cloudflare edge IPs (104.16.0.0/12, 1.1.1.1/8). Monitor for repeated connections to same Cloudflare IP with variable request content patterns. Correlate with suspicious parent process or command-line indicators.

suggestion.title: Polymorphic Encrypted Payload Generation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states Python tool 'wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables or DLLs'—high-entropy, mutating malware artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes writing high-entropy EXE/DLL files to temp or Documents directories. Alert on unsigned binaries loaded from user-writable paths immediately after write events. Flag DLL/executable loads with non-standard parents (Python, cmd.exe spawned by Python).

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Linux Kernel Vulnerable Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' via Splunk SPL and Defender KQL templates; pipeline generated zero use cases. This is CISA KEV (actively exploited, federal due date 2026-06-05) — asset exposure is the baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Linux hosts with kernel versions vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492 cgroups v1 release_agent improper authentication bypass. Query asset inventory, patch-management systems, and vulnerability scanners for systems matching affected kernel versions that are either unpatched or deployed past the federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-05.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release_Agent Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature'; this describes the exploitation mechanism but pipeline generated no detection for the actual privilege-escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious cgroups v1 release_agent write operations or execution of scripts/binaries written to cgroup release_agent paths. Correlate with process execution from unprivileged contexts followed by elevated-capability process spawning, indicative of post-exploit privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Public-Facing Service Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article maps to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application'; pipeline did not surface this technique or generate corresponding behavioral detections for exploitation attempts against exposed Linux services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic to public-facing Linux services (web servers, SSH, containers) for anomalous request patterns consistent with CVE-2022-0492 exploitation probes (e.g., cgroup-related syscall sequences, cgroups filesystem mount discovery, release_agent path traversal attempts).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2025-48595 in Android Framework
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references standard asset-exposure hunt templates as the entry point. Baseline detection for all unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Android devices or systems running Android Framework where vulnerability scans detect CVE-2025-48595. Cross-reference against patch management to confirm unpatched status. Escalate any unpatched systems facing network exposure or untrusted inputs.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack vector: 'integer overflow vulnerability that allows for code execution.' Detecting exploitation attempts is critical to stop attacks in flight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework component logs and system logs for signs of integer overflow exploitation: abnormal memory access patterns, segmentation faults, or unexpected process crashes in Framework services. Correlate with suspicious input patterns or unusual network requests to the device immediately before crashes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Android Framework Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow for local privilege escalation.' Detecting post-exploitation privilege escalation blocks the attacker's path to system compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected privilege elevation initiated by Android Framework processes or child processes spawned from them. Flag requests for elevated capabilities, uid 0 acquisition, or permission grants beyond the Framework's standard allowlist. Correlate timing with detected exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Brute Force Attack Detection — Authentication Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'brute-force attack' as the attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for T1110 despite clear mention in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequences of failed authentication attempts against Dashlane web portal or SSO, particularly from a single source IP or against multiple user accounts within short time window. Establish baseline for failed login attempts per hour and alert on 10x+ deviations. Correlate with successful login immediately after failure spike.

suggestion.title: Vault Exfiltration — Bulk Encrypted Data Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded' — direct evidence of data exfiltration phase. Pipeline generated no detection for T1537 or T1020.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusually large data transfers from authenticated Dashlane user accounts (>100MB vault files). Flag downloads of multiple user vaults from single source within short timeframe. Correlate large downloads immediately following brute-force attempt spike with successful login.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise Indicator — Post-Breach Login Pattern Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies credential compromise. Article implies attackers obtained working credentials but pipeline identified no T1098 technique for account takeover detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24 hours of incident detection, monitor for logins to compromised user accounts from impossible travel locations, unusual time-of-day patterns, or new device identities. Dashlane users whose credentials were brute-forced would show login activity during the attack window and post-compromise access from attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing / Password Spray Against SaaS Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attack against password vault service implies attacker targeting high-value credential store. Pipeline did not identify T1110.004 password spray or T1078 account enumeration techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect distributed brute-force attempts: monitor for 3+ failed logins to distinct Dashlane accounts from different source IPs within 60-second window (spray pattern). Flag authentication failures where user enumeration preceded the attempts (404 errors on account lookup endpoints then failed auth).

suggestion.title: Incident Timeline Correlation — Attack Window Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses specific attack occurred on specific date range. Pipeline extracted no temporal IOCs or timeline data, missing the window for detecting other intrusions or copycat attacks during the same period.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish confirmed incident timeline from Dashlane disclosure. Cross-reference organization's authentication logs, VPN access, and firewall logs for any login attempts to Dashlane accounts during the disclosed attack window. Flag any concurrent access from IPs geolocating outside normal user patterns.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Exploitation via Malicious Archive Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver...' — indicates CVE-based or patched-flaw exploitation in archive extraction. Pipeline extracted no initial-access UC despite clear phishing/spearphishing delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious WinRAR.exe process spawn with archive file paths containing embedded executables, or extraction of PE files to %TEMP% / %AppData% followed by immediate child-process execution. Alert on WinRAR.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe within 5 seconds of extraction.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm / GammaSteel Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two specific malware families (GammaWorm, GammaSteel) delivered via WinRAR; pipeline generated zero malware-detection UC. Expected file-hash IOCs, behavioral signatures, or memory patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GammaWorm/GammaSteel execution via known file hashes, behavioral patterns (e.g., unusual DLL injection, encrypted C2 callbacks), or command-line artifacts. Flag processes spawned by WinRAR that load suspicious DLLs or establish outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation C2 Communication from GammaWorm/GammaSteel
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery implies command-and-control callback; article title references two malware families but pipeline extracted no network-based detection UC or C2 infrastructure IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS requests from processes spawned by WinRAR extraction to non-whitelisted external domains. Look for suspicious User-Agent strings, encrypted payloads, or beaconing patterns consistent with GammaWorm/GammaSteel command-and-control.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Process Anomaly Detection (UAC-0010 / Gamaredon TTPs)
suggestion.rationale: Article references Gamaredon, a known APT group with documented TTP patterns. Pipeline missed TTP-specific detections for WinRAR abuse by this threat actor (e.g., specific malware staging techniques, parent-process relationships, timing patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WinRAR.exe spawning unexpected children or with unusual command-line arguments (e.g., -x flags combined with password bypass attempts). Correlate with Gamaredon YARA rules or registry persistence patterns documented in prior attacks (e.g., Run keys, startup folders).

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Spearphishing Delivery Chain (Ukraine-Targeted)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Ukraine as target; Gamaredon is known for spearphishing campaigns. Pipeline identified no initial-delivery or targeting-context UC despite 'Against Ukraine' in title indicating geopolitical targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spearphishing emails containing WinRAR attachments with .rar extensions or masqueraded file types. Correlate recipient domain/organization with Ukraine-based entities. Flag emails from spoofed senders matching Gamaredon's historical pretexting patterns (e.g., government, defense, utility sectors).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Device Detection Post-Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes patch release baseline: 'Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws.' Detection must cover devices not applying patches within SLA window, especially given 'high' severity and one known active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android patch application timestamps against device inventory. Flag devices remaining 2+ weeks behind current patch level post-release. Cross-correlate against threat intelligence for active exploitation of the 124 patched CVEs to identify priority-remediation targets.

suggestion.title: Android 0-Day / Known CVE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One Actively Exploited' flaw. This establishes real-world attack traffic exists targeting the June 2026 patch set. Pipeline must include behavioral and signature-based detection for exploitation of this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploit payloads via Android crash signatures, SELinux denial spikes, and memory corruption indicators. Correlate privilege escalation attempts with known exploit patterns for the actively-exploited CVE.
