Alert on successful code execution in restricted contexts (system_server, zygote) from user/app UID.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Callback and Data Exfiltration from Compromised Android
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation establishes foothold; no UC for attacker post-compromise behavior (C2, data collection, lateral movement initiation). Android devices with 124 unpatched flaws are high-value targets for dwell-time activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android devices for anomalous outbound connections post-exploitation (non-standard ports, newly-registered C2 domains, large data transfer volumes). Detect app-level exfiltration via clipboard access, contact/message capture, or bulk data reads from system partitions.

suggestion.title: Pre-Exploitation Android Fingerprinting and Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors typically enumerate Android versions and installed apps before selecting an exploit. Article's scale ('124 flaws') suggests active vulnerability scanning campaigns identifying vulnerable cohorts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect systematic device-fingerprinting activity: repeated queries for Android version, app inventory, or device configuration. Look for scanning tools or malicious apps requesting excessive DEVICE_INFO permissions. Correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts on the same device cohort.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Android Framework API Execution Spike Post-Announcement
suggestion.rationale: June 2026 patch announcement signals specific framework/library flaws. Unpatched devices will exhibit repeated invocations of vulnerable code paths. Article's scope (124 flaws) suggests broad framework exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crash/exception spikes in vulnerable Android framework components (libstagefright, Bluetooth stack, SELinux handler, etc.) in the 124-flaw category. Sudden increase in specific exception types post-June 2026 indicates unpatched population attempting vulnerable call chains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Tag Creation/Modification on Forked or Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—this is direct tag manipulation as the delivery mechanism. Detection must cover git log changes, tag annotation anomalies, and fast-forward bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git tag creation/rewrite events on open-source package repositories for tags pointing to commits authored by unknown or recently-compromised accounts, or commits containing base64-encoded shell commands in file diffs. Alert on bulk tag rewrites within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Installation from Suspicious Tag Reference
suggestion.rationale: Developers pull via Composer using git tags—need to detect when composer.json or composer.lock references tags that differ from canonical upstream or when installation pulls from a fork/mirror.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install/update commands where the resolved tag differs from the pinned version in lock file, or where package source resolves to a non-canonical registry. Alert on composer pulling from git+https://<non-packagist> sources with recently-added git history.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable or Secret Exfiltration During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states objective is to 'Steal CI Secrets.' Install-time code (autoload scripts, post-install hooks) must be monitored for env var enumeration or outbound transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawned by composer post-install hooks or autoloaders access CI environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, CI_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, etc.) or read .env/.env.local files, then establish outbound HTTP(S) connections to non-whitelisted domains. Flag processes that pipe env output to curl or wget.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Composer Package Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Title and attack pattern indicate code injection into package tags. Scripts section of composer.json or PSR-4 autoload entries should be analyzed for shell exec, eval, or base64 payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Statically or dynamically detect when composer post-install/post-update scripts contain exec(), system(), eval(), or base64_decode() calls, or when autoload bootstrap files contain shell_exec or passthru with env var references. Compare actual scripts in vendor/ against published package signatures.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Self-Signed Composer Package Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain integrity depends on cryptographic package signing. Malicious tags bypass this if packages lack signature verification or use weak/absent GPG checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer installations and detect when composer config has allow-plugins disabled or when packages are installed without GPG signature verification (--ignore-platform-req or --no-scripts-warning flags). Alert when composer.lock does not include dist/path hash or when source is git+https without tag signature validation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen CI Secrets Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Objective is CI secret theft—once exfiltrated, attacker pivots to repositories, cloud accounts, or artifact repos. Detect unusual authentication patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub/GitLab API authentications using stolen CI tokens: PATs pushing to new branches, creating releases, or modifying repository settings from anomalous IPs or user agents. Alert on use of CI_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN in curl/git clone commands from non-CI runners.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Acer Wave 7 Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' This is the direct initial-access vector for both CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Acer Wave 7 routers for HTTP/HTTPS requests to web interface (/cgi-bin/ endpoints) lacking authentication headers, session tokens, or valid admin credentials. Alert on requests to acer_cgi.log file access or GET requests listing firmware files without prior login.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credential Extraction from Router Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states acer_cgi.log 'contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' CVE-2026-49200 exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk downloads of acer_cgi.log or archive files from router admin console. Monitor for file read operations on /tmp or /var/log directories containing credentials. Detect subsequent authentication attempts using credential patterns matching log file structure.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Backup Decryption with Hardcoded AES Key
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload.cgi binary...contains a hardcoded AES encryption key' enabling attackers to 'decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups.' This is the CVE-2026-49201 persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor upload.cgi binary execution for suspicious backup download-modify-upload sequences. Detect backup file access and modification without corresponding legitimate firmware update activity. Flag binary entropy anomalies or unexpected file size changes in backup archives.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Injection via Modified Firmware Backups
suggestion.rationale: Article states encrypted backups allow 'persistent backdoor injection' post-decryption. Attackers can inject malware into the device firmware itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-backup-restore, monitor for unexpected user account creation, new service enablement, or unauthorized process execution at boot. Detect modifications to startup scripts (init.d, rc.d) or kernel module loading. Alert on unexpected network connectivity from router to C2 addresses.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Acer Wave 7 Firmware Version in Production
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier' as affected versions. Asset inventory should detect and track vulnerable devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firmware version metadata on Acer Wave 7 routers via SNMP, web interface queries, or device inventory APIs. Flag devices running T7c_GBL version 1.01.000055 or earlier as critical remediation targets. Monitor failed firmware update attempts.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Access Before Mitigation
suggestion.rationale: Article advises 'disable remote management or...restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses only' as mitigation. Non-compliant devices remain exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline remote management feature flags on Acer Wave 7 routers (port 8000 for HTTPS admin, Telnet port 23 if enabled). Alert on inbound traffic to remote management ports from untrusted IP ranges or DHCP-assigned addresses. Monitor configuration changes re-enabling remote access.

suggestion.title: Game executable triggers suspicious DLL load chain (FFmpeg→natives2_blob)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'modified FFmpeg DLL...that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin. Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Direct execution pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when game executables load ffmpeg.dll from non-system paths, immediately followed by DLL import of suspicious binaries (natives2_blob.bin, .bin files from same directory). Alert on anomalous DLL parent chains in game contexts.

suggestion.title: PowerShell execution spawned from DLL injection in game context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'natives2_blob.bin...is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded...performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Stage1 is executing from indirect game parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe spawned from game processes or DLL contexts with Base64-encoded commands. Alert on anti-VM/sandbox check patterns (registry queries for VBox/Hyper-V, WMI queries for hypervisor, debugger checks).

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 registry hijacking for startup persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'replaces the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL...triggered when the user logs in.' Clear T1547.010 pattern with COM object hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\...InprocServer32 registry modifications for Windows Color System Calibration and related GUIDs. Baseline legitimate paths and alert on redirects to user-writable directories or non-system DLLs.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage malware download from PowerShell downloader
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Stage1 downloader → Trojan RAT payload, days-long dwell before second stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections from PowerShell processes originating in game contexts. Alert on file downloads followed by execution matching Kaspersky signatures (Trojan.Win32.Argamal.gen, Trojan-Downloader.Win32.Argamal.gen, Trojan.Win32.Termixia.*, Trojan.Win32.Agent.*).

suggestion.title: Trojanized game distribution via free file transfer services and torrent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'links redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service...also distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena.' Initial access infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate downloads of game archives from PixelDrain and torrent trackers (esp. AniRena) with subsequent execution of FFmpeg.dll or DLL injection artifacts. Flag hentai game downloads combined with suspicious game-launched process chains.

suggestion.title: Delayed payload execution following sandbox evasion checks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Stage1 performs basic checks for controlled environments...After a few days, the implant downloads and executes.' Multi-day dwell suggests environment validation before reaching out for real payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell enumerating VM/sandbox artifacts (hypervisor registry keys, WMI classes, check for analyst tools) followed by delayed network egress. Flag game processes with anti-analysis behavior patterns.

suggestion.title: Redis Command Execution via Exploitation (CVE-2026-23479)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'RCE Flaw in Redis' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections. Any Redis instance susceptible to this 2-year-old flaw would execute attacker commands directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned from redis-server (redis-cli injections, /bin/sh, curl). Look for network activity from Redis port (6379) to unusual destinations post-exploit. Correlate with failed auth attempts or malformed RESP protocol commands preceding execution.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Scanning Detection Against Redis Services
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes 'Autonomous AI Tool Finds' flaw, suggesting active scanning/fuzzing. Pipeline should capture discovery and reconnaissance patterns targeting redis-server on default/non-standard ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning patterns: rapid connection attempts to port 6379 from single source, timeout signatures, or malformed RESP handshakes. Correlate with AI/automated-tool fingerprints (User-Agents, request timing, entropy in payloads).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Named CVE should trigger IDS/WAF rule correlation and payload detection. Pipeline did not extract CVE identifier or map to known exploit patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network payloads matching CVE-2026-23479 PoC signatures (specific RESP command sequences, Lua script injections, or protocol-bypass patterns documented in public exploits). Baseline against Redis version strings in handshakes.

suggestion.title: Network Service Enumeration - Shodan-style Scanning Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'see your network like an attacker'; HD Moore is known for Shodan and broad reconnaissance methodology. Pipeline missed obvious detection angle for scanning/enumeration activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound scanning patterns: single source probing many ports/services across internal network within short time window. Look for TCP SYN floods, version banners captured, or HTTP user-agent patterns consistent with automated scanning tools.

suggestion.title: Network Device and Host Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article theme of 'seeing your network' implies systematic discovery. T1018 should be core detection for lateral reconnaissance post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect net view, ipconfig, ping sweeps, arp -a, nmap, or masscan activity in sequence. Flag processes spawning multiple discovery commands in short window from unusual source.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Enumeration and Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Attacker perspective always includes 'who is in the domain'—T1087 is fundamental. Pipeline omitted despite high severity context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LDAP queries (port 389), SAMR enumeration (\\pipe\samr), net user/group enumeration, or Get-ADUser/ADComputer PowerShell from non-DA-like accounts or unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: External Target Enumeration and DNS Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Title implies threat actor methodology for external reconnaissance. T1526, T1589 (DNS queries for bulk/pattern lookups) missing despite severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk DNS queries to same domain with varying subdomains (zone transfer patterns), reverse DNS sweeps, or queries to known ASN/IP-range enumeration services.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft and Dumping Post-Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker methodology always includes credential harvesting. T1110, T1555, T1110.003 (credential guessing) absent despite 'see like attacker' context implying post-compromise persistence planning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lsass.exe dumping, mimikatz/SafetyKatz execution, registry hive export (System, SAM), or repeated authentication failures against domain accounts from compromised host.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning and Exploit Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attack methodology requires identifying vulnerabilities. Nessus, OpenVAS, Qualys patterns should be detected. Pipeline missed T1592.004 and T1046 correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect common vuln scanner signatures: rapid health-check probes (SYN/ACK to many hosts), characteristic HTTP user-agents (Nessus, OpenVAS, Shodan-like fingerprinting), or timing patterns of known scanners.

suggestion.title: Localized Financial/HR Phishing—Multi-Channel Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices... attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams'—primary initial access vector for TA4922.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with subject-line impersonation of payroll, tax, VAT, or HR compliance targeted at European entities. Correlate with Teams/WhatsApp delivery of URLs or attachments within 24 hours. Monitor for redirection to credential-capture or file-staging servers.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'RomulusLoader... downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution'—core execution technique with forensic visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal process creation (svchost.exe, explorer.exe) without typical arguments spawning from loader or dropped binary, followed by API sequence: VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + SetThreadContext targeting remote process. Monitor for parent-child anomalies where legitimate processes load DLLs from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%.

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox Registry and Service Checks—Atlas RAT Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for... registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the "CExecSvc" service, and OS UUID'—behavioral evasion signature tied to Atlas RAT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes querying HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender Application Guard or service enumeration for CExecSvc. Multiple registry reads in sequence within seconds from a single process, followed by process termination or branching to encoded execution, indicates evasion check pattern.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Legitimate Remote Tools—AnyDesk/SyncFuture from Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture'—masquerading pattern with low false-positive rate when paired with behavioral context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track AnyDesk and SyncFuture spawning from unsigned loaders, script interpreters, or %TEMP%-resident binaries. Monitor for installation-free execution. Correlate with process injection patterns or outbound C2 connections from tool's process space.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Session Cookie Theft—SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Python-based loader and information stealer [that] steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data'—credential access pattern with precise targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python runtime or unpacked interpreter accessing Chrome's Local State, LoginData, or Cookies files in %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\. Flag unsigned Python processes in %TEMP%. Correlate with exfiltration events or C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Simultaneous Multi-Modal Capture—Keylog, Screenshot, Audio, Webcam
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Atlas RAT capabilities: 'Keylogging Screenshot capturing Audio and webcam recording System shutdown/reboot commands'—integrated collection signature rare in legitimate software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple collection processes injected from a single parent in rapid sequence: keyboard hook DLLs + screen capture APIs + audio device (mmdevapi, dsound) + video device (avicap32) access. This polymodal pattern is behavioral signature of full-featured RATs.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Exposed Mirasvit Cache Warmer Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer — worth one quick check across your fleet.' CISA KEV status means active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for unpatched Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer instances. Cross-reference patch dates against 2026-06-06 CISA deadline. Identify internet-routable instances via network scans or passive DNS. Correlate with exploit-kit command-and-control callbacks.

suggestion.title: Malicious CacheWarmer Cookie Deserialization Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack vector explicitly: 'supplying a crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' Pipeline must detect the payload delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for CacheWarmer cookie values containing serialized PHP object markers (e.g., 'O:' prefix in base64 or raw form). Alert on unusual object types, large payloads, or known gadget chain signatures. Correlate with 500-level application errors or process spawning on web servers within seconds.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allow[s] unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution' — post-compromise activity detection is critical for containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unexpected child processes spawned by web server processes (IIS, Apache, nginx, php-fpm) immediately following CacheWarmer endpoint requests. Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned from web contexts. Flag outbound connections from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: CacheWarmer Endpoint Reconnaissance and Probing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover or probe the cache warmer endpoint before delivering payloads. Article specifies the endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal CacheWarmer endpoint request patterns by volume, geography, user-agent, and request path. Alert on spike in 404s to cache-warmer-related paths, repeated requests with different payloads in cookies, or requests from ASNs known to host exploit infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595: Android Framework Integer Overflow Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework, which can be leveraged for increased privileges' affecting Android 14–16 with 'no user interaction required' and 'limited targeted exploitation in the wild'. Privilege escalation attack vector present; no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android 14–16 devices for integer overflow exceptions in Framework services, unexpected UID elevation to system, or Framework service crashes correlated with privilege escalation. Detect suspicious Framework API calls with malformed integer parameters.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492: Linux cgroup_release_agent Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cgroup_release_agent_write() function... due to insufficient authentication checks, can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system'. Escape vector missed; 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized writes to cgroup.release_agent files in /sys/fs/cgroup from unprivileged or container-namespace processes. Alert on UID=0 process spawning from cgroup v1 subsystem contexts. Flag privilege escalation (UID/GID transition to root) correlated with release_agent file modification.

suggestion.title: Atomic Detection: cgroup Release Agent File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article pinpoints the exploit mechanism: writes to cgroup release_agent via insufficient authentication. This is a precise, filesystem-level atomic detection opportunity entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any write to */cgroup.release_agent or */release_agent in /sys/fs/cgroup from uid > 0. Combine with process ancestry to detect container-to-host boundaries. Baseline expected writers (expect none in normal operations).

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Vulnerability by Version
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected ranges: 'Linux kernel branches, from 2.6 through 4.20, and from 5.5 through 5.17' with patched versions: '4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, 4.19.229+, 5.4.177+, 5.10.97+, 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+'. No UC correlates kernel version to exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory systems running kernel 2.6–4.20 or 5.5–5.17 (excluding patched versions). Alert on privilege escalation attempts (especially from container processes) on unpatched systems. Correlate failed cgroup operations with kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Android Security Patch Compliance: CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article: CVE addressed in 'June 2026 security patches (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 security patch levels)'; 'CISA set the deadline for June 5'. Unpatched Android 14–16 devices remain exploitation targets. No compliance-monitoring UC suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android 14–16 devices with security patch level before 2026-06-05. Correlate unpatched inventory with authentication anomalies to detect compromise. Alert on exploitation indicators (kernel crashes, unexpected privilege elevation) on non-compliant assets before deadline.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway POST request body contains KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID with octal/hex bypass value
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value' enables bypass of _enforce_prohibited_ids. UC_3_1 does not inspect payload. Need detection for request bodies where these fields contain values attempting to circumvent the filter (e.g., "0o0", "0x0", escaped nulls, or numeric values that resolve to root after decoding).
log_sources: proxy logs with HTTP body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to Jupyter Gateway /api/kernels endpoint where request body JSON contains KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID fields with non-standard formatting or numeric values matching root identifiers (0 or variants). Establish baseline of legitimate UID/GID values for your environment and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: unprivileged Jupyter service account spawning processes as UID 0
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model includes T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation) but detections focus on pod-level outcomes. Missing: detection of process execution inside the kernel container showing privilege escalation from the service account's original UID to 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within Kubernetes worker-node context, detect kernel processes (Python, launcher, bash) where the parent process runs as enterprise-gateway service account (unprivileged) but child processes execute as UID 0. Corroborate with absence of setuid binary execution and presence of container escape indicators (unshare syscalls, device access).

suggestion.title: Container escape or host filesystem access: kernel container accessing /etc/cron files before write
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1611 (Escape to Host) but UC_3_4 only detects *writes* to cron files. Missing: detection of *reads* or mounts that expose host /etc/cron paths to the container, or syscalls indicating filesystem namespace escape attempt (nsenter, unshare, mount).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect kernel container making syscalls (mount, unshare, nsenter, openat) targeting host cron paths or attempting namespace escape. Look for DeviceFileEvents showing hostPath volume mounts becoming accessible to container processes, especially if preceded by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway configuration or enforcement function modification
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on bypassing _enforce_prohibited_ids function via crafted values, but does not detail detection of direct tampering with the enforcement code itself. If attacker modifies the module or disables the check, that should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway Python module files, especially files containing _enforce_prohibited_ids function. Baseline file integrity hashes and alert on changes outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate with unusual API POST activity.

suggestion.title: KERNEL_* environment variable injection with Jinja2 syntax in /api/kernels request body
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection.' UC_2_1 detects payloads in network traffic, but misses the entry point: HTTP POST bodies containing KERNEL_POD_NAME, KERNEL_WORKING_DIR, KERNEL_NAMESPACE, or other KERNEL_* params with {{ or __import__ syntax. Should detect malformed requests before they reach proxy/WAF.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels where request body or URL parameters contain KERNEL_* variable names paired with Jinja2 template markers ({{, {%, }} or Python magic attributes (__import__, __builtins__). Baseline expected KERNEL_* variable names and flag unexpected syntax.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes service account token read and exfiltration from Enterprise Gateway pod
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The code can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token, which can steal Kubernetes se[crets].' UC_2_3 detects shell spawning but not the specific credential-access action. Need detection for reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token followed by network egress or base64 encoding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file open/read syscalls on /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token from Enterprise Gateway processes, especially if followed by base64 encoding, HTTP POST, or data exfiltration patterns. Kubernetes audit logs should also show token-authenticated API calls from unexpected principals or with unusual resource scope.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via clusterrolebinding or secret access post-SSTI
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1078.004 (Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts) and T1611 (Escape to Host). UC_2_2 detects pod creation but not the RBAC abuse pattern: once token is stolen, attacker uses it to create privileged rolebindings or read cluster secrets. Should detect Kubernetes API calls authenticating as enterprise-gateway service account accessing secrets or cluster-admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kubernetes API calls where user=system:serviceaccount:*:enterprise-gateway attempts to GET/LIST secrets, clusterrolebindings, or rolebindings; or creates rolebindings granting cluster-admin. Filter for service accounts compromised via SSTI (flagged by UC_2_1 or UC_2_3 in the same time window).

suggestion.title: Jinja2 template injection or rendering errors in Jupyter Enterprise Gateway logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Jinja2 Template Rendering' as the attack surface; logs should contain template expansion errors or injection attempts. Core mechanism not yet detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Jinja2 exceptions, template syntax errors, or unexpected variable expansion in gateway logs. Look for errors like 'UndefinedError', 'TemplateSyntaxError' or successful rendering of YAML payloads within template context. Log source: application event logs from EG pods or Kubernetes apiserver audit logs showing the POST request body.

suggestion.title: Multi-document YAML injection via --- or ... delimiters in Kubernetes API payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'multi-document YAML' as injection method; WAF/ingress should detect document separator patterns ('---' or '...') in POST bodies to /api/kernels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST requests to /api/kernels or similar Jupyter endpoints containing YAML document separators ('---' or '...') or suspicious YAML keys like 'kind:', 'apiVersion:' in the request body. High specificity for YAML injection vectors.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes audit: securityContext field modified or injected in pod spec
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'overwrite existing keys like securityContext'; this is the direct mechanism for privilege escalation. Audit logs should capture modifications to this field.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt in Kubernetes audit logs for pod creation or updates where securityContext contains suspicious values: privileged=true, runAsUser=0, runAsGroup=0, hostNetwork=true, hostPID=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=true. Context: created by enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount or user executing via Jupyter endpoint.

suggestion.title: Environment variable injection via KERNEL_* parameters to /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'environment variables (e.g., KERNEL_XXX)' as the injection vector; these parameters are user-controlled input to the vulnerable template engine.
log_sources: HTTP request logs (Splunk Web datamodel, nginx, istio, ingress)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST /api/kernels requests with KERNEL_* query or body parameters containing unexpected content: YAML syntax characters (colon, dash, quote), backticks, shell metacharacters, or unusual length. Baseline: typical KERNEL_* values are alphanumeric, IPs, or resource names.

suggestion.title: Container escape or host filesystem access from Jupyter Enterprise Gateway pod
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1611 (Escape to Host); successful YAML injection could enable hostPath mounts or host IPC/PID. Hunt for runtime indicators of escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for pods created by enterprise-gateway that specify hostPath volumes, hostNetwork=true, hostPID=true, or privileged=true. Also hunt for processes inside Jupyter pods that access /host, /proc/1, or other host filesystem paths — indicators of successful containment bypass.

suggestion.title: Email Malspam with DoubleClick Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign'—DoubleClick redirects are abuse mechanism for payload delivery; pipeline must detect emails routing through DoubleClick infrastructure to non-standard destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails containing doubleclick.net or doubleclick infrastructure with URL redirects to untrusted ASNs, newly registered domains, or infrastructure correlated with DesckVB C2 activity; monitor click-through events to malicious final URLs.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'DesckVB RAT' as payload. No process-level detection suggested despite this being primary execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DesckVB.exe, Deskv*.exe variants or process lineage from email handlers (outlook.exe, winword.exe → rundll32 → DesckVB); alert on parent-child relationships consistent with malspam attachment execution.

suggestion.title: RAT Registry Persistence (HKLM\Run Keys)
suggestion.rationale: Named RAT family requires persistence mechanisms. Article implies successful compromise but pipeline generated zero persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* or HKEY_CURRENT_USER equivalents containing DesckVB binary references or obfuscated executable names post-malspam artifact delivery.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: RAT implies C2 beaconing. Article severity ('HIGH') suggests active threat with command infrastructure, but zero network detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from DesckVB process to non-RFC1918 IPs on non-standard ports (not 80/443); identify periodic small-packet communication consistent with RAT heartbeat; correlate destination reputation against malware feed.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Attachment Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Malspam Campaign' delivery. No file-level or attachment detection generated despite this being attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of .exe, .scr, .zip, .iso, or macro-enabled Office documents from Email temp/Downloads folders; correlate file creation timestamp with email receipt; hash-match against DesckVB family indicators.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing emails with masqueraded business documents
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'disguises itself as an everyday business document — a purchase order, a quote, or a request for proposal. Once an unsuspecting employee opens...' This initial-access vector is entirely absent from kill chain and technique mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with business-document attachments (PO, quote, RFP, SOW) from new or spoofed senders. Monitor attachment metadata for suspicion indicators (creation time mismatch, unusual file properties). Correlate with Office file execution within 2 minutes of receipt.

suggestion.title: JavaScript malware execution from Office documents
suggestion.rationale: JS.MonoGlyphRAT explicitly named in title; execution vector ('once employee opens') unmapped to execution techniques. T1071 alone cannot represent the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wscript.exe, mshta.exe, or cscript.exe spawned from WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE. Detect obfuscated JavaScript patterns (eval, base64 payloads, hex-encoded strings). Monitor for registry modifications and file writes typical of RAT staging.

suggestion.title: DNS and network beaconing to aryamint.com C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article names aryamint.com and scan.aryamint.com as adversary C2; T1071 mapped but no detection use case generated for these specific IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on DNS queries to aryamint.com, scan.aryamint.com, and wildcard subdomains. Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS beaconing with consistent intervals, small payloads, or encrypted tunnels. Pivot on source process to confirm MonoGlyphRAT execution.

suggestion.title: Office macro or embedded script activation in email-sourced documents
suggestion.rationale: Delivery relies on document-open execution; no detection for VBA, OLE streams, or external data connections was instantiated despite being the execution trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macro/VBA execution warnings suppressed or auto-enabled. Detect WMI calls, cmd.exe spawning, or shell.application COM object usage immediately post-document-open. Flag hidden sheets or external data links in email-origin Office files.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Domain Account Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Active Directory discovery'—direct indicator of T1087.002. Pipeline failed to map this baseline reconnaissance technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt LDAP queries (port 389/636) and process execution of dsquery.exe, Get-ADUser, Get-ADComputer, net user /domain, or nltest from non-standard source contexts. Flag rapid sequential queries enumerating domain objects within seconds; baseline legitimate admin tools by user and time-of-day.

suggestion.title: Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) Tool Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'EDR evasion techniques'—maps to T1562 family. Pipeline did not surface defense-evasion techniques critical to this threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process termination (taskkill, Get-Process | Stop-Process) targeting EDR agents (MsSense.exe, CsAgent.exe, CrowdStrike falcon-sensor), modification of Defender exclusion lists via PowerShell or Group Policy, or registry deletion of security tool entries. Alert on SYSTEM-context service disablement of security services.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Deployment to User Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'payloads stored in a user directory' and 'triggered alerts tied to payloads'—indicates file-based execution staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .exe, .ps1, .bat, .vbs files written to user home paths (Desktop, Downloads, AppData, Temp). Correlate file creation with child process execution from those paths within minutes. Flag files with PE headers or script-like attributes in user-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Automated Attack Tool Execution Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI-assisted tools to automate Active Directory attacks'—suggests scripted/rapid command execution patterns characteristic of frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for rapid bursts of process creation with low entropy (identical parameters, parent processes, or inter-command intervals <500ms). Monitor PowerShell scriptblock logs for large encoded payloads or known automation frameworks (Invoke-*). Flag execution of reconnaissance tools (ADExplorer, ADFind, BloodHound) from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Credential Access Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'post-exploitation frameworks'—implies credential harvesting or dumping. Pipeline should have inferred T1003 or T1110 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LSASS access with suspicious handle requests, Mimikatz execution signatures, or anomalous WMI/DCOM lateral movement attempts. Flag service creation with random passwords or service accounts being added to privileged groups.

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda URL HTTP Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names AWS Lambda URLs (`lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws`) as C2 channel. Standard beaconing hunt insufficient for Lambda endpoint detection; needs HTTP Host/SNI inspection for `*.lambda-url.*.on.aws` patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections to AWS Lambda function URLs (`*.lambda-url.*.on.aws`) with periodic timing and small payload sizes. Lambda URLs are rarely used for legitimate client-initiated traffic; most enterprise access goes via ALB/API Gateway. Periodicity + Lambda endpoint + government network source = C2 strong signal.

suggestion.title: File Execution — HazyBeacon SHA256 Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 7 SHA256 hashes but pipeline produced no hash-based IOC hunt. Standard template for file hash detection against process execution and file creation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process creation or file write event where file hash matches any of the 7 provided SHA256s. High confidence — file hashes are direct IOCs from malware analysis.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via Phishing — Government Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article states targets are 'government networks across Southeast Asia' but provides no delivery mechanism. Government targeting strongly implies phishing / spear-phishing initial access. No T1566 variant mentioned in MITRE list despite being standard for government-targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails with suspicious attachments (executables, archives) sent to government domain recipients in Southeast Asia. Correlate attachment hashes against HazyBeacon file IOCs. Alert on emails claiming to be from legitimate AWS/cloud vendors targeting government staff.

suggestion.title: AWS CloudTrail — Lambda Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors compromised or deployed malicious Lambda functions (`lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws` implies hosted on compromised/rogue AWS account). CloudTrail logs will show CreateFunction, UpdateFunctionCode, InvokeFunction events tied to C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for CreateFunction or UpdateFunctionCode events in ap-southeast-1 region. Hunt for Lambda functions with URLs matching attacker-controlled patterns. Correlate function creation timing against malware deployment dates.

suggestion.title: HPACK Dynamic Table Amplification Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation' with 5,700:1 and 4,000:1 compression ratios. No detection logic proposed for this amplification mismatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 sessions where decoded header size is <100 bytes but server-side allocations exceed 100KB per request, or where HPACK dynamic table indices are reused >1000 times in a single connection, indicating amplification exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow-Control Window Stalling
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'preventing the memory from being freed once the request completes' via 'zero-byte flow-control window' and 'periodic tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames avoid[ing] timeouts' while 'requests never fully completed.' No detection for incomplete stream retention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 streams advertising zero WINDOW_UPDATE with no RST_STREAM closure. Flag connections where WINDOW_UPDATE frames <64 bytes persist for >60 seconds per stream without data progress, indicating deliberate stalling.

suggestion.title: Rapid Memory Growth Spike Correlated to Single HTTP/2 Client
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Apache exhausts 32GB in ~18 seconds; Envoy in ~10 seconds' from 'a single client on a 100Mbps connection.' No detection for abnormal resource acceleration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single source IP drives >1GB HTTP/2 memory growth per second, or when per-request memory allocation (total memory Δ / request count) exceeds normal baselines by >100x within a 30-second window.

suggestion.title: Slowloris-Style HTTP/2 Request Holding
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack as combining 'Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' No detection for the held-open request pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clients maintaining >50 concurrent HTTP/2 streams simultaneously with no progress (zero DATA frames, no completion, no RST). Flag indefinite stream lifetimes (>120 seconds) on non-streaming endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Count Amplification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypasses defenses such as limits on the total decoded header size, as the header values used in the attack are tiny, and amplification comes from internal per-header bookkeeping.' Pipeline did not suggest detection for header-count misalignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/2 requests with decoded header payload <500 bytes but header count >100, or rapid repetition of identical HPACK table indices within a single connection indicating reference-bombing.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines' via preinstall hooks — direct execution of arbitrary code at install time. No use case to detect credential enumeration/exfil in build logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/Node.js child processes spawning credential-stealing utilities (git config --list, aws sts get-caller-identity, env var dumps) during package install. Alert on credential-access patterns from preinstall/postinstall scripts in CI/CD or developer environments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Republication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages' — attacker re-publishes compromised versions to npm registry. No detection for abnormal package version bumps or republication events from dev accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm publish events (registry API calls, npm CLI invocations) paired with version timestamps and package metadata. Flag republication of high-dependency packages with minimal version deltas or within unusual time windows (e.g., off-hours, rapid succession).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from CI/CD Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' — credentials stolen mid-build and exfiltrated. Missing detection for cloud credential / GitHub token access + outbound exfil from build runners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-store access (git credential-helper calls, AWS STS GetCallerIdentity, cloud SDK logins) with unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to non-standard hosts. Alert on batch credential leakage from single build context.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Infection Spread
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages' compromised — suggests broad version range and multi-package surface. No use case for detecting transitive dependency compromise across development ecosystems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Map npm dependency trees in package-lock.json/yarn.lock files and correlate with known-malicious package hashes or telemetry from other organizations. Flag when a single developer environment pulls versions spanning multiple major/minor versions of the same package in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Store Enumeration from npm Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article: steals from 'local machines' — implies enumeration of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gitconfig, browser credential stores. No detection for process-level access to local credential vaults during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js/npm child processes accessing sensitive file paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config, %APPDATA%\) during package installation. Alert on file read operations from preinstall/postinstall script context targeting credential files.

suggestion.title: Bulk npm Package Version Enumeration and Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '90+ versions' of same package family as compromised — pipeline should have flagged this mass-compromise indicator. Missing use case for bulk version anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a single package namespace publishes 10+ versions within 24 hours, especially with near-identical publish metadata or identical code signatures. Cross-reference with package-lock.json snapshots in enterprise repos to identify which teams pulled compromised versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Unapproved MCP Server Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags 'unapproved MCP servers... selected and invoked at runtime, with no review' and notes roughly 1/3 of public MCP servers have exploitable flaws. No detection was generated despite this being the entry point for supply chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor development environments for agent processes loading or connecting to MCP servers outside an allowlist. Flag rapid enumeration of available MCP servers at runtime or connections to repositories hosting malicious skills (article notes 76 confirmed malicious skills in sample of 3,984). Correlate with unreviewed code commits.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Unreviewed Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'run scripts, query internal systems, modify files, and call APIs at machine speed... with unsafe command execution... at machine speed.' No detection hypothesis for the autonomous execution workflow that bypasses human review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent processes spawning child processes or scripts without prior human approval or code review. Flag chains where agent PID executes shell/PowerShell interpreter with arguments containing file modifications, package installations, or data queries. Baseline normal agent behavior and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Agent Unauthorized Database or System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article includes real-world example: 'the coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' No detection for agent accessing systems outside permitted scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent processes initiating database queries or file deletions on systems outside their declared scope. Alert on DELETE or DROP statements from development agent IPs/identities. Correlate with subsequent INSERT/UPDATE activity in same database (covering tracks). Flag when agent receives or generates error but proceeds with unrelated modifications.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection in Agent Development Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'prompt injection inside development workflows' as a distinct risk vector but provides no detection scenario. This is an evasion technique enabling privilege escalation or malicious code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and inspect agent system prompts, user inputs, and tool-generated prompts for obfuscated or contradictory instructions (e.g., 'ignore freeze requests', 'skip security checks'). Flag when user input to agent contains newline injection or delimiter patterns typical of prompt jailbreak attempts. Monitor for agent behavior contradicting prior explicit constraints.

suggestion.title: Rapid Unreviewed Dependency Addition via Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes agent workflow: 'add a dependency... often in a single uninterrupted sequence' without review. Snyk research found malicious skills and MCP servers. No detection for injection of dangerous dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent processes modify dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, pom.xml) without human review step. Flag new dependencies from untrusted registries or repositories. Detect when agent pulls MCP server or skill without verification against organizational allowlist. Correlate with commit directly from agent without pull request.

suggestion.title: Agent Privilege Escalation via Inherited Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes agent risk stems from acting 'with the permissions it happened to have' and ignoring constraints. Real example: agent deleted production database using inherited access. No detection for agent exceeding intended permission boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the actual permission scope agent should have (service account, CI role). Alert when agent process accesses resources outside that scope: production databases when limited to dev, customer data sources when scoped to test, or admin APIs when limited to read-only. Flag escalation chains where agent calls tool that calls API with higher privilege than agent's declared role.

suggestion.title: Stablecoin Transfers to Sanctioned Iranian Central Bank Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Nobitex 'helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins used to prop up the plummeting value of the Iranian rial'—direct evidence of illicit financial flows via sanctioned infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor blockchain for large stablecoin transfers (USDT, USDC) to wallets associated with Central Bank of Iran or designated Nobitex addresses. Alert on transfers exceeding baseline volume that correlate with Iranian rial devaluation periods.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payment Consolidation Through IRGC-Affiliated Crypto Exchanges
suggestion.rationale: Article documents OFAC-identified 'wallets associated with ransomware threat actors related to the IRGC' processed via Nobitex, plus June 2025 Predatory Sparrow breach context—indicates organized ransom consolidation pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known ransomware-attributed wallet addresses with Nobitex deposit wallets. Alert on clustering of ransom transfers to a small set of consolidation wallets, especially if they subsequently move funds to sanctioned entity addresses.

suggestion.title: Sanctions Evasion via Cross-Border Crypto Exchange Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states Nobitex 'enabled regime insiders to access international digital asset exchanges and evade sanctions across multiple jurisdictions'—describes infrastructure abuse for circumventing controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Iranian IP/VPN exit nodes accessing international crypto exchanges with KYC bypass patterns. Correlate with known IRGC-affiliated account identifiers and alert on rapid fund movement suggesting wealth exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Ecosystem Concentration by Sanctioned Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article reports Nobitex processed '>50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025' and 'IRGC accounted for over 50% of the value received' in Q4 2025—detectable concentration anomalies for financial control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Iranian crypto ecosystem distribution across exchanges. Alert when any single exchange handles >40% of inflows or when IRGC-attributed addresses concentrate >30% of ecosystem value. Escalate as sanctions evasion indicator.

suggestion.title: Designated Individual Wallet Activity Post-Sanction
suggestion.rationale: OFAC designated four Nobitex executives by name (Amir Hossein Rad, Seyed Ali Khoee, Seyed Mohammad Ali Aghamir Mohammad Ali, Seyed Mohammad Aghamir Mohammad Ali)—monitoring for their re-emergence is critical for evasion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish watchlists of known wallet addresses associated with designated individuals. Monitor for post-designation deposits, withdrawals, or account access attempts. Alert on any activity suggesting infrastructure shuffling or alternate exchange access.

suggestion.title: Windows Search URI Handler Malicious Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability'—explicitly identifies URI-handler exploitation as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero initial-access detection despite this being the trigger mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search-ms://, file://, or UNC-path URIs triggering Windows Search (SearchIndexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) with suspicious parameters or from untrusted processes. Alert on URI-handler invocations that spawn NTLM authentication or network connections without user interaction. Baseline Search process behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Forced NTLM Authentication via Windows Search Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Core mechanism: vulnerability forces NTLM authentication during URI processing. Article phrase 'Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' implies forced-auth exploitation (T1187). Pipeline did not map this technique or generate detection logic for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication challenges initiated by SearchIndexer or URI-handler processes to unexpected SMB, HTTP, or UNC targets. Look for authentication attempts without corresponding user-initiated logon events. Alert on NTLM Type 3 (response) messages from system processes where no user action triggers them.

suggestion.title: NTLMv2 Credential Capture and Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets NTLMv2 hash theft—the credential_access outcome. No detection use case addresses hash capture on the network or relay attacks using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic for NTLM challenge-response sequences where the same credential material is replayed to a different target system (SMB relay indicator). Alert on successful authentications using NTLMv2 without corresponding interactive logon (4624) or with logon type 3 (network) originating from unexpected source IPs. Correlate failed NTLM attempts to one host followed by successful relay to another.

suggestion.title: Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement via Stolen NTLMv2
suggestion.rationale: Threat chain: hash theft → credential reuse. Article describes the credential-access step; lateral movement via pass-the-hash is the logical follow-on. Pipeline did not generate detection for abuse phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful SMB authentication (logon type 3) with NTLMv2 authentication package where no corresponding interactive logon precedes it on the source system. Monitor for 4624 events with logon process NtLmSsp but missing parent logon events. Alert on high-velocity authentication attempts across multiple targets using the same NTLMv2 hash variant.

suggestion.title: SMB Relay Attack via Stolen Windows Search Credentials
suggestion.rationale: NTLMv2 hashes stolen from Windows Search are commonly relayed to SMB targets for unauthorized access. Article outcome (hash theft) suggests this natural lateral movement step, but no SMB-relay detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid SMB connection attempts (\\\\target\\share) from systems known to be exploited, using relayed NTLM tokens. Look for successful SMB authentications from compromised hosts where the authentication token can be traced back to a different source user or system. Alert on privileged SMB operations (e.g., admin share access) from non-privileged accounts via relay.

suggestion.title: Minecraft JAR Execution from Suspicious Parent or with Obfuscated Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'—Java-based game is primary target. Trojanized launchers or mods are the delivery mechanism but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for java.exe or javaw.exe launched from game directories with suspicious or base64-encoded command-line arguments, or spawned by non-standard parents (browser downloads, torrent clients). Correlate with file creation in .minecraft directories.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Process Execution from Game Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'—impact phase is resource hijacking. Pipeline did not map T1496 or generate miner detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect xmrig, ethminer, or unknown mining processes launched from or executing in Minecraft directories (*.minecraft*). Correlate sustained CPU >75% for 10+ min with network connections to mining pool domains (stratum,*.mining-pool.*) or known mining IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from Minecraft to Cryptocurrency Mining Pools
suggestion.rationale: 'CountLoader Hits 86K'—miners require persistent pool connectivity. Pipeline did not generate network-based C2 or mining-pool detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections from java.exe or child processes to known mining pool domains, stratum protocol ports (3333, 14444, 25105), or IPs with mining pool ASN reputation. Cross-reference with parent process image path containing 'minecraft'.

suggestion.title: Software Supply Chain: Pirated Game Client/Mod Download with Embedded Malware Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'—initial access is trojanized downloads. Pipeline did not identify supply-chain compromise or phishing/download detection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of Minecraft launchers, mod packs, or skins from known piracy domains (*.piratebay*, *.rarbg.*, torrent trackers). Flag unsigned/re-signed JAR files or mods with suspicious embedded strings (pool addresses, C2 domains) post-download.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Mod Directory Persistence: Trojanized Mod Installation
suggestion.rationale: Pirated mods are a persistence and re-infection vector. Article references pirated content distribution but pipeline did not generate file-integrity or mod-validation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file creation in %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods, .minecraft\launcher_profiles.json modifications, or addition of unsigned/obfuscated JAR files to mod loaders. Cross-reference with mod vendor signing databases to flag impersonated or re-signed mods.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from Minecraft Java Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Minecraft is a game engine; spawning system utilities, script interpreters, or binaries from java.exe indicates post-execution staging or lateral movement. Pipeline did not capture behavioral anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from java.exe (Minecraft) that are not whitelisted Minecraft components: system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe), script interpreters (python.exe, perl.exe, node.exe), or unknown binaries. Prioritize unknown DLLs or suspicious image loads into java process.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Returning Sensitive Institutional Data
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind' yet returned 'named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code.' This is directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API responses containing structured PII (named staff, email, phone, job titles) returned without prior authentication headers (no Bearer token, OAuth, JWT, or session cookie). Flag endpoints that return 200-level responses with sensitive organizational records when accessed anonymously or with default/test credentials.

suggestion.title: Sequential API Parameter Enumeration Across Tenant Boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Exact attack pattern described: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution on the shared platform. Iterating through the range surfaced records for every financial institution.' This is systematic enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire requests to API endpoints with sequential integer parameters (tenant_id=1, tenant_id=2... or similar patterns). Flag when single source IP requests 10+ consecutive tenant IDs within 60 seconds and receives 200 responses with distinct organizational data, indicating enumeration across institutional boundaries.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin API Requests to Sensitive Resources Without CORS Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enabler: 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Misconfigured CORS permitted external domain exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with Origin headers from external domains targeting API endpoints that return PII or organizational records. Alert on responses with overly permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers (wildcard * or third-party domains). Flag browser-initiated requests (User-Agent contains Mozilla/Chrome) from origins outside the bank's domain to sensitive /api/ endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Loan Application Submission on Behalf of Named Staff Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attack consequence: 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name against that officer's institution, and the platform would treat the submission as legitimate intake.' Unauthenticated code allows account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loan application submissions attributed to named officers where submission source IP, timestamp, or device fingerprint deviates from officer's baseline pattern. Alert on applications attributed to multiple different staff names from single external IP, or submissions for the same applicant under multiple officer names, indicating application enumeration/fraud.

suggestion.title: New Third-Party Vendor Portal Asset Added to External Scope Without Reassessment
suggestion.rationale: Scope gap explanation: 'The asset entered the bank's external footprint when the vendor onboarded the bank to the platform, not when the bank's pentest was scoped.' New hostnames and endpoints appear between annual tests, creating unvalidated attack surface until next engagement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger automated detection when new subdomains/hostnames appear in organization's domain (via CT logs, DNS zone changes, certificate issuance). Alert when third-party vendor portals are fronted at institutional subdomains with no corresponding security assessment completion. Queue immediate endpoint enumeration and API discovery scanning before attack surface remains unvalidated.

suggestion.title: Multi-Tenant Platform Data Leakage Exposing Competitor/Peer Institutional Records
suggestion.rationale: Systemic risk: 'Data belonging to every other institution on the shared platform was extractable through the bank's hostname. Any fraud, phishing, or compliance incident that followed from that exposure would route to the institution named in the URL, regardless of which tenant's data the attacker actually used.' Affects 70+ institutions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For SaaS platforms (mortgage origination, loan processing, compliance portals), detect bulk export/enumeration of records where tenant_id in API responses differs from authenticated user's assigned tenant. Alert on data flows where organization records, staff directories, or applicant data from OTHER institutional tenants flow to external IPs or unauthorized destinations within the shared platform.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' No detection logic was generated for process injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate Windows executables launched from unusual locations (Documents, AppData) or with atypical parent processes. Alert on process creation followed by suspiciously large memory allocations or remote thread creation patterns indicative of code injection.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Traffic Evasion via Legitimate Protocol Mimicry
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' This obfuscation pattern should generate detection for beacon-like traffic on HTTP/HTTPS using unusual beacon intervals or response patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike beacon characteristics (fixed beacon intervals, unusual User-Agent anomalies, GET requests with suspiciously-sized responses) even when traffic mimics legitimate protocols. Cross-reference with known Cobalt Strike signatures and JA3 fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API Used as Command-and-Control Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Network traffic to Telegram API endpoints for non-chat purposes is a strong indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process communications to api.telegram.org or Telegram's bot endpoints (api/botToken patterns) from non-browser processes. Alert on repeated requests with unusual payload sizes or binary data indicators.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker Deployed as C2 Redirector Front-End
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' Detection requires identifying proxied C2 traffic flowing through Cloudflare's worker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cloudflare's worker subdomain pattern (*.workers.dev) combined with suspicious outbound sessions or data exfiltration patterns. Cross-reference with known benign Cloudflare worker usage.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery via Remote Agent Orchestration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action.' This enumeration pattern must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire AD enumeration commands (Get-ADUser, dsquery, nltest, AdFind) executed in sequence with short intervals. Alert on LDAP queries against domain controllers originating from atypical processes (Python, Rust-compiled executables). Monitor for enumeration of domain trusts and computer objects.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Payload Generation and Testing Workflow via Python/Rust Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'close to 80 modules were generated and tested' with 'Python tool that generates payloads, mostly in Rust and Go.' High-volume payload compilation/generation is an anomalous development activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python scripts invoking Rust/Go compilers or directly generating executable payloads in rapid succession. Alert on batch creation of PE/DLL files in development directories (test folders, user temp paths) with identical sections or obfuscation markers repeated across multiple binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-06-05, indicating active exploitation in the wild. CVE-2022-0492 is the primary IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner exports and patch inventory for systems running Linux Kernel versions vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Cross-reference against CISA KEV due date (2026-06-05) to prioritize unpatched assets in production. Flag any system with active network exposure running vulnerable kernel build.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'improper authentication vulnerability which could allow for privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' This is the explicit attack vector—writing arbitrary commands to release_agent triggers execution on cgroup cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to cgroup release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/*/cgroup_procs modifications). Detect process execution spawned from cgroup cleanup handlers, particularly when subprocess runs with elevated privilege relative to parent. Flag patterns consistent with post-exploitation shell invocation after cgroup release event.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation via Cgroup Subsystem Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation mechanism; privilege elevation without corresponding privilege-request events (sudo, UAC, RunAs) via cgroup manipulation is anomalous and indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process privilege escalation (UID/GID increase) without corresponding sudo, su, or capability-request events in audit logs. Correlate with any cgroup manipulation or cgroup release_agent access in time window preceding privilege elevation. Focus on unprivileged process (UID > 1000) transitioning to root without privilege escalation infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Cgroup Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Cgroups are foundational to Linux container isolation; release_agent exploitation can escape container to host. Article's kernel-level vector applies to containerized workloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In containerized environments, detect container process accessing host /proc, /sys, or spawning processes outside container namespace boundaries. Monitor for cgroup path traversal or manipulation from within container context. Flag processes exiting container cgroup namespace to access host-level resources or execute host commands.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Patch Compliance for KEV CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Federal remediation is mandatory; patch lag is a critical risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for Linux Kernel version compliance across all asset groups. Identify systems that are out-of-date relative to CISA KEV remediation timeline (due 2026-06-05). Generate compliance report showing time-to-remediation for each vulnerable asset, surfacing any systems exceeding SLA.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and provides template reference for asset-exposure hunts. This is the canonical detection for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings matching CVE-2025-48595 on Android devices and frameworks. Escalate any unpatched instances given CISA KEV status and federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-05. Prioritize federal civilian agencies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution on Android Framework
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability 'allows for code execution'. Detect unintended process spawning or code execution patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation on Android devices running vulnerable Framework versions, especially processes spawned by framework components or system services. Correlate with CVE-2025-48595 scanner findings.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Integer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'local privilege escalation' as the attack outcome. Detect elevation-of-privilege attempts consistent with LPE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes requesting privilege escalation from low-privilege context to system/root on vulnerable Android devices. Correlate with CVE-2025-48595 exploitation indicators and anomalous code execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Attack - Multiple Failed Logins to Dashlane
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack' as the attack vector. Detectable via failed authentication rate anomalies and clustering. No UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >N failed login attempts against Dashlane (or password-manager service principals) within T seconds from single or distributed source IPs. Correlate failure with successful authentication immediately following, indicating brute-force success.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Encrypted Vault Download - Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—explicit exfiltration event. No collection or exfiltration phase in kill-chain output.
