suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS traffic to Telegram bot API endpoints (api.telegram.org) from non-messaging processes or system binaries. Detect patterns of repeated API calls with bot tokens, message sending/receiving. Monitor for Python or Go processes initiating these connections.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Enumeration and Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel...AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire LDAP queries, net.exe group enumeration, or repeated dsquery commands targeting AD objects (users, groups, computers). Flag high-volume AD discovery from single source within short timeframe, especially when followed by targeted credential access or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Python-Driven Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python.exe or python.exe processes spawning Windows executables with unusual arguments (e.g., ctypes, os.system, subprocess calling WinAPI). Detect legitimate Windows binaries (notepad.exe, calc.exe) with mismatched parent processes or execution from unusual directories, especially those generated or copied immediately before execution.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker Proxy for C2 Infrastructure Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag traffic to Cloudflare Worker endpoints (*.workers.dev domains) from compromised hosts. Correlate with C2 traffic patterns, identify backend redirects, and flag when Cloudflare Workers are used as proxy infrastructure instead of legitimate CDN/website acceleration use cases.

suggestion.title: Modular Payload Generation with Multi-Layer Encryption and Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Python tool that generates payloads...wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables or DLLs.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of packed/encrypted executables with unusual entropy, multiple UPX/custom packing layers, or Go/Rust-compiled payloads (rare in enterprise). Monitor for rapid generation of similar but distinct executable files. Correlate with Python script execution and EDR testing activity (e.g., repeated EDR-specific payload generation).

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release Agent Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states privilege escalation occurs 'via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' No detection UC was generated despite this being the core exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to /proc/*/cgroup_release_agent, modification of release_agent files in /sys/fs/cgroup/*, or execution of shell scripts from unexpected cgroups directories. Linux EDR / auditd logs should flag processes not running as root attempting cgroups v1 release_agent manipulation followed by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Unprivileged to Root via Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper authentication vulnerability which could allow for privilege escalation' but no UC targets the actual privilege escalation pattern post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent/child process relationships to detect transitions from low-privilege (e.g., apache, www-data) to root execution within seconds of CVE-2022-0492 exploitation attempts. Flag EUID/EGID changes in auditd logs or unexpected UID 0 execution chains.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Kernel Version Inventory (CVE-2022-0492 Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes federal due date requires patch compliance audits. Pipeline should generate detection UC for systems running vulnerable kernel versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Linux hosts running kernel versions < 5.16.11, 5.15.x < 5.15.25, 5.14.x < 5.14.21, 5.10.x < 5.10.102, or 5.4.x < 5.4.173. Cross-reference with exposed services (SSH, web apps, container registries) to identify public-facing attack surface.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cgroup Namespace/Mount Operations Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies cgroups v1 release_agent as the privilege-escalation vector; exploitation requires manipulation of cgroup namespace/mount operations not explicitly hunted in generated UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag executions of nsenter, unshare, or cgroup manipulation tools (cgroup-kill, cgexec) preceded by network exposure or vulnerability scanning. Monitor for creation of user namespaces or cgroup v1 hierarchies by non-root or service accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Primary baseline detection for identifying vulnerable Android Framework systems before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners detect CVE-2025-48595 on Android Framework systems. Correlate positive scan results with asset inventory; trigger on any findings indicating unpatched vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes integer overflow 'allows for code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation.' Kill chain requires correlation of framework exploitation with subsequent privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation following Android Framework exceptions or crashes. Monitor for uid/gid transitions from app or framework context to system context; correlate system_server/surfaceflinger crashes with subsequent capability elevation.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure – Android Framework Internet-Facing Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Identifying exposed systems is prerequisite to exploitation timeline analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Android systems or devices with Android Framework accessible via Internet-facing ports or services. Cross-reference with vulnerability scan results showing CVE-2025-48595 presence; flag assets matching both criteria.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance – Federal CVE-2025-48595 Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Deadline-driven compliance detection aligns with SOC risk-mitigation priorities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any unpatched CVE-2025-48595 instances remaining after 2026-06-05. Query patch management systems for Android Framework versions; compare installed versions against CISA advisory remediation guidance.

suggestion.title: Integer Overflow Memory Corruption Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'integer overflow vulnerability' which typically manifests via memory protection signals, heap corruption detection, or specific syscall patterns characteristic of overflow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework processes for heap corruption detection, memory protection violations, or abnormal memory allocation patterns. Flag syscall sequences (mmap/brk/mprotect) inconsistent with normal framework behavior.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attack Against Password Manager Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article lead explicitly states 'brute-force attack' but pipeline generated zero kill-chain phases and no detection use cases. Brute force is a well-defined MITRE technique with clear detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for Dashlane or similar password manager services. Alert on ≥5 failed login attempts to the same user account within 10 minutes, especially from distinct source IPs or rapid geographic movement. Escalate if followed by successful authentication within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Vault Data Export After Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded'—explicit exfiltration event. Pipeline missed detection opportunity for bulk credential store access/export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vault export, sync, or backup API calls originating from compromised account post-brute-force. Flag: vault download requests, bulk credential retrieval calls, or encryption key exports from newly-authenticated sessions after failed login spike.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Password Manager Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force compromise implies attacker accessing stolen vaults from unexpected locations/times post-breach. No detection for abnormal vault access sessions was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vault access from new device, browser, or geographically impossible origin post-compromise. Correlate successful brute-force login with subsequent vault viewing from unusual time/location. Flag bulk credential viewing patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Replay from Exfiltrated Vault Contents
suggestion.rationale: Once vaults are downloaded, attackers will attempt to use stolen credentials across other services. Pipeline lacks detection for post-breach lateral movement using vault credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vault compromise timeline with subsequent failed/successful logins across monitored services using credentials stored in Dashlane. Alert on same account/username attempting login to 10+ distinct services from single IP within 1 hour, or credential spray pattern post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Dashlane Authentication Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks are typically preceded by reconnaissance. Pipeline should surface pre-attack scanning for user enumeration or endpoint mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dashlane login/auth endpoints for credential enumeration attempts: repeated requests to password-reset, username-validation, or auth API endpoints returning 40x/50x responses. Detect scanning patterns preceding brute-force spike.

suggestion.title: WinRAR RCE Exploitation — Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver'; the pipeline did not flag detection for WinRAR spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other child processes as the exploitation→execution bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when WinRAR.exe or UnRAR.exe spawns child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, wscript.exe) with command-line arguments suggesting script or malware execution. Baseline WinRAR behavior typically does not spawn these processes without user action.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel Malware Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel' as delivered payloads, but pipeline produced no execution detection use cases; should detect process creation, module injection, or registry artifacts matching these malware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or module load events indicative of GammaWorm/GammaSteel signatures (e.g., known function names, import tables, injected code patterns). Cross-reference against Gamaredon IOC feeds if available; flag any process tree with WinRAR as ancestor and known malware indicators as descendant.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Extraction to Suspicious Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits WinRAR to Deliver' but pipeline did not surface detection for anomalous file extraction paths; legitimate WinRAR use vs. malware delivery differs in destination (user-chosen folder vs. %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, system dirs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WinRAR file extraction (detected via child process execution or file write sequences) to temporary directories (%TEMP%, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, C:\Windows\Temp) or system-sensitive paths (C:\Windows\System32, C:\ProgramFiles) without explicit user approval logs.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon C2 Beaconing — Known Malware Domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'Deliver GammaWorm and GammaSteel' but pipeline produced no C2 communication detection use cases; malware families typically establish C2 to exfiltrate or receive commands, a critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from processes spawned post-WinRAR execution to known Gamaredon C2 infrastructure. Monitor for anomalous ports (443, 8080, 8443, 53 for DNS tunneling) and domains associated with this actor. Cross-reference against recent Gamaredon IoC publications.

suggestion.title: Archive-to-Execution: WinRAR Artifact Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation chain ('Exploits WinRAR to Deliver') but pipeline did not detect the forensic artifact chain: *.rar file → WinRAR extraction → payload execution. This chained detection improves confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Construct a detection for the artifact chain: suspicious .rar file creation/modification → WinRAR.exe invoked within seconds → child process execution from extracted file path. High specificity if extracted file path is user-writable non-standard location and child process is scripting engine or command shell.

suggestion.title: Active Android CVE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One Actively Exploited' CVE in Android patch. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for exploitation. Should detect attempts to trigger the flaw(s) before patches deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or network activity patterns characteristic of Android CVE exploitation (e.g., unexpected Java/Dalvik runtime activity, WebView process crashes, suspicious intent handling). Cross-reference against AOSP/Google Security Advisory payload indicators if CVE details emerge.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation on Android
suggestion.rationale: Patch articles typically fix privilege escalation flaws. Article mentions 124 patches; at least some enable priv-esc. No detection for elevated access after exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for transitions from low-privilege app context to system_server or kernel execution, unusual capability requests, or SELinux denials followed by policy bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution Post-Android Update
suggestion.rationale: Article states one CVE is actively exploited; attackers will race patch deployment. No detection for post-exploitation shell or ADB command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected shell invocation (sh, bash), ADB commands over non-standard channels, or system property modifications immediately post-patch release, especially on unpatched or slow-rolling devices.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Device Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: "Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws"—one is actively exploited. No detection use case for tracking which devices remain vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Android devices by OS build date and patch level; flag any still running pre-June-2026 patch after grace period (e.g., 30 days). Correlate against exploit telemetry for critical flaws.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Android Device
suggestion.rationale: Successfully exploited Android device is a foothold. Article implies active exploitation in the wild. No detection for lateral movement to enterprise network or other devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound connections from Android devices to internal servers, VPN tunnel establishment, or credential forwarding to adjacent systems post-exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Version Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—attackers modified version control tags to inject malicious code. Pipeline should detect git tag modifications or unexpected package version rollbacks in dependency manifests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected rewrites, force-pushes, or tag modifications in PHP composer.json/composer.lock files or upstream package repositories. Baseline normal tag promotion cadence and flag deviations that introduce code changes without corresponding security reviews.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Credential Exfiltration via Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Steal CI Secrets'—malicious package code executes during `composer install`, accessing and exfiltrating GitHub Actions secrets, API tokens, and SSH keys stored in build environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for environment variable enumeration (env, printenv, Get-ChildItem env:) or credential file access (*.pem, ~/.ssh, /root/.ssh) during package installation phases. Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS from build agents immediately after dependency resolution.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from Package Manager Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages inject code that exfiltrates secrets; composer.exe/composer and PHP child processes should have minimal egress. Article implies C2 or credential dump destination exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for composer/PHP egress (typically only to packagist.org, github.com, github.com raw-content). Flag connections to unusual TLDs, newly-registered domains, or IPs with no prior package-management context.

suggestion.title: Repository Package-Metadata Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires modifying package repository metadata or account compromise. Article implies attacker had write access to package tags across multiple repos—detect unauthorized repository modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual repository-level events: tag creation without corresponding release workflows, commits authored by accounts outside normal committer list, force-pushes to production branches, or package versions published from non-standard CI/CD runners.

suggestion.title: Malicious PHP Code Injection in Composer Autoload/Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Composer supports pre/post-install scripts and autoload directives. Article's phrase 'rewritten' implies code was injected into composer.json scripts or package-level PHP files that execute on installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json for suspicious `scripts`, `config.scripts-descriptions`, and autoload sections containing exec(), shell_exec(), or curl commands. Flag PHP files added to `bin/` directories that invoke external commands or access environment variables.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Suspicious or Cloned Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must push malicious code to Composer registry or compromise official repo. Detect when composer pulls from forked, newly-registered, or geographically anomalous sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate package sources per repository. Alert on VCS origin changes in composer.lock, unexpected domain registrations matching package names, or composer pulling from non-standard registries (private proxies, development servers).

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Propagation via Malicious Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack 'spreads like a worm'—this is self-replication behavior across the dependency graph. Pipeline detected no phases or UCs for propagation mechanics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install invoking child npm install processes or unusual package.json modifications during build. Detect packages that insert themselves into parent package dependencies or trigger downstream installations recursively.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Modifications and Native Module Compilation
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is the attack's execution vector ('binding.gyp: An npm Supply Chain Attack'); the article implies malicious build configuration is rewritten. No UC for build-time compromise was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node-gyp, npm, or cc/clang processes spawning unusual child processes (curl, wget, powershell) during npm install. Monitor binding.gyp files for injected install/build hooks that execute shell commands outside the expected compiler chain.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication During npm Build Phase
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like propagation implies exfiltration or C2 callback. Article describes attack spreading; network callbacks during npm install are not detected by current rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTP/HTTPS from npm processes to non-registry domains (non-registry.npmjs.org, non-github.com/raw) during install phase. Alert on DNS queries for dynamic C2 infrastructure during package installation.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Injection and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via npm commonly inject post-install hooks into package.json. The article describes execution during dependency installation; no UC targets post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install triggers undocumented shell/node scripts via postinstall, preinstall, or prepare lifecycle hooks. Correlate script execution with package name entropy or recent package modifications.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Exfiltration via npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Worm-based attacks typically steal credentials or system data. Article implies data movement; no UC covers exfiltration of sensitive files by npm package contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm processes reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, or source control credentials, followed by base64 encoding and outbound connections to non-repo URLs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Router Log Files (Acer Wave 7 CVE-2026-49200)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface. This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet).' This is credential access at the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP GET/POST requests to /acer_cgi.log or similar log-export endpoints on Acer Wave 7 routers (192.168.76.1, acerconnect.com). Flag successful reads of files containing credential material without prior authentication tokens or without admin session cookies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized System Backup Decryption (Acer Wave 7 CVE-2026-49201)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Core persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to upload.cgi with backup-file payloads showing signs of manipulation (file entropy spikes, unexpected binary modifications post-decryption, timestamp inconsistencies in backup manifests). Monitor for repeated backup upload attempts in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing via Harvested Router Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials from acer_cgi.log are obtained via CVE-2026-49200, attackers would use them for unauthorized web and Telnet access. Article notes credentials are 'for web and Telnet,' enabling lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed login attempts to Acer Wave 7 web interface (192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com) or Telnet (port 23) followed by successful auth using credentials matching leaked acer_cgi.log patterns. Flag logins from external/unexpected IP ranges for router admin.

suggestion.title: Post-Backdoor Command Execution on Compromised Router
suggestion.rationale: After persistent backdoor injection via CVE-2026-49201, attacker gains execution capability. Article describes injection of backdoor into system backups for persistence, implying shell access follow-on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor router system logs, syslog exports, or CLI audit logs for unexpected command execution following backup restore cycles. Look for non-standard shell commands (curl, wget, nc, telnet outbound) originating from upload.cgi or unauthenticated web context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious System Backup Restore Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'persistent backdoor injection' via modified backups. Any restore operation on Wave 7 with modified backup content is realization of the persistence attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on system-initiated backup restore operations, especially without corresponding user-initiated restore request in web UI logs. Cross-reference restore timestamps against backup upload timestamps; flag restores that occur hours/days after upload (suggests attacker-delayed activation).

suggestion.title: Access to Acer Router Management Console from Unexpected Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article advises mitigation by disabling remote management or restricting to 'trusted IP addresses only,' implying baseline should be limited, local-only admin access. External access is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate admin IPs accessing 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com web interface. Alert on access from new external IP ranges, especially those exhibiting scanning/probing behavior (repeated 404s, parameter fuzzing, version enumeration requests).

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via Modified FFmpeg Import Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states modified FFmpeg DLL 'imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin' and 'the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' This is a clear DLL sideload/search-order hijack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor game processes (RenPy, RPG Maker MV engines) loading ffmpeg.dll and subsequent access to or execution of natives2_blob.bin from same directory. Detect unsigned or mismatched versions of ffmpeg.dll in game installation paths.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via Windows Color System Calibration Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKLM/HKCU registry InprocServer32 subkeys under Windows Color System Calibration Loader or similar system service CLSIDs. Correlate with suspicious DLL registration or redirection to non-system paths during game execution.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Script Execution from Binary Blob
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' and 'Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Clear obfuscation and sandbox evasion pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell child processes spawned from game engine executables or DLL injection contexts. Look for Base64 decoding patterns in PowerShell command lines or process memory; detect calls to [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String(...)).

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Trojan Downloader with Delayed Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' Indicates staged payload delivery with time-based trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from game-related processes days after initial infection. Monitor for secondary payload downloads and unusual process spawning from persistence mechanisms (COM-hijacked services). Alert on processes launched from scheduled tasks or login hooks downloading executables.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL Loading from Game Installation Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions RenPy (Python-based) and RPG Maker MV (JavaScript-based) games both trojanized. 'Contents of the game archive: fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL.' Detection should target legitimate game processes loading non-standard dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor RenPy (python.exe child) and RPG Maker MV (node.exe or game engine) processes for loading unsigned or non-canonical DLLs (natives2_blob.bin, suspicious FFmpeg variants). Flag DLL loads from user-writable game directories during initial game launch.

suggestion.title: Hentai Game Torrent Distribution via Compromised Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trojanized games have also been distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena' and 'a number of websites hosting game screenshots and download links. These links redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service.' Indicates supply-chain compromise detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads from known adult-game torrent trackers (AniRena, similar) or PixelDrain file transfers combined with Game-Engine-to-Windows.System32 DLL registration/persistence events. Flag if game .exe or launcher triggers suspicious registry modifications within minutes of execution.

suggestion.title: Redis Process Spawning Unexpected Children
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaw in Redis allows arbitrary code execution. Article establishes Redis as exploit vector ('Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis'). Post-exploitation, redis-server should not spawn shells or unrelated processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent=redis-server.exe spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, etc.). RCE exploitation typically results in process execution from the vulnerable service context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis EVAL or Script Commands
suggestion.rationale: Common Redis RCE vectors exploit Lua scripting (EVAL/EVALSHA) or command injection. Article confirms RCE exists; detection must cover script-based exploitation paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT, or CONFIG commands in Redis wire traffic. Look for payloads containing system call attempts (os.*, io.*, require, load) or shell metacharacters within serialized Lua.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections Initiated by Redis Process
suggestion.rationale: Redis is a cache server and should not initiate outbound connections. RCE exploitation typically leads to reverse shells or C2 beaconing; article establishes code execution is possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on redis-server.exe or redis-cli processes initiating outbound TCP/UDP connections to non-standard ports or external IPs. Correlate with process creation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Redis CONFIG GET/SET Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation or post-exploitation may involve querying/modifying Redis configuration (e.g., logfile path, requirepass removal). Article confirms RCE; attackers often disable security after initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis CONFIG GET/SET commands. Flag changes to requirepass, logfile, dir, or appendonly. Spike in CONFIG commands post-RCE exploitation indicates attacker lateral movement in Redis.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Redis Exploitation Attempt (Network Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-23479 as a 2-year-old RCE flaw. Network-based detection of exploitation attempts on port 6379 is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If vulnerability details become public, inspect TCP port 6379 traffic for known exploit payloads or version-specific attack signatures. Monitor for rapid probing of Redis instances across the environment.

suggestion.title: Localized Government/Tax/Payroll Phishing Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attacker uses localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications.' Primary attack vector with language/locale-specific indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with German/Italian/UK-localized subject patterns (tax keywords, payroll, VAT, compliance) paired with suspicious sender domains or archive attachments. Correlate Teams/WhatsApp/LINE contact attempts from same sender within 48h as secondary confirmation.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Anti-Analysis Registry Discovery Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malware features several anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the CExecSvc service, and OS UUID.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process querying HKEY_*\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Defender paths, enumerating CExecSvc service, or retrieving Win32_ComputerSystemProduct UUID via WMI. Flag clustering of 3+ discovery calls within 10s from single parent as evasion signature.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article: RomulusLoader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' High-fidelity execution technique with behavioral artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CreateRemoteThread or WriteProcessMemory sequences targeting legitimate processes (AnyDesk, SyncFuture, svchost). Flag parent-child process mismatches where legitimately-signed tools spawn from user-writable paths or low-integrity processes.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Cookie Theft by Python Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: SilentRunLoader is 'Python-based loader and information stealer [that] steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data,' deployed against UK and Southeast Asia targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python.exe or child processes accessing Chrome Local State, Default/Login Data, or Cookies SQLite files outside of Chrome.exe context. Flag file access patterns combined with base64 encoding or network exfil to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Keylogging and Multi-Modal Surveillance Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Atlas RAT capabilities: 'Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording'—collection-phase indicators of surveillance-intent malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes loading screen-capture APIs (BitBlt, DirectX), microphone/webcam drivers (WASAPI, camera device), combined with persistent hooks (SetWindowsHookEx, keyboard filters). Keylogger pattern: low-privilege process with kernel-mode callback registration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Remote Management Software Execution (AnyDesk, SyncFuture)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture, [which] was used in attacks targeting German entities.' Persistence and lateral-movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AnyDesk or SyncFuture spawned from loader processes, non-standard install paths, or with suspicious command-line arguments (headless flags, auto-accept). Correlate with outbound TCP/UDP to residential IP ranges or known proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CVE-2026-45247 Vulnerable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution...Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer.' Canonical asset-discovery hunt for exposed vulnerable product.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installations exposed to untrusted networks via fingerprinting HTTP banners, scanning known product paths, or querying endpoint inventory for vulnerable package versions. Correlate with patch status for CVE-2026-45247 against federal due date 2026-06-06.

suggestion.title: CacheWarmer Cookie Deserialization Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie' is the explicit attack vector. Direct detection of the exploit payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests containing CacheWarmer cookie with Base64-encoded or obfuscated payloads. Flag payloads with PHP serialization markers (O: for objects, C: for class references). Correlate with HTTP 500 errors or deserialization exceptions in Mirasvit error logs indicating exploitation attempt or success.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...remote code execution.' Hunt for artifacts of successful exploitation: process execution, file creation, outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After CacheWarmer exploitation, monitor for suspicious process spawning from web-server user context (php.exe, bash under httpd). Flag unauthorized files in web-accessible directories. Detect outbound connections from Mirasvit process that deviate from expected cache-warming behavior (DNS queries, reverse shells, C2 beacons).

suggestion.title: Scanner Patch-Lag Detection for CVE-2026-45247
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly advises: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check.' Catch discrepancies between scanner assertions and actual deployed versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner reports marking systems as unpatched for CVE-2026-45247 against actual package versions from endpoint telemetry. Identify scanner false negatives, missing assets, or patch lag on exposed Mirasvit instances. Escalate unpatched public-facing installations by federal due date.

suggestion.title: PHP Deserialization Exception and Error Log Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability.' Failed and successful exploitation attempts generate distinct log signatures (exceptions on failure; silent execution on success).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Mirasvit and PHP error logs for deserialization markers: unserialize() calls, __wakeup/__destruct invocations, or 'Uncaught Exception' from CacheWarmer request handlers. Cluster by cookie payload signature to detect attack campaign. Baseline normal deserialization activity to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Integer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2025-48595 as high-severity integer overflow in Android Framework affecting versions 14–16, with no user interaction required and active limited targeted exploitation. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or use cases despite this being the lead threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for integer overflow exploitation patterns targeting Android Framework processes (system_server) on devices 14–16. Alert on unexpected privilege elevation or memory access anomalies in framework services pre-patch (before 2026-06-05 security update).

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel CVE-2022-0492 cgroup_release_agent_write Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article details CVE-2022-0492 exploitation via cgroup_release_agent_write() function: 'due to insufficient authentication checks, can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' No detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect local processes writing shell commands to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent files from container namespaces or unprivileged contexts. Alert on writes to cgroup subsystem paths originating from containerized processes, particularly on affected kernel versions (< 5.15.20).

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Namespace Isolation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack enabling namespace isolation bypass: 'can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation'. Container escape is the critical outcome but no use case exists to detect this attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect syscalls or file operations that cross namespace boundaries unexpectedly. Flag access to host /proc, /sys, or cgroup infrastructure from processes with restrictive namespaces. Alert on privilege escalation from container context (UID<1000) to UID 0 on host.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Elevated Container Capabilities (cgroups v1)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes flaw 'is especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities'. Should detect abuse of CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_ADMIN for cgroup manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On containerized hosts, flag processes assigned CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_NET_ADMIN that subsequently write to cgroup files or execute cgroup-related syscalls. Correlate capability grants with subsequent privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detection of Unpatched Vulnerable Systems (CVE-2025-48595 / CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions and patch versions (Linux 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+; Android patches 2026-06-01/2026-06-05). Unpatched inventory is direct attack surface requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory detection: flag Android 14–16 devices lacking June 2026 security patches. Identify Linux hosts running kernel < 5.15.20 (or branch-specific thresholds) without CVE-2022-0492 patches. Prioritize containerized environments as highest-risk.

suggestion.title: Host-level Root Access from Container Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ultimate attack outcome: 'escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system'. Pipeline missed detection for this post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes originating from container context (cgroup, namespace ID, container ID) that achieve UID 0 on the parent host. Correlate containerized process execution with host-level root file creation, host process execution as root, or modifications to host configuration.

suggestion.title: Jupyter kernel process running as UID 0 on Kubernetes worker
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID...by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID'. UC_6_2 detects pod *creation* with runAsUser=0, but miss the actual kernel process already executing as root. Need earlier detection of malicious kernel runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Jupyter kernel process (spawned by /usr/local/share/jupyter or similar paths) executing with UID 0 on Kubernetes worker node. Look for kernel launcher child processes running under root after enterprise-gateway spawned them.

suggestion.title: Container runtime escape—host filesystem mount from non-volume path
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'escape to host' (T1611). UC_6_3 detects *declared* hostPath volumes, but misses the actual exploitation—when kernel process accesses host paths (/etc, /root, /var/lib) outside the mounted volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file system access (open, read, write) from kernel process inside container (identified by cgroup, container ID, or PID namespace) attempting paths like /etc/shadow, /root, /var/lib/kubelet that are not declared in pod.spec.volumes. Cross-correlate container PID with host-side filesystem access.

suggestion.title: Container-spawned shell or command execution after kernel launch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit leading to code execution on host. After escape, attacker will spawn shell or execute commands. Need detection of /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or unusual exec() calls from kernel process or runc context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect interactive shell (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or command execution spawned as child of Jupyter kernel process, especially if running as UID 0. Also monitor for runc or containerd-shim executing unexpected binaries outside container initialization sequence.

suggestion.title: Enterprise-gateway service account privilege escalation via kernel deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deploy container' (T1610) with root privileges. Service account itself may be compromised or abused. Detect abnormal deployment patterns—e.g., rapid pod creation, pods with unusual security contexts, or repeated failures followed by root-uid success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor enterprise-gateway service account for unusual patterns: (1) rapid pod creation/deletion cycles (scanning for bypass), (2) sudden shift from normal UID to UID 0 in pod specs, (3) creation of pods with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or privileged=true after normal operations.

suggestion.title: Jupyter kernel environment variable injection with restricted values
suggestion.rationale: Article: bypass works via 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value' in environment variables. UC_6_1 misses the actual parameter passing. Need detection at kernel-spawn time, not HTTP endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container or pod-creation events with KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID environment variables set to 0, negative values, or reserved system UIDs. Parse kernel launcher command line and environment from audit logs or container runtime to catch malicious env variable injection.

suggestion.title: Unusual capability or seccomp bypasses requested by Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation to root implies capability elevation. Article lists T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation) but no detection looks for kernel or container requesting CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or seccomp filter removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kubernetes API calls or pod specs from enterprise-gateway requesting elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE), allowPrivilegeEscalation=true, or securityContext.privileged=true. Cross-correlate with timing of failed UID enforcement.

suggestion.title: KERNEL_* environment variable containing Jinja2 expressions (CVE-2026-44181 pre-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'environment variables (`KERNEL_XXX`) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection.' Pipeline should detect the **injection point itself**—environment variables with `{{` or `{%` patterns before execution, not just during request.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for KERNEL_POD_NAME, KERNEL_WORKING_DIR, KERNEL_NAMESPACE, or other KERNEL_* environment variables being set with Jinja2 template syntax. Look in container create events, pod specifications, or application logs for `KERNEL_.*={{` or `KERNEL_.*{%` patterns. Legitimate kernel configuration would not contain template delimiters.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API calls to list/read secrets after Enterprise Gateway RCE (CVE-2026-44181 credential access)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The code can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token, which can steal Kubernetes se...' Detection should monitor for API calls to read secrets or service accounts **immediately after** RCE signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate RCE process activity (Python spawning shell) with subsequent API calls (verb=get/list, objectRef.kind=Secret or ServiceAccount) from the same Enterprise Gateway pod. Alert on unauthenticated or service-account-only reads of token or tls.crt secrets in kube-system or default namespaces.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API audit logs showing pod creation with elevated capabilities from Enterprise Gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article implies post-exploitation container escape: 'escape to host' (T1611). This uses Kubernetes API to create pods with hostPath or hostNetwork. Should detect via K8s audit logs, not just container logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Kubernetes audit logs, detect verb=create where user matches the Enterprise Gateway service account AND the Pod spec contains hostPath volumes, hostNetwork=true, or privileged=true. Correlate with prior SSTI detection for attack chain confidence.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_* YAML-injection payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_4_2 with phase 'exploit' and Medium confidence. Detects POST requests to */api/kernels* with KERNEL_* environment variables containing YAML injection indicators (---, ..., securityContext, runAsUser, fsGroup, privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID). Complete SPL and KQL provided in article but pipeline produced empty use-case array.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ingress and WAF logs for POST requests to /api/kernels endpoint. Correlate with presence of KERNEL_* parameters and YAML document separators or privilege-escalation keywords in request body. Join Web datamodel with HTTP server logs to reduce false positives from scanner activity.

suggestion.title: Privileged or root pod created by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_4_3 with phase 'install' and High confidence. Detects Kubernetes pod creation (verb=create, stage=ResponseComplete) by enterprise-gateway service account with privileged security contexts (privileged=true, runAsUser=0, runAsGroup=0, hostNetwork=true, hostPID=true, hostPath). Complete SPL and KQL provided but pipeline did not extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes audit logs for pod create operations where requestor is *enterprise-gateway* service account and pod spec contains any privilege-escalation indicators. Aggregate multiple pod creations per namespace-sa pair; flag if count ≥1 to detect single malicious pod injection.

suggestion.title: launch_kubernetes.py process execution and /home/jovyan file modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_4_1 with phase 'exploit' and High confidence. Detects execution of launch_kubernetes.py (Kubernetes manifest rendering entrypoint) and file creation/modification in /home/jovyan* (Jupyter working directory). Directly ties to template rendering abuse described in vulnerability. Pipeline failed to extract despite SPL and KQL provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process_name=launch_kubernetes.py or FileName in~(launch_kubernetes.py) execution. Correlate with file-system events (FileCreated, FileModified) in /home/jovyan* path. Enrich with process command-line and parent process to detect injection payloads in arguments.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: CVE-2026-44182 Jupyter Enterprise Gateway inventory correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names template-based hunt 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' (phase: recon, High confidence). Matches CVE-2026-44182 against software inventory to identify vulnerable Jupyter Enterprise Gateway instances. Standard but critical recon-phase detection. Pipeline did not extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-44182 against asset inventory to list Jupyter Enterprise Gateway instances across infrastructure. Prioritize instances reachable from untrusted networks (public IPs, DMZ, internet-facing Kubernetes ingress). Cross-reference with network flow logs to identify active scanner/attacker probing.

suggestion.title: Malspam with DoubleClick Redirect Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign.' Pipeline generated zero email or redirect detection. DoubleClick ads as initial-access vector is the campaign signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing links to ad networks (*.doubleclick.net) or DoubleClick redirects that terminate at non-Google, non-CDN destinations. Monitor for suspicious referer chains in proxy logs starting from DoubleClick ad domains.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT File Execution and Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names DesckVB RAT as payload. Pipeline produced no detection logic for RAT execution, file creation, or behavioral indicators—critical omission for a malware campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of DesckVB RAT binaries via file hash, code signing anomalies, or behavioral patterns (registry modification, C2 connection attempts). Monitor for child processes spawned from suspicious temp/appdata locations post-execution.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT C2 Communication Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: RAT requires C2 callbacks. Article title indicates delivery mechanism but pipeline extracted no C2 domains, IPs, or communication pattern detection—essential for post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from systems post-DesckVB infection to known C2 infrastructure. Alert on unusual port/protocol combinations, encrypted traffic patterns, or DNS requests to C2 domains that should be extracted from article IOCs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Downloaded File Execution from Email Links
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain is phishing email → DoubleClick link click → malware download → execution. Pipeline identified zero detection for the download+execution correlation post-user-interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file downloads (via proxy or email link) with subsequent execution from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or Downloads directories within 2-5 minutes. Alert on rundll32/regsvcs/certutil execution of recently-downloaded DLLs.

suggestion.title: Persistence Registry Modification Post-RAT Installation
suggestion.rationale: RATs establish persistence; article title does not detail mechanism, but pipeline should have prompted for persistence-phase detection. No runkey, scheduled task, or WMI detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications in HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or scheduled task creation with obfuscated names/executables correlating with DesckVB infection timestamps.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Document Delivery: Fake PO/Quote/RFP Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'disguises itself as an everyday business document — a purchase order, a quote, or a request for proposal. Once an unsuspecting employee opens.' This is T1566.001 + T1204.002—the entire attack vector—yet pipeline detected nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with procurement-themed filenames (PO*.js, Quote*.exe, RFP*.jar, Invoice*.hta) from external senders to finance/procurement staff. Correlate with email gateways that strip Office macro protections or allow embedded scripts in documents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Document Open Followed by Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: JS.MonoGlyphRAT is JavaScript-based; employee opens fake PO → script execution occurs. Article says 'Once an unsuspecting employee opens the [...]' but no execution-chain detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cscript.exe/wscript.exe spawned <30s after document file open by Office processes or user Explorer interaction. Look for unsigned or temp-folder scripts with outbound network attempts.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing: JS.MonoGlyphRAT to aryamint Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted T1071 but failed to generate corresponding detection. Article provides C2 domains and IPs; no use case for network-signature detection or behavioral hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script runtime processes (cscript.exe, wscript.exe, mshta.exe) establishing outbound connections to aryamint.com or scan.aryamint.com. Flag regular callback intervals (beaconing); correlate with process creation from user temp directories or recent document activity.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land JavaScript Engine Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware name itself signals JavaScript runtime as attack vector. No detection recommended for wscript.exe/cscript.exe abuse, a critical Living-off-the-Land indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawned with uncommon parent processes (Explorer.exe, Outlook.exe, Acrobat.exe) or from non-standard script locations. Baseline legitimate script use and flag outliers in TEMP/AppData.

suggestion.title: Procurement Team Email Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Campaign specifically targets enterprise procurement workflows (fake POs). No detection for attacker reconnaissance of procurement staff. T1598.003 (spearphishing link/attachment click) should trigger investigation into prior reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate emails with fake PO/invoice themes sent to procurement, AP, or purchasing teams with unusual sender patterns (domain-homograph, new external sender). Detect clicks on embedded links or attachment opens; flag as high-risk if sender WHOIS/email infrastructure is newly registered.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Account Enumeration via Net/ADFind
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Active Directory discovery'—this is an explicit reconnaissance technique with no corresponding detection UC. Standard post-exploit activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of net user, net group, dsquery, adfind, or sharphound with AD enumeration arguments. Flag process execution from unexpected principals (service accounts, system processes running in user context) querying LDAP or AD objects.

suggestion.title: EDR/Security Software Disablement or Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'test endpoint detection and response (EDR) evasion techniques.' Explicit defense evasion activity with zero corresponding detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable EDR agents, modify security software configuration, or terminate EDR processes. Monitor for suspicious registry modifications targeting Windows Defender, tamper detection flags, or event log clearing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Launch from User Profile Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspicious endpoint triggered alerts tied to payloads stored in a user directory.' Direct indicator of malware execution; no execution-phase UC captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable process creation from user-writable paths (Desktop, Downloads, AppData\Local\Temp, Documents). Correlate with recent file write events from network sources or unusual parent process chains.

suggestion.title: Automated/Scripted Active Directory Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'AI-assisted tools to automate Active Directory discovery.' Batch enumeration patterns (rapid sequential queries, script-driven commands) differ from manual reconnaissance and are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for time-boxed clusters of LDAP queries or net/dsquery invocations indicating scripted enumeration. Look for PowerShell/cmd execution patterns with AD module imports or high-volume LDAP filters over short time windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Framework Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'post-exploitation frameworks' as 'structured collection of malicious components.' No UC targets framework deployment or command-execution signatures typical of frameworks (Covenant, Empire, Sliver).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for obfuscated script execution, staged payload loading, in-memory injection, and command channels consistent with known post-exploitation frameworks. Cross-reference against VirusTotal and GitHub abuse reports for emerging AI-enhanced tooling.

suggestion.title: Beaconing to AWS Lambda C2 — periodic outbound with low variance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actors use AWS Lambda for 'stealthy communications' with 'periodic outbound' behavior to a 'small set of destinations.' The article itself includes a detailed Beaconing use case (UC_BEACONING) with Splunk SPL and KQL, which the pipeline failed to generate or extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic outbound connections from internal hosts to AWS Lambda endpoints (ap-southeast-1 region) with inter-arrival times of 30–600 seconds, low standard deviation (<5 sec), and high repeat count (>30 connections). Exclude legitimate AWS workload patterns.

suggestion.title: Network connections to AWS Lambda C2 domain
suggestion.rationale: Campaign 'hides inside... Amazon Web Services' using 'lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws' as explicit C2 infrastructure. Article designates this domain as high-fidelity IOC. Pipeline should generate network-IOC-driven hunt but generated none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for any network connection or DNS resolution to 'lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws' from internal networks. Correlate with process execution, parent process chain, and timing to identify C2 callbacks and command relay.

suggestion.title: Malware hash matching — HazyBeacon campaign samples
suggestion.rationale: Article lists seven SHA256 hashes marked as high-fidelity IOCs for malware samples used in the campaign. Pipeline should generate endpoint file/hash-driven detection hunts but produced none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file write, process execution, or module load matching any of the seven SHA256 hashes. Correlate with parent process and command-line arguments to identify obfuscation and beaconing payloads. Escalate on lateral movement or credential access following hash match.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion via trusted cloud service masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes threat actors 'turn trusted cloud infrastructure against organizations' and 'hide inside one of the world's most trusted platforms.' This is explicit masquerading of legitimate AWS services. Pipeline should flag this defense-evasion technique but did not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate AWS services (Lambda, CloudFront, S3) being invoked as C2 endpoints from internal hosts or non-standard AWS accounts. Flag atypical Lambda invocations, CloudFront distributions returning executables, and API calls from hosts that normally do not interact with AWS infrastructure.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 HPACK Compression Amplification Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector stated: 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation, with Envoy and Apache httpd demonstrating worst ratios at 5,700:1 and 4,000:1, respectively.' No detection rule generated for compression-ratio anomalies or HPACK table explosion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 streams for asymmetric resource consumption: flag connections where bytes received << server memory allocated (>1000:1 ratio). Instrument HPACK dynamic table growth and alert on tables exceeding 100MB. Correlate single-source HTTP/2 traffic volume with server heap delta—>500MB allocation per 1MB sent is anomalous.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow-Control Window Stalling and Memory Retention
suggestion.rationale: Second attack component explicitly described: 'preventing memory from being freed...advertising a zero-byte flow-control window...requests never fully completed, and allocated memory keeps growing without being freed.' No detection for indefinite stream holds or flow-control abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE sequences from single sources where flow-control windows are reset to zero and periodic tiny updates follow, holding stream state >60 seconds without data transfer. Alert on connections with open streams in pseudo-idle state (no RST/FIN) while server buffers remain allocated.

suggestion.title: Single-Source Rapid Memory Exhaustion to DoS
suggestion.rationale: Quantified impact: 'a single client can consume and hold 32GB of server memory in roughly 20 seconds' (Apache, Envoy: 10-18s; nginx 45s; IIS 45s). Pipeline missed resource-exhaustion baselines entirely—no alert for memory spike + single source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when server heap/RSS grows >80% within 60 seconds sourced from ≤3 IPs on HTTP/2 streams. Establish per-connection memory budgets (baseline: 10-50MB). Flag connections exceeding 1GB or exhibiting >50MB/sec sustained allocation. Include both peak and cumulative metrics.

suggestion.title: Oversized HTTP/2 Header Count Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Mitigations cited: 'enforce hard header-count limits' and nginx patch added 'max_headers directive.' Article implies headers are the attack payload, yet no detection rule for abnormal header counts per stream or per connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 stream headers: flag streams >100 headers (typical baseline 20-60). Alert on connections from single source sending repeated identical headers across multiple streams in <10 seconds. Combine with memory-growth correlation: >200 headers + memory spike = protocol exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Unprotected HTTP/2 Endpoint Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'systems running behind CDNs or reverse proxies do not expose the vulnerable HTTP/2 endpoint.' Pipeline missed asset-level detection: identifying critical servers exposing raw HTTP/2 without proxy/load-balancer protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory servers running vulnerable HTTP/2 versions (Envoy 1.37.2, Apache 2.4.67 unpatched, nginx <1.29.8, IIS, Pingora unpatched) without reverse proxy/CDN/load-balancer in front. Alert on external direct HTTP/2 connections to these endpoints from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Slowloris-Style HTTP/2 Stream Staleness
suggestion.rationale: Attack combines 'HPACK compression amplification and Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' Slowloris component (keeping connections alive indefinitely without completing) lacks a dedicated detector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/2 streams from single client that remain open >120 seconds with minimal payload transfer and no FIN/RST/error termination. Monitor concurrent streams per source; flag sources with stream counts approaching or exceeding server limits (e.g., >100 open streams from one IP).

suggestion.title: npm postinstall script credential access during installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines' — this execution occurs via postinstall scripts when npm install runs, with direct access to .ssh, .aws, .git config, .kube directories and environment variables in developer/CI environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.js/npm processes spawned during dependency installation access credential file paths (*/,.ssh/*, .aws/*, .git/config) or invoke command-line tools (grep, cat, curl) that enumerate environment variables. Flag if followed by encoded data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Worm-like npm package republishing to supply chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack behavior: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages' — detection must identify when previously-published package versions are re-uploaded with modified content to npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls for republish/re-upload operations on package versions from developer accounts lacking historical publish permissions for those packages. Alert on rapid sequential version updates with byte-level content drift (indicating mutation and re-seeding).

suggestion.title: CI/CD environment variable and credential exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack 'silently infect[s] CI/CD environments' — CI/CD agents run npm install with elevated permissions and access to deployment credentials, cloud keys, and repository tokens that must be exfiltrated and detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS requests from CI/CD runners/build agents containing patterns matching AWS access key IDs, GitHub PATs, or base64-encoded credential structures. Correlate with npm install events. Monitor for credential contents in HTTP request bodies or DNS queries.

suggestion.title: Malicious child process spawning from npm postinstall phase
suggestion.rationale: npm postinstall scripts in compromised packages execute arbitrary code — article's 'malicious code' mechanism requires spawning shells or utilities (curl, wget, powershell) to exfiltrate credentials. Must detect unusual child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when node.js or npm processes spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget, or similar data-exfiltration utilities during package installation phases. Alert on execution from non-standard paths or with redirected output/pipes.

suggestion.title: Package version hash mutation and re-registration
suggestion.rationale: Article states '90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages' were compromised — suggests coordinated republishing of multiple versions. Detection must catch when package checksums diverge from official builds or when versions are re-published after release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare published npm package version hashes against canonical sources (GitHub releases, upstream registries). Alert on hash mismatches or re-publication timestamps that postdate original release. Flag accounts re-publishing packages without maintainer status.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage credential theft and attestation bypass in supply chain
suggestion.rationale: Attack achieves 'preinstall to persistence' lifecycle — article's title signals multi-stage attack with initial infection (preinstall) and ongoing access (persistence). Detection must track the full lifecycle from first install through credential theft to self-propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlation rule: (1) npm install of @redhat-cloud-services → (2) file access to credential stores (.ssh, .aws, .git) → (3) outbound network call to non-npm-registry IP → (4) subsequent npm publish/update call from same account/machine. Flag full chain with high severity.

suggestion.title: Fortinet CVE Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fortinet vulnerability exploitation' as primary attack vector with 6 specific CVEs (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-32433, CVE-2025-33073, CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2023-4966, CVE-2020-5135). No detection rule for FortiGate RCE payloads, web shell uploads, or post-exploitation reconnaissance patterns in FortiOS logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiGate device logs for HTTP requests matching known RCE pattern strings (e.g., '/admin' paths with non-admin credentials, POST to '/api' endpoints from unauthenticated sources, file upload attempts to unexpected directories). Correlate with outbound C2 connections within 5-10 minutes post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Custom C2 Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'custom command-and-control framework that most security tools simply do not see coming'—a distinct claim that generic beaconing may miss. No detection for non-standard protocols, custom encryption wrappers, or out-of-band signaling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unrecognized TLS ciphers, mismatched SSL certificate issuers, or periodic outbound connections on high ephemeral ports to residential IP space. Flag Fortinet-exploitation-infected hosts that beacon but do NOT match known C2 signatures (negative-space detection).

suggestion.title: Pre-Encryption File Discovery & Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware impact but no hunt covers the reconnaissance/staging phase that precedes encryption—file enumeration, exclusion list creation, or shadow copy deletion that typically occurs 30-60 minutes before mass encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual parent-child process chains (e.g., compromised service spawning cmd.exe spawning 'dir' or 'vssadmin delete shadows'). Monitor for high-velocity directory listing operations (100+ 'dir' or 'Get-ChildItem' calls within 2 minutes). Correlate with later encryption events.

suggestion.title: MCP Server or Skill Invocation Outside Approved Catalog
suggestion.rationale: Article: agents 'pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs...often selected and invoked at runtime, with no review' and 'Snyk's research found 76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984 analyzed.' Unapproved tools becoming part of the supply chain without detection is the core risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent process execution for invocation of external MCP servers, skills, or development tools not present in a maintained approved-tools inventory. Flag skill downloads or API calls to public skill repositories during agent runtime.

suggestion.title: Agent Database Modification or Deletion Outside Defined Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'the coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This is direct-impact evidence of agent boundary violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DROP TABLE, DELETE, or TRUNCATE operations originating from known agent identities or service accounts typically used for agents. Alert especially when preceded by access-denied or parameter-validation errors, indicating scope deviation.

suggestion.title: Installation of Malicious or Unvetted Skill from Public Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Snyk's research found 76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984 analyzed...roughly a third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.' Runtime selection creates supply-chain entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for skill/plugin downloads or installations from public repositories (npm, PyPI, GitHub, etc.) by agent processes. Cross-reference against known-malicious skill databases or absent from internal approval manifests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Queries or Exfiltration via Agent Tool Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'data exposure through tool calls' and notes agents 'query internal systems' at 'machine speed' with 'no review' of what data flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical API/database queries issued by known agent identities. Alert on queries to sensitive tables, schemas, or data categories outside the agent's documented scope, or large result-set transfers.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Causing Agent Instruction Bypass or Scope Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'prompt injection inside development workflows' as a key risk. The database-deletion incident may represent post-injection behavior despite 'repeated freeze instructions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent input (prompts, external data feeds, tool responses) for unusual instruction patterns, encoded payloads, or role-play directives that contradict prior approval/freeze states. Flag when agent behavior contradicts documented constraints or authorization policies.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Known-Vulnerable MCP Server to Escalate Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'roughly a third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.' Agents inherit parent permissions; vulnerable MCP servers become privilege-escalation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API sequences or tool interactions known to trigger CVEs in public MCP servers. Alert when agent processes gain elevated privileges immediately after interacting with known-vulnerable MCP server versions.

suggestion.title: Predatory Sparrow Infrastructure and Campaign Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'In June 2025, the pro-Israel Predatory Sparrow hacking group claimed to have breached Nobitex, stealing digital assets worth roughly $90 million.' Named threat actor with recent confirmed operational activity; critical to track infrastructure, indicators, and follow-on operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Predatory Sparrow-attributed C2 infrastructure, malware signatures, and domain registration patterns. Track IOCs from breach disclosure disclosures and threat intelligence feeds. Alert on any network traffic or endpoint artifacts linking to Predatory Sparrow campaigns or infrastructure used in Nobitex operation.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Transactions to Sanctioned Iranian Exchanges
suggestion.rationale: Article states Nobitex processed '50 percent of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025' and facilitated IRGC-linked transactions. OFAC sanctions now make any U.S. entity involvement with Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex illegal. Ransomware actors use these exchanges to cash out—detect outbound transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor blockchain and payment system logs for cryptocurrency transfers to wallet addresses known to be associated with Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex, or other Iranian exchanges. Cross-reference against OFAC SDN list. Alert on any U.S.-linked entity sending value to sanctioned exchange addresses, particularly from ransom payment addresses.

suggestion.title: IRGC-Affiliated Ransomware Operations and Wallet Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'wallets associated with ransomware threat actors related to the IRGC' and states 'addresses associated with the IRGC accounted for over 50% of the value received by the Iranian crypto ecosystem in Q4 2025.' These are named threat actors conducting ransomware operations; tracking their wallet infrastructure and payment flows is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain known IRGC-affiliated wallet clusters and ransomware group addresses from Chainalysis/TRM Labs feeds. Correlate ransom payments across incidents to identify consolidated wallets or exchange deposit patterns. Alert when new ransomware samples, ransom notes, or payment instructions reference Iranian exchanges or known IRGC-linked wallets.

suggestion.title: Nobitex Executive Access and Crypto Custody
suggestion.rationale: Article states Nobitex 'helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins used to prop up the plummeting value of the Iranian rial, while enabling regime insiders to access international digital asset exchanges.' Designated executives (Amir Hossein Rad, Seyed Ali Khoee, et al.) are now sanctioned; track their infrastructure and any successor or shell operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new exchange registrations, verified user accounts, or wallet creation activity linked to previously identified Nobitex executives or associated phone numbers/email domains. Flag any new cryptocurrency exchange platforms launched from Iranian infrastructure or using personnel overlaps with Nobitex leadership.

suggestion.title: Central Bank of Iran Stablecoin Custody and Movement
