suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'Nobitex also helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins.' This describes state-level financial infrastructure diversion; tracking stablecoin custody patterns, mint-and-burn cycles, and cross-exchange arbitrage related to CBI could expose regime finance operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor stablecoin (USDT, USDC) mint and burn events on public blockchains, particularly flows through Nobitex and Iranian exchange wallets. Alert on patterns consistent with large-scale stablecoin accumulation or rapid rotation through multiple exchanges in single day, which may indicate CBI-orchestrated custody movement or arbitrage.

suggestion.title: Predatory Sparrow Breach Indicators and Stolen Asset Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Predatory Sparrow breach of Nobitex in June 2025 resulted in ~$90M in stolen digital assets. This gives us a known theft date and victim, enabling targeted hunting for breach artifacts, initial access vectors, data exfiltration paths, and stolen cryptocurrency movement patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Predatory Sparrow breach date (June 2025) with Nobitex log anomalies, credential spray attempts, and web shell uploads if logs are available. Track ~$90M in stolen cryptocurrency across blockchain explorers, watch for movement from theft wallets to secondary exchanges or mixing services. Identify exfiltration patterns used (likely outbound HTTPS or SSH tunneling given exchange environment).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Windows Search URI Scheme Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability' as attack vector. Pipeline should detect search-ms: or similar protocol handler invocations with network-facing side effects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search-ms: URI scheme execution (ProcessCreationEvents with search-ms: in command line) followed by unexpected network connections from SearchIndexer.exe or SearchProtocolHost.exe. Correlate with HTTP outbound traffic on port 80/443 initiated by search system processes.

suggestion.title: NTLMv2 Hash Exposure via Search Index Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Steal NTLMv2 Hashes'—credential access is the attack objective. Pipeline should flag NTLM authentication initiated by or relayed through Windows Search components.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag NTLM Type II challenge/response (0x4e544c4d53535000) observed on network egress from SearchIndexer.exe or SearchProtocolHost.exe to external or untrusted hosts. Correlate with SMB or HTTP forced-auth patterns.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Search Protocol Host Lateral Movement Beacon
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Unpatched Windows Search' vulnerability. Pipeline should alert on version checks or exploit attempts targeting SearchProtocolHost.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SearchProtocolHost.exe spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or initiating connections to internal hosts. Search for version-detection attempts (e.g., WMI queries for Windows.Search assembly versions) prior to exploitation.

suggestion.title: Windows Search IndexerProcess Abnormal Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft via URI implies network exfiltration. SearchIndexer.exe is a background indexing service and should not normally initiate outbound HTTP/SMB.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline SearchIndexer.exe and SearchProtocolHost.exe network behavior (typically file:// and local named-pipes only). Alert on any outbound TCP to non-local addresses or suspicious SMB shares (e.g., \\attacker-ip\share). Exclude legitimate Windows Update / Microsoft telemetry ranges.

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension Installation via github.dev Webview
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'install[s] an extension that extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev' and 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension.' Pipeline missed the execution/persistence chain entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code spawning extension installation processes or writing extension manifests immediately after user navigates to github.dev or clicks suspicious link. Correlate webview process activity with unexpected extension manager invocations.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev and queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories.' Pipeline did not flag token extraction as a credential access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub OAuth tokens appearing in process arguments, environment variables, or webview message-passing contexts. Flag tokens that deviate from normal application use patterns (e.g., tokens in JavaScript contexts).

suggestion.title: GitHub API Repository Enumeration Burst
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack that 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access.' No detection use case for bulk API enumeration was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid GET requests to /user/repos, /orgs/{org}/repos, or similar endpoints within short timeframe from single GitHub token. Alert if pagination depth exceeds normal user behavior (e.g., >50 consecutive page requests).

suggestion.title: Webview Sandbox Message Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'abuses this system by running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor.' No detection for webview exploitation was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on unusual webview-to-editor message passing in VS Code, especially synthetic keypresses or programmatic extension installation commands originating from webview context. Baseline normal webview IPC patterns and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: github.dev OAuth Token Injection via Phishing Link
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows attackers to steal GitHub authentication tokens by tricking users into clicking a link' and 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev.' No initial-access or social-engineering detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails or messages containing github.dev links followed by immediate auth flows. Correlate suspicious github.dev visits with new extension installations or GitHub API token usage from that session.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Usage Anomaly - Scope Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The token is not scoped to the particular repo you interacted with, meaning it has full access to every other repo that you have access to.' No detection for abnormal token scope or permission escalation was flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of token scopes per user/service. Alert if a token suddenly queries repositories outside its defined scope, accesses org repos when previously limited to personal repos, or makes API calls inconsistent with token purpose.

suggestion.title: Weedhack Malware Execution on Minecraft Java Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Weedhack as targeting Minecraft users with no detection logic generated. Title phrase: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned from Minecraft Java launcher (javaw.exe) or process injection into minecraft.exe. Correlate with known Weedhack samples and unsigned binaries downloaded alongside pirated game distributions.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Execution and C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: CountLoader explicitly cited at scale (86K impact) with no detection use case for its execution or network behavior. Title phrase: 'CountLoader Hits 86K'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CountLoader typically performs staged C2 communication. Alert on unusual outbound connections from java.exe or game-related processes to low-reputation/newly registered domains, paired with in-memory loading indicators.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Persistence and Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' as the impact vector but pipeline captured no mining-specific detection. Title phrase: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect known miner process names (xmrig, cryptonight, stratum) spawned from game installation directories. Monitor for sustained CPU saturation from unexpected processes and memory-mapped access patterns typical of mining pools.

suggestion.title: Pirated Game Content Repository Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Distribution mechanism identified as pirated content but no detection for initial compromise or supply-chain compromise step. Title phrase: 'spread via pirated content'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of Minecraft .jar or launcher files from non-official repositories (non-launcher.mojang.com, non-Microsoft CDNs). Flag extraction of archives to game directories followed by immediate child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Sequential Tenant ID Enumeration Against Unauthenticated API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution on the shared platform. Iterating through the range surfaced records for every financial institution.' Pipeline missed a primary attack vector: sequential guessing of numeric identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single source executing 5+ API calls to same endpoint with incrementing numeric parameter values (e.g., tenant_id, customer_id) within sliding 5-minute window. Baseline normal application behavior; flag deviations with ≥3 sequential requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Returning PII and Internal Codes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind...Each one contained named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code.' Pipeline missed auth-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to endpoints returning 200 status with email regex matches, phone number patterns, or job titles, where Authorization header is absent and response size exceeds baseline (indicates data payload).

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin API Requests with Permissive CORS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Pipeline missed CORS misconfiguration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when API responses contain 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' or reflect untrusted Origin headers, AND response contains sensitive data patterns (email, phone, internal IDs). Flag especially for third-party vendor-hosted endpoints at institution-owned subdomains.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Loan Application Submission with Mismatched Officer Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name against that officer's institution, and the platform would treat the submission as legitimate.' Pipeline missed insider-impersonation fraud pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on loan application submissions where submitted officer_code differs from authenticated user's assigned code, or officer_code's institution differs from user's home institution. Flag submission source IP geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Identifiers Hardcoded in Public-Facing Application Files
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The tenant ID itself was visible in the portal's own public-facing files, so an unauthenticated caller did not need to guess it.' Pipeline missed source-code/client-side exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan HTTP responses for hardcoded numeric patterns (tenant IDs, customer IDs) in JavaScript bundles, HTML comments, or inline API calls. Alert when same identifier appears across multiple institution-fronted portals.

suggestion.title: New Third-Party Vendor Portal at Institution Subdomain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The asset entered the bank's external footprint when the vendor onboarded the bank to the platform, not when the bank's pentest was scoped.' Pipeline missed asset-discovery trigger for continuous testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when new CNAME/A-record appears under institutional domain resolving to third-party infrastructure (identified by WHOIS/reverse-DNS owner mismatch). Escalate if portal not documented in asset management or pentest scope history.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to Wave 7 Router Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes exploitation vector: 'unauthenticated remote exploitation' and 'poses a significant risk due to unauthenticated remote exploitation.' This defines initial-access activity via T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to Wave 7 router management interfaces (typical ports 80, 443, 8080) from external sources without corresponding authenticated session establishment. Alert on repeated probing or successful exploitation of vulnerable firmware versions.

suggestion.title: Inventory Acer Wave 7 Routers Running Vulnerable Firmware
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 'devices running firmware versions earlier than [version]' (truncated). Asset enumeration is prerequisite for impact assessment and exposure hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset databases, SNMP polling, or configuration management systems for Acer Wave 7 routers below the patched firmware version threshold. Cross-correlate with network exposure data to identify internet-facing or externally-accessible instances.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Configuration Tampering on Wave 7 Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies vulnerability as 'critical,' implying full device compromise. Successful exploitation grants attacker management-level access, likely enabling persistence via configuration or credential manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor affected Wave 7 routers for unauthorized configuration changes (firewall rules, DHCP, DNS, routing tables), new administrative accounts, or unexpected file system modifications in critical directories. Alert on any changes without corresponding change-management records.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is a native build config file; attackers use post-install scripts in compromised packages to execute arbitrary code during npm install. Article title identifies worm-like spread, implying lateral propagation via build system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning with parent=npm or node during package installation. Flag processes executing from node_modules/.bin or system temp directories with network outbound. Correlate with package.json or binding.gyp modification timestamps within 60s of install.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Package Dependency Chain Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes spread 'like a worm'—infection of downstream projects when they depend on compromised package. Need to detect transitive dependency pull of malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package.json entries resolving to known-compromised versions. Monitor lockfile changes introducing flagged packages. Detect installation of multiple versions of same package (version confusion).

suggestion.title: Lateral Spread via Shared npm Cache or Monorepo Infection
suggestion.rationale: Worm behavior suggests horizontal movement—infection of sibling projects in shared npm cache (~/.npm) or monorepo workspace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to .npm cache directory followed by cross-project process spawning. Alert on build system processes accessing multiple package.json files in sequence without user interaction.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp File Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title centers on binding.gyp—attacker likely modified this file to inject malicious native code compilation steps or override build targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on binding.gyp creation or modification in compromised packages. Flag additions of unusual sections (e.g., 'variables', 'conditions') that override compilation steps. Correlate with unexpected include_dirs or lib_dirs pointing to external sources.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Mismatches (Author / Repository Takeover)
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often exploit stolen credentials or abandoned packages. Need to detect sudden changes in package owner, repository URL, or metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for sudden package version bumps from new or recently-reactivated accounts. Flag packages whose GitHub repository URL changed in the last 30 days. Alert on npme/npm-enterprise user permission changes.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Post-install scripts in binding.gyp attacks commonly exfiltrate data or contact C2. Need to detect unexpected egress during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS/HTTP requests to non-CDN domains from processes spawned during npm install. Flag connections to newly-registered domains or known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for data exfiltration patterns (POST with file paths, base64 payloads).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution from Fake Installer Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states criminals 'trick users into running commands that quietly steal credentials'. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections despite this being the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where cmd.exe or powershell.exe parent is cmd.exe, launcher.exe, or installer process recently downloaded from malicious domains. Alert on child processes spawned from recently-created executables matching fake Claude/OpenAI installer filenames. Correlate with network connections to article IPs/domains within 10 minutes prior to execution.

suggestion.title: Access to Local Credential Stores Post-Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core payload: 'steal their credentials and other sensitive personal data'. Pipeline generated no detection for credential-store access (LSASS, SAM, browser vaults, SSH keys) despite being the stated primary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to LSASS.exe, credential manager APIs (VaultOpenVault), or browser credential databases (Chrome LocalState, Firefox logins.json, Edge Data). Alert on child processes of installer-spawned chains accessing %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh. Flag cmdkey.exe, runas.exe, or use of secretsdump.py / credential-access utilities.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration of Data to Attacker C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline provided 3 attacker IPs + 31 C2 domains in IOCs but generated zero network detection for exfiltration. Article describes stolen data being transmitted; no hunt for C2 beaconing exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from processes spawned by fake installers to known C2 IPs (145.249.109.147, 8.217.190.58, 109.107.170.111) and domains. Flag non-standard ports, sustained connections, or encrypted traffic from installer child processes. Detect DNS queries to article's 31 malicious domains even if DNS sinkholed. Correlate with credential-access process chains and file I/O to sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Detection of Fake Installer Page Access and Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phishing via fake pages hosted on Google Sites, Squarespace, GitHub Pages, Framer. Pipeline generated no initial-access detection for users visiting these malicious endpoints or downloading fake installers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web requests to article's domains (claudedesktop-apps.squarespace.com, claude-code-macos.framer.ai, claude-desktop.github.io, etc.) especially from browsers or download managers followed by local file execution. Flag downloads with suspicious naming (Claude*Installer*, setup.exe, *installer*.exe) from these domains. Alert on credential entry on pages mimicking official Claude/OpenAI branding but hosted on abuse-prone platforms (GitHub Pages, Squarespace, Framer).

suggestion.title: Behavioral Detection: System and Browser Data Harvesting Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing 'sensitive personal data from their devices' but pipeline generated no collection-phase behavioral hunt for local data exfiltration despite clear data-theft component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor spawned child processes accessing browser profile directories (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), system credential stores, SSH/AWS keys, .env files, temp directories, and clipboard. Flag file enumeration, archiving (7z.exe, tar, zip), or bulk read operations on sensitive directories from installer-spawned processes. Detect process chains: installer → credential-access tool → compression/exfil staging.

suggestion.title: Hash-Based Malware Detection on Endpoint File Writes
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to extract 6 SHA256 hashes provided in article IOCs. No hash-matching detection was generated despite hashes being high-confidence malware indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/write events matching provided SHA256 hashes (2546a45f..., d04208c0..., e1369e95..., 363df5e7..., cda84f03..., 39ff5c82...). Detect process execution of files with these hashes. Monitor for file downloads to temporary directories, user desktop, or Downloads folder matching hash values. Correlate file hash matches with network connections to article IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Acer Router Credential Log
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' This is the primary attack vector for CVE-2026-49200 and should be detected on first access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/POST requests to Acer Wave 7 routers (HTTP 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com) targeting /acer_cgi.log or similar firmware log paths. Flag any unauthenticated access (HTTP 200 responses without valid session tokens) or successful downloads of log archives containing credential strings.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credential Extraction from Acer Router Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states log file 'contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' This is the exploitation of CVE-2026-49200 and should be detected post-access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect extraction of acer_cgi.log followed by pattern matching for hardcoded Telnet/web service credential strings (user=admin, password= patterns, or Telnet port 23 references in plaintext). Correlate log retrieval with subsequent Telnet or HTTP auth attempts using extracted credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Acer Router Backup Modification (CVE-2026-49201)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Backup file access should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to upload.cgi endpoint on Acer Wave 7 routers; flag any backup file uploads (especially .tar or .gz files) or downloads of system backups. Correlate with AES cryptography operations or entropy anomalies in backup file modifications. Detect reboot events shortly after backup uploads, indicating backdoor execution.

suggestion.title: Telnet Authentication with Harvested Router Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article notes credentials in acer_cgi.log include 'login credentials (for web and Telnet).' Successful Telnet logins using leaked credentials should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TCP port 23 (Telnet) connections to affected Acer Wave 7 routers (firmware ≤T7c_GBL_1.01.000055) from external or untrusted sources. Flag successful authentication events where credentials match patterns extracted from log files or known harvesting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Acer Wave 7 Remote Management Access to Vulnerable Firmware
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends mitigation: 'disable remote management or restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses only.' Uncontrolled remote access to the web interface (port 80/443 on 192.168.76.1) on vulnerable firmware versions is the prerequisites for both CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS access to Acer Wave 7 admin interfaces (192.168.76.1:80, 192.168.76.1:443, acerconnect.com) from non-local IP ranges or geographies inconsistent with legitimate organization usage. Cross-reference source IPs against threat intelligence for known scanner/exploit infrastructure. Alert on firmware versions ≤T7c_GBL_1.01.000055.

suggestion.title: Acer Router Firmware Update Bypass or Delayed Patching
suggestion.rationale: Article states patches target 'end of June 2026' and are not yet available. Until patch deployment, all Acer Wave 7 routers ≤T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 are vulnerable. Monitor for patch non-compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Acer Wave 7 routers in production and flag devices still running firmware versions T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier 30+ days after June 30, 2026 (patch availability target). Flag devices with firmware update disabled via policy or failed update attempts, indicating management gaps.

suggestion.title: Game Engine Process Loading Unsigned DLL from Game Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL.' This DLL sideloading via game execution is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag game executables (RenPy, RPG Maker, or browser-based engines) loading unsigned or modified DLLs with anomalous import tables. Specifically detect natives2_blob.bin or variant FFmpeg DLL names from unexpected paths. Cross-reference against known-good FFmpeg signatures.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Base64-Decode Execution from Unsigned DLL Load Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' Staged PowerShell execution is key to Stage1 functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell invocation with -enc or -EncodedCommand preceded or triggered by game process or natives2_blob.bin DLL load. Look for System.Convert.FromBase64String in command line or event correlate game parent → unsigned DLL → PowerShell child.

suggestion.title: COM Object InprocServer32 Registry Hijacking for System DLL
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM and HKCU registry paths matching *\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 for modifications. Alert on value replacements of known system DLLs (Windows Color System Calibration, etc.) with unsigned or modified binaries. Correlate with game execution and login events.

suggestion.title: Virtualization and Hypervisor Artifact Detection from Game Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Stage1 performs basic checks for controlled environments' (VM/sandbox detection). Game processes should not perform evasion checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect game executable querying registry for virtualization markers (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\HARDWARE\Description\System, Hyper-V, VMware, VirtualBox artifacts), WMI queries for Win32_ComputerSystem properties, or checking for debugger/analysis tools. Flag as anomalous if parent is game or natives2_blob.bin context.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game Archive Distribution via Free File-Share and Torrent Trackers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Trojanized games have also been distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena' and 'redirected users to PixelDrain, a free file transfer service.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads from PixelDrain and known adult game torrent trackers (AniRena). Detect archive files containing both legitimate game binaries and natives2_blob.bin or ffmpeg.dll variants with anomalous timestamps. Monitor for archive extraction followed by suspicious game process behavior.

suggestion.title: Delayed Command-and-Control Downloader Activity from Persisted Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Delayed downloader indicates active C2 and RAT capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from game process or child process to unknown C2 domains, initiating several days post-execution. Monitor for executable/DLL downloads to temp or AppData directories. Correlate with COM-persisted process activation on login.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE Exploitation (CVE-2026-23479)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)' — the primary subject of the article. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for this critical vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis processes (redis-server) spawning unexpected child processes or executing shell commands. Alert on connections to port 6379 sending EVAL, SCRIPT LOAD, or CONFIG commands from untrusted networks. Baseline normal redis operational commands and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Redis Port Scanning & Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article context: autonomous tools discover the flaw through scanning. Pipeline did not suggest detection for reconnaissance phase activity targeting Redis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scanning patterns against Redis ports (6379, 6380) from single source across multiple targets or multiple sources to single Redis instance. Monitor for INFO command probing which reveals server version (enabling CVE validation).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Command Sequence
suggestion.rationale: RCE in Redis typically exploits command-injection or Lua scripting: 'RCE Flaw in Redis' implies command-execution pathway. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal command patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of Redis commands that should not coexist: SCRIPT LOAD followed by EVALSHA, or EVAL with shell-metacharacter payloads, or CONFIG SET directives from external clients. Alert if redis process spawns children after receiving such commands.

suggestion.title: Redis Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: 2-year-old flaws are often in default/legacy configurations. Pipeline should flag initial-access patterns for Redis with weak or absent auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful connections to Redis without AUTH command or with empty password. Correlate with subsequent EVAL/SCRIPT/CONFIG commands. Flag if source IP is external or unusual.

suggestion.title: Network Service Enumeration via Multi-Port Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'See Your Network Like an Attacker' directly implies adversarial reconnaissance techniques. HD Moore's work centers on Metasploit and network discovery; the webinar almost certainly discusses how attackers perform service enumeration across networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source IP initiating connection attempts across multiple destination ports (50+ unique ports within 5 minutes) or sequential port ranges, characteristic of nmap/masscan reconnaissance. Alert on SYN-scan patterns with low completion rates.

suggestion.title: Host-based Protocol Analysis for Vulnerability Scanning Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Webinar with HD Moore would include guidance on how attackers scan for vulnerable services. The phrase 'See Your Network Like an Attacker' implies understanding attack reconnaissance methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with common vulnerability-scanner User-Agent headers (Nmap, Masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, Shodan) or malformed HTTP requests (incomplete headers, unusual HTTP methods) sent during rapid port-sweeping activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Enumeration via SMB/LDAP Queries
suggestion.rationale: HD Moore's emphasis on 'seeing your network like an attacker' includes post-initial-access reconnaissance. Common attacker workflow includes LDAP enumeration and SMB share discovery once inside network perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual SMB queries (SAMR calls for user/group enumeration) or LDAP queries with high volume of distinguished names resolved from single source within 10-minute window. Flag recursive group lookups or Forest/Domain enumeration patterns.

suggestion.title: Attacker Perspective: Credential Spraying Detection from External Network Vantage
suggestion.rationale: Webinar teaches defensive teams to think like attackers; credential enumeration is standard post-reconnaissance activity. Title implies dual perspective (attacker/defender).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect coordinated failed authentication attempts across multiple user accounts (>10 unique users) from external IP ranges within 15 minutes, with no preceding successful interactive login. Correlate failed login patterns with observed port-scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Attacker Tooling Artifact Detection: Command-Line and Process Execution from Scanning Tools
suggestion.rationale: HD Moore background suggests discussion of common pentesting/attack tools (Metasploit, Empire, etc.). Article likely covers how these tools manifest on target systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command-line invocation of common scanning/enumeration tools (whoami, net.exe with group/user flags, ipconfig, tasklist, systeminfo) in rapid succession or within a short timeframe on non-administrative user accounts, especially post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RomulusLoader's 'process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution' to launch AnyDesk and SyncFuture. No UC captures hollow-process signatures or parent-child anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspended process creation followed by remote thread injection, or legitimate tools (AnyDesk, SyncFuture) spawned by rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, or unusual parent. Monitor for NtCreateThreadEx calls into suspended processes.

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox Registry Enumeration (Atlas RAT)
suggestion.rationale: Article states Atlas RAT performs 'checks for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, CExecSvc service, and OS UUID.' None of these sandbox-evasion patterns are in detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes querying registry paths for 'Microsoft Defender Application Guard', enumerating 'CExecSvc', or reading OS UUID via WMI. Alert on OS UUID queries combined with subsequent malware execution.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential Theft via SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies SilentRunLoader as Python-based stealer that 'steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' This specific credential-access pattern must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python.exe or suspicious processes accessing Chrome Local State, Login Data, or Cookies SQLite files. Alert on sqlite3 queries or file reads from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data outside Chrome process context.

suggestion.title: Keylogging, Audio, and Webcam Capture (Atlas RAT)
suggestion.rationale: Article details Atlas RAT's 'keylogging', 'audio and webcam recording' capabilities. Absence of detections for keyboard hook injection, audio device enumeration, or Win32 webcam APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SetWindowsHookEx (keyboard logging), IAudioClient/IAudioCaptureClient COM interfaces, or Windows.Media.Capture APIs being invoked by non-browser processes. Alert on unexpected audio/video device access outside Media Player contexts.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Lure Detection (Payroll, Tax, VAT)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications' as lures. Need email-content rules for region-specific tax/payroll language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with German/Italian/UK tax keywords ('Steuererklärung', 'dichiarazione', 'VAT notice') in subject/body, impersonating government or HR, with suspicious attachment types or external links. Correlate against known TA4922 sender infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Software Abuse for RAT Delivery (AnyDesk, SyncFuture)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes RomulusLoader 'was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture.' Absence of rules for unexpected installation or execution of these tools via loader chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AnyDesk or SyncFuture being installed or executed by non-standard parents (e.g., rundll32, regsvcs, mshta). Monitor for registry persistence mechanisms (Run keys) for these tools. Flag if execution follows unusual loader process chains.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-45247 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]'. Pipeline failed to generate even this baseline detection—any Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer instance exposed to the internet is immediately at risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installations (product identification from web banners, module lists, or version endpoint responses) that are network-accessible and not patched past the vulnerability. Cross-reference scan results with CVSS scores and CISA KEV due date (2026-06-06).

suggestion.title: HTTP: Malicious CacheWarmer Cookie Deserialization Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'supplying a crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie'. Pipeline extracted zero indicators despite this being the explicit attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing 'CacheWarmer' cookie with serialized PHP object signatures (strings starting with 'O:' followed by digit-length pairs, or containing PHP namespace indicators like 'namespace' or 'class'). Flag requests to paths known to process cache-warming requests (e.g., /cache/, /full-page-cache/). High entropy or base64-encoded cookie values combined with error responses (500, 502) may indicate failed RCE attempts.

suggestion.title: Process: Unexpected Code Execution Post-Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RCE outcome ('achieve remote code execution') but pipeline did not model post-exploitation execution detection. Successful exploitation will result in shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with suspicious parents (CacheWarmer-triggering requests), especially sh/bash shells, curl/wget downloaders, or perl/python script engines. Correlate with HTTP access logs showing CacheWarmer cookie activity in the same minute window.

suggestion.title: Web Application: Error/Exception Logs from Deserialization Failures
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts will generate PHP exceptions. Article mentions 'deserialization of untrusted data' without safe guards, implying error conditions will be logged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for PHP exceptions/errors containing 'unserialize()', '__wakeup()', '__destruct()', or 'Mirasvit' class names in error logs, especially preceded by CacheWarmer-cookie-related access attempts. Successful gadget-chain exploitation may be silent, but malformed payloads will trigger verbose stack traces.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability: Mirasvit Module Detection in Magento Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer is a Magento extension; pipeline should identify and catalog all instances to determine exposure scope. Article emphasizes federal due date (2026-06-06) makes inventory critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Magento instances in your environment; query app/etc/modules/ directories or Magento admin API (if accessible) for 'Mirasvit_FullPageCache' or 'Mirasvit_MirasvitFullPageCache' modules. Cross-reference with patch management records to identify unpatched instances before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Integer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2025-48595 is 'a high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework, which can be leveraged for increased privileges' with 'no user interaction to exploit.' Requires detection hypothesis for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework process anomalies (e.g., unexpected privilege elevation, memory-corruption-like behavior, or spawning of elevated-context child processes) following patched system baselines for Android 14–16. Correlation with failed/successful memory access patterns may indicate integer-overflow exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Linux Cgroup v1 Namespace Escape (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2022-0492 in detail: 'local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' Specifically targets 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cgroup v1 subsystem manipulation attempts, particularly writes to cgroup_release_agent or release_agent files from unprivileged container processes. Cross-reference with container-escape indicators: host root-level process spawns originating from container namespaces, uid/gid map anomalies, or capability escalation sequences.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Container Host Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'is especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities' and states CVE-2022-0492 requires patching by June 5, 2026. Detection needed for hosts still vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query systems with Linux kernel versions <4.9.301, <4.14.266, <4.19.229, <5.4.177, <5.10.97, <5.15.20, <5.16.6 running containers with elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SETUID). Correlate with any cgroup manipulation attempts or container escape logs.

suggestion.title: Android June 2026 Security Patch Compliance Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'June 2026 security patches (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 security patch levels)' address CVE-2025-48595. Inventory mismatch indicates exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Android devices running versions 14–16 with patch levels before 2026-06-05 or missing the June 2026 security update. Correlate with any framework-level exceptions or crashes in that period.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation in Containerized Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2022-0492 allows 'root-level access on the host system' from within a container. Detection needed for lateral-movement escalation after initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden uid/gid transitions from container-constrained IDs to root (0:0) in processes launched from container-origin ancestors. Alert on /etc/sudoers modification, capability-set syscalls, or namespace-crossing file operations from container-scoped pids.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection' and 'By including Jinja2 template expressions it is possible to execution Python code'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to /api/kernels with KERNEL_* environment variables containing Jinja2 metaclass/builtin payloads (__globals__, __class__, os.popen, subprocess, __subclasses__). High-confidence indicator of active exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Post-exploit Kubernetes privilege escalation via privileged pod creation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'code can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token' enabling creation of privileged/escalation pods with hostPath, hostNetwork, and RBAC modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Enterprise Gateway service account creating pods with privileged=true, hostPath mounts, hostNetwork=true, or modifying rolebindings/clusterrolebindings. Indicates post-exploitation and lateral movement.

suggestion.title: RCE: Python child process spawning shell from Enterprise Gateway container
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE allows 'execution Python code and OS Commands in the Enterprise Gateway service'; post-exploit shell spawning from Python runtime is primary execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process python/python3/python3.10+ spawning sh, bash, dash, or accessing file paths /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/* from Enterprise Gateway containers. High-confidence RCE activity.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes service account token credential theft from Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states RCE vulnerability allows 'use or steal the Kubernetes service account token, which can steal Kubernetes [secrets]'—credential access is primary post-exploitation objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads, copies, or exfiltration of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token from Enterprise Gateway pod, including base64 encoding or outbound transmission. Confirms credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes YAML Multi-Document Injection via Environment Variable Rendering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'inject multi-document YAML to create additional unintended Kubernetes resources'—this is a distinct attack outcome from single-key injection. Requires detection for YAML document separators (---, ...) appearing in rendered manifests or audit trail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor K8s API audit logs for pod creation where the requestObject.spec contains multiple YAML document separators (--- or ...). Flag if initiated by EG ServiceAccount and the responseObject differs from the requestObject in pod count or resource definitions.

suggestion.title: Host Filesystem Access via Injected hostPath Volume Mounts
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1611 (Escape to Host) as a technique; the vulnerability explicitly enables container escape via injected hostPath volumes. UC_7_3 catches privilege escalation but not the specific host-access vector necessary for escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify pod creation events in K8s audit logs where spec.volumes[] contains hostPath entries AND the creating ServiceAccount matches jupyter-enterprise-gateway*. Escalate if combined with securityContext.privileged=true or runAsUser=0.

suggestion.title: Post-Injection Host Execution Anomaly from Escaped Container Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1611 (Escape to Host) and T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation) as outcomes. No existing hunt targets anomalous process spawning from within an exploited kernel pod post-injection—the 'impact' phase execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container runtime (containerd, Docker) logs or eBPF for process execution with uid=0 from within a kernel pod shortly after a suspicious /api/kernels POST. Cross-reference pod name with EG ServiceAccount and presence of hostPath mounts to confirm escape attempt.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Process Execution and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title names DesckVB RAT as the delivered payload. No use case for execution or persistence indicators. Article states 'Deliver DesckVB RAT' but pipeline generated zero coverage for RAT behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DesckVB-associated process creation patterns (typically PowerShell or rundll32 child processes) and registry modifications under HKCU\Software indicating scheduled task or Run key persistence for known RAT families. Correlate with malspam delivery artifacts.

suggestion.title: Malspam with Embedded or Redirected Payloads via DoubleClick
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign.' Article explicitly states DoubleClick is the abuse vector, yet pipeline generated zero detection for malspam delivery mechanisms or ad-redirected URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails containing shortened URLs or DoubleClick (doubleclick.net) redirect chains pointing to suspicious domains. Correlate recipient patterns, sender reputation, and landing-page file signatures associated with DesckVB dropper campaigns.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication for DesckVB RAT (Known IP/Domain Infrastructure)
suggestion.rationale: DesckVB is a known RAT family with documented C2 infrastructure. Article states delivery of DesckVB but pipeline provided no IOCs for C2 IPs, domains, or protocol signatures enabling network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to known or suspected DesckVB C2 infrastructure by domain, IP, or behavioral pattern (unusual ports, TLS certificates, DNS query sequences). Cross-check against public DesckVB threat feeds and passive DNS records.

suggestion.title: Macro-Based or Script-Based RAT Dropper Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malspam campaigns typically deliver via Office macros or script files. Article title indicates malspam delivery but no use case for detecting macro/script execution characteristic of RAT droppers (e.g., OleObject, PowerShell invocation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office processes (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning PowerShell, cmd.exe, or unusual child processes; flag .ps1 / .vbs / .bat execution from user-writable or temp directories. Correlate timing with email receipt events.

suggestion.title: Known DesckVB File Hash and Malware Repository Correlation
suggestion.rationale: DesckVB is a named, known malware family. Pipeline should have extracted or cross-referenced documented file hashes, sample signatures, or YARA rules but provided zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain and alert on detection of known DesckVB sample hashes (MD5, SHA1, SHA256) via file analysis, endpoint telemetry, and sandbox detonations. Flag any file matching documented DesckVB YARA rules or behavioral clusters from public threat intel (VirusTotal, AlienVault, etc.).

suggestion.title: DoubleClick Ad Network Compromise Indicators and Credential Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights DoubleClick abuse as the distribution vector. Pipeline provided zero IOCs or detections for identifying compromised ad slots, malicious ad creatives, or user redirects from legitimate DoubleClick domains to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for users loading legitimate doubleclick.net URLs but receiving unexpected or uncached 3xx/4xx responses; detect suspicious script injection into ad-serving responses. Flag clicks on DoubleClick ads that redirect to non-Google second-stage domains or known malware-distribution hosts.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing with business document templates
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'disguises itself as an everyday business document — a purchase order, a quote, or a request for proposal. Once an unsuspecting employee opens...' Initial access vector is clearly phishing attachments mimicking procurement docs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with high-confidence business document subject lines (PO, quote, RFP, invoice) but originated from external, non-verified senders. Inspect attachments for embedded scripts or suspicious macros. Cross-reference sender domain against procurement whitelist.

suggestion.title: JavaScript malware execution from downloaded files
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'JS.MonoGlyphRAT' and describes malware 'disguises itself' in documents. JS execution, especially from user temp or Downloads, is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cscript.exe, wscript.exe, or jscript.exe spawned from typical phishing download paths (AppData\Local\Temp, Downloads). Correlate with recent email-delivered files or Office macro-launch patterns. Establish baseline of legitimate JS execution and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malware ingress via supply-chain document templates
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealthy new threat...disguises itself as an everyday business document.' T1105 applies to the delivery and execution of the RAT payload following document opening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated immediately after document opening (via WinRAR, Office, or PDF readers). Flag file writes to suspicious directories post-document interaction. Correlate timing of file creation in temp/appdata with subsequent C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: C2 domain resolution and repeated polling
suggestion.rationale: Article lists aryamint.com and scan.aryamint.com as IOCs. RATs typically beacon repeatedly; detect periodic DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS requests to these domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated DNS lookups for aryamint.com or subdomains, especially from endpoints outside normal business workflow. Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to aryamint.com subdomain endpoints with short inter-request intervals (RAT heartbeat pattern).

suggestion.title: Registry persistence or execution artifacts from JS.MonoGlyphRAT
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies JS.MonoGlyphRAT but provides no details on persistence mechanisms. RATs commonly modify Run keys, startup folders, or WMI event subscriptions for longevity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or user-level Run keys coinciding with JS execution. Flag WMI event consumer/filter creation tied to script execution context. Monitor startup folder for .js or .vbs files not attributed to known software.

suggestion.title: Process parent-child anomalies: Office/WinRAR → cscript/wscript → network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes document-triggered execution. Behavioral chain of (email attachment opener → script interpreter → network connection) is highly suspicious and differs from legitimate workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build detection for parent process chains: WinRAR.exe or Excel.exe/Word.exe → cscript.exe/wscript.exe → svchost.exe or rundll32.exe → network connection. This chain is rare in legitimate use and indicates document-delivery exploitation.

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda URL C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actors 'hide inside Amazon Web Services' using 'lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws' for command channel. Article phrase: 'Rather than using easily blocked servers, the threat actors hide inside one of the world's most trusted platforms.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from user endpoints to *.on.aws domains (Lambda URL namespace). Pair with data volume anomalies (>1MB/min) or connection clustering (same 5-tuple repeating 30+ times in 1hr). Correlate with CloudTrail for corresponding Lambda invocations from unexpected IAM principals.

suggestion.title: HazyBeacon Malware Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article provides seven SHA256 hashes for HazyBeacon samples but no execution behavior described. Given T1027 (Obfuscation) technique and multi-hash variants, pipeline missed behavioral detection for polymorphic malware. Article phrase: 'multiple SHA256 hashes' indicate variant family requiring behavioral clustering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create behavioral YARA/sigma rules for process injection, command-line obfuscation patterns, and registry persistence mechanisms expected from HazyBeacon variants. Hash alone will miss polymorphic generations. Cluster variants using SSDEEP fuzzy hashing.

suggestion.title: Southeast Asia Government Network Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'targets government networks across Southeast Asia' but provides no delivery mechanism (phishing, exploit, watering hole). Pipeline missed initial-access detection gap. Malware delivery must have occurred before C2 beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Southeast Asian government domain patterns for phishing delivery (suspicious TLDs impersonating .gov.sg, .gov.th, etc.). Detect URL clicks followed by SHA256 execution within 15min. Flag email senders from outside region with government employee targeting signals.

suggestion.title: Compromised AWS Credential Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign uses AWS Lambda infrastructure in specific region. Article provides no evidence of misconfiguration; implies credentials were compromised or IAM roles abused. Pipeline missed credential-access phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CloudTrail for: (1) sts:GetSessionToken / sts:AssumeRole calls from unexpected IPs outside AWS IP space; (2) creation of new Lambda functions or API Gateway endpoints from non-admin principals; (3) lambda:InvokeFunction calls from external, non-approved AWS accounts.

suggestion.title: Multi-Sample Campaign Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article lists campaign identifier 'CL-STA-1020' and provides seven SHA256 samples, indicating coordinated malware family. Pipeline missed campaign-level detection that ties variants together. Article phrase: 'Known as HazyBeacon and tracked under cluster identifier CL-STA-1020'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multiple hosts in same environment connecting to same Lambda C2 URL (lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws) with similar beaconing intervals (±30sec). Tag as CL-STA-1020 cluster activity rather than isolated incidents.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP/2 HPACK Dynamic Table Amplification Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack works by 'inserting a header into the HPACK dynamic table and referencing it repeatedly via a compact indexed representation that can be one byte large' with 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation' at ratios of '5,700:1' (Envoy) and '4,000:1' (Apache httpd). This compression amplification is the attack's core vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 HPACK processing for abnormal per-byte allocation overhead. Baseline normal header reuse ratios (typically 1:1–10:1 for legitimate traffic). Flag connections exhibiting sustained amplification >100:1 or repeated references to single HPACK table entries within short time windows as compression exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP/2 Flow-Control Stalling for Memory Retention
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack second phase: 'preventing the memory from being freed once the request completes' via 'advertising a zero-byte flow-control window' and 'server periodically sends tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames to avoid timeouts.' Requests 'are never fully completed, and the allocated memory keeps growing without being freed.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 stream states exhibiting WINDOW_SIZE=0 paired with repeated WINDOW_UPDATE frames (sender artificially stalling response) and no corresponding DATA frames. Flag streams outstanding >60 seconds with zero-byte flow-control windows as potential resource-holding attacks.

suggestion.title: Detect Rapid Server Memory Exhaustion Under HTTP/2 Load
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'exhausted 32 GB RAM in about 10 seconds' (Envoy), '~18 seconds' (Apache), '~45 seconds' (NGINX), '~45 seconds' (IIS 64GB). Memory consumption rate from single or few clients is the impact signature and primary operational alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2-enabled servers for sustained memory growth exceeding 1 GB/min or reaching >90% utilization within 60 seconds from single or small-set client IPs. Correlate with concurrent HTTP/2 streams in incomplete state (no FIN, no payload data frames).

suggestion.title: Detect Evasive HPACK Tiny Header Values with Large Internal Allocations
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'bypasses existing defenses such as limits on the total decoded header size, as the header values used in the attack are tiny, and amplification comes from internal per-header bookkeeping and memory allocations.' This defense evasion pattern must be detected at protocol level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HPACK indexed header references where encoded size (1–4 bytes) triggers disproportionate server-side memory allocation (>1 KB per reference). Flag connections where total decoded header size remains within limits but internal bookkeeping memory grows unbounded, indicating per-header allocation exploit.

suggestion.title: Detect Slowloris-Style HTTP/2 Stream Stalling Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack mechanism as 'Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' This classic DoS pattern retargeted to HTTP/2 protocol must be detectable via stream resource locks without progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 streams remaining in 'open' state without DATA frames for >30 seconds, blocked by zero-byte WINDOW_SIZE, with repeated WINDOW_UPDATE frames but no actual payload transmission. Flag patterns with multiple concurrent stalled streams from single client as Slowloris-HTTP/2 variant.

suggestion.title: Identify Deployments of Vulnerable HTTP/2 Server Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article lists patched versions: nginx 1.29.8 (max_headers added), Apache httpd mod_http2 2.0.41 (CVE-2026-49975); unpatched: IIS (Windows Server 2025), Envoy 1.37.2, Cloudflare Pingora. Version reconnaissance is prerequisite for attack targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and alert on deployments running vulnerable HTTP/2 stacks: NGINX <1.29.8, Apache httpd mod_http2 <2.0.41 (CVE-2026-49975), any IIS version with HTTP/2 enabled, Envoy 1.37.2, Cloudflare Pingora. Prioritize assets for protocol disabling or patching.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—occurs via postinstall hooks reading ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, cloud config. Pipeline generated zero UCs for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/node process trees with file read access to credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.git, ~/.aws, ~/.config, HKCU:\Software\Git). Alert on postinstall or prepare scripts accessing multiple credential paths in sequence, or reading files followed by outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republish with Version Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—indicates attacker republished @redhat-cloud-services with 90+ compromised versions. No detection for unexpected version spikes, new publish events from unusual contexts, or packages with injected dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: (a) new minor/patch releases for dormant @redhat packages outside normal cadence, (b) package versions with new postinstall/prepare scripts added, (c) npm publish or npm adduser commands from unexpected geographic locations or IPs, (d) unexpected new transitive dependencies in package-lock.json.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline npm Install with Environment Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'silently infecting CI/CD environments'—postinstall runs with access to GITHUB_TOKEN, cloud credentials, deploy keys. No detection for npm execution in CI pipelines followed by credential exfiltration or outbound data transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install or npm ci in CI runners (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins agents) with subsequent HTTP/HTTPS requests containing credential patterns (Bearer tokens, AWS SigV4 signatures). Flag node.exe/npm making connections to unknown/rare IPs during or immediately after postinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Package.json Postinstall Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism is postinstall scripts injected into package.json and package-lock.json. Pipeline failed to flag modifications to these critical files or injection of new scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json and package-lock.json for additions/modifications of postinstall, preinstall, prepare scripts. Alert on scripts containing shell invocations (sh, bash, powershell, curl, wget). Flag changes committed by unexpected accounts or in unexpected branches; correlate with package-lock.json version mutations.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Credential Compromise—Account Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker obtained credentials for @redhat-cloud-services npm account to republish 90+ versions. No detection for npm account takeover or anomalous publish/login activity from that namespace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm login events from: (a) new geographic locations or IP ranges, (b) off-hours or unusual timing, (c) unusual User-Agents. Monitor npm publish commands to @redhat-cloud-services namespace from new accounts, new API tokens, or contexts outside normal maintainer behavior. Baseline: publish frequency, timing, types of versions released.

suggestion.title: Developer Workstation Credential Harvesting via npm
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'infecting developer systems'—when developers run npm install, postinstall hooks access .ssh/id_rsa, .gitconfig, cloud config, stealing local credentials. No UC for credential access from npm on non-CI systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On developer machines, monitor npm/node child processes accessing: ~/.ssh/id_rsa*, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/*, ~/.aws/credentials, HKCU:\Software\Git, HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU. Alert if single npm postinstall reads 3+ different credential stores or reads credentials followed by spawning curl/wget.

suggestion.title: Untrusted MCP Server or Skill Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Agents don't build from a blank slate; they pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs, external tools... These inputs can become part of your software supply chain even though they were never declared as traditional dependencies... Additionally, they're often selected and invoked at runtime, with no review.' Cites '76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984' and '~1/3 of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent runtime instantiation or registration of MCP servers, external tools, or skills that are not in an approved inventory. Flag sources pulling from public registries (npm, PyPI, GitHub) without commit or artifact approval. Detect dynamic tool loading where the tool source is not pre-authorized by security policy.

suggestion.title: Agent Executing System Commands Without Human Approval Gate
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Agents don't just suggest a change and wait; they run scripts, query internal systems, modify files, and call APIs at machine speed.' and lists risks including 'unsafe command execution' and 'unpredictable chains of action.' This represents execution speed that outpaces human review, a key operational gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire command execution sequences originating from agent service accounts or containers (e.g., scripts, curl, docker, kubectl) within a short time window. Flag shell commands that contain variable substitution or dynamic construction. Alert on commands modifying code repositories, config files, or production systems issued from agent contexts without prior approval tokens or signatures.

suggestion.title: Agent-Driven Unauthorized Data Access or Lateral Query
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'query internal systems' and risk includes 'unauthorized access to systems or data' and 'data exposure through tool calls.' The specific example: agent with certain permissions reasoning forward and accessing systems it should not have touched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent service accounts querying or enumerating internal databases, credential stores, or knowledge repositories (wikis, repos, cloud storage) that fall outside the agent's declared operational scope. Detect API calls from agent contexts to systems that require human authorization. Flag access to sensitive data repositories (secrets managers, config stores) at unusual times or from unusual agent instances.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Dependency or Code Generation Without Review Checkpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'An agent can... add a dependency... often in a single uninterrupted sequence' and 'they pull in... dependencies... with no review.' This breaks the traditional artifact inspection model and introduces supply-chain risk inline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected or unapproved package installations, imports, or version pins added to dependency files (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml) without human code review or merge approval. Flag commits to repositories authored by agent service accounts that include new dependencies. Detect out-of-band dependency injection (transitive or runtime-loaded dependencies not declared in lockfiles).

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring Safety Instructions or Continuing After Freeze Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article gives explicit example: 'agent that ignored repeated "freeze" instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This represents an agent not halting on control signals and escalating to destructive action (T1561 - disk wipe proxy).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of destructive commands (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, DELETE, truncate) issued by agent service accounts shortly after a kill-switch or safety signal was logged but did not prevent execution. Monitor for agent processes continuing to operate after a timeout, pause, or stop event was recorded. Flag cover-up operations (INSERT, UPDATE, TRUNCATE) on the same system immediately following deletion events.

suggestion.title: Agent Making External API Calls or Tool Invocations with Sensitive Context
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'data exposure through tool calls' and notes agents 'call APIs' at machine speed. This creates risk that agent context (credentials, code, data) leaks through external integrations never meant to receive it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent processes making outbound API calls or HTTP requests to external domains not in an allowlist. Flag calls that transmit code snippets, configuration details, credentials, or repository contents. Detect unusual User-Agent patterns or API authentication tokens in external requests. Alert on agents invoking third-party SaaS tools with code or data payloads in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Windows Search URI Handler Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability'—pipeline should detect when Windows Search processes receive or handle malicious URIs designed to trigger the vulnerability. No use case generated despite this being the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Search (SearchIndexer.exe, Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls.dll) processes receiving or parsing unusual URI schemes or opening network connections to attacker-controlled hosts. Flag URIs with embedded NTLM auth tokens or UNC paths.

suggestion.title: NTLM Hash Capture via Windows Search
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Steal NTLMv2 Hashes'—core attack outcome. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect forced NTLM authentication from Windows Search processes to external SMB/WebDAV shares, or monitor for unusual NTLM Type-2/Type-3 message exchanges initiated by search-related processes. Alert on hash relay patterns.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Process Spawning Unusual Children
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerabilities often lead to code execution; pipeline should cover execution phase following the initial handler trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SearchIndexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe, or Windows.UI.Xaml-related processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network utilities (curl, certutil, etc.). Monitor for unusual parent-child relationships and command-line argument passing.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification of Windows Search Handlers
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation or persistence of URI handler vulnerabilities often involves registry manipulation of URI schemes or handler associations—no detection suggested despite this being common attack pattern for this class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to HKLM\Software\Classes\<URI_scheme> or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FileExts registries tied to search, particularly creation of new shell\open\command values or unexpected handler changes.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Index Database Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Hash-theft attacks may target Windows Search index store (edb files); pipeline should detect unusual read/write patterns to search database files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes other than SearchIndexer.exe reading windows.edb, catalog.wci, or other search index files, or unexpected file access from network-connected processes to search database locations.

suggestion.title: Forced SMB Authentication Originating from SearchIndexer
suggestion.rationale: The 'steal NTLMv2 hashes' mechanism likely involves triggering NTLM auth to attacker SMB server—article implies this attack chain but pipeline generated no detection for out-of-band hash capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SearchIndexer.exe or Windows Search components initiating SMB connections (port 445) or WebDAV requests (port 80/443) to non-corporate/external IP addresses, especially with UNC path resolution patterns typical of hash-relay setups.

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension Installation via github.dev Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers to install malicious extensions that steal GitHub OAuth tokens by tricking users into clicking a link'—this is the primary attack vector requiring immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension installations initiated from webview/browser context immediately following user clicks on suspicious URLs. Monitor extension name patterns mimicking GitHub integration to detect trojanization.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Theft and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev'—core attack is token interception and forwarding, requiring visibility into github.dev authentication flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens appearing in suspicious process contexts, webview memory, or network streams. Alert on github.dev authentication tokens being accessed by extensions or JS running outside github.dev origin.

suggestion.title: Simulated Input Events to Bypass Interactive Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor'—automated interaction to bypass user approval prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on synthetic KeyboardEvent or MouseEvent objects created programmatically within webview contexts targeting the host editor. Correlate with rapid extension installation or permission grants.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Repository Enumeration Post-Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access'—the token scope grants full repository access, enabling API-based discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub API calls (list_user_repos, list_org_repos) with bearer tokens recently associated with new extension installations. Alert on enumeration patterns lacking prior history in user's API activity.

suggestion.title: Webview Sandboxing Bypass via Message Passing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploits VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system'—the fundamental vulnerability is inadequate isolation between webview and main editor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostMessage calls between github.dev webview and VS Code editor for unexpectedly privileged operations (install extension, access tokens). Alert on cross-origin message passing with action commands.

suggestion.title: Cleartext GitHub Token Exposure in Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation guidance: 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev'—implies attacker threat is token residence in DOM storage accessible to extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB API calls accessing github.dev domain data, especially from extension or webview contexts. Monitor for token patterns in DOM.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CountLoader Hits 86K' with no execution-phase UC. Named malware at this scale demands process-creation monitoring; pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation matching CountLoader naming patterns, suspicious command-line arguments (mining parameters, C2 URLs), or child processes spawned from pirated-application directories. Correlate with unsigned binaries or known malicious code-signing certificates.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Mod Injection & Unauthorized Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'—implying malicious mod/plugin injection. Title reveals pirated content as delivery vector. Zero detection generated for Minecraft process anomalies despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor javaw.exe for unexpected child processes, DLL injection, or module loads from non-standard mod directories. Flag connections from Minecraft to known malware C2 or cryptocurrency pool domains.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Resource Consumption Anomaly
