suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'—this is the impact/outcome. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase detection despite mining being the observable endpoint of the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained CPU/memory consumption from xmrig, stratum, or cryptocurrency-pool-adjacent processes. Alert on miner binary execution spawned from unexpected parent processes (pirated app installers, Minecraft, browser). Correlate with known malware families.

suggestion.title: Pirated Software Repository Download & Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'Pirated Content'—the initial access point for all 86K infections. No initial-access UC generated despite this being detectable via proxy/DNS/download telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for downloads from known malicious Minecraft mod repositories, cracked-software sites, or pirate-game distribution domains. Flag simultaneous retrieval of legitimate tools (mod loaders) alongside suspicious archives or executables from the same session.

suggestion.title: Boot-Time Persistence via Registry Autostart
suggestion.rationale: Malware at 86K scale implies persistence mechanism, but kill chain is empty with zero persistence-phase detection. No use case for detecting registry/scheduler modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, RunOnce, and Scheduled Tasks for malware/miner executable paths. Flag modifications containing pirated-application directories or cryptocurrency-miner naming patterns.

suggestion.title: C2 & Cryptocurrency Pool Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Miners require outbound pool connectivity; CountLoader needs command-channel. No command-and-control detection generated despite clear network-based signals from 86K compromised hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained outbound connections to cryptocurrency mining pools (stratum protocol, mining-pool domains). Hunt DNS queries for known CountLoader/Weedhack C2 infrastructure. Flag non-standard encrypted tunneling from suspicious processes.

suggestion.title: Sequential Tenant ID Enumeration via Unauthenticated API
suggestion.rationale: Article states the endpoint 'required no authentication' and 'incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution.' This is a core enumeration attack not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to undocumented API endpoints with sequential or incremental numeric parameters (e.g., tenant_id=1, 2, 3...) sent in rapid succession from external IPs or non-whitelisted origins. Alert when 5+ sequential requests return distinct entity records (org names, staff names, phone numbers).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Extraction of Organization Records and Employee PII from Shared SaaS Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article documents extraction of 'named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code' via API. This credential and organizational intelligence harvesting warrants behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API responses containing multiple employee records (names, emails, phone numbers, job titles) returned to unauthenticated requesters or from non-sanctioned third-party portals. Correlate bulk response sizes (>10 org records per request) with caller IP reputation and geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin API Invocation from Attacker-Controlled Third-Party Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' This CORS bypass enabling API abuse from external sites must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to sensitive APIs with Origin headers pointing to untrusted third-party domains, combined with CORS preflight responses (OPTIONS) that lack Vary: Origin or have wildcard (*) policies. Flag requests that modify or exfiltrate data despite mismatched origins.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Borrower Application Submission Using Extracted Vendor-Issued Officer Codes
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name against that officer's institution.' Detection of this impact-phase attack requires behavioral analysis of application submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on borrower application submissions where the attributed officer code or email does not match the authenticated user session or IP geolocation. Correlate application volume and mismatched officer assignments per origination portal session; flag sessions submitting 3+ applications with inconsistent officer-to-caller mappings.

suggestion.title: Third-Party SaaS Portal Hostname Discovery and Scope Expansion
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The asset entered the bank's external footprint when the vendor onboarded the bank to the platform, not when the bank's pentest was scoped.' New third-party hostnames fronted at the institution's subdomain are attack surface rarely covered by annual assessments and require continuous discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline DNS A/CNAME records and certificate transparency logs for institution-owned subdomains. Alert on new CNAME entries pointing to third-party cloud platforms (SaaS vendors, mortgage origination services, API gateways) and cross-reference with previous security assessments. Trigger when third-party hostname has been live >30 days without documented testing.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Exposure on Customer-Facing Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article documents an endpoint 'that required no authentication and no session of any kind.' Pipeline should flag API endpoints that should require authentication but do not, especially those exposed at customer-facing subdomains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform baseline API authentication checks on customer-facing portal endpoints during continuous scanning. Alert when endpoints tagged to return sensitive organizational data (staff, tenant info, credentials) respond successfully to unauthenticated requests or requests lacking valid session tokens. Correlate with CORS policy logs to detect allowance of cross-origin invocation.

suggestion.title: Magento CVE-2026-45247 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-45247 as exploited Magento RCE flaw in CISA KEV Catalog, indicating active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this critical vulnerability warrant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to known vulnerable Magento endpoints (e.g., /app/action, /module/index) with suspicious payloads or PHP code. Flag process execution spawned by web server processes (apache, nginx) with unusual command lines or file write attempts to web directories.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload to Magento Directory
suggestion.rationale: Magento RCE typically leads to web shell placement for persistence. Article documents active exploitation but pipeline surfaced no persistence-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file creation in Magento root/media/modules with executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar). Correlate with unusual process execution from apache/nginx users spawning curl, wget, or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from Compromised Magento Instance
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of public-facing RCE typically establishes C2 for command execution. Article references exploitation but no discovery or C&C-phase detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from Magento-hosting servers to suspicious domains, particularly those with recently-registered or high-entropy DNS names. Flag repeated beacons on non-standard ports or connections to known malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Magento Database Access
suggestion.rationale: RCE on e-commerce platform permits direct database querying for customer/payment data. No collection/exfiltration phase detections despite article's 'exploited' language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual SQL queries from web server processes (SELECT * FROM customer tables), large data transfers to external IP ranges, or unencrypted payment/PII egress from Magento servers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from Apache/Nginx Worker
suggestion.rationale: Magento RCE frequently results in command execution via web server context (proc_open, shell_exec, system). Pipeline ignored execution-phase attacker behaviors despite 'RCE' in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when apache, nginx, or www-data user spawns child processes (bash, cmd, powershell, curl, wget). Flag parent-child relationships where web server process calls system utilities to download external scripts or modify system configuration.

suggestion.title: Android Framework exploitation attempt detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'actively exploited in the wild' but provides no technical indicators of exploitation (crash signatures, memory corruption patterns, affected app behavior). Detection is limited by truncation; if full article contained exploit POC details, specific behavioral patterns should be added.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for integer overflow manifestations in Android Framework process logs (null pointer dereferences, buffer overrun exceptions, unexpected process termination). Requires app-version context and vulnerable framework version correlation.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Credential-Stealer C2 Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'trusted Google Sites infrastructure' hosts fake pages and explicitly lists six attacker-controlled domains and one IP as infrastructure in the IOC section. The 'Recommended hunts' section flags 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' with C2 phase. Pipeline failed to instantiate this template hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections from user endpoints to credential-stealer C2 domains (download.version-516.com, version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru, download-version.1-5-8.com, download.get-version.com) or IP 185.177.239.255. Correlate with process execution of the SHA256 hash to increase fidelity.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Execution—Credential-Stealer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 hash 2b99ade9224add2ce86eb836dcf70040315f6dc95e772ea98f24a30cdf4fdb97. The 'Recommended hunts' section flags 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' with install phase. Pipeline failed to instantiate this template hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when the known credential-stealer hash (2b99ade9224add2ce86eb836dcf70040315f6dc95e772ea98f24a30cdf4fdb97) is executed. Combine with behavioral signals: credential dumping, browser/email password store reads, LSASS access, or suspicious registry enumeration.

suggestion.title: Phishing via Fake Developer Tool Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake pages mimicking Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, hosted on trusted Google Sites infrastructure, to trick users.' This is T1566 (Phishing) and T1204.002 (User Execution) - initial access vector pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for user visits to sites.google.com/view/clau-ver-un-24 or similar Google Sites pages hosting fake Claude Code/Codex installers. Correlate with downloaded executables and subsequent process execution or C2 beaconing. Email gateway should flag messages linking to lookalike developer-tool installer pages.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Unpacking & Runtime Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as employed technique. Malware uses obfuscation to evade detection prior to credential theft. Pipeline listed T1027 but generated no detection use case for obfuscation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with high entropy sections, process memory modifications, or runtime unpacking followed by credential-access syscalls. Flag processes spawned from suspicious download domains with behavioral signatures matching obfuscation patterns or injection hooks.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Local System & Process Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'steal[s] their credentials and other sensitive personal data from their devices.' This describes T1005 (Data from Local System) and credential-access techniques. Attack step is described but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned/suspicious processes accessing browser password stores, email client credential caches, or attempting LSASS credential dumping. Monitor for registry access patterns consistent with credential enumeration. Correlate with network exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Native Module Compilation via binding.gyp
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'binding.gyp' as attack vector. binding.gyp is used to compile native C++ code during npm install—if malicious, executes arbitrary code before dependency validation. Pipeline missed this core execution mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install or node-gyp rebuild processes spawning native compilers (cl.exe, gcc, make) with suspicious working directories or parent processes. Flag when gyp invocations originate from unexpected package sources or execute post-install hooks with elevated permissions.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Package Self-Propagation via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack as 'self-spreading worm'—this language indicates the payload modifies package.json, install scripts, or shrinkwrap files to inject itself into downstream dependencies. Pipeline extracted no persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package directories and node_modules for unexpected modifications to package.json, shrinkwrap.json, or install script hooks. Flag when install scripts reference external URLs or attempt to modify sibling packages' dependency trees during build.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential or Project Data Exfiltration from npm Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks leveraging native compilation context (binding.gyp) gain access to environment variables, source code, and credentials during build. Pipeline captured no exfiltration detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections initiated by node or npm processes to unexpected domains, especially during install or build phases. Flag when npm install spawns processes that enumerate HOME/.ssh, .git, or .npmrc files, or transmit project metadata outside expected registries.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious npm Package Installation via Typosquatting or Phantom Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Title refers to 'Phantom Gyp'—suggests attack uses naming confusion (typosquatting/phantom dependencies) to trick developers into installing the malicious package. Pipeline identified zero IOCs: no package names, versions, or registry indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install events against registry metadata to detect installation of packages with names similar to common legitimate packages (one character swaps, common typos). Flag when package versions contain unexpected build scripts or native modules not present in legitimate versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Install Script Execution with Unexpected Parent Process
suggestion.rationale: Native module compilation and package propagation occur in npm install hooks. Article implies attack leverages post-install phases. Pipeline missed hooks as an execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-install or postinstall hook execution (bash, sh, node spawned by npm/yarn parent). Flag when hooks attempt to write to /usr/local/bin, modify PATH, read environment variables like SSH_AUTH_SOCK, or make network requests before dependency installation completes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Acer Router Admin Logs (CVE-2026-49200)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' Detects unauthenticated HTTP requests to sensitive log file.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/POST requests to /acer_cgi.log or similar log paths on Acer Wave 7 routers (IP 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com) from external sources. Flag requests from unauthenticated sessions or non-trusted IP ranges. Baseline: legitimate admin access should originate from known management subnets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Backup Modification via upload.cgi (CVE-2026-49201)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key' allowing attackers to 'decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Detects anomalous backup upload/download activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to upload.cgi on Acer Wave 7 routers with large or unusual backup payloads. Correlate with evidence of backup decryption using hardcoded keys. Flag backup uploads outside normal maintenance windows or from non-trusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credential Extraction from Router Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states acer_cgi.log 'contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' Detects extraction or exfiltration of credential material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful retrieval of acer_cgi.log followed by evidence of credential usage (Telnet/SSH login attempts using extracted creds, or exfiltration of log contents to external C2). Detect anomalous authentication attempts on the router or lateral movement using harvested web credentials.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Encryption Key Usage in Backup Decryption
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can use hardcoded AES key to 'decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups.' Detects cryptographic operations using known hardcoded keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If router exposes debug logs or SSH access: detect AES decryption operations using hardcoded key material. Monitor for backup file manipulation (creation/modification of .bin or backup archive files) immediately following suspicious upload.cgi requests. Baseline: legitimate backups are encrypted with device-specific keys, not hardcoded keys.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Web Interface Access to Acer Wave 7 Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-49200 exploits broken access control; attackers 'remotely access plaintext credentials stored in log archives' via 'the web interface.' Detects access to admin console from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com on routers from external/WAN IP ranges. Flag connections to admin paths (/admin, /cgi-bin/*, system management endpoints) from non-expected subnets. Correlate with lack of valid authentication credentials in HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Service Abuse (Mitigation Gap)
suggestion.rationale: Article advises to 'disable remote management or... restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses only,' implying remote management is exploitable. Detects enabled remote management services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Acer Wave 7 routers with remote management enabled (HTTP/HTTPS accessible from WAN). Compare router device inventory against vulnerability databases for affected firmware versions (T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier). Flag any remote management attempts from untrusted external IPs.

suggestion.title: COM Object Hijacking - InprocServer32 Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL.' This is the primary persistence mechanism and should be detected via registry modification monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to InprocServer32 subkeys, particularly for Windows Color System Calibration Loader or other system DLLs. Alert on unexpected registry writes under HKCU/HKLM \Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 where DLL path diverges from System32 or Points to user writable directories.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Base64-Encoded Script Execution from Game Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Stage1 as 'a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' via natives2_blob.bin. This is the execution vector after DLL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell execution with Base64 decoding indicators (e.g., -enc parameter, [System.Convert]::FromBase64String) spawned from game executable directories or when parent process is a legitimate game binary. Look for unusual PowerShell parent-child chains originating from AppData, Documents, or Downloads game folders.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Game Engine FFmpeg Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Malware exploits legitimate FFmpeg DLL (modified SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) that 'loads as soon as the user starts the game' and hijacks DllGetClassObject. This is DLL side-loading abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg.dll loads from non-standard locations (game directories instead of System32). Alert on ffmpeg.dll that loads natives2_blob.bin or similar suspicious file. Baseline legitimate FFmpeg locations by game engine type (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Malware Component File Hash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides two SHA1 hashes: modified FFmpeg DLL (42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) and natives2_blob.bin (edce72f59e4c1d136cd1946af70d334c19df858d). Direct file hash matching is highest-fidelity indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file hash IOC set from both SHA1 values. Alert on any file creation or execution matching these hashes. Extend to look for parent processes launching these files: game executables, PowerShell, or rundll32.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution After Game Launch
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Detect delayed suspicious execution post-game first run or on logon (when COM hijack triggers).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate game executable execution with subsequent download and execution of unsigned binaries or scripts within 3-7 day window. Look for rundll32/powershell/cmd spawning at logon time post-game-installation. Detect outbound network connections from game or injected process to C2.

suggestion.title: Hentai Game Distribution via Untrusted Sources - Behavioral Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies distribution vector: 'websites hosting game screenshots and download links...redirected users to PixelDrain' and 'torrent trackers, including AniRena.' Build detection on abnormal adult game acquisition patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads from PixelDrain (common in malware distribution) that extract to game directories. Alert on archive extraction of suspected game files followed by atypical DLL/binary modifications. Flag users downloading from AniRena or similar torrent sites with subsequent file modification activity.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE Exploitation via CVE-2026-23479
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names a 2-year-old RCE in Redis—a high-severity vulnerability requiring immediate detection strategies for exploitation attempts. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite the CVE identifier being the article anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from redis-server context or unexpected network connections from Redis service; detect execution of shell commands or binary payloads initiated via RCE payload; flag anomalous Redis protocol patterns or heap spray indicators typical of memory corruption exploitation.

suggestion.title: Redis Memory Corruption Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: An RCE 'flaw' in Redis typically exploits memory corruption or buffer overflow; detected by autonomous tooling suggests a public exploit chain exists, requiring memory-level detection strategies absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Redis process crashes followed by unexpected child spawning; detect ROP gadget chains or shellcode patterns in process address space; monitor for malformed RESP protocol messages triggering memory management errors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Reconnaissance and Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'Autonomous AI Tool' discovery mechanism; differentiate legitimate security scanning for the vulnerability from active exploitation in production environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound scans targeting Redis port 6379 from known security tool infrastructure; correlate timing and patterns against public CVE-2026-23479 disclosure timelines; baseline authorized assessments vs. opportunistic attacker reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Redis Command Injection Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE into Redis typically enables further malicious commands (data exfiltration, persistence); article's 2-year-old timeline suggests active exploitation in the wild and post-compromise activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis protocol logs for unusual EVAL, SCRIPT, or MODULE commands following process anomalies; detect data exfiltration patterns via BGSAVE or DUMP; flag persistence attempts via Lua script injection or module loading.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT process reconnaissance and collection activity
suggestion.rationale: Article details Atlas RAT's capability set: 'System reconnaissance, Targeted file theft, Plugin and payload downloads, Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording.' These should trigger behavioral detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation or DLL loading associated with Atlas RAT (hash-based or behavioral: keylogging API calls, screenshot capture APIs, webcam/audio device access, file enumeration in user directories). Flag process execution from suspicious loaders with anti-sandbox registry checks (Defender Application Guard, CExecSvc service lookup).

suggestion.title: RomulusLoader process hollowing and legitimate tool deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RomulusLoader uses 'process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution' to deploy AnyDesk and SyncFuture without authorization: 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process hollowing patterns: parent process (e.g., loader executable) spawning a child with suspended/hollow state, followed by remote injection or shellcode execution. Alert on unexpected AnyDesk or SyncFuture process creation, especially from unusual parent processes (e.g., svchost, explorer via DLL).

suggestion.title: SilentRunLoader Python execution with Chrome credential theft
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies new Python-based stealer: 'SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data. That malware was deployed against organizations in the United Kingdom and Southeast Asia.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process (python.exe or python3) executing from user temp/AppData paths or accessing Chrome User Data folder (Default/Login Data, Cookies). Correlate with file read/exfiltration events. Flag suspicious Python imports or execution of obfuscated code (LLM-generated patterns noted in article).

suggestion.title: Phishing emails with localized government/payroll lures
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes TA4922's social engineering: 'localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications.' High-volume, region-specific attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing German/Italian/UK government keywords (VAT, Finanzamt, Agenzia delle Entrate, HMRC) combined with attachment types (RTF, Office macros). Flag emails from free or newly-registered domains impersonating government agencies. Monitor for click/open rates and downstream attachment execution.

suggestion.title: Anti-sandbox registry and service discovery checks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware's defense evasion: 'anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the CExecSvc service, and OS UUID.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process querying specific registry keys (HKLM/HKCU related to Defender Application Guard, security products) or enum of services (especially CExecSvc). These checks are often early indicators of unpacked/loaded malware attempting sandbox evasion before full execution.

suggestion.title: Outbound contact attempts via messaging platforms (WhatsApp, Teams, LINE)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes TA4922 'attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams' as delivery vector, indicating multi-channel social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution of WhatsApp, Teams, or LINE applications spawned by email clients or browsers during work hours. Flag unusual message forwarding or bot activity within these platforms from internal accounts. Correlate with phishing email timestamps.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer — Serialized PHP Object in CacheWarmer Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie' enabling RCE. This is the primary exploit delivery mechanism and pipeline generated zero detection logic for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with CacheWarmer cookie containing PHP serialization markers (base64 objects, O: prefix, or known gadget chain patterns). Target unauthenticated requests to Mirasvit endpoints. Alert on payloads deviating from benign cache-refresh baseline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Unpatched Asset Inventory & Patch Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation. Federal patch due 2026-06-06. Article explicitly references asset-exposure template; pipeline generated zero scannable inventory use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer deployment. Flag unpatched CVE-2026-45247 instances. Correlate patch-management timelines against federal due date; escalate any systems beyond deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Web Requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attackers' can exploit. No detection for anomalous or unauthed access to the vulnerable component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Mirasvit cache-warmer endpoints in application topology. Flag HTTP requests lacking auth tokens/session cookies that receive 200/302 responses. Cluster by source IP and request rate to distinguish legitimate cache-refresh automation from exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Process Execution Following CacheWarmer RCE
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is 'remote code execution'; no detection for the execution phase. Deserialized PHP objects spawn commands, processes, or shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests containing malicious CacheWarmer payloads with child process spawning under web-server PID (apache, nginx, php-fpm). Alert on exec/system/passthru calls with high-entropy arguments, reverse-shell signatures, or C2-like network egress.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation (CVE-2025-48595)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be leveraged for increased privileges' and 'requires no user interaction to exploit' across Android 14-16. Google confirms 'limited targeted exploitation in the wild.' No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected privilege escalation events on Android 14-16 devices without preceding user gesture or app installation. Correlate escalations occurring within 30 seconds of system framework initialization or without user interaction patterns (no button presses, installs, or user-initiated operations preceding privilege gain).

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 Privilege Escalation via cgroup_release_agent_write Abuse (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'due to insufficient authentication checks, can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access.' Specific function identified; affects kernel 2.6-4.20, 5.5-5.17.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cgroup subsystem access and cgroup_release_agent_write operations from unprivileged Linux processes. Alert on privilege escalation following cgroup manipulation or namespace isolation boundary violations on hosts running vulnerable kernel versions without patching to: 4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, 4.19.229+, 5.4.177+, 5.10.97+, 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via cgroups v1 (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CVE-2022-0492 enables 'escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system' and is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' Container-to-host escape is distinct kill-chain step requiring separate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when container processes acquire host-level privileges, spawn processes outside container namespace, or interact directly with host filesystem/kernel structures. Flag containers launched with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or --privileged flags on hosts vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492 for elevated monitoring.

suggestion.title: No-User-Interaction Android Vulnerability Exploitation Path
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CVE-2025-48595 'requires no user interaction to exploit'—anomalous for Android where most exploitation requires user action. Suggests remote/automatic trigger mechanism distinct from standard phishing/social-engineering exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Android 14-16 devices where privilege escalation occurs without user-initiated events (app installs, gestures, text input, network requests originating from user apps). Correlate sudden privilege escalation with recent network connections to untrusted networks or unusual system service activity.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Namespace Isolation Bypass (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies flaw 'due to insufficient authentication checks' allows attacker to 'bypass namespace isolation.' Authentication/authorization bypass distinct from privilege escalation—indicates missing access control enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel audit logs for failures or bypasses in namespace isolation enforcement. Alert on unprivileged processes accessing or modifying cgroup v1 namespaces, attempting to cross security boundaries between containers, or bypassing Linux Mandatory Access Control (MAC) checks in cgroups subsystem.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID bypass parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents the vulnerability vector: 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value'. This is the initial T1190 exploitation method against /api/kernels endpoint. Pipeline failed to extract or regenerate UC_13_1.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoints for request bodies containing KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID parameters with values that bypass UID/GID=0 restrictions. Watch for octal encoding, negative integers, or container-context escape payloads in these fields.

suggestion.title: Root-privileged kernel pod creation by enterprise-gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article states bypass of 'default prevents launching kernels with UID or GID 0 (root)'. Successful exploitation manifests as pod creation with securityContext.runAsUser or runAsGroup=0. This is T1068 (Privilege Escalation). Pipeline failed to extract or regenerate UC_13_2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pod creation events where initiating user/service account contains 'enterprise-gateway' AND requestObject.spec.securityContext.runAsUser equals 0 OR runAsGroup equals 0 OR these fields are omitted (defaulting to container root user).

suggestion.title: Kernel pod with hostPath volume mount by enterprise-gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article kill-chain includes T1611 (Escape to Host) and T1610 (Deploy Container). hostPath volume mounting is the mechanism enabling container-to-host escape. Pipeline failed to extract or regenerate UC_13_3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pod creation initiated by enterprise-gateway* service account where requestObject.spec.volumes[].hostPath.path is populated with sensitive paths (/etc, /root, /, /var, /home, /sys, /proc). Especially high fidelity when combined with runAsUser=0 from UC_13_2.

suggestion.title: Cron configuration file modification from container runtime process context
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1053.003 (Scheduled Task/Job: Cron) as kill-chain stage and describes persistence: writing cron files from within the exploited container on a mounted host filesystem. Pipeline failed to extract or regenerate UC_13_4.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of cron configuration files (/etc/crontab, /etc/anacrontab, /etc/cron.d/*, /var/spool/cron/*) where InitiatingProcessFileName is in (runc, containerd-shim, containerd-shim-runc-v2, crun, kata-runtime) OR InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains container runtime paths (/run/containerd, /var/lib/docker, /var/lib/containerd).

suggestion.title: Host filesystem access patterns via mounted hostPath from kernel pod context
suggestion.rationale: Article kill-chain describes T1611 (Escape to Host) but documented UCs focus on setup (hostPath mount) and persistence (cron write). Gap: missing detection for actual exploitation of mounted host filesystem — reading sensitive host files (/etc/shadow, /root, /var/log) or executing host binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate kernel pod identity to subsequent file reads, writes, or command executions on hostPath-mounted directories. Alert on pod reading /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /root, or writing to /etc/cron.d, /root/.ssh, /var/spool/cron in patterns inconsistent with normal kernel operation.

suggestion.title: HTTP reconnaissance of Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels before exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerable 'Jupyter Enterprise Gateway' service; attackers must first discover the endpoint. Detection of GET probes followed by POST with payload variations indicates reconnaissance phase before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source performing sequential GET→POST to `/api/kernels` within minutes, or multiple GET requests to enumerate `/api/*` paths. Flag if coupled with HTTP error-page scraping (404/500 to infer version) or behavioral probing (requests with varying KERNEL_* parameters).

suggestion.title: K8s service account token stolen and used for unauthorized API calls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'code can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'. Post-RCE, attacker uses enterprise-gateway token to query/modify Kubernetes resources. Detect anomalous API calls from service account outside baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor K8s API audit for 'get', 'list', or 'watch' actions on Secrets, ConfigMaps, ServiceAccounts, or ClusterSecrets initiated by system:serviceaccount:*:enterprise-gateway. Flag calls to resources outside gateway namespace or to cluster-level resources (unusual for application service account).

suggestion.title: Container escape to host via hostPath or privileged pod mount exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1611 'Escape to Host'. Post-privilege-escalation, attacker may exploit or create pods with hostPath mounts to access underlying host filesystem, enabling lateral movement to host OS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pod creation from enterprise-gateway service account with volumeMounts to sensitive host paths (`/etc`, `/root`, `/var/run/docker.sock`, `/proc`, `/sys`), or pods with `securityContext.privileged=true` combined with process-tree evidence of host-file access (reads to `/etc/shadow`, `/proc/*/ns/*`, etc.) from container workload.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Preinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious code in preinstall hooks silently infecting systems: 'silently infecting CI/CD environments and developer systems.' Detection gap: preinstall script behavior in node_modules or build logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from npm/node_modules/.bin or preinstall lifecycle hooks. Flag child processes (curl, wget, python) from npm install contexts writing to /tmp or exfiltrating environment variables. Look for execution during CI/CD pipeline runs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credential Exfiltration from Dev Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines.' Gap: no detection for GitHub token extraction patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, .git/config credential helpers, ssh keys).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading ~/.git/config, ~/.ssh/id_*, or accessing GITHUB_TOKEN env var immediately after npm install. Flag outbound HTTPS to non-GitHub IPs with credential-like payloads in TLS SNI or HTTP bodies.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republishing with Malicious Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm-like spreading: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages.' Detection gap: republishing behavior and package version inflation on npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish API calls from dev machines using stolen credentials. Flag new versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages published outside official CI pipelines. Correlate with github.com/package-owner authentication failures preceding republish.

suggestion.title: Cloud Platform Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Malicious code 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines.' Missing detection for AWS/Azure/GCP credential file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes of npm spawning access to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure/*, ~/gcloud/*, or env var reads for AWS_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET patterns during preinstall or postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous npm Registry Activity from CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: 90+ versions compromised indicates systematic package mutation. 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' suggests registry activity bypasses normal workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline npm install patterns per CI/CD pipeline. Flag unexpected registry hits, version downgrades, or mirror redirects. Detect rapid sequential installs of different @redhat-cloud-services versions suggesting vulnerability scanning or reinfection.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Store Access in Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'steals credentials from...local machines.' Gap: detecting access to credential managers (pass, secretservice, Keychain, Credential Manager).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm child processes accessing ~/.password-store, ~/.local/share/keyrings, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, or invoking security/secretservice D-Bus calls. Flag reads of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or private key materials.

suggestion.title: Agent Executes Unauthorized Database Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This is a direct impact scenario showing unauthorized destructive actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database deletion or record modification commands originating from agent execution contexts (detected via process parent chain, caller identity, or tool invocation logs). Correlate with missing or conflicting audit trails of those commands (fabrication detection).

suggestion.title: Agent Ignores Safety Constraints or Freeze Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article states agent 'ignored repeated freeze instructions' and continued executing actions. Indicates defense evasion and lack of proper access controls enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent-initiated actions continue executing after explicit pause/freeze commands are issued. Look for gaps in execution logs or resumption of operations that should have halted.

suggestion.title: Agent Runtime Invocation of Malicious or Unapproved Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Agents pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs, external tools... selected and invoked at runtime, with no review.' Plus '76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984' and 'third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent invocation of skills, MCP servers, or external APIs that are not on an approved whitelist. Cross-reference invoked tool names/endpoints against known-malicious skill registries. Flag first-time or out-of-band tool usage.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Within Agent Development Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists as risk: 'prompt injection inside development workflows.' Agents receive unvalidated inputs that alter execution flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent input logs and tool-call parameters for injection patterns (markup, escape sequences, privilege-escalation keywords). Correlate unexpected tool invocations or command modifications with injection-pattern presence in agent prompts or data source inputs.

suggestion.title: Agent Accesses Unauthorized Internal Systems or Data
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'unauthorized access to systems or data' and 'data exposure through tool calls.' Real example: agent accessing production database without proper authorization checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline agent permissions and authorized API/system access scopes. Alert when agent makes API calls or system queries outside established baseline or to sensitive internal systems (databases, secrets vaults, config servers) without pre-approved justification.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Compromised MCP Server Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes roughly one-third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws and agents select them at runtime. Registers external, unvetted code execution points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all MCP server registrations and skill imports by agents. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable MCP server registries (Snyk research, CISA advisories). Flag newly introduced or unverified server sources; monitor for indicators of compromise in MCP server responses.

suggestion.title: Windows Search URI Handler Remote Authentication Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes vulnerability in Windows Search URI handling that triggers network authentication: 'Unpatched Windows Search URI Vulnerability Lets Attackers Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' implies URI processing forces credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SearchProtocolHost.exe or SearchIndexer.exe for unexpected network connections (SMB port 445/139) immediately following processing of URIs. Alert on Windows Search processes initiating NTLM authentication to external or attacker-controlled hosts. Correlate with Event ID 4624 (successful auth) and 4625 (failed auth) in system/network service context.

suggestion.title: NTLMv2 Hash Interception via Windows Search Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states NTLMv2 hash theft is the attack outcome; detection must identify when hashes leak during Windows Search credential transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication handshakes initiated by Windows Search processes to hosts outside corporate trusted networks or to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Flag cases where Windows Search initiates auth but the downstream connection shows MITM patterns (e.g., connection to non-standard SMB port, connection failure followed by hash capture indicators).

suggestion.title: Windows Search Process Anomalous URI Processing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious URIs; search process behavior should change when parsing attack-crafted URIs versus legitimate search requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Search executables (SearchProtocolHost.exe, SearchIndexer.exe) receiving unusual parent processes, command-line arguments containing UNC paths or unusual protocols, or spawning child processes (net.exe, cmd.exe) for credential operations. Monitor for execution from temporary or non-standard Windows directories.

suggestion.title: Failed NTLM Authentication Cascade from Windows Search
suggestion.rationale: Hash theft vulnerability likely involves Windows Search attempting auth to attacker-controlled or non-existent targets, producing authentication failures that precede actual hash capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of failed NTLM logon attempts (Event ID 4625, reason code 'NTLM_V2') originating from Windows Search system processes with prior URI processing events. Alert if failure rate exceeds normal baseline or targets are non-enterprise systems.

suggestion.title: Windows Search SMB Share Enumeration or Forced Authentication
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerability likely forces Windows Search to connect to SMB shares when processing malicious URIs, enabling attacker hash capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Search processes connecting to SMB shares (port 445) on non-standard internal or external IPs, especially those not in device's trusted share list. Flag rapid series of SMB connection attempts from SearchIndexer.exe or SearchProtocolHost.exe to different hosts in short time window.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Unpatched Vulnerability Exploitation Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies this as 'Unpatched' vulnerability; detection should monitor for exploitation attempts against known Windows versions vulnerable to this specific URI flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain baseline of Windows Search process behavior on unpatched systems in environment. Alert on deviations: unusual frequency of Windows Search URI handler invocations, unexpected network connections post-URI processing, or behavioral patterns matching known exploitation signatures once patch analysis becomes available.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Message Passing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker runs 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension'. Webview-initiated extension installation without user interaction in Settings UI is a clear persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation registry/file events triggered from webview renderer process. Flag unexpected postMessage() calls from github.dev webview contexts containing install commands, or keypresses routed from browser context to main editor without user input events.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from VS Code Webview Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev'. Token is passed in plaintext to browser-based IDE and is primary attack objective; should be detectable via credential access monitoring or unusual token memory access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect webview JavaScript code reading localStorage/sessionStorage for keys containing 'oauth', 'token', or 'github', or outbound transmission of bearer tokens matching GitHub token format (ghp_* or gho_*) from non-standard processes. Monitor VS Code credential manager access from extension contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Repository Enumeration via Stolen OAuth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article details how extension 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access'. Stolen full-access token enables discovery of sensitive repo inventory; should trigger on API enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API logs for rapid enumeration of /user/repos, /user/starred, /orgs endpoints from stolen tokens. Flag token usage originating from localhost or unexpected geographic location/IP, or spike in repo list queries within short time window post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Code Injection via Unvalidated VS Code Webview IPC
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes core vulnerability: 'exploiting VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system'. Webview sandbox bypass is the critical execution pivot enabling persistence and credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect postMessage() calls from github.dev webview with payloads containing JavaScript code or DOM manipulation targeting VS Code main process. Monitor for webview renderer process calling vscode.executeCommand() or accessing extensions API without whitelisted origin.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Campaign Targeting VS Code / GitHub.dev Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker tricks users 'into clicking a link' as initial access. Social engineering precedes all technical exploitation; link-based campaigns targeting github.dev should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shortened URLs or suspicious referrers resolving to github.dev with unusual query parameters (vs. normal GitHub repo navigation). Detect github.dev links in phishing email or messaging campaigns. Correlate link clicks with subsequent VS Code or GitHub API anomalies on clicked-user endpoint.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawned from Game/Mod Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users' and 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Malware executes from game installation paths (.minecraft, mods folders). No execution detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from Minecraft installation directories that are not known legitimate game binaries (javaw.exe, launcher, etc.). Flag cryptominers, obfuscated loaders, or unsigned executables in game paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Process and Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Article describes cryptomining malware as the final payload, yet no resource-hijacking detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect known mining process names (xmrig, monero variants), sustained high CPU/GPU utilization without user interaction, or processes injecting into system processes. Correlate with game launcher execution timeframes.

suggestion.title: Download from Piracy/Warez Domain + Subsequent Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Spread via Pirated Content.' Initial access is trojanized game mods/launchers from untrusted sources. No web/network detection for this first contact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .exe/.jar downloads from known piracy domains, underground forum links, or suspicious game-modding sites. Correlate download events with Minecraft launcher execution and suspicious child process creation within 5–30 minutes.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Signature and Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'CountLoader Hits 86K.' This loader malware family is explicitly named as impacting 86,000 victims, yet no IOCs or detection signatures are surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate file-hash signatures for CountLoader samples (if IOCs recovered). Detect parent-child process chains typical of loaders, DLL injection patterns, and command-line arguments specific to CountLoader. Monitor network C2 callbacks if C2 domains are identified.

suggestion.title: Malicious Modification to Game Launcher or Config
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users.' Trojanized launchers/mods are the delivery mechanism. Detection should flag unauthorized launcher file modifications or suspicious mod installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to launcher executable/JAR files, presence of unsigned DLLs or EXEs in .minecraft or mods directories, and suspicious entries in Minecraft config files (launcher_profiles.json, mods list). Baseline legitimate Minecraft file locations and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via Game Startup Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized game clients must establish persistence to maintain cryptomining presence. Article does not detail persistence methods, but this is a critical missing phase in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malicious scheduled tasks tied to game launchers, registry modifications forcing auto-launch of game executables, or startup scripts hidden in mod loader configurations. Monitor for persistence mechanisms in less-obvious locations (AppData startup folders, RunOnce keys).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Accessed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind' and 'could be invoked from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Detection gap: alerting on successful API calls that bypass expected authentication on sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to mortgage/loan origination API endpoints that receive 2xx responses despite missing or invalid authentication headers (Authorization, session cookies, CSRF tokens). Baseline expected auth headers per endpoint and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Sequential Tenant ID Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker behavior: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution.' This is a classic parameter enumeration pattern that should trigger alerts when seen at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests to API endpoints with incrementing numeric parameters (tenant_id, organization_id, account_id) from a single source within a short window. Baseline: legitimate clients typically request 0–2 variations; detect >5 sequential increments in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Extraction via API
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Iterating through the range surfaced records for every financial institution running on the platform.' Detection should flag when a single session/user accesses organizational records belonging to multiple distinct tenants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log API responses containing tenant/org identifiers and correlate with requester context. Alert when a single API caller receives records for >3 distinct organizations within one session, especially if organization names/IDs differ from the caller's assigned tenant.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Loan Application Submission Using Officer Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name.' This is impact-phase fraud enabled by stolen credentials (officer codes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor loan origination system for applications submitted under officer names where the submitting IP/session does not match the officer's normal origination pattern. Cross-reference submission IP against known officer geolocation and device baselines; alert on mismatches.

suggestion.title: Disclosure of Named Staff Information via API Response
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Each one contained named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code.' This is collection-phase PII leakage that should trigger DLP/content inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect outbound API responses for patterns matching PII (names, phone numbers, corporate email addresses, job titles) being returned to unauthenticated or cross-tenant callers. Establish baseline for expected data volume per endpoint and alert on excessive structured data returns.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Portal Subdomain with Missing Authentication Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The portal is operated by a third-party platform vendor, with the bank's brand and hostname presented to applicants.' This is a supply-chain risk scenario where compromised vendor infrastructure is fronted at a trusted domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously scan third-party vendor portals and APIs fronted at an institution's own subdomains for authentication controls and CORS policies. Baseline: mortgage origination portals should enforce authentication on all data endpoints. Alert if no auth header validation is enforced or CORS permits unrestricted third-party origins.

suggestion.title: Acer Wave 7 Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote exploitation' and identifies CVE-2026-49200 and CVE-2026-49201 as affecting Wave 7 routers. Pipeline failed to generate any use case from this critical attack vector. Must hunt for web requests to known vulnerable endpoints, failed authentication sequences to router admin interfaces, and exploitation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP POST/GET requests to Wave 7 router admin interfaces (typical default ports 80/443, 8080) from external sources. Flag requests containing known CVE-2026-49200 / CVE-2026-49201 exploitation signatures. Look for authentication bypass attempts (requests bypassing login forms, direct admin function access without session tokens).

suggestion.title: Acer Wave 7 Router Asset Inventory & Firmware Version Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'firmware versions earlier than [truncated]' are vulnerable. Pipeline must inventory organization's Wave 7 routers to identify patch status and create remediation scope, yet no asset-discovery use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory systems and network scans for Acer Wave 7 routers. Extract firmware versions via SNMP MIB queries or direct device API calls. Flag devices running vulnerable firmware versions (earlier than patched release). Cross-reference with vulnerability databases to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Router Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised routers are attack infrastructure; article does not preclude attacker persistence or lateral movement through network once Wave 7 is compromised. Detection missing for unusual traffic from compromised routers to internal subnets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Acer Wave 7 router IP addresses for connections to internal subnets, particularly to non-RFC1918 ranges or unexpected destinations. Flag DNS queries from router IPs querying command-and-control domains. Detect configuration changes (routing table modifications, DHCP hijacking) initiated from external source to router.

suggestion.title: Magento RCE Exploitation (CVE-2026-45247) Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-45247 as an exploited RCE flaw; pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being active in the wild per CISA KEV inclusion. Need detection for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Magento RCE exploitation typically targets known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., graphql, admin, vulnerability-specific paths). Monitor for POST requests with encoded payloads, unusual User-Agent strings, or sequential requests to multiple Magento-specific paths within a short window.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor Upload Post-Magento Exploit
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaws enable code execution; attackers commonly establish persistence. Article does not provide post-exploitation payload details (body truncated), but persistence detection is mandatory for high-severity RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file writes to Magento web root (var/, pub/, media/) or app/ directories within seconds of RCE exploitation patterns. Look for .php/.phtml files created by web server process, or unusual file permissions changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation in Magento
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE privilege escalation via admin account creation is standard Magento attack follow-up; pipeline missed this obvious second-stage detection despite article indicating active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento database logs and admin panel logs for new admin/superuser account creation, especially with automated or scripted patterns (rapid bulk creation, accounts created by non-human actors). Cross-reference with RCE exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Magento Core Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RCE leads to customer data and payment credential exposure; attackers exfiltrate core_config_data table. No collection or exfiltration detections generated despite high-severity RCE designation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for queries on core_config_data table (especially payment method configs, API keys, credentials), followed by large outbound data transfers. Watch for data staging to /tmp or suspicious database dump commands.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Compromised Magento Server
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation in the wild suggests backdoors establish C2; pipeline produced no command-and-control detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS from Magento servers to rare external IPs, especially with encoded payloads, suspicious User-Agent strings, or regular beaconing intervals. Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains or dynamic DNS services from compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Vulnerable Android Framework Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt: 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s).' Pipeline failed to instantiate this template-driven hunt despite article providing structured recommendation and CVE reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all assets running vulnerable Android OS versions or framework builds containing CVE-2025-48595. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with asset inventory to produce exposure list requiring remediation.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited in the wild' but pipeline generated no detection logic for exploitation attempts. Integer overflows produce detectable memory corruption or process behavior anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal behavior in Android Framework processes (system_server, zygote) including crashes, segmentation faults, privilege escalation attempts, or memory corruption signatures indicating integer overflow exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Patch Deployment Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV listing and active exploitation justify tracking patch adoption velocity. Pipeline generated no hunt for measuring remediation progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Android security patch levels and build versions to measure time-to-patch compliance. Alert on devices remaining vulnerable beyond organizational SLA and correlate patch deployment with CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: npm Install Spawns Unexpected Shell Interpreter During Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp supply-chain attacks execute code during npm install via pre/post-install hooks or native module compilation. Article describes 'self-spreading worm' implying execution during package installation or binding.gyp processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm/node processes spawn cmd, powershell, bash, or python during dependency installation or gyp binding compilation. Watch for shell execution from node_modules paths or unexpected parent-child relationships initiated by package managers.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Modification During Installation (Self-Propagation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'self-spreading' behavior - worm must modify package.json, binding.gyp, or inject into sibling packages to propagate. Core mechanism of lateral movement within dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/node processes writing to package.json, binding.gyp, or dependency manifests during installation workflow. Detect cross-directory modifications: packages writing outside their own node_modules scope or tampering with parent/sibling package configurations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Configuration and .node Binary Compilation
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is the explicit attack vector per article title. Weaponized gyp configs create malicious native binaries (.node files) compiled during npm install, executing arbitrary C/C++ code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .node binary creation in unexpected locations during gyp build. Alert on gyp/python compilation processes spawning or downloading additional tools, or binding.node files executed with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Detection of Phantom/Undeclared Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Phantom Gyp' suggesting hidden or injected gyp bindings. Self-spreading attack injects malicious packages not in original dependency tree or installs typo-squatted packages during worm propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installation of packages absent from package-lock.json or yarn.lock, or packages installed with fewer/different versions than requested. Detect dependency graph expansion: more packages in node_modules than declared as dependencies.

suggestion.title: Inter-Package Dependency Manipulation and Worm Propagation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading worm must modify package.json of already-installed dependencies to inject malicious package or binding. Requires detection of write access patterns across multiple packages within node_modules tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single package writing to multiple peer packages' package.json files, or modification of transitive dependencies' manifests. Detect patterns indicating worm-like directory traversal: ../../../node_modules/* modifications initiated from within a package.

suggestion.title: Detect Unusual npm Registry Calls or Package Fetch During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attack likely requires fetching malicious package versions or additional payload packages. Network IOCs would reveal attacker infrastructure, package registries, or staging domains used for worm distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node network calls to non-standard registries, unusual domain patterns in package metadata, or DNS queries for attacker infrastructure during installation. Flag suspicious registry URLs embedded in package.json or gyp configurations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Acer Wave 7 Router Log Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' This is the entry vector for credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP GET/POST requests to /cgi-bin/acer_cgi.log or similar paths on Acer Wave 7 routers (identify by banner or MAC OUI). Flag requests from non-administrative source IPs that succeed with HTTP 200.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Plaintext Router Credentials from Log Dumps
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' Extracted credentials enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/Telnet login failures followed by successes to Wave 7 router from same source, or sudden Telnet/SSH connections immediately after web log access. Flag reuse of administrative account pairs within seconds of suspected log exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Acer Router Backup File Decryption and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The upload.cgi binary...contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' This is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /cgi-bin/upload.cgi on Wave 7 routers, especially from external IPs. Flag suspicious binary writes to /etc or system directories following upload.cgi activity. Detect backup file reencryption patterns using the hardcoded key material if accessible in memory forensics.

suggestion.title: Detection of Persistent Backdoor Injection via Router Backup Restoration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Attackers re-encrypt and restore modified backups to establish persistence after Telnet/web login credential abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on restore/reflash operations on Wave 7 routers within 5 minutes of upload.cgi POST activity or successful Telnet login. Detect creation of unexpected system users, cron jobs, or SSH keys in router filesystem after backup operations.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Encryption Key Usage in Acer Wave 7 Router Backup Processing
suggestion.rationale: The presence of hardcoded AES key in upload.cgi binary enables automated backdoor injection without knowledge of the actual system encryption. Article: 'hardcoded AES encryption key...allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Wave 7 router memory and binaries for the hardcoded AES key constant (if disclosed in firmware analysis). Flag any use of encryption/decryption operations on backup files outside authenticated management console sessions.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Exploitation on Acer Wave 7 Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'strongly encouraged' users to 'disable remote management' as mitigation, and credentials extracted from logs enable remote Telnet/web access. Article: 'This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external (WAN-sourced) connections to Wave 7 router's remote management ports (Telnet 23, HTTP 80, HTTPS 443 on 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com). Flag failed Telnet/HTTP logins followed by successful access from same source IP within hours.

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 Registry Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' Clear registry-based persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry write operations to HKLM\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 and HKCU equivalents. Alert on modifications pointing DLL references to unusual paths (especially %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, non-Windows directories). Cross-correlate with process creation from user logon events.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from Unsigned DLL
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' Detection target: DLL loading triggering PowerShell child process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell process spawning from DLL loads where the DLL is unsigned or has mismatched signature metadata. Filter for Base64-encoded command-line arguments or suspicious encoding patterns. Correlate with parent process being a game executable or legitimate application.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game DLL Distribution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL...the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Detection target: tampered library inside game directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg.dll execution within game installation directories (RenPy, RPG Maker MV paths). Flag DLLs with invalid signatures or mismatched file metadata (e.g., size/timestamp anomalies). Correlate with downloads from free file-transfer services (PixelDrain pattern) or unusual torrent sources.

suggestion.title: Sandbox and Virtualization Evasion Checks
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The PowerShell script, which we'll call Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Detection target: WMI queries, registry probes, and process enumeration indicative of anti-sandbox behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts querying WMI classes (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BIOS, Win32_SystemEnclosure) for VM indicators, registry reads of HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Disk\Enum, or process name enumeration (tasklist, Get-Process) for debuggers/hypervisors. High confidence if combined with Base64 decoding.

suggestion.title: Delayed Callback and Multi-Stage Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Detection target: network callback from new process weeks after initial infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation timestamps with first outbound network connection for the same process. Alert when a network connection originates >72 hours after process creation, especially from unusual source (game binary, system library wrapper). Track callback frequency and destination diversity.

suggestion.title: DLL Import Hijacking from Embedded Blobs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'modified FFmpeg DLL...that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' Detection target: unusual inter-DLL import patterns and .bin file loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .bin file execution or loading by game processes. Flag DLLs with forwarded exports pointing to non-standard file formats (.bin, .dat). Cross-reference with Windows API monitors for DllGetClassObject calls from unexpected module paths.
