suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' This is payload delivery and living-off-the-land abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Invoke-WebRequest process execution with file creation in user AppData or Temp directories, especially .ps1 files. Look for parent process cmd.exe or PowerShell. Combine with network IOCs for C2 destination validation.

suggestion.title: curl.exe Outbound Connection to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' curl is a LOTL binary; baseline legitimate usage per environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl.exe making outbound connections to ASNs or IPs matching C2 reputation lists or custom threat intel (e.g., EVILEMPIRE ranges). Timeframe correlation with other suspicious processes on same host increases signal.

suggestion.title: Post-Execution File Cleanup via Remove-Item
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' Anti-forensics execution indicates attacker intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Remove-Item or del commands targeting recently created .ps1 or script files in user-writable directories. Correlate with prior Invoke-WebRequest or Invoke-Expression in process tree. Time window: deletion within minutes of creation.

suggestion.title: Firewall + EDR Multi-Domain Correlation: Connection Event to Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Pivoting to Cisco Secure Endpoint data for the same DeviceIP, we pulled the full process history around the time of the connection.' Demonstrates that firewall alone cannot confirm C2 execution; endpoint context is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For outbound connections to known C2 IPs/ports, correlate with EDR process execution on the same device within ±2 minute window. Look for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl.exe, or other process execution touching the C2 destination. Correlation eliminates firewall-only FPs.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System (TDS) Redirect Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'outbound ConnectionEvents to 144.31.221.82 on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856. This pattern is consistent with a Traffic Direction System (TDS) infection, where a compromised website redirects visitors through a chain of intermediate servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known TDS hosting ranges (reputation-based) with suspicious path patterns (e.g., /capcha*, /redirect*). Correlate with user context (admin? normal?) and baseline per environment. Flag if device is not a web server or proxy.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth Device Authorization Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'tricking users into authorizing fake device login requests.' No UC detects this OAuth/device registration pattern. Missing entirely from kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal device authorization approval patterns in Azure/Okta logs: multiple consecutive device registration attempts from same user in short timeframe, device rejects followed immediately by approval, authorization requests from anomalous geolocation or IP range, or device registered then immediately used for sensitive operations (e.g., accessing high-risk resources).

suggestion.title: Okta Device Registration from Malicious IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states expansion 'to target Okta.' No Okta-specific detection provided despite being top-line threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device registrations in Okta where source IP matches known phishing infrastructure IPs (172.67.156.83, 104.21.32.229) or when device is registered from one geography but immediate login attempt from another. Cross-reference with email phishing indicators.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email to OAuth Credential Exchange
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phishing operation that leads to credential theft and authorization. No UC correlates phishing delivery to subsequent authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery of phishing link (known PhaaS domain or suspicious redirect pattern) to unusual OAuth/device authorization approval within 2-4 hours on recipient's account. Flag if phishing link IP range differs from subsequent successful authentication IP.

suggestion.title: Kali365 PhaaS Infrastructure C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 7 infrastructure domains (securehubcloud.com, worker.dev subdomains, attachedfile.com) used as phishing panel/C2. No UC targets infrastructure specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to Kali365 infrastructure domains. Flag any resolution of panel.securehubcloud.com, api.securehubcloud.com, boss.securehubcloud.com, greatness-marketing.top, or *.workers.dev redirects. Correlate to subsequent authentication anomalies or device registration on affected user account.

suggestion.title: Rapid Credential Validation Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates stolen credentials are used; PhaaS typically tests harvested creds immediately. No detection for pattern of failed logins followed by success or multiple accounts tested from single source IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed sign-in attempts (credential validation) for different user accounts within short window from same source IP, followed by successful authentication. Particularly sensitive if IP geolocates to high-risk region or is known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: MAX Messenger Authentication Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article title and expansion explicitly mention 'target Okta and MAX Messenger.' No MAX-specific detections provided. Threat actors often alter targeting after platform expansion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If MAX Messenger logs are ingested, flag unusual authentication or authorization flows. If not ingested: monitor for cross-platform account access—e.g., M365 token used to authenticate to MAX API, or unusual OAuth scopes requested during MAX login flow.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution in npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on self-spreading worm via npm package with malicious binding.gyp. Title explicitly states worm propagation mechanic—article must describe post-install hook exploitation. Zero use cases generated for detecting anomalous script execution during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by npm or node during package installation (postinstall/preinstall scripts) that execute obfuscated code, spawn curl/wget, or connect to unexpected domains. Baseline legitimate postinstall activity per application; flag deviation.

suggestion.title: Native Module Compilation and .node Binary Loading Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article attacks via 'phantom gyp'—binding.gyp is Node.js native binding config that triggers C/C++ compilation. No detection for suspicious node-gyp invocation, .node binary loading from cache, or unexpected compiler spawning (cc, gcc, cl.exe).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.js process spawning build tools (node-gyp, cc, gcc, cl.exe, cmake) during package install. Detect loading of .node binary files from npm cache with unexpected hash or origin. Monitor for pre-built .node binaries downloaded from non-npm registries.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Unexpected npm Package Installation or Version
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector. Article title references 'Miasma npm supply chain attack'—describes compromised or typosquatted package distribution. Pipeline extracted zero package names, versions, or package registry anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of unexpected npm package versions (unusual semver, pinned to 0.0.x, hash mismatches), packages with names phonetically similar to popular libraries (typosquatting), or packages installing undeclared transitive dependencies. Cross-reference package.json declared deps against installed packages.

suggestion.title: Lateral Propagation via Dependent Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'self-spreading worm' characteristic—implies infection spreads when dependent packages are installed. No use case for detecting recursive or chain-reaction package installations triggered by compromised upstreams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected cascading npm installs triggered by a single package. Flag situations where a package installation spawns dozens of child package-install operations outside normal dependency resolution. Detect modification of node_modules after install completes (post-install persistence).

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook execution accessing credential files
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'executes via preinstall' and 'targets 20 credential files...SSH keys...cryptocurrency wallet files.' Primary execution + collection vector with clear log signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm preinstall script processes accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.vault, ~/.kube, Exodus/*, or .bitcoin/* directories. Flag Rust binaries or unexpected child processes in npm install context. Prioritize accounts with <30 days age or new package publishers.

suggestion.title: Stolen npm credentials republishing packages with trojanized versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm' and 'can publish trojanized versions of packages owned by the victim.' Observable credential-use and version-mutation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm publish operations deviating from account's historical pattern (IP, geolocation, device, time-of-day). Alert on rapid package version increments with preinstall/postinstall hook introduction. Cross-reference with npm Trusted Publishing credential exposure.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions artifact exfiltration with innocuous filenames
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output' and uploads as 'build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.' Avoids C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows creating artifacts named 'lint', 'format', 'cache', 'temp', 'output', 'results' from CI pipelines with environment variable access or credential file read patterns. Monitor artifact downloads by unfamiliar accounts or from Tor/VPN IPs.

suggestion.title: Bulk credential environment variable enumeration by preinstall process
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'targets 86 environment variables' including 'OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials.' Bulk enumeration of credential-bearing variables is abnormal for legitimate package installation hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect preinstall script spawning 'env' command or child processes enumerating AWS_*, OPENAI_*, ANTHROPIC_*, NPM_*, GH_*, KUBE_* variables in sequence. Prioritize Rust binaries and processes with file I/O to credential paths within same execution window.

suggestion.title: Git commit timestamp spoofing (backdated commits, recent pushes)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'commit author appears as claude, timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Clear temporal evasion tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits where author_date is >2 years older than push_date or commit_date, especially from new/recently-created accounts or accounts publishing to npm simultaneously. Flag author names matching threat actor indicators or placeholder names ('claude').

suggestion.title: Supply-chain worm propagation via package republication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'conceptually similar to Shai Hulud' and 'can publish trojanized versions of packages owned by the victim, which then infect additional developers and CI systems.' Describes self-spreading package ecosystem attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm packages for rapid version increments (multiple updates within hours/days) with dependency additions or preinstall hook introduction from same account. Flag when >3 related packages update simultaneously. Cross-reference with account compromise indicators and credential theft signals.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious binding.gyp Command Expansion Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)  form runs a shell command during the configure phase... The compromised packages abuse this directly.' Exact 157-byte PoC shown in @vapi-ai/server-sdk@1.2.2 and autotel@3.4.3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor binding.gyp files for <!(...)  command expansion syntax during node-gyp rebuild operations. Alert on node-gyp execution without corresponding preinstall/postinstall hooks in package.json. Flag packages where binding.gyp differs significantly between consecutive published versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous npm Package Version Jumps and Rapid Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Many of the inflated version numbers (for example, autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range, or autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4) are themselves a side effect of the worm's automated republishing.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect major version jumps inconsistent with release patterns, multiple package versions published by same account within 60 seconds, or version sequences that skip stable release sequences. Cross-reference against git tags and changelog entries to identify orphaned registry versions.

suggestion.title: Detect GitHub Actions Workflow Injection Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence.' Malware executes during npm install, then modifies .github/workflows/ in target repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .github/workflows/*.yml files created or modified by commits immediately following npm package installations in CI/CD. Alert on workflows that call external HTTP endpoints, create new secrets, or execute from unusual service accounts. Correlate git commits with package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Detect Multi-Provider Credential Harvesting During Build Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The payload harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes.' Occurs during node-gyp rebuild phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned during npm install that access credential files: ~/.npm/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.config/gcloud/*, KUBECONFIG environment variables, or HashiCorp Vault APIs. Flag file reads of known secret stores in build contexts. Alert on cat/grep commands targeting credential patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration to GitHub via Repository Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' Stolen credentials pushed to GitHub post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git push operations to new or non-standard GitHub repositories immediately after npm package installation. Monitor for Base64-encoded or obfuscated credential blobs in commit messages. Alert on GitHub API calls creating repositories from CI/CD environments. Flag unusual pushes to newly-created repos by compromised developer accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Worm Propagation via Unauthorized npm publish Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach.' Single account 'jagreehal' published 25+ autotel-* packages with malicious versions; 'many of the 57 packages cluster around a single npm account.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm publish commands from automated/CI contexts without human approval workflows. Alert when single maintainer accounts publish to multiple unrelated package scopes within hours. Flag npm publish from containers or CI runners. Monitor for reuse of compromised credentials to publish to packages outside original scope.

suggestion.title: Network Beaconing to TA4922 C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists five C2 IPs and three domains ('206.238.115.58', 'aeya388.club', etc.). Deployment narrative 'against organizations in Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, and Southeast Asia' establishes geographic scope. RATs ('Atlas RAT', 'ValleyRAT') require persistent callback channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to the eight listed IPs and domains. RATs beacon at regular intervals; flag non-standard ports, repeated connections from unexpected processes, and encrypted tunnels consistent with C2 callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 13 SHA256 hashes of Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, ValleyRAT samples. Phrase 'deploying...malware...against organizations' establishes execution as a direct kill-chain step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match all 13 provided SHA256 hashes against endpoint file creation and process execution logs. Flag matches with HIGH priority and inspect parent process chains for loader-to-RAT staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Loader Stage-and-Execute Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'RomulusLoader' and 'SilentRunLoader'—loaders by definition transfer and execute secondary payloads. This is the T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loader process execution spawning unexpected child processes, performing network I/O, or injecting code. Look for unsigned binaries executing from temp directories, process hollowing indicators, and memory-only payload execution.

suggestion.title: RAT Persistent Command-Control Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Atlas RAT' and 'ValleyRAT' families. Phrase 'financially motivated...campaigns' indicates data theft motive, requiring persistent C2. RATs establish long-lived callback channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for periodic beaconing patterns: outbound traffic at regular intervals (5–60 sec), connections from unexpected processes, non-standard ports, and encrypted channels. Correlate with registry/startup persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as observed technique. 'RomulusLoader' and 'SilentRunLoader' names imply code obfuscation for evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on runtime deobfuscation: Base64-encoded command execution, script decoding (PowerShell -EncodedCommand), VBScript eval, or dynamic code generation. ASR rules should block script obfuscation patterns.

suggestion.title: MCP Server Registry Substitution or Untrusted Source Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs, reusable skills, open source components—any of which may be vulnerable, malicious, or misconfigured.' and 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' CVE-2025-6514 instantiates the risk class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent-initiated MCP server instantiation for registry switching, version downgrades, or sourcing from non-approved package registries. Flag instantiation of mcp-remote or other known-vulnerable server versions. Correlate with agent execution logs to establish whether tool selection was policy-approved.

suggestion.title: Agent Execution Exceeding Declared Permission Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments—often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' and 'controls inside the execution loop' are required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each agent, establish per-action permission policies (read-only vs. write, local vs. remote, interactive vs. batch). Alert on command execution or API calls outside declared scope. Flag chained multi-step actions that individually pass whitelist but combine into unauthorized outcome.

suggestion.title: Production Database Modification or Data Fabrication by Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article directly cites Replit failure: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Impact of agent autonomy without governance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor production database operations initiated by agentic service accounts: bulk deletes (>100 rows without matching business process), bulk inserts with anomalous patterns (rapid insert/delete cycles suggesting record covering), or DDL changes. Cross-check against approved agent workflows and human DBA activity logs.

suggestion.title: Agent Continuing Execution After Freeze/Circuit-Breaker Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions.' Agents bypassing control signals represent critical governance failure and potential defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all agent freeze/stop/emergency-stop commands with timestamp and target agent. Alert if target agent spawns new child processes, makes new API calls, or writes files within 30 seconds post-signal. Verify freeze acknowledgment in agent runtime telemetry; orphaned execution post-freeze is critical.

suggestion.title: Embedded Credentials in Agent-Generated Code Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article: agents 'generate code and dependencies faster than human review can validate...may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' and 'validating code at the moment of creation' is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor files written or committed by agent processes for embedded secret patterns (AWS key IDs, Bearer tokens, database connection strings, SSH private keys). Trigger immediate credential rotation. Correlate file-write timestamp with agent execution log to establish code-generation context.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Vulnerable Skill/Plugin Installation from Shared Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Snyk research has already identified malicious agent capabilities in shared ecosystems...critical flaws in widely used agent infrastructure.' Supply-chain compromise at the skill/plugin level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track agent skill or plugin installations against threat intel feeds on compromised shared repositories. Flag unsigned packages, packages from secondary/tertiary registries, or version changes that deviate from agent configuration. Monitor for package substitution or typosquatting attacks on widely-used skills.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Malvertising Delivery Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit IP 144.172.104.205 and domain openew.app as delivery nodes. 'Malvertising campaign...delivering malware' requires network detection to identified infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections to 144.172.104.205 and openew.app from internal hosts. Cross-reference web proxy logs for HTTP/HTTPS requests. High confidence IOC from recent campaign (2026-06-04) with single-source attribution (Evalian SOC).

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Known Hash on Download/Temp Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three SHA256 hashes from malware delivered via fake download site: '56cc26e88c064b0c423aa8ad6530e58f91d1e4d28fab1a8bcedef16a6582b4d2', '7e5b708f6659b1fad3aae7b589a706434fbf21708aeec5af5910189b96e25fef', 'd9ad44d43e57b870793fa5cf7fb3a813990d0cbd0c7087bde70a5e61fb1f1fe6'. Target executable hash match + process creation from Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match on process creation SHA256 hashes or file creation events from %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, %TEMP%, or ~/Downloads directories. Prioritize Windows and macOS process events per article's stated targets. Combine with parent process = browser for higher confidence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download from OpenAI-Impersonating Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'weaponized fake download site' with 'convincing OpenAI branding' hosted at openew.app. Detection must flag domain masquerade + executable download pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP GET requests to openew.app returning .exe/.dmg/.app file with high Content-Length, followed by DeviceFileEvents showing write to Downloads directory. Alert on domains containing 'openai'/'chatgpt' variations except official OpenAI domains (openai.com, *.openai.com).

suggestion.title: Search Engine Ad Poisoning / Malvertising Click Referrer
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'promoted...via sponsored search results.' Detection must identify user clicks originating from search ad traffic (Google Ads / Bing Ads) redirecting to openew.app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP Referer headers from paid search domains (google.com/search?tbm=shop, bing.com/shopping) pointing to openew.app. Alert on anomalous click velocity (> 100 unique source IPs in 1 hour) to same malvertising domain, indicating successful campaign.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Web Interface Access to Device Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' This is the initial foothold and credential harvesting vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Acer Wave 7 router web interface (typically 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com) for GET/POST requests to paths containing 'cgi' or 'log' without valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Flag attempts to access /acer_cgi.log or similar endpoints from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Extraction of Plaintext Credentials from Router Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states acer_cgi.log 'contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' Detection should flag credential harvesting from log files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large or repeated read access to log archive paths on Acer Wave 7 routers, especially when originating from external IPs or followed by exfiltration patterns. Alert on download of log files exceeding normal baseline size.

suggestion.title: Suspicious upload.cgi Binary Access and Backup Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes upload.cgi as 'responsible for processing device backups' and containing a 'hardcoded AES encryption key' that allows decryption, modification, and re-encryption of backups. This is the persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to upload.cgi endpoints with backup files, especially when not preceded by a legitimate backup export. Monitor for repeated encryption/decryption operations targeting backup files on the router. Alert on backup file modifications outside of scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Firmware Version Detection for Wave 7 T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or Earlier
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerabilities affect 'firmware version T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier.' Inventory and version detection are table-stakes for vulnerability-specific alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of Acer Wave 7 routers and their firmware versions. Flag devices running T7c_GBL_1.01.000055 or earlier versions as high-risk. Correlate with any suspicious log access or backup manipulation activity on these specific versions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Access via Stolen Telnet Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states that plaintext credentials stored in acer_cgi.log include 'Telnet' credentials. Once credentials are stolen, attackers will use them for persistent backdoor access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful Telnet connections to Acer Wave 7 routers from unexpected source IPs or geographies. Correlate failed web authentication attempts on the router with successful Telnet logins using the same credentials shortly after. Alert on concurrent Telnet and web interface access from the same external IP.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence via Hardcoded Key-Encrypted Backup Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack as 'persistent backdoor injection' via modified backups encrypted with the hardcoded AES key. This is the persistence mechanism that survives reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious backup restore operations or firmware flashing events preceded by upload.cgi activity. Monitor for modified system binaries or configuration files following backup restore cycles. Alert if backup files show signs of tampering (checksums, timestamps inconsistent with legitimate updates).

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via InprocServer32 Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL.' No use case generated for this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 modifications, particularly targeting Windows Color System Calibration Loader (colorui.dll proxy). Flag suspicious DLL paths, unsigned DLLs, or references to non-system directories.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Stage1 Execution from DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' and mentions 'Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' No detection for this encoding-then-execute pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell processes spawned from unsigned DLLs loaded by legitimate executables (e.g., games). Flag execution of Base64-encoded command blocks, especially containing environment checks for debuggers, WMI, or registry artifacts typical of sandbox detection.

suggestion.title: Modified FFmpeg DLL Proxy Loading natives2_blob.bin
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85), that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' DLL proxy/hijacking load sequence has no dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ffmpeg.dll (from game directories, not system) that loads unusual DLLs (natives2_blob.bin, *.bin files) via DllGetClassObject import. Correlate with game process (RenPy, RPG Maker MV engines). Flag if ffmpeg.dll hash deviates from known legitimate versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Game Download and Installation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'This archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL' distributed via 'websites hosting game screenshots' and 'torrent trackers, including AniRena.' No use case for detecting trojanized game delivery and archive extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for game executable launches (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) followed by unusual DLL loading from the same directory, especially from user-writable temporary or download folders. Flag archive extraction of game files containing .bin files alongside legitimate game assets.

suggestion.title: Stage1 PowerShell Sandbox/Environment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Stage1 'performs basic checks for controlled environments.' No detection for anti-analysis behavior at the PowerShell stage before secondary payload download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts that enumerate WMI Win32_ComputerSystemProduct, registry HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\services\kvm* checks, or VMware/Hyper-V/VirtualBox signatures. Flag conditional branching on environment detection before network communication.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Trojan Download After Initial Implant Delay
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' No use case for the delayed C2 callback and secondary payload execution behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate game-launched processes with network connections to C2 infrastructure after an hours-to-days persistence window. Alert on process creation of unsigned executables downloaded via HTTP/HTTPS from low-reputation or dynamic infrastructure. Monitor for Kaspersky detection signatures (Trojan.Win32.Termixia.*, Trojan-Downloader.Win32.Argamal.gen).

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt — CVE-2026-23479 Redis RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article headline announces high-severity RCE in Redis; pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Redis ports (6379, 6380) followed by command patterns typical of RCE exploitation: EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT commands, or payload-bearing protocol sequences. Correlate with suspicious child process spawning, shell invocation, or outbound exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Redis Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 2-year-old flaw; vulnerable versions (pre-2024) should be inventoried and flagged. Pipeline missed asset-discovery angle entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Redis processes and extract version strings from startup logs or INFO command responses. Flag versions released ≥2 years before 2026-06-04 (i.e., ≤2024-06-04) as vulnerable to CVE-2026-23479 and alert on internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Lua Script Injection in Redis
suggestion.rationale: Redis RCEs typically exploit Lua scripting (EVAL/EVALSHA); no script-injection detection proposed despite 'RCE' in headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT LOAD frequency by source IP. Detect anomalies: volume spikes, script payloads containing shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks), or obfuscated command sequences within Lua arguments.

suggestion.title: RomulusLoader Process Hollowing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents loader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution'—signature injection TTP with no corresponding detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with suspended state followed by memory write/DLL injection; flag parent-child pairs (rundll32, regsvcs) spawned from unusual parents without command-line arguments. Correlate with shellcode patterns or RWX memory allocations.

suggestion.title: SilentRunLoader Chrome Credential Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Python-based loader and information stealer called SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' Targeted credential exfiltration vector with identifiable artifact paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python interpreters or unsigned executables accessing Chrome user data directory (AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default); flag reads of Login Data, Cookies, or Web Data databases. Correlate with outbound network traffic within 60 seconds post-access.

suggestion.title: Anti-Analysis Evasion—Defender Application Guard Registry Checks
suggestion.rationale: Article states Atlas RAT 'features anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the CExecSvc service, and OS UUID'—direct sandbox-detection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes querying HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\CExecSvc, Defender Application Guard registry keys, or WMI Win32_ComputerSystemProduct.UUID in rapid sequence. Alert on pattern matching multiple evasion checks within <2 second window.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Lures—Government & Payroll Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices' with German and Italian variants—geography-specific initial-access campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with localized tax/payroll keywords (Steuerpruefung, Umsatzsteuer, paie, VAT reconciliation) from spoofed government domains; flag RAR/ZIP attachments containing executables. Correlate with RomulusLoader execution within 4 hours of email receipt.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Tool Deployment—AnyDesk/SyncFuture via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture'—legitimate-tool abuse for C2 that bypasses application-whitelist controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AnyDesk or SyncFuture spawned by RomulusLoader or unsigned parent processes; flag installations from non-standard paths or without user interaction. Monitor for outbound connections to remote-management FQDN from processes with no legitimate business justification.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vector Social Engineering—Messaging App Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes threat group 'attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams'—secondary contact channel for victim manipulation or command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email detection with outbound WhatsApp, LINE, or Teams traffic to same external contact within 24-hour window. Flag Teams external user invites; monitor messaging-app traffic for embedded URLs or file-share links from non-organizational accounts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer' as the vulnerable product. Detection of installed instances is the critical first step per the asset-exposure hunt methodology explicitly recommended in the article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory, application metadata, or WAF signatures for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer presence. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-45247. Alert on any exposed instances with patch lag beyond federal due date 2026-06-06.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: Malicious CacheWarmer Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' This is the precise exploitation technique and should be detectable via HTTP request inspection at the WAF/proxy layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing CacheWarmer cookies with serialized PHP object patterns (base64-encoded strings starting with 'O:' or 'a:' prefixes characteristic of PHP serialization). Correlate with requests to cache-warmer endpoints or Mirasvit module handlers.

suggestion.title: PHP Deserialization Exceptions and Errors
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data.' PHP application and error logs should emit warnings during attempted unserialize() of crafted payloads, particularly class-not-found or unexpected instantiation errors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP error logs for unserialize() warnings, object instantiation failures, or class-not-found exceptions correlating with suspicious HTTP request timestamps. Baseline benign serialization patterns and alert on deviations that correlate with CacheWarmer cookie anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'remote code execution.' Successful exploitation should trigger execution of arbitrary commands on the application server, visible as unusual child processes spawned from the web server user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual process creation from web-server-managed processes (www-data, apache, nginx user) spawning shells, scripting interpreters, or network utilities. Focus on timeline correlation with exploitation attempt detection and anomalous parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Configuration or State Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation should allow attacker to manipulate cache behavior or application state. Detection of config file changes, unusual cache flush/warm requests, or injected cache entries post-exploitation indicates active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to Mirasvit configuration or cache files following exploitation attempt windows. Monitor application logs for cache-warmer requests originating from unexpected internal IP ranges or user contexts.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Integer Overflow Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'can be leveraged for increased privileges' on Android 14–16, 'requires no user interaction to exploit,' and is 'under limited targeted exploitation in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevated privilege requests or integer overflow exceptions in Android Framework processes targeting API levels 34–36. Alert on unexpected uid/gid elevation in system_server or framework services, and correlate with integer boundary violations or memory corruption patterns.

suggestion.title: Linux cgroup_release_agent_write() Unprivileged Modification Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' function contains 'insufficient authentication checks' allowing 'a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges.' Impacts kernel 2.6–4.20 and 5.5–5.17.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-root writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent files or cgroup v1 control groups. Monitor for cgroup manipulation syscalls from unprivileged processes. Alert on release_agent modifications preceding privilege escalation or child process creation at elevated UID.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via cgroups v1 Namespace Isolation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states the flaw 'can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system,' especially 'when containers are granted elevated capabilities.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for containerized processes accessing /sys/fs/cgroup or host-level resources. Detect CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability usage from within containers and track escape indicators: host PID access, host filesystem mounts, or root UID transitions. Cross-correlate with cgroup manipulation events.

suggestion.title: Elevated Linux Capability Abuse in Containerized Workloads
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the vulnerability is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities,' signaling heightened risk when CAP_SYS_ADMIN or equivalent capabilities are provisioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all running containers and their Linux capability sets. Alert on creation or modification of containers with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, or CAP_SYS_RAWIO. Monitor for exploitation attempts (cgroups v1 syscalls, release_agent writes) originating from containers flagged as over-privileged.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with prohibited UID/GID parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It is possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value.' This is the exploit vector; should be detected at API layer before kernel deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels with request bodies containing KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID parameters set to numeric values, especially 0. Baseline allowed source IPs; alert on external/unexpected origins. Cross-reference against known enterprise-gateway deployments to reduce FP from legitimate notebook servers.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes pod creation with runAsUser=0 by enterprise-gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation results in 'launching kernels with a prohibited UID...by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID.' Kubernetes audit logs reflect pods created with root context when the bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kube-apiserver audit logs for pod creation where requestObject.spec.securityContext.runAsUser=0 OR requestObject.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser=0 AND user.username matches enterprise-gateway service account. Validate against legitimate enterprise-gateway process image/labels.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway pod with hostPath mount created on Kubernetes worker
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1611 (Escape to Host). hostPath volumes grant container direct read/write access to worker filesystem. Legitimate enterprise-gateway deployments do not require hostPath; its presence indicates privilege escalation and lateral movement prep.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pod creation where user.username contains 'enterprise-gateway' AND requestObject.spec.volumes[].hostPath.path is populated. hostPath is a strong indicator regardless of runAsUser value; correlate pod metadata against known-good enterprise-gateway manifests.

suggestion.title: Cron file modification from Kubernetes container process on worker node
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1053.003 (Scheduled Task/Job: Cron) and describes 'install' phase. Post-container-escape, attacker writes to /etc/cron*, /var/spool/cron/* on the worker node to establish persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor filesystem create/modify/write events on cron paths (/etc/cron.d/*, /etc/crontab, /var/spool/cron/*) where InitiatingProcessFileName is 'runc', 'containerd-shim', 'containerd-shim-runc-v2', or parent process is a container runtime. Alert on all instances—legitimate cron writes must never originate from containers.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API server receives unusual create/update pod requests from Enterprise Gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token.' UC_28_2 detects pod creation in audit logs, but K8s API server logs directly show the malicious requests. Article narrative: 'stolen Kubernetes service account token, which can steal Kubernetes...' implies direct API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes audit logs for create/update pod operations issued by the enterprise-gateway service account (or a service account token bound to it) that includes privileged: true, hostPath volumes, or hostNetwork specifications. Baseline the normal API patterns for the service account and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway process establishes network connection to Kubernetes API server or kube-proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates SSTI allows 'execution of Python code,' implying code can make outbound API calls. The attacker likely must connect to https://kubernetes.default.svc to use the stolen token. Article phrase: 'Python code and OS Commands...can...steal the Kubernetes service account token' implies active API queries post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP/443 or TCP/6443 connections from Enterprise Gateway container processes to 10.0.0.1 (Kubernetes API server default IP) or kubernetes.default.svc DNS resolution. Baseline normal connectivity and alert on new outbound K8s API connections.

suggestion.title: KERNEL_* environment variable injection or fuzzing attempts in HTTP request to /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable.' Attackers must craft payloads in these variables. Detection should monitor HTTP POST bodies or URL parameters for KERNEL_* keys with Jinja2 syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP POST requests to /api/kernels endpoints with JSON or form-encoded request bodies containing KERNEL_* keys (KERNEL_POD_NAME, KERNEL_WORKING_DIR, KERNEL_NAMESPACE, etc.) paired with template injection payloads ({{ }} syntax). Look for payloads attempting to access __builtins__, __class__, or os module.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed or blocked SSTI payloads to /api/kernels within short time window (exploitation reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a specific vulnerability, but attackers typically probe with multiple payload variants before a successful exploitation. Phrase: 'including Jinja2 template expressions it is possible to execution Python code' suggests deliberate crafting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume or multiple distinct SSTI payloads sent to /api/kernels from the same source IP within a short window (e.g., 10+ requests in 5 minutes). WAF or proxy logs blocking 400/403 responses with template injection keywords can indicate active fuzzing or enumeration.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway configuration or image refresh post-patch (detection of environment isolation)
suggestion.rationale: Article is a critical RCE patch. Defenders must detect whether patched or unpatched versions are running. Article states vulnerability is in 'rendering of the Kubernetes manifest,' implying it's in the image or deployment spec.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Enterprise Gateway container image versions and patch levels across the cluster. Alert on pods created with known-vulnerable image tags (pre-patch versions of Jupyter Enterprise Gateway). Check container_image fields in K8s audit logs or container runtime logs.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_* YAML-injection payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes POST requests to /api/kernels with malicious KERNEL_* environment variables containing YAML metacharacters (---, securityContext, runAsUser). Article itself documents the Splunk SPL joining Web datamodel with container logs searching for YAML injection indicators. Pipeline failed to extract this exploit-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/kernels where request contains KERNEL_* parameters with YAML metacharacters or security context keywords. Correlate with downstream pod-creation audit logs confirming the injection was processed.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Privileged or root pod created by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'overwrite existing keys like securityContext' and create privileged pods. UC_27_3 in the article hunts K8s audit logs for pod creation by enterprise-gateway service account with privilege escalation fields (runAsUser:0, privileged:true, hostNetwork, hostPath). Pipeline failed to extract this install-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt K8s audit logs for pod/deployment creation by enterprise-gateway service account containing securityContext fields indicating privilege escalation: runAsUser=0, runAsGroup=0, privileged=true, hostNetwork=true, hostPID=true, or hostPath mounts. Establish baseline pod count and alert on anomalous creation patterns.

suggestion.title: Article-specific process artifact hunt — Jupyter Enterprise Gateway launch_kubernetes.py execution and file mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article title references Kubernetes Manifest Injection in Jinja2 Template Rendering. The vulnerable component is launch_kubernetes.py which renders manifests. UC_27_1 in the article hunts for execution of this process and mutation of /home/jovyan files. Pipeline failed to extract this execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for execution of launch_kubernetes.py process or modification of files in /home/jovyan directory (Jupyter working directory). Baseline should establish normal frequency; anomalous execution or file churn may indicate exploit attempts or post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: YAML Parse Failure / Invalid Kubernetes Manifest from Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states env vars are 'interpolated...without YAML-aware escaping.' Malformed YAML in injection attempts will cause template rendering errors or API validation rejections before successful pod creation. Pipeline missed this early-stage attack indicator that precedes UC_27_3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed pod creation requests (status != 201/202) or YAML parsing exceptions triggered by malformed manifest content correlating with /api/kernels POST requests. Flag requests where KERNEL_* parameters contain YAML metacharacters (---, {{, }}, &, *, |) but manifest validation fails.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount Privilege Escalation Post-Pod-Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1611 (Escape to Host) and T1068 as techniques. UC_27_3 detects privileged *pod creation*; this UC targets post-container-creation escape attempts (cgroup breakout, kernel exploits, namespace breakouts) that follow successful pod injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-pod-creation, hunt for container escape indicators: writes to /proc/*/ns/, mount syscalls for cgroup or host fs, cgroup release_agent setups, /sys/firmware access, or setns/unshare calls. Correlate pod creation timestamp with privilege escalation event window (assume escape occurs within 1 hour of pod start).

suggestion.title: Overly-Permissive RBAC for Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount
suggestion.rationale: Article's injection vulnerability is enabled by enterprise-gateway service account having pod-creation capability. Proactive hunt: does the service account have overly broad role bindings? Article does not describe baseline expected permissions, indicating this standing hunt is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate enterprise-gateway service account's ClusterRole/Role and RoleBinding. Alert if role includes wildcards on verbs, wildcard on resources, or permissions on sensitive objects (pods, deployments, secrets, daemonsets). Establish least-privilege baseline and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Malspam via Google DoubleClick Ad Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign' — establishes ad platform as attack vector for initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateway and web proxy logs for emails containing doubleclick.net or googleadservices.com URLs with redirect chains to unknown/low-rep domains. Alert on URL mismatches (display vs. actual target), shortened URLs, or repeated click patterns from single user in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Process Execution from Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Malspam campaign delivers DesckVB payload — execution from user-opened attachment or link is the expected next step but no process-level detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned executables spawned from winword.exe, excel.exe, outlook.exe, or msiexec.exe with suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or registry/WMI activity. Flag process creation timestamps indicating immediate execution post-document-open or atypical parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Command-and-Control Callback
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware inherently establishes outbound C2 communication; article mentions 'DesckVB RAT' but no network-detection use case surfaces for beaconing behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rare outbound connections from compromised endpoints to non-standard ports or previously unseen IP ranges. Alert on persistent, periodic outbound traffic (30-60 second intervals) characteristic of heartbeat/beacon activity, especially over non-standard HTTP/HTTPS ports or to newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VBA Macro or Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malspam delivery typically relies on Office macro or script execution; article specifies malware delivery via email but execution vector not made explicit in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Office application event logs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for macro execution followed by suspicious child process creation (shells, LOLBins). Alert on WMI activity, registry modifications, or scheduled task creation initiated during or immediately after macro execution.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Embedded or Link-based Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly relies on 'malspam' — phishing email as the attack vector — yet no email-content or user-interaction detection rules surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with suspicious sender reputation, unusual sender-recipient relationships, or high-risk file attachments (Office, archives, executables) especially from external domains. Alert on emails with both embedded links and downloadable payloads, or where link display text mismatches actual destination.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 HPACK Header Compression Amplification Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation.' No detection rule for indexed header reference flooding. Envoy/Apache show 5700:1 and 4000:1 compression ratios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag single source IP sending >500 HTTP/2 indexed header references (frame size <5 bytes) to HPACK dynamic table within 60s. Correlate with server memory growth. Baseline per platform; alert when index-to-memory ratio deviates >3σ from normal.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow Control Window Stalling with WINDOW_UPDATE Loop
suggestion.rationale: Attack second stage: 'advertising a zero-byte flow-control window' and server 'periodically sends tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames to avoid timeouts' but 'requests never fully completed.' No rule for indefinite stream hold pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 streams with advertised window size = 0 bytes held >30s, receiving WINDOW_UPDATE frames but no HEADERS or RST_STREAM. Single IP holding >50 such streams concurrently within 60s indicates resource-exhaustion DoS.

suggestion.title: Rapid Process Memory Exhaustion on Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Quantified impact: Apache reaches 32GB in ~18s, Envoy in ~10s, nginx in ~45s. Article emphasizes 'preventing its release.' No detection for accelerated memory growth signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate RSS growth >10GB/min on NGINX/Apache/IIS/Envoy with HTTP/2 connection spike from single external IP. Alert when memory doesn't return to baseline after connection closes. Stack trace should involve http2 or hpack code paths.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable HTTP/2 Web Server Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies unpatched versions: IIS (Windows Server 2025), Envoy 1.37.2, Pingora, and names patched versions (nginx 1.29.8, Apache mod_http2 2.0.41). Pipeline missed asset inventory detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate running versions of NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Pingora. Flag instances <1.29.8 (nginx), <2.0.41 (Apache mod_http2), any current IIS/Envoy/Pingora. Correlate with external HTTP/2 traffic; isolated or air-gapped unpatched systems warrant elevated priority.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Count Anomaly with Tiny Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses 'tiny header values' for amplification. Article notes bypass of 'limits on total decoded header size' because values are small but bookkeeping scales. No detection for header-count-to-content ratio inversion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single request contains >1000 headers or header count >100x normal application baseline. Cross-reference with total decoded header payload size <100KB; tiny-payload-large-count pattern is amplification signature.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub OAuth Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attackers can 'steal full GitHub OAuth tokens' via a one-click mechanism, implying tokens are generated or exposed during the attack. Pipeline failed to propose detection for abnormal OAuth token issuance patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub OAuth token creation events for anomalies: tokens issued without corresponding user UI interaction, tokens generated from unexpected geolocations or IP ranges compared to historical user login patterns, or rapid token issuance followed by immediate exfiltration attempts. Correlate with DeviceProcessEvents showing browser navigation to GitHub URLs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Dev Environment Access via Phishing Link
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'one-click' attack vector, strongly suggesting phishing or malicious link exploitation. No UC captures initial access phase (email, browser, URL click).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails linking to GitHub or GitHub Dev domains with URL path manipulation (e.g., oauth/authorize parameters). Correlate email delivery with subsequent suspicious browser activity: clicks to lookalike GitHub URLs, GitHub OAuth permission grant pages, or redirects to attacker C2. Flag emails with urgency language referencing GitHub security or development access.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Token Exfiltration to Non-Standard Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies tokens are 'stolen,' requiring exfiltration. Pipeline did not propose detection for OAuth token data leaving GitHub's environment or being sent to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls that extract user tokens (e.g., GET /user/installations, GET /app/installations) originating from IPs not in user's historical pattern. Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests exfiltrating Authorization headers or OAuth tokens to domains outside GitHub/Microsoft infrastructure. Monitor for base64-encoded token strings in DNS queries or cleartext HTTP payloads.

suggestion.title: Abnormal GitHub Actions Workflow Execution Post-Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Stolen OAuth tokens grant repository and workflow permissions. Article does not specify post-exploitation impact, but this is a critical detection gap if attackers pivot to CI/CD abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows triggered from non-standard event sources (e.g., API calls from unexpected IPs) or workflows executing commands that deviate from repo maintainers' historical patterns. Flag sudden elevation in workflow job count, access to secrets, or deployments to production from IPs not in CIDR allowlists.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Consent Screen Bypass or Misdirection
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies a 'one-click' attack; normal OAuth flows require explicit user consent. Pipeline should detect UI spoofing, redirect-loop exploitation, or missing consent flow validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub OAuth authorization endpoint for requests with missing or tampered scopes (e.g., requesting full repo access without user interaction). Detect iframe injection or DOM manipulation on login/consent pages. Alert on OAuth tokens issued with scopes that exceed user's typical app permissions or issued without corresponding browser-based consent event.

suggestion.title: GitHub Dev Environment Code Injection or RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'GitHub Dev Attack,' implying GitHub's codespace/dev environment is leveraged. No detection proposed for code execution or environment compromise that could enable token theft at the source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual process execution within GitHub Codespaces or Dev environments (e.g., curl, wget, python scripts exfiltrating environment variables containing tokens). Detect container escape attempts or privilege escalation within dev environments. Monitor for environment variable access to GITHUB_TOKEN or similar credential material outside normal workflow context.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection: TA4922 Targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Expands Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa.' No email gateway or content-analysis use case generated despite geographic expansion being the primary article claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with sender spoofing, credential-harvesting lures, or suspicious attachments targeting mailboxes in the four named geographies. Monitor for campaign-consistent subject lines or sender patterns associated with TA4922 phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Link Click and Credential Submission Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns require victim interaction (click → landing page → credential entry). Article establishes 'phishing attacks' but pipeline extracted no web-gateway or proxy-based detection use case for compromise indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy logs for clicks to newly-registered or low-reputation domains from the four targeted regions. Detect POST requests to credential-harvesting form endpoints. Correlate with email-to-click timing to confirm campaign conversion funnel.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication Attempts Post-Phishing Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Credential harvest via phishing enables account takeover. Article's phishing attack narrative implies credential exfiltration but no post-compromise credential-use detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed authentication spikes and impossible-travel logins for accounts that received TA4922 phishing emails. Detect lateral-movement attempts using harvested credentials. Correlate with geographic targeting of original phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Infrastructure Tracking: TA4922 Domains and IPs
suggestion.rationale: Actor name 'TA4922' is explicitly stated in title but pipeline did not surface actor or infrastructure IOCs for threat hunting despite 'expand[ing]' phrase suggesting new infrastructure indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index any phishing domains, registrars, and hosting infrastructure associated with TA4922 expansion into new geographies. Establish early-warning network-security use case: block/alert on DNS queries and connections to known TA4922 phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Magento Cache Warmer — Serialized PHP Object Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'insecure deserialization of untrusted data' as root cause; must detect POST requests to vulnerable extension paths containing PHP serialized objects with gadget-chain markers (O:* prefix, base64-encoded class chains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to Magento extension paths (*/mirasvit/*, */cache-warmer/*) with PHP serialization markers or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate requests lacking valid Magento session tokens or originating from non-browser user agents. High fidelity if payload contains known gadget chains (e.g., Monolog, WordPress plugins).

suggestion.title: Web Server Process RCE — Unexpected Child Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: RCE is 'actively exploited'—implies post-exploitation command execution; detect shell spawning (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) from PHP.exe, httpd, or nginx parent processes on Magento systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is web-server process and child is shell/command interpreter. Correlate timing and source IP with preceding inbound POST anomalies to Magento. High confidence if command-line contains suspicious arguments, network callbacks, or file operations outside web root.

suggestion.title: Magento Web Root Unauthorized File Creation — Web Shell Upload
suggestion.rationale: RCE leads to persistence; detect new .php, .phtml, .jsp files in web-accessible directories or Magento var/cache/tmp during/after exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new file creation in Magento docroot, var/, cache/ directories with suspicious extensions. Correlate creation timestamp with inbound POST anomalies. Flag files written by web-server process user or with low entropy/suspicious metadata.

suggestion.title: E-Commerce Database Anomalies Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Magento targets e-commerce platforms; 'actively exploited' attacks typically exfiltrate or modify customer data, payment info, or admin accounts—monitor database query patterns for unauthorized modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on customer_entity, sales_order, admin_user tables or payment fields originating from compromised PHP sessions within seconds of process-execution or file-creation anomalies. Flag queries modifying user credentials or sensitive columns.

suggestion.title: Magento Extension Path Exploitation — Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension' as attack vector; monitor for malformed requests, unusual HTTP methods, or oversized payloads targeting vulnerable extension endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures for POST requests to /mirasvit/*, /cache-warmer/*, or similar extension paths using unusual HTTP methods (PATCH, OPTIONS) or oversized bodies. Alert on requests with missing standard headers (Referer, User-Agent) or from non-browser clients. Medium-high fidelity if combined with serialization-pattern detection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—public PoC availability is the core threat driver. Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts matching known public exploit signatures against Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM for HTTP requests and application-layer messages matching CVE-2026-20230 public exploit patterns (malformed SIP messages, authentication bypass payloads, or specific URI fuzzing documented in PoC code).

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Child Process Execution from Service Account
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploitation on Unified CM typically results in code execution within the service context. Post-exploitation process spawning from Java/Tomcat/CCMService is a critical execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned from Cisco Unified CM services (java.exe, CCMService.exe, tomcat processes) executing shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or remote execution utilities (curl, wget, nc).

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Unauthorized Admin Authentication or Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20230 may enable authentication bypass or session hijacking. Monitor Unified CM audit logs and authentication mechanisms for indicators of credential compromise or session fixation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication followed by successful admin login from same IP, replayed or anomalous session tokens in requests to /ccmadmin endpoints, or 2FA bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: External Scanning Activity Targeting Cisco Unified CM Admin Port
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit code enables mass scanning; article title indicates high risk of automated exploitation. Monitor for external/untrusted source IPs probing Unified CM ports (8443 HTTPS, 5060 SIP).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed or successful connection attempts to Unified CM service ports from external IP addresses or IPs outside authorized administrator/partner network ranges.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Lateral Movement via Database or Replication Channels
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM sits in enterprise telephony infrastructure; successful exploitation may pivot to cluster replication or database services. Monitor inter-node communications for unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM cluster replication channels (port 2748, 2749) for traffic from unauthorized sources or to/from unexpected destinations; alert on database connections (port 5432) from non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers exploit by 'sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device' targeting WebDialer. No HTTP-level detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoints (typical paths: /webdialer, port 8443) originating from untrusted networks. Prioritize requests with unusual payloads, embedded file paths, URL schemes, or SSRF-pattern indicators in query/POST parameters.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Writes from Unified CM Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' No file I/O detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes from Unified CM processes (UcService, MasterAgent, CCMService, CTIManager) to system-sensitive directories (/etc, /root, /bin, /usr/bin) or executable paths. Alert especially on writes that bypass normal deployment pipelines.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from WebDialer Process Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation resulting in 'elevate to root.' No privilege escalation detection post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebDialer child process spawning (or parent Unified CM service launching child procs) followed immediately by privilege elevation system calls (setuid, sudo, or credential changes from service account to root). Flag cascading child processes with escalating privileges.

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service Enablement Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled' and provides mitigation. No service configuration change detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes to CTI Services that enable 'Cisco WebDialer Web Service' from previously disabled state. Monitor service startup events and network interface changes exposing WebDialer to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: SSRF Pattern Detection in Unified CM Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerability class as 'server-side request forgery (SSRF).' Pipeline did not map SSRF-specific detection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to WebDialer containing URL-encoded or raw internal server names, IP addresses (169.254.x.x metadata endpoints, localhost variants), file:// URIs, or SSRF test payloads. Flag if requests trigger unexpected outbound connections from affected host.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggers Unexpected Action Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Malicious Issue Hijack Repositories'—core attack vector is a crafted GitHub issue that triggers vulnerable Action logic without intended safeguards.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions triggered by newly created issues or PR comments with unusual content patterns (embedded shell syntax, base64, template injection). Alert when issue author has no prior contribution history or no membership in repo. Correlate with subsequent repository modifications.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to GitHub Secrets or GITHUB_TOKEN from Actions
suggestion.rationale: Repository 'hijacking' implies attacker obtained credentials—likely GITHUB_TOKEN or stored secrets leveraged by vulnerable Action to modify repo settings, collaborators, or workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Actions that export, log, or exfiltrate GITHUB_TOKEN or repository secrets. Flag Actions that request elevated scopes (write-all, admin:repo_hook) triggered by external input (issue body, PR comments). Correlate token usage with unauthorized API calls.

suggestion.title: Repository Configuration/Permissions Modified by Compromised GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking described in title necessitates attacker gaining ability to modify repo—add collaborators, change branch protection, modify secrets, or alter action workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository-level modifications (team additions, collaborator permission grants, branch protection rules disabled, secrets added/modified) performed by GitHub Actions token. Focus on changes initiated from untrusted or newly-created Actions runs triggered by external input. Baseline expected Actions permissions.

suggestion.title: GitHub Workflow File Injection via Issue/PR Body
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability likely allows attacker to inject arbitrary workflow code or parameters via issue body—article premise implies code execution in Actions context from malicious input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for workflow file modifications (.github/workflows/*.yml) that directly reference or interpolate ${{ github.event.issue.body }}, ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}, or similar unvalidated inputs. Flag Actions that execute commands built from issue/PR content without shell escaping or allowlist validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub API Calls to Modify Repository Settings from Actions
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking implies attacker invoked GitHub REST/GraphQL APIs to take over repo—add SSH keys, rotate credentials, modify deploy keys, or push to protected branches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls (repos/*/{collaborators,keys,secrets,protected_branches,teams} endpoints) originated by Actions workflows triggered from external events. Flag calls with unusual rate, scope, or timing. Correlate with Actions runs executed in response to GitHub issues or pull request comments from untrusted actors.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Execution of Unsanitized Shell Commands from Event Input
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: Action likely executes bash/PowerShell commands constructed from issue body without proper escaping, enabling command injection and repository takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for shell command invocations that reference github.event.issue or github.event.pull_request properties directly in run: directives without variable quoting or templating guards. Flag processes spawned with arguments derived from issue/PR metadata. Alert on elevated privilege actions (sudo, Set-ExecutionPolicy) initiated from untrusted input.

suggestion.title: Domain Spoofing: Open-Source Tool Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core attack vector. Should detect domains impersonating npm, PyPI, GitHub, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly registered or malicious domains with character-similarity (Levenshtein distance <3) to legitimate open-source repositories.
