Correlate with HTTP traffic from users whose search queries match the tool name (e.g., searching 'python requests package' and landing on fake pypi-request.com).

suggestion.title: Search Result Spoofing via SEO Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites 'Rank High on Google'—SEO manipulation is the enabling prerequisite. Pipeline did not surface detection for search result injection or ranking fraud.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume automated HTTP requests with search-engine bot User-Agents to attacker-controlled domains. Detect rapid backlink injection patterns, domain-authority gaming signals, and DNS query spikes associated with typosquat/lookalike domains masquerading as legitimate tools.

suggestion.title: TDS Traffic Redirect Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Deliver Malware via TDS' (Traffic Distribution System). Pipeline did not generate detection for TDS fingerprinting or multi-hop redirect behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify redirect chains where request from search referrer → fake tool domain → intermediary infrastructure → final payload. Flag rapid sequences of 301/302/307 responses with domain hops to unknown/low-reputation IP space. TDS systems often fingerprint User-Agent and geolocation before payload selection.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution Post-Fake Tool Download
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is malware delivery ('to Deliver Malware'). Pipeline should correlate suspicious download + child process execution (e.g., downloaded executable spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or rundll32).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to fake tool domains with subsequent suspicious process creation (unsigned binaries, LOLBins abuse, known malware families). Flag downloads followed by process tree anomalies within 1–5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Search Query → Malicious Domain Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Users are searching for legitimate tools ('Open-Source Tools') and being served malicious results. Detection should correlate search referrers with malicious domain visits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users whose HTTP referrer is Google Search with legitimate tool keywords, followed by navigation to lookalike/typosquat domain. Trigger on repeated user queries for well-known open-source projects (pip, npm, requests, pandas) landing on unrelated infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Click to Backdoor Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states FlutterShell spread 'via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads.' No use case proposed for detecting the ad-click-to-payload chain despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes (Safari, Chrome, Firefox on macOS) initiating unexpected downloads or spawning child processes immediately after visits to ad-serving infrastructure (doubleclick.net, adwords, YouTube ad CDNs). Monitor for redirect chains terminating in executable downloads with suspicious naming or from high-entropy domains.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific malware family targeting macOS. No detection use case proposed for execution phase despite 'backdoor' indicating post-execution persistence or C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS for suspicious process launch from ~/Downloads or /tmp with characteristics matching Flutter-based malware: unexpected binary execution, suspicious library loading, unsigned or ad-hoc signed Mach-O binaries, or processes with names masquerading as system utilities.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from FlutterShell Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Malware identified as 'backdoor' implies command-and-control capability, yet no detection logic proposed for C2 beacon or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound connections from processes spawned by malicious ad clicks to non-standard ports or high-entropy domains. Look for patterns consistent with HTTP/HTTPS C2 (regular beacons, POST requests with binary payloads, DNS tunneling). Correlate process lineage from browser → backdoor → C2.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft or Data Exfiltration via FlutterShell
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies threat as '[HIGH]' severity backdoor but pipeline does not suggest detections for post-exploitation collection or exfiltration typical of backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor backdoor processes for suspicious file access patterns (keylogger indicators, screenshot/screen capture libraries), unusual volume of data being read from sensitive directories (~/.ssh, ~/Library/Keychains), or anomalous network exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ad Network Compromise or Malicious Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'Google and YouTube Ads'—if legitimate ad networks are compromised or malicious campaigns deployed, detection should focus on ad-serving infrastructure poisoning, not just client-side payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ad-serving domains (doubleclick.net, gstatic.com, YouTube CDNs) hosting or redirecting to suspicious payloads. Cross-reference ad creative URLs with malware sample repositories. Flag anomalous ad network traffic patterns (unexpected countries/languages, unusual landing page domains, shortened URLs with high click-through rates).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Injection into Web Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject and execute arbitrary PHP code.' No detection hypothesis for PHP creation/execution from plugin paths. Detection should catch webshell or payload staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-write events in WordPress plugin directories (/wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro/) creating .php files, especially from web server process context. Correlate with PHP process spawning system commands or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to Vulnerable Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attackers' exploiting CVE-2026-3300. Need hunt for HTTP requests triggering the vulnerable code path without session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST requests to WordPress plugin endpoints (likely /wp-admin/ or /wp-content/) for Everest Forms that lack authentication cookies or have suspicious parameters. Look for payloads containing PHP delimiters (<?php, eval, system, exec, passthru) in request body.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: PHP code execution ('execute arbitrary PHP') typically manifests as web-server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) executing system commands. Article implies command execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by web server processes (httpd, apache2, nginx, php-fpm) executing reverse shells, netcat, curl, wget, or scripting interpreters. Focus on variants running from /tmp, /var/tmp, or other writable plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Rapid Enumeration of WordPress Plugin Versions
suggestion.rationale: CVE affects versions up to 1.9.12; attackers must identify vulnerable targets. Article implies reconnaissance to find affected sites. Missing pre-exploitation discovery hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or high-frequency requests to WordPress plugin fingerprinting endpoints (readme.txt, version.php, or predictable plugin-enumeration paths) from single source IPs, especially combined with requests to suspected CVE-2026-3300 exploitation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outlook Forwarding Rule Creation on Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes five-month mailbox access by unauthorized actors. Attackers maintaining persistent email access typically create forwarding rules to exfiltrate copies of sent/received mail; rules may be hidden or point to attacker-controlled inboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of Outlook forwarding rules on accounts belonging to high-value targets (C-suite, board, trading desk) outside business hours or from anomalous IP geographies. Alert on rules forwarding to external domains or hidden folders. Cross-reference rule creation time with failed authentications in prior 48 hours.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Geographic or Device Access to Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker sustained mailbox access over five months. Unauthorized access likely shows login patterns diverging sharply from executive's normal behavior—unusual countries, times, or devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate mailbox access for each executive by time-of-day, geography, device type, and IP range over 60 days. Detect logins from countries where the user has never worked or traveled, time zones >12 hours offset from registered office, or VPN/proxy exit nodes. Alert with severity increase if combined with high-volume mail search or rule creation.

suggestion.title: Unseen Email Delegation or SendAs Permission Assigned to Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: A second method for sustained email access is granting SendAs or SendOnBehalf permissions, allowing the attacker to compose mail as the executive without logging in directly. This persists across password resets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor all Outlook permission grants (Add-MailboxPermission, Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfTo) on executive-tier mailboxes. Alert on permissions granted to accounts outside the organization, service accounts, or mailboxes inactive >30 days. Require approval workflow for any delegation changes.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Email Search or Content Exfiltration from Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates hackers 'spied on' the mailbox for five months—implying systematic collection of email content. Expect large search queries or bulk export activity (PST export, message trace searches with high result counts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline mail search frequency and result cardinality for each user role. Flag searches returning >1000 items, searches run during off-hours, or bulk PST export commands initiated from non-admin accounts or outside the organization's IP ranges. Correlate with mailbox rule changes or unusual login patterns.

suggestion.title: Deleted or Hidden Email Forwarding Rules on Compromise Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: When attackers are detected or campaigns wind down, they often delete forwarding rules to erase evidence. Detection of rule deletion combined with forensic mail recovery can indicate compromise duration and scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Remove-InboxRule or Remove-ForwardingAddress commands run by users not owning the rule, or rules deleted immediately after unexpected login spike. Cross-correlate with authentication anomalies within 48 hours prior. Retention of deleted rule audit logs is critical—ensure AuditLog retention >90 days.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts Preceding First Successful Compromise Access
suggestion.rationale: Initial access likely required credential guessing, spray, or phishing. Expect spike in failed logins preceding the first successful unauthorized mailbox access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each executive account, detect ≥5 failed login attempts within 24 hours followed by a successful login from a new geography or device. Correlate failed-attempt IP with publicly known VPN/proxy services or datacenter IPs. Trigger MFA enforcement and password reset on detection.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with Base64-encoded command
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' Confirmed in KongTuke case study as initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe or explorer.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand or -E flags. Decode Base64 payload and inspect for Invoke-WebRequest, Add-Type, or reflective DLL injection. Correlate with subsequent network connections to confirm C2 signaling.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest fetching payload to ApplicationData
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' High-fidelity payload staging pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest or DownloadFile cmdlets executing with output redirected to ApplicationData, TEMP, or %APPDATA% subdirectories. Correlate file creation timestamp with network connection logs to confirm external source. Check destination domain reputation and WHOIS ASN.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to known C2-hosting ASNs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes hunt: 'Connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges. Certain autonomous systems have a long, documented history of hosting command-and-control infrastructure.' Firewall case study confirms 144.31.221.82 on port 6060.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to ASNs flagged for C2 hosting (DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, etc.) regardless of destination IP, particularly on non-standard ports (6060, 8888, etc.). Correlate with EDR process telemetry to rule out legitimate use cases (CI/CD, development, cloud infrastructure).

suggestion.title: curl.exe making secondary C2 connections
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' curl.exe absence in non-development environments is rare; presence with suspicious network activity is high-confidence signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor curl.exe process creation on non-developer machines. Flag if curl spawns from PowerShell, cmd.exe, or unusual parent processes. Correlate curl network connections with firewall-flagged C2 infrastructure. curl in production environments outside CI/CD pipelines warrants investigation.

suggestion.title: Remove-Item cleanup post-payload download
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' This anti-forensics behavior directly follows payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell processes executing Remove-Item or del commands targeting ApplicationData, TEMP, Downloads, or %APPDATA% subdirectories, particularly within 1-5 minutes of Invoke-WebRequest or file creation events. This sequence is high-confidence for malware cleanup.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent initiating HTTP(S) connections
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hunt: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In firewall proxy or connection logs, identify HTTP User-Agent headers containing 'MSIEXEC' or 'Windows Installer' making outbound requests. MSIEXEC should not be a direct HTTP client in normal operations. Flag connections to untrusted ASNs or non-standard ports (>10000). Encrypted HTTPS payload bypasses content inspection—User-Agent becomes primary signal.

suggestion.title: Okta/MAX Messenger Token Theft — POST to Adversary C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states expansion to 'target Okta and MAX Messenger'; credential theft is the operation's goal. Article mentions 'stealing login tokens' but hunts focus only on delivery, not credential exfiltration. No hunt detects HTTP POST to the securehubcloud.com infrastructure with serialized token data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to C2 domains (panel.securehubcloud.com, api.securehubcloud.com, boss.securehubcloud.com) within 5 minutes of phishing link click or Office child-process execution. Look for request bodies containing Base64-encoded or JSON-structured credentials (bearer tokens, refresh_tokens, Okta session IDs). High confidence if source IP matches internal network and user account was recipient of a phishing email.

suggestion.title: Fake Device Authorization Prompt (MFA Bypass Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article states operation 'trick[s] users into authorizing fake device login requests' — this is a specific social engineering attack vector. No hunt detects the phishing page that mimics legitimate Okta/M365 MFA screens. Need behavioral hunt for unusual authorization grant patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Okta/AAD logs, detect device authorization events (T1111) immediately following clicks to suspicious domains from the IOC list. Look for 'Device approval' or 'Authorization grant' events from users who are not known to perform MFA-less flows. Correlate against Okta/AAD session logs for same-hour failed MFA attempts on the same account before the approval, indicating phishing page capture.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Workers URL Hosting Phishing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Cloudflare Workers domains (open-box-rpps.jeff-1fd.workers.dev, data-form-o5pu.p-ntz8agp6.workers.dev) as phishing landing pages. These are legitimate cloud infrastructure abused for hosting. No hunt detects suspicious HTTP GET requests to workers.dev subdomains housing credential-harvesting forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to *.workers.dev subdomains matching the pattern '[a-z0-9\-]+\.p-[a-z0-9]+\.workers\.dev' (Cloudflare Workers namespace pattern). Flag if the request contains form-submission patterns (POST with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded containing email, password, token fields) or if visited within 30 seconds after email click.

suggestion.title: PhaaS Infrastructure Reconnaissance — Bulk Domain/IP Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365 as a 'fast-growing' PhaaS platform, implying active customer acquisition and operations. Affiliates/customers of the service likely perform DNS/WHOIS reconnaissance on the Kali365 infrastructure (panel.securehubcloud.com, api.securehubcloud.com, boss.securehubcloud.com). This reconnaissance by threat actors is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious bulk DNS queries or WHOIS lookups for the article's domain IOCs from external IP space (non-corporate). Look for single source querying all three .securehubcloud.com subdomains within 10-minute window, or querying them alongside known malicious infrastructure. Exclude known security research organizations (Shodan, etc.).

suggestion.title: C2 Certificate Pinning / JA3 Signature Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article provides two Cloudflare-hosted IP addresses (172.67.156.83, 104.21.32.229) that serve the malicious domains. TLS traffic to these IPs for command-and-control should have distinctive TLS handshake signatures (JA3) that differ from Cloudflare's typical legitimate customer traffic, enabling anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the JA3 TLS signature of legitimate Cloudflare customers. Flag inbound or outbound TLS connections to 172.67.156.83 or 104.21.32.229 (resolved from securehubcloud.com) with JA3 signatures that deviate from the baseline and match known malware/C2 patterns (e.g., Emotet, Cobalt Strike, etc.). Confidence increases if traffic is bidirectional and uses non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Modified build.gyp Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'binding.gyp' as attack vector and 'Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp' indicating build-script execution during install—zero UC generated for this core attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install operations followed by unexpected process execution from npm cache directories (node_modules/.bin or .gyp folders) or suspicious node-gyp invocations with obfuscated arguments or network egress. Alert on build.gyp files containing base64-encoded shell commands, eval() statements, or inline JavaScript that diverges from legitimate package signatures.

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating npm Dependency Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Self-Spreading Worm'—requires detection of malicious transitive dependencies being injected into install graphs. Pipeline captured no persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm dependency resolution for insertion of new/previously-unknown dependencies across multiple packages in a single install session, or packages with sudden dependencies on newly-created accounts. Correlate mass installations of same dependency tree across enterprise hosts to detect worm propagation pattern.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Publication or Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires either account compromise or unauthorized package upload; article title 'npm Supply Chain Attack' establishes initial-access phase. Pipeline missed entry point detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish operations from anomalous IP geolocation or login history, rapid version bumps with minimal code changes, or package metadata modifications without corresponding git commits. Monitor for 2FA bypass indicators in npm account activity logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in npm Preinstall/Postinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp files invoke arbitrary build commands; article emphasizes this as attack mechanism. No detection UC for obfuscated install-time script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages where preinstall, postinstall, or install scripts contain obfuscated bash (base64, ROT13, hex-encoding), eval/exec patterns, or downloads from external URLs. Cross-reference script content against npm registry canonical version; detect script injection into otherwise-known packages.

suggestion.title: Worm-Like Dependency Propagation via Shared Transitive Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Self-Spreading Worm' indicates lateral propagation mechanism through dependency trees. Pipeline generated zero detection for mass-infection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect packages that automatically install or invoke other packages without explicit user dependency declaration. Alert on singular package appearing as transitive dependency in >N diverse, unrelated root packages within 24h window. Correlate process execution across multiple host installation contexts sharing same malicious transitive dependency.

suggestion.title: npm Package Preinstall Hook Execution — Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'published package versions containing the Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall.' This is the delivery mechanism and must be detectable at package installation time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of compiled binaries (ELF or PE) spawned by npm package installation, particularly from node_modules/.bin or temporary extraction directories. Correlate with package.json presence of 'preinstall' script field. Suspicious: execution of Rust binaries or any compiled artifacts during npm install in non-build CI environments.

suggestion.title: Mass Credential File and Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware targets 86 environment variables and 20 credential files… OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials, vault configuration files, SSH keys, and Exodus cryptocurrency wallet files.' Detection must catch the enumeration footprint before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to known credential storage locations ($HOME/.ssh, $HOME/.aws, vault config, $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, $OPENAI_API_KEY) in a single execution context within short time window (< 1 minute). Malware will enumerate multiple credential types; baseline legitimate access per process then alert on anomalous breadth (5+ credential file types accessed by a single process).

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Propagation via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Once a developer is compromised, the malware republishes trojanized versions—this is repeating compromise and must be detected at the npm API layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish events for anomalies: publishes from unusual geographies, times, or IPs; publishes using Trusted Publishing tokens that were recently rotated or accessed; rapid version bumps of multiple packages by a single account; or publishes after a developer account went quiet (first activity after dormancy). Cross-reference against GitHub Actions CI environment IPs—if npm publish originates from a non-CI IP or outside normal CI time windows, flag as account takeover.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration with Obfuscated Names
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'serializes the secrets into a single value and then writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output… uploading the file as a build artifact.' This is a C2-evasion technique that bypasses network detection—must be caught in artifact-upload telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows that upload artifacts with names mimicking lint output, test reports, or build artifacts but contain serialized data (high entropy, structured delimiters). Correlate artifact creation timing with process access to credential files (from UC #2). Alert on artifact uploads from modified or injected workflow steps, especially in runs triggered by pull requests from external contributors.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Module Loading and Rootkit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IronWorm is written in Rust, hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' The rootkit provides kernel-level hiding; detection must target eBPF module load events and suspicious kernel trace instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bpf() syscalls with BPF_PROG_LOAD, BPF_MAP_CREATE, or BPF_ATTACH_* operations outside of authorized system tools (cilium, falco, tetragon). Alert on any unprivileged process loading eBPF programs. Cross-reference with presence of LLVM/Clang compiler tools (llvm-objdump, clang) in the same execution chain, which would indicate on-device eBPF compilation.

suggestion.title: Tor Network Egress from Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'communicates with the operator over the Tor network.' A developer or CI machine establishing Tor connections is extremely anomalous and indicates command-and-control or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on DNS queries to Tor directory servers (.onion SLD names, known Tor gateway IPs). Detect any process (especially non-VPN utilities) establishing HTTPS or SOCKS5 connections to Tor entry nodes. Baseline: development environments should not initiate Tor sessions. High-confidence hit if correlation exists with credential access or artifact upload events.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp with shell command expansion syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exact attack vector: GYP build configuration syntax supports command expansion '<!(...)' form that runs shell commands during configure phase. The malicious binding.gyp is byte-for-byte identical across compromised packages—detectable as IOC pattern. No UC generated despite being the novel attack technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations and node-gyp rebuild execution. Flag packages with binding.gyp files containing command expansion syntax '<!(shell_cmd)' or '$(shell_cmd)' in GYP configuration. Correlate with packages lacking preinstall/postinstall scripts but triggering child process spawning during install.

suggestion.title: Anomalous npm package version jumps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes worm signature: 'inflated version numbers (for example, autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range, or autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4) are themselves a side effect of the worm's automated republishing, not legitimate releases.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm packages with version increments that deviate from semantic versioning patterns (e.g., 0.1.14 → 29.0.1) or multiple malicious versions published within same minute from single maintainer account. Baseline legitimate release cadence per package.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting from standard secret stores
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes.' Attack stage documented but no detection use case for credential material exfiltration or file access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install processes or child processes reading standard credential locations: ~/.npm/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/*, env files, .env, GitHub token locations in shell history/configs. Flag reading of AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, VAULT_TOKEN environment variables by unknown package build processes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions workflow file injection and exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence, and self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach.' GitHub repository compromise and workflow manipulation is a persistence and lateral movement vector not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml) for unexpected creation or modification during npm install or package build cycles. Flag workflows that exfiltrate environment secrets, republish packages, or modify repository settings. Correlate workflow creation timing with npm package installation events.

suggestion.title: npm package republishing from compromised maintainer account
suggestion.rationale: Core propagation mechanism: 'the worm enumerates and republishes everything one compromised account can touch: autotel-* family (24 packages, plus autotel itself).' Single account pushing multiple malicious package versions is a mass-publishing signature absent from generated use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single npm maintainer account publishing unusually large batch of package updates (>5 packages or >3 versions in <10 minutes). Flag accounts republishing packages they do not normally maintain. Correlate with known worm-affected accounts (jagreehal in this incident).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration data transmission to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' Network/API indicators for credential exfiltration to external GitHub repos not extracted or mapped to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS connections from npm install/node-gyp processes to GitHub API (api.github.com) or github.com with POST/PUT requests to repo contents endpoints. Flag unprompted credential transmission to repositories not in corporate GitHub org allowlist. Track git clone/push operations initiated during package installation.

suggestion.title: UC_RANSOM_ENCRYPT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact). Recommended hunts section provides proven Splunk and KQL queries for detecting mass file rename/modification patterns typical of ransomware payload detonation—completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ransomware typically modifies or renames hundreds to thousands of files per user per host within minutes. Aggregate file-rename/modify events by (account, host, 1m window); threshold ~200 unique files/minute is well above P99 of legitimate bulk operations (backup, AV quarantine, deployment tools). Key FP filter: service accounts ($) and known legitimate bulk tooling.

suggestion.title: UC_LSASS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly maps T1003.001 (LSASS Memory) and T1003 (OS Credential Dumping). Kill-chain progression from credential theft to lateral movement is implicit in the threat narrative ('well-worn [attack patterns]'). Article's recommended hunts include proven detection rules for lsass access that pipeline failed to generate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Threat tools (Mimikatz, procdump, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, rundll32 variants) spawn or inject into lsass.exe to extract plaintext credentials. Detection: OpenProcessApiCall with FileName=lsass.exe AND InitiatingProcessFileName ∉ {MsSense.exe, MsMpEng.exe, csrss.exe, svchost.exe, services.exe, lsm.exe}. Alternatively: process_name in (rundll32.exe, comsvcs.exe, procdump.exe) AND command-line contains 'lsass' or 'MiniDump'.

suggestion.title: UC_LATERAL_PSEXEC
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1021.002 (SMB/Windows Admin Shares) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) as observed techniques. Recommended hunts explicitly include detection for PsExec and wmic /node: lateral-movement patterns—all absent from pipeline despite being core to ransomware pre-encryption reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PsExec, paexec, SMBexec, or wmic /node: spawn remote service execution. Detection via process: FileName in (psexec.exe, psexesvc.exe, paexec.exe, smbexec.py) OR (FileName='wmic.exe' AND CommandLine contains '/node:'). Network-layer: SMB traffic to IPC$ followed by child process creation with different owner. High-confidence FP filter: SCCM, authorized remote-admin frameworks, scheduled-task execution.

suggestion.title: UC_HASH_HUNT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists two SHA256 hashes as 'high-fidelity' IOCs in dedicated section. Recommended hunts mention standard IOC-driven template for file-hash matching at endpoint install/execution phase. Pipeline failed to extract IOCs or generate hash-based detection despite having clear reference material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match Payouts King malware samples by SHA256 hash: 335ad12a950f885073acdfebb250c93fb28ca3f374bbba5189986d9234dcbff4, d68ce82e82801cd487f9cd2d24f7b30e353cafd0704dcdf0bb8f12822d4227c2. Detection: hash mismatch in DeviceFileEvents (file_create, file_modify), DeviceProcessEvents (child process creation, image load), or EDR/AV memory-scan hashes. Expected FPs: legitimate software with same hash (low), build artifacts, test files.

suggestion.title: UC_OBFUSCATION_SYSCALL
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Evades EDR With Obfuscation and Direct System Calls'. T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) is mapped but no detection UC addresses the syscall-based EDR bypass tactic, which is a known evasion vector for bypassing kernel32/ntdll API hooks that EDRs rely on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Obfuscated payloads and direct-syscall techniques evade hook-based EDR detection. Indicators: high file entropy (>7.0), absence of kernel32.dll/ntdll.dll in module-import list, direct syscall instruction sequences (opcode patterns: 0F 05 for syscall, mov RAX + syscall), or anomalous memory-execution patterns. Expected FPs: legitimate packed software (.NET reflective loaders, UPX binaries, installer frameworks), debugging tools, some security software.

suggestion.title: Network connections to TA4922 C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists five C2 IPv4 addresses and three domains as 'high-fidelity' indicators. Recommended-hunts section specifies 'Network connections to article IPs/domains (c2 phase, high confidence)' but pipeline generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections and DNS queries to 206.238.115.58, 154.211.86.110, 43.156.77.97, 103.214.172.33, 18.139.83.110, aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com. Monitor for both successful connections and failed attempts; RATs typically exhibit periodic beacon patterns.

suggestion.title: File hash detection for Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, ValleyRAT
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 13 SHA256 hashes for TA4922 malware samples. Recommended-hunts explicitly calls for 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match (install phase, high confidence)' yet pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, execution, or load events matching any of the 13 known malware hashes. Prioritize detections in %TEMP%, %AppData%, Downloads, or unusual system paths. Correlate with parent process name and command line to identify dropper/loader relationships.

suggestion.title: Loader-to-RAT execution chain detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies RomulusLoader and SilentRunLoader as delivery mechanisms for Atlas RAT and ValleyRAT, establishing multi-stage execution. No detection for loader behavioral signatures (process hollowing, DLL injection, suspicious module loading) despite being the execution bottleneck.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loader patterns: suspicious parent-child relationships (temp files spawning unexpected children), CreateRemoteThread/WriteProcessMemory call sequences, LoadLibrary from unusual paths, process creation with mismatched executable vs. command line, hollow-process indicators.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation reconnaissance and data harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes TA4922's 'financially motivated' campaigns deploying RATs inherently designed for data exfiltration and credential theft, yet no behavioral detections for typical reconnaissance activity (process enumeration, registry queries, file discovery) are mentioned despite being core RAT functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious command sequences: tasklist/Get-Process execution, registry queries to HKCU/HKLM/SAM/credential locations, dir/Get-ChildItem recursion, access to credential manager or LSASS. Flag clusters of multiple discovery commands from same parent process within minutes.

suggestion.title: Agent Runtime Invocation of Untrusted / Unapproved MCP Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they continuously pull in MCP servers...untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' Directly detectable at agent execution time by monitoring external tool/MCP server resolution against allowlist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agents invoke external MCP servers, plugins, or third-party tools not in pre-approved registry. Monitor for novel tool registrations or unsigned MCP server connections initiated by agent processes. Correlate agent task intent with tool selection to flag anomalous tool choices.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Agent Command / Script Execution Bypassing Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agents don't just suggest; they execute actions autonomously...run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure...often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' Detectable as privileged process execution or file modifications initiated by agent-controlled processes without corresponding approval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent processes execute system commands or modify files without human approval event in agent logs. Baseline agent permissions and flag executions exceeding historical profile (e.g., execution of scripts in production, database modification, infrastructure access).

suggestion.title: Agent Override of Safety Constraints / Execution Continuing After Freeze Directive
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'an AI agent ignored explicit "freeze" instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Detectable by monitoring whether agent halts execution after safety/pause directives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate agent safety directives (pause, freeze, abort) with subsequent command execution in agent logs. Alert when agent process continues executing commands after receiving explicit halt instruction from operator or safety control system.

suggestion.title: Production Database Modification / Record Fabrication by Agent
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: agent 'deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Detectable as unexpected DELETE/DROP or bulk INSERT operations from agent-identified database connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor production database access logs for DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE, or large INSERT operations issued from agent-controlled or agent-attributed database sessions. Alert on operations that do not align with agent's stated task or normal data pipeline patterns.

suggestion.title: Rapid AI-Generated Code Commits Bypassing Human Review Gates
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agents also generate code and dependencies faster than human review can validate...AI produces code continuously at machine speed and often outside the review processes.' Detectable as anomalous commit velocity from agent accounts or commits bypassing pull request approval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when code commits attributed to agent accounts exceed baseline developer rates or when commits bypass required code review/approval workflows. Flag direct commits to protected branches from agent processes. Correlate rapid commit velocity with vulnerability scanning to detect poisoned code in bulk submissions.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secrets and Credentials in AI-Generated Code Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article: agent output 'may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' Detectable through secret scanning of generated code at commit time or artifact creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all agent-generated code artifacts for credential patterns (API keys, DB passwords, tokens) immediately post-generation. Alert on hardcoded secrets before artifact is committed or deployed. Track which secrets were exposed and downstream reuse by other agents or systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Data Access via Incremental Resource Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details IDOR vulnerability: 'an API endpoint that takes an incrementing user ID parameter and returns user data, but when changing the user ID value it returns data from a different user, without appropriate authorization checks.' This pattern is directly observable when exploited against APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests to object endpoints with sequential or enumerable identifiers (user_id, account_id) issued in rapid succession returning distinct user objects, especially when lacking proper authorization tokens or when observed across multiple distinct user accounts in short time windows.

suggestion.title: Bypassed Authentication Enforcement in API Handlers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability pattern: 'We forgot to add any authentication or authorization checks; any user can request any other user's balance.' Application logs should reveal when sensitive operations execute without prior security validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for sensitive database queries or API operations executing without prior invocation of authentication/authorization validation routines, indicating security checks were omitted or short-circuited.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export from Registration Database - Beneficiary Records
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'gained access to personal data... names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' from '600,000 Palestinian households.' This represents exfiltration of ~600k records; should detect via database audit logs, proxy egress, or application query logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries returning >100k rows from beneficiary tables, or large data transfers (>1GB) from WFP SRA servers to external IPs/cloud storage. Correlate with non-standard service accounts and timestamp around May 14 breach window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Self-Registration Application - Credential Spray
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies SRA as attack surface: 'self-registration application... was breached.' Initial compromise likely involved credential brute-force or vulnerability exploitation; should detect anomalous authentication patterns and failed-to-successful login sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SRA login endpoints for rapid credential spray (>50 failed attempts → success within minutes), access from non-Gaza geolocations, or API calls to registration/beneficiary endpoints from anomalous source IPs. Flag successful logins using low-privilege or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Campaign Impersonating WFP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns beneficiaries: 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money.' This threat of follow-up phishing attacks is actionable and distinct from the initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with WFP-impersonating sender domains (typosquatting wfp.org), requesting password resets or re-registration from beneficiaries, especially targeting compromised phone numbers. Correlate with known beneficiary email patterns and alert on unusual sender reputation.

suggestion.title: Administrative or Privileged Account Abuse Against Registration Platform
suggestion.rationale: Breach required database-level access to extract 600k records. Should detect privilege escalation, lateral movement from a compromised web tier to backend database, or stolen service account credentials used for administrative queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database access from service accounts outside normal business logic (e.g., direct SELECT * on beneficiary table), privilege escalation of compromised user accounts, or access to SRA database from unexpected source IPs. Baseline normal DBA and application queries.

suggestion.title: Web Application Vulnerability Exploitation - SRA Endpoint Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states breach occurred on 'self-registration application.' Public-facing web applications are typical exploit vectors (SQL injection, auth bypass, RCE). Should detect exploitation attempts in WAF/IDS logs prior to or at breach timestamp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SQLi/path-traversal/auth-bypass payload attempts in WAF logs with database access anomalies on May 14. Focus on SRA API endpoints (`/api/registration`, `/beneficiary`, `/user`) and search for 400-499 errors followed by 200 responses indicating bypass.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Router acer_cgi.log
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface. This file contains cleartext login credentials.' Attackers gaining unauthenticated access to this specific log file should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST requests to router management interface (192.168.76.1, acerconnect.com) targeting /acer_cgi.log or similar paths without prior authentication tokens. Flag failed authentication followed by successful log file access. Baseline normal admin credential rotation patterns and flag plaintext credential strings in HTTP traffic post-access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious upload.cgi Access or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Access to or modification of backup files should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to upload.cgi endpoint without prior admin authentication. Monitor for backup file (.bin, .backup, .cfg) extraction or download attempts via router management interface. Detect file modification events on device backup partitions or firmware storage, especially writes that occur outside scheduled update windows.

suggestion.title: Extracted Plaintext Credentials Usage from Router
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials in acer_cgi.log can be extracted leading to 'unauthorized system access.' Detection should flag use of router-extracted credentials for Telnet or web console access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated log file access on router with subsequent Telnet login attempts or web console authentications from the same source IP or within minutes. Flag credential reuse across multiple sessions. Monitor for non-standard admin account creation post-backup access.

suggestion.title: Device Backup Decryption and Re-encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the hardcoded key vulnerability: 'attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' This cryptographic manipulation is a detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-entropy file writes to backup storage locations or temporary directories following upload.cgi access. Alert on unusual timing of backup extraction and upload operations (especially encryption operations on non-standard schedule). Flag attempts to read hardcoded keys from binary files or memory dumps of upload.cgi process.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Access Before Patches Released
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Acer customers are advised to disable remote management or, if the firmware allows, restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses.' Enabled remote management on unpatched routers is a significant risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Acer Wave 7 routers (T7c_GBL firmware versions ≤1.01.000055) with remote management enabled via port scans, vulnerability scans, or network telemetry. Alert on external IP ranges accessing router web interface before firmware patching completion (deadline: end of June 2026). Flag geographically anomalous access to router admin console.

suggestion.title: Modified FFmpeg DLL Execution from Game Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states trojanized FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) as vector: 'Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FFmpeg.dll loads from game directories (RenPy, RPG Maker) and correlate with immediate Base64 PowerShell spawning. Unsigned or anomalous FFmpeg imports are high-signal.

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 Hijacking – Windows Color System
suggestion.rationale: Article directly names persistence: 'replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL... triggered when the user logs in.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID and HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\Interface for InprocServer32 modifications. Alert on entries pointing outside System32 or to AppData/Temp paths.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Stage1 behavior: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell -EncodedCommand execution within 1-5 seconds of suspicious DLL loads. Filter on parent process originating from game/temp directories. Decode and scan for environment check commands.

suggestion.title: Delayed Multi-Stage Payload – DLL to Trojan Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sequential phasing: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' This multi-day dwell pattern is an attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track processes spawned from game executables or Stage1 PowerShell that remain dormant for 3+ days before initiating outbound network connections or child process execution. Alert on secondary executable retrieval.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game Archive – DLL + Binary Blob Combo
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies file pairing: 'archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL... that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor archive extraction (7z, zip, rar) to game directories. Alert on DLL + unnamed binary blob (.bin, .dat) pairings without legitimate game-engine associations. Check file creation timing clustering.

suggestion.title: Sandbox/VM Evasion Checks in PowerShell Stage1
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Stage1 'performs basic checks for controlled environments,' indicating explicit evasion logic deployed at execution time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor encoded PowerShell for WMI queries (Win32_ComputerSystemProduct), CPUID probing, Registry checks for VM artifacts (VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V keys), and debugger detection. Alert on evasion-pattern clustering.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE via EVAL/EVALSHA Script Injection (CVE-2026-23479)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-23479 as a Redis RCE flaw. RCE exploits unsafe Lua scripting (EVAL, EVALSHA commands) or serialization gadgets; pipeline produced no execution-phase detection for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor redis-server for unexpected child process creation or anomalous system calls. Flag RESP protocol frames containing EVAL, EVALSHA, or SCRIPT commands from external/untrusted sources. Correlate with shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned by redis-server PID following script execution.

suggestion.title: Inbound Network Exploitation of CVE-2026-23479
suggestion.rationale: A 2-year-old RCE flaw gaining sudden attention via autonomous AI discovery warrants network-layer detection. Pipeline missed reconnaissance and exploitation indicators targeting Redis ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections to Redis port 6379 (or non-standard Redis ports) from external IPs attempting EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT LOAD, or command-execution payloads within seconds of connection (before INFO/PING handshake). Correlate with known CVE-2026-23479 PoC signatures.

suggestion.title: Redis Authentication Bypass or Unauthenticated RCE
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-23479 likely involves bypassing requirepass authentication or targeting unprotected Redis instances. Pipeline did not detect AUTH evasion or code execution without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TCP connections to Redis (6379+) that skip AUTH entirely and immediately issue code-execution commands. Monitor for repeated AUTH failures followed by successful exploitation. Detect redis-cli or custom binaries connecting without credentials from non-admin subnets or external sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised Redis
suggestion.rationale: Article frames flaw as 2-year-old and recently discovered, implying live exploitation risk. Impact phase should detect lateral movement after RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on redis-server spawning reverse shells, curl/wget, or known pivot/exfil tools post-compromise. Monitor for unusual process lineage: redis-server → bash → ssh/scp/nc. Detect redis-server making outbound connections to non-standard ports or C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CacheWarmer Serialized PHP Object Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' This is a specific, observable behavioral signature requiring direct detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing CacheWarmer cookie values with PHP serialization prefixes (e.g., 'O:', 'C:', 'R:' indicating object/class/reference serialization). Flag unauthenticated requests from external sources with serialized payloads to Mirasvit endpoints.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CVE-2026-45247 Unauthenticated RCE Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attackers' achieving 'remote code execution'—this zero-auth RCE combination warrants distinct detection correlating HTTP exploitation attempts with post-exploit process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST/GET requests to Mirasvit endpoints lacking authentication headers with subsequent child process spawning from web server/PHP parent processes. Monitor for shell execution, reverse shells, or suspicious command execution immediately following CacheWarmer cookie requests.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries target actively exploited vulnerabilities on exposed systems. Article names 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer' as product—requires inventory scan matching federal patch deadline (2026-06-06).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network telemetry and vulnerability scanner results for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installations. Match on application fingerprints (HTTP response headers, cookies, server banners), cross-reference with CVE-2026-45247 patch status, flag unpatched instances on internet-facing systems.

suggestion.title: PHP Untrusted Deserialization Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability class 'deserialization of untrusted data' is a known PHP exploitation vector beyond this CVE. Generic signature detection captures variants and related exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic for PHP object serialization patterns in POST bodies, query strings, and cookie headers. Alert on serialized objects with gadget chain indicators or suspicious class instantiation attempts in requests to public-facing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Privilege Escalation (No User Interaction)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework' affecting Android 14-16 with 'requires no user interaction to exploit' enabling privilege escalation. Pipeline generated zero Android exploitation detections despite active exploitation implied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android processes for unexpected system call sequences, integer boundary violations in framework calls, or privilege transitions (UID/GID changes) without corresponding user interaction events (input, gesture, IME). Flag suspicious behavior from apps targeting Android 14-16 with kernel-level permissions.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CVE-2022-0492 cgroup v1 Namespace Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability where 'local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system' affecting cgroups v1. This is a critical container-escape vector with zero detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to cgroup_release_agent files from processes running in container namespaces, or privilege escalation (UID 0 transitions) from unprivileged container processes. Alert on host processes spawned with parent PID originating from container process namespace.

suggestion.title: cgroup_release_agent_write() Function Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article pinpoints 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' function in cgroups v1 with 'insufficient authentication checks' as exploitation vector. Specific function name and mechanism provided but zero technical detection rules derived.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write() syscalls targeting /proc/*/cgroup or cgroup filesystem paths, specifically writes to cgroup.event_control or release_agent paths from non-root processes. Correlate with subsequent shell command execution in unrelated process context (escaping container namespace).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Linux Kernel Host Privilege Escalation (CVE-2022-0492 Versions)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable kernel branches (2.6-4.20, 5.5-5.17) and patched versions (4.9.301+, 5.15.20+, etc.), enabling version-based risk scoring and behavioral thresholds. Pipeline failed to create version-aware detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint kernel version from running host. For unpatched versions matching 5.5-5.17 or 2.6-4.20 ranges, lower detection thresholds for privilege escalation and container-escape behavioral patterns. Flag any suspicious cgroup manipulation on known-vulnerable kernels as high-confidence.

suggestion.title: Android 14-16 Framework Exploitation (Patch Levels 2026-06-01, 2026-06-05)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'June 2026 security patches (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 security patch levels)' as remediation. Pipeline missed opportunity to correlate unpatched device inventory with exploitation detection thresholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Android 14-16 devices running patch levels prior to 2026-06-01 (or 2026-06-05 for specific variants) exhibiting privilege escalation activity, integer overflow symptoms in framework logs, or unexpected system capability acquisition.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST request with KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID in request body
suggestion.rationale: Article states bypass is 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value.' The hunts provided lack parameter-level specificity; should detect the actual malicious parameters, not just all POST requests to the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoint where request body contains KERNEL_UID=0, KERNEL_GID=0, or non-numeric bypass-attempt patterns. Correlate with subsequent pod creation as root to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Kernel pod created with SYS_ADMIN or host-escape capabilities from enterprise-gateway SA
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1611 (Escape to Host) but provided hunts detect post-escape persistence, not the escape capability acquisition itself. Article narrative emphasizes container privilege context; should detect pods requesting CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pod creation in k8s_audit where requestObject.spec.containers[].securityContext.capabilities.add contains SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, or SYS_PTRACE, AND created by enterprise-gateway service account, AND correlates with prior /api/kernels POST.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway pod escapes containment: process execution in host namespace or privileged mode
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1611 and UC_33_3 describe escape path via hostPath volumes; should also detect active escape indicators such as container processes escaping to host PID/network namespace or requesting privileged mode.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in runc/containerd) executing commands outside container namespace or accessing /proc/[pid]/ns/net from host. Alternatively, detect pod creation with hostNetwork=true AND hostPID=true AND hostIPC=true.

suggestion.title: Forensic: Jupyter kernel pod environment variable inspection for KERNEL_UID bypass evidence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass using 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value'; this would be preserved in pod spec and describe API request logs. Pipeline should suggest detection of env vars containing escape-bypass payloads or unusual UID/GID values in kernel pod configs post-creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query k8s_audit audit logs for pod creation events where spec.containers[].env[] contains KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID with non-standard values or special characters suggesting bypass attempt. Cross-reference with securityContext.runAsUser in same pod spec.

suggestion.title: UC_32_1: Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection'—pipeline extracted zero use cases despite article providing complete Splunk SPL and Defender KQL for this exploit-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoints for Jinja2 template markers ({{ }}, {%...%}) combined with Python introspection patterns (__globals__, __class__, __mro__, __builtins__, cycler.__init__) or OS command methods (os.popen, os.system, subprocess). Correlate by source IP and track timing for incident attribution.

suggestion.title: UC_32_2: Enterprise Gateway service account creates privileged/hostPath/RBAC-escalating Kubernetes resources
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'—post-exploitation phase where the compromised gateway pivots to K8s API abuse is explicitly described in article's recommended hunts but pipeline surfaced zero detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pod, rolebinding, or clusterrolebinding creation/modification by the enterprise-gateway service account where manifests contain privileged: true, hostPath mounts, hostNetwork: true, or hostPID: true. Alert on RBAC modifications that escalate the service account's own permissions.

suggestion.title: UC_32_3: Enterprise Gateway Python process spawns shell or reads Kubernetes service-account token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Python code execution via SSTI 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'—RCE post-compromise child process and credential access are essential detections but pipeline produced zero process-level hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (sh, bash, curl, wget, kubectl, nc) spawned under python/python3 parents, or any process reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Filter to containers with 'enterprise-gateway', 'jupyter', or 'jeg' in name. High-fidelity indicator of SSTI→RCE chain completion.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 SSTI attempt blocked or logged in WAF/API gateway (pre-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies KERNEL_XXX environment variables as the injection point—intermediate detection of Jinja2 syntax in request payloads before reaching the templating engine provides defense-in-depth and earliest possible alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Enterprise Gateway endpoints containing Jinja2 filter chains known to bypass sandbox isolation (e.g., cycler, lipsum). Baseline legitimate API schema against malicious payload patterns. Track blocked attempts separately from detected-but-allowed; the latter indicates WAF misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes service account token read or exfiltration from container (post-RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that stolen tokens are 'powerful' for cluster escalation—detection of the token being read from disk or transmitted over network post-compromise is not explicitly covered in article hunts despite being critical for incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token from non-privileged processes or processes not in the control plane. Correlate with outbound network traffic patterns (exfil). Track Kubernetes API calls authenticated with the enterprise-gateway service account from unusual source IPs or with verb/resource patterns abnormal for Enterprise Gateway workload.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes manifest with injected YAML delimiters in KERNEL_* environment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'environment variables used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest allow YAML injection' and 'inject multi-document YAML.' Detection should hunt for KERNEL_* variables containing YAML document separators (--- or ...) or securityContext keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Kubernetes API audit logs and Enterprise Gateway container logs for POST requests to /api/kernels where request body or environment variables contain KERNEL_* parameters with YAML delimiters (---, ...) or securityContext field references. Correlate with pod creation from the enterprise-gateway service account within seconds.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 template rendering exceptions or YAML parse failures in Jupyter Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Malicious YAML injection may trigger template parsing errors or YAML parsing exceptions. Article describes interpolation of 'untrusted environment variables' into manifests—failed parsing is a sign of attack attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Jinja2 TemplateError, YAML ParserError, or manifest validation failures in Enterprise Gateway pod logs correlating with /api/kernels POST requests within the same time window. High precision if combined with URL pattern match.

suggestion.title: Multi-document Kubernetes manifests created by enterprise-gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'inject multi-document YAML to create additional unintended Kubernetes resources.' This is the actual impact—creation of extra pods or resources beyond the intended one.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Kubernetes API for create/patch operations on pods, deployments, or daemonsets from the enterprise-gateway service account where the manifest contains multiple YAML documents (detectable via '---' separators in requestObject). Anomaly: single API call producing multiple child resources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious securityContext escalation in pod specs from Jupyter Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes overwriting securityContext to enable privilege escalation. Detect pods created by EG with privileged:true, runAsUser:0, runAsGroup:0, hostNetwork:true, or hostPID:true—especially if these differ from prior baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Kubernetes audit logs for pod creation from enterprise-gateway service account where securityContext.privileged=true, securityContext.runAsUser=0, or hostNetwork=true. Cross-reference against enterprise-gateway's normal pod specs in the same namespace to detect deviations.

suggestion.title: Escape-to-host indicators from Jupyter Enterprise Gateway pods
suggestion.rationale: T1611 is mapped in the article but no hunt directly targets container escape. Exploit creates privileged pods that can attempt escape. Monitor for suspicious host filesystem access, privileged syscalls, or kernel module loading from EG pod context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for privileged pods created by enterprise-gateway attempting to mount host paths (/proc, /sys, /dev, /host), execute privileged operations (iptables, insmod), or issue escape-related syscalls (clone with CLONE_NEWNS/CLONE_NEWPID). Pair with pod-creation audit events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44182 vulnerability scan results or patch-gap assessment
suggestion.rationale: Primary recon-phase indicator: enumerate hosts running vulnerable Jupyter Enterprise Gateway versions. Article CVE and version information enable asset-scoped detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results, container image inventories, and application inventory for Jupyter Enterprise Gateway versions prior to the patched release. Cross-reference image digests and pod specs in audit logs to confirm runtime exposure.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious Link to TA4922 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Phishing Attacks' as attack vector; no use case generated despite this being primary initial access method for TA4922.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with suspicious links pointing to TA4922-attributed domains or IP infrastructure. Look for sender spoofing patterns matching targets in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa regions, and URL rewrite/redirect patterns common in phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks typically culminate in credential theft; article describes 'expanded' campaign suggesting credential harvesting intent, but no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to credential harvesting landing pages mimicking legitimate services targeted at the four countries. Detect form submissions with username/password pairs to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload Delivery Post-Click
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'expands' phishing attacks; multi-stage phishing with secondary payload (malware) is standard TA4922 progression, but no malware-related detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads and execution of suspicious files from phishing redirects, focusing on Office macro-enabled documents, ISO/IMG archives, or obfuscated scripts common in TA4922 campaigns targeting regional targets.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Domain Registration Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted despite article clearly identifying threat actor TA4922; domain infrastructure and registration patterns are foundational IOCs missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and registrations of domains matching TA4922 known patterns (homoglyphs, typosquatting legitimate UK/German/Italian/South African entities). Cross-reference against passive DNS and WHOIS history.

suggestion.title: Geographic Targeting Signal - Regional Language Phishing Content
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names four target countries (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa); no geo-specific detection generated to identify localized phishing content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate incoming phishing emails with language/locale indicators, business entity spoofing, and currency/regulatory references specific to UK (GBP, FCA), Germany (EUR, BaFin), Italy (EUR, Consob), South Africa (ZAR, FSCA). Flag campaigns targeting all four simultaneously as high-confidence TA4922 indicator.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' — direct signal of weaponized threat and imminent exploitation attempts against Cisco Unified CM. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite CRIT severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco Unified CM admin interfaces (ports 8080, 8443) for payloads matching CVE-2026-20230 signatures. Alert on HTTP 400/500 error sequences following suspicious parameter injection to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Admin Account Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' implies widespread exploitation and attacker persistence attempts. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection for unauthorized admin account creation in Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM audit logs for unexpected admin/super-user account creation outside change-control windows. Alert on privilege grants within 1 hour of detected exploitation attempts or reconnaissance activity against Unified CM.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230' — explicit signal to track patching status. Pipeline failed to generate detection use case for patch deployment verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco Unified CM versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20230 (versions prior to patch release date). Flag unpatched instances in production environments. Monitor version strings for obfuscation or timestamp manipulation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Scanning for Cisco Unified CM Instances
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' establishes scanning phase precedes exploitation. Pipeline generated zero discovery-phase detections despite clear attacker motivation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting TCP 8080/8443 from external/untrusted sources. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS probes to /ccmadmin, /admin endpoints. Track scanning patterns consistent with Unified CM enumeration (multiple targets, repeated similar probes).

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Configuration and Voicemail Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' establishes breach probability and attacker incentive to exfiltrate sensitive voice/config data. Pipeline did not model exfiltration-phase behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound SFTP/SCP/HTTP transfers from Cisco Unified CM servers to external IPs. Alert on backup/export command execution (mysqldump, tar, database exports) outside scheduled maintenance. Track large data transfers containing voice files or XML configurations.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Remote Code Execution via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20230 type vulnerabilities involve web RCE. Title establishes code execution as primary attack vector; pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from Cisco Unified CM application processes (Java/Tomcat). Alert on shell invocation (bash, cmd, powershell) from Unified CM service account. Correlate HTTP admin-interface access with child process creation events.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM SSRF HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' WebDialer endpoints should be monitored for anomalous HTTP patterns and SSRF indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer service endpoints for SSRF patterns (requests targeting internal addresses, unusual URIs, or suspicious headers). Focus on requests that deviate from normal dialer workflows (non-standard query strings, file:// URIs, local service probes).

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service File Write Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' File creation by the WebDialer service should be monitored for suspicious paths and timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification by the Cisco WebDialer process (or its child processes) in sensitive OS directories (/etc, /root, /var/spool/cron, system startup folders). Alert on files that map to known privilege-escalation vectors or have suspicious ownership changes.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation via Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article states privilege escalation outcome: 'A successful exploit could...elevate to root.' Escalation events following WebDialer activity should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (UID 0 or root group assignment) initiated by or correlated with Cisco Unified CM processes. Alert on sudo/su calls, capability escalations, or setuid binary execution that follow anomalous WebDialer HTTP activity within a short time window.
