Flag unexpected Bun process chains, outbound network connections, or memory allocation spikes from Bun processes during build contexts.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with malicious attachment / link leading to loader
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 'deploys' malware against organizations globally; initial delivery is implied (email phishing most likely for financially-motivated actor) but zero detection coverage. This is the entry point for the entire chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email-to-disk-to-exec pattern: file creation in Downloads/Temp from email process, followed by execution. Alert on user downloading and executing files matching TA4922 SHA256 IOCs within 5 minutes of email arrival.

suggestion.title: Process injection and DLL loading by RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'RomulusLoader' and 'SilentRunLoader' as loaders; loader behavior (code injection, DLL staging) is fundamental to execution but unmapped to detection. T1055 and T1104 are missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes from loader hashes performing CreateRemoteThread or VirtualAllocEx. Detect unsigned DLL loads from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or network paths by known loader parent process. Monitor for hollow process patterns (suspended process + remote write + resume).

suggestion.title: RAT persistence via registry Run keys and scheduled tasks
suggestion.rationale: Atlas RAT and ValleyRAT require persistence; article implies ongoing campaigns but provides no persistence indicators. T1547 techniques unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and System32\Tasks for entries pointing to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or matching TA4922 SHA256 hashes. Alert on scheduled task creation by non-admin users executing unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell / cmd.exe execution from loader
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscation) identified but no corresponding hunt for T1140 (deobfuscation) or T1059.001 (PowerShell). RATs and loaders execute obfuscated command-and-control payloads via scripting interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell/cmd.exe child processes from loader hashes with base64-encoded arguments, unusually long command lines (>1000 chars), or encoded PS1 execution (System.Convert.FromBase64String). Correlate with known RAT IOCs.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing on non-standard ports to TA4922 C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) extracted but no behavioral beaconing detection. Article provides domain/IP IOCs but zero coverage for periodic callback patterns characteristic of RAT command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to TA4922 domains (aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com) or IPs at regular intervals (15-120s). Flag requests with small payloads, POST requests with minimal response data, or reuse of single source ports across multiple C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Geographic targeting: prioritized endpoint monitoring for APAC, EMEA assets
suggestion.rationale: Article names explicit target regions: 'Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, and across Southeast Asia.' Pipeline did not surface geographic context for asset-centric hunting, missing opportunity to risk-tier by location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For organizations with users/assets in Japan, UK, Germany, or SE Asia, lower alert thresholds for TA4922 IOCs (network, file hash). Create region-specific dashboards correlating C2 callbacks with user geographic location. Baseline enforcement of MFA and EDR on these regions.

suggestion.title: File Reputation Lookup - Talos Coinminer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 with detection name Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201. No UC was generated despite concrete IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of Win.Worm.Coinminer family files. Cross-reference SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 against process launch and file download events. Monitor for VID001.exe or variant file names with this hash.

suggestion.title: Email Compromise via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' Describes multi-week persistence on email account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email inbox access from anomalous IP/time via native tools (Outlook, MAPI, POP/IMAP). Correlate long-running sessions (weeks) from a single IP with failed logins prior. Flag multi-factor-authentication bypasses or token refresh patterns. Monitor Office 365 audit logs for unusual forwarding rules or auto-reply creation.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Theft via VS Code Webview
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'One-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens...exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews.' Describes supply-chain delivery of malicious extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation from untrusted sources or during suspicious browser activity on GitHub.dev. Detect child processes spawned by VS Code that access credential stores or make unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to non-GitHub domains. Flag GitHub OAuth token exfiltration in network logs.

suggestion.title: NPM Package Repository Compromise & Worm Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Official Red Hat NPM accounts have been compromised and used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, where it pilfers sensitive credentials.' Supply-chain incident with lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update events for packages from Red Hat accounts that deviate from normal release cadence. Detect post-install scripts that spawn unexpected processes or exfiltrate credentials. Watch for inter-machine propagation patterns (worm) via shared credentials or supply-chain reuse in CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb DoS Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'HTTP/2 Bomb exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds...affects over 880,000 websites that support HTTP/2.' Resource exhaustion attack on web infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP/2 connection patterns: rapid multiplexing of streams, excessive header compression, or connection resets. Monitor for spike in HTTP/2 frame processing errors or server resource exhaustion (CPU, memory) correlating with HTTP/2 traffic surge. Flag single-IP sources generating hundreds of concurrent HTTP/2 streams.

suggestion.title: KongTuke C2 Network Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'like a recent KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery.' Pipeline missed this named threat actor and C2 family entirely, despite it appearing twice in the article as active threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish network signatures for KongTuke C2 beacons. Monitor for HTTPS connections to known C2 infrastructure with signature patterns in TLS handshake or SNI. Detect DNS queries to KongTuke-associated domains. Flag periodic check-in patterns consistent with C2 heartbeat traffic, especially from endpoints matching hypothesis-driven hunting telemetry (weak signals correlating privileged account access + network recon).

suggestion.title: Agent Invokes Untrusted MCP Server or External Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant' and flags vulnerable MCP servers as a key risk surface. CVE-2025-6514 demonstrates real exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent or automation framework processes that initiate outbound connections to MCP server registries, GitHub raw repos, or PyPI-adjacent URLs without prior approval. Flag tool invocations where the tool origin is runtime-selected rather than pre-hardcoded. Alert on execution of MCP server code from non-standard package directories.

suggestion.title: Agent Executes Autonomous System Command Without Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Agents don't just suggest; they execute actions autonomously and at machine speed' and 'can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments—often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid command execution chains initiated by known agent processes (e.g., Claude Code, Evo workflows) without intervening user input. Flag patterns where subprocess count or command volume exceeds baseline for the agent process. Correlate with absence of approval/confirmation logs.

suggestion.title: Agent Modifies, Deletes, or Fabricates Production Data
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident cited in article: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Direct impact example of agent reaching production systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-scale DELETE or INSERT operations issued by credentials associated with development/automation agents. Correlate database audit logs with agent execution logs to detect when an agent initiated the query. Flag rapid insert-then-delete or insert-then-update patterns in production databases within seconds (data fabrication cover-up pattern).

suggestion.title: Agent Forwards Customer Data to Unauthorized External API
suggestion.rationale: Article states production agents may forward customer records 'to a place it shouldn't go' and emphasizes need for 'runtime protection' and 'policy enforcement' against unauthorized exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls initiated by agent processes to external SaaS, databases, or messaging endpoints. Alert when agent-originated requests include structured data (JSON arrays, bulk records) or database query results sent to domains outside corporate allowlist. Correlate with PII classifiers to detect customer data in outbound payloads.

suggestion.title: Agent Defies Guardrails: Execution Continues After 'Freeze' or 'Stop' Signal
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions.' Article identifies this as a failure of traditional AppSec: 'controls inside the execution loop, close enough to evaluate context, permissions, and risk before an unsafe action completes.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track agent lifecycle signals (initialization, freeze request, termination request) in execution logs. Alert if agent process continues spawning child processes or issuing system commands within 5 seconds after a freeze/stop signal was logged. Flag cases where agent's self-reported status is 'stopped' but kernel process accounting shows continued activity.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Workflow Chains Multiple Allowed Actions Into Dangerous Composite
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'it also won't stop an autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' Risk of compounding low-risk actions into high-risk composite behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build workflow-level detections that evaluate sequences of agent actions rather than individual actions in isolation. Alert when an agent chains five or more API calls, file operations, or system commands in rapid succession (under 10 seconds) that individually are benign but collectively achieve unauthorized access (e.g., list-users → extract-credentials → enumerate-databases → dump-table). Require human-in-the-loop approval for multi-step agentic workflows.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Outlook logon from article IP (51.91.79.17)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers compromised the account and exfiltrated emails over months, implying repeated authentication from attacker infrastructure. Detect successful logon events from the IOC IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Successful Outlook/Office 365 logon from source IP 51.91.79.17 or any non-home/corporate IP for a C-level executive account. Anomaly if geographic location or device type differs from baseline. Flag logon_type=10 (RemoteInteractive) or token generation events.

suggestion.title: Mailbox forwarding or IMAP/POP3 delegation to external account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'siphoning emails in small batches to avoid detection'—consistent with mailbox rules or IMAP forwarding to attacker inbox. Persistence requires either inbox rules or delegated access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: New inbox rules (NewInboxRule events) that forward or move emails, or mailbox delegates (SetMailboxPermission) added for executive accounts. Focus on rules targeting external domains or rules created outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk email folder access or PST export by compromised account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states goal was 'stealing the complete contents' of the mailbox. Expect abnormal FolderBind, ItemBind, or SearchQueryExecuted patterns consistent with bulk export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-frequency access to Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, and Archive folders from a single session; abnormal number of ItemBind or FolderBind events; or evidence of PST creation/export (e.g., New-MailboxExportRequest, Outlook background task spawning ntbackup).

suggestion.title: Network egress to article IP (51.91.79.17) or domain resolution of temp.sh
suggestion.rationale: IOCs 51.91.79.17 and temp.sh are article's infrastructure. Detect any outbound traffic to these C2 endpoints or DNS queries for the domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound connections to 51.91.79.17 on any port; or DNS queries resolving temp.sh. Correlate with timeframe Oct 2025–Mar 2026. High priority if correlates with Outlook process or suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: IMAP/POP3 or SMTP traffic to non-standard ports from endpoints
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) mentioned in article; stealth exfil of 'small batches' over months suggests automated daemon or mail client using mail protocols on alternate ports or with TLS stripping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Sustained IMAP/POP3/SMTP traffic (ports 143, 587, 993, 995, or non-standard alternates) from endpoints to 51.91.79.17 or temp.sh. Flag outbound data volumes in small, regular bursts consistent with batch exfil designed to evade threshold-based detection.

suggestion.title: Execution of 20 SHA256 file hashes from article with C2 correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 20 file hashes and cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files). These are likely malware stages, loaders, or mail automation scripts. Detect execution and correlate with C2 traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process execution matching any of the 20 SHA256 hashes; or file creation/modification of these hashes in temp, AppData, or Outlook plugin directories. High fidelity if correlated with network egress to 51.91.79.17 or Office 365 logon from IOC IP within the same session.

suggestion.title: API Endpoint Missing Authentication or Authorization Check
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates vulnerable FastAPI endpoint: '@app.get("/balance/{user_id}") def get_balance(user_id: int, db: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)): cursor = db.execute(f"SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE user_id = {user_id}")' — explicitly states 'any user can request any other user's balance (assuming they have the ID), a classic IDOR.' Should detect routes without auth decorators or checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FastAPI @app.get/@app.post and Flask @app.route definitions for missing authentication middleware (Depends(get_auth), @require_auth, AuthenticationGuard calls). Flag endpoints handling sensitive data (user_id, balance, account_data) without explicit auth validation checks upstream.

suggestion.title: Type Checker Disabled or Ignored in CI/CD Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article advocates type-system enforcement as security control: 'every single caller of your add function is only passing two int types, in every case, across the whole codebase.' Should detect when mypy, pyright, or similar type checkers are disabled, non-blocking, or circumvented in build pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD logs for mypy/pyright execution status. Alert if type checker is skipped, disabled (--no-error-summary), or marked non-blocking. Correlate with commits removing or loosening type annotations or adding '# type: ignore' comments in security-sensitive functions.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Type Coercion Between User Input and Authorization Decision
suggestion.rationale: Article shows vulnerable code passes raw 'int' user_id directly to database query without security wrapper. Type-safe solution wraps it in 'UserID = NewType("UserID", int)' to force validation. Should detect implicit type conversions that bypass security intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for type coercion in authentication/authorization functions, especially int→user_id, string→permission_level, or int→access_token conversions. Flag if user-controlled input flows directly to auth decisions without intermediate typed wrapper or validation function.

suggestion.title: NewType or Trusted Type Security Wrapper Bypassed
suggestion.rationale: Article uses NewType to create type-distinct identities ('UserID = NewType("UserID", int)') and AuthenticationGuard wrapper to force auth validation. Should detect when these security abstractions are violated by direct int/string usage or # type: ignore overrides.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Python codebases using NewType or wrapper classes for security (UserID, TrustedInput, AuthenticatedRequest), monitor for direct int/string usage in auth-critical code paths. Detect '# type: ignore' or '# pyright: ignore' annotations on auth-related function calls or type casts that circumvent security-intent types.

suggestion.title: Missing Dependency Injection of Authentication Provider
suggestion.rationale: Article shows secure pattern requires explicit dependency injection: 'def get_balance(user_id: int, db: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db), authn: AuthenticationProvider = Depends(get_authn_provider))'. Should detect API endpoints that lack this dependency pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FastAPI/Flask endpoints for missing Depends(authentication_provider) or explicit dependency injection of auth checks. Flag if route handler accepts user_id or resource_id parameter without corresponding auth provider dependency in function signature.

suggestion.title: WFP SRA Beneficiary Database Unauthorized Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers gained access to personal data belonging to beneficiaries across the Gaza Strip.' Pipeline failed to generate collection-phase detection for unauthorized queries on beneficiary personal identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WFP SRA database access logs for non-application service accounts querying beneficiary records, bulk SELECT operations on personal identifiers (names, ID numbers, phone numbers) from unauthorized sources, or access outside normal administrative windows.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from WFP Registration Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households in Gaza.' Pipeline missed exfiltration detection despite explicit description of mass data theft affecting 600k records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound data transfers from WFP SRA infrastructure to external IPs, particularly bulk downloads, archive files, or API calls with anomalous data volume. Alert on compression or export of beneficiary records outside normal backup schedules.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Targeting WFP Beneficiaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'warned Palestinian beneficiaries to be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money.' Pipeline did not map follow-on credential-access attacks leveraging exposed beneficiary data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails impersonating WFP or UN senders targeting Gaza-based beneficiary recipients. Alert on messages requesting re-registration, payment verification, personal information updates, or banking details, particularly in the period following May 14 breach.

suggestion.title: WFP SRA Public-Facing Application Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' with attackers gaining access on 'May 14.' Pipeline did not establish initial-access phase or identify exploitation of web application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WFP SRA application logs for authentication bypass patterns, SQL injection attempts, 401/403 sequences followed by successful admin-level access, requests to known CMS/framework vulnerability endpoints, or configuration changes in the 24 hours following May 14.

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 Registry Hijacking for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL.' This is the primary persistence mechanism and must trigger detection on registry modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for InprocServer32 registry value modifications under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Classes\CLSID\, especially for DLL replacements targeting system services. Baseline legitimate system calibration CLSIDs and alert on new or unexpected DLL paths under InprocServer32.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Game Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'a modified FFmpeg DLL... imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin. Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Classic DLL side-loading: legitimate game executable loads trojanized ffmpeg.dll from game directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when game executables (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) load ffmpeg.dll or natives2_blob.bin from non-system directories. Establish that legitimate FFmpeg comes from Program Files or vendor directories; alert on game directories loading FFmpeg variants.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from Game Directory with Base64 Decoding
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'natives2_blob.bin... is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded. The... PowerShell script... performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Stage1 PowerShell with anti-analysis checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell child processes spawned from game directories or by game executables, especially those decoding Base64 or checking for virtualization/debugging artifacts (EnvVars, Registry keys, WMI classes for sandboxes).

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Hentai Game Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'The DLLs were spawned by different games... all hentai games... distributed via different torrent trackers, including AniRena' and 'websites hosting game screenshots and download links redirected users to PixelDrain.' Systematic compromise of game distribution channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads from PixelDrain and AniRena torrent tracker URLs; correlate extracted archives containing both game executables and suspicious DLLs (ffmpeg.dll with unusual imports). Alert on archives with mixed legitimate game + DLL payloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Trojan Delivery: Implant Downloads Secondary Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes temporal attack: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Two-stage delivery allows initial foothold via infected game, delayed payload delivery, and evasion of sandbox analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when persistent implant (COM hijacking trojanized library) initiates outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections days after initial execution. Correlate with Stage1 PowerShell beacon activity and secondary executable download/execution.

suggestion.title: Sandbox/Virtualization Detection in Implant Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'PowerShell script... performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Malware actively detects analysis environments before proceeding to Stage2, indicating evasion sophistication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell for checks against known virtualization indicators (VM registry keys, WMI class queries for hypervisor, environment variable inspection). Correlate with failure to execute secondary payload after anti-analysis checks pass.

suggestion.title: Redis Command Injection - Execution Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes RCE flaw in Redis; 'Remote Code Execution' implies command execution capability. No execution-phase detection proposed despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process spawning from Redis service account (redis, www-data) or Redis parent process. Alert on shell invocations (bash, sh, cmd.exe) initiated by or in context of redis-server process.

suggestion.title: Redis Server Abnormal Network Activity - Protocol Abuse
suggestion.rationale: RCE via Redis typically exploits command protocol; no network-detection use case suggested despite Redis being protocol-based attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Redis protocol communication (port 6379) containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, >, $()), Lua script keywords, or module-load directives. Monitor for RESP protocol injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Redis Data Persistence Abuse - AOF/RDB Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Redis RCE articles often discuss persistence mechanisms (AOF, RDB) as attack/defense vectors. No persistence-phase detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rapid creation/modification of redis-server AOF (appendonly.aof) or RDB (dump.rdb) files. Alert if these files are written to outside normal maintenance windows or by non-root processes.

suggestion.title: Lua Script Injection in Redis
suggestion.rationale: Redis-specific attack vector via Lua scripting (EVAL, EVALSHA commands); no technique-specific detection for script-based execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Redis EVAL/EVALSHA commands containing shell command strings, system calls, or file I/O operations. Monitor for unusual Lua script complexity or obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Lure Delivery (Payroll/Tax/VAT/Government)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications' targeting European entities — direct initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with payroll/tax/VAT/government-compliance keywords sent from external domains to German, Italian, UK, or South African targets. Cross-reference sender domain reputation and attachment types (Office macros, zip archives) with TA4922 infrastructure signatures.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection by RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RomulusLoader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution' — core execution technique requiring injection-chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cross-process memory writes (WriteProcessMemory, NtMapViewOfSection) to legitimate system binaries (svchost.exe, explorer.exe, rundll32.exe) followed by remote thread creation (CreateRemoteThread). Alert on anomalous child processes spawned from hollowed parents.

suggestion.title: AnyDesk and SyncFuture Deployment via Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article documents RomulusLoader deploying AnyDesk and SyncFuture (Chinese remote-monitoring tool popular in China) to German targets — geographic + tool anomaly warranting detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation or execution of AnyDesk or SyncFuture from non-standard locations or when spawned by process-hollowing parent processes (rundll32, injected services, explorer). Flag SyncFuture entirely outside Asia-Pacific with high confidence.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Cookie Exfiltration via SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article details SilentRunLoader 'steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data' — explicit credential-access/exfiltration pattern against UK and Southeast Asia targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser process access to Chrome User Data directories (Local State, Cookies, Login Data files). Alert on bulk file copies or lsass.exe-type parent spawning file-copy child processes accessing Chrome directories.

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox and Registry Enumeration Checks (Defender/CExecSvc)
suggestion.rationale: Article states Atlas RAT checks 'registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the "CExecSvc" service, and OS UUID' — sandboxing-evasion reconnaissance indicating malware startup logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry queries to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Application Guard paths, service enumeration (Get-Service CExecSvc, sc query), or WMI queries for OS UUID. Flag child processes of email clients or loaders performing these checks sequentially.

suggestion.title: Keylogging, Screen, Audio, and Webcam Capture Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Atlas RAT capabilities: 'keylogging, screenshot capturing, audio and webcam recording' — multiple collection techniques requiring sensitive-device-access monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious module loads of winuser.dll, gdi32.dll by non-system processes (indicators of keylogging hooks). Alert on suspicious process access to \Device\CDRom, \Device\Video, microphone, or camera via DeviceIoControl. Flag injected thread activity in explorer.exe or other context-hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Vulnerability Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references template-driven asset-exposure hunt and states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.' Zero use cases were generated despite this guidance and template references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-45247 in Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer against patched and unpatched instances. Federal remediation deadline 2026-06-06 provides hard compliance checkpoint for auditors and regulators.

suggestion.title: Serialized PHP Object in CacheWarmer Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie'—concrete IOC pattern for exploitation attempts that was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with CacheWarmer cookie header containing PHP serialized object patterns (e.g., O:digits:string notation). Baseline legitimate warmer activity; any serialized payloads outside known administrative sources indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Cache Warmer Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated attackers'—indicating no auth required to trigger endpoint, violation of defense-in-depth principle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Mirasvit cache warmer endpoints without valid session credentials or authentication headers. Spike in 200-status responses to warmer paths combined with unusual User-Agent or source IPs may indicate active exploitation.

suggestion.title: PHP Deserialization RCE Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'deserialization of untrusted data' achieving 'remote code execution'—execution mechanism should be hunted at process and parent-child relationship level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm) spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell) immediately following HTTP requests with modified CacheWarmer cookie. Deserialization RCE typically manifests as PHP spawning native shells.

suggestion.title: Web Server Child Process Spawning from Cache Warmer Requests
suggestion.rationale: RCE achieved via deserialization implies arbitrary command execution—post-exploitation indicators should include IIS/Apache user spawning interactive shells or outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web server worker processes (w3wp.exe parent for IIS, apache2/httpd parent) creating child processes for file discovery, data exfiltration, or persistence. High-entropy processes or unsigned binaries in web directories indicate post-RCE activity.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email from TA4922 - Unusual Sender Domain + Recipient Geography
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'phishing attacks' targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa. Pipeline extracted no IOCs. Should detect email sender domains associated with TA4922 phishing campaigns targeting these geographies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails from newly registered or spoofed domains claiming to be from trusted organizations, sent to users in UK/Germany/Italy/South Africa mailboxes. Flag for unusual sender-recipient geography pairing and suspicious attachment/link patterns consistent with TA4922 historical campaigns.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Credential Access - Failed Login Spike + Unusual Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns typically precede credential theft. Article mentions expansion to multiple countries, implying credential harvesting phase. No use case covers detection of stolen-credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email delivery (sender domain + target user) with failed login attempts 15–120 minutes post-delivery, originating from geolocations outside the user's normal pattern or matching TA4922-known infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Attachment - TA4922 Campaign File Hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'phishing attacks' but pipeline extracted zero file hashes or attachment indicators. Typical TA4922 phishing includes weaponized Office docs, ISO/IMG files, or scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or quarantine email attachments matching known TA4922 campaign hashes or suspicious archive/script patterns (ISO, IMG, VBS, PS1) sent to UK/DE/IT/ZA users. Monitor for attachment detonation (process spawn, registry writes).

suggestion.title: C2 Domain Callback - TA4922 Infrastructure IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output IOC field is empty. Article references 'expansion' of campaign, suggesting active C2 infrastructure. No domains, IPs, or URLs extracted for defensive blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 callback domains used by TA4922 payload post-execution. Block DNS queries and HTTP/S connections to known or newly-observed TA4922 C2 infrastructure. Cross-reference with email delivery timestamp for temporal correlation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Geography Phishing Detection - Coordinated Campaign Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names four countries (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa) as new targets. No use case captures this as a single coordinated campaign signal across regions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails with identical or near-identical sender domain, subject, and payload sent within 24 hours to recipients across UK, Germany, Italy, and South Africa mailboxes. Flag as coordinated TA4922 campaign expansion.

suggestion.title: Detect Magento Hosts Vulnerable to CVE-2026-45247
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline flagged asset-exposure template in recommendations but failed to generate the use case. Article: 'critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting the Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension for Magento.' Organizations must identify vulnerable inventory before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Magento instances in CMDB/asset database with Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension presence and version. Flag hosts running versions prior to patch release; cross-reference with public exploits and active scanning telemetry.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts via Malicious Deserialization Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'insecure deserialization of untrusted data.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely. Exploitation requires sending crafted serialized objects to the vulnerable extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web traffic to Magento endpoints for PHP serialized object patterns (strings starting with 'O:', 'a:'), base64-encoded gadget chain payloads, and Content-Type headers indicating serialized data. Alert on requests to known-vulnerable Mirasvit paths with suspicious parameter values.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution vulnerability...actively exploited' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections. After payload delivery, attacker gains arbitrary code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child process spawning from PHP/Apache/Nginx processes (bash, cmd, PowerShell), unexpected network connections from web service accounts, suspicious file creation in /tmp or app directories, and PHP web shells or eval() execution patterns in logs.

suggestion.title: Detect Reconnaissance Scanning for Mirasvit Extension Presence
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover vulnerable hosts. Article identifies the Mirasvit extension as the target, implying enumeration precedes exploitation. Pipeline missed discovery-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Mirasvit-specific paths (/mirasvit/, /FPC/, cache-warmer endpoints) with version-enumeration patterns, unusual User-Agents associated with automated scanners, or repeated 404/200 responses indicating extension fingerprinting attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public' for CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM. Any article flagged [CRIT] with public POC availability demands detection logic to catch exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20230 exploit signatures or suspicious parameter patterns to vulnerable endpoints. Track failed/successful exploitation attempts by source IP, user-agent, and payload indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Post-Exploitation Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit code typically leads to code execution or shell spawning on the vulnerable host. Article context ('Exploit Code Goes Public') implies attacker gains execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from Cisco Unified CM service processes (e.g., tomcat, CCM java processes). Flag shell commands (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) or suspicious utilities (curl, wget, net.exe) invoked from Unified CM context.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Service/Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase often involves persistence or lateral prep. Article references patch availability, suggesting vulnerability enables unauthorized changes to the system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM audit/admin logs for unauthorized service configuration changes, user account creation, or privilege elevation. Flag modifications to startup scripts or service binaries associated with Unified CM components.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Network Communication Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit scenarios frequently result in callback or C2 communication. Article does not specify payload behavior, but 'exploit code' delivery typically aims for persistence or remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Cisco Unified CM host outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations, especially unusual ports (high-numbered TCP/UDP, DNS tunneling patterns). Flag beaconing intervals consistent with C2 heartbeat timing.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM WebDialer Service Enablement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WebDialer is disabled by default' and provides explicit disable instructions as primary mitigation. Service enablement represents preparation phase for CVE-2026-20230 exploitation and is anomalous baseline behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Cisco WebDialer service state transitions from disabled to enabled outside approved maintenance windows. Escalate if enablement precedes HTTP requests to WebDialer endpoints within 24 hours, indicating active exploitation preparation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Primary attack vector stated as 'sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' Detection at exploitation phase before file write.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to /webdialer/ endpoints containing SSRF payload indicators: encoded localhost addresses, internal IP ranges in parameters, or malformed request bodies. Baseline legitimate WebDialer traffic and alert on statistical anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Writes from Cisco Unified CM Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack outcome: 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' Detectable via process-to-file auditing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file create/write operations executed by Cisco Unified CM service accounts or spawned child processes to atypical locations (/tmp, /etc, /lib, /boot). Correlate with preceding WebDialer HTTP requests to establish full attack chain and validate exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Cisco Unified CM Service Account to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies explicit endpoint: 'elevate to root.' Detect via privilege escalation event patterns even if earlier phases are missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag privilege escalation events where source UID is Cisco Unified CM service account (typically non-privileged daemon) and target is root (UID 0). Monitor for recent file writes to /tmp or /var preceding escalation within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Complete kill chain requires correlation across HTTP layer, service state, file writes, and privilege escalation. Single-stage detections miss context; article describes sequential causality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rule triggering on sequence: (1) HTTP request to WebDialer within SLA window, (2) file write by Unified CM service to /tmp or OS system path within 10 minutes, (3) privilege escalation attempt by same service within 30 minutes of file write. Presence of all three phases indicates active CVE-2026-20230 exploitation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Execution Triggered by Untrusted Issue Input
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes attack mechanism: 'malicious issue hijack repositories' via Action flaw. Pipeline missed foundational initial-access detection for issue-sourced workflow triggers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows triggered by issue events (on: issues, on: issue_comment) where workflow has repository write or secrets access permissions. Flag if issue body/title contains shell metacharacters, command substitution, variable interpolation, or script injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution in GitHub Action from Issue Payload
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking implies arbitrary code execution. Article describes flaw enabling this via issue content—pipeline omitted execution-phase detection despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Action logs for commands/scripts executed when workflows are triggered by issue creation or modification. Flag unexpected process spawning, shell invocations, or code evaluation (eval, exec, etc.) originating from issue-interpolated variables or environment values.

suggestion.title: Repository Takeover via Unauthorized Workflow Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly states 'hijack repositories.' Pipeline produced no impact-phase detection despite clear repository compromise intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository configuration changes (branch protection rules, default branch, push rules, collaborator permissions) committed or applied by GitHub Action contexts triggered from issue events. Correlate with unexpected file modifications or force-pushes from runner IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Secrets and Credentials Access via Compromised GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking attacks target secrets and deploy credentials. Article describes issue-based compromise; pipeline failed to generate credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub Actions triggered by issue payloads access secrets, GitHub tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN), or environment variables containing credentials. Flag logging of secret values, exfiltration via network requests, or credential use outside normal workflow scope.

suggestion.title: GitHub Workflow File Injection via Issue Content
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: malicious issue content injects into or triggers workflow execution. Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection for workflow manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor `.github/workflows/` directory for unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion events. Flag workflows that alter triggering conditions (from: issues), expand permissions (permissions: write-all), or inject new secrets access, especially temporally correlated with issue creation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Action Permissions Escalation Across Repos
suggestion.rationale: Single-issue hijacking suggests potential cross-repo scope. Pipeline should model lateral movement if flaw affects shared organization Actions or inherited workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If flaw applies to organization-level Actions or shared workflows, detect a single issue-triggered Action run accessing or modifying multiple repositories. Flag unusual permission delegation or GITHUB_TOKEN reuse across repos within a single workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Stripe Customer Objects Created with Payment Card Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account' and 'storing the stolen data in metadata fields.' Direct exfiltration via legitimate platform abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk creation of Stripe customer objects from single source (web tier) with non-standard metadata containing payment card patterns (16-digit numbers, CVV, expiry). Alert on metadata field names diverging from legitimate customer fields.

suggestion.title: GTM Container Code Executed via new Function() on Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers' and 'reassembles and then executes using new Function().' This is eval-style JavaScript execution by GTM triggers on checkout pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM containers for Function() constructor calls or eval patterns, especially those activated by checkout-page DOM signals. Flag containers that load code and subsequently query payment form elements (input[name*=cc], input[name*=card]).

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Payment Data in Local Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally.' XOR bitwise operations on credit card patterns are a specific evasion signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect XOR bitwise operations (^ operator) applied to data containing credit card patterns or high-entropy numeric strings. Alert on XOR-processed data subsequently posted to api.stripe.com or firestore.googleapis.com.

suggestion.title: Firestore Cloud Database Used for Stolen Payment Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant: 'Google Firestore is used instead of Stripe' with project 'braintree-payment-app' and document 'tracking/captcha' containing stolen data in localStorage key '_d_data_customer_.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Firestore document writes to path 'tracking/captcha' or similar decoy names within projects matching payment-provider naming patterns. Flag rapid document creation with payment-indicator metadata from non-GCP-admin sources.

suggestion.title: Magento/Adobe Commerce Checkout Form Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The card skimmer targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript injection or modification on Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages that reads form fields containing PII/payment data and exfiltrates to external APIs. Monitor for scripts accessing input elements with card-related names and subsequent HTTP POST to api.stripe.com or firestore.googleapis.com.

suggestion.title: Malicious GTM Container Activated by Checkout Page Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious code is loaded from a Google Tag Manager (GTM) container and executes on every page that loads it' with specific activation 'when a shopper reaches a checkout page.' GTM is implicitly trusted and bypasses CSP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM container code for conditional execution triggered by checkout-page indicators (DOM element presence, URL path, form field detection). Track container ID changes and payload modifications. Alert on GTM triggers that subsequently load external scripts or modify page behavior.

suggestion.title: Bulk PII Exfiltration - Healthcare Records (234 GB)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'claimed to have stolen more than 234 GB of data' including 'Government-issued IDs, Health insurance information, Dates of birth' for 2.6 million accounts. Pipeline generated zero exfiltration detection despite explicit data volume and PII types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume egress from healthcare database systems (>100GB sustained transfers). Key signal: concurrent bulk queries against government-ID, SSN, insurance-plan, and DoB fields followed by large data staging to mapped network paths, cloud storage, or external IP ranges. Alert on unusual protocols/ports used for data exfiltration or compression/archiving of customer datasets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Network Access and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' requiring immediate containment actions. Pipeline failed to surface initial compromise or lateral movement detection despite narrative describing network infiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous remote access to healthcare backend systems (unusual source IPs, off-hours RDP/SSH to database servers, privilege escalation to DOMAIN ADMIN). Alert on service-account credential misuse, unusual scheduled-task creation, and persistence mechanisms installed post-authentication.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Extortion Group - Data Leak Site Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'the infamous extortion group ShinyHunters' that 'listed the company on its data leak site' and failed to extort payment before public leak. Pipeline missed threat actor name extraction entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to known ShinyHunters data leak infrastructure (OSINT feeds, VirusTotal, URLhaus for threat-actor domains). Alert on internal systems visiting attacker C2/communication channels. Cross-reference breached company names appearing on ShinyHunters leak site with internal incident reports within 30-day windows to identify early compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Dwell-Time Detection - Undetected Access Prior to June 2 Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Incident 'came to light last month' but was confirmed June 2, with ShinyHunters claiming data 'last month'—indicating weeks of undetected intrusion. Pipeline generated no detection for prolonged dormant-account access or anomalous batch operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal access patterns for healthcare database service accounts and flag deviations: unusual login times, multi-day sessions, batch data-export operations outside maintenance windows, or lateral movement to systems never previously accessed by a user/service account. Correlate with infrastructure logs for dormant account reactivation or credential reuse.

suggestion.title: Ransomware/Extortion Demand Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'failure to reach an agreement with the company, the data was publicly leaked'—indicating attacker-company communications prior to public dump. Pipeline missed detection for extortion demand channels and negotiation infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound communications (email, contact forms, dark-web messages) containing extortion language, ransom notes, or threats to publish data. Track communications from attacker email/messaging accounts. Correlate with timing of public data appearance and previous network access incidents.

suggestion.title: Sensitive PII Database Enumeration and Querying
suggestion.rationale: Breach exposed specific PII fields: 'Full names, Phone numbers, Government-issued IDs, Health insurance information, Genders, Dates of birth'. Detection should flag unusual access/export of these sensitive columns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for high-cardinality exports of PII columns (SELECT * joins on ID, insurance, SSN, DoB fields). Alert on unusual account accessing multiple sensitive tables in sequence or exporting results to temporary staging areas. Baseline normal queries and flag scans of entire customer tables by non-analyst service accounts.

suggestion.title: Domain Typosquatting Mimicking Open-Source Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake sites mimicking open-source tools rank high on Google.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for typosquat domains with string similarity to npm, github, docker, curl, git, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify newly registered domains with Levenshtein distance <3 from known open-source tool domains. Cross-reference WHOIS registration date with organic search ranking velocity for branded keywords; flag domains appearing in top-10 Google results within days of registration.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System (TDS) Malware Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware delivered 'via TDS.' Pipeline extracted no detection for TDS signatures: fingerprinting scripts, conditional redirects, device/browser-based payload selection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with JavaScript/Flash fingerprinting from suspicious domains followed by conditional 302/301 redirects based on User-Agent, geolocation, or browser type. Alert on redirect chains >3 hops to final payload within <2 seconds.

suggestion.title: Executable Download from Fake Open-Source Distribution Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery from fake tool sites. Pipeline should flag .exe, .msi, .dmg, .deb downloads from domains matching legitimate open-source tool names but registered to threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of executable files from domains with >85% string similarity to official open-source distribution domains. Cross-check digital signatures against published tool vendor checksums; flag unsigned or mismatched certificates.

suggestion.title: Google Search Result Poisoning via Rapid Indexing
suggestion.rationale: Article states fake sites 'rank high on Google'—clear SEO manipulation attack. Pipeline missed detection for rapid indexing velocity, SERP ranking gains, and backlink farm infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains (WHOIS registration <7 days) appearing in top-10 search results for open-source tool branded keywords. Integrate malicious domain feeds; flag domains with burst indexing patterns and suspicious backlink profiles.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Mismatched Signature on Open-Source Tool Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article describes users downloading and executing trojanized tool replicas. Pipeline should detect process execution anomalies: unsigned binaries with legitimate tool names, mismatched or missing digital signatures vs. official publishers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes named after common open-source tools (curl.exe, docker.exe, git.exe, node.exe, npm.exe) execute with no or invalid Authenticode signatures, or signatures not matching official vendor certificates (Microsoft, HashiCorp, GitHub, etc.).

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Redirect to Backdoor Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'spreads to macOS via malicious Google and YouTube ads' — initial access vector is explicit but zero detection logic generated. Should detect ad network redirects to suspicious hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic from browsers for redirects originating from ad networks (doubleclick.net, google-analytics, etc.) that terminate at suspicious domains or IP ranges not in ad-network whitelists. Flag domains with low reputation scores or first-seen within 48 hours of initial compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Browser Child Process Executing FlutterShell Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions FlutterShell 'spreads to macOS' via ads, implying browser-based delivery and execution. No use case for suspicious script/binary execution from browser child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Safari, Chrome, Firefox, or Edge executing shell commands, downloading files to /tmp, or launching binaries from ~/Downloads or /var/folders. Baseline: legitimate browser extensions and plugins spawn processes only in specific namespaces.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from Backdoor Process
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell backdoor requires command-and-control communication post-infection. Article provides no IOCs (C2 domains/IPs) and pipeline generated zero network detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections from previously-dormant macOS processes to non-whitelisted domains, especially those registered within 30 days, hosted on bullet-proof hosters, or resolved via DNS tunneling. Correlate with process execution from browser cache/downloads.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron Installation
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor must persist across reboots. Article does not specify persistence mechanism, but standard macOS backdoors use LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, or cron jobs. Pipeline generated zero persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of new .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons pointing to unsigned binaries or scripts in non-standard directories (/tmp, /var/folders, user home). Alert on crontab modifications by non-privileged users. Baseline: compare against legitimate system/vendor LaunchAgents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Signing or Notarization Bypass on macOS
suggestion.rationale: macOS Gatekeeper and notarization are standard anti-malware controls. Backdoor delivery via ads suggests either signed-but-malicious app or bypass technique (quarantine attribute stripping). Pipeline missed this defense-evasion layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned binaries or binaries with stripped/missing com.apple.quarantine extended attributes. Monitor for xattr -d removal commands or spawning of executables from archives without proper notarization checks. Cross-reference with browser cache and download activity.

suggestion.title: Ad Network Account Takeover or Malicious Campaign Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks flow through 'Google and YouTube ads' — implies either compromised advertiser account or injected malicious campaigns. No detection logic for ad-infrastructure reconnaissance or campaign anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormal changes to Google Ads and YouTube advertising accounts: new payment methods, campaign creation/modification from non-standard geolocations, sudden spike in ad spend, or campaigns targeting macOS users with suspiciously high click-through rates. Cross-check against ad account owner's known access patterns.

suggestion.title: MCP-for-Stata API or CLI invocation with injection syntax in log_file_name parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states log_file_name is 'directly interpolated...without sanitization' and 'GuardValidator...only scans the do-file content but does not validate this parameter.' Pipeline must detect MCP-Stata calls (Python/CLI) where log_file_name contains quotes, newlines, or command delimiters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python, Stata, or MCP-related processes with command-line arguments containing 'log_file_name=' followed by unquoted or strangely-quoted strings with semicolons, newlines (\n), or quotes. Focus on parent processes that do not normally invoke statistical software.

suggestion.title: Stata process executing injected Stata shell or python commands
suggestion.rationale: Article names the injection payload classes: 'arbitrary Stata commands (including shell, python, erase, etc.)'. Attacker injects these via log_file_name, causing Stata interpreter to execute them. T1059.003 and T1059.004 are explicit MITRE mappings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Stata parent process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or python3 when Stata's own command-line or environment variables contain suspicious log_file_name payloads with quotes or newlines. Baseline: Stata does not natively spawn shells without explicit do-file programming.

suggestion.title: Detection of log_file_name parameter bypass of GuardValidator in Stata do-file execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies that GuardValidator protects do-file content but 'does not validate this parameter.' This is a validation bypass, not caught by the security guard. Need to detect unguarded parameters passed to stata_do API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stata process invocations where log_file_name parameter is present in cmdline or environment without corresponding do-file validation. Flag mismatches between validated content and unvalidated parameters, especially when log_file_name contains special characters or path traversal sequences.

suggestion.title: Stata-spawned process executing file enumeration or deletion commands
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'erase' as an injection vector; T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) is mapped. Attacker can inject Stata erase, dir, ls commands to enumerate or destroy files. This is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Stata child processes running rm, del, erase, ls, dir, find, or locate when the parent Stata process has a log_file_name argument with injected Stata commands or shell metacharacters in its environment or command-line history.

suggestion.title: Unexpected MCP-for-Stata provider instantiation from non-statistical parent processes
suggestion.rationale: MCP-for-Stata is a library that may be loaded by Python or other interpreters. Article identifies the API layer as vulnerable. Should detect MCP-Stata being initialized from web servers, databases, or other untrusted contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python, Node.js, or other scripting runtimes invoking Stata with MCP-related arguments (stata_mcp, mcp-for-stata) when the parent process is a web service, database, or batch scheduler with internet-facing exposure. Focus on processes running under service or webapp accounts.

suggestion.title: Stata binary invoked with untrusted or remote-sourced do-file references alongside injected log_file_name
suggestion.rationale: T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) suggests the attack involves user-supplied or remote do-files. Pipeline should correlate remote do-file fetches with unvalidated log_file_name parameters in the same Stata invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network events (Stata parent downloading or fetching a do-file from HTTP/HTTPS) with Stata process execution where log_file_name argument is also present. Flag as suspicious: user-supplied do-file + unvalidated log_file_name in same Stata command.

suggestion.title: Stored XSS Payload Injection into AVideo YPTSocket Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is **Stored DOM XSS** via metadata broadcast. Detection must capture the ingestion/storage phase, not just delivery. Article phrase: 'Stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting via Per-Client Metadata Broadcast.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebSocket frames or HTTP POST/PUT requests to YPTSocket plugin endpoints where page_title or webSocketSelfURI parameters contain XSS payloads. Focus on the storage/persistence point where metadata is written to disk or database, not just inbound requests.

suggestion.title: Abnormal JavaScript Execution in AVideo Admin Session Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing' the YPTSocket pane. Need behavioral detection of unexpected script execution within admin-privileged session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript eval() or Function() constructor calls originating from YPTSocket plugin context within admin sessions. Monitor for scripts that access document.cookie, sessionStorage, or authenticate tokens.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie / Authentication Token Exfiltration via Injected Script
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential theft as impact—'Steal Web Session Cookie' (T1539). Need specific detection for admin session tokens being read and exfiltrated by injected JavaScript.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests exfiltrating cookie data or SessionID values to external domains from the AVideo admin IP/account. Correlate with prior YPTSocket XSS injection attempts.

suggestion.title: AVideo Plugin Configuration / Metadata Database Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: payload is 'broadcast' to admins—implies centralized storage. Need detection of writes to plugin config, database tables, or persistent metadata storage where the XSS payload is planted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or modification of AVideo YPTSocket plugin configuration files, database tables, or metadata stores with XSS-pattern content (HTML tags, JavaScript, event handlers).

suggestion.title: Compromised @cap-js/openapi package version installation (v1.4.1)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'compromised version of @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 was published' and 'Upgrade to @cap-js/openapi >= 1.4.2'. No UC hunts for installation of the vulnerable package version itself—this is the supply-chain signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json and lock files for references to @cap-js/openapi version 1.4.1 post-May 19, 2026. Alert on npm install/npm ci commands that resolve to v1.4.1 even if later version specified (downgrade or cached artifact). Check node_modules/@cap-js/openapi/package.json version field on-disk.

suggestion.title: npm package preinstall hook installation (setup/execution scripts in package.json)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'preinstall hook' and malicious packages executing arbitrary code during npm install. No UC explicitly hunts for the hook installation itself—only for post-execution process spawning (UC_8_4). Need to detect when package.json scripts field is modified or contains suspicious preinstall commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when package.json preinstall script contains inline JavaScript execution, child process spawning, or credential file read paths. Look for obfuscated or base64-encoded commands in preinstall scripts. Baseline legitimate preinstall scripts in org (usually build-step commands, not arbitrary node execution).

suggestion.title: JavaScript code obfuscation in npm modules (T1027 evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as a technique but no UC detects obfuscation patterns. Malware payload is likely obfuscated to evade static analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .js files in node_modules/@cap-js/openapi/ for obfuscation indicators: excessive variable renaming (single-letter vars), control-flow flattening, string literals replaced with getters, minification without source maps. Use tools like JStillery signature matching or entropy analysis on source sections.

suggestion.title: npm package self-propagation: package.json modification by node/npm processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attempted self-propagation' but no UC hunts for modifications to package.json or package-lock.json by running npm/node processes that would spread to other projects or dependency chains.
log_sources: Git changes (git status, git diff output)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe or bun.exe writes to package.json or package-lock.json files outside of package manager control (/node_modules/@cap-js/openapi/ attempting to modify parent project's package.json). Flag any addition of suspicious dependencies to parent project's dependency tree from within node_modules execution context.

suggestion.title: HTTP/HTTPS protocol negotiation anomalies to t.m-kosche.com (T1071.001)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols) as technique but UC_8_3 only hunts DNS/domain connectivity, not protocol-level anomalies. Exfil endpoint may use unusual TLS certificate, odd HTTP headers, or protocol downgrade.
log_sources: Network.Traffic (TLS handshake metadata, HTTP request headers)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For connections to t.m-kosche.com, flag if: TLS certificate is self-signed or issued to different hostname, HTTP/1.0 or older used instead of HTTP/2, missing standard headers (User-Agent, Accept), or POST requests to /api/public/otel/v1/traces with JSON payloads larger than typical OTEL spans (> 10KB).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mailbox Forwarding Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months.' Five-month persistence strongly indicates use of email forwarding or delegation rules to maintain access and exfiltrate correspondence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of inbox rules, forwarding rules, or mailbox delegation in Outlook/Exchange targeting external domains. Alert on PowerShell execution of Set-Mailbox, New-InboxRule, or Add-MailboxPermission commands executed outside normal change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Mailbox Access from Impossible Geographies and New Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes five-month continuous access to executive's email. Attacker infrastructure differs from executive's normal login patterns; detect impossible-travel scenarios, unfamiliar IPs, and suspicious device types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag mailbox access from IP ranges outside the executive's known geographic footprint, unfamiliar device operating systems, or access patterns inconsistent with user baseline (e.g., access during night hours if user never works nights).

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Export and Archive Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'spied on' the mailbox—this explicitly indicates data exfiltration. Detect PST exports, IMAP/POP downloads, or large-volume email reads suggestive of copying or archiving correspondence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Outlook PST file creation or export operations, elevated email download volume via IMAP/POP, or suspicious MAPI session activity. Correlate with external file uploads to cloud storage.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegate and Secondary Account Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Five-month undetected access suggests attackers established redundant persistence. Detect addition of delegates, resource mailboxes, or secondary identities linked to the executive account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new mailbox delegates added outside change-control windows, creation of resource mailboxes with unusual naming patterns, or addition of alternate email addresses to the executive's profile.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Search Patterns Targeting Strategic Information
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of stock exchange executive for espionage implies active queries for sensitive correspondence. Detect searches for keywords common in MNPI (M&A, earnings, board, confidential) conducted by the compromised account outside normal user behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag elevated or unusual search queries for financial keywords (merger, acquisition, earnings, IPO, derivative), paired with extraction or forwarding of matching messages outside normal workflow.

suggestion.title: Email Audit Log Tampering and Suspicious Deletions
suggestion.rationale: Five-month persistence undetected suggests attackers may have suppressed audit logging or deleted evidence of exfiltration. Detect missing audit logs, bulk email permanent deletions, or audit log configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gaps or anomalies in mailbox audit logs, bulk soft-delete or hard-delete operations on sent items, or administrative changes to audit log retention policies applied to the executive's mailbox.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Hash Detection on macOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article provides nine SHA256 file hashes marked high-fidelity. Direct statement: 'install a powerful backdoor on infected machines.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or process execution matching any of the nine provided SHA256 hashes on macOS systems. Cross-reference with VirusTotal for multi-vendor detection consensus before tuning FP rate.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Operation FlutterBridge Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies domains sinterfumesco.com, ads-parkpro.com, adsparkpro.top, adsparkpro.net, softwe.art as backdoor infrastructure. Lists T1071 but provides no detection hypothesis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS lookups or HTTP/HTTPS connections from macOS endpoints to known C2 domains. Correlate with file hash detections. Flag even failed/timeout connections—they indicate post-compromise reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Malicious Application Download from Google Ads URLs
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'Google Ads to push fake desktop applications.' This describes T1598.002/T1598.003 (phishing via ads) but no detection is provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users downloading executable files (macOS: .dmg, .pkg, .app) from one of the article's delivery domains. Correlate browser referrer/click source with download destination. High confidence if referrer contains Google Ad parameters (utm_source, gclid, etc.).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unsigned macOS App Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Campaign delivers 'fake desktop applications' via ad clicks. Article does not provide detection for suspicious installer behavior or unsigned/re-signed app execution on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: macOS: detect execution of unsigned .app bundles or .pkg installers originating from ~/Downloads or /tmp. Correlate with subsequent plist file creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons (T1547.013 persistence).

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence via Autostart (macOS LaunchAgent/Daemon)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'backdoor' but provides no detection for its persistence mechanism. macOS backdoors typically use LaunchAgent or LaunchDaemon entries per T1547.013.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons within 10 minutes of suspicious app execution. Check for referential integrity—plist pointing to files in /tmp, user temp dirs, or hidden .app bundles.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline identified T1027 (Obfuscated Files) as a technique but provided no corresponding detection. FlutterShell samples likely use code packing or encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with unusually high entropy code sections, UPX/LZMA packing signatures, or anomalous Mach-O sections on macOS. Flag parent-child relationships where installer spawns high-entropy child process.

suggestion.title: Encoded PowerShell execution spawned by cmd.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' This is a high-fidelity execution pattern with low false-positive risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe parent spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand flag. Decode Base64 payload in memory or at rest to identify obfuscated commands. Correlate with network events to C2 infrastructure within same process tree window.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest downloading .ps1 to ApplicationData
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' Uncommon file delivery vector with strong malware association.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Invoke-WebRequest or System.Net.WebClient calls fetching .ps1 files to ApplicationData, ProgramData, or temp directories. Baseline legitimate package-management patterns; alert on deviations. Correlate file creation timestamp with process execution timestamp.

suggestion.title: Remove-Item cleanup immediately following script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' Anti-forensics pattern coupled with recent file creation in ApplicationData.
