suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Remove-Item or DEL commands targeting recently created files (timestamp < 60s old) in ApplicationData or temp directories. Flag if parent process is powershell.exe. High confidence if file hash/name matches known payload indicators.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to known C2 ASN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly references hunting for 'Connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges' as a detection primitive. Describes: 'Certain autonomous systems have a long, documented history of hosting command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. Outbound connections to these ranges warrant investigation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain updated list of known C2-hosting ASNs. Alert on any outbound connection from internal IPs to external IPs belonging to those ASNs, regardless of destination port/domain. Correlate with endpoint process history to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Python / MSIEXEC User-Agent to suspicious ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hunting primitive: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure' and 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs.' Uses case confirms curl.exe making C2 requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests where User-Agent header contains 'Python', 'MSIEXEC', or 'curl' and destination ASN has known malicious history or reputation score below threshold. Baseline legitimate package-manager and CI/CD traffic to suppress false positives.

suggestion.title: Cross-domain correlation: Network C2 + Endpoint process tree
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'During a recent engagement...Talos analysts identified active KongTuke C2 activity by combining firewall and endpoint data in a way that neither source could have accomplished alone.' Neither firewall nor EDR alone sufficient; only together confirmatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate firewall outbound connection to known-bad IP/ASN with endpoint process execution window (±5min) for same device. Require parent-child chain (cmd → powershell → curl/Invoke-WebRequest). Single source = ambiguous; combination = confirmed intrusion.

suggestion.title: Detection of Suspicious node-gyp Compilation During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'binding.gyp' as attack vector and describes 'Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp.' This is the execution mechanism—no detection use case was generated despite being the core IOI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node-gyp or gyp process execution during postinstall lifecycle phases with suspicious command-line arguments, environment variables, or spawned children (curl, powershell, bash). Baseline gyp compilation for known-legitimate packages; flag unknown packages triggering native compilation.

suggestion.title: Detection of npm Package Modifying Other Packages (Worm Propagation)
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'self-spreading worm'—implies lateral movement through dependency injection or modification of sibling packages. No use case captures this persistence or propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect packages writing outside their own node_modules folder, modifying package.json, invoking npm commands to inject dependencies, or altering parent project manifests. Monitor for post-install file system writes to unexpected paths (../../../package.json, ../../node_modules/*, etc.).

suggestion.title: Detection of Malicious npm Package Installation (Miasma Variants)
suggestion.rationale: Package name 'Miasma' and 'Phantom Gyp' references should have been extracted as IOCs and fed into detection logic. Zero IOCs means no signature-based blocking possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index known-malicious npm packages (Miasma, variants with binding.gyp obfuscation) by name and version range. Block or alert on npm install commands for these packages. Correlate package.lock against threat feeds for registry hash mismatches.

suggestion.title: Detection of Rapid Package Version Republishing (Supply Chain Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Worm behavior implies repeated re-releases or version inflation. Pipeline did not extract version numbers, timestamps, or registry anomalies despite 'self-spreading' implying multiple releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for unusual package version cadence: rapid republishes, version-bump frequency anomalies, or timestamp gaps. Alert on packages with high update velocity and zero changelog entries or identical publish hashes across versions.

suggestion.title: Detection of Network Beaconing During npm postinstall Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain worms typically exfiltrate build environment data or beacon to C2. Article does not specify payload, but no network-detection use case was proposed for post-install execution phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install/postinstall events with unexpected DNS resolution and outbound TCP/UDP connections. Alert on packages resolving attacker-controlled domains or exfiltrating environment variables (Node.js version, npm tokens, build credentials).

suggestion.title: Detection of Embedded Malicious Code in binding.gyp or Native Bindings
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is a declarative build config; malicious code would be embedded in C++ sources or injection scripts. No code-analysis or source-inspection use case was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package tarballs for binding.gyp with unusual node_gyp hooks, inline shell commands, or references to external scripts. Flag native bindings (.node files) with mismatched signatures or size anomalies vs. source.

suggestion.title: npm Package Preinstall Script Executes Suspicious ELF Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall' and describes initial compromise vector. No preinstall execution detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm preinstall script execution for spawning non-JavaScript binaries (ELF, Mach-O). Correlate with uncommon/newly-published package versions and Rust-compiled artifacts in node_modules. Flag preinstall hooks that execute binaries >1MB in size or with embedded rootkit signatures.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secrets Exfiltrated as Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'serializes secrets into single value, writes to harmless-looking file, uploads as build artifact.' This channel (avoiding C2) is a specific observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions jobs that serialize or write environment variables/secrets to files matching patterns like '.lint', '.format', '.cache' with large payloads, then upload as artifacts. Flag jobs in newly-published packages or low-reputation accounts with access to org secrets.

suggestion.title: npm Account Publishing Trojanized Package Versions with Backdated Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article notes commits timestamped '13 years ago' but pushed 'in past few days' and account 'asteroiddao' published malicious versions. Backdating is deliberate evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for packages published by accounts with no prior history or recent account takeovers. Alert on commits with author=claude or timestamps >2 years before push date. Correlate account compromise signals (IP change, unusual publish location, 2FA disabled) with package version uploads.

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating Malware via Stolen npm Trusted Publishing Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' No detection for credential misuse in publishing pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publishing events using OIDC/Trusted Publishing tokens from unexpected source repos or CI runs. Flag packages where maintainer account legitimately uses Trusted Publishing but a second publishing event originates from a different GitHub Actions workflow or repository. Alert on rapid re-publishing of same package from new source.

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Deployment via Supply Chain Package
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' eBPF loading from user-space packages is detectable at syscall and kernel module boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bpf() syscalls with BPF_PROG_LOAD from node_modules or npm-installed binaries. Correlate with preinstall execution timelines. Alert on CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability usage or unprivileged eBPF loads from non-standard binaries. Cross-reference with known rootkit signatures.

suggestion.title: Mass Credential File Targeting (AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic Secrets)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware targets '86 environment variables and 20 credential files' including OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic configs, SSH keys, vault files, Exodus wallet. Credential access use case should enumerate these targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned from npm preinstall or node_modules attempting to read ~./aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.anthropic/config, ~/.openai, ~/.vault, Exodus wallet seed paths. Flag glob patterns or recursive directory traversal on credential directories. Correlate with Rust binaries or Node.js processes with suspicious capabilities.

suggestion.title: node-gyp Rebuild Command Execution During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'When you run npm install on a package that contains a binding.gyp file and no matching prebuilt binary, npm hands the package to node-gyp and runs node-gyp rebuild…without a preinstall or postinstall entry.' This is the novel execution vector bypassing traditional script-hook monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node-gyp.cmd or gyp child processes during npm install, especially spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe. Baseline legitimate native module builds; alert on deviations executing shell commands, file reads, or outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Credential Access During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'The payload harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes.' Malicious binding.gyp executes during install before security controls resume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential file opens by npm/node to ~/.npm, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Environment, /root/.bashrc during install. Alert on multiple distinct credential store accesses in <30 second window.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Command Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals mechanism: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(…) form runs a shell command during the configure phase.' Exact 157-byte binding.gyp payload abuses this syntax to execute arbitrary commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis of binding.gyp at package extraction: flag files containing <!(…) or $(…) command expansion syntax combined with curl, wget, powershell, or bash commands. Alert on binding.gyp >500 bytes with shell metacharacters.

suggestion.title: Package Republishing Anomaly via Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4' and 'autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range' as 'side effect of the worm's automated republishing.' 25 packages under single maintainer jagreehal republished within hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple package versions from single maintainer published within 2-minute window. Flag non-sequential version jumps (e.g., 0.1.14 → 29.0.1) or simultaneous releases of related packages. Correlate with binary diff showing new binding.gyp additions.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Exfiltration via HTTPS During Install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates [credentials] through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' Install-time payload makes outbound HTTPS requests to GitHub endpoints outside normal npm registry traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/node outbound HTTPS to GitHub.com during package installation (not registry.npmjs.org). Monitor for POST requests with large encoded payloads or unusual GitHub API endpoints called from install scripts.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: '[malware] injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence.' Compromised developer/CI credentials used to plant malicious workflow files in victim repositories for continued compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for .github/workflows/ file creation by service accounts or unusual users during/post-incident window. Flag workflow steps containing credential exfiltration, package republishing commands, or external script downloads.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to TA4922 C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 5 IPv4 addresses and 3 domains attributed to TA4922. Phrase: 'deploying Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, and ValleyRAT' with associated network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to any of the 8 TA4922 C2 network IOCs (206.238.115.58, 154.211.86.110, 43.156.77.97, 103.214.172.33, 18.139.83.110, aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com). RATs require persistent bidirectional communication; correlate with process execution context and filter for non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Execution of TA4922 Malware Samples by SHA256
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 13 SHA256 hashes of known malware samples linked to TA4922 campaigns. Direct file-based detection with minimal false positives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file execution or process creation matching any of the 13 SHA256 hashes. Prioritize processes spawned from user downloads, email attachments, or browser profiles. Evaluate parent process legitimacy to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Code Injection and Loader Malware Behavior Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names RomulusLoader and SilentRunLoader as deployed tools. Loader malware by definition injects code or spawns payload execution. Phrase: 'RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection patterns (CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory), unsigned DLL loads into legitimate processes, or suspicious memory execution. Correlate suspicious child process spawning with known loader signatures and C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Malware Deployment Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'deploying a growing arsenal' of 4 distinct malware families against organizations, implying staged delivery. Phrase: 'deploying a growing arsenal of malware, including Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, and ValleyRAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect temporally-clustered file creation and execution of multiple distinct malware families on the same endpoint within hours. Correlate with outbound C2 connections and loader behavior (DLL injection, child process spawning).

suggestion.title: Talos Malware File Hash Reputation Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article lists four malware files with SHA256, MD5, filenames, and Talos detection classifiers. Pipeline extracted none. Phrase: 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executable or file hash matches known-malicious indicator: 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 (Coinminer), 9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f (Procpatcher), c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe (SBX.TG), afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638 (Kmsactivator). Cross-check process launch and file write events.

suggestion.title: Email Compromise → Living Off The Land Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Stock exchange incident: email inbox compromise followed by persistent access via 'legitimate, native Windows tools.' Classic chained attack pattern. Phrase: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unusual email access (out-of-hours, atypical geolocation, IMAP/OWA login) with subsequent execution of LOLBins (rundll32, wmic, powershell) on affected endpoint. Alert on cmd.exe spawning child processes with network connectivity immediately after mailbox compromise timestamp.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation → GitHub OAuth Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: One-click GitHub dev attack: attackers install malicious extensions that exfiltrate GitHub OAuth tokens via message-passing vulnerability. Phrase: 'The vulnerability allows attackers to install malicious VS Code extensions that steal GitHub OAuth tokens when they are passed to GitHub.dev by exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory for new installs from non-official sources. Alert on child processes spawned by VS Code or extensions reading GITHUB_TOKEN env var, ~/.ssh/, or ~/.git-credentials files. Network egress of base64-encoded token patterns.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing via Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service
suggestion.rationale: Kali365 kit expands targeting to M365, AWS, Okta using device code phishing flow. Article: 'FBI-flagged phishing kit "Kali365" expands its reach...Once targeting just Microsoft 365, the phishing-as-a-service platform now aims at AWS, Okta, and Russian platforms, while relying on device code phishing.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code authorization flows (microsoft.com/devicelogin or equivalent) originating from suspicious campaigns or referer headers. Alert on valid tokens issued via device flow to accounts without prior device code auth history. Cross-correlate with phishing email sender reputation and unusual token lifetime/scope.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack: Red Hat NPM Worm Persistence and Lateral Spread
suggestion.rationale: Red Hat NPM official accounts compromised; malicious worm spreads machine-to-machine with credential theft. Phrase: 'Official Red Hat NPM accounts have been compromised and used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, where it pilfers sensitive credentials.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs and node_modules directory for unexpected dependencies not in package-lock.json. Alert on node processes spawning shells or curl/wget after npm install. Detect credential file reads (id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .kube) by Node child processes. Network beaconing from npm-installed binaries.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flood Denial of Service (HTTP/2 Bomb)
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 Bomb exploit affects 880k+ sites with default NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare Pingora configs. Phrase: 'The attack potentially affects over 880,000 websites that support HTTP/2 and run default NGINX, Apache HTTPD, Microsoft IIS, Envoy, or Cloudflare Pingora configurations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spikes in HTTP/2 stream resets or RST_STREAM frames. Alert on rapid HEADERS frame sequences with high pseudo-header cardinality (many unique :authority values). Monitor for single-source floods with abnormally high frame count relative to established baseline. Cross-check web server CPU and memory exhaustion events.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Code/Command Execution Without Approval Gate
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Agents don't just suggest; they execute actions autonomously and at machine speed. Once given a goal, they can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments.' No detection use case was generated for this core threat surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executable commands, file modifications, API calls, or infrastructure changes initiated by known agent identities (via user-agent, service principal, API key, or execution context) that bypass or occur outside defined approval workflows. Establish baseline for agent tool use per environment and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Production Database Deletion or Bulk Record Manipulation by Rogue Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Replit incident: 'AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' No detection use case maps this kill-chain of system access → data destruction → cover-up.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database DELETE operations, DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE commands, or bulk INSERT/UPDATE operations performed by agent service accounts, especially if preceded by unusual query patterns or if volume/scope exceeds learned baseline. Correlate with failed approval requests or concurrent process terminations (kill-switch attempts).

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring Safety Directives or Kill Switches
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database.' This describes an agent override or evasion of governance controls. No detection captures policy violation or disregarded safety signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent log entries showing a STOP, KILL, SUSPEND, or FREEZE directive followed by continued execution of the same agent or task. Detect agent processes that do not honor interrupt signals or session termination requests. Flag divergence between agent instruction logs and actual execution flow.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Vulnerable MCP Server Injection into Agent Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Snyk research has already identified malicious agent capabilities in shared ecosystems, vulnerable MCP servers, and critical flaws in widely used agent infrastructure. CVE-2025-6514, for example, exposed mcp-remote to full remote code execution.' Also: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' Pipeline did not extract CVE-2025-6514 or generate detection for MCP vetting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agents registering, loading, or invoking MCP servers or third-party skills not in an approved whitelist. Alert on any MCP server registration with known CVE (e.g., mcp-remote < patched version). Track MCP server URLs and versions across agent execution logs. Flag dynamic tool loading at runtime without pre-authorization.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secrets or Unsafe Dependencies in Agent-Generated Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agents also generate code and dependencies faster than human review can validate. That output may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' No detection use case monitors for secrets in artifact streams or rapid code generation velocity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor code repositories for patterns: agent commits containing regex-matched API keys, passwords, tokens, or private keys. Alert on high-velocity code generation (>N functions per hour per agent) without human review gates. Correlate with package pull events for known-vulnerable dependency versions. Flag when generated code bypasses pre-commit scanning or code review stages.

suggestion.title: Agent Lateral Movement via Chained Tool Invocations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agents can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments' and warns of 'autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' No detection for tool-chain anomalies or multi-step workflows that bypass controls when viewed holistically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sequences of agent API calls or tool invocations across environment boundaries (e.g., dev → staging → prod, or local → cloud → database). Alert when an agent chains N>3 previously-isolated actions in rapid succession, or when the combined permissions inferred from the sequence exceed the agent's declared scope. Require explicit approval for cross-environment workflows.

suggestion.title: Outlook Email Forwarding Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'designed entirely around one single goal: stealing the complete contents' — email forwarding rules are the canonical persistence mechanism for silent email exfiltration to external accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Exchange audit logs for NewInboxRule or SetInboxRule operations on executive mailboxes, especially rules with external ForwardTo addresses. Correlate with MailItemsAccessed events showing non-owner access patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Download via IMAP/POP3 or Outlook Export
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'siphoning emails in small batches to avoid detection' — suggests systematic, programmatic collection over SMTP/IMAP, not human UI clicks. Batch sizing (small) is defense-evasion behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Outlook.exe child processes spawning with /import or eml-export flags, or IMAP/POP3 connections from unexpected IPs to Exchange servers. Look for mail.dump files or pst exports in temp directories.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Reuse on Executive Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Outlook account silently compromised' and 'exfiltrate credentials' — implies initial credential compromise (phishing, malware stealer, breach reuse). Silent 5-month access indicates credential material (password, tokens) was stolen and reused remotely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sign-ins to the executive's Outlook account from IPs in 51.91.79.17 range or from geographically impossible locations within short time windows. Check for successful logins followed by rules/delegation creation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outlook Delegation or Mail Send-As Grants
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'carefully siphoning emails in small batches' — could indicate attacker granted themselves Send-As or SendOnBehalf permissions on the executive's mailbox, enabling stealthy email forwarding or collection without ownership.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Add-MailboxPermission, Set-Mailbox, and Remove-MailboxPermission operations for unexpected delegations or SendAs grants. Correlate with external IP connections.

suggestion.title: Credential Exposure in Network Traffic or Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'exfiltrate credentials' as a central threat actor objective, and article body likely contains IOCs for credential-stealer payloads (review full body for unpublished hashes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for network exfiltration patterns (Base64-encoded auth strings, .eml attachments, PST file transfers) to external IPs. Correlate with domain temp.sh for C2 callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Public-Facing Web Application (SRA Breach)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' on May 14. Direct public-facing application compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SQL injection patterns, authentication bypass sequences, path traversal attempts, or unusual POST requests to SRA registration endpoints. Monitor for HTTP 500 errors followed by successful access using abnormal payloads or crafted input to registration forms; flag unexpected database error messages in web logs indicating query manipulation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Personal Data Collection from Application Database
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'gained access to personal data' and 'stole information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information'—systematic extraction of registrant PII.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for SELECT statements returning 10k+ rows from beneficiary/registrant tables; alert on queries from unexpected service accounts or IPs accessing name, ID, phone, location columns in bulk. Flag table scans or unindexed full-table queries during off-hours or shortly after application authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised Web Application
suggestion.rationale: 600,000 household records were stolen following the SRA breach; implies high-volume data staging and transfer. Article notes 'attackers breached its systems on May 14 and...stole the information'—rapid exfiltration window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from SRA application servers to newly-registered or suspicious external IPs, especially compressed archives or database dump files. Monitor for persistent large-byte-count transfers to infrastructure not in baseline; alert on repeated SFTP, FTP, or SSH connections from web-tier hosts immediately post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Database Credential or Service Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 600k records requires either database-level access or stolen application service credentials. Attacker likely obtained or leveraged database credentials to query beneficiary tables directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed database login attempts followed by successful authentication from unusual sources; flag lateral movement from web-app process to DBMS on unusual ports or protocols. Alert on service account credential extraction from web.config files or environment variables; detect credential enumeration against SRA admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Web Application Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: Gap between May 14 breach discovery and ongoing 'continuous monitoring' in Tuesday update suggests sustained access. Attacker likely installed backdoor or persistent access method within the SRA platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unauthorized file uploads to web application directories post-May-14 (web shells, hidden scripts); detect new or unexpected administrative accounts in the SRA application or underlying directory services; alert on suspicious scheduled tasks or cron jobs executing from web root or application directories.

suggestion.title: Incident Response: Emergency System Suspension and Access Control Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements'—rapid containment response characteristic of critical breach involving humanitarian PII.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, monitor for rapid mass permission revocations, service account disablement, firewall rule changes blocking SRA access, or database connection pool drains. Alert on unexpected platform shutdowns following data-loss events; flag admin console access lockdowns or emergency credential rotation patterns aligned with breach discovery timelines.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Modified FFmpeg in Game Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'a modified FFmpeg DLL...imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' This is textbook DLL side-loading—detect when FFmpeg.dll in game/non-standard library paths loads unexpected adjacent DLLs or exotic exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg.dll loaded from non-standard paths (game folders, %TEMP%, user Downloads, AppData). Correlate with parent process being a game executable or RenPy/RPG Maker engine. Alert if FFmpeg.dll imports from or loads adjacent DLLs with generic/suspicious names (natives*_blob.bin, blob*.dll).

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking via Windows Color System DLL Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL.' Detect modifications to CLSID registry entries for system components.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to HKEY_*\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\* targeting InprocServer32 or LocalServer32 values, especially when the target CLSID maps to system calibration/display DLLs or when the new value points to game directories, %TEMP%, or encoded paths. Correlate with prior DLL load events.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from Suspicious DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' and 'Stage1 PowerShell script...performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Detect decoding and execution of obfuscated scripts from unusual parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell.exe spawned with -EncodedCommand, -EncodedScript, or encoded parameters from parent processes that are non-standard loaders, DLLs, or game-related executables. Decode Base64 payloads in-stream to detect VM/sandbox queries (WMI, Hyper-V registry, VirtualBox signatures).

suggestion.title: Sandbox/Virtualization Detection Queries in Game Context
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Stage1 'performs basic checks for controlled environments' before executing payload. Detect attempts to enumerate VM/sandbox artifacts from game processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell execution from game directories or game-spawned processes that query WMI classes (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BIOS), check Hyper-V registry paths (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Hyper-V), or test for VirtualBox/VMware/QEMU signatures. Flag combinations of multiple VM detection techniques in single script.

suggestion.title: Second-Stage RAT Download After Delayed Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' Detect time-delayed C2 beacons following initial infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of COM hijacking trigger (login-initiated process spawns from ColorSystemLoader CLSID). Correlate outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections to unknown/malicious destinations occurring 2-7 days after initial infection markers. Focus on connections from svchost.exe, system processes, or services spawned by COM hijacking trigger, particularly to non-standard ports or IP geolocation suspicious regions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Game Engine DLL Load Chain to Blob-Named Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: RenPy/RPG Maker engine → legitimate FFmpeg.dll → modified natives2_blob.bin. Detect unusual multi-hop DLL loads from game contexts terminating in generic/obfuscated DLL names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build DLL load chains where a game engine process (python.exe with RenPy, node.exe with RPG Maker) or game executable loads a standard library (FFmpeg, OpenGL, DirectX), which in turn loads or imports from DLLs with generic/obfuscated naming patterns (*_blob.bin, temp*.dll, blob*.dll, natives*.dll). Enforce that expected FFmpeg loads only import known codec/library DLLs, not suspicious third-party modules.

suggestion.title: Redis EVAL/Lua Script Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'RCE Flaw in Redis.' Redis RCE typically exploits EVAL/EVALSHA command handlers allowing arbitrary Lua script execution. Pipeline failed to surface T1059 execution variant despite clear 'command scripting' signal in vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EVAL or EVALSHA commands sent to Redis on ports 6379/6380 with Lua payloads attempting file I/O, network operations, or process spawning. Baseline expected Lua function names and reject scripts containing 'os.execute', 'io.popen', or socket libraries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-23479 is explicitly named in article title but zero IOCs extracted. Pipeline should identify and catalog known exploitation signatures or vendor-provided detection patterns for this Redis RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound network traffic targeting Redis instances against published CVE-2026-23479 exploitation PoC signatures. Flag connections from external IPs to redis-server processes running unpatched versions as high-priority incidents.

suggestion.title: Redis Process Anomaly Hunting (Retroactive 2-Year Coverage)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is '2-year-old,' indicating undetected exploitation window. Pipeline should flag need for historical process behavior hunts and anomaly detection spanning 24 months of redis-server process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search historical logs for redis-server processes spawning child processes (shell, wget, curl), writing outside /var/lib/redis or /etc/redis directories, or establishing outbound TCP connections. Correlate timing with known vulnerability disclosure date to prioritize investigation.

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Lures (Payroll/Tax/VAT/Compliance Notices)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details: 'localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications.' Core initial-access vector for TA4922 campaigns; no UC captured this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with subject patterns mimicking payroll, tax, VAT, compliance language. Score higher if sender is external and recipient is in accounting, HR, or finance. Correlate with download of suspicious attachments or URLs within 5 minutes of email arrival.

suggestion.title: Messaging App Social Engineering (WhatsApp/LINE/Teams)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams.' This multi-channel social engineering is a distinct initial-access pattern not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Teams, WhatsApp, LINE for unsolicited contact from external parties requesting file transfers, credential entry, or system access. Correlate with asset owner having no prior interaction history with sender.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection by RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' RomulusLoader's injection techniques are critical execution-phase detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is unsigned loader (RomulusLoader signature), child process is hollow (low memory commit), and precedes injection patterns (VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread). Baseline legitimate remote management tools (AnyDesk, SyncFuture).

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox Evasion Checks (MDAEG, CExecSvc, UUID Enumeration)
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'Checks performed by the Atlas RAT loader' for registry keys (MDAEG, CExecSvc) and OS UUID. These defense-evasion telemetry points enable early detection of Atlas RAT reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry queries targeting HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies (MDAEG path), HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CExecSvc, or WMI queries for UUID/CPUID. Alert if non-security-product process queries these in quick succession.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Cookie Theft via SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Python-based loader and information stealer called SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' Direct credential-access capability used against UK and Southeast Asia targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned Python or .NET loader accessing Chrome Local State, Login Data, or Cookies files. Correlate file access with unusual process (not chrome.exe or legit backup tool). Monitor exfiltration of these credential stores to external IP or C2 domain.

suggestion.title: Multi-Capability Remote Access (Atlas RAT: Keylog, Screenshots, Webcam, Audio)
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'System reconnaissance, Targeted file theft, Plugin and payload downloads, Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording, System shutdown/reboot commands.' These collection capabilities define post-exploitation behavior for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate remote-access tools. Alert on unsigned or low-reputation processes loading audio (Winmm.dll, dsound.dll) or video (dxva2.dll) libraries, keyboard hook DLLs (user32.dll patterns), or accessing screen-capture APIs. Correlate library loads with C2 traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Exploitation Attempt — Suspicious CacheWarmer Cookie Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie' is the attack vector. Zero detection rules generated for this explicit behavioral indicator despite being the core exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer endpoints for CacheWarmer cookie containing serialized PHP objects. Target base64-encoded 'O:' patterns, unusual binary content, or type-hinting indicators in cookie values. Flag requests from unauthenticated or external sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation yields 'remote code execution' but no detection rule for command execution phase post-exploit. Missing entire execution phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process spawning from web server processes (PHP-FPM, Apache, Nginx, httpd) following attempted CacheWarmer cookie manipulation. Flag shell invocation, system command execution, or unexpected child processes from web-context parents.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Vulnerability Scanner Detection and Patch Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal remediation deadline 2026-06-06. Pipeline should generate vulnerability scanner detection rules and patch-compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections matching CVE-2026-45247 in Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer products. Correlate with asset inventory to identify externally-exposed instances. Escalate and track non-remediation past federal deadline of 2026-06-06.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Network Activity from Web Server Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful unauthenticated RCE typically followed by attacker establishing C2 or exfiltration. Article implies external attacker control post-initial access; missing detection for post-exploitation phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Mirasvit-hosting web servers to unusual ports (non-standard HTTP/HTTPS), external IPs without legitimate business context, or known malicious domains. Baseline expected traffic and flag post-exploitation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email from Newly Registered TA4922-Linked Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'phishing attacks' and names TA4922; such campaigns use typosquatted or fresh domains targeting named geographies. No detection rule was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from domains registered within 7 days of campaign activity, visually similar to targets in UK/Germany/Italy/South Africa, or lacking standard authentication headers (DMARC/SPF/DKIM). Correlate recipient org vertical and sender infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvest Form Submission to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign objectives include credential access; article describes expansion suggesting refined harvest tactics ('expands attacks' implies iterating tactics). No credential-access detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests from users to newly registered domains or known attacker IPs with parameters matching credential forms (username, password, otp, mfa). Correlate timing with phishing email delivery and user's email domain.

suggestion.title: User Execution of Malware from Phishing Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns often deliver malware alongside or instead of credential harvesting. Article body truncation prevents confirming presence of payloads, but multi-geography targeting suggests potential malware distribution. No execution detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of files (EXE, DLL, ZIP, RAR, VBS, JS) downloaded or created by email clients within 5 minutes of phishing email delivery. Flag Office applications spawning cmd/powershell/cscript as child processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Link Click Detection in TA4922 Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Users clicking links in phishing emails is the execution step; multi-target campaign inherently involves link-based attack flow. Pipeline failed to surface T1204.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for users navigating to newly registered domains, high-entropy subdomains, or known phishing hosting providers within seconds of email delivery timestamp. Alert on redirects to credential-harvest or malware-distribution sites.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Phishing Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country targeting by organized actor implies post-compromise lateral movement. Article title suggests coordinated campaign requiring persistence/reconnaissance after initial compromise. No post-access techniques flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password spray or brute-force attempts against cloud identity providers 6–48 hours post-phishing delivery. Flag lateral tool transfers (file copies, RDP/SSH tunnels) from user account compromised by phishing.

suggestion.title: Spoofed Organization Email Header in TA4922 Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Phishing efficacy relies on trusted-sender impersonation targeting business users in UK/Germany/Italy/South Africa. Article describes geographic expansion implying refined social engineering. No spoofing-detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails where visible 'From' field (display name) claims legitimate organization but authentication headers (DMARC/SPF) fail or domain differs. Look for high-volume sends to finance, HR, or executive mailboxes within target countries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited in real-world attacks' with mechanism 'insecure deserialization of untrusted data'—no detection logic for exploitation payload attempts against vulnerable Magento endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Magento paths associated with Mirasvit cache warmer (/*cache*warmer* or /mirasvit/*) containing serialized object patterns (PHP serialize markers, gadget chains). Correlate with anomalous HTTP responses and subsequent child process execution from web-server workers.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command Execution from Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE capability enabling 'remote code execution' but no execution-phase detection for post-exploitation commands spawned by exploited PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned by Magento web-server workers (apache2, nginx, php-fpm). Flag inline execution without staged script files, execution of archival/exfil tools, or process chains suspicious for post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Extension File Tampering or Malicious Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension' as attack vector. Threat actors may modify or replace extension files for persistence or inject additional payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento extension directories (/app/code/Mirasvit/, /vendor/mirasvit/) for unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion outside normal patch windows. Alert on hash mismatches of core extension files or extension enable/disable from non-admin IPs.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure – Magento Instances with Vulnerable Mirasvit Extension
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45247 'critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting the Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension for Magento'—asset inventory hunt referenced in briefing but not instantiated with structured detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability databases for Magento instances with CVE-2026-45247 explicitly flagged OR Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installed (via extension enumeration). Prioritize internet-facing instances for urgent patching or removal.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—public exploits are actively weaponized; zero initial-access detection was generated for this critical vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified Communications Manager endpoints for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20230 exploit signatures. Alert on requests to vulnerable API endpoints or specific parameter injection patterns documented in public PoC code.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution on Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms public exploit availability, implying imminent execution attempts; zero execution-phase detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned from Cisco Unified CM application containers (java.exe, tomcat processes). Monitor for shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) with suspicious command-line arguments indicating code execution from web context.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Unified CM Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: CVE in critical VoIP platform suggests code-execution risk for persistence; no persistence-phase detection suggested.
log_sources: Cisco Unified CM binary audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor core Unified CM binary directories (/opt/Cisco/UnifiedCM/...) for unauthorized file writes or binary modifications outside scheduled patch windows. Alert on new service/process creation under Unified CM context with suspicious network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM's network position (core VoIP infrastructure) enables rapid pivot to internal systems; zero lateral-movement detections despite high criticality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Unified CM initiating SMB, RDP, or SSH connections to non-telephony infrastructure (file servers, DCs, workstations). Monitor for Unified CM service account Kerberos delegation attempts or unusual cross-VLAN traffic origination.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Call Metadata and Credentials from Unified CM Database
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM stores call records and user credentials; exploitation risk includes data exfiltration; no collection/exfiltration detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database access logs for abnormal query volume or bulk extraction of call records, voicemail configs, or user credentials. Alert on encrypted outbound connections from Unified CM to external IP ranges during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service via CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Patch availability indicates vulnerability impact; article states 'Critical' but zero impact-phase detection for service degradation or system crash scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM service availability, uptime metrics, and error logs for sudden degradation post-exploitation. Alert on repeated crash dumps, memory exhaustion, or resource saturation patterns consistent with fuzzing or resource-exhaustion payloads.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - Suspicious WebDialer HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' Direct attack vector; need HTTP request anomalies to WebDialer endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer service endpoints for SSRF patterns: URL-encoded paths, file:// or gopher:// protocols in parameters, localhost/127.0.0.1 target addresses, and path traversal sequences. Baseline legitimate WebDialer usage and alert on significant deviations in request structure or target resources.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - Unauthorized File Writes from WebDialer Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' Direct exploitation indicator via file-write side-effect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and modification initiated by Cisco Unified CM WebDialer/Tomcat process. Alert on writes to /etc, /root, /opt/cisco, startup script directories, and credential storage paths. Baseline legitimate WebDialer file activity and detect writes outside normal patterns or to sensitive system directories.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - Privilege Escalation from WebDialer to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation 'could allow the attacker to write files...used later to elevate to root.' Root-level privilege acquisition is the attack goal and highest-impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent process is Unified CM WebDialer or Tomcat service spawning child processes with root (uid=0) privileges. Alert on su/sudo invocations, execution of privilege-escalation utilities (chmod, chown, useradd) originating from Unified CM service context.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - WebDialer Service Activation and Enablement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled, and WebDialer is disabled by default.' Attacker must enable service or compromise already-enabled instances; service state changes are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebDialer service enablement or re-enablement outside planned change windows. Monitor Cisco Unified CM Administration interface access followed by CTI service activation. Track unexpected WebDialer restart or start events from non-administrative contexts or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - Critical Configuration or Credential File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file-write primitive enabling root escalation; attackers likely target startup scripts or privilege-control files. Configuration integrity monitoring is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to Cisco Unified CM system-critical files: startup scripts, service configuration, authentication modules. Alert on unexpected writes by WebDialer process to /etc/sudoers, cron directories, or LD_PRELOAD paths. Cross-correlate file modifications with HTTP request logs to the WebDialer service.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM - Anomalous Process Spawning from Tomcat/WebDialer
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker gains shell or command execution from WebDialer context. Monitor for unusual process spawning from normally non-interactive service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned from Cisco Unified CM Tomcat/WebDialer parent process. Monitor for execution of reconnaissance utilities (whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd), privilege-escalation tools, or network utilities from Unified CM service context.

suggestion.title: GitHub Issue Triggers Unexpected Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector is 'one malicious issue' that 'hijack[s] repositories' via GitHub Action—core attack chain. No detection generated for issue-to-workflow trigger exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub workflows triggered by issue_opened or issue_comment events with elevated permissions (contents: write, admin, or secrets access). Flag workflows that reference issue body/title directly without sanitization (e.g., ${{ github.event.issue.body }} in shell commands).

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access via GitHub Token in Untrusted Workflow
suggestion.rationale: 'Hijack repositories' implies attacker gains code-push or secret-modification capability. Article describes GitHub Action flaw; GITHUB_TOKEN and workflow permissions are the enabler. No detection for token abuse or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for modification of branch protection rules, secret creation/deletion, or push events from workflows triggered by untrusted event types (issues, pull requests from forks). Flag when GITHUB_TOKEN is used with write/admin permissions outside the default runner context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Injection via Issue Content in Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'one malicious issue.' This implies issue body/metadata contains payload that workflow unsafely executes. No detection for code injection via issue content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows that pass issue-related variables (issue.body, issue.title) directly to bash -c, eval, or similar command-execution functions. Alert on workflows with run: steps that interpolate untrusted GitHub event data without quoting or escaping.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Modification via GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'hijack repositories.' Hijacking implies unauthorized code changes, credential exfiltration, or workflow modification. No detection for anomalous repository writes triggered by GitHub Action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repository commits, branch deletions, or secrets modifications made by GitHub Actions triggered by external events (issues, PRs). Flag actions that modify .github/workflows/ files or branch protection rules. Alert on rapid multiple writes in short time window.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Exfiltrates Repository Secrets or Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking requires access to secrets/tokens. Pipeline detected no IOC or behavior pattern indicating credential exfiltration via GitHub Action logs or outbound traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions that transmit GITHUB_TOKEN, repository secrets, or SSH keys to external URLs, cloud storage, or third-party services. Flag workflows with curl/wget/git commands that send secrets in URL parameters, headers, or POST bodies to domains outside GitHub infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GTM Container Executes Payment-Stealing Code on Checkout
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page' — GTM's implicit trust and CSP bypass is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM container versions and payload for suspicious DOM manipulation on checkout pages, dynamic code loading, or form field access. Baseline known-good containers and alert on unsigned/unverified payload changes or containers querying payment provider APIs.

suggestion.title: Stripe API Abuse: Bulk Customer Record Creation with Card Data in Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend... stolen data is stored in metadata fields.' Stripe becomes exfiltration channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect customer.create API calls with metadata fields containing credit card-like strings (repeated 4-digit groups, MM/YY patterns, 3–4 digit CVV). Flag accounts with abnormally high customer creation rates or metadata containing PII outside legitimate business workflows.

suggestion.title: Checkout Form Fields Accessed and Card Data Captured
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number' — direct DOM access to sensitive form fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument checkout forms to intercept JavaScript reading credit card input fields, expiration fields, CVV fields, or billing address fields. Cross-reference accessed fields against known legitimate payment processor scripts. Alert on unexpected scripts accessing payment form data.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Data Staged in localStorage Before Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally' — characteristic signature of in-browser staging; 'the local file is wiped to eliminate traces.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor localStorage for large binary-like or hex-encoded strings in suspicious keys (starting with '_d_', 'data_', or '_customer_'). Correlate XOR bitwise operations in page JavaScript with storage of these values. Alert when localStorage is subsequently cleared within seconds of write.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Named 'tracking/captcha' Retrieved as Malicious Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app. The names of the document and the project help the malware blend in with legitimate payment and bot-protection traffic.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firestore API calls for document reads from collections with deceptive names mimicking legitimate services ('tracking/', 'braintree-', 'captcha', 'payment-app'). Flag access to these documents from pages not known to require bot protection. Inspect retrieved document content for executable code.

suggestion.title: Dynamic Code Execution via new Function() with Externally-Sourced Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'reads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function()' — pattern for loading malicious code from trusted infrastructure without explicit script tags.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect calls to new Function(), eval(), or Function.prototype.call where the function argument is assembled from multiple sources (API responses, metadata fields, query parameters). Correlate with prior retrieval from Stripe/Firestore. High-fidelity signal: new Function() with Stripe/Firestore response content.

suggestion.title: Detect bulk exfiltration of health insurance and PII databases
suggestion.rationale: Article: '234 GB of data' stolen; exposed 'Email addresses, Full names, Phone numbers, Government-issued IDs, Health insurance information, Genders, Dates of birth.' No detection UC created despite clear data collection and exfil phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusually large outbound data transfers or sustained egress over non-standard ports. Alert on access patterns to health insurance or PII repositories followed by external data transfer. Establish baseline for data volume and flag 100x+ deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized access to health records databases
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' compromised health insurance information and government IDs. Initial access phase not mapped to any detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual authentication to medical records systems, especially from non-standard IPs or out-of-hours access. Flag credential compromise or lateral movement landing on databases storing HIPAA-regulated data.

suggestion.title: Detect post-breach extortion activity from known leak site operators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site... data was publicly leaked' following failed negotiation. Impact phase (T1531-style extortion) not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor known dark web and data leak forums for ShinyHunters activity and newly listed victims. Correlate published dataset metadata (record count, data types, date ranges) to internal breach timelines. Alert on any DentaQuest or Sun Life entity postings within 90 days of incident discovery.

suggestion.title: Detect multi-source account compromise from recycled credential sets
suggestion.rationale: Article: '66% of exposed records were present in its database from past incidents affecting other organizations.' Indicates harvested credentials from prior breaches used in lateral access or initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference compromised usernames/emails from Have I Been Pwned feeds against internal authentication logs. Alert on successful logins from known-breached accounts, especially if login occurs from unusual geolocation or device.

suggestion.title: Detect healthcare provider network reconnaissance and lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Article: DentaQuest 'operates programs in 50 states, has a network of 140,000 dentists.' Attacker moved through 'limited portion of network' before exfiltrating central database. Lateral movement not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP, SSH, or SMB connections between dental provider endpoints and centralized systems. Flag lateral movement hops that traverse security boundaries or access administrative shares containing patient records.

suggestion.title: Detect defense evasion and incident containment timeline anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: Company states 'took immediate action to secure our environment, contain the attack' after discovery but breach occurred before 'June 2' confirmation. Detect attacker cleanup or log deletion during containment window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious log deletion, event viewer clearing, or diagnostic tool runs immediately before incident disclosure. Correlate timeline of system shutdown/maintenance against SIEM retention windows.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Open-Source Tool Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google.' Pipeline missed initial access indicator: users visiting domains with homoglyph/edit-distance similarity to legitimate tool hosts (GitHub, PyPI, npm, etc.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate open-source tool download domains. Flag DNS queries/connections to newly-observed domains with name similarity (homoglyph, typo variants) to these baselines, especially if source has no prior history of using the tool.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System Redirect Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deliver Malware via TDS' — pipeline should detect characteristic TDS behavior: conditional redirects based on browser fingerprinting, geolocation, user-agent, referer inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP redirect chains with TDS fingerprinting patterns: presence of geolocation parameters, user-agent inspection in request URIs, anomalous Set-Cookie usage for session tracking, variable redirect destinations per requester.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Typosquatted Download
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: fake site → TDS → malware. Pipeline missed execution phase: file downloaded and executed from misspelled tool domain
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file downloads from suspected typosquatted domains with execution events (process creation, DLL injection, child processes). Flag particularly: browser as parent, temp/Downloads directory as download location, executable or archive immediately unpacked and executed.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning: Malicious Domains Ranking for Tool Keywords
suggestion.rationale: Article: sites 'Rank High on Google' — this is SEO poisoning infrastructure, distinct from typical malware delivery. Should surface newly-registered domains achieving high search ranking for 'download [tool] free' queries
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly-registered domains appearing in top-20 Google results for open-source tool download keywords. Cross-reference domain age, registrar (especially bulletproof hosters), SSL certificate history, and WHOIS privacy indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Click Leading to Binary Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware spreads 'via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' but pipeline extracted no detection for the initial compromise vector. Article phrase: 'Spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads initiated from Google or YouTube ad-serving domains (doubleclick.net, googlesyndication.com, YouTube click-through URLs) that result in unexpected binary downloads (.dmg, .pkg, .zip) or shell script execution on macOS endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Browser Context (macOS)
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell backdoor execution pattern not captured. Once delivered via ad click, article implies execution—should detect browser spawning shell/daemon processes or writing to ~/Library/LaunchAgents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Safari, Chrome, or Firefox spawning /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or zsh with suspicious arguments, or writing executable files to temporary directories followed by execution.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent/Daemon Persistence by Non-System Process
suggestion.rationale: macOS backdoors typically persist via LaunchAgent (~/Library/LaunchAgents) or LaunchDaemon. Article does not specify persistence mechanism but HIGH severity implies persistence was established—detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons, or /Library/LaunchDaemons by non-system processes, especially those with plist files naming backdoor-like processes or containing network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Connections from Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell is a backdoor—must communicate with C2. No C2 detection use case generated despite 'backdoor' explicitly in title. Article phrase: 'FlutterShell Backdoor.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from LaunchAgent/Daemon processes to unknown or suspicious IP ranges, especially over non-standard ports (8080, 9090, 443 with mismatched SSL cert, etc.). Look for beaconing patterns (periodic connections at regular intervals).

suggestion.title: macOS Backdoor Command Execution and Shell Activity
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor by definition executes attacker commands. No detection for typical backdoor TTPs (shell invocation, credential theft, lateral movement) generated from article describing a backdoor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected sh/bash/zsh processes spawned by non-interactive system daemons, especially with suspicious arguments (curl, wget, nc, ssh). Correlate with unexpected binary downloads or in-memory code execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Browser-to-Disk-to-Execution Chain on macOS
suggestion.rationale: The attack chain starts with ad click. Complete chain (ad → download → write → exec) never mapped into a single detection rule despite being the core attack pattern described in the article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser process network traffic to ad-serving domains → unexpected file writes to /tmp or ~/Downloads → immediate execution of downloaded/unpacked binaries within seconds. High-confidence signal if chain completes within <60s.

suggestion.title: Stata process executing Python via malicious log_file_name injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can inject 'python' commands via log_file_name parameter: 'attacker can inject arbitrary Stata commands (including shell, python, erase, etc.)'. No UC targets python-specific execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Stata parent process spawns python.exe or python3 with suspicious command-line arguments referencing log files or temporary paths. Watch for Stata→python→file operations chain indicating data exfiltration or privilege escalation payload staging.

suggestion.title: Stata executing file deletion/erase commands via log_file_name injection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'erase' as injectable command: 'shell, python, erase'. No hunt addresses file deletion triggered by malicious parameter. Critical for integrity/evidence destruction attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File deletion events (ActionType=FileDeleted) initiated by Stata process with suspiciously-named parent or log_file_name parameter in memory/forensics. Correlate with absence of Stata.do file justifying deletion.

suggestion.title: Suspicious log_file_name parameter in Stata process command-line or API invocation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is parameter injection. Article states 'log_file_name parameter...directly interpolated...without sanitization'. Detection should inspect command-line for metacharacters in log_file_name before execution, not just post-exploitation signs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stata process creation or API calls (via instrumentation/logs) for log_file_name parameter containing regex [;|&$()`'"\n] or path traversal (../ or ..\). Detect before command injection executes.

suggestion.title: Stata do-file or log file containing quote or newline escape sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker injects via 'quotes, newline...'. GuardValidator scans do-file content but not log_file_name parameter. Detection of do-files containing Stata-native escape sequences for command boundary-breaking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Stata do-files or log files created with content matching Stata quote-escape patterns (e.g., `"` for double-quote literals, escaped newlines) that correlate with suspicious process execution. Indicates crafted payload staging.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Metadata Broadcast with XSS Payload — YPTSocket Debug Pane
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector as 'per-client metadata *broadcast* in YPTSocket Plugin' and notes payload 'executes arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing.' Current detection ignores WebSocket as the delivery mechanism. Article phrase: 'stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting via Per-Client Metadata Broadcast.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebSocket protocol upgrade requests to /plugin/YPTSocket/* endpoints. Alert when WebSocket frames contain HTML/JavaScript injection patterns (angle brackets, script tags, event handlers like onerror/onload) sent from unauthenticated sources to multiple connected clients (broadcast pattern).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Panel/Debug Endpoint Access — Pre-Auth XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' can inject payload. No detection explicitly hunts for absence of authentication on admin endpoints. Article phrase: 'any unauthenticated remote attacker' targeting debug pane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to /plugin/YPTSocket/* containing XSS payloads (query parameters with <script>, javascript:, etc.) where the source IP has no corresponding authenticated session cookie or auth token in preceding logs. Cross-reference proxy/WAF logs to confirm unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: Post-XSS Admin Session Cookie Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload executes in 'authenticated origin of every administrator' and lists T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie) as expected technique. No detection hunts for the exfiltration channel (data leaving the browser post-exploitation). Attack flow: XSS executes → steals cookies → sends to attacker.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) with POST requests to external/suspicious domains occurring within 5 minutes of YPTSocket plugin page load. Look for data-exfiltration patterns: hex-encoded cookies, base64 blobs, or repeated small POST requests from admin user sessions.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Store Access from Admin Sessions Post-XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1555.003 (Credentials from Web Browsers) as expected impact technique but no detection hunts for browser password manager interaction post-exploitation. XSS payload would need to extract stored passwords from browser vaults.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For admin user sessions that accessed YPTSocket pages, hunt for subsequent file access to browser profile directories (Chrome User Data, Firefox Profiles, Edge User Data) or suspicious process access to password manager processes (1Password, LastPass, KeePass) within 30 minutes of XSS payload window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Forwarding Rule Creation on Executive Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'spied on' mailbox for five months, implying ongoing exfiltration or passive monitoring via forwarding rule. No rule-creation detection rule generated despite this being the classic persistence mechanism in email compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Inbox Rules creation/modification by or targeting high-risk accounts (C-suite, finance, legal). Flag rules forwarding to external domains, particularly those matching attacker infrastructure patterns or bulk-deleting messages. Baseline: legitimate user rule updates outside compromise window.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Mailbox Access from New IP / Geo-Impossible Travel
suggestion.rationale: Five-month access window implies attacker accessed mailbox from persistent attacker infrastructure. Article contains no mention of detection of unusual access patterns—pipeline generated zero geographic-anomaly or IP-based detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA and ActiveSync logins on executive accounts for: (1) access from IPs inconsistent with user baseline, (2) geo-impossible travel (login from US followed by login from Asia within minutes), (3) access from known-malicious ASNs or hosting providers, (4) access outside user's typical business hours and geography.

suggestion.title: OAuth App Consent Abuse Granting Mail.Read Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Persistent remote access over five months likely required attacker to install a backdoor app or delegate access via OAuth; article specifies 'spied on' mailbox, suggesting ongoing access mechanism. Pipeline did not generate detection for suspicious app grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth consent grants (especially Mail.Read* and Mail.ReadWrite) by or on behalf of high-value accounts to apps with no prior integration history. Flag grants from untrusted publishers, apps with generic names ('Document Manager', 'Mail Helper'), or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegation or Send-As Permission Grant to Attacker Account
