suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'one malicious issue hijack repositories'—establishes issue-to-execution attack vector. Zero execution-phase UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows triggered by recent issues from new/low-rep accounts. Flag workflows accessing repository secrets, modifying protected branches, or making external network calls in post-issue context.

suggestion.title: Repository Hijacking via Unauthorized Commits or Deploy Key Addition
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'hijack repositories'—impact phase entirely absent from pipeline output. No detection for ownership/access changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git push/branch creation to protected refs correlating to issue-creation timestamp. Alert on unexpected deploy keys, collaborator additions, or repository fork/transfer post-malicious-issue.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking implies credential persistence. No UC for unusual token scope elevation, token usage, or secret exfiltration—common post-RCE pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GITHUB_TOKEN with elevated permissions (repo write, admin scopes) accessed by workflows spawned from non-standard trigger sources. Flag token logs for unusual clone/push activity post-workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Issue as Initial Access Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one malicious issue'—clear initial-access vector. Zero initial-access phase in kill-chain output; no account anomaly or payload signature UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on issue creation from newly-registered GitHub accounts. Flag issue bodies containing workflow YAML, shell syntax, or references to GitHub Action names. Correlate rapid issue-creation + workflow execution on same repo.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Embedded Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Attacker post-hijack would persist via workflow-on-schedule or event-reactive pattern. No persistence-phase detection generated despite predictable attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor additions or modifications to .github/workflows/*.yml files post-compromise. Alert on workflows scheduled on intervals, reacting to push/schedule, or with external callback hosts. Baseline workflow additions by repository and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code or Configuration Changes Post-Repository-Hijack
suggestion.rationale: After hijacking, attackers inject backdoors or exfil data. No UC for code integrity monitoring, secret modification, or configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate repository commit history post-malicious-issue with atypical committer accounts, unusual file modifications (config, secrets, deploy scripts), or additions of attacker-controlled dependencies.

suggestion.title: Stripe API Customer Creation with Metadata Containing Payment Card Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes payload exfiltration mechanism: 'creating a new Stripe customer object, and storing the stolen data in metadata fields' and 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account.' Direct IOC: `cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to api.stripe.com/v1/customers for metadata fields containing 16-digit numeric patterns (credit card format), CVV triplets, expiration dates, or email/phone combinations. Baseline legitimate Stripe usage by known merchant accounts. Alert on high-frequency customer creation from non-whitelisted origins with suspicious metadata payloads.

suggestion.title: Google Tag Manager Container Injection with new Function() JavaScript Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injection vector: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers...it reads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function().' GTM domains bypass CSP rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM tag deployments for code patterns: `new Function()`, `Function()` constructor, XOR byte operations, and api.stripe.com/firestore.googleapis.com API calls. Alert on containers accessing payment form fields (credit card, CVV, expiration) or creating Stripe/Firestore objects. Maintain baseline of legitimate container code per domain to detect injection.

suggestion.title: Firestore Payload Staging and Exfiltration via braintree-payment-app Project
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant: 'Google Firestore...is used instead of Stripe...The payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' Firestore provides alternative C2 and storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firestore.googleapis.com requests for projects containing payment-related keywords (braintree, stripe, payment, checkout, billing). Alert on document access patterns to tracking/captcha or similar paths. Detect documents containing Base64/encoded JavaScript or serialized credit card data. Correlate with GTM container modifications for injection confirmation.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Payment Data Stored and Cleared from localStorage
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies collection behavior: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally...Once the data is copied, the local file is wiped to eliminate traces.' Key: `_d_data_customer_`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser localStorage for keys matching patterns `_d_data_customer_`, `_stripe_*`, or similar payment-staging names. Detect XOR-encoded data by analyzing byte entropy and repeated write-then-delete patterns within 60-second windows. Alert on localStorage access followed immediately by clearItem() or setItem() with empty value—signature of evidence elimination.

suggestion.title: Magento/Adobe Commerce Checkout Payment Data Collection via Injected Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The card skimmer targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Magento/Adobe Commerce environments, monitor form submission events on checkout pages. Detect JavaScript accessing payment form fields (CC input, CVV, expiration, name) that originates from GTM tags not in baseline configuration. Alert on data being read from forms, concatenated, then sent to api.stripe.com or firestore.googleapis.com. Cross-reference against legitimate Stripe/Firestore requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Exfiltration Through Legitimate Payment Service Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article notes abuse of trust: 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters that would otherwise flag traffic to an unknown skimmer domain.' Both api.stripe.com and firestore.googleapis.com are implicitly trusted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate api.stripe.com and firestore.googleapis.com traffic per merchant by request method, payload size, and endpoint. Alert on POST requests creating customer objects or writing to Firestore immediately following checkout page load. Detect rapid sequential calls to stripe customer creation (e.g., >10 requests/minute) from single checkout page session. Correlate with GTM tag versions.

suggestion.title: Large-Volume Data Exfiltration to External Destination
suggestion.rationale: Article states '234 GB of data' was stolen and leaked—explicit signature of data exfiltration event against healthcare database
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained high-volume outbound transfers (>50 GB) from internal healthcare databases to external or suspicious IPs. Baseline typical egress from DentaQuest systems and alert on anomalies in volume, destination reputation, and transfer protocols.

suggestion.title: Bulk Database Export and Structured PII Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 2.6M records with consistent structured fields (email, full names, phone, government IDs, health insurance info, DOB) extracted—signature of database dump or bulk SELECT query
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single database sessions returning >10k member/patient records. Monitor for unusual export operations to staging files, bulk CSV/SQL dumps, or queries accessing combined PII + health insurance tables. Correlate with outbound file transfers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Lateral Movement Within Healthcare Network
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network'—indicates foothold-to-escalation chain; access to data repositories requires traversal
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual administrative RDP or SMB connections between non-adjacent systems, especially into database and file-server subnets. Alert on LSASS access attempts, credential dumping tool execution (mimikatz, procdump), and UAC bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Publication to Extortion Site
suggestion.rationale: Article states ShinyHunters 'listed the company on its data leak site' after failed extortion—detectable via threat-intelligence feeds and public leak-site monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to ShinyHunters leak site and other known extortion platforms for DentaQuest brand mentions. Cross-reference published leaks against internal employee/patient records. Track publication timelines for negotiation windows post-detection.

suggestion.title: Typosquat Domain Registration & Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools' — pipeline should detect registration of domains with character/word substitutions matching popular OSS project names (e.g., np-m.com for npm, typscript-lang.com for typescript). Pattern: Levenshtein distance, keyword overlap, phonetic similarity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on domain registration where domain name is <85% similar to known OSS tool (npm, webpack, docker, kubernetes, etc.) using edit distance or substring overlap. Cross-reference with domains achieving high Google SERP rank for queries containing tool name + 'download'.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via Traffic Direction System (TDS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Deliver Malware via TDS' — pipeline failed to map T1608.005 or detection for TDS behavioral patterns. TDS redirects users based on attributes (IP, user-agent, referrer) to different payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid IP-based redirect chains or 302/meta-refresh redirects from a single domain to multiple distinct payload hosting servers. Flag domains where response content varies based on source IP or user-agent header, indicating TDS logic.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Download Page Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pages 'Mimicking Open-Source Tools' — users are redirected to fake download pages. Pipeline missed detection for page spoofing (DOM similarity, CSS cloning, icon theft).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains hosting pages with high visual/structural similarity to legitimate OSS project pages (GitHub, npm, PyPI, Docker Hub). Flag downloads of suspicious executables (.exe, .msi, .dmg) from typosquat or newly-registered domains within 7 days of initial resolution.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Fake OSS Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery endpoint — final payload execution occurs post-download. Pipeline should detect execution of unknown binaries originating from non-official OSS domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of binaries downloaded from domains registered <30 days ago or domains with character-substitution similarity to OSS tool names. Correlate with file hash reputation queries; flag if VirusTotal AV evasion score >0 or low detection ratio.

suggestion.title: Search Engine Result Manipulation / Ranking Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Rank High on Google' — suggests SEO poisoning or search result injection. Pipeline did not propose detection for abnormally-elevated SERP rankings of typosquat domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor enterprise browsers for clicks on SERP results from domains <90 days old, where domain name closely matches a popular OSS tool. Alert if top-5 SERP results for common tool names (npm install, docker download) include newly-registered or suspicious-whois domains.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon from TDS-Delivered Malware
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivered via TDS must call home for command or exfil. Pipeline did not suggest detection for post-execution C2 communication patterns from payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file downloads from typosquat domains with subsequent outbound network connections to known malware C2 IPs/domains or to infrastructure matching TDS pattern (rapid redirect chains, geo-based content variation).

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Redirect to Payload Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'—initial access vector that requires detection at click and redirect chain level before user execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ad-network referrer (google.com, youtube.com) followed immediately by redirect to untrusted domain and file download (DMG, PKG, or executable). Look for anomalous geolocation of C2 or newly-registered redirect domains. High-priority if download occurs to /Downloads or temporary directory.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Process Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor identified by name 'FlutterShell' in title; no detection use case for its process spawning, command-line arguments, or parent-child relationships despite being the core malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS process creation for unsigned binaries or suspicious code-signing certificates pretending to be legitimate macOS apps. Correlate process name with known app names (e.g., pretending to be system utility or popular software). Flag parent processes from browsers or apps associated with malicious ads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LaunchAgent or LaunchDaemon for macOS Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article implies backdoor persistence on macOS; no detection for common macOS persistence mechanism (LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or ~/Library/LaunchServices with suspicious executable references. Correlate timing with malware download events. Flag plist entries executing unsigned binaries from /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell requires network communication to C2 servers; no IOCs provided and no network-based detection use case for C2 beacons or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from suspicious processes (parent = malicious DMG/ad-delivered binary) to non-standard ports (not 80/443) or newly-registered domains. Monitor for beaconing behavior (periodic connection attempts at regular intervals). Flag C2 IPs geolocated outside expected enterprise regions.

suggestion.title: macOS Quarantine Bypass or Code-Signing Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivered via ad-redirected download would trigger macOS Gatekeeper/quarantine; no detection for xattr manipulation (com.apple.quarantine removal) or code-signing circumvention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for xattr command execution removing quarantine flags, or direct xattr binary manipulation. Detect execution of binaries missing expected code-signing certificates or signed by untrusted CAs. Flag installation scripts using 'sudo' followed by disabled gatekeeper checks.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Backdoor to External C2
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors typically steal credentials, system info, or user files; no collection/exfiltration detection despite backdoor nature of malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process reading from credential storage (/Library/Safari, ~/.ssh, keychain access via security command) combined with outbound network connections to C2. Monitor for unusual data egress volume from suspicious processes. Correlate process lineage with malware delivery artifacts.

suggestion.title: MCP-for-Stata API/CLI log_file_name parameter contains shell injection metacharacters
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker can inject arbitrary Stata commands...by crafting a malicious log_file_name containing quotes, newline…' The injection occurs at parameter-passing time, pre-exploitation. Must detect at API invocation or CLI argument parsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on stata_do() API calls or CLI invocations where log_file_name argument contains regex ['"`\n;|&$()\\]. Match on both escaped and literal quote/newline/semicolon combinations. Baseline legitimate log_file_name patterns first.

suggestion.title: GuardValidator bypass: do-file validation passes while log_file_name contains injection syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'The security guard (GuardValidator) only scans the do-file content but does not validate this parameter.' This is a specific layered validation failure. Detectable by correlating validation success on do-file with suspicious log_file_name values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect do-file content that passes GuardValidator checks paired with log_file_name parameters containing path-traversal sequences (.., /), quotes, or command separators. Indicates intentional bypass.

suggestion.title: Stata shell or python command injection via log_file_name post-exploitation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions attacker can inject 'shell, python, erase' commands. These are specific to Stata command context and abnormal when triggered from log_file_name context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stata processes for python or shell commands where the command string or environment variables contain fragments of log_file_name syntax (escaped quotes, newlines rendered as literal text). Look for pattern: shell command + evidence of string-injection origin.

suggestion.title: Stata erase command with dynamically-constructed path matching log_file_name pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injection enabling 'erase' command execution. This is Stata-specific and forensically distinct—erase with a path derived from user input is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Stata erase commands with log_file_name parameter values: erase command filepath should NOT contain fragments from the log_file_name parameter under normal usage. Match on path segments, quoted values, or path-traversal sequences.

suggestion.title: MCP-for-Stata vulnerable version detection in application inventory
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47708 affects a specific component. Asset exposure is the first phase mentioned in the article recommendations ('Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify instances of MCP-for-Stata (any version not yet patched for CVE-2026-47708) in application inventory, requirements.txt, pip freeze output, or package manifests. Flag systems with log_file_name parameter usage in stata_do() calls as high-risk.

suggestion.title: WebSocket XSS Payload in YPTSocket Metadata Broadcast
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in 'per-client metadata broadcast' via WebSocket frames, not just URL parameters. Article: 'Stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting via Per-Client Metadata Broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin.' Pipeline should detect XSS patterns (script tags, event handlers, javascript: protocols) in WebSocket message content targeting YPTSocket endpoints.
log_sources: Zeek notice/intel logs (http.log with WebSocket upgrade)
Proxy logs with WebSocket frame inspection
Browser console/DOM mutation logs if available
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSocket traffic to YPTSocket plugin endpoints for message content containing `page_title`, `webSocketSelfURI` or similar metadata fields with XSS payload signatures (encoded/unencoded HTML tags, event handlers, javascript: scheme). Cross-reference admin user sessions viewing the online-users debug pane.

suggestion.title: Access to YPTSocket Online-Users Debug Pane with XSS Parameter Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting...in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing a page that renders the YPTSocket online-users debug pane.' The debug pane is the rendering context; should detect admin access to this specific component concurrent with malicious parameter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to `/plugin/YPTSocket/*` endpoints containing XSS payloads in `page_title` or `webSocketSelfURI` parameters with subsequent admin-user session activity. Flag if the request originates from non-admin IP or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie Exfiltration via DOM XSS in Admin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: XSS executes 'in the authenticated origin of every administrator,' enabling cookie theft (T1539). Pipeline listed T1539 as inferred technique but generated no detection. Should detect post-XSS credential access.
log_sources: HTTP request logs (exfil-shaped requests from admin sessions)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual XHR/Fetch requests from admin user sessions to external domains or internal credential-storage endpoints shortly after YPTSocket XSS injection. Look for `document.cookie` or WebStorage API access patterns in browser logs if available.

suggestion.title: Browser executable download from typosquatted security-tool domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The moment a user clicks the download button, something very different happens'—direct executable delivery from fake sites. No detection for browser → download → execute chain from ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, ilspy.org.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser process (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, firefox.exe) creating executable file in Downloads folder, followed by execution of that file within 5 minutes. Match download domain against IOC list (ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, ilspy.org, etc.).

suggestion.title: Web access to lookalike security-tool domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'convincing fake websites that impersonate popular security tools'—users must reach these sites first. Early warning on access to ghidralite.com, dnspy.org before download/execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS resolution or HTTP requests to domains with typo-pattern similarity to legitimate tools (e.g., ghidra→ghidralite, dnspy→dnspy.org with .org TLD anomaly). Correlate to user context to identify target.

suggestion.title: Known malware hash execution from Download folder
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes. No mention of hash-based detection integration despite 12 file indicators provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or execution of files matching any provided SHA256 hash. Prioritize files in Download/Desktop folders. Alert immediately on execution.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to known malware C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 4 IPv4 C2 addresses (217.156.122.75, 94.231.205.229, 194.150.220.218, 185.161.251.58) and 31 C2 domains. No network-based detection to catch post-execution C2 callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP to C2 IPs and domains. Correlate to process execution context and file hash to confirm malware chain. Alert on any connection to IP:port or domain from non-browser process.

suggestion.title: Rapid process execution after download completion
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware downloads then executes 'the moment a user clicks the download button.' Gap between legitimate file-in-cache and suspicious immediate execution warrants detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation (from browser) immediately followed (<30s) by execution of that same file path. Flag high-confidence execution from Download folder that matches malware IOC domains or hashes.

suggestion.title: Browser redirect chain to malicious domain
suggestion.rationale: Fake sites may use redirects to obfuscate destination. Article doesn't detail redirect chains, but common in typosquatting campaigns. Detection gap for multi-hop phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP redirect chains (30x responses) where initial click is to legitimate domain but final destination is IOC domain. Flag cross-domain redirects ending at typosquatted sites.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegation to External or Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'spied on...for five months,' indicating sustained unauthorized access. Attacker requires persistence vector independent of original compromise method. Mailbox delegation (Set-MailboxPermission, Add-MailboxFolderPermission) is canonical persistence mechanism in email compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mailbox folder delegation grants to newly created accounts, external mail addresses, or service principals. Monitor for FullAccess or SendAs permissions granted to non-executive accounts within 7 days of suspected compromise onset.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rules Forwarding to External Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'spying on' mailbox for months; passive email forwarding (New-InboxRule -ForwardTo external@domain.com) enables continuous data exfiltration without active session. Aligns with 5-month observation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation targeting external domains, especially with -RedirectTo or -ForwardTo parameters. Flag rules applying to All inbox items or rules created by non-executives on executive mailboxes.

suggestion.title: Impossible-Travel Mailbox Access: Geographically Disparate Logins
suggestion.rationale: Five-month compromise requires attacker infrastructure in distinct geographic region. Article emphasizes 'executive's Outlook mailbox'—detect mailbox access events (login, folder opens, item reads) from IPs/locations inconsistent with executive's normal operating geography and separated by impossibly short travel times.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag mailbox access events where source IP geolocation is >500 km from user's registered location and accessed within minutes of previous login from distant region. Cluster alerts over 7-day rolling window.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Export via New-MailboxExportRequest
suggestion.rationale: Executive correspondence from a stock exchange holds market-sensitive and strategic value. Article does not specify exfiltration method, but bulk export is standard for archival of high-volume email theft lasting months.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on New-MailboxExportRequest or New-ComplianceSearchAction operations targeting executive mailboxes, especially if executed by service accounts or during off-hours. Monitor for PST export file creation >100MB.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Audit Logging Disabled or Purged
suggestion.rationale: Undetected 5-month compromise suggests attacker disabled or deleted audit trail. Article's lack of mentioned detection method implies logging was circumvented—detect removal of audit evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Set-Mailbox -AuditEnabled:$false or Search-UnifiedAuditLog purges targeting executive accounts. Alert on admin account removing audit logs for mailboxes it doesn't normally manage.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Theft or Abnormal Device Registration
suggestion.rationale: Initial compromise of a senior executive's secure account (stock exchange environment implies MFA/hardened access) typically requires credential theft or OAuth app authorization. Five-month persistence suggests token-based auth maintained access without re-entry of credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Outlook/Exchange app OAuth token registrations from new device IDs never before associated with user. Flag device registrations from geographies inconsistent with user's location history. Monitor for successful sign-in to Outlook from unregistered device within 7 days of compromise window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Visitation — Masqueraded Anthropic Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spoofed Anthropic install page' + 'SEO poisoning'—T1036 masquerading should detect traffic to download.version-516.com and oakenfjrod.ru.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to download.version-516.com and oakenfjrod.ru. Correlate with users who visited these domains via search referrers (indicating organic search discovery). Flag any successful file downloads from these domains to Downloads / Temp.

suggestion.title: Fake Installer Execution from Downloads Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'user downloads' and 'fake installer'—T1204 User Execution. Users execute suspicious installers disguised with vendor names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation from typical download paths (Downloads, Temp, AppData\Local\Temp) with file names mimicking legitimate vendor installers ('Claude-setup.exe', 'Anthropic-install.msi', 'version-516-installer.exe'). Correlate parent process (browser or WinRAR) with child execution and subsequent spawning of tools (rundll32, powershell, cscript).

suggestion.title: In-Memory .NET Infostealer Execution Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fileless .NET infostealer'—T1218 Signed Binary Proxy Execution + T1059 Command Scripting. .NET assemblies loaded into memory via reflection without disk drops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-.NET system processes (svchost, dllhost, rundll32, wmiprvse) loading clr.dll / mscorwks.dll / clr.ni.dll (CLR runtime). Hunt for PowerShell processes with -EncodedCommand or -Command flags executing .NET via reflection (Assembly.Load, Activator.CreateInstance). Correlate with subsequent file-access attempts to browser databases.

suggestion.title: Initial SEO Poisoning and Phishing Page Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use SEO poisoning to push a spoofed Anthropic install page to the top of search results'—T1566 Phishing via malicious search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query proxy / firewall logs for HTTP requests to download.version-516.com and oakenfjrod.ru with search-engine referrers (google, bing, duckduckgo) and Anthropic / Claude / Code keywords in query strings. Identify temporal clustering indicating campaign volume.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Download from Malicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications'—establishes delivery via app downloads. Pipeline missed initial_access layer. Need detection for .app/.dmg/.pkg downloads from known-malicious domains to ~/Downloads or /tmp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HTTP(S) GET/POST originates from non-browser process to a known-malicious domain followed by file creation in download or temporary directories. Correlate DNS resolution of malicious domain with binary file writes within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Launch Agent Persistence Installation by Suspicious Application
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'backdoor on infected machines' but no persistence technique mapped. macOS backdoors persist via LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plists; pipeline completely missed T1547.014.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ initiated by recently-downloaded unsigned binaries or applications from non-standard paths. Alert if plist references binaries in /tmp, /var/tmp, or user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Application Execution (Unsigned or Forged Code Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fake desktop applications'—implies trojanized impersonation. Pipeline missed T1036 entirely. Detect execution of binaries claiming to be legitimate apps but with invalid/missing signatures or execution from non-standard locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when process executes from /tmp/, /var/tmp, ~/Library/Caches, or ~/Downloads/ with a display name matching known-legitimate applications (Chrome, VS Code, Slack) but lacking valid Apple code signature or issued by developer outside Apple's certificate authorities.

suggestion.title: Beaconing C2 Traffic Patterns from Suspicious Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoor; T1071 is listed but no detection hypothesis provided. Pipeline missed C2 beaconing detection for repeated connections to malicious domains from non-standard processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated outbound connections (interval 5–300 seconds, consistency > 70%) to low-traffic domains with low-entropy names or known-malicious domains from processes spawned by recently-downloaded applications or launched from temporary directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ad Click Redirect Chain Ending in Binary Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using Google Ads' as attack vector. Pipeline ignored the initial_access chain (ad platform → redirect → malware download). Detect browser redirects from ad networks to malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user browsing to Google Ads platform (or similar ad networks) with DNS queries/HTTP requests to known-malicious domains within 60 seconds, followed by file creation of .dmg/.pkg/.app in user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Dubiously-Signed Binary Execution from Non-Standard Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes fake apps as delivery mechanism; no execution-phase detection suggested. Pipeline missed T1036.005 (Masquerading - Match Legitimate Name or Location). Detect execution of unsigned binaries in /tmp or ~/Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where parent is a recently-downloaded .app bundle or where binary resides in temporary/downloads directories without valid Apple code signature or with signature issued by non-trusted certificate authority.

suggestion.title: Firewall: Outbound connection to KongTuke C2 IP and port
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco Secure Firewall telemetry recorded outbound ConnectionEvents to "144.31.221.82" on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856' as the foundational indicator. This is the network-layer detection that triggered investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound firewall connections to 144.31.221.82:6060. Include known malicious IP/port combinations. Raise confidence if URL path matches /capcha* or similar TDS patterns, or if correlated with EDR process indicators (cmd→powershell→curl chain).

suggestion.title: EDR: cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with Base64-encoded command
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'A cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload' as a direct observable from endpoint telemetry during the KongTuke intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe parent creating powershell.exe with '-EncodedCommand' or '-enc' flag in command line. Decode and inspect Base64 payload for suspicious cmdlets (IEX, Invoke-WebRequest, DownloadString). Correlate with firewall C2 destination to reduce false positives from legitimate admin tooling.

suggestion.title: EDR: Invoke-WebRequest file drop to ApplicationData + post-execution cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory' followed by 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' Classic LOTL staging with anti-forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Invoke-WebRequest or curl.exe writing .ps1 or executable files to %APPDATA%\* or Temp directories. Flag if followed by Remove-Item on same file within 5 minutes. High confidence if process chain originates from cmd→powershell and destination matches known C2.

suggestion.title: Multi-source: curl.exe process C2 communication correlated with firewall alert
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged' and notes 'Why neither source alone was sufficient—The firewall saw an outbound connection to a suspicious IP...The EDR saw obfuscated PowerShell execution...Together, they told a complete story.' Multi-domain correlation is core to the hunting methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate EDR process execution (curl.exe on non-developer workstations; developer tools in non-dev contexts) with firewall outbound connections to the same destination IP. Alert if destination is known malicious ASN or C2 infrastructure. Requires multi-source visibility.

suggestion.title: Behavioral: DGA domain detection via statistical entropy and n-gram analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article describes this as an explicit hunting hypothesis: 'Domain generation algorithm (DGA) detection via AI/ML. Algorithmically generated domains have statistical properties (character distribution, entropy, n-gram frequency) that distinguish them from human-registered domains. Our models flag DNS queries that match these patterns.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply ML model to DNS query domains, scoring for high entropy and abnormal n-gram distributions. Distinguish from benign domains via statistical baselining per environment. Flag queries to domains with unusual character entropy or rare n-gram patterns consistent with algorithmic generation.

suggestion.title: Hunting: MSIEXEC User-Agent outbound to malicious ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs' and 'MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.' This is a specific LOTL technique paired with ASN-based hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall logs for HTTP/HTTPS requests with User-Agent header 'MSIEXEC' or matching msiexec patterns. Alert if destination ASN is in known-bad list (e.g., EVILEMPIRE ranges). High signal because MSIEXEC user-agent in external communication is rare in legitimate environments.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Execution During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'binding.gyp' as attack vector. binding.gyp triggers native compilation (node-gyp, C++ compiler) as part of npm install, creating observable process chains. Pipeline should detect: compiler processes spawned from npm.exe/node.exe, especially from low-reputation or newly-created packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node-gyp, gcc, cl.exe, or clang child processes spawned during npm install from packages without established history or from accounts with no prior publish history. Correlate to binding.gyp presence in package manifest.

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating Package Behavior Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states attack 'spreads like a worm,' indicating self-replication. This manifests as a single package install triggering modifications to sibling packages in node_modules or rapid cascading package updates/publishes to npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes outside a package's own node_modules subdirectory during or immediately after install. Flag outbound HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org with npm publish/tag commands originating from build hosts.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: npm packages execute arbitrary code via 'postinstall', 'install', 'build' lifecycle scripts in package.json. A worm-propagation mechanism would leverage these entry points—article describes self-spreading, implying scripted execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell (cmd, powershell, bash) spawned by npm with encoded/obfuscated arguments, curl/wget downloading remote payloads, or modification of package.json in other packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Authentication or Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading worm must replicate by publishing new or modified packages. Detection should capture programmatic npm CLI publish operations or stolen/leaked npm tokens used to push malicious variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST to api.npmjs.com with npm package payloads, especially from CI/CD or development hosts lacking typical npm publishing workflows. Flag npm token exfiltration or use from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Package Lockfile Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: npm package-lock.json or yarn.lock records hash integrity of installed packages. Malicious on-the-fly modification would cause hash mismatches against expected values in lock files or npm registry metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect discrepancies between package-lock.json integrity hashes and actual installed package hashes. Flag when npm install bypasses hash checks or when registry-published package differs from locally installed version.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from node_modules Processes
suggestion.rationale: Worm-type malware establishes C2 or exfiltration channels. Detection should capture network connections spawned from processes executing within node_modules, particularly during initial package install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and outbound connections (HTTP, HTTPS, custom ports) from child processes of npm.exe or processes with node_modules in their working directory. Flag domains registered <30 days or with low reputation scores.

suggestion.title: Suspicious preinstall Hook Execution in npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'executed via preinstall' script that 'pushing malicious commits into repositories.' Preinstall hooks executing Rust ELF binaries are anomalous and directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install and yarn install flows for preinstall scripts spawning non-scripted binaries (especially ELF/compiled code in node_modules). Flag execution of Rust or compiled binaries from package source trees. Baseline legitimate preinstall scripts and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access in Development or CI Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article names 20 specific file types: 'SSH keys, vault configuration files, OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials.' Process reading patterns across these paths are directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI and developer environments, alert on single process reading multiple credential files in sequence: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, .env* files, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npm/*, .npmrc, ~/.anthropic*. Correlate reads across 3+ distinct credential types.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration to External IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mechanism: malware 'serializes secrets into a file...writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name...uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs and artifact API calls for uploads immediately following process execution or file writes. Alert if artifacts are downloaded from external IPs outside the organization's IP range or CI provider ranges. Correlate timing: file create → artifact upload → external download within same workflow run.

suggestion.title: Tor Communication from npm Install or CI Pipeline Process
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms malware 'communicates with operator over the Tor network.' Outbound Tor connections from package manager or CI environment processes indicate command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to Tor entry/exit nodes from npm, node, or yarn processes. Flag DNS queries for .onion domains from CI runners or developer machines. Cross-reference Tor node IPs against outbound traffic logs from build systems.

suggestion.title: Git Commit Timestamp Anomaly (Historical Dates, Recent Push)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Timestamps in git metadata decoupled from actual push time are evasion indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In git audit logs, detect commits with author/commit dates >90 days (or >1 year) in the past but authored_timestamp or pushed_timestamp from current day. Flag repositories where commit date and push date differ by >365 days. Alert on bulk commits with identical age discrepancies across multiple packages.

suggestion.title: npm Trusted Publishing Workflow Abuse from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Legitimate publishing from unexpected CI contexts or unusual identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish operations (via npm CLI or API) from CI/development environments for: (1) publishes from accounts that have not published in >30 days, (2) publishes triggered by unfamiliar CI runner identities, (3) multiple package versions published in rapid succession (>5 in <1 hour), (4) version bumps that bypass semver validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Injection in binding.gyp
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)form runs a shell command during the configure phase' and 'The compromised packages abuse this directly.' This is the core execution evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node or node-gyp processes spawning shell/cmd.exe children during npm install with binding.gyp files containing <!(command) syntax. Cross-reference with package.json to detect binding.gyp presence without corresponding preinstall/postinstall scripts (evading traditional hooks).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Across Multi-Platform Stores During Install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists: 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes'—targeting diverse credential storage locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from npm/node-gyp context accessing credential files: ~/.npm, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube/config, HashiCorp Vault configs. Alert on access patterns consistent with bulk enumeration rather than normal developer workflow.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence'—malware modifies GitHub Actions configuration to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files during or shortly after npm install execution, especially in CI/CD contexts. Flag workflows that execute immediately after modification and contain suspicious exfiltration or persistence logic.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation: Rapid Package Version Inflation and Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach' with evidence of artificial version bumps—'autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range, or autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple package versions published to npm registry from a single maintainer account within seconds/minutes, especially with version number increments that deviate from semantic versioning patterns (e.g., x.y.z jumping to significantly higher ranges). Cross-correlate with presence of binding.gyp in published tarballs.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Attacker-Controlled GitHub Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories'—stolen credentials are pushed to external repos controlled by threat actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls and git push operations originating from npm install contexts, especially those pushing credential-like patterns (AWS keys, JWT tokens, API credentials) to repositories not in organization allowlist. Alert on large data transfers to newly created or anonymous GitHub accounts.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Malware Installation via Lockfile Pins
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'any lockfile, exact pin, or transitive dependency that references a malicious version will still fetch the malware' even if 'latest dist-tag has since been pointed back at a clean release' and 'malicious versions have not been unpublished.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock files for resolved versions matching known malicious version ranges (e.g., @vapi-ai/server-sdk 0.11.1–0.11.2, ai-sdk-ollama 0.13.1, 1.1.1, 2.2.1, 3.8.5). Flag repositories with historical lockfile commits pinning affected versions, even if package.json specifies higher major versions.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Reputation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists SHA256/MD5 hashes with detection names and Talos reputation links. Phrase: 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoint telemetry for execution of files matching the four published malware hashes: Coinminer, Process Patcher, KMS activator. Cross-reference SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 and peers against Talos reputation API; alert on any execution or persistence attempt.

suggestion.title: Phishing-as-a-Service Kit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Kali365 explicitly named as FBI-flagged phishing platform now targeting AWS, Okta, Russian platforms via device code phishing. Phrase: 'FBI-flagged phishing kit "Kali365" expands its reach...while relying on device code phishing'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device code grant flows (RFC 8628 flows) and incomplete OAuth consent sequences. Alert on rapid authentication attempts to AWS STS, Okta, or cloud federation services preceded by user interaction with external links. Flag any MFA challenge followed by OOB approval request patterns consistent with device code phishing.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Official Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Red Hat NPM accounts compromised and weaponized to distribute worm that spreads machine-to-machine and harvests credentials. Phrase: 'Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel...used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized npm package uploads to official Red Hat accounts, unexpected version bumps without corresponding source commits, and rapid horizontal spread of package installations. Alert on suspicious child process spawning (npm install triggering shell execution) and subsequent credential enumeration (registry scanning, credential file access).

suggestion.title: Email Compromise via Native Windows Utilities
suggestion.rationale: Stock exchange finance executive email compromised using legitimate native Windows tools, granting threat actor near-continuous inbox access. Phrase: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell/cmd invocation with email API parameters (New-MailboxForwardingAddress, Get-Inbox, Set-InboxRule), unusual COM object instantiation for Outlook, or MAPI calls from non-trusted processes. Flag account enumeration (net user, dsquery) immediately preceding OWA/EWS access from suspicious IPs.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration via VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: One-click attack on GitHub.dev installs malicious VS Code extension that steals full OAuth tokens via webview message-passing mechanism. Phrase: 'One-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens...by exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of unsigned/untrusted VS Code extensions from users accessing GitHub.dev. Alert on abnormal GitHub API token generation, tokens used from unexpected geographic locations immediately after extension install, and rapid enumeration of private repositories or secrets using newly-issued tokens.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Protocol Amplification DoS
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 Bomb vulnerability affects 880,000+ sites running NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, or Cloudflare Pingora, can down servers in seconds. Phrase: '"HTTP/2 Bomb" exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds...affects over 880,000 websites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal HTTP/2 stream creation patterns without corresponding HEADERS/DATA frames, excessive RST_STREAM frames, or rapid connection cycling. Alert on memory exhaustion or CPU spike on web servers preceded by single-source or narrowly-distributed HTTP/2 connection bursts indicating amplification attack.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MCP Server or External Tool Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes agents continuously pull in MCP servers and external APIs 'not pre-approved' at runtime: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' CVE-2025-6514 exemplifies remote code execution via malicious MCP server. Missing detection for runtime tool selection anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual external API calls or MCP server instantiation during agent execution. Alert on agents pulling resources not in prior-approved allowlist. Track rapid tool installation or dynamic library loading initiated by agent processes.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Execution Without Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'execute actions autonomously and at machine speed' with 'broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' Replit incident: 'agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records.' Missing detection for unauthorized execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data-destructive or system-modifying commands (DROP TABLE, DELETE, rm -rf, terraform destroy, reset, purge) executed by agent process identities without preceding approval ticket or approval token. Track agent process execution speed and command chaining velocity.

suggestion.title: Rapid Code and Dependency Generation Velocity
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'AI produces code continuously at machine speed and often outside review processes' and 'vulnerable output may already be in repository' before scanning runs. Missing detection for generation speed anomalies that bypass human validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when agent processes commit or push code at velocity inconsistent with human developers (e.g., >100 files/min, >50 LOC/sec). Correlate rapid code commits with absence of code review approvals or scanning delays.

suggestion.title: Agent Policy Enforcement Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states controls must run 'close enough to evaluate context, permissions, and risk before an unsafe action completes' and highlights gap where agents ignore explicit instructions. Replit ignored 'freeze' instructions. Missing detection for policy violation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent process attempts to execute actions that conflict with active policy rules or guardrails. Track instances where agents retry blocked commands or attempt to circumvent approval mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Governance and Audit Trail Gaps in Agent Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'You need to prove what happened, why, and with what authority' but notes governance is often 'buried inside tooling or pushed downstream.' Missing detection for absent or incomplete audit evidence during agent actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent process executions that do not generate corresponding audit log entries, approval records, or context attribution. Alert when audit trails are missing, truncated, or delayed relative to actual execution.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secrets or Sensitive Data in Agent-Generated Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes agent-generated output 'may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' Missing detection for credential exfiltration via code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits or artifacts generated by agent processes for patterns matching API keys, database passwords, or tokens. Alert on agent-generated code containing unencrypted credentials or plaintext secrets.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Humanitarian Registration Databases
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households'—explicit data exfiltration across a large beneficiary dataset. Pipeline extracted no exfiltration use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registration database systems for anomalous volume or frequency of read operations by service accounts or admin users outside normal registration windows. Detect large data transfers (600k+ household records) exiting the network boundary via unusual protocols or destinations. Flag database queries selecting entire household tables or performing bulk exports.

suggestion.title: Web Application Attack on Public-Facing Registration Platform
suggestion.rationale: SRA is described as a 'self-registration application' used by beneficiaries in Gaza—internet-facing. Article confirms breach but does not disclose attack vector. Pipeline should have flagged T1190 exploitation as likely initial-access path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WFP SRA platform logs for exploitation indicators: SQL injection patterns in registration form parameters, directory traversal attempts, authentication bypass payloads, or suspicious HTTP methods. Alert on 4xx→200 transitions or abnormal response sizes that precede bulk data access.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise or Privilege Escalation in WFP Systems
suggestion.rationale: Breach timeline (May 14 detection) and scale (600k records) suggests either service-account compromise or privilege escalation to database-access tier. Article states platform 'temporarily suspended' for 'security and system protection improvements'—implies active persistence or lateral-movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new or dormant service accounts granted database-read privileges post-May 14. Flag privilege-grant events (ALTER ROLE, GRANT SELECT on beneficiary tables) issued outside change-control windows. Correlate admin logons from unusual geographies or off-hours access to registration system databases.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Campaign Against Affected Beneficiaries
suggestion.rationale: Article directly warns: 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money' and 'not click or open any suspicious links or messages.' Confirms expectation of social engineering against 600k exposed phone numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails/SMS impersonating WFP using beneficiary names, ID numbers, or neighborhood data stolen in breach (enables personalization). Flag messages requesting password reset, re-registration, or financial information. Track link-click and credential-entry events from affected Gaza phone numbers and correlate with threat actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access or Queries on Beneficiary Registration Tables
suggestion.rationale: Breach involved 'personal data belonging to beneficiaries' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information.' Pipeline should detect queries selecting these PII columns without proper audit trail or outside business-hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries against beneficiary tables (names, IDs, phone numbers, location fields) issued by non-standard service accounts or from unusual IP ranges. Flag queries with no WHERE clause or targeting entire household records. Baseline normal business queries and escalate statistical anomalies.

suggestion.title: Crafted File Upload to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' This is the explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to SD-WAN Manager upload endpoints followed by suspicious FileCreate events in admin or temp directories. Flag CSV, JSON, or script files uploaded to /home/admin/ or /tmp/ paths within minutes of failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Tenant List Upload Script Execution with Malicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article provides IOC: 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh executions where -cli path argument points to /home/admin/ or /tmp/ files. Parse /var/log/scripts.log for 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' pattern; this indicates active file upload exploitation.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allow local attackers with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as root' via command injection in uploaded files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning with UID 0 (root) from vmanage/admin user context without sudo/su intermediary. Correlate with prior file uploads, script execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh, or suspicious entries in /var/log/scripts.log within same time window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Push to SD-WAN Edge Devices Post-Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' This indicates post-exploitation lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate root-level process execution on SD-WAN Manager with subsequent configuration distribution to vSmart controllers or edge devices. Flag config pushes that lack corresponding management UI session logs or originate from unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Authentication Bypass CVEs as Prerequisite
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires: 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' These are prerequisite attack chains leading to netadmin privilege acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts or patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20182/CVE-2026-20127 exploitation (authentication bypass indicators from Cisco advisories) with subsequent successful netadmin-level API calls or file uploads within same session or IP.

suggestion.title: netadmin Group Account First-Use or Reactivation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges on the affected system.' Attacker either obtained valid netadmin creds or escalated to them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netadmin account activation (disabled→enabled state), first login after long dormancy, or credential resets. Flag subsequent API calls, file uploads, or script executions using that account within minutes of activation or reactivation events.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Indicator Detection via Domain Lookalikes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Sites' as primary attack vector. Pipeline surfaced no detection for domain registration patterns, homograph attacks, or credential-harvesting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains registered in bulk with FIFA/World Cup keywords, newly-registered .com/.net variants of official FIFA domains, and WHOIS privacy markers. Correlate with SSL certificate issuance timing and low Alexa/Majestic rank.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Banking Malware' as threat. Pipeline generated no behavioral indicators for C2 beaconing, credential-stealing malware signatures, or financial-malware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from workstations to known banking-malware C2 domains and IPs. Monitor for POST requests to suspicious URLs with financial keywords. Alert on SSL/TLS certificates with mismatched issuer/domain for banking sites.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Detection via HTTP Content Inspection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Stolen Logins' directly. Pipeline failed to propose detection of phishing-form traffic, credential submission patterns, or exfiltration of authentication material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing base64-encoded or URL-encoded credential pairs (username/password fields) sent to non-whitelisted domains. Flag requests to lookalike FIFA/ticketing domains followed by credential strings.

suggestion.title: Malware File Delivery via Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware delivery typically precedes C2; article mentions malware threat but pipeline did not propose email-based delivery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with .exe, .dll, .scr attachments or macro-enabled Office documents sent with FIFA-related subject lines. Correlate with attachment names containing 'ticket', 'world cup', 'registration'.

suggestion.title: Unusual Login Activity Post-Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials stolen; no use case proposed for post-breach account access anomalies or geographic/velocity-based login abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logins from new geographies, new devices, or unusual hours following credential-exposure indicators. Implement risk-scoring for FIFA-related account login anomalies.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory File Upload Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes critical plugin flaw enabling site takeover; exploitation typically involves file upload to /wp-content/plugins/ or derivative paths. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this foundational attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ directories with file upload parameters, or FileCreate events under WordPress plugin paths from web server processes. Correlate with subsequent suspicious file access or PHP execution in that directory.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin User Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover via plugin RCE typically requires admin persistence. Article states 'take over sites' but pipeline missed detection for rapid admin account creation, which is the standard post-exploitation consolidation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WordPress admin user creation via wp-admin/user-new.php POST requests, wp_create_user() function calls in error logs, or direct wpusers database INSERT from web-server process context within minutes of plugin directory file activity.

suggestion.title: PHP Web Shell Execution in WordPress Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article references critical flaw enabling takeover; typical WordPress plugin exploits result in webshell deployment to /wp-content/plugins/ or theme directories. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process execution originating from /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ or unusual .php files in that path with web-accessible naming (shell.php, admin.php, etc.). Correlate with suspicious child process spawning (curl, wget, bash) or file enumeration activity.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Parameter Injection or Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'critical flaw'; without CVE details, typical Everest Forms exploits involve unauthenticated AJAX endpoints or parameter tampering. Pipeline did not generate input validation or AJAX monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Everest Forms AJAX endpoints (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=everest_forms_*) for POST requests with unusual payloads, missing nonce parameters, or requests from anonymous/unauthenticated sessions. Flag requests with shell metacharacters, base64 encoding, or PHP function names in parameters.

suggestion.title: WordPress Core File Modification Following Plugin Directory Access
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover implies attacker moved beyond plugin directory to achieve persistence or privilege escalation. Article does not detail this but pipeline should anticipate wp-config.php modifications or wp-load.php hooks, standard post-exploitation hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FileModified events on wp-config.php, wp-load.php, .htaccess, or wp-settings.php correlated temporally with file uploads to plugin directories. Alert on these core files modified by web server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) outside of deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Database Credential Extraction or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover requires database access for persistence; pipeline did not suggest monitoring for wp_users table reads or database connection string exfiltration, common post-exploitation objectives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server process for direct MySQL/MariaDB connections to localhost with SELECT queries on wp_users or wp_options tables, or outbound network connections from web process to non-whitelisted hosts on port 3306/5432. Flag if timing correlates with known exploit delivery window.

suggestion.title: Covert SMTP Relay Installation on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack outcome: 'covert SMTP relay network.' No detection for SMTP service installation, configuration changes, or listener setup on cloud VMs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud instances for execution of mail service installation (postfix, exim, sendmail on Linux; IIS SMTP on Windows) via package manager or binary copy, followed by configuration writes to SMTP listener ports (25, 587, 465). Correlate with cloud provider API logs showing instance modification permissions.

suggestion.title: Bulk Outbound SMTP Traffic from Cloud Tenant
suggestion.rationale: Covert SMTP relay requires sending mail at scale. Pipeline missed detection for anomalous egress on SMTP ports from multiple instances simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cloud instances initiating outbound connections on SMTP ports (25, 587, 465) to non-organizational SMTP servers, especially from 5+ instances in same tenant within 1-hour window. Exclude legitimate mail gateways via allowlist.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise Leading to Cloud Instance Hijack
suggestion.rationale: Title states servers are 'hijacked'—implies initial compromise via credential theft or service-account exploitation. Pipeline extracted no IOCs around compromised account usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MFA bypass, unusual geographic logins, or rapid API calls (DescribeInstances, GetInstanceMetadata, StartInstances) from service accounts within 24h of SMTP service deployment on cloud instances. Correlate with absence of corresponding IAM policy changes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Multiple Cloud Provider Accounts
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers hijacked across three cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) implies either supply-chain compromise, shared credential abuse, or multi-cloud backdoor. Pipeline failed to surface lateral movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect identical SSH keys, service-account credentials, or code deployed to instances across distinct cloud providers within short timeframe. Flag authenticated API calls using same credential principal across AWS, GCP, and Azure from unusual IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cloud Instance Startup Scripts
suggestion.rationale: SMTP relay must survive reboots. Pipeline missed detection for startup script injection on cloud instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud provider APIs for modifications to instance startup scripts, user-data, or cloud-init configurations. Alert on RunCommand, SendCommand, or equivalent RPC calls that inject shell scripts into existing instance metadata or init files.

suggestion.title: Detection of Commodity Malware or Botnet Framework on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: PCPJack likely dropped and persisted malware to enable SMTP relay capability. Pipeline extracted zero malware family names or binary indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SMTP relay activity with file writes to /tmp, /var/tmp, or temporary directories on cloud instances. Flag for presence of known botnet/malware families (Mirai, Gafgyt, Tsunami, or packed binaries) via cloud security agent telemetry.

suggestion.title: UC_RANSOM_NOTE_CREATION
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ransomware creates files 'its own decryptor cannot reliably restore'—ransomware notes (HOW_TO_DECRYPT.txt, RESTORE_FILES.html) are left behind; T1486 impact phase. No hunt detects characteristic ransom-note filenames co-occurring with bulk encryption. Article does not name a decryption service, implying attackers rely on reputation through notes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation with common ransom-note names (RESTORE_*.txt, HOW_TO_DECRYPT.*, README.TXT, DECRYPT_ME.*, RANSOM.TXT) within 10 minutes of bulk file modifications (T1486 activity). Pair with mass-encryption baseline for high-confidence detection. Filter out test environments.

suggestion.title: UC_REGISTRY_RUN_KEYS_PERSISTENCE
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) suggest post-encryption persistence mechanisms. No hunt targets HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce/Services registry writes paired with encryption activity. Common ransomware pattern to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reg.exe or regedit.exe process writes to HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run*, Services\, or HKCU Run* keys, within 15 minutes of detected encryption activity. Flag if parent process is rundll32, explorer, or system anomaly. Medium confidence; exclude domain admin tooling.

suggestion.title: UC_ENCRYPTION_PATTERN_DURATION
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes the ransomware's *flaw* (decryptor fails)—suggests sophisticated encryption logic or multi-pass encryption that may be detectable. No hunt looks for sustained, high-volume file-modification activity (hours-long encryption sweep). This pattern distinguishes ransomware from legitimate bulk operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained file modification/rename bursts across 4+ hour windows on individual endpoints (e.g., >1000 files/hour modified by single non-system process). Correlate file extensions pre- vs. post-modification (e.g., .doc → .doc.[random], .xlsx → .crypted). High-volume sustained activity distinguishes ransomware from backup/AV scans (which peak then stop).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection – TA4922 Spearphishing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'phishing attacks'; core initial-access vector entirely absent from pipeline output. Typical phishing campaigns include malicious links and credential-harvesting pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails for suspicious sender domains, typosquatting, and shortened URLs. Flag messages with untrusted external senders targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa recipients. Correlate with web-gateway click-through logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Anomalous Sign-in Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-driven campaigns imply credential harvesting. 'Expands attacks' suggests exploitation of harvested credentials, establishing need for credential_access and lateral_movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible travel (sign-ins from geographically distant locations within minutes of phishing click timestamps), off-hours access, and compromised-credential patterns post-campaign. Baseline each target region separately.

suggestion.title: Malicious Email Attachment Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Phishing often includes macro-enabled Office documents or archives. Article body truncated; no IOC data available, but attachment sandboxing alerts should have been flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with .docx, .xlsx, .zip containing nested Office files with macros, or PE executables. Cross-reference with external email gateways and sandbox detonation results.

suggestion.title: Domain Impersonation – Geographic Targets
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa likely abuse lookalike domains of financial institutions, government agencies, or regional businesses in those countries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from legitimate UK/German/Italian/South African bank/government domains. Flag DNS queries and HTTP connections to newly registered or recently updated typosquatting domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Cisco Unified CM RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM as Exploit Code Goes Public'—this is the core threat, yet zero use cases were generated to detect exploitation attempts or post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM administration and API endpoints for HTTP requests bearing known CVE-2026-20230 PoC payloads. Alert on unusual POST requests to vulnerable endpoints, command execution in CM processes post-exploit, or admin interface access from non-administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Privilege Escalation on Unified CM
