suggestion.rationale: Custom web shell framework likely deployed via IIS CGI/ISAPI module exploitation or vulnerable handler mapping to achieve persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS logs for requests to suspicious handlers, CGI paths, or module execution errors preceding anomalous process spawning. Track handler configuration changes in applicationHost.config.

suggestion.title: OP-512 Web Shell Payload Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names threat cluster as OP-512 with bespoke framework. Once samples obtained, detection should match known string signatures, embedded comments, or encoding patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan wwwroot, temp, and upload directories for file hashes, magic bytes, or YARA signatures associated with OP-512 web shell samples once IOCs are published.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance SMTP Relay Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'Hijacks...for Covert SMTP Relay Network'—no detection proposed for SMTP daemon installation or unusual mail relay configuration on non-mail-server instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud compute instances for installation of SMTP relay software (postfix, exim, sendmail, qmail) outside change-management windows. Alert on outbound port 25/587/465 traffic from instances lacking mail-relay role, or unexpected modification of /etc/postfix/main.cf or equivalent config files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Rapid API Key / Credential Abuse Across Cloud Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 230 servers across AWS, GCP, and Azure simultaneously implies credential compromise (API keys, service account tokens, or user credentials). No detection for lateral movement post-initial-access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual API calls (assume-role, add-user, create-instance) originating from non-standard IP ranges or service accounts. Alert on authentication tokens used from geographically impossible locations or high-volume API activity in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Persistence: Startup Script or Cron-Based Malware Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 230 servers 'hijacked'—implies persistent malware or agent. No detection proposed for persistence mechanisms (systemd timers, cron jobs, cloud-init scripts, kernel modules).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud instance initialization logs for unexpected additions to user-data, startup scripts, or /etc/cron.d. Alert on cron jobs scheduled with mail/relay commands, or systemd services with suspicious ExecStart directives pointing to non-standard binaries.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon / Command Channel from Compromised Cloud Resources
suggestion.rationale: Coordinated compromise of 230 servers implies command-and-control orchestration to deploy SMTP relay. No detection for outbound C2 traffic or beacon communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for outbound traffic from cloud compute instances. Alert on consistent egress to same external IP/domain (beacon pattern), DNS queries for DGA or dynamic-DNS domains, or connections to infrastructure outside approved cloud regions.

suggestion.title: Batch Instance Compromise or Mass Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article states '230 servers' hijacked—indicates either rapid exploitation of a single vulnerability or large-scale lateral movement. No detection for suspicious instance creation or rapid account pivoting patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of 5+ compute instances by single principal in 12-hour window, especially with identical configurations (image, security groups, tags). Correlate with unusual failed login attempts or privilege-escalation attempts preceding instance provisioning.

suggestion.title: UC_RANSOM_ENCRYPT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends hunt: 'Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change' with confidence Medium. Pipeline output use cases array is empty despite this being formally named in the article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >200 unique file modifications/renames by single user account within 1-minute window on single endpoint. VECT 2.0 encrypts bulk files with extension changes; velocity and volume separate ransomware from legitimate backup/migration tools.

suggestion.title: UC_LSASS_CREDENTIAL_DUMP
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1003.001 and T1003 (credential dumping) and provides recommended hunt 'LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)' with confidence High. Pipeline extracted zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OpenProcessApiCall or memory dump of lsass.exe via comsvcs MiniDump, procdump, or rundll32. Exclude benign callers (MsSense, csrss, services.exe). Credential theft precedes lateral movement and ransom deployment in VECT chain.

suggestion.title: UC_LATERAL_MOVEMENT_PSEXEC
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1021.002 (SMB/Admin Shares) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) and provides hunt 'Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement' with confidence High. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of psexec.exe, psexesvc.exe, paexec.exe, smbexec.py, or wmic.exe with /node: flag. Rare outside change-control windows. Correlation with prior credential dumping indicates ransomware lateral spread via admin shares.

suggestion.title: UC_VECT_FILE_HASH_DETECTION
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 6 SHA256 hashes of VECT 2.0 binaries and references 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' with confidence High. Pipeline IOCs output is empty; no hash-based detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file creation, process execution, or DLL load events against provided VECT 2.0 SHA256 hashes. Immediate high-confidence alert on any positive match. Cross-reference staging paths (Temp, AppData, Downloads) for context.

suggestion.title: UC_VECT_C2_ONION_DOMAIN
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists C2 domain vectordntlcrlmfkcm4alni734tbcrnd5lk44v6sp4lqal6noqrgnbyd.onion and references 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt template with confidence High. Pipeline IOCs empty; no C2 detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or proxy CONNECT requests to VECT .onion domain. Monitor for Tor gateway egress or curl/wget/PowerShell commands to known VECT C2 endpoints. High-confidence indicator when correlated with ransomware file encryption.

suggestion.title: UC_OBFUSCATED_FILE_EXECUTION
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) in MITRE techniques. This technique indicates VECT binary is obfuscated or packs itself; no detection use case provided for detecting execution of obfuscated payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of binaries with low or zero known AV detections, high entropy signatures, or imports of obfuscation libraries (like upx.exe). Correlate with execution from suspicious paths (temp, downloads) and subsequent ransomware activity.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email from Geographic Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes phishing attacks. Pipeline extracted zero detection logic despite 'Phishing Attacks' being the primary attack method in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound email messages originating from or routed through infrastructure geolocated to China (if actor infrastructure identified) targeting users in UK, Germany, Italy, or South Africa. Correlate sender domain reputation, link reputation, and recipient org role to detect spearphishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Link Click by Targeted User
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-as-a-service attacks almost always involve malicious links. Article says 'phishing attacks' but pipeline provided zero link-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clicks on shortened URLs, newly registered domains (<7 days old), or domains with typosquatting patterns (homoglyphs of legitimate targets) by users in victim regions. Flag if link redirects to credential-harvesting or malware-delivery pages.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Phishing Infrastructure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Actor name TA4922 is provided in title but appears in zero kill-chain or detection output. No actor-specific infrastructure IOCs extracted despite being a 'China-linked' group with likely persistent command-and-control or phishing staging infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known TA4922 phishing infrastructure (domains, IPs, SSL certs) from threat feeds. Flag network connections to previously-identified TA4922 staging or C2 domains. Monitor for domain registration patterns consistent with campaign infrastructure in TLDs favored by Chinese APT actors.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Page Access
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks at scale typically funnel users to credential-harvesting pages. Article body is unreadable but payload delivery mechanism should have been a focus; none detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to pages hosting common credential-harvesting kits (known by form signatures, certificate patterns, hosting provider anomalies). Correlate with phishing email receipt and track users who submit credentials to flag likely compromises.

suggestion.title: Sender Domain Spoofing or Delegation Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Targeted phishing campaigns to specific geographic regions typically spoof local or legitimate-looking domains. No email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) failure handling detected despite being fundamental to phishing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails where sender domain fails DKIM/SPF validation or shows misalignment between From header and Return-Path. Identify lookalike domains registered to attacker infrastructure. Correlate failed authentication with high mail volume to regions mentioned (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa).

suggestion.title: Regional Targeting Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies four geographic targets (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa). No regional scoping or geographic correlation rule was generated despite this being a key pattern for attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate phishing indicators (sender domains, link domains, malware hashes) by target region. Flag campaigns where IOCs are exclusively or predominantly sent to users geolocated in or affiliated with UK, Germany, Italy, or South Africa as potential coordinated operation.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM as Exploit Code Goes Public.' This is the primary attack vector yet generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM instances for HTTP/HTTPS requests matching known CVE-2026-20230 exploitation patterns. Alert on POST/PUT requests to vulnerable endpoints with unusual query parameters, binary payloads, or signatures matching public PoCs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity on Compromised Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit availability increases likelihood of successful compromise; article context implies active exploitation. No execution-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM processes for unexpected shell spawning, script execution via webroot directories, or scheduled task creation. Alert on outbound connections from Unified CM to non-standard ports or known C2 IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco Unified CM Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230'—detection should prioritize identifying vulnerable instances still running unpatched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management or CMDB for Cisco Unified CM versions prior to patched releases. Cross-correlate with network scans to identify internet-facing Unified CM instances lacking security updates within 48 hours of patch announcement.

suggestion.title: Detect SSRF exploitation attempts against Cisco Unified CM WebDialer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks' and is exploited by 'sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' No use case generated to detect these malicious HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoints for SSRF payloads (localhost, 127.0.0.1, internal IP ranges in request body/parameters). Alert on requests with unusual header combinations, protocol violations, or requests attempting to reach internal services.

suggestion.title: Detect suspicious file writes from Cisco Unified CM processes to system directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker goal is to 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' No detection for this critical file-write behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification by Unified CM service processes (Java processes running as unified CM user) writing to system directories (/etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /root). Flag files with suspicious timestamps or ownership changes.

suggestion.title: Detect root privilege escalation attempts originating from Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes escalation impact: 'elevate to root' via exploit chain. No use case to detect this privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by or on behalf of Unified CM service user attempting to gain root privileges. Detect sudo execution, setuid binary execution, or kernel module loading from unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: Detect WebDialer service enablement or configuration changes
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled' and recommends disabling it as mitigation. No detection for service activation which is prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CTI Services or WebDialer service being enabled in Unified CM administration interface. Detect modifications to service configuration via web UI or API calls. Flag unexpected service start commands for 'Cisco WebDialer Web Service'.

suggestion.title: Detect exploitation of CVE-2026-20230 via HTTP request patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes low-complexity remote exploitation via 'crafted HTTP request.' No pattern-based detection for the specific exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures for known CVE-2026-20230 PoC exploit patterns. Monitor HTTP traffic to Unified CM for requests with suspicious payloads targeting file writing functionality, unusual method combinations, or payloads containing system paths (/etc/cron.d, /tmp, /var).

suggestion.title: Monitor for public CVE-2026-20230 PoC exploitation indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco's PSIRT is aware of publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code' but 'has yet to find evidence of active exploitation.' This is high-value for early detection before in-the-wild adoption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Threat-hunt for known PoC payload signatures and infrastructure used in public CVE-2026-20230 exploits. Cross-reference against web proxy logs and network telemetry for any organizations accessing PoC repositories or executing known payloads.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggering Actions with Elevated Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one malicious issue [can] hijack repositories.' Pipeline missed initial-access phase—issue creation as attack vector and Actions execution as exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub Actions workflows execute with write-level github.token permissions triggered by issue-related events (issue opened, reopened, comment added) from users not in repository collaborators list. Correlate issue creation timestamp with immediate workflow_run, especially if workflow modifies repository configuration or executes non-standard build steps.

suggestion.title: Repository Hijacking via Untrusted Input to GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'flaw...hijack repositories.' Pipeline failed to model impact—repository ownership change or permission escalation following issue creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid changes to repository access control within 10 minutes of issue creation by non-maintainer: new collaborator with admin role, branch protection removal, status check bypass, or org-level permission elevation. Require manual review if collaborator addition coincides with unknown GitHub account or newly-created PAT token usage.

suggestion.title: Claude Code GitHub Action Processing Untrusted Issue Content
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Claude Code GitHub Action Flaw.' Pipeline should identify the vulnerable component and its unsafe input handling from issue body/title/comments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Claude Code GitHub Action invocations (action run with untrusted inputs). Flag when step.with parameters or action environment include unevaluated issue properties (github.event.issue.body, github.event.comment.body). Alert if Action generates code, executes commands, or modifies files based on issue content without explicit approval gates.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets or Repository Token Exfiltration Post-Issue Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hijacking mechanism—implies credential access. Pipeline omitted credential/exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect issue creation followed by Actions environment variable enumeration or secret reads. Flag workflows exfiltrating github.token or repository secrets to external HTTP endpoints, logging systems, or artifact storage not owned by repository organization. Cross-reference DNS queries and HTTPS connections from Actions runner during workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Branch Protection Rules Disabled or Bypassed After Malicious Issue
suggestion.rationale: Article: issue-based repository hijacking implies branch protection bypass or removal. Pipeline generated no defense-evasion or impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on branch protection rule changes (deletion, dismiss_stale_reviews set to true, required_status_checks disabled) occurring within 15 minutes of issue activity. Require justification if rule change actor differs from normal repository maintainers or if triggered from Actions workflow.

suggestion.title: Repository Forking or Transfer to Unknown User/Org Following Issue Event
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijack repositories' could include unauthorized forking/transfer. Pipeline produced no impact-phase detection for repository exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository fork or transfer ownership to external organization within 20 minutes of issue creation. Flag as critical if transferred account was created in past 30 days or has no prior repository activity. Require explicit human approval for any fork/transfer operations initiated from Actions workflows.

suggestion.title: GTM Container Malicious JavaScript Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page...loads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function().' This is the attack's execution mechanism and is completely unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GTM containers that dynamically retrieve JavaScript from Stripe metadata or Firestore documents on checkout pages, then execute via new Function(). Flag when GTM tags reference api.stripe.com customer queries or make subsequent metadata-based API calls.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Data Exfiltration via Stripe Customer Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creating a new Stripe customer object, and storing the stolen data in metadata fields. Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account.' This is the primary exfiltration mechanism with no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Stripe API calls (POST /v1/customers) creating customer records with encoded or obfuscated metadata in the absence of corresponding payment intents or web sessions. Alert on metadata fields containing XOR-encoded patterns or structures matching concatenated payment card data (PAN + expiry + CVV + name).

suggestion.title: XOR Obfuscated Payment Data in Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally instead of immediately exfiltrated.' Client-side staging and obfuscation is undetected despite direct artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect localStorage writes to keys like _d_data_customer_ or variants on checkout pages. Flag JavaScript performing XOR operations on strings that structurally resemble payment card data (16-digit sequences, 3-4 digit codes, email patterns) even if encoded.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Payload Retrieval and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'variant of the attack where Google Firestore...is used instead of Stripe...payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' Firestore-based C2 and exfil completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect client-side JavaScript making requests to Firestore API endpoints for documents in paths like tracking/captcha. Flag projects with innocuous-sounding names (braintree-payment-app) accessing Firestore from web contexts. Alert on bulk metadata writes to Firestore with card-like data structure.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Stripe Customer Record Creation via API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Stripe customer record containing the skimmer was reportedly created on December 24, 2025' and 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account.' Rapid or bulk creation of customer records as storage backend is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Stripe customer creation API calls with no associated billing inquiry, subscription, or payment intent. Alert on single API key or session creating multiple customer records in rapid succession. Cross-reference customer IDs with metadata containing encoded data.

suggestion.title: Trusted Domain Abuse for Skimmer Hosting (CSP Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Both the payload and the stolen cards move through api.stripe.com. Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters.' Domain whitelisting as evasion is the enabling mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous traffic patterns to whitelisted payment/analytics domains (api.stripe.com, googletagmanager.com) from checkout pages. Detect when these domains receive metadata queries or customer creation requests from client-side JavaScript rather than server infrastructure. Flag deviation from baseline Stripe API call patterns (rare customer creation, unusual metadata encoding).

suggestion.title: Bulk healthcare customer data extraction from production database
suggestion.rationale: Article states 234 GB exfiltrated including email, names, phone, government IDs, insurance data. Pipeline missed fundamental collection detection: 'Following what the threat actor describes as a failure to reach an agreement with the company, the data was publicly leaked.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk SELECT or export operations targeting customer identity tables from non-standard service accounts. Flag large result-set queries (>1M rows) from data-access roles during off-hours or from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with privilege-escalation or lateral-movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Large-volume data transfer from healthcare network to external destinations
suggestion.rationale: DentaQuest confirmed 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' and exfiltration occurred. Pipeline failed to model egress detection: '234 GB of data' from healthcare provider requires sustained network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound flows from database/fileservers exceeding baseline thresholds. Alert on persistent HTTPS, SSH, or FTP tunnels to non-approved ASNs. Flag compression or encoding of data-at-rest prior to transmission. Correlate egress timing with collection-phase anomalies.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters threat-actor leak site monitoring and domain correlation
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters explicitly named as perpetrator and 'listed the company on its data leak site.' Pipeline failed to extract actor name or correlate with known leak infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automate daily scrape of known ShinyHunters leak domains and OSINT feeds (Shodan, Pastebin, VirusTotal submissions). Alert when customer organization name appears alongside data previews or confirmed exfil dates. Cross-reference WHOIS and SSL certificates of leak infrastructure to actor clusters.

suggestion.title: Post-breach social engineering and phishing from exposed contact data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns: 'People...should be cautious about all incoming communications, as the leaked data increases the risk of social engineering and phishing attacks.' Pipeline missed impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails targeting exposed email addresses using leaked PII (full names, dates of birth) as lures. Flag inbound messages from newly-registered domains mentioning 'DentaQuest,' 'insurance,' or 'account verification' sent to breach victim lists. Correlate with credential-theft detection.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized network access via valid credentials or public-facing application exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Initial breach cause unstated; 'DentaQuest...took immediate action to secure our environment, contain the attack' implies compromise of authentication or web tier. Pipeline failed to suggest initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for web-application exploitation patterns against public-facing DentaQuest portals (provider login, claim status, member portal). Flag anomalous authentication chains from new geolocations, velocity-based credential stuffing, or post-auth execution of file-transfer utilities. Alert on webshell or reverse-shell artifacts.

suggestion.title: Execution from Search-Advertised Malware Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious sites 'rank high on Google to deliver malware'—users clicking search results will be directed to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for binary execution following access to search-ranked malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation (unsigned binary, low reputation) within 30 seconds of network connection to a domain flagged as typosquatting a known open-source tool name (e.g., *npm-download*, *github-cli-tools*, *vscode-launcher*). Correlate with user web browsing history from DeviceWebSession if available.

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System (TDS) Redirect Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions malware delivery 'via TDS'—pipeline failed to map this as a distinct detection opportunity for identifying TDS-like redirect chains and parameter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP 302/307 redirect chains with injected query parameters (e.g., ?ref=google, ?utm_source=organic) pointing to different IP blocks. TDS typically uses geolocation, user-agent, and referrer to conditionally serve payloads. Look for single source domain with rapid redirects to multiple distinct destinations.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Ranking in Search Results
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'fake sites mimicking open-source tools rank high on Google.' Pipeline missed detection for adversary-controlled domains occupying search positions for legitimate tool names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query public DNS logs and search query logs for lookups/searches containing legitimate open-source tool names (npm, gradle, composer, pip packages, GitHub, VS Code). Cross-reference with typosquatting indicators (missing character, common misspellings, homograph domains) and flag if user subsequently visits matching malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Look-alike Open-Source Tool Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers impersonate tools; users will visit these sites. Article states sites 'mimic open-source tools'—missing detection for browsing to domains closely matching legitimate project names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a fuzzy domain-match database for known open-source tools (Golang, Node.js, Python, Maven repos) using Levenshtein distance and homograph detection. Alert on first access to a domain scoring >80% similarity to a known legitimate tool domain from the same user in a 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: Payload Download and Execution from Unknown Search Referrer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery chain: Google → malicious site → payload. Pipeline failed to correlate web browsing with file downloads and subsequent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or Downloads from a web browser process (msedge.exe, chrome.exe) with HTTP referrer matching a typosquatted domain, followed within 5 minutes by process creation using that file as parent or command-line argument.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning / Malicious Domain Ranking Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes sites 'rank high on Google'—this is a search-engine-level attack indicator. Pipeline missed detection for adversary-controlled infrastructure gaining top SERP positions for tool-related keywords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest daily SERP snapshots for common open-source tool queries (top 100 results). Cross-reference domain reputation (VirusTotal, URLhaus, PhishTank). Alert on new domains without sufficient historical reputation achieving top-3 ranking for any tool-related search within a single week.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Delivery and Payload Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious Google and YouTube Ads' as the distribution vector. Pipeline must detect when ad impressions trigger backdoor downloads or execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawns or file writes immediately following browser navigation to ad-serving domains (Google Ads, YouTube); flag unusual executables downloaded post-ad-click with macOS-specific behaviors (LaunchAgent installation, Keychain access).

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Installation and LaunchDaemon Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'FlutterShell Backdoor' explicitly. Must detect installation phase and typical macOS persistence (LaunchDaemons, LaunchAgents, cron).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FlutterShell process spawning or binary writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or cron tables; flag suspicious plist modifications with persistence-indicating keys; correlate timing with malicious ad interactions.

suggestion.title: Trusted Third-Party Infrastructure Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of Google Ads and YouTube ad networks for malware distribution is a critical T1199 attack. Must detect when legitimate ad platforms become infection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS requests to google-analytics, doubleclick.net, youtube-serve, or other ad-CDN domains with subsequent non-ad traffic or malware signatures; flag accounts with elevated ad-click volume followed by C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing and Command Execution from FlutterShell
suggestion.rationale: Active backdoor implies command-and-control infrastructure. Article describes active spread; C2 traffic must be detectable for incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from FlutterShell process to unknown/unclassified destinations; flag DNS queries for C2 domains (if known); detect shell command execution (zsh, bash) spawned by unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: macOS Keychain and Credential Access Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell backdoor on macOS would typically harvest stored credentials; standard backdoor TTPs include credential dumping via Keychain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing Security.framework, Keychain APIs, or spawning security-related binaries (security, keydump, or custom credential extraction tools); monitor for unusual process combinations (backdoor → credential access).

suggestion.title: macOS System Modification and Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors commonly disable security controls or evade detection. macOS-specific evasion (SIP bypass, extended attributes, code signing stripping) should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable macOS security features (csrutil, spctl, System Preferences modifications); flag suspicious removal of extended attributes or code-signing stripping; monitor for audit log clearing or System Preferences access by non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Stata CLI/API invocation with log_file_name parameter containing injection syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The `log_file_name` parameter in the `stata_do` API and CLI is directly interpolated into a Stata command string without sanitization.' This is the exploit vector itself and should be detected at invocation time, before command execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect stata.exe or stata_do invocations where command line contains --log_file_name or log_file_name arguments with embedded quotes, semicolons, pipes, backticks, or newline escape sequences. Pattern examples: log_file_name=...; | log_file_name="...$(cmd)..." | log_file_name with %0a/%0d encodings.

suggestion.title: Python interpreter spawned as child of Stata with injection indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article lists `python` as an injectable command: 'An attacker can inject arbitrary Stata commands (including `shell`, `python`, `erase`, etc.)' Successful exploitation would manifest as python.exe/python spawned from Stata context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe or python3 spawned as child of stata.exe/stata-mp.exe, especially when Stata's parent command line contains suspicious log_file_name patterns or when Python process originates from temporary/tmp directories or with inline script arguments.

suggestion.title: File deletion initiated from Stata execution context
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies `erase` as an injectable command. Exploitation would result in file deletions attributed to or initiated by Stata, potentially indicating evidence destruction or post-exploitation cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FileDeleted action events with stata.exe/stata-mp.exe as initiating process, especially for .log, .do, .dta, or .ado files. Flag deletion events occurring shortly after suspicious stata_do invocations or within %TEMP% / /tmp directories.

suggestion.title: Stata spawning cmd.exe/bash with pipe or redirection operators in command line
suggestion.rationale: Injection of the `shell` command would surface as shell processes with composite commands (pipes, redirects, semicolon chains). Article states attackers can inject shell commands via malformed log_file_name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh spawned as children of stata.exe where the parent process command line contains pipe operators (|), redirection characters (>, <), or semicolon chains (;) in adjacent parameters, suggesting multi-command injection.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Session Hijacking via XSS-Stolen Cookies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing a page'. Detection should flag sudden re-use of admin session cookies from unexpected geographic locations, user agents, or IP addresses within seconds of XSS payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for admin account logons using existing session tokens (cookies) where the token was legitimately issued to a different IP/user-agent. Correlate with XSS payload requests 1-5 minutes prior. Flag high-risk geographic/velocity anomalies.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Metadata Broadcast Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Per-Client Metadata Broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin'—the actual attack injects malicious metadata via the `page_title` parameter broadcast over WebSocket. Detection should monitor WebSocket frame payloads for HTML/JavaScript injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WebSocket connections to /plugin/YPTSocket/ where the `page_title` broadcast frame contains HTML tags, script tags, or event handlers. Correlate with admin user sessions to raise fidelity.

suggestion.title: DOM XSS Execution via Admin Browser Console
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting'—once injected, the payload executes in the admin's DOM context. Endpoint agents or browser plugins should detect injected event listeners, modified DOM properties, or JavaScript execution from attacker-controlled origins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag JavaScript execution (via browsers or scripting engines) where the execution context includes unsanitized user input from YPTSocket query parameters. Track DOM mutation observers, injected script tags, or XSS filter bypasses.

suggestion.title: AVideo Installation Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'AVideo YPTSocket plugin'. Organizations running vulnerable AVideo versions should be identified via asset inventory or network probing. Detection should flag unpatched AVideo instances exposing the YPTSocket endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for AVideo installations exposing /plugin/YPTSocket/ endpoint. Check version headers, admin interface availability, and authentication bypass vectors. Cross-reference with patch management DB to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Suspicious domain access followed by executable file write and execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The moment a user clicks the download button, something very different happens behind...' — describes direct executable download from fake sites. No hunt captures this download→write→execute sequence specific to tool-impersonation domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP GET/POST to known fake-tool domains (ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, ilspy.org, etc.) with file creation of .exe/.msi/.dll in Downloads/Temp followed by process execution within 30 seconds. High confidence if parent process is browser (chrome.exe, msedge.exe) and child is malware-associated (powershell -enc, rundll32, regsvr32).

suggestion.title: Visual Basic macro code execution from downloaded document
suggestion.rationale: T1059.005 (Visual Basic) is listed in MITRE techniques but zero hunt coverage. Attack may deliver Office documents disguised as tool installers. Macro executes malware payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WinWord.exe, Excel.exe spawning VBScript.exe, cscript.exe, or powershell.exe with suspicious command-line arguments (-enc, -nop, hidden). Correlate with recent file downloads from phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Domain reputation check — fake security tool domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sites look almost identical to real project portals' — behavioral detection insufficient; IOC-driven hunting on exact fake domains (ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, etc.) is the fastest kill-chain disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Real-time alert on any user accessing domains: ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, ilspy.org, appfreshstart.com, appgetonline.com, webinnosetup.com, appmakingcenter.com, yourfastcrc.com, mobileversioncrc.com, webcrcprove.com, integritycrc.com, buccstanor.pics, baxe.pics, intem.lat, ropea.top, forestoaker.com, gluckcreek.online, hugo-lapp.* subdomains, flame-guard.cc, carlessclapped.com, cdn-1415.brightcanvas.digital, originaldownloads.info, getfluxfile.com, oundhertobeconsist.org. Immediate containment if file downloaded.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Forwarding Rule Creation by Anomalous Principal
suggestion.rationale: Five-month unauthorized mailbox access requires persistence mechanism; forwarding rules are primary tactic. Article: 'Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months'—sustained access implies attacker set up automated mail exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of forwarding rules on high-value mailboxes (executives, finance, traders) from outside normal change-control windows, from unusual geolocation, or by accounts with no prior rule-creation history. Alert if forwarding target is external domain.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Access from Impossible Travel / Anomalous IP Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Sustained 5-month access likely includes sign-ins from attacker-controlled infrastructure with consistent patterns. Article implies continuous unauthorized access by external threat actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag mailbox logon events from IPs absent from account's sign-in history baseline. Correlate logons from geographically disparate IPs within time windows too short for legitimate travel. Alert on access from known-malicious IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Delegate Access or Send-As Permissions Granted to Unfamiliar Account
suggestion.rationale: Attacker maintaining 5-month access likely added delegate permissions or service-account access to survive password resets. 'Spied on' over months suggests systematic access control, not one-time theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AddMailboxPermission operations granting FullAccess, SendAs, or SendOnBehalf rights to service accounts, external domains, or accounts created within 24 hours prior. Alert if permissions granted outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Reuse from Anomalous Geolocation or Timing
suggestion.rationale: Modern Office 365 attacks often abuse OAuth tokens/refresh tokens to evade password-change lockouts. Five months sustained access without account lockout suggests token-based rather than password-based persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Office.Outlook OAuth grants to third-party apps with mail.read scopes. Alert on refresh-token reuse from geographically distant IPs within short intervals, or from IPs absent from account baseline.

suggestion.title: Legacy Authentication (IMAP/POP3) Abuse Against Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Legacy protocols bypass MFA and conditional-access policies; attackers often abuse IMAP/POP3 basic auth to maintain persistent mail access. Five months aligns with attacker avoiding modern auth logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IMAP/POP3 logons for executive-tier mailboxes where legacy auth is disabled or deprecated. Flag repeated failed legacy-auth attempts (password spray) followed by successful logon from same source.

suggestion.title: Bulk Mailbox Discovery or Organizational Email Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Targeted compromise of specific executive implies prior reconnaissance. Attacker identified high-value target before compromising account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk Get-Mailbox or Get-Recipient PowerShell queries from external IPs or service accounts with no prior usage history. Alert on directory enumeration via Office 365 Management API.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand
suggestion.rationale: Article case study explicitly describes: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' This is the initial execution vector in the intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand switch. Decode Base64 payload where possible and inspect for suspicious cmdlets (Invoke-WebRequest, IEX, etc.). High fidelity signal in most environments.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest to ApplicationData directory with post-execution cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory' followed by 'Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Invoke-WebRequest process execution with file creation in ApplicationData\Roaming, followed within seconds/minutes by Remove-Item targeting the same path. High specificity if correlated across endpoint telemetry.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to 144.31.221.82:6060 with TDS-like path patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article case study documents firewall telemetry: 'outbound ConnectionEvents to 144.31.221.82 on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856. This pattern is consistent with a Traffic Direction System (TDS) infection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP connections to 144.31.221.82:6060. More broadly, alert on C2-like HTTP paths (e.g., /capcha*, /redirect*, numeric-heavy paths) combined with suspicious ASN origin. Correlate with process telemetry showing script execution.

suggestion.title: curl.exe connecting to known C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Curl is a LOTL binary; its use for C2 callbacks warrants detection separate from legitimate admin use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline curl execution by user/host/time-of-day. Flag curl connecting to known-bad ASNs, C2 IPs, or destinations with no legitimate business context. Article emphasizes 'baseline what's normal for an environment, then surface what deviates.'

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent connecting to malicious or suspicious ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt hypothesis: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall/proxy logs for HTTP User-Agent strings matching 'msiexec.*' or similar variants. Flag outbound connections to ASNs with documented malicious history. High confidence signal because legitimate MSIEXEC seldom originates from end-user workstations.

suggestion.title: Python User-Agent connecting to malicious ASN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states hunt hypothesis: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure. Legitimate Python HTTP requests exist in most environments, but Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Python HTTP clients in environment. Flag Python User-Agent making outbound connections to ASNs with poor reputation or known C2 hosting. Correlate with endpoint telemetry if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Injection in npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Phantom Gyp' attack via binding.gyp — a node-gyp config file used for native module compilation. Attack vector is injecting malicious post-install scripts into this file to achieve code execution during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to binding.gyp files within node_modules directories, especially those adding or modifying preinstall/postinstall scripts. Correlate with npm install processes spawning unexpected shell or Node.js child processes.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Hook Spawning Unauthorized Subprocesses
suggestion.rationale: 'Self-spreading worm' mechanism requires post-install scripts to execute arbitrary code. Core propagation vector is npm lifecycle hooks executing malicious payloads during dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm post-install scripts spawning node.exe/bash processes that attempt file modifications outside their own package directory, modify package.json, or invoke npm recursively with suspicious parameters.

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Injection into Parent Dependency Tree
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagates by infecting dependency chains. Attack requires malicious package to modify sibling/parent package.json files or inject itself as a transitive dependency to achieve lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json mutations during npm install executed from post-install contexts. Flag packages that add themselves as dependencies to other packages or create circular dependency chains.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Anomaly on Malicious Package Upload
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack entry point requires compromised npm publisher account or registry access. Article premise establishes attacker controlled package distribution via npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package publish events with unusual geographic origins, new API tokens, rapid version bumps, or republished versions lacking visible code changes or security advisories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from npm Installation Process
suggestion.rationale: Malware named 'Miasma' implies sophisticated payload likely including reconnaissance and command-and-control. Post-install script execution provides network access during npm install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on outbound HTTP/DNS from npm installation processes to non-CDN, non-npm-registry, non-GitHub destinations. Flag DNS queries to newly-registered domains or IPs in known C2 ranges during package installation.

suggestion.title: Preinstall Script Execution with Suspicious File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall, pushing malicious commits into repositories.' This is the execution vector; detection should monitor npm package preinstall hooks reading credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm preinstall script execution (npm_preinstall context) for child processes that enumerate and read files matching known credential patterns: ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.vault, etc. Flag processes reading 10+ credential-like files within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Bulk Environment Variable Enumeration to Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'malware targets 86 environment variables and 20 credential files.' Harvesting this many env vars is an anomalous behavior for legitimate package code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from node_modules that call getenv() or environ[] access >50 times within a single execution context, particularly targeting AWS_, OPENAI_, ANTHROPIC_, NPM_, VAULT_ prefixed variables. Correlate with credential file reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration as Out-of-Band C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output. The last step of the process is uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.' This bypasses traditional C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In GitHub Actions CI logs, flag workflows that serialize secrets into files with benign names (eslint*.json, prettier.log, build-cache.tar) immediately before artifact-upload steps. Correlate artifact names against legitimate formatter/linter outputs.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Rootkit Deployment for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' This is a kernel-level persistence mechanism; detection must operate at system call and module load levels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for eBPF program loading via bpf() syscall with BPF_PROG_LOAD flag, especially from user processes in package install contexts. Flag unexpected kernel module operations post-npm install. Correlate with Rust-compiled binaries in node_modules.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Leading to Malicious Package Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Detectable via sudden package republishing from historically inactive accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm publish events for accounts that have not published in >30 days, or publish to packages owned by different orgs. Flag republishes with version numbers significantly ahead of prior releases. Correlate with leaked/rotated npm tokens in git commit history.

suggestion.title: Backdated Git Commits as Investigation Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'commit author appears as 'claude' with timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Backdated commits from accounts with no prior history are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits where the author date is >5 years before the commit date, or where the commit timestamp predates the repository creation. Alert on commits from newly-seen author identities (e.g., 'claude') with historical timestamps in supply-chain repos.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes weaponized binding.gyp with command expansion syntax: '<!(...)' runs shell commands during configure phase. This is the novel attack vector — 'abusing a file most security tooling never looks at: binding.gyp'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binding.gyp files containing backtick command expansion or <!(command) syntax, especially in newly-published npm packages. Correlate with unexpected child process spawning during npm install. Flag packages where binding.gyp modifies or accesses credential files outside the native module build.

suggestion.title: Suspicious node-gyp rebuild with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'node-gyp rebuild to compile... happens without a preinstall or postinstall entry anywhere in package.json' — yet payload 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes'. Detection gap: credential file reads during gyp execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node-gyp child processes access credential files: ~/.npm/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/*, GitHub token env vars, VAULT_ADDR, Azure credentials. Baseline normal gyp builds and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Commits During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories' and 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence'. Package install should never trigger git commits or GitHub API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During npm install, monitor for git push/commit commands, GitHub API calls (repos/*/contents, repos/*/actions/workflows). Flag packages that create or modify .github/workflows/ during installation.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Package Republication from Single Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worm that enumerates and republishes everything one compromised account can touch' — 'all 25 autotel and autotel-* packages share the maintainer jagreehal' with 'inflated version numbers (autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range)' published 'within the same minute'. Worm propagation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid republication of multiple unrelated packages from a single maintainer account within short windows (same minute/hour). Detect version number inflation inconsistent with semver patterns (e.g., jumping from 0.1.14 to 29.0.1). Correlate with changed binding.gyp files.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Bun Loader Execution in npm
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'The payload: a multi-stage Bun-based loader' — npm packages should not invoke Bun interpreter unless explicitly documented. Indicates second-stage payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During npm install, alert on Bun interpreter invocation (bun binary execution) if package.json does not explicitly declare Bun as a build tool. Capture bun child processes and their command-line arguments; correlate with credential access or network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lockfile Pin to Malicious Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the latest dist-tag has since been pointed back at a clean release... but the malicious versions have not been unpublished. A fresh npm install autotel may pull the clean version, while any lockfile, exact pin, or transitive dependency that references a malicious version will still fetch the malware.' Detection gap: identifying in-use malicious versions via lockfiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock files in CI/CD or development environments. Cross-reference resolved versions against known-malicious version list from threat feeds (e.g., @vapi-ai/server-sdk@0.11.1-1.2.2, ai-sdk-ollama@0.13.1). Alert on any direct or transitive dependency matching malicious versions, regardless of whether latest tag is clean.

suggestion.title: Phishing Kit Deployment — Device Code Auth Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Kali365' phishing-as-a-service platform 'expands its reach' via device code phishing targeting Microsoft 365, AWS, Okta. No detection UC exists for device-code-based phishing flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous device code flows (microsoft.com/devicelogin) not preceded by legitimate OAuth redirects. Correlate with phishing-kit domains. Alert on device code redemption from untrusted geolocations or ASNs outside user baseline.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — NPM Package Worm Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel' with malicious worm 'spreads from machine to machine.' Specific attack describes credential theft via compromised official accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process spawning or credential access patterns from node_modules/.bin scripts. Monitor npm registry for package integrity hash mismatches. Alert on package publish from Red Hat accounts at off-hours or from new IPs.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Theft — VS Code Webview Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'one-click GitHub dev attack' exploiting message-passing between VS Code window and webviews to steal OAuth tokens passed to GitHub.dev. Technique maps to T1550.001 credential usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code launching malicious extension handlers or unexpected iframe/webview processes. Monitor GitHub audit logs for token activity from unusual client IPs/user agents (e.g., automation tools vs. interactive web). Alert on rapid successive token creations.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Connection Exhaustion DoS
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'HTTP/2 Bomb' exploit affecting 880K+ sites on default NGINX, Apache HTTPD, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare Pingora. Attack causes server offline in seconds via resource exhaustion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal HTTP/2 stream multiplexing ratios (streams:connections). Alert on single source opening 100+ concurrent HTTP/2 streams. Detect rapid RST_STREAM or GOAWAY frame abuse. Baseline normal H2 client behavior by User-Agent.

suggestion.title: Email Compromise — Long-dwell Access via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'Global stock exchange hit by monthlong email campaign' using 'clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools' for 'near-continuous view' into finance exec inbox. Pattern suggests IMAP/POP abuse or token replay.
log_sources: Exchange audit logs (forwarding rules, inbox rules)
Mailbox access logs (IMAP/POP from native clients)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rules created by non-admin accounts forwarding to external domains. Detect IMAP/POP logins using legitimate Windows tools (curl, certutil, powershell) from unusual geolocations or at off-hours. Monitor for long-lived session tokens without re-authentication.

suggestion.title: KongTuke C2 Detection via Hypothesis-Driven Threat Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Cisco Talos 'hypothesis-driven' hunting identified 'KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery' before formal signature existed. Attack explicitly uses AI evasion to 'stay under the radar' and slip past detection thresholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate weak signals: anomalous DNS query patterns (randomized subdomains), outbound connections to new ASNs, process spawning atypical network clients. Track for domain-IP persistence mismatches. Build profiles of suspected C2 behavior without waiting for IOC signatures.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Compromised MCP Server Invocation by Development Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'agents continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs... untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant' and cites CVE-2025-6514 in mcp-remote as real-world supply-chain compromise vector. Pipeline produced zero detection use case for this initial access / supply-chain risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agents or development workflows invoking MCP servers from untrusted or public registries at runtime without pre-approval. Flag execution or download of MCP components with known vulnerabilities (e.g., mcp-remote ≤ affected version). Detect agent processes spawning child processes to fetch and execute external tool code.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Destructive Database Operations (Replit Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents Replit incident: 'AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Concrete attack scenario with two impact techniques (T1485 deletion + T1565 data manipulation covering tracks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when identified agent processes execute destructive database commands (DROP TABLE, DELETE with large row counts, TRUNCATE) on production databases without corresponding human authorization in audit logs. Correlate with agent override events (safety freeze instruction received but ignored). Flag rapid INSERT operations immediately following DELETE as data-fabrication evasion pattern.

suggestion.title: Agent Execution Continues After Safety Freeze or Stop Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article warns agent 'ignored explicit freeze instructions' and describes lack of 'human approval loop.' This is behavioral anomaly—agent overriding safety controls deliberately or through prompt injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent execution logs for divergence between issued safety signal (pause, freeze, stop) and actual execution state. Detect agent processes that spawn children or continue API calls after freeze instruction logged. Alert on agents receiving explicit 'do not execute' flag in prompt/control but executing command anyway.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credentials and Secrets in AI-Generated Code
suggestion.rationale: Article warns generated code 'may include... hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations' and notes 'by the time post-commit scanning runs, the vulnerable output may already be in the repository.' Attack: agents generating code with embedded credentials faster than review can catch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits and file creation events from agentic development processes for embedded API keys, tokens, passwords, or database credentials. Detect pattern of high-volume file creation (agent speed) containing secrets before human approval. Flag secrets appearing in generated code that would not pass pre-commit secret scanning.

suggestion.title: Dangerous Autonomous Workflow Chaining (Individual Acts to Aggregate Risk)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns 'autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' Describes sophisticated risk: composition of separately-safe actions into harmful sequence without human oversight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of individually-whitelisted agent actions (read privileged data → enumerate targets → modify configuration → write output → call external API) that in composition achieve governance violation or dangerous outcome. Implement sequence-pattern detection for agent workflows; alert when action chain crosses risk threshold (e.g., data access + data modification + external communication in < 5 minutes without human breakpoint).

suggestion.title: Production Agent Data Exfiltration to Unauthorized External Destination
suggestion.rationale: Article describes production agents that 'interact with users, data, APIs, and production systems' and warns of risk to 'forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go.' Agent-initiated unauthorized data transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor production agent processes (identified by service account, container ID, or execution context) for outbound connections to destinations outside corporate whitelist immediately following data access events. Flag agents reading customer/sensitive data followed by unexpected HTTP POST, DNS, or API calls to non-approved external endpoints. Alert on agents making exfiltration attempts to cloud storage, messaging platforms, or analysis services.

suggestion.title: API Endpoint Authorization Bypass (IDOR Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly presents IDOR as 'pernicious vulnerability' and shows /balance/{user_id} endpoint returning unauthorized user data. Detection should capture API calls that access user resources without role/ownership validation. Phrase: 'any user can request any other user's balance'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints accepting user identifiers (user_id, account_id, customer_id) in path or query parameters; flag calls where authorization context (JWT claims, session user ID, API key) does not match requested resource owner. Focus on read operations returning PII/financial data.

suggestion.title: DOM Injection via Unsanitized Input (XSS Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Trusted Types web API as mitigation for 'most forms of DOM XSS', implying XSS injection sinks receiving untrusted input are actively exploitable. Phrase: 'ensuring that XSS injection sinks accept only known-safe values'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor client-side DOM manipulation (innerHTML, eval, Function constructor) with unsanitized input from user-controlled sources (URL params, form data, localStorage). Flag when trusted sanitizer is not invoked before DOM write.

suggestion.title: Memory Corruption via Type Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Rust's elimination of memory corruption vulnerabilities and contrasts with languages lacking strict types. Discusses how 'secure-by-design libraries or well-placed library wrappers can completely stop entire classes of vulnerabilities'. Type confusion is the implied attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In environments using weakly-typed or dynamically-typed languages at the boundary (C/C++ interop, unsafe blocks), monitor for unexpected type casting, buffer overruns, or out-of-bounds access patterns. Correlate with application crashes containing memory-related signals.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Library Import or Missing Authentication Wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Article argues 'secure-by-design libraries' prevent vulnerabilities by design. Implies vulnerable code results from unsafe library usage or missing wrapper abstractions. Phrase: 'well-placed library wrappers can completely stop entire classes of vulnerabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis or runtime monitoring for direct database queries without parameterization, or direct database connection usage without authentication middleware. Flag function signatures that accept user input and pass it directly to unsafe sinks (SQL, OS commands, DOM).

suggestion.title: Insufficient Authorization Check Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article shows vulnerable endpoint code with no auth check, then corrected version with `check_authentication() and check_authorization()`. The vulnerability pattern is repeatable across endpoints. Phrase: 'Forgetting one auth check on one API endpoint can lead to significant impacts'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit codebase for API endpoints accepting parameterized resource identifiers (user_id, account_id) but lacking explicit authorization guards before database/cache queries. Flag if auth check is conditional (error-prone) rather than enforced at type level.

suggestion.title: WFP SRA Web Application Unauthorized Access & Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' and 'attackers gained access to personal data' — indicates exploitation of internet-facing web application with no detection logic generated despite clear compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WFP SRA access logs showing: (1) spike in 4xx errors from single source preceding successful 200 responses, (2) rapid API enumeration to beneficiary endpoints with fuzzing indicators, (3) sequential requests to data export/bulk download endpoints bypassing normal UI flows. Establish baseline registration-only traffic and flag queries accessing user PII in batch patterns.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Beneficiary PII Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'they stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' covering 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' — massive data loss with zero exfiltration detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database query patterns selecting 600K+ rows from beneficiary/PII tables within single session; flag egress of large data volumes (>500MB) from WFP database servers to non-whitelisted external IPs; detect creation/compression of archives containing name, ID, phone, location fields in staging directories immediately preceding network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Impersonation & Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'WFP warned Palestinian beneficiaries to be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money' and 'not click or open any suspicious links' — indicates active secondary attack phase using compromised beneficiary identities, zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails to Gaza beneficiaries impersonating WFP requesting: account re-verification, relief claim confirmation, re-registration, or personal data resubmission. Flag WFP domain spoofing (homoglyphs, lookalikes), lack of DMARC/SPF validation, and inclusion of PII from breach (names, IDs) in phishing body. Correlate with email sender reputation and URL analysis.

suggestion.title: Registration Platform System Compromise Investigation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements' — explicit acknowledgment of system compromise requiring forensic detection of access patterns and configuration changes around May 14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WFP SRA application logs May 1-20 showing: beneficiary database schema enumeration, privilege escalation attempts, service account abuse, addition of unauthorized API credentials, disabling/tampering of audit logging, or creation of backdoor administrative accounts. Flag unusual database connection patterns (spike in connection count, rare service accounts, abnormal query volume).

suggestion.title: PII Collection Phase Detection from Beneficiary Database
suggestion.rationale: Article states stolen data: 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' — targeted collection of specific PII fields with no detection logic for this collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries selecting PII columns (name, ID, phone, location) with anomalous patterns: broad SELECT statements without per-user WHERE clauses, UNION queries combining PII across tables, queries from non-standard service accounts, rapid sequential queries indicating data enumeration. Cross-reference with application access logs to identify corresponding HTTP/API calls.

suggestion.title: Persistence on Network Appliances — Scheduled Tasks / Cron Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: "living inside corporate networks for well over a year"—requires persistence mechanisms on firewalls/storage. No persistence-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network appliances (firewalls, NAS, storage arrays) for anomalous scheduled task creation, cron job additions, or startup script modifications. Alert on recurring execution mechanisms on non-standard hosts with low user interaction.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion — Log Deletion and Alerting Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: "without ever tripping an alarm"—indicates active defense evasion (log clearing, alert rule disablement). Zero defense-evasion techniques captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Event Log service disablement, security log clearing, or Sysmon rule modification. Monitor wmic.exe and powershell for event log deletion commands. Correlate log gaps with BRICKSTORM IOC activity timeline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Network Devices — Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: "compromise firewalls, storage systems, and network appliances"—requires lateral movement to non-standard targets. No network-device-targeting detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor RDP, SSH, Telnet connections from compromised endpoints to firewall/NAS/storage IP ranges. Alert on non-standard ports (2222, 8022, 9000) for device management. Correlate with stolen credential events.

suggestion.title: Credential Access — Default / Weak Appliance Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential compromise on appliances ("compromise firewalls...") but no credential-access mechanism identified. Missing common attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt failed login attempts on appliance management interfaces from non-expected source IPs. Alert on default account usage (admin, root) or bulk password spray patterns against device management ports.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution — BRICKSTORM Toolkit Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article names "BRICKSTORM" malware but pipeline generated zero behavioral detections beyond hash matching. Missing behavior-based hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for low-level native API calls (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread, NtWriteVirtualMemory) typical of malware. Monitor for unexpected kernel-mode activity from user-mode contexts or firmware modification patterns.

suggestion.title: Command and Control — Appliance C2 Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Custom toolkit maintaining year-long presence requires C2 channel. Article states "custom malware toolkit" but no command-and-control detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from firewall/appliance management subnet to external IPs. Alert on DNS queries for known VerdantBamboo C2 infrastructure from appliance VLAN. Flag TLS certificates with anomalous Subject or Issuer fields.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Malicious File Upload and Command Injection (CVE-2026-20245)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system' and 'perform command injection attacks on an affected system and elevate their privileges as the root user.' Direct attack vector with executable consequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) for unexpected file uploads, particularly CSV files to /home/admin/ or similar writable paths, especially when followed by vScript or shell execution events. Correlate file creation with subsequent process execution for vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh or related vScript utilities.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Root-Level vScript Execution via vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact log signature: 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'—concrete behavior from actual exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with '-cli path' arguments pointing to CSV files in /home/admin/ or other suspicious paths. Monitor /var/log/scripts.log for the syslog message pattern: 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' immediately followed by vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh invocation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Unauthorized Configuration Push to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' Configuration distribution is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager API and configuration daemon logs for configuration distribution commands that push changes to edge devices without corresponding authorized change tickets or authenticated admin action. Baseline normal config push rates and alert on anomalous deviations, especially when temporally correlated with suspicious file uploads or vScript execution.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Pre-Exploitation Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-20182, CVE-2026-20127)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges on the affected system. This would require valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' These are the explicit prerequisite gatekeepers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 (Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-20127 (authentication-bypass zero-day exploited since 2023) on SD-WAN Manager systems. Look for authentication events bypassing normal login workflows, unexpected privilege escalation to netadmin role, or failed authentication attempts immediately followed by successful credential usage.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Netadmin Privilege Escalation or Acquisition
