Correlate with workflow run logs showing unexpected curl/wget/PowerShell -WebRequest calls.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Poisoned Agentic Model Instructions
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'agentic world' threat model: adversary could poison training data or system prompts of Claude Code to make agent autonomously inject backdoors into repositories during 'helpful' refactoring or feature implementation tasks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits authored by 'Claude Code' or AI bot accounts that introduce shell metacharacters, base64-encoded payloads, or suspicious imports in unexpected files. Flag commits that bypass code review or are merged by service accounts with elevated permissions. Cross-reference commit content against known malware/backdoor signatures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Lateral Movement from CI/CD to Production via AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Agentic AI in GitHub Actions context can pivot to cloud resources (AWS, Azure, GCP) using credentials available in CI/CD secrets or role assumptions. Article 'securing CI/CD' implies threat of lateral movement post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub Actions workflow execution with subsequent cloud API calls (AssumeRole, assume-role, get-secret, read-instance-metadata) originating from CI/CD service IPs. Flag cases where the caller identity changes from GitHub Actions service role to human-assumed role in <5 minutes, suggesting credential theft or misconfiguration abuse.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modification by Compromised Agent
suggestion.rationale: If agentic AI is compromised or manipulated, it could modify .github/workflows files to persist backdoors or introduce data-exfiltration steps in legitimate builds. Article context implies defense against agent autonomy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits that add or modify .github/workflows/*.yml files with unexpected additions: new environment variables (especially cloud credentials), new job steps that call external scripts or fetch from URLs, or runner images changed to custom/untrusted containers. Require approvals for workflow changes even if pushed by trusted service accounts.

suggestion.title: Agentic AI Extracting Source Code and Dependencies from Repository
suggestion.rationale: Claude Code and similar agents can read entire repos during code review/refactor tasks. Threat model includes exfiltration of proprietary source, dependencies, or secrets embedded in code during agent execution in CI/CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows running Claude Code that call git clone, checkout, or archive commands to fetch entire repository trees, followed by tar/zip operations and outbound file transfer. Flag cases where agent tools are granted repo read access but produce no code review artifacts—only exfiltration.

suggestion.title: UC_RANSOM_ENCRYPT_MASS_FILE_OPS
suggestion.rationale: Article title and threat profile describe ransomware encrypting files and causing irrecoverable damage. T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact) is the primary technique. Pipeline must detect high-cardinality file modifications/renames in short time windows as the encryption signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single account or process modifying/renaming >200 files in 1-minute window. Tune to exclude backup software and system utilities. Correlate with preceding credential-access or lateral-movement indicators to increase confidence.

suggestion.title: UC_CREDENTIAL_ACCESS_LSASS_DUMP
suggestion.rationale: T1003.001 (LSASS Memory) and T1003 (OS Credential Dumping) are explicitly listed as observed techniques. This is the standard initial pivot point for ransomware to obtain credentials for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OpenProcessApiCall to lsass.exe from any process outside a whitelist (csrss, svchost, services, wininit, lsm, etc.). Also flag rundll32.exe + comsvcs.dll + MiniDump argument chains, procdump.exe targeting lsass, and command-lines containing 'sekurlsa' or 'MiniDump'.

suggestion.title: UC_LATERAL_MOVEMENT_SMB_PSEXEC
suggestion.rationale: T1021.002 (SMB/Windows Admin Shares) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) are explicitly listed. Remote service execution is the bridge from credential theft to mass encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of psexec.exe, psexesvc.exe, paexec.exe, or smbexec.py. Also detect wmic.exe with /node: or /action: parameters. Correlate execution with prior LSASS access on the same host to reduce false positives from legitimate remote admin tools.

suggestion.title: UC_C2_ONION_DOMAIN_COMMUNICATION
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) listed as observed. Article explicitly provides vectordntlcrlmfkcm4alni734tbcrnd5lk44v6sp4lqal6noqrgnbyd.onion as C2 domain. Network detection must flag connections and DNS resolution attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolution attempts for vectordntlcrlmfkcm4alni734tbcrnd5lk44v6sp4lqal6noqrgnbyd.onion or outbound HTTPS connections to Tor exit nodes attempting SOCKS proxying. Correlate with execution of malware hashes from this briefing.

suggestion.title: UC_MALWARE_FILE_HASH_EXECUTION
suggestion.rationale: Article provides six SHA256 hashes. Pipeline must generate file-hash IOC hunts across process and file-write events to catch execution or staging of these VECT 2.0 samples.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or file creation where file hash matches any of the six provided SHA256 values. Tune to require either unusual parent process/file location or subsequent behavioral trigger (LSASS access, mass file operations, C2 connection) to lower false positives.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection - TA4922 Geographic Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'TA4922 Expands Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa.' Phishing is the stated attack vector. Pipeline generated zero email-based detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails sent to/from UK, German, Italian, South African organizational domains. Flag emails with credential-harvesting URLs, OAuth-phishing redirects, or malicious attachments. Correlate sender reputation and URL indicators to TA4922 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL Detonation and Landing Page Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references phishing attacks but pipeline produced no URL-based IOCs or detonation use cases. Phishing requires malicious links or credential-harvesting pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detonate URLs in phishing emails targeting the four regions. Flag landing pages spoofing cloud services, SSO portals, or email platforms. Alert on SAML token theft, OAuth phishing redirects, and forced MFA interception patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Credential Reuse and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes TA4922 'expansion'—implies successful compromises enabling broader access. Pipeline missed post-compromise activity (login anomalies, lateral movement, persistence).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor harvested-credential logins: impossible travel, off-hours access, new geographies matching phishing targets. Flag credential spray, unusual forwarding rules, or mailbox delegation on compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Persistence Mechanisms Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article names TA4922 as China-linked threat actor. Pipeline did not map actor-specific persistence techniques (Office macros, email rules, service principals, scheduled tasks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for TA4922 persistence post-phishing: unusual macro execution in Office files, email auto-forward/delete rules, service principals added to O365, suspicious scheduled tasks. Correlate with phishing email timestamps.

suggestion.title: Phishing Attachment Analysis - Malware and Macro Detection
suggestion.rationale: TA4922 phishing typically includes attachments (Office files, archives); pipeline generated no attachment-based detection despite phishing being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Quarantine and detonate phishing attachments. Flag Office docs with enabled macros, archives with executables, or embedded scripts. Correlate detonations with known TA4922 malware families.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Infrastructure and C2 Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns require attacker-controlled infrastructure (phishing-page hosts, C2 endpoints, email relays). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite multi-country campaign scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block domains and IPs hosting phishing pages and C2. Monitor DNS queries to TA4922-associated infrastructure. Alert on VPN/proxy logins from phishing-infrastructure IP ranges post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public' and names RCE vulnerability. Pipeline produced zero detection rules despite active exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM web interface (default 8443) for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20230 exploitation signatures: unusual parameter injection, encoding anomalies, or requests to known vulnerable endpoints documented in Cisco security advisory.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Unified CM Services
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability enables arbitrary code execution. Article confirms exploit availability but pipeline missed execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell, bash) from Unified CM application processes (tomcat, asterisk, ccmciscodir). Flag unusual parent-child process trees where UCM service accounts launch interpreters with remote input indicators.

suggestion.title: Unified CM Database or Config File Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence requires file writes. Public exploit increases likelihood of rapid fileystem-based payload delivery, but pipeline generated no file-integrity detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized modifications to Unified CM configuration, database, or startup script directories (e.g., /opt/cisco/*/conf, /var/www/tomcat, Windows UCM install paths). Correlate file modification timestamps with exploitation windows and process anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unified CM Outbound C2 Communication Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploit-code-public scenarios drive rapid post-exploitation pivot activity. Pipeline failed to surface lateral-movement or C2 detection hypotheses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM systems for outbound connections to non-whitelisted infrastructure (non-Cisco, non-corporate repositories). Flag DNS requests for unknown domains, HTTPS traffic to IPs with newly-registered domains, or encrypted tunnel protocols (SSH tunnels, reverse shells).

suggestion.title: Unified CM Administrative Console Unauthorized Logon
suggestion.rationale: RCE + public exploit enables rapid credential compromise and admin-account hijacking. Article implies system takeover scenario but pipeline detected no account-compromise indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Unified CM admin-console authentication logs for impossible-travel patterns, out-of-hours access, rapid failed-login spikes followed by successful logon, or privilege-escalation attempts (role changes) coinciding with exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to surface CVE-2026-20230 as a primary IOC despite it being the article's core threat intelligence. High-severity RCE with public exploit mandates immediate vulnerability-index flagging and patch-status correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index CVE-2026-20230 and correlate with inventory of all Cisco Unified CM deployments. Flag unpatched instances; cross-reference with network telemetry to detect exploitation attempts against known-vulnerable systems and alert on patch-deployment delays.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggers Unexpected Action Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'one malicious issue' hijacks repositories—this is the initial access mechanism. Detection must cover issue creation patterns that precede GitHub Action execution and repository modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly-created GitHub issues (especially from low-reputation accounts or outside collaborators) that immediately trigger GitHub Action executions and are followed by repository code or configuration changes. Correlate issue creation timestamps with workflow trigger times.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Modifies Repository Code Without Authorization
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'hijack repositories'—attacker gains ability to modify repository contents via GitHub Action execution. Detection should flag unauthorized push/write operations by GitHub Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows that perform code commits or pushes to protected branches or the default branch. Alert on Actions that bypass branch protection rules or perform writes with elevated permissions triggered by external events (issues, comments).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Action Accesses Repository Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking implies access to deployment credentials and secrets. GitHub Actions with overpermissioned access to GITHUB_TOKEN or repository secrets should be monitored when triggered by potentially malicious external events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions that access repository secrets (AWS keys, deployment tokens, NPM credentials) when triggered by issue creation, issue comments, or pull request events from outside collaborators. Flag jobs that exfiltrate secrets to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Workflow File Modified by External Issue Comment
suggestion.rationale: If the vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution through issue content, the attack likely modifies .github/workflows files to persist malicious Actions. Detection should cover workflow YAML changes triggered by external input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits that modify files in .github/workflows/ directory triggered by or correlated with recent GitHub issue creation or comment activity from low-trust accounts. Correlate with presence of suspicious shell commands or credential references in modified workflow files.

suggestion.title: Rapid Repository Permission Changes Post-Issue Creation
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking implies ability to change access controls. Detect sudden addition of new collaborators or elevation of existing collaborators' permissions correlated with malicious issue activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repository collaborator additions and permission changes within 5 minutes of issue creation from external accounts. Flag additions of service accounts or bot accounts following GitHub Action exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Vulnerability Version Used
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Claude Code GitHub Action Flaw'—specific Action name and vulnerable versions should be IOC-extracted and tracked. Detection should cover deployment of vulnerable Action versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all uses of the 'Claude Code' GitHub Action (or similar affected Actions) in workflows and identify which repositories use vulnerable versions. Flag new deployments of known-vulnerable versions post-disclosure date.

suggestion.title: GTM Container executing code from external API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious code 'loaded from a Google Tag Manager (GTM) container' that 'reads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function()'. Detection of GTM containers making API calls and executing fetched code is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GTM container tags triggering HTTP requests to api.stripe.com with customer record queries (cus_*), followed by evaluation via Function() constructor. Monitor for GTM containers making outbound API calls to payment processors not in allowlist.

suggestion.title: Stripe API abuse for stolen payment data storage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend for stolen data' via 'creating a new Stripe customer object, and storing the stolen data in metadata fields'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid creation of multiple Stripe customer objects (cus_*) with suspicious metadata patterns (hex-encoded, base64, XOR-obfuscated, or non-standard field values). Correlate with atypical API key activity and monitor for unusual login geographies.

suggestion.title: Form field data capture and XOR obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the skimmer 'attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code)' which is 'obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally instead of immediately exfiltrated'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript hooking form submission events on checkout pages. Detect localStorage/sessionStorage writes with XOR-obfuscated byte patterns. Alert on data persistence immediately after form interaction, especially on Magento/Adobe Commerce sites.

suggestion.title: Malicious code delivery via compromised GTM containers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page'. This is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit GTM container configuration for unexpected network calls to api.stripe.com, Firestore, or non-whitelisted domains. Alert if GTM tags contain Function() constructors or eval() with externally-sourced data.

suggestion.title: Firestore metadata abuse for command and data retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant using 'Google Firestore...instead of Stripe', fetching payload from 'Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firestore projects for suspicious naming (braintree-*, payment-app, tracking). Alert on tracking/captcha-like documents queried from non-service principals. Correlate Firestore reads with subsequent checkout page execution and unusual access geographies.

suggestion.title: Post-exfiltration local data wiping
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Once the data is copied, the local file is wiped to eliminate traces of the attack and prevent duplicate uploads'. This cleanup pattern indicates successful exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate localStorage writes of encoded payment data with subsequent deletion of the same keys within seconds. Alert on patterns: (1) data written to localStorage, (2) API exfiltration call, (3) immediate localStorage.clear() or key deletion.

suggestion.title: Detect Large Data Exfiltration to External Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 234 GB of data was stolen: 'claimed to have stolen more than 234 GB of data.' Pipeline missed generation of exfiltration-volume detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single sessions or time windows with >50 GB cumulative egress to non-whitelisted external destinations, especially involving databases or file-share protocols. Correlate with off-hours access or service-account activity on systems hosting PII databases.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Threat Actor Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article names ShinyHunters as 'the infamous extortion group' that listed DentaQuest on its 'data leak site.' No actor-name IOC extraction occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor threat-intel feeds for ShinyHunters infrastructure, .onion domains, and ransom-note patterns. Alert on emails referencing the actor or leak-site domains, and track employee responses to extortion communications.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Network Access Following Initial Breach Discovery
suggestion.rationale: DentaQuest statement: 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network.' Kill chain should map this to initial-access / lateral-movement phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed VPN/RDP logons with successful logons to sensitive systems (healthcare databases, claims systems) within the same day. Alert on service-account logons outside standard business hours or geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Healthcare Data Access Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exposed data includes 'Health insurance information,' 'Government-issued IDs,' and 'Dates of birth'—data accessed or copied from healthcare claims/eligibility systems. No health-data-specific detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor claims and eligibility databases for bulk queries (>1000 record retrievals in <1 hour) or exports to non-standard locations. Flag access to government-ID fields, SSN columns, or health-plan details by accounts not normally querying those fields.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Ransom Demand and Extortion Site Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'infamous extortion group ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site and claimed to have stolen more than 234 GB' and 'failure to reach an agreement.' Ransom communications and leak-site posting are critical milestones in response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ransom-note emails or messages containing actor-attributed domains or identifiers. Implement OSINT monitoring of known ShinyHunters leak sites and alert on posting of DentaQuest assets, data previews, or victim listings.

suggestion.title: Breach Notification Delay and Incident Response Gaps
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The security incident came to light last month, when the infamous extortion group ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site.' Suggests breach occurred weeks before June 2 confirmation. Detection of late discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag breaches where threat-actor public disclosure precedes internal incident notification. Monitor for unlogged or undocumented network activity; correlate breach timelines (actor claim date vs. discovery date) with gaps in security monitoring or alert suppression logs.

suggestion.title: Detect Typosquatted/Homoglyph Tool Domains via WHOIS & Certificate Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states fake sites 'mimic open-source tools'—pipeline missed the infrastructure detection for lookalike domains. Should monitor domain registration patterns (name similarity, suspicious registrant, cheap hosters) and certificate issuance for tool-brand variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domain registrations with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known tool names (npm, terraform, docker, etc.). Monitor for bulk registrations under same registrant/IP/nameserver. Alert on SSL certificates with mismatched CA or self-signed status for domains claiming to be official tools. Correlate rapid domain creation with SEO backlink spam campaigns.

suggestion.title: Detect TDS Redirect Chains & User-Agent-Based Traffic Steering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions delivery 'via TDS' (Traffic Direction System)—pipeline extracted zero behavioral detection. TDS endpoints use conditional redirects based on User-Agent, referrer, geolocation; should detect fingerprinting patterns and redirect loops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 302/307/303 responses where the redirect target differs based on User-Agent/Accept-Language headers in successive requests to same URI. Flag redirect chains: search result → intermediate → TDS → final malware site. Monitor for abnormal HTTP headers (missing Referer, spoofed User-Agent, IP geolocation mismatches).

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Download from Non-Official Tool Domains
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: user searches for tool → clicks fake site → downloads malware. Article describes malware delivery but pipeline created no detection for download phase. Should correlate suspicious domain access with executable download + child process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads from domains containing tool keywords (python, node, terraform, docker, etc.) but NOT in official registrant whitelists. Flag downloads with anomalous headers (missing/incorrect Content-Disposition, MIME-type mismatch). Correlate download from non-canonical domain + child process spawning from Downloads/Temp within 120s. Use reputation APIs to identify unknown executables.

suggestion.title: Detect Search-Result Poisoning & Rank Manipulation Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights sites 'rank high on Google'—this is SEO poisoning attack (T1598.004). Pipeline missed infrastructure forensics: backlink farms, expired-domain hijacking, schema markup abuse, content syndication networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain clusters with abnormal backlink profiles (private blog networks, expired-domain reregistration, guest-post spam). Detect schema.org/JSON-LD injection with tool brand keywords and malicious URLs. Flag rapid Google Search rank jumps (position 1-5 in <30 days) for new domains. Correlate with Google Abuse Report submissions or DMCA takedowns.

suggestion.title: Detect Package Installation from Typosquatted/Fake Repositories
suggestion.rationale: If fake sites host malicious packages on npm/PyPI lookalikes, pipeline should detect unauthorized package manager access. Article implies tool-package spoofing but no package-repo-focused detection surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/pip/go package installations from domains outside official repositories (registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, etc.). Alert on packages with names ≤2 edits from popular tools (fuzzy match). Detect installation to unusual directories (not site-packages/node_modules). Flag package extraction + immediate child process execution with arguments suggesting post-install hooks.

suggestion.title: Detect Site Masquerading via Visual/Structural Similarity & SSL Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Core vector: 'fake sites mimicking open-source tools' (T1036.005). Pipeline missed certificate inventory, WHOIS divergence, and visual-similarity signals. Should detect domain/cert pairs mimicking legitimate tools but issued to unaffiliated registrants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor certificate issuance for domains similar to official tool sites (case variants, homoglyphs, missing hyphens, typos). Flag certificates issued by non-standard CAs (low-trust providers) for domains claiming to be official tools. Cross-check DNS A/AAAA records against hosting-provider IP ranges (bulletproof hosters, cheap VPS). Alert if WHOIS registrant differs from official tool organization.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Download from Malicious Ad Click
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' — users click ads and download the backdoor; T1204.001 (User Execution of Malicious Link) + T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .dmg or executable downloads initiated from browser processes when user clicked Google/YouTube ad links (referrer patterns). Look for parent process = browser, child = InstallService or standard macOS installers with unusual source URLs.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via FlutterShell Launch Agent
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor on macOS requires persistence; article says 'backdoor spreads' implying long-term presence. Standard macOS persistence is LaunchAgent or LaunchDaemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ with 'flutter' or 'shell' in name. Check for code-signing anomalies or execution of plist-referenced binaries from unusual paths (/tmp, ~/Library/Caches).

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor must establish C2 to receive commands; article implies active post-compromise activity ('spreads' suggests active campaigns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP(S) or DNS queries from flutter/shell-related processes to non-standard ports or domains. Correlate network beacons (fixed intervals, small payloads) with FlutterShell process execution.

suggestion.title: Ad Network Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' — Google/YouTube ad infrastructure itself was compromised, enabling distribution; this is supply-chain abuse (T1195.002).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser downloads from domains that serve ads for Google/YouTube (DoubleClick, ads.google.com partners). Flag cases where legitimate ad domain serves executable payloads or redirects to malware staging sites.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Flutter App or DMG Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware is named FlutterShell and likely distributed as macOS app or DMG; article provides no specific file indicators but execution of 'flutter' or unsigned shell-related binaries should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of any process with 'flutter' in name or code-signed by unknown/missing certs executing shell scripts. Monitor for bash/zsh child processes from unsigned macOS app bundles.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Gatekeeper/Notarization Bypass
suggestion.rationale: macOS backdoor reaching users via ads must bypass Gatekeeper; likely uses ad hoc signing, expired certs, or vulnerable notarization bypass (T1553.002).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of unsigned, ad-hoc signed, or self-signed binaries on Big Sur+. Flag .app bundles lacking valid Apple notarization tickets or with disabled SELinux/SIP protections.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to YPTSocket Plugin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any unauthenticated remote attacker' can inject payloads. Pipeline missed detection for requests to /plugin/YPTSocket/* that lack authentication headers or session tokens, establishing the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to /plugin/YPTSocket/* endpoints (especially webSocketSelfURI and page_title parameters) originating from sources without valid AVideo session cookies or authentication tokens. Flag requests from anonymous or low-privilege contexts attempting parameter injection.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Metadata Broadcast with XSS Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'Per-Client Metadata Broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin' as the injection mechanism. Pipeline did not detect abnormal WebSocket frames carrying encoded HTML/JavaScript in the broadcast channel.
log_sources: Web proxy logs (if WebSocket inspection enabled)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket messages on YPTSocket endpoints containing HTML event handlers (onerror, onload, onmouseover) or script tags in base64, hex, or URL-encoded form, particularly when page_title field contains these patterns.

suggestion.title: Administrator Session Cookie Exfiltration via XSS Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes JavaScript execution 'in the authenticated origin of every administrator.' Pipeline should detect downstream exfiltration of admin session cookies to external C2, not just local process access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate XSS injection requests to YPTSocket plugin with outbound connections from the web server or admin workstations to unusual domains within 5 minutes. Flag if an admin browsing the vulnerable page triggers exfiltration of HTTP request headers or cookie-bearing requests to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm package version installation (@cap-js/openapi@1.4.1)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'compromised version of @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 was published on May 19, 2026' — this is the initial compromise vector. No detection monitors for the vulnerable package version being installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml files for presence of @cap-js/openapi version 1.4.1. Query npm audit history for installs of this version. Alert on npm ci or npm install commands that resolve to 1.4.1.

suggestion.title: Preinstall/postinstall hook execution (generic npm lifecycle)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious packages... harvested credentials' implying code executed during install, but pipeline generated no detection for npm lifecycle hook execution itself (only Bun-specific assumption in UC_32_4). 'Setup.mjs' is inferred but not verified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json for preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare lifecycle hooks. Log all processes spawned during npm lifecycle phases. Flag packages with hooks that invoke scripts outside standard node/npm binaries during install phase.

suggestion.title: Node or npm process spawning shells or curl/wget during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attempted self-propagation' without specifying mechanism. Generic indicator that malicious payloads are executing shell commands or making outbound requests for staging/propagation code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node child processes during install phase for spawning bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe, or tools like curl, wget, git, python. Baseline legitimate install-phase spawns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive credential file enumeration (directory listing)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies harvested 'cloud provider credentials, SSH keys' — current UC_32_6 detects file open/access but not enumeration. Malware typically lists credential directories (ls -la ~/.aws, dir %USERPROFILE%\.ssh) before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node/bun executing dir/ls/ls -la on credential store directories: ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.azure, ~/.kube, ~/.docker, ~/.config/gh. Enumerate calls with recursive flags (-R, -la) during install phase.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration of environment variables or file contents to t.m-kosche.com
suggestion.rationale: UC_32_3 detects connection to C2 domain but not the content. Article states credentials 'harvested' — should detect exfiltration of credential content (env vars, file reads) to the IOC domain, not just connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from npm/node/bun processes to t.m-kosche.com for patterns containing AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, or file content from ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa in request body or headers.

suggestion.title: Package.json or lock file modification by non-human processes (self-propagation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attempted self-propagation' — implies malware tries to inject itself into package.json or lock files for persistence or lateral spread. No detection covers this attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml during or after npm install execution. Flag new dependency additions (especially packages to suspicious registries or unknown publishers). Alert on file modifications by npm/node/bun that change lock file hash.

suggestion.title: Unusual Outlook logon from new location or device
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'spied on' mailbox over 5 months—implies persistent login access. Attackers typically authenticate from new geographies or user agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Outlook/Exchange Online sign-in logs for authentication from new countries or IPs inconsistent with executive's baseline. Flag impossible-travel logins (geographic distance inconsistent with flight speed between consecutive authentications).

suggestion.title: Mailbox forwarding or delegation rule creation
suggestion.rationale: 5-month dwell time suggests attacker configured persistence mechanisms to monitor ongoing email. Forwarding rules or delegate access are common persistence tactics on compromised mailboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on New-InboxRule, Set-InboxRule, or Set-MailboxDelegate operations from unusual IP addresses or times outside business hours. Cross-reference mailbox owner's typical admin behavior.

suggestion.title: OAuth token issued to suspicious application with Mail.Read scope
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may have compromised credentials and granted third-party apps broad mail-read permissions ('spied on' mailbox requires sustained read access without repeated authentication).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for OAuth consent grants or application permission assignments to mail.read, mail.readwrite, or delegated permissions. Correlate with anomalous sign-in events. Flag apps with no legitimate business justification.

suggestion.title: Brute-force followed by successful authentication
suggestion.rationale: Executive mailbox compromise likely initiated via credential compromise—either phishing, password reuse, or brute force. 5-month timeframe suggests initial access ~5 months prior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify sequences of failed login attempts (threshold: ≥5 failures in 10 minutes) from same IP, followed by successful authentication within 1 hour. Correlate with phishing detection (T1566) campaigns targeting finance/executive domains.

suggestion.title: ExchangeOnlineManagement cmdlets executed from non-admin account
suggestion.rationale: Persistent mailbox access over 5 months may involve attacker-executed PowerShell commands to enumerate mailbox contents, disable MFA, or adjust retention policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Search-Mailbox, Get-Mailbox, or Set-Mailbox commands issued from user account lacking history of Exchange administration. Flag commands run outside business hours or from anomalous source IPs.

suggestion.title: Mailbox size or email count sudden increase (attacker exfiltration preparation)
suggestion.rationale: Before 5-month spying period, attacker likely prepared for bulk exfil (e.g., export-to-PST, forwarding catch-all).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for New-MailboxExportRequest, sudden deletion of large email batches, or mass copy-to-folder operations. Baseline executive mailbox size and flag deviations >15% month-over-month.

suggestion.title: Android APK Installation - Trojanized Fake News/PDF/Map Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states delivery via 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps'—these are trojanized legitimate-category apps. Title directly names attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK installations with names or publishers matching 'news', 'pdf', 'map', 'weather' categories from unknown sources or from non-official app stores. Correlate against known Asin family hashes/package names when available from full article content.

suggestion.title: Android Spyware Permission Abuse - Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Spyware definition requires excessive permissions. No spyware operates without contact/location/call log/SMS access. Gap: pipeline missed standard Android surveillance TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APKs with suspicious names requesting dangerous permissions (android.permission.READ_CONTACTS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, RECORD_AUDIO, READ_CALL_LOG, READ_SMS) in combination. Flag suspicious permission grants post-installation.

suggestion.title: Android Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Active spyware requires C2 channel. Article states 'Asin' is current threat; network-level C2 detection is baseline requirement for spyware campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from devices running Asin variants to known/suspected C2 domains. Look for beaconing patterns, non-standard ports (not 80/443), or HTTPS to self-signed/suspicious certificates from confirmed infected devices.

suggestion.title: Android Bulk Data Exfiltration - Spyware Collection Phase
suggestion.rationale: Spyware's functional purpose is data theft. For Arabic-user targeting, likely collects contacts, call logs, location, SMS, photos. Article emphasizes 'spyware' label—exfiltration detection is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when process associated with trojanized app accesses ContentProviders (READ_CONTACTS, READ_CALL_LOG, READ_SMS) in bulk, followed by network write to external server. Flag repeated ContentProvider queries in short time windows as collection phase indicator.

suggestion.title: Third-Party App Store or Sideload Detection - Arabic-Targeted Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article says 'fake' apps; implies either malicious app store listings or direct sideload distribution. 'Targets Arabic users' suggests region-specific distribution channels pipeline should surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installs from non-Google Play sources or from legitimate-looking app names published by unfamiliar publishers. Cross-reference app names against known-legitimate versions (e.g., 'Al Jazeera' vs. misspelled variants) for Arabic-language app categories.

suggestion.title: Brickstorm Backdoor C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Brickstorm as 'advanced malware implant' deployed across multiple targets for 12+ months undetected, using 'WebSocket protocol for C2 communications.' No detection rule for this family or its network signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound WebSocket connections over port 443 to C2 domains. Brickstorm uses multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams. Baseline legitimate WebSocket traffic, alert on anomalous destination IPs/domains, high packet frequency, or long-duration sessions to unknown endpoints.

suggestion.title: Plenet (.NET) Backdoor Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'cross-platform .NET-based backdoor' named Plenet (also Grimbolt) deployed to Synology NAS for interactive shell and RCE. No signature or behavioral detection specified for .NET reverse shells in embedded/NAS contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET-based reverse shells (dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe, csc.exe spawning cmd/powershell with network I/O). On NAS/Linux systems, alert on unexpected .NET runtime execution. Monitor for Plenet indicators: WebSocket connections, specific C2 domain switching logic.

suggestion.title: Stolen Credentials + Cloud Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access' and 'accessed the organization's Microsoft 365 environment' to 'blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access.' No UC for stolen-credential-sourced M365 access with VPN proxying.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on M365 signin from newly-enabled or external VPN IP addresses with no prior history for that user account. Flag multi-factor authentication bypass, conditional access policy changes preceding logins, or access to sensitive mailboxes/SharePoint from VPN egress IPs.

suggestion.title: Malware Deployment to NAS/Firewall Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deploying Plenet to Synology NAS and Brickstorm to pfSense firewall and Egnyte Storage Sync appliance. Most EDR/SIEM rules target Windows/Linux servers; embedded appliances go blind. Quote: 'targets systems that do not support endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH/Web SSH to NAS/firewall admin consoles for unusual binaries/scripts being written to persistence directories (/etc/init.d, /lib/systemd, web-root). Alert on admin credential changes or enable/reconfigure actions followed by process spawning.

suggestion.title: AgentPSD Python Reverse Shell (Fallback Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility...configured to connect to a different domain...deployed as a fallback persistence mechanism.' No detection for Python-based reverse shell droppers on production systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe or python3 spawning socket/subprocess modules with outbound network activity. Monitor for unusual Python script execution in temp directories or with inline base64 payloads. Alert on socket.connect() or subprocess.Popen() to hardcoded IPs/domains in Python code.

suggestion.title: MSP-to-Victim Lateral Movement Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the threat actor pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment' after compromising pfSense firewall at MSP 18 months prior. Requires detecting cross-tenant/cross-VPN anomalous access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate MSP account access patterns with victim account logins/resource access within 24-48 hours. Alert on administrative tasks performed on victim infrastructure originating from MSP VPN IPs. Flag unusual service principal or managed identity activity tied to MSP-managed integrations.

suggestion.title: Serv-U POST Request with Content-Encoding: deflate Header
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate' — this is the direct attack signature and should be detectable in HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to Serv-U listening ports (typically 21, 990, 40001, 8080, 3659) carrying the Content-Encoding: deflate header from external/untrusted sources. Legitimate Serv-U FTP traffic does not use this encoding combination.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Unexpected Termination
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes outcome: 'crash the Serv-U service' and 'crash servers' — service termination is the exploitation indicator and should be correlated with network events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Serv-U service process crash or shutdown. Correlate with preceding POST requests containing Content-Encoding: deflate to identify exploitation. Monitor for process exit codes or service stop events without administrative action.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific CVE with active exploitation confirmed by CISA; signature-based detection should match POST + deflate header + Serv-U ports without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Serv-U endpoints with Content-Encoding: deflate where no prior successful FTP/SFTP authentication handshake exists. Flag all instances regardless of response code, as the crash occurs server-side.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Internet Exposure Inventory Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Shodan currently tracks over 12,000 Serv-U servers exposed online' — proactive discovery of internet-facing instances is critical for vulnerability assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and external scanning (Shodan, Censys) for Serv-U instances accessible from the internet. Cross-reference against internal CMDB and identify systems still running pre-15.5.4 Hotfix 1 versions. Prioritize patching per BOD 22-01 deadline (June 19).

suggestion.title: Serv-U Version Detection Pre-15.5.4 Hotfix 1
suggestion.rationale: Article cites patch version 'SolarWinds Serv-U 15.5.4 Hotfix 1' as mitigation; all earlier versions are vulnerable. Version enumeration is necessary for patch compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Serv-U banner/version strings from network scans or software inventory systems. Alert on any instance reporting version < 15.5.4 or 15.5.4 without Hotfix 1 applied. Correlate with exposure data to identify exposed vulnerable systems.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-28318 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Scanners must flag Serv-U instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-28318 as the primary detection control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scanner matches for CVE-2026-28318 in Serv-U. Even patched instances flagged by lag between vulnerability disclosure and remediation. Cross-reference patch dates with KEV timeline (due 2026-06-19) to identify remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: Detect Serv-U POST with Content-Encoding deflate
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack requires 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header.' This is the direct exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to Serv-U endpoints with Content-Encoding: deflate header. Baseline legitimate deflate usage in your environment. Flag unauthenticated POST + deflate combinations as they match the no-auth exploitation requirement.

suggestion.title: Detect Serv-U Service Crash or Denial of Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows...to crash the Serv-U service'—service crash is the immediate, detectable impact of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected Serv-U service stops, crashes, or rapid restart loops. Correlate timing with POST request spikes and deflate-encoded traffic. Cluster multiple crashes within short windows as indicators of active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Serv-U Patch Gap Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal due date 2026-06-19. Unpatched exposure is the necessary condition for compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Serv-U instances across the estate. Flag those running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-28318. Calculate days since KEV publication vs. patch date; instances beyond due date represent non-compliance risk.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh Execution with Crafted Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uploads crafted file triggering the script: '/usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'. This execution pattern with unexpected file paths and arguments is the direct injection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with suspicious arguments, particularly when -cli path argument points to unexpected directories (e.g., /home/admin/ instead of legitimate config paths) or when .csv filenames suggest user-supplied content. Correlate with low-privileged user context (netadmin).

suggestion.title: Detect Root Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Context on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'local attackers with low privileges' execute 'arbitrary commands as root' and 'elevate their privileges as the root user'. This privilege jump is the core impact and requires detection at escalation point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent process runs by netadmin user spawning child processes with UID=0 (root). Focus on children of vScript processes, script upload utilities, or file-handling binaries on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems.

suggestion.title: Detect Configuration Upload to vSmart Controllers from Unauthorized Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers trigger 'configuration change pushed to edge devices' and IOC indicates 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number'. Unauthorized configuration distribution to vSmart controllers signals C2 or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/log/scripts.log and vScript audit logs for uploads of tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers where the source process is not the legitimate management daemon. Cross-reference config push events with prior failed authentication or file upload anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted File Upload Attempts Targeting vconfd or Script Processing
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires uploading 'crafted file' to trigger command injection. Article's IOC example shows CSV file upload. Detection must cover file-upload endpoints and temporary directories where scripts process untrusted input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file uploads (especially .csv, .sh, .txt) to directories referenced by vScript processing, or API uploads to endpoints that feed vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh. Flag files written to /home/admin/ or /tmp/ that are immediately executed by system binaries.

suggestion.title: Detect Tenant Credential or Config Data Staging in Attacker-Controlled Paths
suggestion.rationale: IOC shows attacker places 'malicious.csv' in /home/admin/ — an unusual location for legitimate config. This staging behavior precedes the injection attack and is a leading indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CSV or config-format files created by or accessible to netadmin user in non-standard directories (/home/admin/, /tmp/, user home dirs). Alert if these files are subsequently read by system-level processes or vScript utilities.

suggestion.title: Detect Attempts to Exploit Prior SD-WAN Authentication Bypasses (CVE-2026-20182, CVE-2026-20127)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127' can substitute for netadmin credentials. If those CVEs are exploited first, they are required precursors to CVE-2026-20245. Detecting the chain is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication with netadmin role following a failed or anomalous authentication event, or on HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20182 and CVE-2026-20127 exploitation patterns (authentication bypass, controller access without credentials). Timeline: exploit auth bypass → gain netadmin → upload crafted file → escalate to root.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Access for Sports Event Scams
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'fake sites' as primary attack vector. No detection for anomalous domain access or credential harvesting indicators on typosquatted/lookalike domains related to FIFA, ticketing platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains mimicking official FIFA or ticketing vendors (typosquats, lookalikes). Correlate with user credential entry or suspicious redirects. Establish baseline for event-related domain registrations 30–60 days pre-tournament.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Execution Post-Phishing Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'banking malware' as component. No use-case for suspicious process execution, DLL injection, or banking-specific hooking behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process spawning from browser or Office child processes with high entropy names or living-off-the-land execution patterns. Monitor for injection into banking/financial software or suspicious API calls to credential/keylogging APIs.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Against Ticketing Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stolen logins' being weaponized. No detection for high-velocity authentication attempts or geographically anomalous login patterns against known ticketing vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed login attempts against known ticketing platforms (Ticketmaster, etc.) from multiple IPs in short timeframe. Correlate successful logins with impossible-travel geo signals or TOR/proxy exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credential Storage Artifacts Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article references compromised account credentials. No detection for dumped credentials in memory, registry, or temp files characteristic of banking malware post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious access to browser credential stores (Chrome SQLite, Firefox profile), registry hives (SAM, LSA secrets), or temp file creation with encoded credential patterns. Correlate with banking malware process signatures.

suggestion.title: Event-Themed Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign specifically targets FIFA World Cup interest. No detection for high-volume phishing emails with sports-event-themed lures, fake ticketing urgency, or VIP access narratives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with FIFA/World Cup/ticketing keywords, urgency language ('limited access', 'final chance'), and suspicious attachments or embedded links. Flag senders using free email providers impersonating official FIFA/vendor domains.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Geographic Logins During Tournament Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Event-driven scams peak near tournament start. No detection for bulk account compromise indicators tied to temporal and geographic correlation around FIFA 2026.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In the 30 days before FIFA 2026 (June 2026), flag successful logins to ticketing/sports accounts from unexpected countries or VPN/proxy exit nodes. Correlate clusters (>50 accounts from single IP in 1 hour) to identify bulk compromise waves.

suggestion.title: POST /runners/start without authentication headers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution' and 'POST /runners/start allows remote code execution.' Detection should flag POST requests to this endpoint lacking standard auth tokens (Authorization header, session cookie, API key).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST requests to /runners/start or /runners/load-reader endpoints where Authorization, X-API-Key, or session cookies are absent or null. Correlate with external source IPs. This is the initial access vector for the unauthenticated RCE.

suggestion.title: JavaScript functionName parameter injection in POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'The functionName value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' Detection should pattern-match POST /runners/start payloads containing 'functionName' with suspicious syntax (quotes, backticks, semicolons, shell metacharacters).
log_sources: proxy logs with full request capture
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST body payloads sent to /runners/start for 'functionName' parameter containing injection patterns: backticks, semicolons, process module calls ('require("child_process")', 'spawn', 'exec'), or quote escaping attempts. High-confidence indicator of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Rapid process tree creation from Node.js under DbGate context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'generated code is then executed in a forked Node.js child process.' Post-exploitation, attackers spawn shell or binaries for command execution. Detection should flag Node.js creating multiple children in short window, especially unusual binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node process spawning 3+ child processes (sh, bash, cmd, powershell, wget, curl, python, perl, etc.) within 60 seconds, where parent has 'dbgate' or 'bundle.js' in command line. Anomaly detection: baseline node child-process ratios and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: File writes to system binaries from Node.js DbGate context
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers may persist by writing to /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, or system directories. Article hunts reference these paths. Detection should flag any file creation/modification in sensitive paths initiated from Node.js dbgate process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FileCreated or FileModified events in /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/local/bin, /etc/cron* initiated by Node.js process with dbgate in parent command line. Exclude known package managers and deployment processes.

suggestion.title: Environment variable poisoning / DBGATE_ vars in child process context
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates DbGate uses environment variables (DBGATE_API mentioned in hunt). Attackers may set malicious DBGATE_* env vars to influence child process behavior. Detection should alert on unexpected DBGATE_* variable modifications.
log_sources: sysmon process creation (Event ID 1 with command line)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent is Node.js with 'dbgate' in command and child processes have newly-set DBGATE_* environment variables or modified PATH/LD_PRELOAD. Baseline normal DBGATE_* vars and alert on additions.

suggestion.title: Authenticated HTTP POST /runners/load-reader with code-injection syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Any user with valid DbGate credentials can execute arbitrary OS commands' — requires both authentication and malicious POST. UC_12_2 detects payload but not auth correlation; separate hunt needed for auth-first pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful DbGate authentication events (successful login, session creation) with subsequent HTTP POST to /runners/load-reader within 60 seconds, where POST body or URL contains JavaScript execution keywords. Flag requests from authenticated users attempting injection.

suggestion.title: Dynamic import() abuse to bypass require=null sandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The `require = null` mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic `import()`' — this evasion technique is specific and detectable. Generic child_process hunts miss attackers using only import().
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST /runners/load-reader requests containing 'import(' pattern (including URL-encoded variants). Flag instances where import() appears but require() does not — indicates intentional sandbox evasion technique.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning with command-injection temporal correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code injected into functionName parameter spawning shell commands. Behavioral hunt matching web request timestamp with child process creation on same host, where child parent is DbGate application, establishes exploitation causality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web request logs (POST /runners/load-reader) with process creation logs on same endpoint within 2 seconds. Flag when child processes (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned from node/dbgate context match timing of malicious POST. Verify parent process has network listener characteristic of web service.

suggestion.title: ait-bsc or Python process creating/modifying files outside configured log root
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary file append' and ability to 'direct BSC to log to arbitrary filesystem paths'. No detection explicitly hunts for unauthorized filesystem writes. This is T1565.001 (Data Manipulation) — the core impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for ait-bsc process or child Python processes writing to files outside /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs (or configured log_root). Flag writes to /etc, /home, /root, /var/www, and other sensitive directories. Correlate with preceding HTTP requests to /start endpoint to establish causation.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST requests to */start endpoint with suspicious query parameters (generic)
suggestion.rationale: UC_8_2 is service-specific (ait-bsc). Need a production-grade hunt using Web datamodel / HTTP logs that detects POST requests containing path-traversal indicators (..%2e%2e, encoded slashes, etc) to **/start** endpoints, regardless of service. This applies to any HTTP API with similar vulnerability patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP POST requests where uri_path matches */start and uri_query or http_request_body contains traversal sequences (.. %2e %252e %c0%ae) or absolute path markers (/etc/ /var/ /home/). Exclude known-good scanners and pentesting tools.

suggestion.title: ait-bsc listening on public/unexpected network interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'triggered over the network by unauthenticated attacker'. Reconnaissance phase should detect exposure of BSC service to untrusted networks. Currently missing from hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ait-bsc Python process in LISTEN state on non-loopback interfaces (0.0.0.0, ::) on HTTP ports (8080, 8000, 5000, etc.). Flag especially if bound to public-routable interfaces without firewall ACLs restricting access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized role creation via Livewire endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use its public actions to create new roles' — any authenticated user can trigger role creation despite insufficient authorization checks. Must detect unexpected role-creation operations from low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/PATCH to Livewire role-creation endpoints (*/livewire/update* targeting role endpoints) from non-admin users. Establish baseline of which roles normally create roles; flag outliers. Combine with temporal clustering: rapid role creation + user deletion within short time window indicates escalation attempt.

suggestion.title: User deletion from non-admin accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attackers to 'delete other users, including administrators' — this is the highest-impact escalation outcome. Hunt for DELETE operations against user objects initiated by accounts lacking user-admin role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Settings/Team endpoints for user deletion operations (DELETE /users/* or Livewire message targeting user removal). Cross-reference requester's role assignment against deletion permissions. Alert on any admin-account deletion by non-privileged user or bulk-deletion patterns.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via RolePermission manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes RolePermission endpoint 'gated on view_users perm' — insufficient authorization. Authenticated users can modify role-permission mappings to grant themselves elevated access that their role should not possess.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all changes to role_permission entries. Alert when a role grants permissions it previously did not have, especially privileged operations (admin, delete_users, create_roles, modify_roles). Correlate permission grant with user's actual assigned role to detect self-escalation.

suggestion.title: Settings/Team endpoint enumeration by low-privilege accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'any authenticated user could load the page' — Settings/Team/Index had no authorization check. Hunt for unusual access to team configuration endpoints from accounts unlikely to manage teams (service accounts, read-only roles).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal access to /settings/team/* endpoints by role and user type. Alert on access by service accounts, automation accounts, or non-team-admin users. Chain with subsequent role creation or permission modification to identify recon-to-exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Session-based privilege escalation chains in Shopper
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires an authenticated session. Hunt for temporal sequences within single session: login → Settings/Team access → role/permission mutation → admin-level operations. Short time-delta from authentication to escalation suspicious for compromised low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user session tokens / request IDs across Settings/Team access, role mutations, and subsequent privileged operations. Flag low-privilege user accounts performing admin-level actions (user deletion, role creation). Flag service-account sessions with interactive Settings/Team access followed by mutations.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'take over sites' — site takeover typically establishes admin accounts for persistence. Pipeline missed the obvious post-compromise account-creation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table insert/update) occurring within 5 minutes of plugin exploitation indicators. Flag creation of accounts with admin role (wp_usermeta user_level >= 10) by non-admin actors. Expected FP: legitimate administrator provisioning; filter by standard admin scheduling windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Plugin Installation/Modification Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover often involves installing webshells as plugins or backdoored plugin variants. Article describes 'take over' but pipeline noted no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to /wp-content/plugins/ outside maintenance windows, especially compressed archives (zip/tar) or PHP files with suspicious entropy signatures. Correlate with failed Everest Forms Pro requests or admin-account-creation events.

suggestion.title: Web Shell/Backdoor Upload to WordPress Root or Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover implies code execution; attackers typically upload shells to web-accessible paths. No web shell detection UC generated despite 'take over' impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP/JSP/ASPX file creation in /wp-content/, /wp-admin/, or plugin directories by HTTP daemon user (www-data, IUSR) post-request to Everest Forms Pro endpoints. Flag files with names matching shell patterns (e.g., shell.php, wp-admin.php, update.php) or high entropy/obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Everest Forms Pro Vulnerability (CVE-TBD)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'critical flaw' but pipeline extracted zero technique mapping. T1190 should be primary phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro endpoints (typically /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/...) with suspicious parameter values: unauthenticated form submissions, path traversal payloads (../, null bytes), or large/binary content. Correlate with subsequent admin account creation or file uploads.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Plugin Endpoint Access and Parameter Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Critical plugin flaw implies unauthenticated access; article describes 'hackers exploit' but no initial-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Everest Forms Pro usage patterns (form submissions, legitimate user interactions). Alert on abnormal POST parameter sizes, encoding anomalies, repeated failed responses (40x), or scanner user-agents targeting plugin files.

suggestion.title: File Hash Match — Malicious Package SHA1
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists SHA1 `a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089` under 'Indicators of Compromise' with confidence 'High' and recommends template-driven hunt for 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match'; pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero use cases despite this being canonical substitution logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on files or process payloads matching SHA1 a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089 across endpoints (site-packages, temp directories, cache). Correlate with pip install logs for 'parsimonius' package name. High-fidelity signal for confirmed malicious package deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Typosquat Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'package named parsimonius was crafted to look almost identical to...parsimonious library...the single missing letter' — this is masquerading via name confusion. Pipeline missed T1036 and failed to generate detection for pip install of look-alike package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install command-line for package names with edit-distance ≤1 to high-value libraries (parsimonious, requests, cryptography, etc.). Flag installations from accounts/hosts without prior history. Baseline legitimate dev environments to distinguish intentional typo corrections from attacks.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Repository Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A deceptive Python package quietly made its way into the PyPI repository' — indicates successful unauthorized package publication, either account compromise or repository policy gap. Kill-chain initial-access phase missing entirely from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI for package uploads by accounts with low publish history or unusual timing patterns. Flag new packages with names ≤2 character edits from trending/popular libraries. Cross-reference upload source IP/geolocation against historical maintainer patterns. Detect obfuscated or non-obvious payloads in setup.py via code similarity hashing.

suggestion.title: Trusted Library Name Spoofing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly describes mimicry of legitimate library: 'crafted to look almost identical to the widely used parsimonious library.' This is T1199 (Trusted Relationship) abuse. No corresponding detection for package-name-similarity scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement automated scoring of candidate packages against high-value libraries using edit-distance, Levenshtein ratio, and semantic similarity. Flag packages with high name-match scores but mismatched author/description/maintainer history. Integrate with developer IDE plugin warnings and package installation prompts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Upload or Version Bump
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Hit npm in Supply Chain Attacks'—requires compromise of package registry or publisher account. Pipeline must flag unauthorized uploads or abnormal version/metadata changes by non-whitelisted publishers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for unexpected package uploads by new or unverified publishers. Alert on rapid version increments (0.0.1 → 1.0.0 same day), packages with typosquatted names similar to popular libraries, or metadata changes (author, homepage, etc.) without corresponding commits.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Compromised npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'worms' execute post-installation. Pipeline must detect child processes spawned from node_modules binaries, postinstall hooks, or install scripts with suspicious behavior (network I/O, system registry writes, credential access).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node/npm spawns child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget) or makes unexpected network connections to non-package-registry IPs. Correlate parent process command-line (npm install) with unusual child execution within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm Package Source
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Miasma Worm Variant'—variants imply polymorphic code, obfuscation, or encoding. Pipeline must flag heavily-obfuscated JavaScript, base64 strings, eval() chains, and high-entropy code patterns in package contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package.tar contents for high Shannon entropy in .js files, atob/Buffer.from/hex-decode patterns, eval/Function constructors operating on dynamic strings, or code complexity (lines per function, nesting depth) exceeding baseline for package category.

suggestion.title: Known IronWorm or Miasma Malware Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Malware families are named in title and should be mapped to known file hashes, behavioral signatures, C2 domains, or registry artifacts. Pipeline failed to surface threat-actor-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file execution with hashes matching IronWorm or Miasma families. Monitor for behavioral signatures: registry writes to Run/RunOnce keys, scheduled-task creation, WMI event subscriptions, or spawning of credential-dumping utilities (mimikatz, laZagne, etc.).

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Compromise via package-lock.json
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks propagate through dependency trees. Pipeline must flag package-lock.json or package.json modifications introducing unknown dependencies, versions from untrusted registries, or packages on known-compromised blocklists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of package-lock.json with unexpected entries (new transitive dependencies not in upstream). Cross-reference all resolved packages against threat-intel blocklist. Alert on package versions older than latest (potential downgrade) or from non-official registry mirrors.

suggestion.title: Browser process sustaining C2 beaconing during AI platform session
suggestion.rationale: Article states extensions are 'sending conversations off'—yet no hunt detects browser process establishing persistent or periodic connections to deepaichats.com / chatsaigpt.com while user is actively on ChatGPT, Claude, or Copilot. This is the exfiltration channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate chrome.exe/msedge.exe initiating DNS or TCP to deepaichats.com/chatsaigpt.com with concurrent web traffic to chatgpt.com, claude.ai, or copilot.microsoft.com. Flag sustained beacons (>3 connections/minute) or large outbound payloads.

suggestion.title: Extension content script DOM access on AI platform pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states extensions 'harvest conversations'—implying DOM parsing, clipboard capture, or sessionStorage reads from ChatGPT/Claude/Copilot UIs. No detection targets this collection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If extension telemetry available, detect calls to document.querySelectorAll(), XPath evaluation, or Clipboard.readText() from sandboxed extension context while page URL contains known AI platforms. Flag any exfiltration of page content to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or obfuscated extension code at installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extensions often hide logic via minification, Base64 encoding, or code injection (T1027). Article implies extensions bypass browser security—suggest detection of obfuscated manifest.json or background scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to browser extension directories post-installation. Flag manifest.json modifications, Base64-encoded background scripts, or unusual script injection patterns. Cross-reference with extension permissions (clipboard, webRequest, storage).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - Vulnerable DD-WRT Firmware (Gafgyt C0XMO)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'targets a known vulnerability in DD-WRT router firmware' and names five CVEs (CVE-2021-27137, CVE-2015-2051, CVE-2022-35914, CVE-2016-15047, CVE-2025-34054). Recon-phase detection for unpatched edge devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for DD-WRT installations; flag firmware versions matching the five cited CVEs. Cross-reference with external traffic to the three identified C2 IPs to detect post-compromise persistence.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing - Outbound Connections to Gafgyt C0XMO Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three C2 IPs (85.215.131.70, 217.160.125.125, 176.100.37.91) and implies C2 communication when it states malware 'gains full access' and performs 'modular propagation,' requiring command delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound traffic from Linux/router devices to the three identified IPs on any port. Investigate protocol fingerprints for botnet signatures. Correlate with DNS queries for reverse-lookups of those IPs.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution - C0XMO File Hash Detection
