suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify encrypted POST/PUT traffic from smart TVs to central collection servers with timing consistency (batch shipment patterns). Alert on large payloads, compression artifacts, or traffic outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from Smart TV Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps execute scraping code — requires detection of unexpected process spawning or shell invocations from app contexts, which smart TV apps should not perform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell processes (sh, bash, curl, wget) spawned from non-system app UIDs or scheduled task creation from installer contexts. Smart TV apps should have minimal process tree depth.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Smart TV Network Destination Profiling
suggestion.rationale: Article describes scraping 'for AI' — implies requests to content sites and model-training infrastructure. Pipeline should flag requests to known data aggregation or AI training service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain list of known web-scraping-hostile domains and AI training data brokers. Alert when smart TV devices make DNS queries or connections to these targets from app-controlled contexts.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Connections to Known Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists C2 domains (proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, etc.) and IPs. This is foundational IOC-based hunt; pipeline generated zero use cases despite having high-confidence network indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections from smart TV devices to any enumerated proxy infrastructure domains (bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io) or IPs (3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114). High fidelity; consumer devices have minimal legitimate reason to contact proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Enrollment Handshake with Proxy Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps 'quietly enroll' devices into proxy network. Behavioral detection: apps making initial contact with proxy infrastructure shortly after installation or launch, suggesting device registration/enrollment in proxy service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps making network connections to known proxy infrastructure domains within minutes of app installation or first run. Look for enrollment/handshake traffic patterns (e.g., registration, device ID transmission) that indicate proxy network enrollment.

suggestion.title: Elevated Sustained Outbound Traffic Forwarding from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes devices being 'turned into proxies' to 'scrape web data.' Detection: smart TV devices exhibiting unusual sustained traffic volume, forwarding traffic to diverse external destinations, or making requests inconsistent with normal user-initiated browsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect smart TV devices with sustained high outbound connection volume, traffic to unusual/numerous unique destinations, or traffic patterns suggesting the device is forwarding requests on behalf of external entities rather than serving local user needs.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Buried Consent Dialogs in Smart TV Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies deception mechanism: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' This is social engineering (T1204). Detection: apps that hide permission prompts in complex UI navigation, making true informed consent difficult.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV app behavior for consent dialog anomalies: dialogs requiring excessive navigation steps, auto-dismissing dialogs, dialogs defaulting to 'accept,' or dialogs rendered off-screen or with reduced visibility relative to normal app UI.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known Malicious Smart TV Free Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific malicious free apps on Samsung, LG, Roku app stores. Requires app name/hash IOCs (not provided in article summary but should be sourced from Include Security research). File-based detection of known malicious apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of known malicious smart TV app names and hashes. Alert on installation or execution of known malicious apps on smart TV devices. Cross-reference with official app store inventory to distinguish legitimate apps from malicious lookalikes.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Code Commits to GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'hit 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories' in a supply chain attack. Malicious code commits would be the primary infection vector for downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API for commits by non-standard service accounts, commits introducing binary files or suspicious scripts to source repos, or commits bypassing branch protections. Correlate with sudden spikes in commit velocity or repo owner alerts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Access to Microsoft GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise of 73 repos implies attacker gained write access through credential abuse, SSO compromise, or PAT token theft. Initial access is critical detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub/Azure AD logins from anomalous IPs, impossible-travel patterns, new SSH keys or personal access tokens added to accounts, or API calls from unfamiliar user agents outside normal working hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Worm-Like Propagation in Code Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Threat explicitly named 'Miasma Worm'—indicating self-replicating malware. Worms propagate across network boundaries; should detect replication patterns across shared development infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file creation across multiple repos or shares, unusual processes spawned from git operations, mass SMB connections from development infrastructure, or scheduled tasks created on developer workstations following GitHub access.

suggestion.title: Detect Execution of Code from Compromised Microsoft Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack impact depends on downstream execution by developers/CI/CD systems using affected repos. Article scope suggests tooling already deployed to consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from git clone/pull operations, scripts executed from repo working directories, PowerShell invocations from .git directories, or build commands executing code from recently updated repos.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Package/Artifact Distribution from Poisoned Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on code repos manifest as poisoned packages or binaries distributed downstream. This is the critical impact vector for a 73-repo compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs for unusual packages from Microsoft orgs, unsigned packages, unexpected dependencies, or spikes in pull/download volume. Alert on mass consumption of packages versioned after compromise timestamp.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Administrative Actions from Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — sudden mass disables of repos within a short window is a hallmark of supply chain cleanup or attacker lockout. No UC was generated despite this being the impact signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single service principal or user disabling/deleting >10 repositories within 60 minutes. Monitor for Repository.Delete, Repository.Disable events in GitHub/Azure audit logs; correlate with out-of-band incident reports or unusual auth patterns (e.g. new session from anomalous location).

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow Injection into GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' via supply chain — GitHub Actions workflows are the primary vector for dependency injection and agent compromise. No detection rule for modified workflows, new steps, or exfiltration commands was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflow YAML additions that execute external scripts (curl/wget), access secrets env vars, or trigger unusual outbound connections. Flag newly-added workflow steps referencing unknown actions or inline script shells in >10 repos within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Worm targets repos directly — likely injects malicious packages or modifies dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, etc). Article states attack targets 'AI Coding Agents' which typically consume language-specific packages; no UC for manifest tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions/modifications to dependency manifests (package.json, setup.py, go.mod, etc.) that introduce new or unexpected package versions, esp. from unknown registries. Correlate with commit history anomalies (unusual committer, timing outside business hours, no PR review).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Azure Functions Action Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Azure Functions Action' as primary target — this is a GitHub Actions action used to deploy functions. No detection for unauthorized modifications to its source, malicious versions, or hijacked workflows referencing it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect changes to azure-functions-action step definitions, new pinned versions to unofficial forks, or workflows using versions with atypical commit hashes. Alert on successful deployments from modified action immediately preceding repo disable events.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Prompt Injection or Command Escape via Compromised Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' explicitly — suggests malware injects prompts or commands that escape sandboxing. No UC for detecting unusual AI tool behavior, code generation anomalies, or escape attempts from agent runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent process spawning: unexpected child processes (bash, PowerShell, curl), file writes outside intended directories, or environment variable exfiltration. Flag if agent generates or executes code that differs from historical baselines.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation via Repository Forks or Clones
suggestion.rationale: Named 'Miasma Worm' implies self-propagating malware. Article affects multiple repos — no UC detects rapid cloning, forking, or mass-distribution patterns typical of worm propagation through software supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single account/session cloning or forking >50 repositories in <4 hours, or simultaneous clone operations from multiple CI/CD agents. Correlate with subsequent commits/pushes to forked repos to confirm propagation intent.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Installation - Malicious durabletask Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — no detection use case for installation of known-malicious package versions via pip, setuptools, or requirements.txt. This is the primary attack surface for downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip/setuptools installation of durabletask with version numbers matching the disclosed compromise window. Track package metadata (timestamp, hash) against known-good baseline. Alert on version downgrades or rapid re-installation of durabletask in development/build environments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution from Compromised durabletask Import
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a supply-chain attack, implying malicious code injection into the package. No detection for execution from the compromised durabletask module or its submodules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned during or immediately after import of durabletask or its submodules. Cross-reference process parent against known legitimate durabletask use cases. Flag execution of system commands, network calls, or file writes originating from site-packages/durabletask/ without correlated application logic.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Repository Anomaly - Version or Signature Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises often involve version tampering or signature replacement. Article does not reveal if package hash/signature changed or versions were hijacked, but pipeline should detect package metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track hash/signature of durabletask installations against PyPI canonical records. Alert on certificate pinning failures, hash mismatches, or unsigned packages. Monitor for duplicated versions or non-sequential version jumps that may indicate compromise window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Activity from durabletask Module Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload in durabletask may establish C2 or exfil data. No detection for network calls from processes that imported the compromised package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate network destinations contacted by durabletask-dependent applications. Alert on new external IPs/domains, unusual ports (esp. non-443, non-80), or DNS queries to C2-hosting registrars from processes that loaded durabletask from site-packages.

suggestion.title: File Modification in site-packages/durabletask Directory Without Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Post-install persistence or further payload staging. Article describes compromise but no detection for unauthorized file changes within the installed package directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or deletion within site-packages/durabletask/ after initial pip install. Alert on .pyc/.pyo recompilation, new .so/.pyd binary injection, or __pycache__ tampering. Exclude legitimate pip updates; flag all other changes.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Propagation - Downstream Compromise of durabletask Consumers
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a compromised upstream package; any application that depends on durabletask is now at risk. Pipeline should track transitive dependency risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build transitive dependency graph from affected durabletask versions. Identify all internal applications and libraries that declare durabletask as direct or transitive dependency. Prioritize for re-deployment review, testing, and incident investigation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Android App Installation from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'Targets Arabic Users via Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps' — delivery explicitly via trojanized apps, not official store distribution. Pipeline missed initial access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Android devices with `pm list packages` output containing suspicious or newly-added packages matching known malware families or suspicious publishers. Track installation from non-Google Play sources via DeviceInfo telemetry or MDE sideload indicators. Correlate with user locale=AR in risk signals.

suggestion.title: Android App Requesting Excessive Surveillance Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Spyware by definition requests SMS (T1434), contact (T1432), location (T1430), and call log (T1433) permissions. Article describes 'spyware' capabilities but pipeline missed permission-grant detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single app requests READ_CALL_LOG, READ_SMS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, and READ_CONTACTS in manifest or at runtime. Establish baseline of legitimate apps with these perms and flag anomalies. Flag apps claiming to be 'news' or 'utilities' with location+SMS+contacts perms.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Beaconing from Android App to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Spyware exfiltrates data via C2. Article implies command-and-control infrastructure ('spyware') but pipeline extracted no domains or C2 indicators and missed network detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect persistent or periodic DNS/IP connections from suspicious app packages to non-CDN IPs using unusual ports (non-80/443). Flag connections from apps claiming to be news/utilities to IP ranges not associated with legitimate ad/analytics vendors. Correlate with app install events.

suggestion.title: Android Malware Family 'Asin' Package Enumeration and Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Asin' as the malware family. Pipeline failed to extract this as a threat actor and create signature-based detection. Specific package names for fake apps (PDF, news, war map variants) should be identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create watchlist for known Asin package names (pipeline should have extracted these from article IOC sections). Monitor for app launch events matching known variants. Flag app processes spawning child processes or loading DEX files at runtime (dynamic code loading, T1407).

suggestion.title: Android Spyware Data Exfiltration via SMS or Contact List Sync
suggestion.rationale: Spyware Asin collects SMS and contacts — article implies exfil but pipeline missed exfiltration detection. Data theft is core capability, not covered by any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk SMS reading (ContentProvider queries to SMS/MMS) followed immediately by encrypted network requests to non-standard ports. Flag contact list access (ContactsProvider) followed by HTTP POST with encoded/gzipped payloads. Alert on ContentResolver queries from non-system apps to call/SMS logs.

suggestion.title: Arabic Locale Targeting & Geo-Specific Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Targets Arabic Users' — geo/locale is targeting signal. Pipeline should flag malware distribution campaigns targeting specific regional user bases via localized app names/content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious app installations with device locale=AR (or Arabic language preference). Flag when apps mimicking Arabic-language news, maps, or utilities are installed on devices in AR-locale environments. Monitor Telegram/WhatsApp distribution links targeting Arabic communities.

suggestion.title: Egnyte Storage Sync Appliance as Persistent Proxy Foothold
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'VerdantBamboo compromised an Egnyte Storage Sync system and accessed it periodically through the victim's web SSL VPN... used Brickstorm proxying features and stolen credentials' to reach M365. 18+ months undetected on untested appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on persistent single-credential access to storage sync appliances over months-long windows from stable source IPs, especially with SSL VPN tunnel patterns. Monitor for appliance config exports or backups accessed by non-admin accounts. Correlate appliance network participation with downstream M365 compromises.

suggestion.title: Brickstorm WebSocket C2 Multiplexing Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Plenet... using the WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams'. Custom multiplexing on encrypted WebSocket bypasses HTTP inspection and connection-per-command assumptions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WebSocket handshakes to newly-observed or uncommon domains on non-standard ports; alert on rapid frame exchanges suggesting multiplexed concurrent streams. Correlate with Golang/Rust service processes or long-running System processes with network I/O. Detect infrastructure teardown patterns (abrupt port 443 service shutdown).

suggestion.title: MSP Firewall Compromise as Customer Lateral Movement Bridge
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'investigation at the customer's MSP, where Volexity found... BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall... compromised at least 18 months earlier' then 'attacker pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment' with medium confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/admin logins to MSP-managed firewalls from non-baseline sources; flag rule additions or tunnel interface creation by service accounts. Monitor for VPN access enabling or credential injection post-patch. Cross-correlate MSP firewall activity timestamps with customer intrusion timelines and Brickstorm C2 patterns.

suggestion.title: Plenet .NET Cross-Platform Backdoor on NAS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Plenet... is a cross-platform .NET-based backdoor that offers interactive shell access, remote command execution, file manipulation' deployed 'to a Synology NAS appliance'. Escapes Windows-centric EDR surveillance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NAS systems for unexpected .NET runtime spawning shell interpreters (bash, sh); alert on file operations by backup/sync service accounts outside scheduled windows. Detect WebSocket outbound connections initiated from storage services on Synology boxes running Plenet fingerprints.

suggestion.title: AgentPSD Python Reverse Shell as Secondary Persistence Fallback
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility that Volexity believes VerdantBamboo used as a fallback persistence mechanism... configured to connect to a different domain than the one Brickstorm used'. Defense-in-depth multi-domain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python interpreter spawning socket, subprocess, or system shell in single execution context. Monitor for scheduled Python tasks or cron jobs on systems lacking EDR. Correlate outbound C2 from Python processes to non-Brickstorm-fingerprinted domains (multi-fallback indicator).

suggestion.title: M365 Conditional Access Bypass via Brickstorm Proxying
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Volexity assesses with high confidence that this was done to blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access policies that would have otherwise prevented access' using stolen credentials and Brickstorm C2 proxying.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: M365 sign-in success from Egnyte appliance / pfSense / NAS network ranges with service accounts or non-human patterns; missing expected EDR device compliance signals (Brickstorm intercepts auth). Flag impossible-travel scenarios (appliance network → LAN internal in minutes). Correlate M365 sessions with Egnyte/pfSense timeline.

suggestion.title: Serv-U DoS via Content-Encoding Deflate Header
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate.' This is an explicit, reproducible attack signature that must be detectable at network or application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Serv-U endpoints (commonly port 2121, or HTTPS listener) containing 'Content-Encoding: deflate' header, without authentication credentials. This may be preceded by enumeration of Serv-U instances on public-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Termination
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'crash the Serv-U service.' Should detect abnormal termination, service restart loops, or availability loss coinciding with POST floods or suspicious HTTP patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Serv-U process termination, high-frequency service restarts, or process crash events. Correlate with network logs for POST request spikes or Content-Encoding deflate headers in the same time window.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Serv-U Version Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'SolarWinds released Serv-U 15.5.4 Hotfix 1 on Thursday to patch this denial-of-service vulnerability.' Any instance running versions prior to Hotfix 1 is at immediate risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan and alert on Serv-U installations with version < 15.5.4 Hotfix 1. Correlate Shodan/Shadowserver data against internal asset inventory to identify publicly exposed vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Public Exposure of Serv-U Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Shodan currently tracks over 12,000 Serv-U servers exposed online.' External asset intelligence should trigger investigation and accelerated patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish automated lookups against Shodan/Shadowserver feeds for organization's IP ranges running Serv-U. Flag any hits and cross-reference against internal patch inventory to prioritize exposed-unpatched assets.

suggestion.title: Clop or DEV-0322 Reconnaissance for Serv-U Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Clop ransomware gang exploited a Serv-U remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2021-35211)' and 'DEV-0322 Chinese hackers also deployed CVE-2021-35211 exploits.' Both threat groups have established patterns targeting Serv-U. Should monitor for their TTPs if CVE-2026-28318 becomes a stepping stone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track indicators of Clop or DEV-0322 tooling and reconnaissance patterns (malware signatures, C2 domains, scanning behavior). Escalate if observed near Serv-U assets, especially in conjunction with POST anomalies or version-detection probes.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Malicious POST with Content-Encoding Deflate
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header to crash the Serv-U service'. This is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Serv-U listening ports (default 22, 3389 in Serv-U contexts; check your asset inventory) with Content-Encoding: deflate header and unusually small or malformed payloads. Correlate with immediate service crash or restart.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'allows...to crash the Serv-U service without authentication'. Service crashes are the direct impact signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process logs and Windows System Event Log for unexpected service terminations (exit codes, crashes) immediately preceded by HTTP POST traffic. Flag if crash frequency increases during a time window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the attack requires 'no authentication'. Unauthenticated POST to a normally-authenticated service is a strong signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Serv-U endpoints that lack valid session tokens, Authorization headers, or known authentication mechanisms. Establish baseline of legitimate, authenticated POST traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Vulnerability Scan Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Verify scanner coverage.
log_sources: Vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate all known Serv-U instances are covered by your vulnerability scanner and flagged for CVE-2026-28318. Cross-reference with patch management records; alert on instances showing as 'vulnerable' or 'patch-delayed' past 2026-06-19 due date.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Public-Facing Exposure Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application), implying Serv-U listening on internet-accessible ports. Unpatched exposure is the precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Serv-U instances and verify none are internet-routable without multi-factor auth or IP allowlist. Flag any instance with inbound HTTP(S) POST access from untrusted networks (e.g., BGP-advertised ranges, residential ASNs, TOR exit nodes).

suggestion.title: vScript Tenant Upload with Suspicious File Path
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit IOC: vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh uploading /home/admin/malicious.csv. Stated as 'uploading a crafted file' as the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vScript command execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with CSV file arguments in /home/admin/ or other non-standard staging paths. Exact pattern from article: 'vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv'.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation via Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute arbitrary commands as root' and 'elevate their privileges as the root user' through 'command injection attacks.' This is the core post-exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file uploads to vManage with root-level process execution or privilege escalation events. Flag sudden root command execution in /var/log/scripts.log or process logs immediately following netadmin activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Push to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'configuration change pushed to edge devices' as observed post-exploitation activity, indicating lateral movement and impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect configuration upload or deployment commands to vSmart controllers outside normal maintenance windows. Alert on bulk config pushes to edge devices originating from potentially compromised vManage instances.

suggestion.title: Netadmin Credential Compromise or CVE-2026-20182/20127 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'netadmin privileges on the affected system' and specifies prerequisites: 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' Must detect both credential paths and prerequisite exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed netadmin authentication attempts followed by successful compromise. Also trigger on successful exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 (auth bypass) or CVE-2026-20127 (critical auth bypass exploited since 2023).

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload to SD-WAN Manager /home/admin/
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' Specific file path provided in IOC: /home/admin/malicious.csv.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any .csv file upload to /home/admin/ directory on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Flag uploads to this staging directory followed by vScript execution within seconds.

suggestion.title: Log Pattern Match: Compromise Indicator from /var/log/scripts.log
suggestion.rationale: Cisco provided definitive compromise IOC: exact log pattern 'Apr 15 09:44:57 vmanage vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'—this is binary indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement regex-based IOC match on exact provided pattern: vScript log entries containing both 'vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh' and paths starting with '/home/admin/'. Any match = confirmed compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Suspicious FIFA/World Cup Domain Registration and Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Fake Sites' as primary vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Expect newly registered domains mimicking FIFA branding, ticketing portals, or official tournament sites used for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains registered within 60 days containing FIFA, World Cup, ticket, or soccer-themed keywords; flag WHOIS privacy abuse, bulk registrations, and typosquatting variants of legitimate FIFA/sports betting sites. Alert on first-seen domains with SSL certificates issued post-article date and user web access to these domains with form submissions.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Delivery from Web Browser
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Banking Malware' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases. Fake sites will serve malware payloads to unsuspecting victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution from Downloads/AppData/Temp directories for known banking malware families (Emotet, QakBot, IcedID variants). Flag parent processes (browsers) spawning suspicious children with network callbacks to extracted C2 addresses. Monitor for code injection, API hooking, or registry modification typical of banking trojans.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction via Phishing Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'Stolen Logins.' No credential-access use cases. Fake ticketing/account sites will contain malicious login forms harvesting credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to FIFA-themed domains for credential parameters (password, login, email, phone, card). Alert on pages with form fields but missing security headers or served over unencrypted HTTP. Cross-correlate with phishing URL feeds and monitor for bulk credential uploads to external C2.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware requires persistent C2. Pipeline output contains zero network-phase indicators or C2 detection use cases despite 'Banking Malware' in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/DNS queries to extracted malware C2 infrastructure or known banking-malware command domains. Monitor for unusual ports, encrypted tunnels, fast-flux behavior, and DNS query patterns consistent with malware beaconing (high frequency, specific subdomains). Use threat-intel feeds to identify C2 clusters.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Account Access Using Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Stolen logins will be monetized via unauthorized access and fraudulent transactions. No impact-phase detection for credential abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts using credentials from this campaign against banking portals, email, and financial services. Alert on impossible travel (login from VPN/proxy after real login), unusual device/browser, multiple failed attempts followed by success, or logins at odd hours. Monitor for downstream fraudulent transactions and account modifications.

suggestion.title: Mass Phishing Campaign Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Scams at this scale require bulk distribution. No initial-access use cases for email/SMS campaigns, mass sender infrastructure, or campaign staging indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk phishing emails/SMS with FIFA, ticket, or World Cup lures and suspicious URLs/shorteners. Alert on email spoofing patterns mimicking FIFA/official sponsors, bulk sender activity from compromised infrastructure, and rate anomalies in outbound mail. Flag shortened URLs and QR codes pointing to extracted malicious domains.

suggestion.title: DbGate POST /runners/start RCE — Code Injection in functionName
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'functionName parameter of JSON script assign commands' being 'interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code' via the /runners/start endpoint. This is the attack entry point and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader on port 3000 (default DbGate) with JSON body containing 'functionName' keys holding code patterns (eval, require(), function definitions, script tags). Correlate with subsequent Node process spawning.

suggestion.title: DbGate Exploit — Node.js Spawning Egress Tools (wget/curl/shell)
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE 'executed in a forked Node.js child process'. This guarantees detectable parent-child spawning: Node spawning curl, wget, sh, bash, nc, or ncat signals exploitation. Article specifically mentions LOLBin/shell egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js (node, node.exe) with parent_process_path containing 'dbgate', 'bundle.js', or '/.dbgate/run/' spawning children: {wget, curl, sh, bash, dash, zsh, powershell, cmd.exe, nc, ncat, python, perl, ruby}. Medium confidence: tuple (parent_name, child_name). High confidence: add commandline contains pipe, redirection, or $(…) substitution.

suggestion.title: DbGate Web Request to RCE Endpoint — Low Auth Posture
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution', indicating no auth token/session required for /runners/start. Detect requests from external IPs directly invoking /runners/start or /runners/load-reader without prior login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader from external IPs to DbGate port 3000. Baseline: internal admin requests. Anomaly: external IP, no session token in HTTP headers, or missing Authorization header entirely. High confidence if JSON body contains 'functionName' + code.

suggestion.title: DbGate File Write to System Directories from Node Process
suggestion.rationale: Article's article-specific hunt UC_28_1 includes filesystem detection: files created/modified in /usr/local/sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, or /root/.dbgate/run/. Node RCE can persist or stage payloads by writing binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileCreated/FileModified from parent process containing 'node' or 'bundle.js' (parent_process_name=node*) into sensitive paths: /usr/local/sbin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/bin, /root/.dbgate/run/*, /home/dbgate*/. High confidence if file extension matches executable (no extension, .sh, .py, .ps1).

suggestion.title: DbGate: Unauthenticated JWT issuance via none-provider /auth/login endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'none auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via POST /auth/login, so this is exploitable by any network user.' This is the attack entry point but no detection exists for auth bypass or missing credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to /api/auth/login returning HTTP 200 with JWT token in response from unauthenticated source (no Authorization header; empty or missing credentials in request body). Correlate successful auth with subsequent API calls to /api/archive/unzip from same source within 5 minutes. Baseline expected user-driven auth patterns vs bulk/automated source behavior.

suggestion.title: DbGate: Zip Slip path traversal via unzipDirectory API with directory-escape sequences in archive
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unzipDirectory() function does not validate that extracted file paths stay within the output directory. A malicious ZIP with ../ entries writes files anywhere on filesystem.' Need pre-filesystem-impact detection at API/WAF layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/archive/unzip, /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip for uploads containing path traversal indicators in ZIP manifest: entries with ../ or ..\ sequences, absolute paths starting with /, or entries targeting system directories. Detect on Content-Length anomalies relative to baseline legitimate archive sizes.

suggestion.title: DbGate RCE via cron/systemd/init persistence—command execution post file-write by root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'writes files anywhere on filesystem...running as root.' Hunts mention cron.d, init.d, systemd but lack follow-on execution detection to confirm RCE was achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After node process creates files in /etc/cron.d, /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/profile.d, correlate with execution of shell (bash/sh/ash) commands originating from those paths within 60 seconds. Flag parent process chain: node → cron/at/systemd → bash executing non-standard binaries or network-based commands.

suggestion.title: DbGate privilege escalation via /etc/sudoers.d or SSH key injection to /root/.ssh
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability enables writes to /etc/sudoers.d (NOPASSWD privilege escalation) and /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (SSH persistence). These are privilege escalation + lateral movement, distinct from cron persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node process modifying files in /etc/sudoers.d (especially entries containing NOPASSWD) or writing SSH public keys to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys. These file writes themselves enable privilege escalation or remote access; no subsequent execution context required.

suggestion.title: DbGate: LD_PRELOAD shared-library injection via /etc/ld.so.preload for web-shell persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1505.003 (Web Shell component) but current hunts miss low-visibility library injection. Writing to /etc/ld.so.preload or /lib paths enables arbitrary code execution in all child processes of compromised services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node process modifying /etc/ld.so.preload, /etc/ld.so.conf, /etc/ld.so.conf.d/, or writing .so/.dll files to /lib, /usr/lib, /usr/local/lib. Correlate with subsequent process creation events for node, httpd, or sshd after library modification; these processes will load the attacker's shared object at startup.

suggestion.title: DbGate: Defensive indicator—abnormal node process listening on network or spawning reverse shells
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, node process running unzipDirectory may spawn network listeners, reverse shell handlers, or secondary payloads. No hunt covers post-compromise behavior if initial file-write detections fail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node process with abnormal network behavior: listening on non-standard ports, establishing outbound connections to non-whitelisted IPs, or spawning child processes (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc) without corresponding parent API handler or package manager context. Flag rapid child process spawning (fork bombs) or reuse of process name for obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized role creation from low-privilege authenticated accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any authenticated user could load the page and use its public actions to create new roles' via missing mount() authorization on Settings/Team/Index.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor role creation operations in Shopper initiated by accounts lacking admin privilege level. Correlate failed/bypassed authorization checks on Settings/Team endpoints with successful role mutations to detect privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Admin user deletion by non-admin authenticated users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'delete other users, including administrators' is direct impact of RBAC bypass — user deletion is takeover confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion of admin-flagged user accounts initiated from authenticated sessions with non-admin RBAC roles. Escalate if deletion precedes or follows unauthorized role creation.

suggestion.title: HTTP 403→200 authorization bypass attempt pattern on team settings endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Mount() bypass vulnerability manifests as authorization probe (403 denied) followed by successful exploit (200 success) on same resource within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single user receiving HTTP 403 then HTTP 200 on identical or semantically identical Shopper /settings/team* endpoint within 60 seconds—indicates probe-then-exploit behavior.

suggestion.title: Livewire component state mutation from non-admin context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Settings/Team/RolePermission gated its write actions on the read-only view_users perm'—authorization check delegated to insufficient permission flag instead of role-based enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PATCH to /livewire/update and /livewire/message/settings.team* endpoints for state mutations (property changes, method calls on RolePermission or Team components) from sessions lacking admin role in authentication token.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw.' Pipeline failed to detect this active exploitation vector despite clear vulnerability naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs for requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ with suspicious query parameters, encoded payloads, or evidence of RCE attempts (eval, system, exec, shell_exec patterns in POST data).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Web Shell Upload and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'take over sites'—requires persistent backdoor. Detect web shell artifacts planted via plugin vulnerability for post-exploitation access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file creation in web-writable directories (wp-content/, uploads/) outside change windows. Correlate with suspicious process spawning (php.exe, apache2) executing from those locations or unusual HTTP requests triggering process creation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Administrator Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Full site takeover ('take over sites') requires persistent administrative access, typically via backdoor user account creation in WordPress database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag INSERT operations into wp_users table with role='administrator' from non-standard sources or outside change-control procedures. Alert on bulk admin account creation or accounts with suspicious naming (admin2, backup-admin, service-admin).

suggestion.title: Database Credential and Content Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover implies database access for credential theft, data exfiltration, and malware injection. Detect abnormal database query patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk SELECT queries from wp_users, wp_posts, wp_postmeta, wp_options tables from web application service accounts. Flag UNION-based queries, unusual subqueries, or data exports outside scheduled backup windows.

suggestion.title: Plugin Code Injection and File Integrity Violations
suggestion.rationale: Critical plugin flaw likely involves code injection or file modification. Detect tampering with Everest Forms Pro plugin files for payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline FIM for plugin directory (checksums, timestamps). Alert on unauthorized modifications to .php files, especially injection of obfuscated code, eval(), base64_decode(), or command-execution functions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Installation by Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides SHA1 `a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089` and states 'putting thousands of developers at risk,' implying code execution during installation. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this concrete IOC and threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install or python setup.py execution with process hash or downloaded package hash matching malicious IoCs. Monitor for setup.py executing child processes (cmd, powershell, curl, wget) during installation, indicating post-install payload execution.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'parsimonius' crafted to 'look almost identical to...parsimonious' with 'The single missing letter' as the attack vehicle. Clear typosquatting pattern missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install commands for package names with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known legitimate packages (parsimonious, requests, numpy, pandas, etc.). Cross-reference pip logs (requested vs. installed names) to surface substitution mismatches.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Hash Verification Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires continuous verification. Article's 'deceptive...crafted to look almost identical' implies metadata spoofing or replacement. Pipeline failed to suggest post-install validation hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare hashes of installed Python packages against official PyPI manifest (via PyPI JSON API). Flag installations where on-disk SHA1/SHA256 does not match PyPI's published hash for that version.

suggestion.title: Python Package Installation from Non-Official Source
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions package 'made its way into the PyPI repository'—implies distribution via official channel. Detection should surface any pip installs from mirrors or local indices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip command-line invocations for --index-url, --find-links, or -i flags pointing to non-official registries or local files. Correlate with any subsequent parent-process spawning or network calls.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly references 'IronWorm and New Miasma Worm Variant Hit npm'—attack vector is poisoned npm packages. No detection use case was generated for npm install events triggering unexpected code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm install or npm ci commands that spawn child processes outside expected build contexts, or package.json scripts executing network calls, child spawning, or file exfiltration immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Suspicious post-install Script Execution in Node Packages
suggestion.rationale: npm packages can define postinstall hooks that execute arbitrary code; article describes malware variants delivered via npm, implying code-execution via package lifecycle scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm postinstall, postuninstall, prepare scripts spawning unsigned executables, reaching out to external domains, or writing to sensitive directories (credentials, SSH keys, user shell configs).

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering & Unexpected Version Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often involve package-lockfile poisoning or version downgrades to force installation of vulnerable packages. Article title indicates worm variants—no UC for detecting downgrade patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json or yarn.lock for unexpected dependency downgrades, new entries from non-official registries (private registries not in org allowlist), or timestamps mismatched from npm registry metadata.

suggestion.title: Cryptographic Signature Validation Failure on npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks may involve unsigned or re-signed packages. No UC exists for detecting package signature mismatches or missing provenance metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install with --ignore-scripts=false (default) on packages missing npm provenance attestation, or packages signed by unexpected signers (not the known publisher).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via npm Registry Sideload or Attacker-Controlled Registry
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivered via npm may exfiltrate data back through registry interactions. Article describes worm behavior; no UC for detecting C2 communication through npm APIs or private registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm client (npm, yarn, pnpm) making unexpected HTTPS requests to non-standard registries or internal IPs, or spawning curl/wget/PowerShell with registry tokens in URLs; flag unusual npm auth token usage post-package-install.

suggestion.title: Malware C2 via Payment API Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'uses Stripe...as both its command center and its data dump' — this is explicit C2 beaconing behavior to a payment processor. Pipeline found T1071 but generated no hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections to Firebase domains (braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com) that correlate with payment processing infrastructure. Flag beacons originating from web-serving hosts (webservers, POS systems) during off-hours or with unusual request patterns (binary payloads, command-like parameters in JSON).

suggestion.title: Card Data Exfiltration Over Payment Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware using Stripe as 'data dump' for 'stolen card data' — exfiltration phase entirely missing from kill chain reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect payment API requests with anomalous payloads (oversized POST bodies, hex-encoded or base64-wrapped data in fields normally containing card tokens). Correlate with successful card captures on affected domains to identify data staging before exfil.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Malware Injection in Payment Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article implies Magecart-style 'credit card skimming malware hiding inside' payment platform — execution/injection phase not captured. This is the delivery vector, not just C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected JavaScript execution in payment form contexts (stripeElementsContainer, payment-form divs). Look for DOM mutations injecting exfiltration hooks, inline event listeners on input fields, or dynamic script loads from non-CDN hosts during checkout.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Reuse — Firebase Domain Abuse for C2
suggestion.rationale: Domain braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com impersonates Braintree (competitor to Stripe) on Firebase — infrastructure abuse/spoofing. Article mentions 'most trusted payment platforms' suggesting social engineering component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firebase and similar legitimate CDN domains for subdomains spoofing well-known payment processors (braintree-, stripe-, paypal-prefixes). Correlate registrations with recent phishing or MitM infrastructure. Flag any Firebase endpoints receiving POST requests with PAN-like payloads.

suggestion.title: Stripe API Anomalies — Unauthorized Webhook or OAuth Registration
suggestion.rationale: Using Stripe 'as command center' implies the attacker either pivoted legitimate Stripe accounts or registered unauthorized webhooks/integrations. Article doesn't specify mechanism — detection gap for account abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious Stripe API usage: new webhook registrations from IP ranges not associated with merchant's infrastructure, OAuth app creation by secondary users, test keys promoted to live, or requests to `/v1/charges` with unusual recipient (not merchant's bank).

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Upload / Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Custom Web Shell Framework' deployed to IIS servers. Pipeline generated no detection for .aspx/.asp/.ashx file creation in IIS directories (wwwroot, inetsrv). This is the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS root directories for suspicious script file creation (.aspx, .asp, .ashx, .ascx) by processes other than authorized deployment tools. Correlate with HTTP requests to newly created paths. Baseline known web application files to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Web shell persistence implies remote code execution through w3wp.exe (IIS worker process). Article describes 'custom' shell framework suggesting non-standard execution chains. No use case maps this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other interpreters; unusual network connections from w3wp.exe; or execution of binaries from web-accessible paths. Establish baseline of legitimate IIS app spawned processes.

suggestion.title: IIS HTTP Request to Web Shell Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names custom framework—implies distinctive URI patterns or payloads. Pipeline missed detection on HTTP traffic to newly deployed shell paths or anomalous HTTP method sequences (PUT/POST to .asp files).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS logs for PUT/POST requests to script file extensions; requests with suspicious parameters (e.g., 'cmd', 'exec', 'shell'); or encoded payloads in query strings. Correlate with DeviceProcessEvents to confirm shell execution.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of IIS Known Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article states OP-512 'targets' IIS—implies CVE or known weak configuration path to initial access (e.g., CVE-2024-XXXXX, misconfigured web.config, ISAPI filter abuse). Pipeline reconstructed zero initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests matching known IIS exploitation patterns (path traversal to web.config, malformed Host headers, requests to admin paths like /remote.axd). Correlate with subsequent file creation or process execution events.

suggestion.title: Custom Web Shell Framework Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'custom' framework—implies signatures, string patterns, or behavioral markers distinct from stock web shells (e.g., specific function names, error pages, encoding schemes). No IOCs or yara/sigma rules provided by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures (regex, yara) for OP-512's custom shell framework based on indicators (obfuscation patterns, unique function names, registry keys, binary footprints). Search endpoint telemetry and web logs for matches. Update as new samples surface.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SMTP Relay Activity from Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states servers were 'hijacked for covert SMTP relay network'—mass outbound SMTP on non-standard ports or from infrastructure not registered as mail servers is the core detection need.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound SMTP (ports 25, 465, 587) initiated from cloud compute instances (EC2, GCP Compute, Azure VMs) that lack mail-relay legitimacy. Correlate with traffic volume and destination diversity. Flag instances with <1 week runtime age sending >1000 SMTP connections per hour.

suggestion.title: Mass Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement Across Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 230 servers across three cloud providers requires either: (1) compromise of shared credentials, (2) exploitation of a common vulnerability, or (3) lateral movement post-initial-access—article implies coordinated access to multiple accounts/subscriptions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid creation of multiple IAM roles, service accounts, or user accounts across disparate cloud accounts within 24–48 hour window. Correlate with failed auth spikes followed by successful logins from anomalous geolocations or IPs. Watch for privilege escalation (role attachment, group membership changes) on newly created principals.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Malware / Agent Deployment Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers don't become SMTP relays without agent installation—article implies automated malware deployment, likely via user data scripts, cron jobs, or container images. Pipeline failed to surface execution-phase tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of curl/wget to remote URLs on freshly launched cloud instances, especially within user-data / cloud-init context. Flag inline shell scripts with obfuscation (base64, hex encoding) in cloud metadata. Monitor for process execution from /tmp or /var/tmp on instances not typically running dynamic workloads.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Compromise or Default Secret Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Attackers likely obtained API keys, SSH keys, or default credentials to access 230 instances across public clouds. Article does not detail entry mechanism, but credential compromise is the most probable initial-access vector for infrastructure this scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk API calls to DescribeInstances, ListInstances, or equivalent discovery APIs from principals not previously seen or from IPs outside normal ranges. Flag failed login attempts followed by successful API authentication. Monitor for secrets.json, credentials.csv, or .pem files accessed or exfiltrated via CloudTrail object-level logging.

suggestion.title: Network Configuration Changes Enabling SMTP Relay
suggestion.rationale: SMTP relay operation requires security group / firewall rule changes permitting outbound traffic on mail ports. Article does not specify rules, but this is a required precursor to the attack's impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of security groups / firewall rules that permit outbound ports 25, 465, 587, or 2525 from compute instances. Correlate rule changes with new instance provisioning. Flag rules that permit 'any destination' or high-entropy IP ranges. Alert on rule changes via service accounts or non-human principals.

suggestion.title: SMTP Relay Infrastructure Sinkhole / Takedown Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Once SMTP relay botnet is identified, defenders must track domains/IPs used as mail relay hops, C2 callback infrastructure, and stolen-credential warehouses. Pipeline offered no IOC extraction—critical for blocking and threat intelligence sharing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a feed of known relay IPs/domains. Cross-reference against internal DNS, email gateway logs, and proxy egress traffic. Flag any instance communicating to a relay node as compromised. Collect SSL certificates, MX records, and SMTP banner grabs for IOC enrichment and infrastructure mapping.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Execution with Elevated Token Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article directly addresses 'Claude Code Github action case' — agentic AI in GitHub Actions creates risk of unauthorized GITHUB_TOKEN scope escalation or workflows accessing secrets beyond their declared needs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows executing with token scope permissions exceeding the workflow's functional requirements. Detect runs that access organization secrets, deploy keys, or third-party credentials when workflow definition only declares read-only permissions.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials or Source Code via Agentic GitHub Actions Output
suggestion.rationale: Frontier AI models (Claude Code) can hallucinate or be prompt-injected to generate workflows that exfiltrate repo secrets, personal access tokens, or source code. Article keyword 'Vulnerability' directly implicates credential leakage risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows that redirect GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH keys, or environment variables to external HTTP/DNS endpoints. Alert on actions that curl, nc, or POST data to IPs/domains outside organizational whitelist, especially from AI-generated or recently-modified workflow YAML.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Injection via Malicious or Hallucinated GitHub Action References
suggestion.rationale: Title keyword 'agentic world' + 'Frontier AI models' establishes risk of Claude Code or similar agents generating backdoored .github/workflows YAML with malicious action references. Attack surface created by AI-recommended code without verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or modified .github/workflows/*.yml files that reference external GitHub Actions from newly-registered or unvetted repositories. Cross-correlate commit authors with agentic tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) and flag workflows with no associated issue/PR context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Org-Level Workflow Secrets or Reusable Action Access
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD article context — once attacker compromises a repository's GitHub Actions, they exploit shared org secrets or reusable workflows to pivot laterally across multiple projects in the organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows accessing organization-level secrets from repositories that normally use only repository secrets. Alert on unexpected calls to reusable workflows in other repos or access to org teams/member lists from action contexts.

suggestion.title: Log Injection or Token Leakage in Action Logs via Unsanitized AI Output
suggestion.rationale: Agentic AI generating GitHub Actions code may inadvertently log secrets, tokens, or credentials to action output/logs. Frontier AI hallucination risk for debug printing GITHUB_TOKEN or SSH keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for leaked GITHUB_TOKEN, ssh-key patterns, base64-encoded credentials, or AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY strings. Alert on actions that echo or print environment variables or secrets to stdout. Cross-correlate with workflows generated or modified by agentic tools.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 responses from third-party JavaScript CDN resources
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'polyfill[.]io...started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests' and 'User browsers...interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt.' This is the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a third-party CDN or external JavaScript resource (polyfill.io, unpkg, cdn.jsdelivr, cloudflare) responds with HTTP 401 status. Correlate with subsequent authentication form submissions or browser auth-prompt events. Legitimate 401 responses originate from first-party auth endpoints, not external dependencies.

suggestion.title: Requests to compromised polyfill[.]io domain
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies polyfill[.]io as compromised in 2024 and reactivated May 2026 serving malicious HTTP 401 responses. Affected websites retain stale references in their code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries, HTTP requests, or XHR calls to polyfill.io after May 2026 reactivation. This domain is a known-malicious CDN source serving credential-harvesting login prompts. Tune for victim domains (Toshiba, Muji, Samsung Smart TVs, Zojirushi, FiNC, Ishiyaku, Hobonichi) loading resources from polyfill.io.

suggestion.title: Stale third-party library references post-domain-discontinuation
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites 'failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained' after polyfill[.]io was discontinued and migrated to polyfill.com, then polyfill.top.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan web properties and version-control repos for references to deprecated third-party library URLs (polyfill.io post-discontinuation). Alert on pages still loading from old CDN URLs when known migration has occurred. Catches incomplete cleanup that leaves sites vulnerable to domain takeover exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected login prompts on non-authentication pages
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'suspicious sign-in screens popping up on their websites could collect credentials.' Users encounter login prompts on product/help pages, not authentication entry points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser auth-prompt events on non-login pages (product, help, homepage). Correlate with XHR or script-load events from unexpected domains. If login prompt appears after loading third-party JS from CDN, especially polyfill.io, flag as credential-harvesting attempt.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for incoming exploitation attempts against Serv-U, the primary attack vector for this flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous HTTP requests to Serv-U management ports (typically 22, 8080, or 3737). Alert on request patterns matching known SolarWinds Serv-U exploit payloads (e.g., unusual parameter injection, oversized POST bodies, or specific malformed requests documented in public POCs). Correlate with Serv-U process behavior for signs of code execution.

suggestion.title: Denial of Service Attack on Serv-U Service
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies this explicitly as a 'DoS Flaw' with active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero coverage for post-compromise DoS impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process for abnormal CPU/memory spikes coinciding with high inbound connection rates or request volume surges on exposed ports. Alert if service becomes unresponsive or crashes after authenticated/unauthenticated sessions. Correlate with network-level packet loss or dropped connections.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: If DoS flaw is a code-execution vulnerability (typical for SolarWinds), pipeline should detect subprocess spawning, file writes, or registry modifications from Serv-U service context post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from Serv-U parent process (srvanyservice.exe, USSTGSERVICE.exe, or variant). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious interpreter execution. Correlate with file I/O to suspicious paths (temp, Startup folders) or registry persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Port Scanning / Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies external reconnaissance is likely precursor step. Pipeline missed detection logic for threat actors scanning for vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scans targeting standard Serv-U listening ports (22, 3737, 8080, 49152–65535). Detect repeated failed connection attempts to Serv-U interfaces from external IPs. Correlate sequential port probes within 5-minute window from single source IP.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Authentication Bypass or Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: No authentication detection UC. Vulnerability may enable bypassing authentication or weak validation, common pre-cursor to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP 401/403 responses from Serv-U interfaces for patterns of brute-force login attempts. Alert on successful authentications following high-frequency failures. Flag auth success via non-standard credentials or from unexpected source IPs if baseline available.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes active exploitation: 'Actively Exploited — No Patch Available'. This is a critical RCE vulnerability in a centralized network management appliance. Detection must cover exploitation payloads and anomalous POST/GET patterns to SD-WAN API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco SD-WAN Manager management ports (default 8443) for malformed or exploit-patterned requests. Flag POST requests with encoded payloads, unusual User-Agent strings, or requests to unpatched endpoint paths. Look for HTTP 500 responses that may indicate failed exploitation or error-based enumeration.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Reconnaissance & Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Unpatched critical vulnerability invites scanning. Article phrase: 'No Patch Available' implies all customers remain vulnerable, driving attacker reconnaissance. Need to detect active scanning for vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests across multiple Cisco SD-WAN IP ranges or known net blocks for this product. Look for requests to management console paths (/api/, /admin/, /login) from non-whitelisted ASNs. Flag GET requests that return HTTP 200/302 with Cisco-specific response headers (Server: Cisco).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'No Patch Available'. This is unusual and means all deployed instances remain at risk indefinitely until a patch ships. Inventory must flag any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances running vulnerable version(s).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB and vulnerability management systems for any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager appliances. Cross-reference version numbers with CVE-2026-20245 affected version range. Generate alerts for unpatched instances; escalate to network/infrastructure teams for remediation prioritization (isolation, access control, out-of-band management, etc.).

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Authentication Bypass or Credential Stuffing Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: If initial exploitation succeeds, attacker will likely attempt to create persistent management access or pivot to other nodes. Article's 'actively exploited' language suggests full compromise chains, not just proofs-of-concept.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager audit logs for successful logins from unexpected IP ranges, new admin account creations, or changes to authentication policy. Watch for CLI/API calls that disable logging or modify TACACS+/LDAP integration. Baseline normal management access patterns and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Complex Calculation PHP Injection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement' — core attack vector is explicitly described with technical detail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms Complex Calculation feature endpoints for single-quote injection patterns in form field values. Flag payloads containing PHP functions (wp_insert_user, system, exec) escaped with comment markers (//) to close string literals.

suggestion.title: PHP eval() Code Execution from Form Input
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability: 'executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function' — this is the literal execution mechanism enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval() function invocations triggered from web request context where input was sourced from HTTP POST form parameters. Alert on eval() calls where argument contains unsanitized user input, particularly from Everest Forms endpoints.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via wp_insert_user() Function
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account' — describes observed exploitation technique in wild, confirmed by Wordfence telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_insert_user() function execution originating from form processing context (non-admin authenticated context). Cross-reference with HTTP request logs to correlate admin user creation events with POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints.

suggestion.title: Rogue Administrator Account Creation with Indicator Username
suggestion.rationale: Article reports active exploitation creating accounts with username 'diksimarina' — specific IOC observed across 29,300+ blocked exploitation attempts documented by Wordfence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation audit logs for any new admin-level accounts with username 'diksimarina' or similar suspicious naming patterns. Alert immediately and trigger account lockdown and investigation workflow.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Traffic from Identified Attacker IP Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' — specific attacker infrastructure identified through active exploitation campaign telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block outbound traffic to and inbound requests from 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26. Alert on any HTTP requests to WordPress Everest Forms endpoints originating from these IPs. Monitor for repeated attempts and distributed attack pattern variations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Admin Account Creation Rate from Web Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability is being exploited in the wild to create rogue administrator accounts' — the account creation itself, especially when triggered by web form processing rather than admin UI, is anomalous and detectable via rate/context deviation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for admin account creation rates and context on each WordPress installation. Alert when account creation events exceed baseline or occur outside expected administrative windows. Prioritize alerts where user creation is triggered by form/web processing rather than wp-admin interface.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Smart TV App
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies.' Implies persistent C2 communication and data exfiltration. No detection for unusual egress from TV devices to non-streaming infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV initiating outbound connections to non-CDN, non-regional-content IPs; high-frequency, low-latency comms to same destination; connections to IPs with abuse history or associated with bulletproof hosting.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion by TV App (CPU/Memory Spike)
suggestion.rationale: Web scraping is computationally intensive. Article: 'web-scraping proxies' requires sustained processing. Title indicates apps are actively scraping, not just installed. No process-level detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: TV app consuming >40% sustained CPU or memory for hours without user interaction. Especially during night hours or when TV appears idle per viewing logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Installation via Store Marketplace
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is free apps via distribution. Article title: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into...' implies app-store compromise or fake/trojanized app. No supply-chain detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Newly-created developer account publishing app to TV app store with generic/deceptive name, zero reviews, requested excessive permissions (network, storage), or exhibiting rapid installation spike across disparate regions.

suggestion.title: DNS Beaconing from Smart TV Segment
suggestion.rationale: Web scraper and C2 proxy require DNS resolution and persistent callback. Article describes 'quieting' behavior suggesting periodic automated activity. No C2 detection or DNS pattern analysis suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV querying non-entertainment domains at consistent intervals (e.g., every 5-10 min). Watch for DGA-like patterns, infrastructure-provider DNS lookups, or known C2 sinkhole IPs. Suspicious if queries occur during off-hours.

suggestion.title: High-Volume HTTP Requests without User Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'web-scraping proxies' implies systematic data collection via HTTP. Need to detect scraper HTTP patterns (rapid requests, bot User-Agents, non-human click patterns). No HTTP behavioral detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: TV app generating hundreds of HTTP GETs/POSTs per minute to multiple news/content domains with zero think-time between requests; User-Agent contains 'bot', 'scraper', or generic patterns. High request volume on bandwidth-constrained TV.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Bulletproof Hosting / VPN IP Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Smart TV acting as proxy implies data sent to attacker infrastructure. Article: 'Proxies for AI' (likely model training data). No detection for IoT→suspicious-infrastructure exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV connecting to IPs in known bulletproof-hosting ranges, VPN provider IP blocks, or hosting providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) with high malware reputation. Flag if connection volume scales with time or device count.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Proxy SDK Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states devices are 'quietly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network.' Detecting enrollment traffic to proxy domains (brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, bright-sdk.com) is direct C2 indicator with high confidence in smart TV network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS and network connections from smart TV device ranges (Samsung, LG, Roku ranges) to known residential proxy infrastructure.
