suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps request broad network access disguised as legitimate utility. Pipeline missed permission-anomaly detection during initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag smart TV apps requesting network access (TCP/UDP, DNS, proxy settings) when app category is listed as 'game' or 'utility'. Alert on apps modifying system proxy settings or installing root certificates post-installation. Correlate permission requests with missing documentation in app store listing.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Web Content via Smart TV User-Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: apps scrape web content 'for AI'. Pipeline missed detection of systematic reconnaissance/web-harvesting behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP requests from smart TV devices with systematic URL patterns (e.g., /page/1, /page/2, ...) or User-Agent strings spoofing web crawlers. Alert on extraction of specific content types (e.g., repeated text extraction from news/social media domains). Correlate with known AI training data harvesters' behavioral signatures.

suggestion.title: Persistent Callback Patterns from Compromised Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes apps as 'proxies' implying persistent C2 relationship. Pipeline missed command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect smart TVs establishing persistent TCP/443 connections to non-streaming infrastructure domains. Alert on beaconing patterns (e.g., heartbeat intervals every 5–30 min). Flag domains with low reputation scores, recently registered (< 30 days), or sharing IP space with known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Trojanized Apps in TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free Apps' as distribution vector. Pipeline missed supply-chain threat assessment and app-integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate app versions/hashes across TVs. Alert when app binary differs from store-listed hash or contains unexpected network code. Monitor for app publishers suddenly publishing multiple utilities with overlapping network permissions. Implement app-store crawling to identify publishers with rapid release cadence and minimal user reviews.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Free App Installation from Official Smart TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku, and other major smart TV platforms have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices'—apps masquerade as legitimate utilities but distribute proxy malware through official channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious app installations on Smart TV platforms; identify apps with rapid adoption post-release, deceptive descriptions (free utility + vague permissions), or permission requests exceeding legitimate use case (network + device ID + location for 'media player').

suggestion.title: Smart TV Device Registration with Commercial Proxy Network C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'secretly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network'—devices establish C2 connections to Bright Data/Luminati infrastructure domains for proxy command and control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from consumer IoT devices (Smart TVs, set-top boxes) to known proxy infrastructure domains (luminati.io, bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, proxyjs.* subdomains). Cross-reference with legitimate Smart TV traffic baselines; whitelist official firmware/app update servers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistent Proxy Execution on Smart TV After App Installation
suggestion.rationale: Apps silently execute proxy functionality on device boot—'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation' enables imperceptible persistence. Proxy process runs continuously to serve C2 requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Smart TV app startup behavior post-installation; identify apps that establish outbound network connections immediately on boot or device wake, particularly to proxy infrastructure. Baseline legitimate app behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Unauthorized Smart TV Proxy Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Devices are 'used to scrape web data for AI training' and proxy external requests—device bandwidth is hijacked to exfiltrate data for third parties. User's residential network is abused without knowledge or consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained, high-volume outbound traffic from Smart TV devices to commercial proxy domains without corresponding user-initiated requests. Spike detection on bytes transferred from residential IPs to proxy infrastructure. Correlate with app activity logs.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Deceptive UI Consent Burial in TV Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Attack deliberately obscures enrollment consent in complex TV remote navigation: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—users click through without understanding implications, evading informed security decisions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app permission grant logs for suspicious permission request sequencing—network + device ID + location requested in buried menus. Identify apps requesting sensitive permissions without clear user-facing justification in UI or changelog.

suggestion.title: Compromised App Store Supply Chain—Malicious Free App Proliferation
suggestion.rationale: Attack compromises legitimate app distribution channels (Samsung, LG, Roku stores)—threat actor or insiders inject proxy code into 'free' app builds, affecting supply chain integrity at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app store distribution for code-signing anomalies, unexpected version updates, or apps with sudden metadata changes (description, permissions) post-submission. Correlate app update timestamps with proxy infrastructure registration. Flag apps by new/unvetted publishers.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Compromise — Unusual Commit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack via 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories indicates attackers achieved write access to commit or merge malicious code; pipeline must detect anomalous git history patterns. Article title explicitly names 'GitHub Repositories' as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for unusual push/merge events to Microsoft-owned repositories outside normal CI/CD windows, commits from newly-added collaborators with no prior history, or mass repository modifications within short timeframe. Alert on commit authors not in whitelist or commits bypassing required code review.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm — Artifact Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Miasma Worm' as payload; must detect execution of worm binaries or suspicious scripts injected into supply chain packages. This is the post-compromise execution phase where worm propagates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of files named or signed with 'Miasma' variant, processes spawning from package installations or repository-cloned code directories, suspicious PowerShell/bash execution from git working directories, or child processes from package managers (npm, pip, nuget) executing unsigned code.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Poisoning — Mass Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attack affecting 73 repositories suggests either mass repo compromise or coordinated injection into published packages; pipeline must detect anomalous bulk modifications to package manifests or source trees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on simultaneous or near-simultaneous commits to multiple Microsoft-controlled repositories from same actor/service account, modifications to package.json/requirements.txt/csproj across multiple repos in same org, or unusual package version bumps/re-publishing from compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credentials Compromise — Unauthorized Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 73 simultaneous repos accessed suggests compromised GitHub personal access tokens, deploy keys, or service account credentials used for write access. Article phrase 'worm hits 73 repositories' implies persistent access capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub PAT/SSH key usage from unusual geolocations, times of day, or IP ranges compared to baseline; multiple failed authentication attempts followed by success; service accounts accessing repositories outside their normal scope; API token usage from non-whitelisted applications.

suggestion.title: Worm Lateral Movement — Cross-Repository Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagation across 73 distinct repositories indicates self-replicating capability or automated fork/clone/push cycles. Must detect programmatic repository enumeration and mass cloning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for burst of git clone/pull operations from single source (IP, service account), rapid sequential repository forks from same account, mass push operations to multiple repos within minutes, or enumeration of repository contents via GitHub API in short burst windows.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Downstream Impact — Dependency Resolution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Microsoft repositories in supply chain likely published as packages (NuGet, npm, etc.) to downstream consumers; must detect when systems resolve/install compromised versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager (npm/pip/nuget) pulling unexpected package versions from affected Microsoft repositories, installation of packages with unusual file hashes compared to known good versions, or code execution patterns consistent with worm payload following package installation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Mass Disabling via Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack.' This is a mass impact indicator that requires detection—repositories being disabled en masse by a single malicious action is a hallmark of supply chain worms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden disabling or deletion of multiple repositories within a short timeframe from a single source or action. Correlate GitHub API disable/delete events with compromised GitHub Actions workflows or service tokens.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled'—indicates a GitHub Actions component was compromised as the attack vector. Attack targets 'AI Coding Agents,' suggesting repository workflow injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modifications to GitHub Actions workflow files (steps, environment variables, secrets access). Alert on workflows executing from newly-added or externally-hosted actions, especially those accessing GitHub tokens or sensitive credentials.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm GitHub Actions Persistence & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Miasma Worm' as a named threat. Worms by nature propagate across multiple targets; the mention of 72+ disabled repos indicates lateral movement across the GitHub ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows cloning or triggering other repositories, especially bulk operations. Detect workflows accessing and reusing GitHub tokens across multiple repository contexts, indicating worm-like replication.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Targeting & Abuse via GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions supply chain attack 'Targeting AI Coding Agents.' This indicates attackers specifically hunting GitHub integrations and automation tools that have elevated privileges or access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows invoking external AI coding agents or automation tools with elevated permissions. Monitor for unusual script execution within AI agent contexts, particularly inline scripts or external URL-sourced code.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: GitHub Actions Ecosystem Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a targeted 'Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents.' This is a foundational indicator of attackers deliberately weaponizing the GitHub Actions supply chain as a distribution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected version updates or changes to popular GitHub Actions, especially those used by AI tools or development environments. Detect actions pulling and executing untrusted external dependencies or scripts.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Compromised GitHub Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise implies attackers gaining access to repository secrets and tokens. The targeting of 'AI Coding Agents' suggests credential theft to maintain persistence or establish C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows accessing or exfiltrating repository secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, third-party API keys). Alert on unusual environment variable expansion, base64 encoding of secrets, or network exfiltration in actions.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Version Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised'; attack vector is installation of poisoned package. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pip/poetry/conda install or import of durabletask with version hash mismatches against known good registry. Monitor for unusual pip sources or offline .whl installs. Alert on installations within known compromise window.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Registry Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker modified PyPI records or account. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for registry account takeover and malicious upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI API audit logs for unusual publish events (new version from atypical account, rapid version sequence, metadata changes). Correlate with account-access anomalies. Alert on package uploads from IP ranges not in publishing account history.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Module Behavior Post-Import
suggestion.rationale: Malicious package executes on import or first use. Pipeline identified no runtime detection for code execution hidden within dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for durabletask imports in development and production environments. Alert on child processes spawned during import, unexpected network connections, or file I/O to sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Version Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Compromised versions are likely a subset or all recent releases. Pipeline extracted no IOCs for version fingerprints or manifest validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan requirements.txt, Pipfile, pyproject.toml, and installed packages for durabletask. Compare hashes against official PyPI checksums. Alert on version mismatches or hash tampering. Maintain blocklist of known-bad versions.

suggestion.title: Development Environment Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Developers installing package in IDEs, CI/CD, containers. Pipeline missed collection/exfiltration phase when malicious code executes in trusted development environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python virtual environments and container images for suspicious durabletask installations. Alert on network exfiltration (HTTP requests to C2, credential uploads, source-code egress) originating from Python processes importing compromised package.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—this is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to `/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent` or `/proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone` by non-root processes. Monitor for shell commands writing paths outside normal container/cgroup management patterns. Privilege escalation via cgroups typically precedes unexpected privilege gains in the same process or child shells.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Load After CVE-2022-0492 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Cgroups v1 privilege escalation chains often load malicious kernel modules; article warns of 'actively leveraged' exploitation implying complex payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed privilege escalation attempts (setuid/setgid failures, permission denied on kernel resources) with subsequent successful insmod/modprobe calls. Flag unexpected kernel module loads with missing or suspicious source files, especially from /tmp or process-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Gains CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_MODULE
suggestion.rationale: Linux capability elevation is the hallmark of local privilege escalation; CVE-2022-0492 exploits are typically gated on capability abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-root processes spawning children with elevated capabilities (getpcaps / setcap / capset syscalls). Flag cap_sys_admin, cap_sys_module, or cap_setuid grants to container processes or unprivileged UIDs. Cross-reference with known exploit POCs for CVE-2022-0492.

suggestion.title: Container Namespace Escape via cgroups v1
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'cgroups v1'—containerized environments relying on cgroups for isolation are primary targets. Escape is the intended impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In containerized environments, detect container processes (PIDs in container namespaces) opening host filesystem paths (/proc/sysrq-trigger, /sys/kernel/uevent_helper), or spawning processes outside their PID/UTS namespace. Monitor for host-level process spawns originating from container parent directories.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Activity for CVE-2022-0492 (POC/Malware Execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns vulnerability is 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—detection of known exploit payloads or staging patterns is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for execution of known CVE-2022-0492 exploit POCs (e.g., Dirty Cows variants, cgroup-escape tools). Flag shell commands that write to `/sys/fs/cgroup/` combined with gcc/cc invocations or curl/wget downloads of exploit archives. Baseline process execution from `/tmp` combined with elevated privilege spawns.

suggestion.title: Syslog/Kernel Error Patterns Associated with CVE-2022-0492 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel vulnerabilities often leave detectable error trails; active exploits typically trigger log patterns like cgroup warnings or capability violation messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel logs for patterns: 'cgroup.*EPERM', 'capability violation', 'namespace.*denied', 'release_agent.*denied'. Correlate repeated errors (failed exploits) with eventual privilege escalation success. Flag on high-volume patterns suggesting active exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FFmpeg Version Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names FFmpeg zero-days discovery; pipeline extracted no CVE IDs or version-based detections despite this being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of ffmpeg binary or related library loads (libavcodec, libavformat) with version strings matching known-vulnerable releases. Correlate process creation with web-facing services or untrusted media input sources.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Chrome Version Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Chrome patch count (429 bugs) directly implies widespread vulnerable installations; pipeline ignored software inventory as a detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Chrome process versions via query and alert on versions below patched threshold. Cross-reference with browser activity logs to identify exposure window for 0-day exploitation.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt Behavioral Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 21 unpatched exploitable paths exist; pipeline created no behavioral detection for post-exploitation activity or unusual FFmpeg/Chrome resource consumption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ffmpeg/chrome child processes spawning reverse shells, DNS exfiltration, or anomalous file writes post-crash. Flag heap spray patterns, memory dump artifacts, or network beacons originating from media-processing workflows.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Process Crash or Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article describes an 'actively exploited DoS flaw'—the core attack manifestation is service unavailability or process termination. Pipeline missed detection for Serv-U crashes correlated with inbound traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when SolarWinds Serv-U process (srvuagent.exe, srvuctrl.exe, or listener process) terminates or restarts unexpectedly, especially within seconds of inbound connection attempts to the Serv-U listening port (default 22 for SFTP, 21 for FTP, 3002 for HTTP). Correlation strength increases if the connection source is external or unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Port Unavailability or Connection Resets
suggestion.rationale: DoS exploits impair service availability; article identifies active exploitation. Pipeline should detect port state transitions and connection refusals on Serv-U listener ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP connection attempts to SolarWinds Serv-U ports that result in RST, timeout, or immediate close within milliseconds. Alert on sustained connection refusal rate spike. Baseline normal reject/timeout ratios and trigger on 5x+ deviation. Exclude expected health-check and administrative traffic.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Rapid or Malformed Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: DoS exploitation often uses crafted protocol messages or connection floods; article's 'actively exploited' status implies reconnaissance or weaponized probes. Pipeline missed detection for anomalous connection patterns targeting Serv-U.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources initiating >10 connection attempts to Serv-U ports within 60 seconds, especially if >50% are incomplete handshakes or drop before login. Detect oversized initial protocol messages (e.g., FTP USER command >256 bytes) or rapidly cycling failed logins from same source IP within seconds.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Memory or CPU Exhaustion Pattern
suggestion.rationale: DoS flaws often trigger resource exhaustion; article establishes active exploitation. Pipeline should detect host-level resource spikes coinciding with Serv-U traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process memory and CPU consumption. Alert when either exceeds 10x baseline within 30 seconds AND coincides with DeviceNetworkEvents showing high inbound connection count or data transfer volume on Serv-U ports. Exclude legitimate bulk-transfer scenarios via whitelist.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Error Log Spike (Crash/Deny)
suggestion.rationale: DoS exploits trigger logged errors in target service; article indicates active probing and exploitation. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal error rates in Serv-U logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest SolarWinds Serv-U application logs and alert on 10x+ spike in error messages containing keywords: 'invalid command', 'buffer overflow', 'memory error', 'segmentation fault', 'fatal', or 'crash'. Correlate timing with external network activity to isolate exploitation events from internal noise.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Actively Exploited' in headline and title; pipeline extracted zero detection use cases. Keyword indicates in-the-wild attack campaigns targeting Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances for requests matching known CVE-2026-20245 exploit payloads. Alert on unusual HTTP methods, oversized POST bodies, or path traversal patterns to administrative endpoints. Correlate successful HTTP 200 responses with subsequent authentication or API activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SD-WAN Manager Configuration Change Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is being actively exploited but pipeline missed execution/persistence phase. Successful exploitation of web interface typically leads to admin-level access and config modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag configuration changes to SD-WAN Manager (policy updates, device registration, admin user creation) originating from IPs not in management-access whitelist. Alert on API calls with admin privileges following exploitation attempts within same session or source IP.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'No Patch Available'—critical asset-management indicator pipeline completely missed. Unpatched vulnerable instances should be flagged as high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances from network inventory against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20245. Prioritize instances exposed to untrusted networks. Monitor for fingerprinting or reconnaissance queries targeting these instances (banner-grabbing, GET /admin endpoints, port scanning of management ports).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PHP Code Injection via Form Fields
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement'—the primary attack vector requires detection of form-based injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Everest Forms endpoints for POST parameters containing PHP syntax patterns: single quotes escaping string literals, comment markers (//), eval() references, or wp_*() function calls in user-supplied Complex Calculation field values.

suggestion.title: Administrator Account Creation via PHP Injection During Form Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account'—admin account creation during form calculation evaluation is the exploitation confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_insert_user() or wp_create_user() calls with role='administrator' that occur synchronously with form submission processing and lack corresponding wp-admin authentication logs. Alert on programmatic admin account creation outside normal workflows.

suggestion.title: Known Malicious Username Pattern in Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article provides direct exploitation signature: 'new administrator account with the username 'diksimarina''—this is an observed IOC from Wordfence telemetry enabling immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new administrator account creation with username='diksimarina' or matching bot-like naming patterns. Correlate account creation timestamp with Everest Forms submission logs to establish causal chain.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests from Known Everest Forms Exploit Attacker IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' with 29,300+ blocked attempts—direct network indicator for immediate blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on HTTP/HTTPS traffic from source IPs 202.56.2.126 or 209.146.60.26 to WordPress endpoints. Log all requests including paths, parameters, and timestamps for incident correlation.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Backdoor and Webshell Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers with admin access can perform 'installing plugins and themes, planting backdoors and webshells'—persistence mechanisms must be detected post-privilege-escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized file uploads, plugin installations, and suspicious PHP files created outside normal deployment windows following successful admin account creation. Flag backdoor patterns in wp-content directories.

suggestion.title: Admin-Level Operations from Unauthenticated Form Processing Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers gain ability to perform 'modifying content, installing plugins and themes'—behavioral detection of admin operations during form processing establishes impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin-level WordPress actions (content modification, plugin/theme installation, settings changes) occurring during or immediately after Everest Forms processing windows, especially correlated with newly created admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Installation on Smart TV Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies.' Initial access via social engineering / app store distribution. Detection must catch installs from unknown developers, permission escalation for network/storage, or installs following phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect app installations on Roku, FireTV, Samsung SmartTV platforms where app metadata lacks verifiable publisher identity, requests unusual permissions (network socket creation, file system access), or installs spike after promotional campaigns or phishing attempts. Correlate with known-bad app signatures.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Egress Traffic from Smart TV Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states devices become 'web-scraping proxies'—requires sustained outbound traffic. Should detect TVs making unexpected HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-CDN destinations, especially over non-standard ports or to newly-registered/suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from smart TV MAC addresses/models for (a) sustained high-volume outbound connections outside user-initiated streaming/browsing patterns, (b) DNS queries to typosquatted or NRD domains, (c) HTTPS handshakes to non-trusted CAs or certificate pinning anomalies.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Acting as HTTP/SOCKS Proxy Server
suggestion.rationale: Article: devices are 'proxies'—implies TV forwarding requests on behalf of external actors. Detect if TV initiates connections for third parties: CONNECT tunneling, Host header mismatches, or simultaneous inbound/outbound correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify smart TVs sending HTTP requests with headers/URIs inconsistent with legitimate user activity (e.g., requests for competitor product pricing, research papers, bulk news archives). Flag SOCKS or HTTP CONNECT tunnels initiated by TV. Correlate request User-Agents with known scraping libraries.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Persistence and Auto-Launch on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: App must survive reboots and run 'quietly' without user visibility. Detect boot-time registration, process hiding, or auto-restart mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned background services on TVs, apps that disable uninstall mechanisms, or modify startup configs. Flag apps spawning hidden processes with network capabilities or attempting to suppress app-list visibility.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Beaconing from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Distributed proxy requires attacker coordination—expect periodic check-ins to C2. Detect heartbeat patterns, domain generation algorithms, or DNS tunneling to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify periodic outbound connections from TVs on fixed intervals (heartbeat), or to hardcoded IPs with no reverse-DNS. Detect DNS queries for parent domains (botnet beaconing pattern). Flag TLS connections with mismatched certificate chains or disabled validation.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to Bright SDK proxy C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names C2 domains and IPs: 'proxyjs.brdtnet.com', 'clientsdk.bright-sdk.com', 'brdtnet.com', 'luminatinet.com', 'bright-sdk.com' and IPs 3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114. States devices 'quietly enrolling' into proxy network, implying persistent C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from Samsung, LG, Roku smart TV devices to Bright SDK, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, or residential proxy C2 infrastructure. Monitor DNS queries for proxyjs.*.com and clientsdk.*.com subdomains. Flag any TV device initiating connections to known Bright Data proxy nodes.

suggestion.title: Trojanized free app installation from smart TV app stores
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku, and other major smart TV platforms have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices' — the attack begins with installation of malicious apps from official marketplaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app installation events on smart TV platforms. Establish baseline of legitimate free apps and flag anomalies: newly-published free utilities with unusual permissions, apps requesting network/proxy access. Correlate app installations with subsequent connections to Bright SDK C2 infrastructure to identify trojanized apps.

suggestion.title: Hidden/obfuscated consent dialogs enrolling devices in proxy networks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes defense tactic: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation' — users unknowingly accept proxy enrollment through UX manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze smart TV app permission and consent flows for hidden, nested, or difficult-to-navigate dialogs. Flag apps where data-sharing or network-forwarding terms are obscured behind menu navigation inconsistent with normal smart TV UX. Correlate apps with hidden consent acceptance to those exhibiting suspicious network behavior.

suggestion.title: Smart TV device acting as residential proxy node
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack objective: 'residential proxy network used to scrape web data for AI training' — devices become relay nodes forwarding traffic and exfiltrating browsing data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify smart TV devices exhibiting unusual proxy/forwarding behavior: high outbound connection counts, traffic relayed from other network sources, persistent connections to proxy C2 during non-viewing hours. Monitor for devices matching residential proxy botnet patterns — consistent beacons, data tunneling, or reverse-proxy configurations.

suggestion.title: Process execution and persistence from smart TV apps
suggestion.rationale: Article states devices 'quietly enrolling' implies persistent background execution from installed apps; free apps must execute silently to maintain proxy enrollment without user awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV process execution for free apps initiating background network tasks. Flag apps spawning child processes or scheduled tasks on TV platforms. Correlate process-level execution to network connections to Bright SDK infrastructure to tie malicious execution to specific apps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Commit to GitHub Repository - Potential Malware Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm 'hits 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories' — implies malicious code committed or PR'd into repos. No detection hypotheses exist for anomalous commits/merges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub webhook/audit logs for commits authored by service accounts or outside normal development windows. Correlate with process execution of newly-cloned/pulled repositories on developer machines. Alert on unsigned commits to critical repos.

suggestion.title: Malware Family Signature - Miasma Worm Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Miasma Worm' but pipeline extracted no malware family indicators, hashes, or file signatures. Standard for any malware-focused report.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known Miasma indicators (hashes, file names, PDB paths) against endpoint telemetry. Flag execution of Miasma samples on developer machines or build systems. Correlate with repository clone/pull activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository or Branch Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack on 73 repos implies unauthorized branch protection bypass, PR merges, or direct writes. Article text missing but title indicates scope of modification activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for disabled/modified branch protection rules, force-pushes to main/master, or merges bypassing review on repos owned by Microsoft. Alert on deletion of recent commits or tags.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GitHub API Activity - Token or Service Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale hit across 73 repos suggests compromised credentials or token. Article describes attack scope but pipeline missed credential-access implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls from unexpected geolocations, IPs, or user agents. Flag rapid successive repo modifications within short timeframe. Monitor for creation of deploy keys or SSH keys on affected repositories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious GitHub Action Version Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body explicitly state 'Azure Functions Action... Disabled After Supply Chain Attack' - indicates compromised marketplace action. The attack vector is dependency poisoning via trusted-but-compromised third-party action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden widespread adoption or version pinning changes to GitHub Actions, especially those targeting CI/CD automation. Correlate action versions against threat intel feeds tracking compromised actions. Alert on repositories that update to a newly-released or recently-updated action followed by unexpected workflow modifications or mass repository disablement.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation Across GitHub Repositories via CI/CD Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Miasma Worm' and '72 Other Repositories Disabled' - worm is self-replicating malware that spreads across multiple repositories. Attack demonstrates cross-repository lateral movement within the supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner environments for abnormal process spawning and file modification patterns outside declared workflow scope. Detect worm signatures: multiple repository push attempts from single runner, self-referential workflow file modifications, mass file creation across sandboxed directories, or runner-to-runner communication.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Disablement After Actions Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' following Azure Functions Action compromise. This is the impact phase - attacker executes disablement logic post-compromise across multiple org repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk repository disablement or deletion events within short time window against recent GitHub Actions updates. Alert on repositories disabled via service-account or automation-runner workflows rather than direct human admin action. Detect pattern of disablement targeting specific org or repositories post-compromise.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token / Secrets Exfiltration via Compromised Action
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Azure Functions Action gains access to GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN and OIDC secrets in runner environment. Standard post-compromise objective is credential harvest for lateral movement and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect environment variable enumeration or secret-scanning patterns within action execution (grep env, printenv, env substitution). Alert on tokens used from unexpected geolocations post-action-execution. Monitor for API calls to fork repositories, modify branch protection rules, or create new org repositories using tokens derived from CI/CD secrets.

suggestion.title: Malware Detection: Miasma Worm Signature / Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Threat named explicitly in title as 'Miasma Worm'. Pipeline should flag malware name for signature/behavior-based detection and correlation with known Miasma campaigns (if any prior intel exists).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any binary or script execution matching known Miasma Worm signatures (file hash, YARA rules, or behavioral indicators). Cross-reference against threat intel feeds for Miasma family indicators. Flag any GitHub runner artifact or downloaded dependency matching known Miasma checksums or code patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation - durabletask
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes compromised durabletask PyPI package. Detection must cover installation from PyPI with anomalous timestamps, hashes, or version mismatches: 'PyPI Package Compromised in Supply Chain Attack'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip install, poetry add, or similar package manager invocations targeting durabletask. Alert on any installation that does not match legitimate pinned versions in internal lockfiles. Track hash mismatches or checksums that diverge from known-good snapshots.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Code Execution Post-Package Import
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package will execute attacker code upon import or module load: supply chain attacks leverage package initialization vectors to drop malware. Detection must catch unexpected child processes, network connections, or file writes triggered by durabletask import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal durabletask module import behavior (expected child processes, network calls, file writes). Alert on unexpected spawned processes, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget, immediately following Python interpreter loading durabletask. Monitor for outbound connections to non-Azure destinations from the importing process.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised supply-chain packages typically beacon to attacker infrastructure. Article describes attack vector; C2 infrastructure IOCs should be central to detection: 'compromised...supply chain attack' implies persistent callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from Python interpreters with durabletask module loaded. Focus on non-standard ports, HTTPS to newly-registered domains, or DNS lookups matching attacker infrastructure patterns. Correlate process ancestry to package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Package Hash/Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks succeed by replacing legitimate binaries with trojanized versions. Detection must verify package authenticity at install and runtime: article describes 'compromised' package, implying file-level tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain golden hashes of all durabletask release artifacts from official PyPI CDN. At install-time and on first import, validate installed file hashes against golden set. Alert on mismatches or installation from alternative mirrors/caches not managed by security team.

suggestion.title: Anomalous durabletask Package Metadata or Version
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages often use unusual version strings, metadata, or installation behavior to evade detection. Article title indicates version control: must detect spoofed or out-of-order version numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install of durabletask with version strings not matching official PyPI release history, or on re-downloads of the same version within abnormal time windows. Monitor pip.log and pip cache for evidence of rollback or re-installation patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Malware injected into supply-chain packages often exfiltrates sensitive data (credentials, source code, config). Must detect unexpected outbound data flows from systems with durabletask installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for network traffic volume and destinations from Python processes using durabletask. Alert on bulk outbound transfers, compression utilities (zip, tar, 7z) spawned by Python, or connections to personal/free cloud storage (Pastebin, GitHub gist, VirusTotal).

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent interface manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—this is the direct attack vector. Pipeline generated zero behavioral detection for writes to `/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent` files, the core exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes or attribute modifications to release_agent paths in /sys/fs/cgroup from unprivileged user contexts (UID > 0) or from container/unprivileged namespaces. Correlate with subsequent shell execution or process spawning at UID 0.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via unshare/setns post-write
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain involves namespace operations (unshare/setns syscalls) coupled with release_agent manipulation. Pipeline missed syscall-level detection for this post-authentication attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unshare(2) or setns(2) syscalls from unprivileged processes (UID > 0) followed within 2 seconds by fork/execve from the same process with elevated capability set (CAP_SYS_ADMIN) or UID transition to 0. High fidelity if parent process is not in known container-runtime whitelist.

suggestion.title: Shell spawn following cgroups manipulation sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—exploitation payload is typically a shell. Pipeline omitted detection for the post-privilege-escalation command-execution phase despite 'being actively leveraged' language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or /bin/dash process creation with: (a) parent PID having prior cgroup/namespace syscalls, OR (b) execution with setuid execution attribute, OR (c) spawned from non-standard parent process without container orchestration context. Exclude systemd, docker-init, runc.

suggestion.title: Instagram Account Takeover via Password Reset Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow'—exploitable credential access vector. Attackers can reset affected accounts and gain access, detectable through impossible-travel logins or new device access within 24h of password reset event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor employee Instagram login events from new geographies within 24 hours of password reset, or cluster password-reset-attempt failures from single source IPs. Correlate with internal account takeover indicators.

suggestion.title: Harvested Email/Phone Information Used in Follow-on Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers'—classic precursor to phishing. Hunt for follow-on attacks: phishing emails sent to harvested employee addresses, SMS delivery spikes, or account-recovery pretexting campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing campaigns targeting employee emails with Instagram account recovery lures or password-reset-flow spoofing. Alert on unusual SMS delivery patterns to employee phone numbers during vulnerability window (June 6, 2026 onward).

suggestion.title: High-Profile/Executive Account Anomalies Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific high-profile victims ('Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez')—VIP accounts are primary targets. Detect post-reset: unexpected followers, content changes, or metadata modifications within 72h.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected metadata edits, new app authorizations, or content publishing on executive Instagram accounts during vulnerability disclosure window. Cross-reference with password-change history and access logs.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Zero-Day Exploitation via Malicious Media File
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' but pipeline generated zero use cases. FFmpeg processes untrusted media across web browsers, email, and media players—a primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by ffmpeg/libavformat, unusual file writes to temp directories during media processing, and network callbacks from ffmpeg process. Alert on ffmpeg parsing crafted media files with suspicious codec parameters or container structures.

suggestion.title: Chrome Browser Exploitation and Post-Compromise Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'—a massive surface. Pipeline missed detection of browser-based exploitation, renderer process crashes, and sandbox escapes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual chrome child processes (renderer, GPU, utility) spawning system binaries or scripts. Alert on rapid chrome process terminations (crash loops indicating exploit failure). Monitor for chrome reading sensitive files outside the profile sandbox or making raw socket connections.

suggestion.title: Staged Malware Delivery via Vulnerable Application Updates
suggestion.rationale: Article context: threat actors may exploit zero-days before patches are widely deployed. Pipeline missed detection of malware delivery disguised as legitimate FFmpeg or Chrome installation/update.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Media Processing
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days in document/image handlers may allow attackers to read arbitrary files and exfiltrate via network. Pipeline did not suggest data-collection or C2 detection UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ffmpeg process for reads of sensitive file paths (cookies, vault files, browser history). Detect encrypted or obfuscated outbound connections initiated by media processing threads. Flag ffmpeg making DNS queries or HTTPS connections outside normal library update behavior.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates actively exploited DoS vulnerability; DoS attacks against Serv-U would manifest as service crashes or restart cycles. Pipeline should detect abnormal termination/restart patterns for Serv-U processes indicating impact phase exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SolarWinds Serv-U (sftpd.exe, sftp.exe) process terminations followed by immediate restart within short time windows, or multiple crashes per hour. Correlate with inbound network traffic spikes to detect DoS attack correlation.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is actively exploited; initial exploitation attempts precede successful attacks. Pipeline should detect anomalous requests to Serv-U service ports and malformed protocol commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated connection attempts to default Serv-U ports (22, 115, 220) with unusual packet patterns, oversized payloads, or protocol violations. Correlate failed connection attempts with subsequent service degradation.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Configuration or Binary Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Actively exploited vulnerabilities often target service binaries or config files post-exploitation. Pipeline should monitor integrity of Serv-U executable and configuration files for unauthorized modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to SolarWinds Serv-U binary paths, configuration directories, or related system files outside of patch windows. Track file hash changes for sftpd.exe and config XML files.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: If DoS vulnerability is used as initial foothold, attackers typically attempt privilege escalation. Pipeline should detect Serv-U child processes spawning with elevated tokens or suspicious parent-child relationships.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SolarWinds Serv-U spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with elevated privilege indicators, or running under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context. Flag if sftpd.exe initiates outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Post-Exploitation Process Execution

suggestion.title: Persistent Webshell Implantation in SD-WAN Manager

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized API Access and Credential Harvesting

suggestion.title: Outbound Reverse Shell and C2 Communication from SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation enables post-breach command-and-control — detect outbound sessions from manager to attacker infrastructure on non-standard ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS from Cisco SD-WAN Manager to non-whitelisted destinations, newly-registered domains, or suspicious geographies. Flag connections on non-standard ports or to IPs associated with attacker C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Network Topology Exfiltration via Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager controls enterprise network routes and policies — compromised manager enables large-scale network-map and device-inventory theft. Detect bulk configuration exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls that export device inventory, network topology, or security policies from SD-WAN Manager to external addresses or to local temp files followed by exfil patterns. Monitor data-export API endpoints for high-volume requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Free App Installation on Smart TV Device

suggestion.title: Smart TV Acting as Proxy: Abnormal Egress Traffic Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes TVs converted to 'web-scraping proxies'—pipeline missed the execution/C&C phase. Detection gap: 'Turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies'—this is the active proxy behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smart TV devices initiating HTTP/HTTPS requests to third-party domains at scale (>50 unique domains/day) not consistent with streaming apps. Detect proxy-like patterns: TV device accepting inbound requests and forwarding outbound traffic, or TV making requests on behalf of external clients.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Device Performing Large-Scale Web Content Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat is web scraping. Pipeline missed collection phase. Cite: 'Web-Scraping Proxies for AI'—describes systematic data harvest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for smart TV devices performing HEAD/GET requests to common web targets (news sites, research databases, social media) in sequential or bulk patterns. Flag requests with User-Agent headers mismatched to device model or requests to domains known to host training data / public corpora.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Web Content via Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Article describes scraped data being transmitted for 'AI' training—exfiltration phase. Pipeline missed: proxy role implies data leaves the TV to external attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smart TV devices uploading large payloads (>10MB/day) to external IP addresses or domains not in approved list. Monitor for encrypted tunnels (HTTPS POST, DNS tunneling) originating from TV device. Correlate with web-scraping request pattern.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege or Permission Escalation on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Free apps require unusual permissions (file access, network interception) to execute proxy functionality. Pipeline missed defense-evasion/privilege-escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps on smart TV devices requesting or exploiting system-level permissions (kernel module load, device driver installation, network stack access). Flag apps with capability/permission requests disproportionate to their declared function (e.g., media player requesting raw socket access).

suggestion.title: Smart TV App Establishes Connection to Known Residential Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: article states free apps 'quietly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network.' Enrollment handshake to domains (bright-sdk.com, luminati.io, brdtnet.com) or IPs (3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114) is the definitive telemetry; pipeline generated zero C2-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device (LG, Samsung, Roku) initiates outbound DNS query or TCP connection to proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io, bright-sdk.com, or ASN-attributed proxy IPs. High confidence if process is app-related and followed by sustained background traffic.

suggestion.title: Free App Installs with Obfuscated Network Permission Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat mechanism: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' Initial access depends on UX deception; pipeline did not flag T1204.001 (user execution malicious app) or T1036 (masquerading) techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Free application from Samsung Galaxy Apps, LG Content Store, or Roku Channel requests network proxy, VPN, raw socket, or packet capture permissions. Alert if app reputation is low, publication date <30 days, or permission prompt is nested >2 EULA/wizard screens deep or uses non-standard navigation (arrow-key sequences vs. standard buttons).

suggestion.title: Smart TV Device Background Service Initialization Without User Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Persistence required for 'quiet' enrollment; article implies apps activate background proxy operation. T1547 and T1565 persistence techniques are entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Application process spawns or registers background service/daemon without corresponding UI wizard or user consent event. Service name obfuscation (SDK tokens, proxy-related keywords) or network connectivity to proxy infrastructure post-service creation strongly indicates persistence for proxy enrollment.

suggestion.title: Consumer Device Becomes Source of Automated Outbound Web Scraping Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Attack purpose stated: 'scrape web data for AI training.' Once enrolled, device acts as exit node; T1041 (exfiltration over C2) and T1083 (reconnaissance/scraping) are required detections but missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device (vendor DHCP hostname or MAC OUI match) issues high-volume HTTP requests to diverse third-party domains with consistent User-Agent strings, automated request patterns (recursive crawls, no user think-time), or indicators of reconnaissance/scanning. Baseline per-device egress; flag 10x+ deviations or requests post-proxy-enrollment connection.

suggestion.title: Known Residential Proxy Provider Domains Contacted from Residential IP Space
suggestion.rationale: Baseline IOC hunt missing entirely. 11 indicators provided (9 domains, 2 IPs)—essential foundation for threat hunting. Zero use cases generated despite these being high-fidelity, corroborated to Bright Data / Luminati infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Residential or Smart TV IP address issues DNS query for proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.luminatinet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io, bright-sdk.com or connects to 3.33.193.183 or 15.197.193.114. High-fidelity indicator for proxy network enrollment.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Smart TV App Setup Wizard with Hidden Permission Nesting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes obfuscation mechanism: consent 'buried in TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' Defense-evasion step is the *delivery method* for initial access—pipeline classified only T1071 (generic protocol), missing T1036.008 (match legitimate appearance) and UI-based social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV app setup wizard or EULA flow contains permission request (network proxy, VPN, raw network) that appears after initial 'Agree' prompt, uses visual de-emphasis (small text, low contrast), or requires non-standard navigation input (arrow-key combinations, remote button sequences) rather than direct touch/click confirmation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repo Compromise via Suspicious Commit Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'—this is the core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for GitHub compromise or commit-based malware injection, which is the delivery mechanism for supply-chain worms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub commit logs for structural anomalies: commits adding/modifying .github/workflows, package.json, or build manifests by new or inactive contributors; commits from newly-rotated SSH keys; commit payloads containing encoded or obfuscated scripts typical of worm propagation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Repository Coordinated Compromise Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Exactly 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories compromised in coordinated attack—this is a distinctive scale signal. Pipeline produced no aggregation rule to detect when multiple repos in a single organization are compromised within a narrow time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when ≥5 repositories in the same GitHub organization exhibit simultaneous anomalies: unusual commits, new SSH key deployments, branch protection rule modifications, or secret rotation—all within 48 hours, indicating coordinated worm propagation.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm File Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names the threat 'Miasma Worm' but pipeline extracted zero file hashes, malware signatures, or behavioral indicators. This is the foundational IOC extraction failure—worm samples should be hashed and detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once Miasma samples are procured, generate hash-based detections for known worm binaries. Supplement with behavioral rules: recursive repo cloning from a single process, self-modification of build scripts, execution of unsigned binaries from .git directories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Poisoning via Build System Injection
suggestion.rationale: Worm targeting GitHub repos implies exploitation of CI/CD pipelines to poison downstream artifacts (packages, containers). Article describes compromise of 73 repos but pipeline generated no detection for build-system injection or artifact pollution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD job logs for: new workflow steps absent from source code (step injection), downloads of unsigned/untrusted binaries during build, execution of scripts from non-standard paths, build artifacts with modified metadata that don't match committed source.

suggestion.title: Recursive Repository Compromise Detection (Worm Propagation)
suggestion.rationale: A 'worm' by definition self-propagates. Article does not detail propagation mechanism but pipeline should have inferred that compromised repos may clone sibling repos and re-inject the worm. No lateral-movement or propagation detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository clone-and-commit cycles: repository A performs unexpected git clone of repository B in the same organization, followed immediately by a commit push back to A or forward to a third repository. Flag recursive patterns (A→B→C, B→A) within <1 hour windows.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Repo Metadata Modification (Bypass of Code Review)
suggestion.rationale: Worms targeting GitHub often disable branch protections, bypass code review, or modify repository secrets. Article mentions widespread compromise but pipeline generated no detection for defensive-control circumvention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository setting changes: branch protection rules disabled, required code reviewers removed, webhooks added to external hosts, deploy keys created, or organization members removed—especially by users who have not performed these actions historically.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Mass Disable Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' after compromise. Pipeline missed detection of rapid/bulk repository deletion or disabling, a signature impact of repository takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Multiple repositories disabled or deleted within a short time window (< 1 hour) by a single actor or from a single source IP. Monitor GitHub GraphQL/REST API calls to `deleteRepository` or `updateRepository(archived=true)` operations. Alert on >5 repo state changes by non-admin accounts or unusual automation tokens.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Action Workflow Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Azure Functions Action' as directly compromised. Pipeline missed GitHub Action file modifications (workflow YAML, JavaScript action entrypoint) or suspicious execution within the action namespace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Commits to `.github/workflows/*` or `action.yml` in the azure-functions-action repository not authored by maintainers, or workflow execution logs showing unexpected commands, environment variable exfiltration, or network calls to non-Microsoft domains. Track webhook events on this repository.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Injection via Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' as the attack vehicle. Pipeline missed detection of injected commands or malicious code funneling through agent dependencies into AI model inference or code generation pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection of unexpected dependencies or code injected into package.json, requirements.txt, or pyproject.toml linked to AI agent libraries (e.g., LangChain, AutoGPT). Monitor for agent runtime execution of code not in the approved baseline. Alert on agent API calls to external command execution or script invocation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack implies compromised packages or dependencies. Pipeline missed IOCs for tampered package manifests, version downgrades, or pre-release publication of legitimate packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (npm, PyPI, NuGet) for unexpected version releases, yanked/re-published versions, or metadata changes (author, maintainer, signed signatures removed) on packages known to be in the Microsoft ecosystem or AI agent dependencies. Alert on version rollbacks or non-semantic versioning jumps.

suggestion.title: Miasma Malware Artifact Detection in Repository Contents
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Miasma Worm' as the threat. Pipeline failed to extract malware signatures, hashes, code patterns, or behavioral indicators associated with this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan repository commit history for known Miasma worm signatures (if available from threat intel feeds), obfuscated code patterns, or embedded binary payloads. Monitor for repository commits containing file hashes or C2 domains associated with Miasma. Cross-reference with YARA rules or malware samples from incident response reports.

suggestion.title: Automated Agent Execution of Injected Payloads
suggestion.rationale: AI coding agents are the stated target. Pipeline missed detection of agent-initiated code execution, file writes, or privilege escalation triggered by crafted prompts or compromised action dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AI agent processes spawning unusual child processes (bash, PowerShell, curl, git) or writing files to unexpected directories. Monitor for agent API calls that invoke code execution without user authorization. Alert on agent environment variable exfiltration or outbound connections from agent processes to non-whitelisted domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — installation of the malicious package is the primary attack surface. Zero detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip or Python package manager execution with arguments containing 'durabletask' package name. Escalate on installation of specific compromised versions. Correlate with environment expectations (should not appear in prod without business justification).

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Compromised Package Import
suggestion.rationale: Article signals 'compromised' package status implying malicious payload. No detection framework for execution phase following package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning, code injection, or network I/O initiated by Python interpreter after durabletask import. Baseline legitimate library behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Package Integrity Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain detections should include pre-execution verification checks. No hash, signature, or checksum validation detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed pip signature verification, package hash mismatches, checksum validation errors, or file metadata inconsistencies during durabletask installation.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Organizations using durabletask as a transitive (indirect) dependency face risk without explicit package listing. Pipeline missed dependency-chain analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query application manifests (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py) to identify where durabletask is a transitive dependency. Flag installations of parent packages that pull compromised versions automatically.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise C2 and Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises enable downstream attack phases. Article's 'compromised' status implies malicious payload, but post-exploitation detections absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections from hosts with confirmed durabletask installation. Flag C2 beaconing patterns, data exfiltration indicators, and deviations from baseline communication profiles.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent file modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability affects 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature'—this is the exploitation vector. Modification of release_agent files is abnormal and indicative of privilege-escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/[pid]/cgroup. Flag writes from unprivileged users (UID > 1000). Cross-reference with process spawning to identify payload execution.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged user namespace + cgroup operation sequence
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 exploitation requires unprivileged user namespace creation (unshare/clone) followed by cgroup manipulation. The article states attackers 'leverage' this flaw from unprivileged context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) or clone(CLONE_NEWUSER) syscalls from non-root users with subsequent cgroup file operations within 5 seconds. High-confidence indicator of CVE-2022-0492 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected code execution via cgroup release_agent trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—release_agent executes commands when cgroups are released. Detection must identify process spawning with cgroup-related ancestry or event hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned with parent=release_agent handler or process creation events triggered by cgroup subsystem events. Flag if parent process does not exist on disk (signature of cgroup-triggered execution).

suggestion.title: Access to unprivileged_userns_clone or kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone sysctls
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 exploitation pathway often begins by checking or modifying kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone setting. Article's mention of 'unprivileged' attackers implies this reconnaissance step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads/writes to /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone from non-root users, especially followed by unshare() syscalls. Low false-positive risk in production systems.

suggestion.title: Bulk Password Reset Requests to Instagram Web Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow.' Pre-June-6 exploitation of this publicly documented vulnerability should be detectable via unusual request volume and patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spikes in POST requests to /accounts/password/reset/ endpoints pre-June-6-2026 from non-standard ASNs or bot-like user-agents. Correlate with account-access anomalies 24-48 hours post-request.

suggestion.title: Email Address Enumeration via Exposed Password Reset Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed unredacted email addresses associated with user accounts.' Attackers enumerate Instagram user emails by probing the flaw, enabling downstream credential-stuffing attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential password-reset requests with username/email variations returning 200-response patterns that leak valid email addresses. Threshold >100 reqs/minute from single source.

suggestion.title: Phone Number Disclosure via Account Recovery Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed...phone numbers associated with user accounts.' Password reset endpoint returned obfuscated recovery phone numbers; mass scraping possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for systematic enumeration of /accounts/password/reset/ responses revealing partial phone format (e.g., +1-***-***-1234). Alert on >50 unique account enum attempts per hour.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Using Exposed Instagram Email-Phone Pairs
suggestion.rationale: Article: exposed 'email addresses and phone numbers' create a correlated dataset for targeted credential abuse. Post-June-6, monitor for abuse of the leaked contact pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-June-6: detect login failures using known-breached credential pairs filtered to emails/phones disclosed by the Instagram flaw. Correlate with external breach databases (Have I Been Pwned).

suggestion.title: Account Takeover of High-Profile Instagram Users Post-Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'high-profile individuals such as Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez' had contact info exposed. These named targets will face intensive credential-recovery and ATO attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >2 failed login/recovery attempts within 1 hour on verified high-profile accounts post-June-6. Flag any successful recovery SMS/email confirmation from out-of-region IPs.

suggestion.title: Malformed Media File Execution in FFmpeg
suggestion.rationale: Article: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — zero-days in multimedia libraries manifest as remote code execution when processing attacker-controlled files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FFmpeg process execution with suspicious file arguments (corrupted headers, unusual magic bytes, oversized metadata). Correlate with process crashes, abnormal memory allocation, or unexpected child processes. Baseline FFmpeg behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Download Exploitation via Malicious Media
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' — browser rendering of crafted media files is a canonical initial-access vector for 0-day chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of media files (.mp4, .mov, .mkv, .webm, .webp) from untrusted sources (emails, malicious sites). Correlate with browser crashes, abnormal memory access, or post-compromise indicators within 1 hour of download.

suggestion.title: Phishing with FFmpeg-Exploiting Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article: '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — high-volume zero-day availability incentivizes email-based weaponization of crafted media files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email attachments with video/image MIME types sent to users with outdated FFmpeg or Chrome (inventory correlation). Detect post-delivery execution of file decompression, media rendering, or codec libraries.

suggestion.title: Memory Corruption Exploitation (Heap/Stack/Use-After-Free)
suggestion.rationale: Article context: 21 + 429 vulnerability count suggests widespread memory-safety bugs in multimedia/browser parsers—canonical ROP, heap spray, ASLR bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg/Chrome memory for ROP gadget sequences, heap spray patterns, or stack pivot instructions. Correlate with control-flow guard (CFG) violations, DEP exceptions, or out-of-bounds memory access. Analyze crash dumps for shellcode markers.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article: '429 Chrome Patches' and FFmpeg zero-days — detection must prioritize identifying unpatched instances across enterprise before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain real-time inventory of Chrome and FFmpeg versions. Flag systems running versions released before the zero-day disclosure window. Correlate version age with lateral-movement attempts or exploit-kit C2 beaconing to prioritize urgent patching.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Fuzzing & Crash-Database Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI Agent Uncovers' zero-days — implies automated fuzzing reconnaissance and crash reporting as part of threat-actor discovery arsenal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect local fuzzing harnesses (parallel FFmpeg/Chrome invocations, rapid temp file creation, memory dumps). Alert on uploads to crash aggregators (OSS-Fuzz, ClusterFuzz, vendor bug-trackers). Baseline multimedia codec behavior and flag reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited' vulnerability; no detection use case provided despite high severity and KEV status indicating adversary activity in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U listening ports for abnormal traffic patterns: sudden spike in connection count, rapid request rate from single or distributed sources, and simultaneous connection failures. Correlate with service CPU/memory exhaustion in performance logs.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires discovery of running Serv-U instances; no reconnaissance detection despite active-threat context of article.
