suggestion.rationale: Article title 'AI Agent Uncovers' zero-days implies automated vulnerability discovery infrastructure. Pipeline failed to identify reconnaissance/discovery phase typical of zero-day research workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known fuzzing frameworks (libFuzzer, AFL++, honggfuzz) or memory sanitizers (ASAN, MSAN, UBSAN). Monitor for iterative test harness execution patterns and rapid input mutation file generation.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited' and added to CISA KEV catalog. No detection use case generated despite critical impact. Article explicitly names SolarWinds Serv-U as target, justifying exploit pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or oversized requests to SolarWinds Serv-U listening ports (default 22, 3389) consistent with known DoS payloads. Correlate with process anomalies in Serv-U process memory/CPU spike or service crash/restart cycles.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Anomaly & Crash Detection
suggestion.rationale: DoS flaw targets Serv-U service stability. Article confirms active exploitation but pipeline generated zero detections for service-level anomalies or repeated restart patterns indicative of DoS attack success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated Serv-U process terminations, service restarts, or hung processes within 5-minute windows. Correlate with inbound network anomalies (high packet count, high connection count to Serv-U ports) to distinguish DoS from legitimate restarts.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation: Unpatched Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: KEV-catalog entry implies widespread vulnerable deployments. Pipeline should have generated asset-based detection to identify unpatched Serv-U instances via banner grab, port scanning, or software inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate internal/external asset inventory (CMDB, Shodan, Censys queries) with network telemetry to identify Serv-U service banners and version strings. Enrich with CVE patch dates to flag vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U: Abnormal Remote Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: DoS flaw explicitly noted as 'actively exploited.' Attackers may chain DoS with access/persistence attempts. Pipeline missed lateral movement or access consolidation detection following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new inbound RDP, SSH, or SFTP connections originating from Serv-U host to internal resources within 10 minutes of DoS-pattern network events. Flag anomalous credential use or process spawns from Serv-U process context.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Actively Exploited – No Patch Available,' indicating in-the-wild exploitation. Pipeline missed detection hypothesis for attack payloads or proof-of-concept patterns targeting the vulnerability in HTTP/HTTPS logs against SD-WAN Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager admin interfaces (default port 8443) for suspicious request patterns, malformed payloads, or known CVE-2026-20245 exploitation signatures. Alert on 4xx/5xx response clusters from public IPs or known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Post-Exploitation Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates active exploitation; pipeline should assume successful compromise and detect lateral movement or data exfiltration from the manager. No detection UC generated for abnormal API calls or data queries after a potential breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk exports of SD-WAN configuration, site lists, or credential vaults from the manager API. Detect unusual data volume or frequency of /api/v1/config or /api/v1/sites endpoints post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized Configuration Modifications
suggestion.rationale: No detection UC for privilege escalation or persistence via configuration tampering. Once an attacker gains access via CVE-2026-20245, they would modify SD-WAN policies, device settings, or user accounts. Pipeline missed config-change auditing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new admin users, modification of SSL certificates, or changes to approved device list without corresponding change request. Baseline config-change velocity during business hours and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Credential Stuffing or Brute Force (Pre-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Before CVE-2026-20245 is exploited, attackers often probe for weak credentials. Article does not indicate auth-bypass, so brute-force detection is relevant as a pre-exploitation layer. Pipeline did not suggest defensive credential-access monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager login endpoints for failed authentication clusters (>5 failed logins in 5 minutes from single source). Correlate with known vulnerable versions or public exploit PoC drops.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PHP Code Injection via Everest Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker closing string literal with single quote, injecting PHP code, and using // comments to evade syntax checking. This is the core exploitation technique but no detection rule was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints (plugin form submission URLs) containing single quote characters or PHP syntax patterns (wp_insert_user, eval, base64) in form field parameters. Flag payloads where semicolon or // comment markers appear in numeric/calculation fields.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker calls wp_insert_user() to create admin 'diksimarina' and recommends 'review administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina.' No use case for detecting this account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress wp_users table INSERT operations for new user creation with admin role. Alert on accounts created outside normal admin workflows. Search logs and database for the string 'diksimarina' or other suspicious account names created during vulnerability exploitation window (April 13, 2026 onwards).

suggestion.title: Traffic from Known Everest Forms Exploitation Attackers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names two attacker IP addresses (202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26) and states Wordfence blocked 29,300+ exploitation attempts. Pipeline provided zero IOC-based rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on any inbound HTTP traffic originating from IP 202.56.2[.]126 or 209.146.60.26. Cross-reference web server logs for requests from these IPs to any WordPress installation running Everest Forms plugin versions ≤1.9.12.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-3300 Patch Application Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states patch released March 18, 2026 for versions 1.9.12 and earlier. No use case generated for identifying unpatched installations or monitoring patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Everest Forms Pro plugin version in all WordPress installations. Alert if version 1.9.12 or earlier is detected. Track plugin update logs to identify sites that have NOT applied the patch since March 18, 2026.

suggestion.title: Form Field Submission with Comment Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article explains attacker injects code followed by // comment marker to 'ensure the rest of the generated PHP code is treated as a comment.' This specific obfuscation technique is missing from detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form submissions to Everest Forms complex calculation fields containing double-slash (//) or hash (#) comment markers within the payload. Correlate with single-quote characters to identify incomplete quote-closure attempts that signal code injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Eval-Vulnerable Plugin Form Processing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: Complex Calculation feature passes user input through inadequate sanitize_text_field() then executes via PHP eval(). No signature rule for detecting this specific vulnerable code pattern exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP execution logs for eval() function calls with user-controlled variables, particularly from form handling contexts. Flag sanitize_text_field() output immediately followed by eval() or create_function() calls. Alert on syntax errors from malformed code injection attempts in form processing.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Installation via Smart TV App Store
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Free Apps...turning Smart TVs into...Proxies'—classic supply-chain compromise. Pipeline captured zero initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious app installations on smart TV platforms. Monitor app metadata (developer name, signature, package hash, permissions requested) against known malicious catalogs. Flag apps requesting network-layer permissions for non-media-streaming applications.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Web Scraping Activity from Smart TV Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title describes apps 'Turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies'—this is the core execution/collection phase. Zero use cases covered this critical attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume HTTP/HTTPS traffic from smart TV app processes to non-whitelisted domains (especially news, research, or public-data sites). Flag requests from apps with media/utility purpose making API or scraping calls. Correlate with user expectation—scraping activity not initiated by user interaction.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Command-and-Control Channel
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates scraped content flows 'for AI'—implying centralized exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline identified zero exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag smart TV apps establishing persistent, encrypted outbound tunnels to non-standard ports or unregistered domains. Monitor for large data transfers occurring at off-peak hours or in patterns inconsistent with legitimate streaming. Detect custom encoding schemes or protocol anomalies in app traffic.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Auto-Update and System Hook Registration
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'quietly turning' implies silent, persistent malicious behavior. Pipeline produced zero persistence-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for smart TV apps auto-starting on boot or surviving factory resets. Detect out-of-band app updates that bypass official OS update mechanisms. Flag registered system services or scheduled tasks spawning from app binaries without user consent.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Network Connections to Known Residential Proxy Provider Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names C2 domains (proxyjs.brdtnet.com, proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.bright-sdk.com, etc.) used by enrolled devices; no detection generated for identifying smart TV devices phoning home to these indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/TLS connections from smart TV platforms (Samsung, LG, Roku user-agents) to Bright Data proxy domains or IPs (3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114). Correlate sustained connections against baseline streaming patterns to distinguish malicious activity from legitimate proxy use.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Data Exfiltration from Smart TV Devices to Proxy Network Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states devices are 'scraping web data for AI training' — high-volume exfiltration activity. No detection for abnormal outbound data transfer from smart TV segments to proxy provider IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high-bandwidth outbound connections from smart TV devices to proxy provider IPs with patterns inconsistent with user-initiated streaming (scheduled traffic, rapid reconnects, volume spikes during sleep hours). Baseline residential TV segment egress and alert on 5x deviations.

suggestion.title: Deceptive Consent Dialog Patterns in Smart TV App Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation' — a defense evasion mechanism hiding proxy enrollment. No use case generated for detecting dark-pattern UI consent flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app telemetry for EULA flows with abnormal input requirements (e.g., requiring >5 remote button presses to reach 'reject' option, consent fields embedded after unrelated settings, opt-out unavailable without scrolling past acceptance). Cross-reference with app store reviews mentioning 'unexpected bandwidth usage' or 'background network activity'.

suggestion.title: Proxy Client SDK or Malicious Payload Execution on Smart TV Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article implies proxy client software is bundled silently in free apps ('enrolling millions of devices'). No detection for process execution patterns consistent with Bright Data SDK initialization or proxy client binaries launching on smart TVs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for background process spawning on Samsung, LG, Roku devices immediately post-app installation with names or command-line arguments matching `bright*`, `luminati*`, `proxyjs*`, or processes initiating network connections to known proxy domains. Correlate with Bright Data SDK package hashes if available.

suggestion.title: Compromised Free Apps with Proxy Enrollment Code in Official Smart TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku' as the distribution vector — supply chain compromise via official app stores. Pipeline missed initial_access detection for identifying which apps contain proxy enrollment code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan apps in official Samsung SmartThings, LG webOS, and Roku stores for: (1) network permission scope exceeding stated app functionality, (2) embedded Bright Data/Luminati SDK strings in binaries, (3) callback URLs matching proxy provider domains, (4) abnormal DNS/IP connections on first launch. Flag apps with >100 user reviews mentioning 'unexpected network usage' or 'high bandwidth'.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DNS Query Patterns from Residential Smart TV IP Segments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'scrape web data' — web scraping activity generates characteristic high-frequency DNS queries and bulk domain probes. No detection for identifying when smart TV IPs exhibit scraper behavior rather than normal viewing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile DNS query patterns from smart TV device segments against ISP residential IP databases. Flag sustained query rate anomalies (>100 queries/min), bulk domain enumeration patterns, queries to data aggregator/scraper-target domains (search engines, social archives, ecommerce price APIs), and automated probing behavior inconsistent with human viewing.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection Across GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article title states '73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'—core attack vector is repository commit poisoning. Pipeline extracted zero detection use cases for this primary attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk commit activity across multiple repos in short timeframe, commits from dormant or new accounts, commits modifying build artifacts or CI config, or commits originating from non-developer IP ranges.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise via Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gained write access to 73 repos simultaneously—implies credential compromise or token theft. Article does not detail initial access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible-travel login patterns, PAT creation from unusual IP/time, bulk API calls using stolen tokens, or authentication followed immediately by mass repository or member additions.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation via Build Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Miasma Worm'—implies active replication mechanism, yet pipeline extracted zero use cases for worm behavior (lateral movement, persistence, self-propagation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning multiple subprocesses, network beaconing to GitHub from build servers, rapid file creation/modification across repo directories, and automated commits without human interaction.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack via GitHub repos—GitHub Actions is high-value execution surface. No detection use cases for workflow tampering, secret exfiltration, or CI/CD pipeline abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on newly-created workflows, workflows accessing org secrets or environment variables, workflows with suspicious curl/wget commands, and workflows executing from unexpected branches or triggered by non-developer actions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Hash Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Attack compromises binaries/packages delivered via GitHub to downstream consumers. No detection for signature mismatches, hash divergence from official Microsoft sources, or certificate anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executables with mismatched certificates, revoked signatures, or hashes absent from official Microsoft repositories. Monitor for unexpected re-downloads or installations of artifacts from compromised repos.

suggestion.title: Repository Settings and Access Control Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attacker compromised 73 repos—likely escalated permissions, disabled branch protection, or hid activity. No use cases for detecting bulk permission changes or settings tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk changes to branch protection rules, repository visibility toggles (public-to-private or reverse), addition of new administrators or deploy keys, and changes to webhook/integration settings.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modification in High-Trust Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled' — implies unauthorized modification of workflow files or disablement of repository automations as attack payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized additions or modifications to .github/workflows/ files in public or fork-of-public repositories; correlate with repo disablement events, unexpected loss of actions, or absence of expected workflow runs. Flag repos with <30-day commit history modified suddenly.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Package Registry Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents' — malware distributed via compromised AI agent packages (likely hosted on npm, PyPI, or GitHub Package Registry).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package installation logs for AI coding agent repos (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, Codeium integrations) for suspicious version jumps, orphaned maintainers, or unsigned packages. Alert on install-time code execution outside known dependency tree.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Disablement Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — mass archival, deletion, or access revocation of repositories is a distinctive impact signature of this worm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >5 repositories disabled/archived/deleted within 15-minute window by same user or via same API token; exclude known bulk-archival events (e.g., org migrations). Correlate with unexpected service principal activity or compromised PAT usage.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm Signature and C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names a specific malware family 'Miasma Worm' — pipeline must extract malware indicators (file hashes, registry keys, C2 domains) from detailed threat analysis that should be in article but was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once article IOCs are properly extracted, hunt for Miasma network signatures, dropped file hashes, and command-and-control registrations. Create artifact-based alerts to catch re-infections or variant samples.

suggestion.title: Dependency Resolution Tampering During Build Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector implies malicious dependencies injected into AI agent tooling; detection must catch suspicious code execution during install phase before dependencies are used.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build pipelines (GitHub Actions runners, local CI/CD) for unexpected child processes spawned during package install phases (npm install, pip install, etc.); alert on network connections to non-standard hosts during dependency resolution.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Invalidly-Signed Package Update Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagates via supply chain; malicious packages likely lack or spoof legitimate code signatures. Pipeline must surface signing anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package updates lacking GPG/RSA signatures or bearing signatures of newly-created keys; flag mismatches between package manifest and registry checksums; correlate with downloads from affected repositories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious durabletask Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised.' Supply chain attacks are detected by flagging installation of known-malicious package versions. Pipeline generated zero use cases for package repository or installer activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install, conda install, or direct import statements targeting 'durabletask' package, especially from non-standard PyPI mirrors or unusual version numbers. Correlate with timestamp of public advisory release.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process from Python After Package Import
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package payload executes during import/initialization. Article states 'compromised'—this implies malicious code execution, but pipeline generated no execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process python.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, or cmd /c within seconds of durabletask import. Flag if child processes access unusual registry hives, network resources, or temp file staging areas.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Activity from Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks establish C2 or exfiltration channels. Article implies payload delivery but pipeline surfaced zero command-and-control or exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) or DNS requests from python.exe to domains not in organizational whitelist, within 24 hours of durabletask installation. Correlate with process command line and file system modifications to user home directory or temp paths.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages commonly exfiltrate credentials, SSH keys, or environment secrets during initialization. No credential-access-phase use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe accessing ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, %APPDATA%\SSH, or credential stores following durabletask import. Alert if those files are subsequently read, compressed, or transmitted.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Python Site-Packages Modification
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain payloads may write additional files to site-packages or import hooks for persistent execution. Pipeline generated no persistence-phase detections despite malicious package context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file writes to Python site-packages directory, __pycache__, or .pth files following durabletask installation. Alert if modifications occur outside of package manager or legitimate deployment tooling.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning or Dependency Enumeration Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages often probe environment for additional targets or dependencies to pivot. Pipeline generated zero discovery-phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe enumerating installed packages (pip list, import sys; print(sys.path)), reading requirements.txt, or scanning for other package metadata within seconds of durabletask import.

suggestion.title: Cron Job Creation in Hidden Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes.' Direct persistence mechanism in /tmp/.sys and similar hidden paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cron job creation or crontab modification referencing hidden directories (/tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys) or suspicious 15-minute interval execution. Monitor cron spawning binaries from atypical paths.

suggestion.title: Shell Startup File Persistence Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'shell startup files are modified to enable automatic execution.' Classic persistence vector via .bashrc, .profile, .bash_login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to shell startup files (.bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile, /etc/profile.d/*) appending executable references or binary paths, particularly those pointing to hidden directories or temporary locations.

suggestion.title: Rival Malware Process Termination and Persistence Removal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients...terminates them...by deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms, including cron jobs, init scripts.' Distinctive defensive behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pattern of rapid multi-process terminations (kill -9) followed by systematic binary deletion from system paths and persistence mechanism removal (cron job deletion, script removal, init.d deletion) within short time window.

suggestion.title: Hidden Binary Deployment to /tmp/.sys
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'copies itself to hidden locations such as /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, and /dev/shm/.sys, and then creates cron jobs that relaunch it.' File creation in world-writable directories with hidden naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation in /tmp/.sys, /var/tmp/.sys, /dev/shm/.sys paths. Correlate with process execution from these locations and immediate cron job creation or startup file modification.

suggestion.title: SSH/Telnet Brute Force with CPU Architecture Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials, detects the CPU architecture.' Indicates lateral movement scanner deploying architecture-specific payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed SSH/Telnet login attempts from single source across ports 22 and 23, followed by successful authentication and rapid execution of architecture detection commands (uname -m, arch, file).

suggestion.title: Python Network Scanner Deployment with Paramiko/Beautifulsoup4
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'downloads a Python script that installs additional packages such as requests, paramiko, and beautifulsoup4, which are required for network scanning and communication...over SSH and telnet protocols.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python process execution with pip install for paramiko/requests/beautifulsoup4 on production systems. Detect Python spawning SSH/Telnet connections to random internal/external IPs on ports 22, 23, and scan port list (7547, 8080, 8443, 8888).

suggestion.title: Linux cgroups v1 release_agent privilege escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2022-0492 affects 'cgroups v1 release_agent feature' and is 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks'; pipeline generated zero use cases for the specific exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or file writes targeting /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent paths, particularly from unprivileged contexts. Correlate with subsequent privilege escalation (UID/GID transitions to root or capability elevation) to identify successful exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Unexpected root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability acquisition following cgroup manipulation
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 improper authentication in cgroups allows attackers to escalate; look for capability or privilege transitions that lack corresponding legitimate setuid/sudo/init patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify effective UID transitions from non-root to UID 0 or acquisition of capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE) without intervening sudo/su/setuid binaries. Flag if preceded by cgroups-related system calls or file modifications within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Rapid Password Reset Attempts on High-Value Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'critical logic bug in Instagram's web-based password reset flow' exposing 'high-profile individuals such as Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and model Georgina Rodriguez.' Attackers could enumerate or brute-force reset endpoints targeting known VIP accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >5 failed or successful password reset attempts against the same account within a 10-minute window, especially for flagged high-value users. Monitor password reset endpoint POST requests from sources with mismatched geolocation or tor/proxy networks.

suggestion.title: Unredacted PII Exposure in Password Reset Response
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers' via password reset flow. Attackers trigger resets and parse response for contact info.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP responses from password reset endpoints (*/forgot*, */reset*, */recovery*) containing plaintext email or phone patterns (regex: \b[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\b or \+?1?\d{9,15}). Baseline by endpoint and alert on deviations from expected PII masking/redaction.

suggestion.title: Account Enumeration via Password Reset Logic
suggestion.rationale: Logic bugs in password resets often leak whether an account exists. Article notes 'critical logic bug' allowed access to sensitive fields—likely exploitable for enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor differential responses from password reset endpoints: HTTP 200 + PII vs. HTTP 404 or generic error. Correlate with bulk username/email list submissions. Alert on patterns consistent with credential-stuffing or account-enumeration campaigns.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Domain Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names phishing domain patterns: '<organization>-itdesk[.]com', '<organization>-it[.]com', '<organization>-helpdesk[.]com' impersonating internal IT portals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS/web requests to domains matching *-itdesk.com, *-it.com, *-helpdesk.com patterns, especially newly registered or with unfamiliar IP resolutions. Correlate with phishing email alerts mentioning invoice/IT themes from consumer email accounts.

suggestion.title: RMM Tool Installation Post-Remote Support Session
suggestion.rationale: Article details workflow: 'convinces employees to join remote support sessions via Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Quick Assist' then 'trick the target into installing remote monitoring and management tools such as AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation of AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps processes within 2 hours of Teams/Zoom/QuickAssist activity from non-IT personnel. Flag unusual Teams/Zoom sessions initiated by external callers or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk Access to Legal/Financial Sensitive Documents
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'search for sensitive legal and financial documents, including contracts, tax records, Social Security numbers, and merger or acquisition files' from document repos and cloud storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >15 file opens in <5 minutes matching keywords: contract, NDA, merger, acquisition, tax, SSN, confidential from endpoints post-RMM install. Flag unusual user/system context or non-business hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via WinSCP or Rclone
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names exfiltration tools: 'exfiltrating the data using tools such as WinSCP or Rclone'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinSCP.exe or Rclone process creation with suspicious arguments (non-standard remote hosts, bulk operations). Monitor outbound SFTP/SSH connections from endpoints running these tools. Correlate with prior bulk document access.

suggestion.title: Privnote Self-Destructing Message Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'use privnote[.]com, a self-destructing messaging service, to share installation links and commands with targets during remote support sessions' to evade forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections to privnote.com/.io from non-security endpoints. Prioritize hits during or within 1 hour of Teams/Zoom/QuickAssist activity or RMM installation attempts.

suggestion.title: Invoice-Themed Phishing Email from Consumer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attack precursor: 'invoice-themed phishing emails from consumer email accounts...do not contain malicious links or attachments and instead serve as a precursor for follow-up phone calls'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect invoicing/payment-themed emails from external consumer domains (gmail, yahoo, outlook) to finance/legal staff lacking file attachments but including callback phone numbers. Correlate with inbound calls to those numbers within 1 hour of email receipt.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Process Crash and Abnormal Termination Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — exploitation typically manifests as buffer-overflow induced crashes. Pipeline missed detection for FFmpeg process crashes and unusual exit codes correlated with media file processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ffmpeg.exe/ffmpeg process termination with exit codes 0xC0000374 (stack overflow) or 0xC0000409 (buffer overrun) within minutes of processing media from external source or email attachment. Cross-correlate with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Chrome Renderer Process Crash from Unpatched Version
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' — pipeline missed detection for exploitation of known Chrome vulnerabilities in unpatched versions through malicious web content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome version inventory against patch advisory. Detect chrome.exe renderer process crashes (status code 0x80004005 or similar) originating from untrusted domains/email links, especially if followed by unexpected code execution in parent process.

suggestion.title: Delivery of Malicious Media Files Targeting FFmpeg Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation requires weaponized delivery. Article states '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' with no immediate user mitigation — detection must focus on malicious file delivery prior to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery and execution of media files (mp4, mkv, webm, flv, mov) via email or phishing links, especially when recipient has previously opened media files through email. Monitor for file size anomalies and entropy patterns consistent with polyglot executables.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-FFmpeg Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies zero-day exploitation could lead to code execution and privilege escalation. Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation and lateral movement post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of SYSTEM/ADMIN-level processes spawned from FFmpeg or media-player contexts. Detect creation of scheduled tasks, services, or registry run-keys from compromised media-processing threads. Alert on unexpected network connections from media services.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Fingerprinting for FFmpeg/Chrome Post-Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses zero-day count; attackers immediately scan for vulnerable versions. Pipeline missed detection for application version enumeration and fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of software inventory tools (wmic.exe, powershell get-itemProperty for Software\Microsoft, etc.) following suspicious process activity. Detect HTTP requests with headers probing for User-Agent/version info on FFmpeg or Chrome.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Actively Exploited'—no use case generated to detect inbound exploitation attempts despite this being the primary attack vector. Should monitor for crafted requests triggering the underlying DoS mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U listening ports (typically 22/TCP for SFTP, custom SSH-like ports) for anomalous request patterns—payloads, sequence violations, or oversized frames characteristic of DoS/buffer-overflow exploits. Correlate with internal Serv-U error logs (authentication failures, crashes, resource exhaustion).

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Availability Degradation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies 'DoS Flaw'—post-exploitation impact (service unavailability, connection resets, latency spikes) should be detectable. Pipeline missed the impact phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Serv-U process behavior (CPU, memory, thread count, network connections) and surface sudden spikes, crashes, or listen-socket closures. Detect elevated ICMP/TCP RST responses from Serv-U endpoints within minutes of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Scanning & Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation campaigns typically begin with reconnaissance. Article does not specify but standard threat behavior warrants detection of port scans, banner grabbing, or version detection queries against Serv-U endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid multi-port probes (22, 990, 991, custom ranges) to internal Serv-U hosts; flag connections that issue SSH version queries without legitimate client signatures; flag failed connection sequences consistent with port scanning.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Catalog Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article references CISA KEV catalog addition—pipeline should have extracted the CVE identifier(s) and cross-walked against internal asset inventory to identify at-risk hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CISA KEV feed; extract CVE(s) tied to SolarWinds Serv-U; query CMDB and endpoint telemetry for matching product/version; alert on any inbound connection to identified affected instances from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited' and 'no patch available'—defenders must detect exploitation rather than rely on patching. Zero use cases generated despite this explicit threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints for exploit patterns: malformed parameters, authentication bypass attempts, or CVE-specific payload signatures. Baseline administrative request volume and URI patterns; flag spike in 4xx/5xx responses or unusual query structures.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Suspicious Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: CVE may enable unauthenticated or low-privilege access to administrative functions. Article context ('actively exploited') implies attackers are achieving meaningful post-exploitation outcomes, not just crashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco SD-WAN Manager immediately following (within 5 minutes) exploit-pattern HTTP requests. Flag role-elevation events (user to admin) from accounts with no prior privilege history.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Network Policy Modification
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SD-WAN Manager (which controls enterprise routing/segmentation) could be weaponized for lateral movement or exfiltration. Article emphasizes active exploitation; attacker goals likely include network persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor configuration change logs for policy edits outside change-control windows, especially VPN/routing policy or access-control rule modifications. Correlate with authentication anomalies or exploit timeframe.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Data Exfiltration via Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of a network hub device (SD-WAN Manager) could enable bulk exfiltration through trusted network infrastructure, bypassing perimeter controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline egress traffic from SD-WAN Manager to external networks. Alert on spike in outbound data volume, new external destinations, or connections to non-standard ports post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro - HTTP POST with PHP Code Injection Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement.' This is the initial exploitation vector and directly observable in HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints (Complex Calculation field) containing payloads matching pattern: single quote followed by PHP keywords (wp_insert_user, eval, system, passthru) and trailing // comment marker. Filter for unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin User Creation with Suspicious Username
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PHP statement that calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account with the username diksimarina.' Persistence mechanism directly logged in WordPress database and recommended for log review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_users table for new INSERT operations creating users with administrator role, specifically username 'diksimarina' or pattern-matching suspicious account names. Correlate creation timestamp with HTTP access logs to identify malicious form submission trigger.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests from Known Everest Forms Attacker IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26, and recommends defenders block them.' Wordfence-attributed source IPs for 29,300+ blocking events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement IP-based blocking and alert on any HTTP traffic from 202.56.2[.]126 or 209.146.60.26 to Everest Forms Pro endpoints. Monitor for both initial reconnaissance (HEAD/OPTIONS requests) and exploitation attempts (malicious POST payloads).

suggestion.title: Wordfence Security Event - CVE-2026-3300 Blocked
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Telemetry data from Wordfence firewall and malware scanner for WordPress shows that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild.' Indicates active WAF detection rule is tuned and measurable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Wordfence firewall blocks and malware scanner detections for CVE-2026-3300 payloads. Escalate on bypass attempts using encoding/obfuscation variants around the single-quote injection technique or wp_insert_user call.

suggestion.title: Admin User Added to WordPress Site Within Seconds of Form Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When the form is processed, and the calculation is evaluated, the injected PHP code is executed, and the malicious administrator account is created.' Tight time correlation between HTTP request and database mutation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints with new user insertion into wp_users table occurring <5 seconds later. Flag if new user has administrator role and creation follows suspicious form payload pattern.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Free App Installation on Smart TV Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs'—identifies initial-access vector via app distribution. Pipeline missed entire initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of unsigned or newly-published apps on Smart TV platforms (Android TV, WebOS, Tizen) with excessive network permissions. Alert on rapid rollout of apps with typosquatted names mimicking legitimate titles. Cross-reference app hashes against known compromised app stores.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Web Scraping Traffic from Smart TV Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'web-scraping proxies'—pipeline missed collection-phase detection. No use case for detecting large-scale HTTP request patterns from TV infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTP request volume per TV device. Alert on sustained anomalies: high concurrency, requests to data-rich targets (news sites, job boards, code repositories), rapid User-Agent cycling, or robots.txt probing patterns. Correlate multiple TV IPs targeting same destinations.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Behavior Originating from IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates TVs serve as 'proxies for AI'—requests originate from consumer residential IPs. Pipeline did not surface exfiltration or C2 communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS tunnels or proxy protocol traffic (SOCKS, HTTP CONNECT) from Smart TV device IPs. Flag rapid connection cycling to different external hosts, low-entropy payloads, or consistent beaconing intervals. Cross-reference residential ISP ranges exhibiting proxy-like behavior.

suggestion.title: App-Level Persistence and Anti-Tamper Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article notes apps act 'quietly'—implies covert persistence and resistance to removal. Pipeline did not map persistence phase or uninstall-protection detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for apps that re-install after user deletion, spawn hidden system daemons, or register with system-level permissions to block uninstall. Monitor for unsigned processes spawned from app containers. Detect auto-start behavior persisting across reboots.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing and Task Distribution to Botnet Smart TVs
suggestion.rationale: Web-scraping-as-a-service requires centralized C2 for task distribution and data aggregation. Pipeline extracted zero C2 indicators or beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify recurring outbound TCP/UDP connections from TV devices to infrastructure outside home/ISP gateways. Look for fixed-interval beaconing, encrypted tunnels, or consistent DNS queries to attacker-controlled domains. Correlate beacon timing across multiple compromised TV device IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TV to Home Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Smart TVs bridging residential networks may pivot to PCs, NAS, routers; article implies scale requiring multi-device compromise. Pipeline did not suggest lateral movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network reconnaissance (ARP scanning, port sweeping) from TV device IPs. Alert on successful SMB/SSH connections from TV to internal PCs. Detect unusual DNS requests from TV processes querying internal hostnames.

suggestion.title: Smart TV App Installation from First-Party Store
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku' and that they're 'quietly enrolling' devices. Need detection for unexpected app installs on TV platforms that then contact proxy infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartTV platforms for app installations from the built-in app stores. Correlate with subsequent network connections to proxy domains. Flag installs from less-known publishers or apps with permission requests for network access disproportionate to declared function.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Consent Dialog Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' This is defense evasion (T1036) — the payload hides user acknowledgment. Need detection for apps requesting network permissions through non-standard UI flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag applications that request network/proxy permissions but surface the consent dialog only through complex navigation sequences (e.g., requiring remote key combinations or scrolling past other dialogs). Baseline normal app permission UX and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTPS to Residential Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'commercial residential proxy network' used to 'scrape web data for AI training.' This is exfiltration (T1041, T1537) over encrypted channels. Need signatures for proxy request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SmartTV devices making outbound connections to known residential proxy providers (Luminati/Bright Data infrastructure). Look for high volume, repetitive GET requests to heterogeneous domains from a single TV source IP — indicative of proxy scraping rather than normal streaming/apps.

suggestion.title: SmartTV Device Anomalous Outbound Data Volume
suggestion.rationale: Devices are 'enrolled into a commercial residential proxy network' and used for continuous data scraping. Normal TV use involves streaming media, not bulk data exfiltration. Need behavioral baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline outbound data volume per SmartTV device model/user. Alert when a device exceeds baseline by 3+ standard deviations AND the traffic is directed to IP ranges associated with proxy infrastructure. Exclude firmware updates and large streaming downloads.

suggestion.title: Application Layer Protocol Tunneling via SmartTV
suggestion.rationale: Article leverages apps to tunnel requests through residential IPs. T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) is listed but no concrete hunt. Apps may masquerade as legitimate streaming/update traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP/HTTPS User-Agent headers and request patterns from SmartTV apps. Flag apps posing as browsers, bots, or legitimate services when their actual behavior is scraping or proxying. Cross-reference against Bright Data SDK signatures.

suggestion.title: Cross-Domain Data Collection from Compromised TV Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Devices are turned into proxies for 'scraping web data for AI training' across many target domains. Need detection for systematic enumeration/collection of third-party sites via a compromised SmartTV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SmartTV devices making requests to hundreds/thousands of unique domains in short time windows, with similar request patterns (identical User-Agent, headers, timing). This indicates proxy scraping rather than organic user browsing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Commits to Microsoft GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise of 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories via Miasma worm. Detection should identify malicious commits: new/suspicious author identities, out-of-hours commits, modifications to build/deployment files, commits from unusual geographies. Phrase: 'Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits by users outside baseline identity sets, commits with mismatched author/committer, or commits modifying .github/workflows, package.json, requirements.txt, or build configuration files. Correlate with VCS authentication logs for lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Injection via Compromised Repos
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack through GitHub implies malicious dependencies or code injection into downstream consumers. Monitor package manifests for newly-added or suspicious dependencies. Phrase: 'Supply Chain Attack'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new dependencies added in commits to Microsoft repos, especially those from newly-created package registry accounts or unfamiliar sources. Baseline and threshold on dependency churn per repo.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credential Compromise and API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 73 repos indicates stolen GitHub credentials or PATs. Detect account takeover signals: rapid repository modifications, PAT/SSH key creation, protection rule changes. Phrase: 'Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories in Major'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag users making bulk modifications across unrelated repositories in short timeframes, or accounts with newly-created PATs/SSH keys followed immediately by repository changes. Alert on disabling branch protection or adding untrusted collaborators.

suggestion.title: Worm Execution on Developer Machines Post-Clone
suggestion.rationale: Named 'Miasma Worm' suggests self-propagating malware. Detect when cloning/syncing a repository is followed by suspicious process execution from the repository working directory. Phrase: 'Miasma Worm'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of scripts or binaries from inside cloned repository directories (.git siblings, .github/workflows, build/ subdirs) shortly after git clone/pull. Flag unsigned or obfuscated code execution from repo contexts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Release Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious commits to Microsoft repos likely flow downstream as published packages or releases. Detect temporal correlation between suspicious commits and package versions. Phrase: 'Supply Chain Attack'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package releases published shortly after suspicious commits, or where package artifact hashes do not match corresponding source tree commits. Monitor for unexpected version bumps or out-of-cycle releases from compromised repos.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Metadata Tampering / Repository Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled after Supply Chain Attack'—indicates the worm compromised official GitHub Actions metadata or repository settings to propagate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub organizations for unexpected modifications to public action metadata, unexpected disabling of popular actions, or unexpected visibility changes to repositories. Alert on bulk repository setting changes within short time windows, particularly targeting widely-used actions and high-visibility repos.

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow Injection via AI Agent Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly 'targets AI coding agents'—suggests the worm exploited AI agent integration in GitHub Actions to generate and inject malicious workflows or code commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected commits authored by AI agents or bot accounts that modify workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml), install-run malicious package managers, or add suspicious environment variables. Correlate with unusual authentication tokens or API usage from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository Worm Propagation via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Named 'Miasma Worm' and disabled 72 repositories—indicates self-replicating payload propagating across repo boundaries, likely via cloned dependencies or shared action references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag identical or near-identical malicious code patterns appearing in commits across unrelated repositories within a short timeframe. Alert on unusual dependency injection into commonly-used packages, unexpected repository cloning from single source, or mass addition of external package dependencies.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Disabling / Mass Availability Impact
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '72 Other Repositories Disabled'—clear impact phase where the worm deleted, archived, or disabled access to multiple repositories at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk repository disabling, deletion, or archival events, especially when performed by unexpected service accounts or from unusual geographic locations. Correlate with unauthorized changes to organization roles or branch protection rules.

suggestion.title: Compromised Upstream Package / Action Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack targeting 'AI Coding Agents' suggests poisoned package versions or action versions were distributed; pipeline should have catalogued the specific version(s) of Azure Functions Action that were compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected version bumps or yanked versions of widely-used packages/actions. Cross-reference dependency lock files against known-compromised versions. Alert on environments pulling from unusual package mirror sources or using pre-release versions of popular actions.

suggestion.title: Compromised PyPI Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised' — core attack vector of installing malicious package. Pipeline extracted zero detection for package compromise, the primary infection mechanism in supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip/poetry install processes for 'durabletask' package or any install from PyPI with mismatched hash signatures. Monitor for installation of unexpected versions or from non-standard PyPI mirrors. Correlate pip operations with subsequent code execution from site-packages.

suggestion.title: Python Module Execution from Compromised Site-Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'supply chain attack' on package, implying malicious code execution through normal import mechanisms. No UC generated for detecting PyPI package code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget) with no corresponding user interaction. Alert on python.exe with suspicious -c or -m arguments executing code outside normal project directories.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Python Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks typically exfiltrate credentials or data. Article mentions 'compromised package' without detection for C2/exfiltration behavior that would follow infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-HTTP/HTTPS network connections initiated by Python.exe to external IPs. Alert on DNS queries from Python processes resolving suspicious domains. Baseline Python's normal outbound connectivity and alert on anomalies (unusual ports, frequencies, destinations).

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion and Version Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: PyPI supply-chain attacks often exploit version confusion. Article implies package compromise but no UC addresses malicious version substitution or downgrade attacks that persist across environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected downgrades of packages (pip install package==older_version) or conflicting versions installed in same environment. Monitor for .pth files or __pycache__ modifications in site-packages pointing to attacker-controlled paths.

suggestion.title: Malicious Entry Point in Python Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Compromised PyPI packages may inject code via setup.py, __init__.py, or entry_points. Article states package is 'compromised' but no UC detects malicious initialization code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to .pth files or entry_points configurations in site-packages. Alert on __init__.py files with obfuscated code, network connections, or subprocess spawning within package initialization. Baseline package installation signatures against official PyPI artifacts.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2021-27137 DD-WRT Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states C0XMO is 'delivered by exploiting CVE-2021-27137, a buffer overflow vulnerability caused by insufficient user input' that 'can be leveraged without authentication and leads to executing arbitrary code.' This is the primary initial access vector and should trigger alerts on unusual HTTP requests to DD-WRT management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT router management endpoints for requests with malformed buffer overflow payloads or high-entropy POST data. Look for HTTP 400/500 responses followed by suspicious process execution. Correlate failed HTTP requests with subsequent shell command execution or binary downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect SSH/Telnet Brute-Force from Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the botnet 'downloads a Python script' that 'attempts to brute-force weak Telnet and SSH credentials' and 'uses worker threads to randomly scan internet-facing systems on common ports like 22 (SSH), 23 (Telnet).' This lateral movement vector should be detectable via failed login storms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid SSH/Telnet login failures (>10 failures per minute per source IP) from non-admin networks. Correlate failed attempts with successful logins within 60 seconds. Cross-reference source IPs against known IoT device subnets and DD-WRT admin networks.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Persistence via Cron Job Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'creates cron jobs that relaunch it every 15 minutes' and the malware 'copies itself to hidden locations such as '/tmp/.sys', '/var/tmp/.sys', and '/dev/shm/.sys'.' Regular cron jobs for newly-placed binaries in /tmp are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crontab modification events and creation of cron entries. Alert on cron jobs referencing /tmp, /var/tmp, or /dev/shm directories, especially with intervals ≤15 minutes. Baseline legitimate system cron jobs and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Shell Startup Script Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'shell startup files are modified to enable automatic execution.' Modifications to .bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile, or similar files should be monitored for suspicious code injections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to shell initialization files in /home, /root, or other user directories. Flag modifications that append commands, set environment variables pointing to /tmp, or invoke binaries from unusual locations. Baseline legitimate administrative changes.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Termination of Competing Malware and Security Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article details C0XMO 'actively scans running processes to identify competitor botnet clients... red-team tools, programming tools, and network services that may interfere with its operation, and terminates them. It does so by deleting binaries and removing their persistence mechanisms.' Mass process kills or selective tool termination is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid process termination events, especially of known security tools, remote-access tools, or competing malware (Mirai, Qbot, etc.). Alert on process kill followed by file deletion of the same binary. Flag patterns where the terminating process is non-standard (e.g., shell script, Python interpreter).

suggestion.title: Detect Network Scanning on High-Risk Port Set
suggestion.rationale: Article states the Python scanner 'scans internet-facing systems on common ports like 22 (SSH), 23 (Telnet), 80/443 (HTTP/HTTPS), 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888, and others.' This distinctive port combination (Telnet + HTTP variants + 7547 UPnP) is characteristic of IoT botnet reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on systematic connection attempts from a single source to the port set {22, 23, 80, 443, 7547, 8080, 8443, 8888} across multiple targets in short time windows. Correlate with failed SSH/Telnet logins. Flag if source is a previously-compromised IoT device (residential IP, router, NVR).

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Modification by Unprivileged Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'affects Linux systems using the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' and is 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks.' Modification of release_agent is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern originating from unprivileged processes (UID > 0). Flag sequences where cgroup file modification precedes privilege elevation or command execution.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Elevation via Cgroup Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2022-0492 'may allow attackers' to escalate—attack pattern involves unprivileged user gaining elevated execution context through cgroup features.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when unprivileged process (UID > 0) spawns child with elevated EUID or capabilities, especially when preceded by cgroup syscalls (cgroup2_mkdir, open/write to cgroup control files) or release_agent path modifications.

suggestion.title: Kernel Privilege Escalation Exploitation Signature — CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes active real-world exploitation; behavioral signatures must supplement asset exposure. Kernel-level cgroup interaction pattern is the tactical indicator of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal kernel interaction sequences: rapid cgroup control file creation/writes by unprivileged user, cgroup2_mkdir syscalls, then openat/write to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent, followed by process execution with privilege transition. Correlate timing between file modification and elevated process spawn.

suggestion.title: Credential Exposure – High-Profile Account PII Leakage Post-Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw 'exposed unredacted email addresses and phone numbers' for accounts including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Exposed contact info creates immediate phishing and account-takeover surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk email/phone pairings from Instagram user accounts appearing in credential paste sites, dark web markets, and OSINT leaks within 48 hours post-disclosure (June 6–7). Cross-reference exposed addresses with corporate directories of high-profile targets.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaigns – Spearphishing High-Profile Users with Exposed Contact Info
suggestion.rationale: Disclosed user emails and phone numbers (Mark Zuckerberg, Georgina Rodriguez named) are prime targets for follow-on phishing/smishing. Article confirms access to sensitive contact metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails impersonating Instagram/Meta targeting disclosed email addresses. Watch for SMS phishing to exposed phone numbers. Flag newly registered domains/phishing infrastructure created June 6–7 with keyword patterns targeting 'Instagram reset' or 'account verification.'

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Credential Stuffing – Exposed Contact Details Enable Reset Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Exposed email/phone pairs directly enable password-reset abuse and account takeover. No authentication bypass needed if attacker possesses valid account email/phone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spike in failed Instagram login attempts using known-exposed email/phone combinations. Flag successful authentications from new geolocations or devices for disclosed high-profile accounts within 24–72 hours post-disclosure. Monitor for password-reset request anomalies.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing + Remote Support Tool Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers send 'invoice-themed phishing emails from consumer email accounts' containing 'no malicious links or attachments' and instead serve as 'precursor for follow-up phone calls' leading to 'remote support sessions' and installation of 'AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, or SuperOps'. Clear execution chain warranting detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for consumer email account senders (domains outside corporate whitelist) followed within 12 hours by network connections to known RMM tool C2 servers (AnyDesk, Zoho Assist, Bomgar, SuperOps). Correlate phishing recipients with subsequent RMM binary execution.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Pattern: Impersonated IT Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers register domains following patterns '<organization>-itdesk[.]com', '<organization>-it[.]com', '<organization>-helpdesk[.]com' to impersonate internal IT portals. These are structural IoCs indicating preparatory reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and URL visits to domains matching pattern '*-itdesk.com', '*-it.com', '*-helpdesk.com' from external sources. Alert on SSL certificate registrations for these patterns within 5 days of known Silent Ransom targets.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via WinSCP and Rclone
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers commonly target document management platforms and cloud storage repositories before exfiltrating the data using tools such as WinSCP or Rclone'. Clear exfiltration vector with named tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of winscp.exe, rclone.exe, or related binaries on systems without prior patch/deployment records. Alert on establishment of SFTP/SCP connections from office networks to external cloud storage providers. Track bulk document downloads from SharePoint/Teams preceding exfil tool execution.

suggestion.title: Privnote Self-Destructing Message Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'use privnote[.]com, a self-destructing messaging service, to share installation links and commands with targets during remote support sessions' specifically 'to reduce forensic artifacts'. Named infrastructure used for C2 obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on all traffic to privnote[.]com from office networks. Monitor email bodies and Teams messages for privnote.com links. Flag employees receiving privnote links during hours matching remote support session timeframes (outside business hours).

suggestion.title: Fast-Flux Leak Site Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'business-data-leaks[.]com' leak site and notes attackers use 'residential proxy networks spread across Latin America, Eastern Europe, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Asia' to hide infrastructure. Named leak domain requires blocking/monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist for business-data-leaks[.]com and related Resecurity-identified infrastructure. Monitor DNS resolution patterns for rapid IP address changes indicative of fast-flux. Alert if any internal user accesses known Silent Ransom leak domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk Sensitive Document Access from Remote Support Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers who 'search for sensitive legal and financial documents, including contracts, tax records, Social Security numbers, and merger or acquisition files' from 'document management platforms and cloud storage repositories' following remote support session establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal bulk access patterns to SharePoint document libraries, Teams file storage, or OneDrive occurring within 30 minutes of RMM tool installation or Quick Assist/Terminal Services session. Alert on access to folders tagged as containing M&A plans, tax documents, or SSN data by accounts with no prior access history.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Process Crash or Memory Corruption via Malicious File Input
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg'—these are almost certainly exploited via crafted media files passed to the ffmpeg binary. Pipeline should detect abnormal termination or crash patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ffmpeg.exe processes spawned with file arguments pointing to unusual or recently-created media files, followed by access violations or segmentation faults. Alert on ffmpeg crash loops or execution timeouts within seconds of launch.

suggestion.title: Chrome Renderer Process Crash or Privilege Escalation Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'—likely includes memory safety issues (use-after-free, buffer overflow). Detection should capture exploitation attempts before patches are deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for chrome.exe or chromium processes with abnormal child processes spawned (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) immediately following a renderer process crash. Also monitor for unexpected elevation attempts from chrome's sandboxed renderer context.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Delivery via Compromised or Malicious Media Server
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploit delivery mechanisms for FFmpeg would typically involve hosting malicious media files on attacker infrastructure. Article mentions AI agent 'uncovered' vulnerabilities, implying active exploitation research.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of media files (.mkv, .mp4, .flv, .mov) from suspicious or newly-registered domains, followed by immediate ffmpeg processing. Correlate with process crashes or high CPU/memory spikes in ffmpeg child processes.

suggestion.title: Automated Vulnerability Research Tool Execution and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly attributes discovery to 'AI Agent'—this suggests automated fuzzing, symbolic execution, or corpus-based testing framework activity. Should detect such tools and their output staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of fuzzing frameworks (libFuzzer, AFL, honggfuzz), symbolic execution engines (KLEE, Triton), or security research tools (IDA, Ghidra, radare2) spawning abnormally high numbers of child processes or file I/O operations. Alert on bulk exfiltration of crash dumps or proof-of-concept payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE or Vulnerability ID Intelligence Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article references '21 Zero-Days' and '429 Bugs' by count, not CVE identifier. Pipeline should have either flagged missing CVE data or generated generic vulnerability monitoring rules pending CVE publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create provisional use-case rules for 'unpatched FFmpeg version X.Y execution on user endpoint' and 'unpatched Chrome version X execution', pending release of official CVE numbers. Use file version signatures or process memory signatures to identify vulnerable binaries in real-time.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'DoS Flaw'—denial-of-service inherently manifests as process termination, hang, or restart cycles. No impact-phase detection was generated despite this being the primary attack observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process (srvagent.exe, FileAgent.exe) for unplanned termination or rapid restart cycles outside maintenance windows. Baseline expected uptime per environment and alert when restarts exceed threshold (e.g., >3 restarts per 10 minutes).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Traffic to Serv-U Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited'—exploitation requires network delivery mechanism. No network-layer indicators or traffic anomaly detections generated despite this being observable at packet level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound traffic spikes or malformed packets to Serv-U listening ports (typically FTP 21, SSH 22). Flag traffic from multiple sources with high request velocity or packet patterns consistent with DoS payloads.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SolarWinds Serv-U Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entries are version-specific. Article title implies a known, documented vulnerability affecting specific Serv-U builds, but no asset inventory or version-matching IOCs were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset query: identify Serv-U installations with version strings matching CISA KEV affected-version ranges. Cross-reference against SolarWinds patch advisories and alert on unpatched instances in production.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states the CVE is 'actively exploited'; this is the core IOC the pipeline missed entirely. Any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployment becomes a detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager admin interfaces with patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20245 exploitation (malformed parameters, known payload signatures, or unexpected API calls from non-authenticated sources). Correlate with administrative access logs to identify successful compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Reconnaissance and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'active exploitation' implying attacker reconnaissance phase; no UC generated for probing or enumeration of vulnerable systems prior to exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning behavior targeting SD-WAN Manager ports and endpoints: version detection probes, admin panel requests to non-existent paths, or repeated failed authentication attempts consistent with fingerprinting.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of a management plane device (SD-WAN Manager) would pivot into internal networks; pipeline did not suggest lateral movement detection despite 'no patch available' language implying persistent compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for internal network connections, file transfers, and command execution originating from the SD-WAN Manager host post-compromise, particularly to non-adjacent network segments or high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro PHP eval() Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'sanitize_text_field() function, which does not escape single quotes (\') or other characters that influence PHP syntax' allowing 'close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code.' This is the core vulnerability mechanism and requires detection of malformed form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Everest Forms calculation form submissions for quote characters, PHP syntax tokens (=, $, ;, //, #), or payloads containing wp_insert_user(). Alert on POST requests to form endpoints containing semicolons or comment markers followed by PHP keywords.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Form Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'call wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account.' Legitimate admin creation occurs through WordPress admin UI, not form calculation logic. Direct detection opportunity for persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_insert_user() function calls originating from form processing code (wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro/). Alert on new user creation with administrator role immediately following form submission, especially with suspicious usernames.
