suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect token theft/replay by correlating sign-in locations, user agents, and device tokens. Flag when same user authenticates from geographically impossible locations within 10 minutes or uses valid tokens from unexpected device contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Tool Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors using AI brand names as social engineering vector implies credential abuse against legitimate AI service accounts. Zero use cases generated for account compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed login attempts against accounts with AI brand names in email/display name. Alert on new API keys generated for AI service accounts, especially if followed by data export or unusual API call patterns.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Email with AI Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering.' Pipeline failed to generate email-based detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with subject lines or sender addresses impersonating AI vendors. Flag emails with urgency language ('verify AI account', 'confirm subscription') linking to newly registered or lookalike domains. High-fidelity: external emails bypassing authentication checks.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume.' Implies detection for inbox-wide surge in phishing emails, likely using ML-generated variations that evade signature detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk increases in emails with phishing indicators (malicious URLs, suspicious sender TLDs, lookalike domains) over a 1-hour window. Aggregate by recipient domain. Baseline against historical volume and adjust thresholds by business unit to account for expected campaign spikes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email URL/Attachment Sandbox Detonation
suggestion.rationale: AI-generated phishing attacks likely use obfuscated or polymorphic payloads to evade static rules. Article mentions 'reducing Tier 1 overload,' implying need for automated payload analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Route flagged phishing emails to sandbox for detonation. Alert on behavioral indicators (network C2 callbacks, persistence mechanisms, credential harvesting) rather than exact malware signatures. Correlate sandbox verdicts with email metadata to suppress FP alerts from known-benign URLs in context of low-risk senders.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Sender Reputation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article notes SOC overload from AI-generated variants. Detection should prioritize **sender behavior shifts**—newly-compromised or spoofed internal accounts sending phishing at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag user accounts with sudden spike in outbound emails containing phishing indicators (malicious URLs, attachment-heavy, external recipient surge). Suppress alerts for known mail-merge tools and distribution list activity. Cross-check against account compromise signals (password resets, MFA changes, non-standard sign-in locations) to escalate internally-sourced phishing.

suggestion.title: Alert Correlation for Phishing Campaign Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload.' Detection should group related phishing attempts into campaigns to reduce alert fatigue and surface attacker intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster emails by sender spoofing pattern, domain similarity (Levenshtein distance to legitimate targets), URL domain registration date, and payload hash. Emit one high-confidence 'campaign detected' alert per cluster with incident context rather than N individual email alerts. Threshold: ≥5 related attempts within 4 hours.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass via IKEv1 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-50751 allows 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication' on VPN deployments using 'deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol.' This is the primary attack vector and requires dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful VPN session establishment without prior credential validation or authentication exchange completion. Monitor Check Point VPN gateway logs for IKEv1 handshake completion without corresponding authentication module logs, or login events where authentication_result=bypass/unauthenticated.

suggestion.title: Legacy IKEv1 Protocol Deployment Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires systems 'configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and accepting 'legacy Remote Access clients.' Configuration audit is a critical control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any IKEv1 protocol negotiation in VPN gateway logs. Query VPN appliance configuration for IKEv1 acceptance settings; correlate with absence of 'IKEv2 only' enforcement cited in mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Breach Ransomware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware' following VPN access, requiring detection of encryption execution immediately after successful VPN compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ransomware-pattern process execution (encryption libraries, high I/O thread counts, system32 manipulation) within 1-6 hours of external VPN session establishment. Monitor for child processes spawned from VPN gateway services or from newly-created privileged accounts used post-breach.

suggestion.title: MITM Attack Detection on Site-to-Site VPN via CVE-2026-50752
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-50752 'affects certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange' and 'can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' Article notes no observed exploitation yet but warrants proactive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site IKEv1 VPN tunnels for certificate validation errors, certificate issuer/subject mismatches during tunnel negotiation, or repeated IKEv1 handshake failures followed by success (MITM interception patterns).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Account Creation Post-VPN Breach
suggestion.rationale: Qilin's 'post-compromise activity' following VPN access implies persistence and lateral movement mechanics typically involving new account creation for C2 access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new local or domain account creation within 2 hours of external VPN session from non-corporate IP. Flag accounts added to administrative groups (Administrators, Domain Admins) within this window as high-priority.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via VPN Tunnel Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Qilin described as RaaS operation claiming ~400 victims on 'dark web leak site,' indicating exfiltration before encryption. Article victims include high-profile orgs (Nissan, Lee Enterprises, Synnovis), implying data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual volume exfiltration through VPN tunnels: bulk archive creation/transfer, database dumps, or multi-GB transfers to non-corporate destinations within VPN session scope. Correlate with file access patterns to sensitive data stores (databases, file shares).

suggestion.title: LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 Patch Status Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and 'worth one quick check across your fleet... Federal due-date [2026-06-22]'. No scanner-based detection generated despite explicit recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag LiteLLM deployments (any version, any OS) via asset inventory or vulnerability scanner. Correlate unpatched instances against CVE-2026-42271 advisory; prioritize alert severity if running version < fixed baseline and public-facing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from LiteLLM Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'run arbitrary commands on the host' is core attack outcome (T1059). Pipeline failed to generate any execution-phase detection despite explicit command-injection language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by LiteLLM parent process (litellm service, python -m litellm, node-based LiteLLM, or gunicorn/uvicorn running LiteLLM app). Flag unusual shells, script interpreters, system utilities, or network tools (curl, nc, whoami, env, ifconfig) with high confidence if command line contains shell metacharacters or base64.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Exploiting LiteLLM via Valid Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'holders of low-privilege internal-user keys... to run arbitrary commands'. Describes authenticated exploitation path (T1078 + T1059) not extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate low-privilege account login/API authentication to LiteLLM with subsequent requests containing command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters, ${}, backticks, pipe/semicolon sequences). Cross-correlate with process execution anomalies from LiteLLM runtime spawning unexpected children.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed LiteLLM Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited'. Pipeline omitted network-discovery and exposure-based detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all LiteLLM endpoints reachable from internet (non-RFC1918 sources or public DNS). Cross-check against asset inventory; flag instances without IP allowlist, authentication gateway, or WAF protection. Prioritize if unpatched for CVE-2026-42271 or deployed after 2026-06-22 deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE substituted. CISA KEV status means active exploitation in the wild; federal agencies must remediate by 2026-06-11.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and network telemetry to identify Check Point Security Gateway instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-50751. Cross-reference patch inventory to detect remediation lag between CISA KEV publication and actual patching.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange that could allow unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication.' Detect unauthenticated IKEv1 negotiations establishing VPN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 phase-1 negotiations for absent or invalid credential validation, then reaching phase-2 without authentication. Flag external-sourced initiations establishing tunnels without corresponding authentication logs.

suggestion.title: VPN Connections Without Valid Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password,' indicating credential-bypass sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN connection logs with authentication logs. Flag remote VPN sessions where tunnel establishment precedes or lacks corresponding credential validation events, or where failed/absent authentication logs precede successful tunnel creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Remote IKEv1 Initiations
suggestion.rationale: Threat profile states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication.' Actor initiates IKEv1 without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound IKEv1 (UDP 500) to Check Point instances. Baseline expected IKEv1 initiators; flag non-whitelisted external sources, especially if followed by successful tunnel creation without user authentication.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance: CVE-2026-50751 Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-11.' Federal agencies are required to remediate by deadline and will be audited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate Check Point Security Gateway fleet patches applied before 2026-06-11. Query patch inventory, firmware version, and configuration management to confirm remediation across all exposed instances pre-deadline.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'By crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization, attackers can bypass authentication.' This is the initial attack vector enabling access to otherwise protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to UniFi OS containing '/api/auth/validate-sso/' with path traversal sequences or URI encoding variations. Monitor for requests to authentication-exempt paths followed by subsequent access to normally-protected internal APIs on UniFi OS versions ≤5.0.6.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Unauthenticated Package Update Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates: 'Once inside, the attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.' The endpoint 'ucs/update/latest_package' is explicitly vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package' endpoint on UniFi OS servers running versions ≤5.0.6. Correlate with shell metacharacters or command-injection payloads in request parameters.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Command Injection via Package Update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-34910 is a command injection flaw that can be exploited to execute commands on affected devices.' Injected commands execute under a privileged service account with passwordless sudo access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned under 'ucs-update' service context. Alert on shell spawning (sh, bash, /bin/sh) or suspicious system utility execution under this service, particularly with parameters suggesting command injection.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'The injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.' This converts service-level RCE to root access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo command execution from the 'ucs-update' service account on UniFi OS systems. Alert on passwordless sudo invocation or root-level command execution originating from UniFi OS service contexts that should not normally escalate privileges.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS File Exposure via Path Traversal (CVE-2026-34909)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'CVE-2026-34909 is a path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system.' This vulnerability is chained with CVE-2026-34908 to bypass authentication and reach the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests containing path-traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, ..%2f) targeting UniFi OS endpoints. Alert on directory traversal attempts combined with authentication-bypass patterns on UniFi OS ≤5.0.6.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Improper Access Control Enabling API Changes (CVE-2026-34908)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'CVE-2026-34908 is an improper access control flaw that can allow unauthorized changes to vulnerable systems.' Combined with CVE-2026-34909, this enables the authentication bypass chain to reach the command injection endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT/DELETE requests to UniFi OS configuration or API endpoints from non-authenticated sessions. Baseline legitimate admin API usage and alert on anomalies accessing sensitive endpoints on UniFi OS ≤5.0.6.

suggestion.title: Gogs User Account Creation Followed by Repository Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance.' Sequential user and repo creation by newly registered accounts is a primary exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Gogs instances where user account creation (POST /user/sign_up, status 200) is followed within minutes by first repository creation by that user (POST /repo/create). High-fidelity signal when rebase is enabled on first repo and no legitimate activity pattern matches (e.g., developer onboarding with supervisor review).

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Rebase Merge Configuration on Suspicious Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and 'the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' Rebase configuration is the exploitation trigger for argument injection in Merge().
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /repo/{owner}/{name}/settings/advanced enabling 'rebase_before_merge'. Correlate with repository creation age and user account age; flag repositories ≤2 hours old with rebase enabled by user account ≤2 hours old.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Gogs Git Merge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects a different code path (Merge())' enabling RCE: attackers can 'compromise the targeted server.' Exploitation spawns unexpected child processes from git merge context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by git.exe or git process (when invoked by Gogs service account) that are unexpected: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget, nc. Gogs normally runs git merge with output to logs; any external process invocation is high-fidelity RCE signal.

suggestion.title: Gogs Private Repository Access from New User Account
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attackers can 'access any repositories (including private ones)' and 'steal credentials' post-exploitation. Unusual repository enumeration or private-repo content access by accounts without explicit permissions is high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GET requests to /api/repos or file access (via .git/config, deploy keys, SSH keys) from newly created user accounts accessing repositories outside their ownership or explicit membership. Baseline: new accounts should only access repos they own or are explicitly added to within hours of account creation.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Content Modification via Merge Following Rebase Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers can 'alter any hosted source code.' Post-rebase exploitation results in unexpected commits or file modifications to application source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits or file modifications to repositories within 10 minutes of rebase-merge operations on those same repositories. Cross-check commit author against repository owner/maintainer list; if commit author is the account that triggered the rebase and is a newly registered user (≤24 hours old), escalate.

suggestion.title: Network Lateral Movement from Gogs Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'move laterally to other systems on the network' post-RCE. Unusual outbound network connections from Gogs service account or spawned child processes indicate lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections (TCP/UDP) initiated by child processes of Gogs git operations to non-standard ports or internal network ranges (RFC1918) that lack baseline approval. Baseline Gogs: primarily HTTP/HTTPS to external Git remotes and internal package repos; unusual SMB, RDP, SSH, or WinRM from Gogs context is RCE + lateral move indicator.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Phishing URL Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'WhatsApp Phishing Attack.' Phishing URLs are the primary delivery vector but zero IOCs were extracted. This is the attack's signature payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks to WhatsApp domain lookalikes (typosquatting, homoglyph variants), URL shortener redirects to phishing pages, and emails with spoofed WhatsApp Reply-To headers. Correlate email send timestamps with URL click spikes to identify campaign distribution windows.

suggestion.title: NSO-Attributed Phishing Infrastructure Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names NSO Group as the attacker, but pipeline output contains no threat-actor-attributed IOCs, no infrastructure reuse patterns from prior NSO campaigns (Pegasus, Candiru infrastructure), and no behavioral pivots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference phishing infrastructure (domains, IPs, SSL certs, WHOIS registrars) against historical NSO Group indicators from VirusTotal, Shodan, and prior Pegasus/Candiru campaigns. Flag WHOIS registrar reuse, hosting provider overlap, and certificate issuer patterns consistent with NSO's operational security posture.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Credential Theft Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks targeting messaging apps aim to steal credentials or session tokens. Article describes 'Phishing Attack' outcome but pipeline provided no credential-access detection logic for WhatsApp account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous logins to WhatsApp/Meta accounts post-phishing: logins from unexpected geographies, new device fingerprints, rapid password reset followed by login, or web login from atypical clients. Correlate email phishing click time against authentication spike timing.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Domain Impersonation at Registration Layer
suggestion.rationale: Meta 'Files Contempt Order' implies infrastructure was seized or identified in court filings. Phishing domains must be newly registered. Pipeline extracted zero domain IOCs despite this being forensically recoverable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt newly registered domains matching WhatsApp patterns (WHOIS delta <30 days, typosquatting, homoglyph variants). Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for SSL issuance to misspelled 'whatsapp' identifiers. Flag free/bulletproof hosting providers and suspicious registrars favored by phishing operations.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Email Header Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Phishing requires distribution vector. Article title alone does not specify email, but 'Phishing Attack' conventionally implies email; no sender headers, reply-to addresses, or message IDs were extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and cluster sender IP ranges, Reply-To domain mismatches (spoofed whatsapp.com), and message-id patterns across phishing emails. Flag emails with forged X-Originating-IP headers or spoofed Message-ID formats typical of bulk phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: IIS w3wp.exe Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cryptographically unique web shell framework' deployed on IIS servers. Pipeline missed persistence detection entirely. Web shells execute via w3wp.exe/aspnet_wp.exe with child process spawning to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe (or aspnet_wp.exe) spawning child processes with names: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe, ipconfig.exe, systeminfo.exe. Baseline normal application spawning; web shell activity shows cmd invocations from web service principal context. Correlate with creation of .aspx/.ash files in wwwroot.

suggestion.title: New .aspx / .ashx / .asmx Files in IIS Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions '.ashx' domain; article describes web shell framework. File creation in c:\inetpub\wwwroot or IIS virtual directories is the primary persistence mechanism for IIS web shells. Pipeline mapped zero persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt creation of .aspx, .ash, .asmx, .jsp, .php files in IIS directories (c:\inetpub\wwwroot, c:\inetpub\vhosts, wwwroot subdirs). Web shells uploaded via PUT requests or vulnerability exploitation. Correlate with HTTP PUT/POST requests in IIS logs from external sources immediately prior to file creation. Baseline legitimate deployments; alert on out-of-band file creation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated / Base64-Encoded Payloads in IIS HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'cryptographically unique' design to 'evade every detection method.' Pipeline missed T1027/T1140 (obfuscation/deobfuscation). Web shells receive base64-encoded or XOR-encoded commands in URL parameters or POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search IIS logs for HTTP request parameters (URL query strings, POST bodies) containing long base64 strings matching regex [A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}. Extract and attempt base64 decode, then scan decoded content for suspicious keywords: cmd, powershell, exec, system, invoke, script, certutil, bitsadmin. Alert on request/response pairs where decoded output matches command patterns.

suggestion.title: HTTP PUT / DELETE / WebDAV Requests to IIS from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes web shell deployment but pipeline generated no hunt for file upload mechanisms. IIS web shells are typically uploaded via HTTP PUT or WebDAV methods. Pipeline missed initial_access/persistence boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP PUT, DELETE, MOVE, MKCOL, PROPFIND from external/untrusted sources to IIS servers. These methods are unusual in typical web traffic and strongly indicate file upload/manipulation attempts. Correlate with source IPs from IOC list (43.160.202.246, 140.206.161.227, 124.156.129.151). Cross-reference with DeviceFileEvents for file creation 0-5 seconds after PUT request.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Scanning for IIS Vulnerabilities and Default Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states OP-512 is 'targeting Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers' but pipeline mapped zero initial_access techniques. Initial compromise requires vulnerability exploitation or default endpoint exposure. Pipeline missed T1190, T1046.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for high-volume requests to known IIS default endpoints: /admin, /iisadmin, /webdav, /web.config, /Global.asax, /.git, /web.config.backup, /.asp. Look for common scanner User-Agent strings (masscan, Nmap, WhatWeb, Shodan) or malformed/unusual HTTP requests. Correlate source IPs with later compromise activity (file creation, shell execution) on the same target within 24-48 hours.

suggestion.title: IIS w3wp.exe Spawning PowerShell with Encoded Commands
suggestion.rationale: Common web shell execution pattern: w3wp.exe → powershell.exe with base64-encoded -EncodedCommand flag. Combines T1071 (Application Layer Protocol), T1059.001 (PowerShell), and T1140 (deobfuscation). Pipeline detected only T1071.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe child process of w3wp.exe with -EncodedCommand parameter. Hunt for powershell.exe process command lines containing base64 strings (40+ character [A-Za-z0-9+/]* sequences). Extract and decode; alert if decoded output contains command keywords: iex, Invoke-Expression, .DownloadString, .DownloadFile, cmd.exe, net user.

suggestion.title: UC_CRYPTO_WALLET
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Targets...Crypto Wallets'; body identifies 7+ specific targets (Ethereum keystore, Bitcoin wallet.dat, MetaMask, Phantom, Exodus, Electrum, Atomic). Non-wallet process access to these directories is the direct attack vector for financial credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-cryptocurrency-wallet processes (e.g., rundll32, cmd, svchost) reading from wallet keystores and config directories. Match against hardcoded wallet paths and exclude legitimate wallet processes by filename.

suggestion.title: UC_BROWSER_STEALER
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Targets 18 Browsers'; body states malware 'goes far beyond stealing a few stored passwords.' Non-browser process access to browser Login Data, cookie stores, and secrets files is the primary infostealer vector for this malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser processes (rundll32, powershell, cmd, svchost) accessing Chrome/Edge/Firefox credential and cookie database files (%APPDATA%\Google\Chrome, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge, %APPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox). Exclude browser executable and associated service processes.

suggestion.title: UC_DISCORD_TOKEN_THEFT
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Discord Tokens'; represents a distinct credential exfiltration target from generic browser cookies. Discord tokens are unencrypted in app config and enable direct account takeover—detection separate from browser stealer hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-Discord processes accessing Discord application directories (%APPDATA%\Discord, %APPDATA%\discordcanary, %APPDATA%\discordptb) or reading cache/local storage files containing auth tokens. Monitor for process chains where unexpected parent processes spawn children that immediately access Discord profile data.

suggestion.title: UC_RAT_BACKDOOR_COMMAND_AND_CONTROL
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'Hidden Remote Access'; body states 'can take full control of an infected machine'. This is explicit RAT capability requiring command-and-control communication, distinct from the infostealer exfiltration vector. Requires both persistence mechanism (T1547) and C2 communication (T1071/T1219).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections from user-space processes to C2 infrastructure (article IOCs: 45.138.16.107, 85.239.155.68, lucidstealer.one, iloveyoulucid.space, ghdfhfjhfg.webhop.me, 0kt.one, storedonutsmp.net). Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP to newly-registered or high-risk domains. Monitor for bidirectional traffic patterns consistent with remote command execution.

suggestion.title: UC_RAT_PERSISTENCE_MECHANISMS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'take full control of an infected machine' implies across-reboot persistence. RAT capability requires startup-entry or scheduled-job persistence vectors (T1547, T1053) to survive reboots and maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, Run Once, or scheduled task creation by suspicious processes. Alert when non-system processes write to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup or create schtasks entries with obfuscated naming.

suggestion.title: UC_INFOSTEALER_EXECUTION_OBFUSCATION
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) in techniques. Infostealers employ living-off-the-land binaries (rundll32, regsvcs, certutil) and process injection (T1055) to evade detection—process tree anomalies indicate execution evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious child-processes spawning from legitimate Windows binaries (rundll32, regsvcs, mshta, wscript) without expected command-line arguments, followed immediately by file access to credential paths. Correlate with memory operations (CreateRemoteThread) in Sysmon to identify process injection.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails with passkey* domain links
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials'—phishing is the primary attack vector. Domains (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) are explicitly credential-harvesting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with hyperlinks to passkey*-themed domains or inline requests to 'verify passkey.' Look for HTML forms embedded in phishing pages that mimic cloud SSO (OneDrive, SharePoint) login screens. Correlate with known Pink infrastructure reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: Failed cloud authentication attempts post-phishing click
suggestion.rationale: Victims click phishing link, enter credentials; attackers test stolen credentials against cloud services. Article: 'steal cloud storage credentials' implies credential testing/brute force.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login attempts to OneDrive/SharePoint/Google Drive with prior network flows to passkey* domains within 5 minutes. Anomalies: multiple failures from same user in short window, MFA bypass attempts, or logins from unusual geos post-click.

suggestion.title: Credential manager / password vault access anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'cloud storage credentials' — harvesting harvests from stored credentials. Article implies enterprise users with managed/synced credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal credential manager access (Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI queries, browser password store extraction) in proximity to phishing domain contact. Flag rapid/bulk access to credential stores by non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Bulk data copying / exfiltration post-credential compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: group 'listed several initial victims'—implies data exfiltration to leak site. Enterprise cloud storage (OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams) is the target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file copy/sync from cloud storage to external cloud accounts or FTP/SMB shares. Baseline by user; flag unusual export/download of sensitive data (files with keywords: 'secret,' 'confidential,' 'source') within hours of failed auth attempts from phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Passkey*-pattern domain registration clustering
suggestion.rationale: Three variants listed (passkeyadd, passkeydeploy, deploypasskey). Threat actor reuses naming patterns; future campaigns will follow same convention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume WHOIS and passive DNS feeds; alert on newly registered domains matching *passkey*, *auth*, *credential*, *mfa*, *verify*. Cluster by registrant, registrar, nameserver, and IP address. Cross-reference against Pink group WHOIS patterns from known infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloud storage delegated access / sharing rule changes post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Extortion requires persistent data access for leverage; article mentions 'sensitive data.' Compromised accounts may grant external access or establish backdoor sharing permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected folder sharing to external domains, new external users added to sensitive sites, or new device registrations from IP ranges associated with 185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66. Baseline by department; flag shares of documents with confidential/PII keywords.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Automated Password Resets via Account Recovery Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers used Meta's AI-powered support system to reset passwords' and 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in.' Detecting bulk or time-clustered password resets to HTS or similar recovery systems is the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous spikes in password reset requests to account recovery endpoints, especially requests that bypass standard email verification. Flag patterns where the same email or account is reset multiple times within a short window, or resets originating from non-typical geographic regions.

suggestion.title: Email Verification Bypass in Account Recovery Flows
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Detect successful password resets where email ownership validation was skipped or improperly verified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag password reset requests where the supplied email address is not confirmed against account registration data before issuance of reset tokens. Monitor for resets initiated via unverified email addresses that bypass multi-factor confirmation steps.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover: Login Immediately After Forced Password Reset
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: 'reset passwords on Instagram user accounts... hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.' Detect logins within minutes of forced or emergency password resets from new/suspicious locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful password reset events with new login sessions from geographically distant or previously unseen IP addresses within 5–15 minutes. Escalate if 2FA is disabled or the account shows unusual subsequent activity (message access, profile changes).

suggestion.title: Post-Takeover Account Activity: Direct Messages and Data Access from New Location
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'attackers could've gained access to... direct messages and communications, account activity and interaction history.' Detect mass data exfiltration or unusual account activity following a password reset.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk read/export of messages, photos, stories, and profile data from newly authenticated sessions originating in atypical locations or from devices not previously associated with the account.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Linked Account Access from Compromised Instagram Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'could've gained access... to other connected accounts and linked services.' Detect cascading account compromise across linked services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins to linked services (email, Facebook, third-party apps) using OAuth or account-linking tokens refreshed from a compromised primary account. Correlate with IP/device anomalies from the initial account takeover.

suggestion.title: Incident Response: Bulk Mandatory Password Reset Campaign
suggestion.rationale: 'Meta... enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint and asked all affected users to reset their passwords again.' Detect large-scale remediation password-reset campaigns indicative of breach disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enterprise-scale forced password reset campaigns targeting thousands of accounts in a compressed timeframe, especially when coupled with security checkpoint enrollment or forced re-authentication demands. Correlate with public disclosures or breach notifications.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious 'Graph ML PyPI Packages' as attack vector. Pipeline created no Initial Access detection for abnormal package installation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip install/upgrade operations with unusual parent processes, abnormal command-line arguments, or installs of known-malicious package names. Correlate with unexpected network connections to PyPI or third-party repositories during package operations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Python Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers' requiring execution. No execution-phase detection for python.exe spawning system utilities or non-standard child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child process spawning from python.exe, python3, pip, or interpreters with suspicious parents or unusual process chains. Detect spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system utilities without corresponding module imports or legitimate package-installation activity.

suggestion.title: Memory-Read API Calls Indicative of Data Scraping
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly cites 'Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers' as primary capability. No collection-phase detection for memory dumping or credential scraping via ReadProcessMemory, VirtualQueryEx, or ptrace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect memory-read APIs called by python.exe or child processes targeting external processes. Monitor for repeated memory access patterns, large sequential reads, or memory queries against LSASS or other credential stores.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from Python Processes
suggestion.rationale: Memory scrapers and 'AI Analyst Misdirection' imply C2 exfiltration. No command-and-control detection for Python-spawned outbound traffic to non-standard infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from python.exe to non-standard ports, internal subnets, or domains outside public package repositories. Flag DNS queries from Python processes to suspicious domains or beaconing patterns outside expected install windows.

suggestion.title: Wiper or Destructive File Operations Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Wiper Deterrent' as third capability. No impact-phase detection for file deletion, encryption, or system destruction initiated by compromised processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file deletion, encryption, or overwrite operations from Python child processes. Monitor for API calls to reboot, shutdown, or low-level disk I/O from non-system contexts. Flag repeated failed file access followed by destruction attempts.

suggestion.title: Decoy or Fake Analysis Process Spawning (Defense Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'AI Analyst Misdirection' strategy. No defense-evasion detection for decoy analysis tools, fake security scanners, or masquerading processes designed to confuse automated analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python or package processes spawning processes with legitimate security-tool names (e.g., rundll32.exe, explorer.exe) but abnormal parent-child relationships. Flag process command-line spoofing or decoy process spawning that does not align with actual execution context.

suggestion.title: Vishing Attempt Followed by Suspicious RMM Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'phone calls, screen-sharing tricks' used to break in—clear vishing/social engineering (T1598.003). No detection for user reports of suspicious calls correlating with subsequent RMM installation or system compromise events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user-reported phishing/vishing incidents (helpdesk tickets, email security reports flagging voice phishing, or internal escalations mentioning phone calls) with unexpected RMM or remote-access process installations within 24 hours on the reporter's endpoint. Flag if installer user matches reported victim. Escalate if target is law firm domain or high-value user.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to business-data-leaks.com and Exfiltration Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing 'sensitive files' from law firms and lists business-data-leaks.com as IOC, implying data exfiltration site. No detection exists for connections to this domain or similar file-staging infrastructure correlated with bulk data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS/FTP connections to business-data-leaks.com and high-entropy C2-like domains registered < 6 months. Correlate with RMM process execution and bulk file reads from sensitive directories (/Legal/Contracts, /Financials, etc.). Alert on data exfiltration volumes > 100MB in a session or unusual file extensions being accessed (*.docx, *.pdf, *.xlsx) from non-standard user accounts.

suggestion.title: RMM Tool Command Execution and C2 Beaconing Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RMM used for 'command execution' and system control. T1219 is listed but no detection for RMM establishing C2 connections or spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, PowerShell) for hands-on-keyboard attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by RMM processes to non-whitelisted external IPs or ports (outside organization's RMM control infrastructure). Detect RMM process spawning command shells, scripting engines, or file-transfer tools without corresponding help desk ticket or user approval event. Flag RMM beaconing to IP ranges matching article IOCs (192.236.x.x, 174.169.x.x, 64.94.x.x).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation or Administrative Action Initiated via RMM
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers using RMM for 'exfiltrate data'—implies file system access and potential credential dumping. No detection for high-privilege operations (LSASS dump, file copy to staging, credential vault access) initiated by RMM child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when RMM process or its spawned children execute sensitive commands: mimikatz, procdump targeting LSASS, xcopy to network shares, reg save HKLM\\SAM, Get-ADUser, taskkill -f. Alert if initiated by non-IT-enrolled account and correlate with RMM installation timestamp. Escalate if RMM user does not match roster of authorized support staff.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement or Discovery via RMM from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Once law firm is breached via vishing and RMM installed, article implies attackers move through network to find sensitive files. No detection for RMM establishing connections to multiple internal systems (other workstations, file servers, domain controllers) in attack sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RMM processes opening SMB, RDP, WinRM, or administrative share connections to 5+ distinct internal IPs within 1 hour of RMM installation. Flag if destinations include file servers or domain controller subnets. Alert if RMM traffic is tunneled/encrypted and target IPs are outside user's baseline lateral-movement profile.

suggestion.title: RMM Installation via Phishing Delivery or Compromised Browser Session
suggestion.rationale: Vishing ('screen-sharing tricks') suggests social engineering may directly lead to RMM download/install. Article does not detect RMM installation from suspicious delivery mechanisms: email attachment, browser download, malicious link.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RMM installer (.exe, .msi) downloaded from external/untrusted sources (non-vendor domains, URL shorteners, file-sharing services) or received as email attachment, followed immediately by execution. Alert if download occurs in user's Temp, Downloads, or AppData folders and followed by process creation < 5 minutes later. Cross-reference with known-malicious hashes and URLs. Flag timing correlation with email receipt or suspicious web activity.

suggestion.title: Inbound Vishing Attempts / Suspicious Voice Call Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states UNC3753 'used vishing' as initial attack vector. Zero use cases generated to detect voice phishing, social engineering calls to employees, or unusual inbound calling patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for calls from external numbers to employee extensions, especially time-clustered calls to multiple employees in same department. Flag calls followed by urgent credential requests or IT impersonation language. Correlate with failed MFA attempts within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Download to Removable Media / Unusual File Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'data theft' in U.S. campaign; physical intrusions imply attackers had on-site access. No detection use case for large file copies to USB, external drives, or cloud staging locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large file copies (>100MB) to removable media in short time window, especially outside business hours. Flag access to sensitive file shares (HR, finance, customer data) followed immediately by external media mount. Detect zip/rar creation of multiple sensitive folders within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Large Encrypted / Compressed Data Exfiltration to External Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Data theft campaign requires exfiltration step. Pipeline missed detection logic for detecting outbound transfer of stolen data, compressed archives, or encrypted payloads to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/TLS to rare destinations with high entropy payloads (signature of encrypted data transfer). Alert on connections to IPs with no prior communication history, especially outside U.S. geolocation. Detect zip files or .7z archives sent to external cloud services in hours after bulk data access.

suggestion.title: Extortion Demand / Ransom Communication Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article headline ends with 'extortion campaign'—UNC3753 is explicitly conducting extortion. No use cases generated for detecting ransom notes, extortion emails, or payment instructions left on compromised systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for text files named 'README_DECRYPT.txt', 'CONTACT_US.html', or similar in public-facing directories, desktop roots, or file shares. Detect emails with keywords (bitcoin, ransom, 'we have your data') sent to company executives or board members. Flag payment gateway references or Tor onion URLs in newly created files system-wide.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting / Social Engineering Artifacts from Vishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Vishing requires pre-text and credential theft to succeed. Pipeline should detect phishing URLs, credential dump files, or email follow-ups sent to targets identified via voice calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound vishing call logs with subsequent phishing emails or Okta/MFA enrollment emails sent to same targets within 4 hours. Detect anomalous logon attempts from non-VPN IPs immediately after vishing timestamps. Monitor for employees clicking suspicious links or submitting credentials via fake SSO pages within 24h of call records.

suggestion.title: Physical Access + Digital Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'physical intrusions' as attack vector. Pipeline should correlate badge swipes, camera footage markers, or after-hours facility access with concurrent unusual file access, data downloads, or malware execution on those systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when after-hours facility access (badge swipe, camera timestamp) is followed within 15 minutes by first-ever logon to previously-untouched workstation with immediate access to sensitive shares or database queries. Flag USB mount or external device connection detected during same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Non-Native Binary Execution on Linux Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances'—cross-OS binary execution (BSD binary on Linux) is an anomaly and delivery indicator that pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of BSD ELF binaries or non-standard architectures on Linux appliance hosts. Monitor for process invocation with architecture mismatches or foreign OS magic bytes in executed binaries.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Malware Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names BRICKSTORM as deployed payload but pipeline generated zero detections for this malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures for BRICKSTORM execution indicators: file names, registry keys, mutex patterns, C2 communication signatures, and process hollowing behaviors specific to BSD/Linux variants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Launch from Appliance Context
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'deployment on Linux Appliances'—appliances typically run fixed software stacks; any process execution outside baseline should trigger. Article implies active malware post-deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal processes on target appliance class, alert on deviation. Monitor for shell spawning, file writes to /tmp or /var/tmp, and unexpected child processes from system daemons.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Lateral Movement / C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Named threat actor (VerdantBamboo) performing coordinated malware distribution implies C2 infrastructure and lateral movement; pipeline missed actor-specific behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network patterns consistent with VerdantBamboo's known C2 infrastructure. Alert on traffic to known BRICKSTORM C2 domains/IPs and abnormal outbound connections from appliances.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Appliance Boot Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Deployment to appliances suggests persistence across reboot; article implies sustained presence but pipeline captured zero persistence-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor boot loader modifications, systemd unit file creation, crontab additions, and firmware-level persistence mechanisms on appliance targets. Alert on /etc/init.d or /usr/lib/systemd/system modifications.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via BSD Binary Disguise
suggestion.rationale: BSD-compiled variant running on Linux is evasion tactic (bypasses Linux-specific defense heuristics); pipeline categorized zero defense-evasion patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution where binary architecture does not match OS expectations. Flag code compiled for different OS/ABI running via compatibility layers or native execution simulators.

suggestion.title: Phishing email impersonating AI brands (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.)
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states threat actors use 'AI brands as bait' in social engineering; metadata keywords confirm phishing + credential theft vector. Pipeline produced zero phishing detection UCs despite this being the primary attack method described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Email messages impersonating known AI service brands (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Microsoft) in sender address, display name, or domain (typosquatting patterns). Correlate with known AI vendor domains and flag senders from non-vendor infrastructure requesting credential verification or urgent action.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attack post-phishing
suggestion.rationale: Metadata explicitly lists 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' as keyword; article describes credential theft via AiTM interception. Pipeline generated zero AiTM-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in events where session tokens are stolen and replayed from different IP/device following phishing engagement. Look for successful logins immediately preceded by sign-in failures from a different geography, or device code flow + refresh token reuse without MFA interaction.

suggestion.title: Suspicious access to fake AI service domains
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via spoofed AI brands implies users visiting attacker-controlled domains mimicking ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot UI. Pipeline missed web proxy/URL filtering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to domains registered within 30 days of known AI brand names, or DNS resolutions to IPs hosting credential-harvesting landing pages. Correlate with phishing email delivery timeframe and user click patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to non-corporate identity provider
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks intercept credentials by positioning a reverse proxy between user and legitimate service. Detection must catch credential entry into attacker-controlled endpoints mimicking Azure AD / corporate IdP login flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Users submitting credentials (form-based input capture) to domains that are not the legitimate corporate identity provider or known SaaS vendor identity endpoints. Cross-reference with authentication logs to identify cases where the credential entry point and successful login source differ.

suggestion.title: MFA bypass or forced re-authentication after phishing
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks often include MFA interception or prompt-bombing to force user re-authentication. Article keywords include credential theft; pipeline missed post-compromise auth anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Rapid sequence of sign-in attempts from the same IP with fresh device tokens, followed by MFA registration changes or password resets. Flag cases where MFA was disabled or altered post-phishing exposure window.

suggestion.title: Legitimate AI service credential reuse across accounts
suggestion.rationale: Users compromised via fake AI tool phishing may have reused credentials across corporate and personal AI service accounts. Credential stuffing detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential reuse signals: user successfully authenticates to corporate services with username/password harvested from fake AI brand phishing, or third-party identity provider logs show login attempts using harvested corporate credentials.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly addresses 'AI Phishing' as a threat vector crushing SOCs. No use case generated despite clear detection need for AI-crafted message patterns (linguistic anomalies, template reuse, sender spoofing).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email campaigns with unusual linguistic patterns (statistical entropy, common LLM preamble/closure patterns), volume surges from new sender domains, and high-fidelity spoofing of known contacts. Correlate message metadata (subject line templates, attachment types, URLs) across recipient populations to identify batch AI-generation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Alert Volume Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'alert volume' and 'Tier 1 overload'—implies coordinated, high-volume campaigns. Detection of sudden phishing detection spike or alert rate change relative to baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor alert generation rate for phishing categories; trigger on 3σ deviation from 30-day baseline over 1-hour window. Correlate with unique sender domains, recipient counts, and payload types to distinguish noise from coordinated campaign.

suggestion.title: Sender Domain Reputation Collapse
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing campaigns often use newly registered or spoofed domains. Article references 'AI-generated' campaigns implying potential bulk domain abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from domains with registration age <7 days, zero prior organizational mail history, or passive DNS records showing recent mass-hosting signup patterns. Cross-reference against WHOIS abuse databases and DNS seed lists.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass Exploitation (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be exploited by unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs'. This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access logs for authentication bypass signatures, unauthenticated connection attempts, or rapid auth failures followed by successful connection from same source. Flag any VPN tunnel establishment without valid credentials in IKEv1 configurations.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Usage in VPN Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects only deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol'. This configuration is the vulnerability precondition and detecting its use identifies at-risk deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory and alert on any Remote Access VPN or Mobile Access deployment still negotiating IKEv1 key exchanges. Flag legacy remote access client connections. Correlate IKEv1 usage with vulnerable Check Point versions.

suggestion.title: VPN Access Followed by Post-Compromise Ransomware Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate', establishing kill-chain linkage between VPN compromise and ransomware deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Check Point VPN authentication events with subsequent suspicious post-compromise indicators: unusual process execution, lateral movement attempts, file encryption activity, or known Qilin ransomware IOCs within 24-48 hours of VPN access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50752 Certificate Validation Bypass in Site-to-Site VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article describes secondary vulnerability affecting 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN tunnel establishment for IKEv1 connections without mandatory machine certificate authentication. Flag certificate validation failures or missing cert checks. Detect potential MITM indicators between VPN peers.

suggestion.title: Machine Certificate Authentication Disabled in Remote Access VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects deployments 'that do not require a machine certificate for connections' and recommends 'set the Machine Certificate Authentication as mandatory' as mitigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access configurations for disabled or optional machine certificate requirements. Alert if certificate authentication is removed or set to non-mandatory. Correlate with IKEv1 usage.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-Breach VPN Lateral Movement Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes Qilin gang affiliation with at least one exploitation case and cites their history of high-profile victims, suggesting detection should correlate VPN compromise with Qilin IOC signatures and behavioral patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlation rules matching Qilin tooling, ransom note patterns, file encryption behavior, and exfiltration indicators following unexplained VPN access. Monitor Qilin's dark-web leak site for appearance of newly accessed organizations.

suggestion.title: Unpatched BerriAI LiteLLM Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and mandates federal remediation by 2026-06-22. CISA KEV status signals immediate exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all BerriAI LiteLLM instances and cross-check version against CVE-2026-42271 patch cutoff. Flag unpatched instances, prioritize those exposed to untrusted networks or the internet. Alert on any instances not remediated by 2026-06-22.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Command Injection Exploitation Signals
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allow any authenticated user... to run arbitrary commands on the host.' Requires detection for command injection payloads in requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag LiteLLM HTTP requests or API calls containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, backticks, $(), command substitution) in authentication headers, tokens, or payload fields. Correlate with HTTP 4xx/5xx error responses indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Lateral Movement via LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploitation by 'holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' enables arbitrary command execution. Represents post-compromise privilege-escalation and lateral-movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevated or system-context processes spawned by LiteLLM service when parent is running as low-privilege account. Alert on token elevation attempts, parent-child relationships where LiteLLM spawns cmd.exe/powershell with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution from LiteLLM Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack culminates in 'arbitrary commands on the host.' Post-exploitation detection requires identifying unexpected child-process spawning or system utilities executed from LiteLLM service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by LiteLLM service (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python, perl, nc, curl, whoami, systeminfo, whoami, dir). Establish baseline of legitimate LiteLLM child-process spawning and alert on deviations. Monitor command-line arguments for credential theft, reconnaissance, or persistence tactics.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated IKEv1 Key Exchange to Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker' and 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange.' Pipeline should detect initial IKEv1 phase exchanges lacking authentication tokens or completing without valid credential exchange.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 phase 1 and phase 2 exchanges to Check Point Security Gateway for sessions that skip authentication handshakes or complete key exchange without successful credential validation. Alert on any IKEv1 initiator that progresses from phase 1 directly to phase 2 without authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: VPN Remote Access Connection Without Valid Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Pipeline should flag VPN logons lacking corresponding authentication events or pre-authenticated session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Check Point Security Gateway remote access VPN connections where no corresponding successful user authentication event exists in the credential store (AD, RADIUS, or local auth). Flag sessions established with null, empty, or system-default credentials.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway CVE-2026-50751 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-50751; pipeline should create asset-exposure detection mapping vulnerable gateway versions and firmware levels to running instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match Check Point Security Gateway instances against vulnerable firmware versions for CVE-2026-50751 (typical range: specific R80/R81 branches pre-patch). Alert if any exposed gateway instance matches the vulnerable version vector.

suggestion.title: Repeated Failed IKEv1 Phase Exchanges from Remote Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper authentication' as the root cause; an attacker exploiting this flaw may generate multiple malformed or incomplete IKEv1 handshakes before successful bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >3 failed IKEv1 phase exchanges from the same remote source IP within 5 minutes to a Check Point gateway, followed within 10 minutes by a successful VPN session establishment. This pattern suggests exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Pattern: Phase Completion Without Certificate or Credential Exchange
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability allows bypass of user authentication during IKEv1 key exchange; detections should look for anomalous IKEv1 message sequences that skip expected authentication steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify IKEv1 sessions to Check Point gateways where the responder accepts phase 2 SA negotiation (child SA) without completing phase 1 authentication (PSK validation, certificate exchange, or ID verification). This indicates the improper authentication flaw is being exploited.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the root cause: 'the authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version.' Attackers craft requests that appear auth-exempt in raw form but resolve to protected routes after normalization, bypassing authentication entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests with URI encoding anomalies (double-slashes, path traversal sequences like ../, %2e%2e/, or normalized equivalents) targeting the /api/auth/validate-sso/ endpoint or similar auth paths. Alert when raw URI and normalized URI differ significantly. Baseline legitimate authentication patterns and flag unauthenticated access to protected backend services.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation in UniFi Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-34909 is a 'path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system.' Article identifies the vulnerable endpoint as ucs/update/latest_package, making file-system access attempts via traversal patterns a direct indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to ucs/update/latest_package containing path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e/, absolute paths like /etc, /proc, /var). Correlate with HTTP responses exfiltrating system configuration files (passwd, shadow, sudoers) or unusually large response bodies suggesting file content leakage.

suggestion.title: Command Injection in UniFi Package Update Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-34910 is a 'command injection flaw' where 'attackers can target a package-update endpoint, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the ucs/update/latest_package endpoint for parameters containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), $(...)). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by the ucs-update service, particularly shell invocations (sh, bash, dash) or unexpected system binaries (id, whoami, curl, wget, nc). Correlate child process spawning with inbound requests lacking authentication context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo by Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article notes injected commands 'do not initially run as root' but 'the affected service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial.' The attack succeeds because the service account has 'passwordless sudo access to several system binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and alert on all sudo invocations by UniFi service accounts (ucs-update or similar). Flag passwordless sudo commands (executing without prior tty authentication). Monitor for sudo invoking system binaries capable of shell spawning (find, awk, sed, perl, python) or privilege change commands (chmod, chown). Correlate with prior unauthenticated API access in the same session window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning Under ucs-update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article advises defenders to monitor 'suspicious child processes under ucs-update' as a key detection indicator. Any child processes spawned by the update service are anomalous if the service is in a passive state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alerts whenever a child process is spawned under the ucs-update parent process (PID matching). Whitelist only legitimate package management tasks; flag all shells, interpreters, network utilities (curl, wget, socat, netcat), or system tools. Include full command line, parent PID, user context, and correlation with inbound HTTP requests in the alert.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unauthenticated Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the attack 'does not require authentication' and notes finding prior exploitation is 'challenging because the attack does not require authentication. There is no failed-login trail to look for.' The ucs/update/latest_package endpoint becomes the direct attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any access to ucs/update/latest_package endpoint from sources without prior successful authentication events. Establish baseline of legitimate package-update request patterns (frequency, source IP ranges, user agents). Flag requests with suspicious payloads, unusually large POST bodies, or rapid successive requests from the same source that lack authentication context.

suggestion.title: Account Creation Immediately Followed by Repository and Merge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Since Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default...an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance. Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner.' Exploit chain requires sequential account→repo→merge actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new Gogs account creation followed within 15 minutes by repository creation and merge operation initiation by the same user. Baseline against legitimate admin/developer timelines. Flag instances with DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false.

suggestion.title: Rebase Merge Setting Enablement on New Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' Rebase is prerequisite for executing the argument injection payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs settings API calls for rebase merge enable on repositories created by low-privilege users within 24 hours of account creation. Alert especially for accounts with no prior merge activity.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Patterns in Git Merge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'argument injection vulnerability' in the 'Merge() code path that was never addressed.' Exploit passes malformed arguments to trigger RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs merge operation logs for branch names or commit metadata containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), ${}, pipes, semicolons, &, ||). Cross-reference with Gogs error logs for merge failures following suspicious argument submission.

suggestion.title: Configuration Changes Weakening Registration and Repository Limits
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable defaults: 'DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false in app.ini' and 'MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = -1 in app.ini.' Changes enabling registration or unlimited repo creation expand attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to Gogs app.ini changing DISABLE_REGISTRATION to false or MAX_CREATION_LIMIT to any value >0 (or -1). Flag any admin panel setting changes by non-root accounts. Prioritize alerts for Internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Credential Extraction and Repository Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'read any repository (including private repos), steal credentials, move laterally to other systems on the network.' Post-exploitation moves include credential theft and unauthorized data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Gogs application processes accessing sensitive file paths (~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, config files), extracting user credential database fields in bulk, or initiating connections to external systems. Alert on non-standard data exfiltration patterns from Gogs running directories.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gogs Version Identification and Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'affects all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev.' Patch released June 7, 2026 as 0.14.3. Shadowserver reports 2,300+ exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Gogs service instances via version banner detection and HTTP fingerprinting. Alert on any instance running 0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev, or earlier. Prioritize alerts for instances responding on public IP ranges or CMSs. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory for unpatched deployments.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader Execution via LOLBin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fileless .NET loader' as the payload. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the execution phase. Must hunt for rundll32, powershell, or similar proxies loading managed code in-memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rundll32.exe or powershell.exe with command-line arguments indicative of .NET assembly loading or managed code execution. Correlate with immediate network egress to malicious domains from IOC list. Hunt for DotNet CLR runtime initialization in process telemetry without legitimate application context.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign with DoubleClick Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body emphasize 'malspam campaign' using Google DoubleClick as the redirect mechanism for initial access. No UC generated for email-gateway detection of malicious redirect chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt email messages containing DoubleClick domain references in headers or body, especially with URL shorteners or suspicious link patterns. Flag if redirect chain resolves to attacker-controlled domain from article IOC list. Correlate with user clicking link and subsequent suspicious process creation within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Legitimate DoubleClick Infrastructure for C2 Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: The campaign's hallmark tactic is using Google's trusted DoubleClick infrastructure to bypass email and network security controls. No UC for detecting this defense-evasion pattern despite being the campaign's defining characteristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to legitimate DoubleClick domains followed by connection to attacker IOC domains within 30 seconds. Alert on DoubleClick referrer headers redirecting to non-Google ASNs. Baseline normal DoubleClick usage and flag statistical anomalies in redirect patterns.

suggestion.title: Network IOC Detection: Malspam Campaign Command Domains
suggestion.rationale: Seven command/staging domains are listed as high-fidelity IOCs but pipeline IOC extraction returned empty dict. Standard network connection detection for these specific IOCs is missing from generated use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on outbound DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections to the seven article IOC domains. Correlate with process execution events to identify which processes initiated contact. Escalate any internal host communicating with these IOCs as confirmed compromised.

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection: Fileless .NET Loader Variants
suggestion.rationale: Five SHA256 hashes are enumerated as high-fidelity IOCs but no hash-based detection use case was generated. Hashes must be deployed to endpoint EDR/AV systems with immediate alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file write or process execution matching any of the five SHA256 hashes. Given fileless nature, hunt for .NET runtime initialization where parent process or loaded assembly hash matches. Escalate immediately as confirmed malware.

suggestion.title: NSO WhatsApp Phishing Link Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'WhatsApp Phishing Attack' — requires detection of phishing links distributed via WhatsApp to harvest credentials. Article phrase: 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to known phishing domains or suspicious WhatsApp link shortener patterns (bit.ly, tinyurl, custom URL shorteners) originating from endpoints with WhatsApp installed. Correlate with failed authentication attempts within 5 minutes of link click.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Campaign Attribution (Behavioral)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names NSO Group as the threat actor — pipeline should surface actor-specific TTPs and correlate with prior NSO campaigns. Absence of actor attribution is critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain NSO Group indicator of compromise (IOC) feeds and correlate messaging patterns, targeting profiles, and infrastructure reuse against incoming phishing campaigns. Alert on WhatsApp-distributed links targeting high-value targets (C-suite, security personnel).
