suggestion.title: WhatsApp Credential Harvesting via Fake Login
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks targeting WhatsApp users historically involve fake authentication pages. Article describes 'Phishing Attack' without specifying payload, but this is the canonical NSO technique against WhatsApp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to phishing domains that mimic WhatsApp login endpoints (fake 2FA pages, credential prompts). Look for pages hosting JavaScript that exfiltrates credentials or session tokens to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Meta/WhatsApp Abuse Report Signal Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Meta 'blocks' the attack — implies Meta's own detection fired. Should correlate user abuse reports, account takeover attempts, and suspicious login locations on WhatsApp accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of WhatsApp account takeovers, login attempts from unusual geographies, and rapid account recovery actions (password resets, 2FA changes) within hours of phishing link distribution.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'purpose-built web shell framework' is the primary attack payload deployed to IIS servers. This is the kill-chain centerpiece but absent from detections. Phrase: 'web shell framework designed to evade every detection method.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS directories (\inetpub\wwwroot\, \inetpub\vhosts\) for anomalous .aspx, .ashx file creation with timestamps outside business hours or by system accounts. Correlate with IIS w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell—indicator of live web shell interaction.

suggestion.title: IIS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies IIS servers as primary target ('targeting Internet Information Services'), implying exploitation as entry vector, but no T1190 technique captured. Phrase: 'Targets IIS Servers With Cryptographically Unique Web Shell Framework.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt IIS access logs for exploitation signatures: unusual HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE), path traversal attempts, RCE payloads in query strings or POST bodies, or requests to sensitive paths (e.g., /admin/, /.git/, /web.config). Cross-reference w3wp process spawns with user-agent strings from log entries.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'designed to evade every detection method that works against similar China-linked actors'—direct indication of evasion tradecraft. This defense-evasion intent has no corresponding UC despite being explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process masquerading (w3wp.exe spawning unusual children or with atypical parent-child relationships), file metadata tampering (modified timestamps preceding creation timestamps), registry key hiding, or suspicious deletion patterns on suspected compromise hosts. Cross-reference with known C2 domains (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing via Domain Names
suggestion.rationale: Two command-and-control domains listed (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com) but network hunt is limited to direct IP/domain IOCs. No behavioral hunt for beaconing patterns typical of web shell C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from IIS hosts to ashx.lhlsjcb.com and hcgos.com with regular intervals (hourly, every N minutes), small request/response sizes, or request patterns consistent with C2 heartbeats. Flag DNS A/AAAA record lookups to these domains from internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Discord token theft — non-Discord process accessing token cache
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly lists 'Discord Tokens' as targeted credential type. No Discord-specific hunt provided despite being a named attack vector at parity with browsers and wallets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for non-Discord.exe processes accessing Discord token files in %APPDATA%\Discord\Local Storage or %APPDATA%\Roaming\discord\Cache. Discord tokens grant API access and account takeover; monitor separately from browser cookies due to reuse exposure.

suggestion.title: RAT persistence and lateral movement — process/service/registry anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can take full control of an infected machine without [...]', indicating persistent RAT capability. No detection for persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, services, registry run-keys, WMI subscriptions) despite this being the declared post-exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services, and WMI event subscriptions from unusual parents (mshta, rundll32, shell injection vectors). Alert on scheduled tasks created by non-admin user processes or with unusual binaries (cmd.exe /c powershell.exe -enc [base64]).

suggestion.title: Process memory credential extraction — LSASS/process handle opening
suggestion.rationale: Malware targets credentials across 18 browsers + crypto wallets + Discord. At this scale, credential harvesting typically requires reading process memory (LSASS for cached credentials, browser memory for session data). No detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious process open/query access from malware-typical parent processes (mshta, regsvcs, svchost.exe with unusual command line, or low-integrity processes) to LSASS.exe with access mask 0x001F0FFF or 0x00100FFF (PROCESS_VM_READ, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION). Exclude legitimate tools (monitoring agents, AV, EDR).

suggestion.title: Code obfuscation and process injection — behavioral defense evasion
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) is explicitly listed in article techniques but no detection hunt provided. Malware delivery and execution likely uses code injection, process hollowing, or reflective DLL injection to evade static detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious process creation patterns: parent-child mismatches (document readers spawning cmd.exe/powershell), base64/hex-encoded command-line arguments, write-execute patterns in normally read-only regions, or Image File Execution Options (IFEO) registry manipulations targeting system binaries.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing emails linking to credential harvesting pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials' and actor registered passkey-themed domains; no phishing UC was generated despite being the documented initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing links to passkey-themed domains (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) or the IOC IP addresses. Flag redirect chains leading to credential-capture HTML forms mimicking OneDrive, Dropbox, or SharePoint login pages.

suggestion.title: Brute force / forced authentication against cloud storage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'steal cloud storage credentials' but zero authentication-anomaly UCs exist to detect attack-phase password spraying or forced auth against OneDrive, SharePoint, Dropbox.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentications (>10 in 5 min) against cloud storage endpoints from atypical geolocations or the IOC IPs. Flag authentication attempts immediately following credential-harvesting phishing email delivery.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to actor-controlled leak site infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states group 'launched its dedicated data leak site' and lists 6 IOC domains/IPs; no exfiltration UC was generated to detect data staging or uploads to this infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers or uploads to the IOC domains/IPs (185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66). Flag SFTP, HTTP POST, or cloud-sync activity to these destinations, especially when correlated with prior compromised cloud credentials.

suggestion.title: Credential-harvesting domain infrastructure and C2
suggestion.rationale: Domain names (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) strongly indicate infrastructure acquisition for credential harvesting; no UC detects domain-registration patterns or C2 communication to these IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to passkey-themed domains or resolution to the IOC IPs. Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS connections to these infrastructure endpoints from corporate networks. Investigate WHOIS creation dates (likely recent, post-May-2026 data leak site launch).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python .pth File Execution in Package Installs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious artifacts included a *-setup.pth file and an obfuscated JavaScript payload named _index.js. Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file' — represents a direct execution mechanism on any Python startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python package directories (.local/lib/python*/site-packages, venv paths) for *.pth files with timestamps matching recent pip installs. Alert on Python process execution immediately following .pth file creation. Correlate with known trojanized package versions from the 37 malicious releases.

suggestion.title: Python Spawning Bun JavaScript Runtime from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script' and 'process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js' — highly suspicious parent-child process relationship and GitHub download pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process python.exe spawning bun executable. Correlate with network events showing urllib/requests/curl downloads from raw.githubusercontent.com or api.github.com in the same parent process context. Flag _index.js file execution from /tmp or similar staging directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Across Multiple Secret Types
suggestion.rationale: Article lists targeted secrets: 'GitHub tokens, npm/PyPI/RubyGems tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes/Vault credentials, SSH keys, Docker credentials, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, shell histories, Claude/MCP configuration files' — indicates file system enumeration and access to credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process (especially Python, JavaScript, or shell) accessing multiple credential-bearing files in a short time window: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/anthropic/*, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc. Alert on access patterns from unexpected parent processes (python.exe from site-packages).

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow or Repository Creation from Compromised Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions' and 'Github workflow... files are also used' for persistence — indicates programmatic GitHub API abuse from developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes (Python, Node.js, Bun) calling GitHub API endpoints (api.github.com) with actions/secrets-writing permissions. Alert on creation of new repositories or workflows from non-browser user agents during off-hours or outside normal CI/CD contexts. Correlate GitHub API calls with credential file access in same process tree.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Systemd Service or LaunchAgent Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used' — indicates multiple boot-persistence techniques in single campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and ~/.config/systemd/user/ for .service files created or modified during suspicious Python/Bun execution. Alert on /Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist creation on macOS from non-standard processes. Correlate with previous execution/credential-access signals in same session.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Locale and Security Tool Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware also features some evasion mechanisms, such as checking for Russian locales/environments, and security tools such as StepSecurity Harden-Runner' — indicates conditional execution and anti-forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript/Python code (especially in _index.js or .pth payloads) checking environment variables related to locale (LANG, LC_ALL) or invoking security tool detection (harden-runner, StepSecurity APIs). Flag processes that check /etc/os-release or locale before executing main payload as evasion signal.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Loaded by Unprivileged User
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'enables local root access' and mentions 'exploits now public'—a one-character kernel flaw likely exploited via insmod or similar kernel module manipulation. Title directly references the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod, modprobe, or direct /proc/modules writes from non-root UIDs. Flag any kernel module load attempt by unprivileged users, especially those immediately followed by elevated process spawning or capability changes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states flaw 'enables local root access'—the primary attack outcome. Pipeline missed mapping this to privilege escalation kill-chain and detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell spawning (bash, sh, zsh) with uid=0 from a process chain originating at uid>0, especially within seconds of kernel-related syscall anomalies (seccomp failures, mmap on /proc/sys, write to kernel memory regions).

suggestion.title: Abnormal Syscall Patterns Preceding Root Shell
suggestion.rationale: A 'one-character flaw' suggests a tight, targeted kernel bug. Exploitation likely triggers detectable syscall sequences or memory access violations before root escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual mmap, mprotect, or prctl sequences that modify memory protections or capability sets, followed immediately by execve of a shell. Correlate with failed CAP_SYS_ADMIN or capability-related syscall failures.

suggestion.title: Known Kernel Exploit PoC Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exploits now public'—pipeline should trigger IOC extraction for public PoC artifacts (file hashes, git URLs, compilation artifacts) and detection for those signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for compilation of C exploit code via gcc/clang targeting kernel headers, execution of known PoC binaries by hash or behavioral signature, and temporary source files in /tmp or home directories that compile privilege-escalation payloads.

suggestion.title: Root Shell Spawned from Non-Root Parent
suggestion.rationale: Core indicator that kernel exploit succeeded. Pipeline completely missed impact-phase detection despite title's emphasis on 'root access'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any shell (sh, bash, zsh, ksh) with effective_uid=0 whose parent process has real_uid>0, especially if parent is a user application rather than sudo/su. Cross-check against allow-lists of legitimate escalation paths (sudo, su, systemd services).

suggestion.title: HTS Email Verification Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts,' establishing the core exploitation vector. Detection must target this specific verification flaw in password reset initiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS account recovery requests where email domain/address validation is bypassed, incomplete, or returns unmatched-user results. Alert on patterns where password reset links are generated for email addresses with no legitimate association to the target account, especially in bulk from single source IP or user agent.

suggestion.title: Mass Account Recovery Requests from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article implies systematic exploitation across 20,000+ accounts: 'over 20,000 Instagram users had their accounts hijacked...attackers used Meta's AI-powered support system to reset passwords.' Bulk recovery requests are the attack's fingerprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single source IP/user agent initiating recovery requests for >10 accounts in 1 hour or >50 in 24 hours. Baseline normal support patterns by endpoint and flag anomalies. Prioritize accounts with no prior recovery activity within 90 days.

suggestion.title: Successful Login After Password Reset Without 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in and hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled,' establishing the post-hijack access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful password resets (via HTS or recovery path) with subsequent successful logins from different IP, user agent, or geography within 15 minutes. Prioritize accounts without 2FA or with recent 2FA disablement. Escalate bulk successful post-reset logins from same attacker IP.

suggestion.title: 2FA Disablement on Hijacked Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes accounts were hijacked 'without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled,' indicating either pre-existing absence or attacker-initiated disablement post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk 2FA disablement across multiple accounts during attack window (April 17 – May 31, 2026). Alert on 2FA changes immediately following password reset or recovery event. Flag accounts where 2FA transitions from enabled → disabled via unusual session.

suggestion.title: Bulk Recovery Contact Information Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers could access 'contact information (email address and/or phone number)' post-hijack. Detection should identify changes to recovery email/phone in bulk as persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk modifications to linked recovery email, backup email, or phone number across multiple accounts. Flag patterns where single IP/session modifies recovery contact for >5 accounts in 1 hour. Baseline against normal recovery contact change velocity.

suggestion.title: Invalid Email Matching in HTS Recovery Flow
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: HTS 'didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Detection must identify repeated email-account mismatches during recovery attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS logs for repeated email validation failures or email-account mismatch conditions (email X submitted for account Y where X is not linked to Y). Alert on patterns where single source iterates through email-account pairs not previously seen in recovery context. Detect template-based or enumeration-style requests.

suggestion.title: Vishing-preceded logon anomalies — failed auth spikes post-call
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'using phone calls' and 'vishing' as primary attack vector. Zero detection UC maps to this. Vishing typically precedes credential stuffing or MFA bypass attempts. Phrase: 'aggressive campaign...using phone calls...to break into corporate systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound call spikes (via PBX/VoIP logs if available) to targeted users with subsequent failed logon attempts, MFA rejections, or password reset requests within 15min-2hr window. Flag calls claiming IT/vendor support.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to data-leak domain business-data-leaks.com
suggestion.rationale: Article objective is to 'steal sensitive files' and explicitly names data-leak domain. No exfiltration UC despite clear C2 infrastructure. Phrase: 'exfiltrate data...data-leaks.com.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to business-data-leaks.com. Flag any successful egress with file-transfer indicators (large uploads, archive extensions, compression artifacts). Correlate timing with RMM session windows.

suggestion.title: Screen-sharing tool activation outside IT workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'screen-sharing tricks' as attack step but no UC covers this tactic. Non-malware RDP/screen-share tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Chrome Remote Desktop) activated by non-IT users or outside business hours. Phrase: 'screen-sharing tricks...remote monitoring software.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect screen-sharing tool spawning by non-IT-department users, especially during off-hours or if process parent is a user-initiated RDP session. Flag if tool connects to external IPs (vs. internal support infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Lateral movement post-RMM-install to law-firm-sensitive shares
suggestion.rationale: Article says 'break into corporate systems' (plural) after RMM installed. Implies lateral movement from initial compromise host. No UC hunts post-RMM lateral spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RMM-install, hunt RDP/SSH initiations from compromised host to other law-firm internal systems. Flag SMB connections to file servers, enumeration of admin shares, or port-scanning activity correlated with active RMM session.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting post-vishing — browser-based capture
suggestion.rationale: Vishing (social engineering) attack is entry point; adversaries harvest credentials after initial contact. Article doesn't detail this but is implicit in 'break into systems.' No UC maps to post-vishing credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-vishing, detect browser-based credential harvesting: fake login pages served locally, password-manager autofill anomalies, unusual API token generation, or clipboard monitoring. Correlate with call event timing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on Linux Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances'—implies malware execution post-compromise. Cross-platform variant suggests adapted command execution tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux appliances for unexpected process spawning, especially shell interpreters (bash, sh) launched by non-standard parents or from /tmp, /var/tmp. Cross-reference with known appliance management processes to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployment implies active C2 infrastructure. 'Deploys BSD Variant' suggests ongoing command and control capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Linux appliances to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Baseline appliance egress and flag deviations, especially to residential IP space or dynamic DNS providers.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cron or Systemd
suggestion.rationale: BRICKSTORM deployment on appliances suggests persistence mechanism installation. 'Deploys' indicates post-exploitation persistence setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of cron jobs on appliances, especially those pointing to /tmp, world-writable directories, or making network connections. Monitor systemd service file creation in /etc/systemd/system/.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Appliance Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Linux appliances often sit in critical network paths (firewalls, load balancers, proxies). BRICKSTORM deployment suggests pivot point for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB, SSH, or RDP traffic originating from compromised appliances to internal hosts. Flag multi-stage file transfers (especially to non-standard paths) on appliances.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Appliance Firmware or Package Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Deployment on multiple Linux appliances (plural, target class) suggests either: pre-compromised firmware, malicious package injection, or infrastructure-level delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate BRICKSTORM detections across multiple appliances of same model/firmware version. Investigate package manager history (apt, yum logs) for unexpected installations or version anomalies around deployment timeframe.

suggestion.title: File Indicators for BRICKSTORM BSD Variant
suggestion.rationale: Specific malware variant (BSD BRICKSTORM) should have distinctive file artifacts, path patterns, or binary signatures. Article should contain hash, path, or naming patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for files matching known BRICKSTORM naming patterns (if disclosed in full article), hidden files in standard locations, or unexpected binaries in /opt, /srv, or appliance-specific directories. Correlate file creation timestamps with known campaign dates.

suggestion.title: Phishing + AiTM Credential Theft Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'AI brands as bait... social engineering'. Keywords 'Adversary-in-the-middle' + 'Credential theft' indicate phishing emails spoofing AI services (ChatGPT/Claude/etc.) followed by AiTM interception of credentials and MFA codes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing emails with AI service domain spoofs to clicks on attacker infrastructure, then credential submissions to proxy-like SSL patterns or HTTP POSTs with username/password fields. Track successful sign-ins to legitimate service within 90s of failed attempt (MFA interception).

suggestion.title: Lookalike AI Brand Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering attack requires attacker-controlled domains impersonating legitimate AI brands. Article describes threat actors using 'AI hype as bait'—implies domain spoofing/typosquatting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and HTTPS certificate issuance for domains with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft AI product names. Flag WHOIS registrations by attacker-associated email patterns or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: MFA Code Interception via AiTM Proxy
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks intercept HTTPS traffic to steal real-time credentials and MFA tokens. 'Credential theft' keyword + social engineering setup implies 2FA/MFA bypass via credential capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA attempts followed by successful authentication from different IP than MFA challenge origin. Look for HTTPS traffic to unknown/attacker proxies that mirror legitimate AI service TLS fingerprints or cert subject names.

suggestion.title: Successful Login Post-Phishing Without Prior Failed Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Victims of AiTM attacks often see successful login (attacker replayed captured credentials) without initiating login themselves. Behavioral anomaly in article's described attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sign-in success for user from geography/IP mismatched to recent phishing email recipient's location. Prioritize if MFA was marked 'completed' but user has no record of MFA prompt on their device.

suggestion.title: Attacker-in-Middle TLS Certificate Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks require HTTPS interception. Article's mention of AiTM keyword implies threat actor deployed proxy capable of forging certs or exploiting certificate pinning gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSL/TLS connection errors (certificate name mismatch, untrusted CA) to legitimate AI service domains from endpoints that subsequently complete login to same service. Track self-signed or attacker-CA certificates for AI service domain spoofs in proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Email Sender Spoofing AI Brand Support Addresses
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via 'AI brands as bait' requires email impersonation of legitimate support/security teams from OpenAI, Anthropic, etc. Article setup centers on phishing lure credibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails claiming to be from support@openai.com, security@anthropic.com, etc., that fail DKIM/SPF/DMARC alignment or originate from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Inspect message body for urgency language typical of social engineering (account compromise, verification required, limited-time access).

suggestion.title: Detect high-volume email clusters with content similarity and anomalous sender diversity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'AI Phishing' and 'alert volume'—polymorphic/obfuscated phishing campaigns using generative AI would manifest as waves of similar emails from rotating sender accounts or spoofed internal addresses. Pipeline completely missed this baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster emails by body-text hash (>85% similarity) and subject-line pattern. Alert when >3 variants with identical content ship from >5 unique sender domains/IPs within 60 minutes to overlapping recipient lists. Exclude legitimate bulk senders via exclusion list.

suggestion.title: Detect email authentication bypass on high-confidence spoofed executive addresses
suggestion.rationale: Spoofing is foundational to phishing. Article says 'crushing SOCs'—implies high false-positive campaigns using internal-looking senders. Impersonation of executives/finance personnel failing SPF/DMARC should trigger alerts but pipeline captured nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails where sender display-name matches known executive (CEO, CFO, COO) or trusted-partner domain but SPF/DMARC fail and sender IP is not in corporate allow-list. Exclude third-party services with pre-approved SPF records.

suggestion.title: Detect user click-through on newly-registered domains in high-volume email campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses reducing SOC 'overload'—implies detection of phishing links that evade static IP/domain reputation. AI-generated phishing would use fast-flux or freshly-registered domains to bypass URL filters. Pipeline missed URL-chain detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate emails containing links to domains with WHOIS registration age <7 days and >10 click-throughs from employees. Cross-reference with endpoint telemetry for subsequent credential-entry, file-download, or browser-exploit patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect polymorphic attachment types in phishing emails
suggestion.rationale: AI-augmented phishing evasion includes novel/obfuscated file containers (ISO, VHD, double-extension, nested archives). Article title signals alert-volume evasion; attachment-type polymorphism is a clear tactic. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with attachment extensions (.iso, .vhd, .img, .7z, .rar) or double-extensions (.xlsx.exe, .pdf.scr). Correlate to endpoint file-execution events and process-launch chains (7z.exe → rundll32 → powershell). Tune for legitimate use of ISO attachments if present in environment.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass Exploitation (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs' and confirms active exploitation. Should detect VPN sessions established without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access for successful connection establishment without credential submission, IKEv1 handshakes completing without machine certificate validation, or connection state transitions from INIT to AUTHENTICATED bypassing credential prompts.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 and Legacy Client Configuration Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'affects only deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' with 'legacy Remote Access clients' and no machine certificate requirement. Configuration detection is prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Check Point Remote Access VPN gateway configured to accept IKEv1 key exchange where legacy remote access clients are supported and machine certificate authentication is not mandatory. Flag absence of IKEv2-only enforcement.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Access Ransomware Activity (Qilin)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' following successful VPN compromise. Must detect lateral movement and encryption phase within hours of external VPN access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful VPN connection from external IP with subsequent lateral movement (SMB scanning, credential dumping), enumeration of administrative shares, and mass file encryption activity on internal hosts within 1–4 hours of VPN session start.

suggestion.title: Site-to-Site VPN MITM and Certificate Validation Bypass (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second flaw: 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' No observed wild exploitation yet but represents active vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IKEv1 site-to-site VPN tunnels for certificate validation failures, unexpected certificate chains, or successful tunnel establishment despite certificate mismatch or expired/invalid certificates that should have terminated negotiation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous VPN Access from High-Risk Geography
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms exploitation window May 7 through early June targeting 'a few dozen organizations.' Detection should surface access patterns inconsistent with known business operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN connection attempts originating from countries with no known business presence, hosting providers, or Tor exit nodes. Correlate with recent failed authentication attempts or repeated connection retries from same external IP within short time window.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Exposed Service Enumeration (T1190 Asset Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability affects 'any authenticated user' on 'public-facing application.' T1190 requires identifying exposed instances before exploitation detection can trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed BerriAI LiteLLM instances: fingerprint service responses on standard ports (443, 8080, custom), correlate with vulnerability scanner gaps (article: 'scanners say not vulnerable' but service present), and identify instances lacking network restrictions or WAF coverage.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Detection in API Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article core vector: 'command injection vulnerability...run arbitrary commands.' Must match shell metacharacters and syntax in API parameters to LiteLLM endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests to LiteLLM endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), ``, >, <, newlines, backticks) in request body/parameters. Establish baseline of normal payload patterns per authenticated user. High-confidence indicator of exploitation attempt or successful RCE testing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Spawning from LiteLLM Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary commands on the host.' Service should spawn only model-inference processes; unexpected interactive shells, compilers, or network utilities indicate post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes from LiteLLM service (lightweight inference calls, logging). Alert on unexpected spawns: /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, gcc, python interpreter, curl, wget, nc from service context outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege API Key Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'low-privilege internal-user keys' sufficient for RCE. Detection must flag behavioral deviation from previously-low-risk credentials suddenly performing exploitation-like activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline activity (request rate, endpoint types, geographies, times) per API key. Alert on sudden deviations: low-privilege key accessing privileged endpoints, spike in request volume, requests from new ASNs/geographies, or rapid failed attempts prior to success.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised LiteLLM Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation: command execution from service account enables reconnaissance and lateral access to internal assets. Article doesn't detail this but standard follow-up to RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from LiteLLM service: unusual remote hosts, high-entropy domains, beaconing patterns, SMB/SSH to internal systems. Baseline expected external calls (model provider APIs, logging backends) and alert on deviations indicating C2 or internal movement.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning Blind Spot: Deployed vs. Scanner State
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable...patch lag is the silent killer.' Requires correlating scanner results against actual service inventory to find gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-42271 marked 'not vulnerable' where BerriAI LiteLLM is actually deployed (via service enumeration, port fingerprinting, asset tags). Identify scanner blind spots or false negatives and trigger manual verification/patching on 2026-06-22 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Vulnerable Check Point Gateway Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-50751 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV mandates remediation by 2026-06-11. Baseline detection is scanner match on exposed gateways.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Check Point Security Gateway devices running pre-patch versions or flagged vulnerable by Nessus/Qualys/Tenable for CVE-2026-50751. Cross-reference with SHODAN/Censys internet-facing inventories to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Authentication Bypass on Check Point Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange.' Exploitation leaves traces in IKEv1 logs: failed auth attempts followed by successful connection, or completed handshakes with no credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Check Point audit logs for IKEv1 key exchanges that complete successfully but lack corresponding RADIUS/LDAP/AD authentication events, or show 'authentication_passed' with null/empty credential fields.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Detection: VPN sessions with no preceding auth success event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN session initiations on Check Point gateways where no successful user authentication event (RADIUS/LDAP/local) precedes the session by >5 min, or where the authenticated username is empty/null.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Lateral Movement from Compromised Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gains VPN access as if authenticated; follow-on activity expected: host discovery, credential theft, persistence. Detect anomalous behavior from VPN-originated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful VPN sessions (originating from exploitation indicators) with rapid internal host scanning, RDP/SSH connection attempts, or process execution patterns typical of reconnaissance or lateral movement within 1 hour of VPN establishment.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will probe gateway version before exploitation. Article specifies vulnerability exists in 'Security Gateway' product; version banners or HTTP headers may leak version info.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated HTTP requests to Check Point admin ports (443/8443) that elicit version banners or error pages disclosing build/patch level, especially from IPs that subsequently attempt IKEv1 connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious UniFi API auth-validate-sso requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states defenders should 'look for requests containing /api/auth/validate-sso/' and details the root cause: authentication validates the raw URI while Nginx normalizes it differently, allowing bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to UniFi OS endpoints containing /api/auth/validate-sso/ patterns, especially with double-encoded characters (%252e), mixed encoding, or path traversal sequences. Alert on requests reaching this endpoint without valid authentication tokens or sessions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized access to ucs package update endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'monitor requests to ucs/update/latest_package' as detection method. This endpoint is targeted with CVE-2026-34910 command injection after authentication bypass by CVE-2026-34908/34909.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to /ucs/update/latest_package endpoint on UniFi OS Server without valid authentication context. Flag requests from external networks or lacking session tokens. Baseline legitimate update operations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected child processes under ucs-update service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'monitor suspicious child processes under ucs-update' as defensive detection method. Command injection (CVE-2026-34910) executes payloads under this service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent is ucs-update service. Baseline legitimate package operations. Alert on unexpected shell spawning (bash, sh, zsh), compilers, Python, perl, or network utilities (curl, wget, nc) under this service account.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via sudo from UniFi service account
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'affected service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial' and instructs to monitor 'unexpected sudo commands'. Service account has passwordless sudo to system binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sudo command execution by UniFi service accounts (unifi, ucs-update). Alert on any sudo invocation, particularly passwordless execution of /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other system binaries. Establish baseline and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: URI normalization bypass attempts on protected endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explains root cause: 'authentication component evaluates raw request URI while Nginx routes based on normalized version. Crafting requests that appear to target auth-exempt endpoints in raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization.' This is the bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests where raw and normalized URI forms diverge on UniFi endpoints. Look for double-encoding (%252e%252f), Unicode escapes (%u002e), mixed case tricks, or double slashes (//). Alert where raw form targets auth-exempt path but normalized resolves to protected API.

suggestion.title: Path traversal attempts in UniFi OS file access
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-34909 is 'path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on underlying operating system'. Article notes attackers chain this with CVE-2026-34908 to bypass authentication and reach vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to UniFi OS endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f, %5c%5c, backslash encoding) or attempting to access files outside intended directories. Flag probing toward /etc/, /var/, /root/, or configuration paths via the management interface.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request with phar:/// Triple-Slash Stream Wrapper (CVE-2026-45034)
suggestion.rationale: Article core exploit mechanism: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner with three or more slashes after the scheme...' This is the direct technical indicator of exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing phar:// (literal or URL-encoded phar%3A%2F%2F) with three+ consecutive slashes targeting web applications. Key differentiator: phar:/// (exploit bypass pattern) vs. normal phar:// (expected behavior). Correlate with applications running PHPSpreadsheet.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Shell or CLI Tool After Spreadsheet Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly maps T1059 Command Interpreter, T1059.004 Unix Shell, T1059.001 PowerShell—all post-RCE indicators. Web-server processes should never spawn shells under normal operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web-server parent processes (php-fpm, php, apache2, httpd, nginx, w3wp) spawn shell interpreters (bash, sh, zsh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or network tools (curl, wget, nc, python) within seconds of processing a phar or malicious spreadsheet file.

suggestion.title: Phar Archive File Creation Initiated by Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in phar extraction and code execution. Article maps T1505.003 Web Shell—phar file creation is the artifact of this post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-creation events where initiating process is a web-server binary and filename ends with .phar, or where file is created in web-accessible directories (webroot, temp). Elevated confidence if timeline correlates with unusual HTTP request to upload/processing endpoint.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PHPSpreadsheet Version Detected in Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45034 is explicitly a bypass of CVE-2026-34084 patch. Unpatched version detection is the primary prevention and recon-phase detection vector for CVSS 9+ advisory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory, dependency manifests (composer.json, composer.lock), and scanning tools for hosts running PHPSpreadsheet versions below the patch level for CVE-2026-45034. Prioritize assets with public-facing file-upload or document-processing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Spreadsheet or Archive File Access in Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker-controlled file delivery (T1566 Phishing, T1190 Public App Exploit). Post-delivery file-access patterns immediately preceding RCE are direct exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events in web-server temp/upload directories: spreadsheet file uploaded, immediately accessed/extracted by web process, followed by phar-related file operations or unscheduled child-process spawning. Timeline clustering indicates active exploitation.

suggestion.title: osascript invoked with AppleScript breakout pattern (nested tell blocks + do shell script)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes payload injection into osascript with nested 'tell application' blocks and 'do shell script' escape. This is the exact exploitation signature; article body states vulnerability 'interpolates a…' (truncated) into AppleScript and shows detection for 'mismatched tell blocks'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect osascript execution where command line contains ≥2 occurrences of 'tell application' and 'do shell script' together—signature of payload injection. Parent process or context may reference browser plugin (Chrome, Brave, Edge) or anyquery binary. Look for quote-escaping and shell-metacharacter breakouts in the AppleScript payload.

suggestion.title: Browser extension (Chrome/Brave/Edge) spawning macOS scripting interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'chrome_tabs plugin (and equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari variants)' and vulnerability is 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection via Unescaped URL'—browser context → osascript/jscript execution chain is the core attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent process chain: Chrome, Brave, Edge, Safari → osascript, jscript, or node with command-line containing unescaped quotes, backticks, or shell metacharacters. Correlation with anyquery extension path or seturl.js increases confidence.

suggestion.title: seturl.js process execution or file modification (Anyquery plugin staging artifact)
suggestion.rationale: Article's recommended hunt UC_1_1 explicitly searches for 'seturl.js' as file name. This is named artifact from the vulnerable plugin; pipeline should have extracted it as file/process IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process execution or file creation/modification events involving seturl.js. Correlation with /Applications/Anyquery or similar plugin directories, and time-proximity to osascript child processes, increases signal.

suggestion.title: JXA (JavaScript for Automation) execution via osascript -l JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection'—JXA is distinct from AppleScript and invoked via 'osascript -l JavaScript'. Should be separated from generic AppleScript detections because JXA can eval() and Function() construct code dynamically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor osascript with '-l JavaScript' flag or .js/.jxa file arguments. JXA payloads may contain eval(), Function(), or ObjC.import('Foundation') to access system APIs and shells. Look for spawn/fork calls from osascript process.

suggestion.title: Malicious URL with unescaped metacharacters triggering plugin code path (T1204.002)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'Unescaped URL in macOS Chrome Plugin'—users are tricked into opening URLs containing quotes, backticks, semicolons, pipes, or newlines that break out of the plugin's script context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser history/visited URLs containing shell metacharacters (\', \", \`, \;, \|, \n) or AppleScript keywords ('tell', 'end tell', 'do shell script') with subsequent osascript execution in <10 second window. URL-to-execution time proximity + plugin context = high fidelity.

suggestion.title: Anyquery application version inventory (vulnerability scoping: ≤0.4.4 commit 0abd460)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Affected version 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460)'—asset-inventory hunt to identify which systems have vulnerable Anyquery version installed and running.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for anyquery process with version string matching ≤0.4.4, commit 0abd460. Check /Applications/Anyquery.app or similar plugin directory timestamps and file manifests. Escalate to patching workflow once inventory is built.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — CA enumeration and credential leakage via /api/v1/cas endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The Web UI gates state-changing routes through loadAccessibleCA...per-CA ownership is enforced only in the Web layer.' and 'CA-management endpoints in internal/api/cas.go'. This indicates /api/v1/cas/* endpoints exist but are not listed in the 5 provided hunts. Direct API calls bypass Web-layer ownership checks, enabling cross-CA enumeration and potential credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /api/v1/cas or /api/v1/cas/*/credentials from non-admin contexts or users who have not previously accessed CA-admin functions. Flag patterns indicating enumeration of all CAs in a deployment vs. only CAs the bearer token's operator should access.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — API key exfiltration and private key harvesting via /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys GET
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1212 (Exploitation for Credential Access) and T1552.004 (Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys) as techniques. UC_0_1 covers minting NEW keys, but no hunt covers extracting EXISTING keys or private key material from other operators' contexts. The bearer-token-alone trust model permits unauthorized GET requests to key metadata and potentially key material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /api/v1/operators/{target_id}/api-keys or /api/v1/operators/{target_id}/api-keys/{key_id} where target_id does not match the bearer token's operator context. Correlate with any response codes ≥ 200 <300 to identify successful key enumeration or key-material disclosure.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — host certificate and enrollment secret harvesting via /api/v1/hosts/{id} GET
suggestion.rationale: UC_0_2 covers re-enrollment (POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll), but no hunt covers initial reconnaissance (GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}) to retrieve existing host certificates, enrollment tokens, or secrets that belong to other operators' hosts. The lack of per-CA ownership checks permits cross-operator read access to sensitive host identity material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /api/v1/hosts/{target_host_id} from a bearer token whose operator differs from the host's owning operator. Alert on any HTTP 200 response indicating successful retrieval of host secrets or enrollment material.

suggestion.title: Gogs Account Creation by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account' and 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false)' — baseline initial access required for exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs registration events for accounts created by external IP addresses. Alert on new account registration followed immediately by repository creation or merge operations within same session.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Creation by Low-Privilege User
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'no limit on repository creation (MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = -1)' and attacker 'creates a repository on any default-configured instance' — mandatory step before merge-based RCE trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid repository creation by newly registered accounts (account age < 1 hour). Flag repos created with suspicious naming patterns or by users with no commit history.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Setting Enabled on Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and exploit 'can be operated without interaction from any other user' — configuration change triggers vulnerable Merge() code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log repository advanced settings modifications, specifically merge strategy changes. Alert when rebase merge is enabled on newly created repos or by accounts with no prior fork/merge activity.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection in Gogs Merge() Function Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'argument injection vulnerability' affecting 'Merge() code path that was never addressed' — direct RCE trigger via merge operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs merge operation logs for unusual branch names containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, backticks, `&`, `$()`) or command sequences. Track unexpected child process spawning from Gogs daemon during merge operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Repository Access via Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers can 'access any repositories (including private ones)' post-RCE — lateral movement within repository access scope after code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when merge/service account context accesses repositories outside expected operational boundaries or reads private repos from merge process context. Flag unauthorized file system reads of .git directories.

suggestion.title: Source Code Alteration via Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'alter any hosted source code' — impact detection on unexpected commits from service/merge account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits from service account, merge account, or system context; commits with non-human authorship metadata; or unexpected code modifications in protected branches. Monitor for commits altering CI/CD configs, build scripts, or deployment mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Malspam with DoubleClick Redirect Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malspam campaign' using 'Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims'. This is the primary initial-access vector (T1566 + T1199) establishing the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with embedded links containing doubleclick.net redirects that ultimately resolve to identified malicious domains. Correlate email recipients with downstream HTTP requests to those C2 domains within 5 minutes of click.

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fileless .NET loader' and 'type of malware that runs', indicating in-memory execution without persistent disk writes. Standard file-hash IOC detection is insufficient.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for System.Diagnostics.Process, AppDomain.Load, or CLR runtime invocations with suspicious/empty command-line arguments originating from email or browser processes. Alert on rundll32.exe or powershell.exe child of explorer/Outlook with .NET CLR execution.

suggestion.title: In-Memory .NET Assembly Loading via Reflection
suggestion.rationale: Fileless execution implies [Reflection.Assembly]::Load() from byte arrays or remote streams without disk presence. Article's '.NET loader' terminology is diagnostic for this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell script blocks containing [Reflection.Assembly]::Load() or [AppDomain]::CurrentDomain.Load with base64-encoded or remote-URI arguments, immediately followed by .Invoke() method calls on unverified types.

suggestion.title: Trusted Infrastructure Weaponized as C2 Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attackers 'hiding behind a name that most systems trust without question'—DoubleClick is legitimate Google infrastructure being abused as a C2 redirect layer (T1199).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirect chains where doubleclick.net is an intermediate hop to non-ad-network terminal destinations, especially to the identified malicious domains (xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net, etc.). Flag DoubleClick-to-C2 proxying patterns.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated .NET Loader File Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Obfuscated Files or Information (T1027)' and provides 5 SHA256 hashes for loader samples. Beyond hash matching, detect obfuscated .NET characteristics (stripped metadata, encrypted resources, high entropy sections).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET PE files with suspicious entropy, renamed CLR metadata streams (#Strings/#Blob mangled), packed sections, or modified CLR headers. Behavioral correlation: recent email delivery + obfuscated .NET file + subsequent C2 domain connection.

suggestion.title: Domain IOC Network Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Seven C2 domains provided (fostercareintheus.optimizationprime.com, bth.startthewave.org, etc.). Pipeline failed to extract; standard network IOC hunt is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or network connections to the seven identified domains. Correlate with process creation (esp. browser/email children) and file hash matches to confirm multi-stage delivery chain.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL detection targeting WhatsApp users
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack' — phishing is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection logic for malicious URLs delivered via messaging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks on suspicious URLs in WhatsApp context, particularly newly registered domains, shortened URLs mimicking WhatsApp infrastructure, or known NSO Group phishing domains. Flag rapid redirects to credential-harvesting pages.

suggestion.title: NSO Group infrastructure and C2 domain blocking
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group explicitly named in title — domain IOCs and malicious infrastructure should have been extracted and mapped to C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on DNS queries and outbound connections to known/suspected NSO Group infrastructure (Pegasus C2, exploit server domains, command infrastructure). Include behavioral signatures for obfuscated C2 communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous WhatsApp account authentication and device registration
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks against WhatsApp aim to compromise accounts or install spyware on devices — account takeover and unauthorized registration should generate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new WhatsApp logins from geographically impossible locations, new device registrations following phishing link clicks, and logins from IP space associated with NSO infrastructure.

suggestion.title: User execution of malicious links from messaging applications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes phishing attack — user clicks on malicious links are the execution mechanism and should be detected as T1204.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on suspicious URLs delivered via WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. Alert on clicks followed by credential entry, binary downloads, or redirects to known credential-harvesting domains.

suggestion.title: Pegasus spyware execution and post-compromise behavior
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group's primary tool is Pegasus — if phishing succeeds at execution level, Pegasus installation and behavior patterns must be detected (process creation, hook injection, privilege escalation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for characteristic Pegasus process patterns, suspicious inter-process communication, kernel module loading, and file creation in known exploit or hook directories on affected devices.

suggestion.title: Emerging NSO Group phishing technique variations post-block
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Files Contempt Order' — indicates repeat activity and legal escalation, suggesting NSO Group is evolving phishing techniques to bypass detection and Meta's enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track new domain registrations, IP ranges, and obfuscation techniques associated with NSO Group post-enforcement. Monitor for phishing payloads using new URL shorteners, new SMTP relays, or compromised hosting.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states group 'deploying tools designed to evade every detection method' to IIS servers. Execution-phase file creation is completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .aspx, .asmx, .ashx file writes to inetpub\wwwroot and application directories. Correlate file creation timestamps with w3wp.exe process activity and HTTP requests to new paths within 60 seconds of write.

suggestion.title: Cryptographic Obfuscation in Web Shell Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat's signature evasion mechanism: 'cryptographically unique web shell framework.' This obfuscation pattern itself is the detectable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt IIS access logs for anomalously high-entropy POST bodies, base64/hex-encoded content, and multi-stage decoding patterns directed at suspicious .aspx paths. Baseline entropy thresholds against known legitimate applications.

suggestion.title: Web Shell C2 Outbound Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies application-layer protocol C2. Web shell persistence requires callback to external command server; outbound HTTP from IIS is primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe outbound HTTP(S) to OP-512 IOC destinations (43.160.202.246, 140.206.161.227, 124.156.129.151, ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com). Flag periodic callback intervals, small encrypted payloads, or User-Agent anomalies.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Process Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Web shells enable arbitrary command execution within IIS context. Article targets IIS exclusively; missing detection for process spawn from w3wp.exe or application pool identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious binaries spawned from w3wp.exe parent or IIS application pool accounts. Suppress known benign application startup sequences via whitelist.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Multi-Vendor Keystore Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets crypto wallets: malware accesses Ethereum, Bitcoin, Exodus, Electrum, MetaMask, Phantom, Atomic keystores. Article phrase: 'Targets 18 Browsers, Crypto Wallets, and Discord Tokens'. Single UC_CRYPTO_WALLET template insufficient; wallet keystore access pattern more specific than filesystem paths alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-wallet-process access to multiple wallet keystores within 60-second window across Ethereum\keystore, Bitcoin\wallet.dat, Exodus wallets, Electrum wallets, and browser-extension wallet Local Storage directories. Escalate on recursive directory enumeration patterns preceding archive creation (RAR, ZIP) to staging directories.

suggestion.title: Remote Access / RAT Behavior Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can take full control of an infected machine'—explicit remote command execution capability. Missing from briefing despite being core attack vector. Phrase: 'Hidden Remote Access'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for interactive session spawning (explorer.exe parent changed, WinLogon spawning cmd.exe), persistence registry paths (Run, RunOnce, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon), and bidirectional network persistence to article IOCs after initial malware execution.

suggestion.title: Discord Token/Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names Discord tokens as explicit target: 'Targets 18 Browsers, Crypto Wallets, and Discord Tokens'. Not covered by generic UC_BROWSER_STEALER. Requires Discord-specific data locations and API patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag non-Discord processes accessing AppData\Local\Discord directories, LocalStorage, or reading leveldb/sqlite databases where tokens are cached. Monitor for HTTPS connections from non-Discord processes to discord.com API endpoints, especially to /api/v*/auth or /api/v*/users/@me endpoints immediately post-malware execution.

suggestion.title: Telegram Underground Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions discovery vector: 'Discovered through underground channels linked to Telegram'. Implies Telegram distribution mechanism should be detected. Phrase establishes infection pathway not in IOC list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Telegram.exe, telegram.exe, or Telegram client process performing file downloads to user temp/Downloads directories, especially .exe/.msi/.scr files. Correlate against article domains/IPs for secondary staging. Monitor for legitimate Telegram infrastructure abuse followed by process execution and pivot to article C2.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Database Bulk Operations
suggestion.rationale: Targets '18 Browsers' but UC_BROWSER_STEALER detects single-file access. Stealers perform batch operations: sequential reads across all browser credential stores in <30 seconds, followed by copy/archive to staging. Current UC misses exfiltration prep phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reading multiple browser credential files (Chrome Login Data, Firefox logins.json, Brave/Edge equivalents) within short time window, followed by file copy/move operations to temp/AppData staging directories, then followed by compression tool invocation (7z, WinRAR, built-in tar).

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails with Credential-Harvesting Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article states group 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials'; domain naming pattern (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) strongly suggests fake authentication portals. No phishing detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with urgency language targeting cloud storage users (Office 365, Google Workspace, OneDrive, Dropbox), containing embedded links to attacker domains. Flag emails requesting password re-entry, MFA re-enrollment, or security verification from external senders. Correlate with user clicks to the identified domains.

suggestion.title: Brute Force and Credential Stuffing Against Cloud Storage APIs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector described as 'steal cloud storage credentials'—requires detection of multiple failed auth attempts and subsequent successful login, yet pipeline generated no credential-access use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts (5+ in 10 minutes) against cloud storage services from internal users, followed by successful login with different client IP/user-agent, particularly from the indicator IPs. Alert on successful login immediately after phishing campaign timing.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Pink Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victim data being 'listed' on dedicated leak site launched May 31, 2026. Pipeline did not generate exfiltration detection for the identified C2 domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file transfers or data exports (compressed archives, database dumps, credential caches) to the identified domains passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com. Correlate with recent successful cloud storage authentication and large volume outbound connections from compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fake Passkey / MFA Enrollment Interception
suggestion.rationale: All three attacker domains contain 'passkey' + administrative verb terminology (add/deploy), indicating modern MFA bypass or FIDO2 interception lures—a critical detection gap given the specific naming pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user navigation to domains containing 'passkey' + (add|deploy|enroll|register|setup) that are not in approved cloud provider CNAME records. Alert especially on clicks from phishing email campaigns and followed by MFA re-setup activity in legitimate cloud account audit logs.

suggestion.title: Enriched Pink Attribution Alerting (CL-CRI-1147)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline identified cluster code CL-CRI-1147 but did not create enriched detection rules tagging network events with Pink actor attribution and kill-chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Any detection hitting the six IOCs should be auto-enriched with CL-CRI-1147 attribution, Pink threat group name, attack narrative summary, and kill-chain phase. Create a master alert that correlates: phishing email → credential harvest domain click → failed auth spike → successful auth from attacker IP → data exfil to leak site domain.

suggestion.title: Python .pth Malicious Startup Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file, which then tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script.' This is the core execution vector but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .pth files created or modified in Python site-packages directories, especially those with recent timestamps or unusual ownership. Correlate with Python interpreter startup followed by child process spawning (curl, wget, Bun binary). Flag process chains where Python → external runtime (Bun) execute immediately after startup with network activity.

suggestion.title: Bun JavaScript Runtime Download and Execution from Python Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states the malware 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script _index.js.' This delivery mechanism and execution chain is specific and detectable but was not captured in any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections from Python processes to github.com for Bun binary downloads (oven-sh/bun releases). Alert on Bun process spawning from non-standard directories (temp, site-packages). Monitor for Python → curl/wget → Bun → _index.js execution chains, especially if the Bun binary is downloaded immediately after Python startup.

suggestion.title: Harvesting and Exfiltration of Developer Secrets to GitHub Actions Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific credential targets: 'GitHub tokens, npm/PyPI/RubyGems tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes/Vault credentials, SSH keys, Docker credentials, .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, shell histories, Claude/MCP configuration files' and exfil method: 'automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions.' No detection use case for this systematic harvesting and staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes (Python, JavaScript) accessing credential files: .env, .npmrc, .pypirc, .ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, .aws/credentials, shell history files. Correlate file reads with GitHub authentication or API operations (git push, gh api). Flag when developer tool subprocesses enumerate multiple credential sources in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Spoofed Anthropic API Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'A second exfiltration method based on direct HTTPS also exists, pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage.' This is an explicit C2 endpoint but was not extracted as an IOC or detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS POST requests to api.anthropic.com/v1/api from Python or Bun processes; this endpoint is non-existent and not used by legitimate Anthropic clients. Alert if credentials or encoded payloads appear in request bodies. Correlate with prior file access to .env, SSH keys, and other credential sources.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd Services, LaunchAgents, and GitHub Workflow Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used.' None of these persistence vectors were captured in detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of systemd service files in /etc/systemd/system or ~/.config/systemd/user with Python/Bun interpreter references. On macOS, alert on LaunchAgent plist creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. Detect modification of GitHub workflows (.github/workflows) and Claude/MCP config files (.claude/claude.json or similar) by non-standard processes. Correlate with supply-chain compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Russian Locale Checks and StepSecurity Harden-Runner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The malware also features some evasion mechanisms, such as checking for Russian locales/environments, and security tools such as StepSecurity Harden-Runner.' This intentional defense evasion logic is not represented in any detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor _index.js execution for conditional logic checking LANG, LC_ALL, or LC_* environment variables for Russian locales. Alert on process execution that invokes grep/findstr/ps commands searching for 'StepSecurity' or 'Harden-Runner' strings, indicating attacker awareness of CI hardening. Flag conditional execution where malicious behavior is suppressed based on these checks.

suggestion.title: Android: Suspicious APK Installation from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes victims 'redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file' for fake banking app updates. No detection coverage for non-Play-Store APK sourcing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK downloads from GitHub domains (github.com, github.io) to Android devices. Correlate with subsequent suspicious permission requests (NFC access). Flag repos created recently (article's April 10 creation date) hosting payment-card-app-named APKs.

suggestion.title: Phishing: Fake Banking Domain with Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins when 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials.' No detection for phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lookalike domains mimicking Italian/Spanish banks (Intesa, Caixa, Banca Sella, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney). Alert on credential submission to these domains followed by APK download offers. Baseline domain creation against banking sector.

suggestion.title: Mobile: NFC Data Exfiltration to WebSocket C2
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands' and 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' No detection for anomalous NFC activity or WebSocket C2 comms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebSocket connections from Android devices to unknown/external endpoints. Correlate with NFC chip access permissions and EMV command execution. Monitor for IsoDep protocol calls in app lifecycle preceding network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Android: Malformed APK Packaging and Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'introduction of malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis' via 'poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP.' Specific anti-analysis technique not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK files with ZIP extraction errors, malformed manifest paths, or incomplete/invalid internal structure. Alert on APK installs that bypass signature verification due to packaging anomalies. Correlate with known malware families.

suggestion.title: Threat Intel: GitHub Repository Abuse for Malware Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GitHub repository used for distributing NFCShare has hosted 56 unique APKs' created April 10, 2026. Enterprise risk signal: legitimate code hosting used as malware CDN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub for newly created repos with payment-app-themed names targeting financial institutions. Flag repos with binary/APK release artifacts and low activity/short lifetime. Alert on mass downloads of APKs from banking-themed repos by Android User-Agents.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering: SMS/Phone Calls from Fake Bank Representatives
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'SMS messages or phone calls from fake bank representatives may also be used as part of the social-engineering process,' establishing multi-channel attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If voice/SMS telemetry available: detect caller ID spoofing mimicking bank numbers, urgency language directing to app updates, requests for personal/card data verification. Correlate with phishing site hits in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Memory Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes 'enables local root access'—textbook privilege escalation. 'One-character' flaw suggests tight code path in privilege-check or capability-handling logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unprivileged processes for privilege transitions to root. Flag unusual system call sequences (prctl, bpf, perf_event_open, capset, mmap with PROT_EXEC) preceding uid/gid changes. Correlate with kernel error messages (dmesg) or capability drops.

suggestion.title: Public Exploit Code Execution for Local Privilege Escalation
