suggestion.rationale: Article states breach affected 'SoFi Securities (Hong Kong) Limited via one of its vendors'—indicates attacker leveraged trusted vendor account to access the subsidiary database. Pipeline should detect lateral movement and privilege misuse via trusted relationships.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vendor-provisioned credentials access SoFi subsidiary databases from unexpected geographies, outside business hours, or with permission escalation. Baseline normal vendor access patterns and flag significant deviations.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Data Export from Production Database
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'database...containing customer information' and company statement 'we do not yet have complete information about...which categories of your personal data was involved' indicate significant bulk exfiltration occurred. Pipeline should detect unusual data volumes leaving the database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk data dumps, database backups, or unusually large data transfers from SoFi Securities database to external IPs or cloud storage, especially when initiated by vendor service accounts. Baseline normal export volumes and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Inbound phone calls followed by credential entry or RMM install (vishing sequence)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'phone calls' and 'vishing' as initial access vector (headline attack method). Pipeline completely missed this. Splunk/Teams/phone logs show inbound call → rapid shift to credential portal access or RMM tool download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phone system logs (Cisco UC, Avaya, Teams call logs) showing inbound call from external numbers, then correlate within 5 min to: (a) failed login attempts to credential portal, (b) successful MFA push acceptance from unusual location, or (c) RMM tool process creation. High fidelity if call duration < 10 min (typical vishing duration).

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration to business-data-leaks.com and related leak marketplaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat goal is 'exfiltrate data' and provides domain 'business-data-leaks.com.' Pipeline detected domain IOC but created no exfiltration hunt. Law firms have massive sensitivity to data loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS requests to business-data-leaks.com and similar known data-leak marketplace domains (maintain list; update monthly from threat feeds). Correlate with RMM user session context or file access patterns from sensitive directories (/legal, /contracts, etc.).

suggestion.title: Screen-sharing software unusual execution or persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'screen-sharing tricks' as attack method but pipeline only detects RMM installation, not actual screen-sharing use or lateral movement via screen-sharing sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect screen-sharing app execution with unexpected parent process (e.g., TeamViewer spawned by wscipt.vbs or cmd.exe, not user double-click). Monitor for persistence registry modifications (Run key additions for AnyDesk, TeamViewer). Flag if RMM tool is launched in user context but connects to attacker-controlled C2 IP (cross-reference IOC list).

suggestion.title: Sensitive file access from RMM-spawned processes
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain includes data exfiltration, but pipeline has no hunt for *what* was accessed. Law firms deal in intellectual property (contracts, depositions, case strategy). Should detect file access patterns anomalous for RMM user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads/writes initiated by RMM parent process (AnyDesk.exe, TeamViewer.exe) accessing shared drives or user profile folders with law-firm-sensitive naming patterns (e.g., files containing 'contract', 'discovery', 'deposition', 'confidential'). Baseline per user; flag reads outside normal job function.

suggestion.title: Vishing Attack: Suspicious Phone Calls to Employees
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Vishing'—social engineering phone calls designed to extract credentials or bypass MFA. Article describes this as primary initial access vector. No use case generated despite being attack name headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phone calls to finance/HR/IT staff claiming to be vendors/contractors requesting password resets, MFA bypass, or access credentials. Correlate with failed login attempts or legitimate password reset requests within 30 min of call logs. Monitor for patterns of calls from external numbers to same department.

suggestion.title: Physical Intrusion: Unauthorized Building Access After Hours
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Physical Intrusions' as explicit attack vector. No detection use case for tailgating, badge cloning, or unauthorized access to data centers/server rooms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on badge access to restricted areas (data centers, server rooms, executive floors) during non-business hours or outside employee scheduled work hours. Detect rapid badge swipes (tailgating indicator). Correlate with CCTV footage requests or badge-holder absence during time of access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Data Exfiltration: Large File Transfers to External Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly targets 'Data Theft' for extortion. No detection for collection or exfiltration patterns despite this being the payload and revenue model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file uploads to consumer cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Mega, etc.) or unknown S3 buckets from corporate network. Baseline normal upload volumes per user; flag >3 std dev. Exclude known backup/sync tools. Monitor for transfers of sensitive data classifications (CONFIDENTIAL, HR, Financial).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting: Secondary MFA Enrollment After Vishing
suggestion.rationale: Vishing attacks typically aim to extract credentials or enroll attacker device in MFA. No detection for abnormal MFA enrollments or secondary device registration post-social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MFA device enrollment (authenticator app, security key, phone number add) from unusual geography or on same day/hour as phishing/social engineering report. Flag if enrolled by user account but from IP/device not previously seen in 90 days. Correlate with failed login attempts before enrollment.

suggestion.title: Extortion Demand Communications: Email/Dark Web Post Mentioning Stolen Data
suggestion.rationale: Campaign goal is 'Data Theft Extortion'—implies adversary will publish extortion demands with proof of stolen data (file lists, screenshots, samples). No detection for ransom communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails for ransom demand language + attachments containing stolen data samples (e.g., database dumps, employee lists, financial records). Cross-reference email sender/subject with known extortion group naming patterns. Alert if company name/data appears in dark web marketplaces or leaked data aggregators.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: SMB/RDP Access from Physical Intrusion Pivot Point
suggestion.rationale: Physical intrusion provides foothold on premises; attacker would then move laterally from access point (reception PC, maintenance terminal, network closet switch) to servers/sensitive systems. No detection for this post-compromise phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP/SMB connections originating from unusual internal devices (lobby kiosks, HVAC terminals, maintenance stations, network jacks in non-IT areas). Flag lateral movement from one unusual source to file servers or domain controllers. Monitor for process execution (cmd.exe, PowerShell) from these low-trust source IPs.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Malware Execution on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'BRICKSTORM' and 'BSD Variant' deployed on 'Linux Appliances'—no detection rule exists for this malware family or its execution patterns on Linux hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of unknown/unsigned ELF binaries or BSD-compiled executables on Linux appliances. Flag processes with names or command lines matching BRICKSTORM signatures (hash-based if available) or suspicious process spawning from /tmp, /dev/shm, or world-writable directories typical of malware deployment.

suggestion.title: Linux Persistence via Cron/Systemd (VerdantBamboo/BRICKSTORM)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'deployment' of malware to appliances—implied persistence mechanism not detailed in title, but typical for appliance backdoors. Article phrase 'Deploys' suggests sustained foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of cron jobs (/etc/cron.d, /var/spool/cron), systemd unit files (/etc/systemd/system), or init.d scripts on Linux appliances within hours of suspicious process execution or file drops. Cross-correlate with BRICKSTORM file signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Suspicious ELF Binary Drop on Appliance
suggestion.rationale: BSD variant of BRICKSTORM implies compiled binary deployment. Title mentions 'Deploys'—file write or drop event should precede execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect write or download of non-signed ELF or BSD binaries to appliance filesystems, especially in /tmp, /opt, /home, or vendor-specific directories. Alert if binary subsequently executed with elevated privileges or network activity follows within seconds.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from Linux Appliance (BRICKSTORM)
suggestion.rationale: BRICKSTORM is named as a malware family (implied to have C2 or exfil capabilities); article does not describe initial access method, but C2 callbacks are expected for an 'appliance' backdoor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections from Linux appliances for indicators matching BRICKSTORM C2 infrastructure (if available from threat feeds). Flag long-duration or periodic beacons to known or suspicious external IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Appliance
suggestion.rationale: VerdantBamboo targeting 'Linux Appliances' (plural, infrastructure context) suggests pivot opportunity; article does not detail internal exploitation but appliance backdoors typically enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After BRICKSTORM execution on appliance, alert on SSH/RDP lateral movement attempts, SCP/rsync file transfers, or exploitation traffic from the compromised appliance to internal network resources.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — FFmpeg Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-39210 through CVE-2026-39218 affecting FFmpeg. Pipeline narrative acknowledges 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' but generates zero use cases. Need detection for installed FFmpeg versions against CVE list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package managers, process listings, and file manifests for FFmpeg binary presence and version. Cross-reference installed versions against CVE-2026-39210..39218 vulnerable ranges. Prioritize cloud infrastructure and surveillance system asset inventories where FFmpeg is embedded.

suggestion.title: Network Packet — 183-Byte FFmpeg RCE Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'single 183-byte network packet' as exploitation vector: 'critical RCE-capable heap buffer overflow reachable with a single 183-byte network packet'. Pipeline identifies T1190 but not the specific packet signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound packets to FFmpeg-listening ports (commonly RTMP 1935, HTTP 80/443 for media streaming) for payloads ~183 bytes. Correlate packet size anomaly with FFmpeg process restarts or child process spawning. Baseline normal media stream packet sizes per deployment.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Child Process — FFmpeg RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes heap buffer overflow leading to 'Remote Code Execution'. Once exploited, attacker gains code execution context within FFmpeg process or escalated shell. Need detection of child processes spawned from or injected into FFmpeg.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal child process creation under FFmpeg parent (ffmpeg.exe, libavformat libraries). Flag shell spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash), reverse shells, or unexpected network utilities (curl, wget, nc) as children of media processing services. Monitor DLL injection into media libraries.

suggestion.title: Surveillance/Streaming Platform Compromise — FFmpeg in Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states FFmpeg 'quietly powers media processing across browsers, streaming platforms, surveillance systems, and cloud infrastructure'. These are high-impact deployment contexts requiring distinct hunt. No use case generated for this detection scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for FFmpeg deployments in surveillance systems, streaming platforms, and CDN infrastructure. Correlate outbound command-and-control or data exfiltration traffic from these nodes. Establish baseline for normal streaming/surveillance packet volumes and flag anomalies post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption Memory Pattern — Buffer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'heap buffer overflow' as root cause of RCE. Behavioral detection for heap corruption can catch exploitation even without IOC matching. Pipeline does not suggest memory anomaly hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg processes for abnormal memory access patterns: repeated allocation/deallocation near heap boundaries, Out-of-Bounds (OOB) writes, or Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE) detection via EDR/CFG logs. Correlate heap exceptions with process dumps and backward-search for triggering packets.

suggestion.title: Browser-Embedded FFmpeg Exploitation — Media Processing RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article lists browsers as deployment context: 'Quietly powers media processing across browsers'. Browser-based FFmpeg exploitation is distinct attack surface (malicious video uploads, crafted media files in web apps) from server-side. Pipeline does not segment by deployment context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe) spawning media-processing subprocesses with unusual arguments or network behavior. Flag video uploads/streams followed by child process creation. Monitor malicious media file uploads to web applications that invoke server-side FFmpeg.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Installation by Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '23 newly discovered malicious PyPI packages' targeting 'MCP developers.' The pipeline generated zero hunts despite the recommended hunts section showing multiple working examples. Need to detect pip/pip3 installation of unknown/suspicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for `pip install` / `python -m pip` commands installing packages not in organization's approved package list, especially with version constraints suggesting typosquatting. Correlate with parent process (IDE, terminal, scripts) and user context (dev account vs service account).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution Post-Python Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as an attack technique. Malicious packages will execute obfuscated payloads on import/install. No hunt was generated for detection of this execution phase despite being a core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter spawning encoded/exec calls, base64 decoding in process command line, or unusual child process launches (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from python.exe context immediately after pip install activity. Look for process command lines containing `exec()`, `compile()`, `__import__()` patterns.

suggestion.title: MCP Development Framework Files/Directories Created by Untrusted Python Packages
suggestion.rationale: Attack specifically targets 'MCP developers.' No hunt addresses behavioral anomalies in MCP-specific development patterns. Malicious packages may install rogue MCP components, configs, or hooks into .mcp, node_modules, or venv directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/modification in Python virtual environments, .mcp directories, MCP plugin directories, or setuptools eggsinfo paths by package-installation processes. Flag creation of shell scripts, compiled binaries, or config files in unexpected locations post-pip-install.

suggestion.title: Network Connections from Developer Machines to Article Domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article provides four IOCs (two domains getsession.org + filev2.getsession.org, git-tanstack.com, one IP 83.142.209.194) implying C2 phase (T1071). The recommended hunts section references 'network connections to article IPs/domains' but the pipeline generated zero UCs. This is a critical gap for C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from developer-workgroup machines to 83.142.209.194, filev2.getsession.org, getsession.org, or git-tanstack.com. Elevated risk if connections occur immediately post-pip-install or from Python child processes. Use whitelisting to exclude legitimate GetSession messenger usage.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Python Module Enumeration / Environment Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often perform victim reconnaissance via `pip list`, module enumeration, or environment inspection to identify target systems. Article mentions tracking by 'Mini Shai-Hulud, Miasma, and Hades threat clusters' suggesting coordinated reconnaissance. No hunt covers this discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python subprocess execution of `pip list`, `pip freeze`, or `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.modules)'` commands launched from unexpected processes (e.g., unattended/background execution). Flag if these enumeration commands execute within seconds of untrusted package installation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45321 Asset Vulnerability Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article lists CVE-2026-45321 as a vulnerability IOC. The recommended hunts explicitly reference 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' but pipeline generated zero UCs. Critical hunt for vulnerability-based asset inventory and prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for systems running software versions affected by CVE-2026-45321. Cross-reference with network access logs to systems that installed or attempted to install packages from the 23 compromised PyPI artifacts identified in the Shai-Hulud campaign.

suggestion.title: AI Vendor Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'threat actors...using the AI hype in social engineering'—initial access via impersonation of AI brands (OpenAI, Anthropic, Copilot, Claude). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial access indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with sender display names or addresses impersonating legitimate AI vendors, with urgency-based payloads (account verification, suspicious activity alerts, free trial sign-up). Correlate with external link clicks to lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: AiTM Credential Interception Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly cite 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' as attack method. Pipeline failed to surface credential access detection despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in patterns showing credential re-use from novel geolocations immediately post-phishing, FIDO2 device registration anomalies, password spray attempts using phished credentials, and authentication bursts from TOR/proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Compromised AI Service Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: AiTM campaigns targeting AI vendors result in credential abuse. Article implies downstream access to cloud services via stolen credentials; pipeline missed lateral movement and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls or unusual service interactions using credentials tied to phishing campaigns—bulk exports from cloud services, access to AI APIs (ChatGPT plugins, Claude integrations) from atypical geographies/times, and privilege escalation within federated cloud environments.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Registration Mimicking AI Vendors
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via AI brand impersonation requires infrastructure. Pipeline produced empty IOCs; should flag domain lookalikes and typosquatting campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference newly registered domains containing keywords from major AI vendors (openai, anthropic, google, deepmind, claude, copilot) against phishing email campaigns and user click telemetry. Flag lookalikes with Levenshtein distance <3 from legitimate domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth/Token Grant After AI Phishing
suggestion.rationale: AiTM enables attacker consent flow abuse—victim credentials captured, attacker grants themselves API tokens/OAuth consent. Pipeline missed persistence/privilege escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal OAuth application consent events (especially mail, calendar, Teams APIs) from IPs/user agents associated with phishing campaigns, followed by unusual API token generation or application permission grants spanning multiple cloud services.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass via AiTM Reverse Proxy Detection
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks often use reverse proxies to intercept MFA tokens. Pipeline should flag suspicious authentication proxy traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS certificate mismatches or suspicious proxy configurations (e.g., domain fronting, SSL stripping indicators) from sign-in sessions immediately following phishing interaction. Flag sessions with unusual User-Agent rotations or IP geolocation discontinuities.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Content Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly centers on 'AI Phishing.' Pipeline should detect emails exhibiting statistical markers of LLM-generated content (unusual token transitions, entropy anomalies, semantic-to-lexical diversity ratios, repeated templates across sender variation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze email body for LLM-generation signatures: high semantic diversity paired with low lexical diversity, unusual word-pair frequencies, or deviation from sender's historical language patterns. Flag emails with >85th percentile entropy + >15th percentile sender-baseline deviation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Alert Volume Spike & Campaign Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states alerts are 'crushing SOCs with alert volume.' Pipeline must detect high-volume coordinated phishing campaigns to reduce false-positive fatigue. Phrase: 'reduce Tier 1 overload' indicates alert clustering is a core missing defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster phishing alerts by content hash, subject-line Levenshtein distance, and sender-domain similarity. Flag when >50 alerts reference structurally identical messages within 60 minutes. Suppress individual alerts and escalate single campaign incident to reduce analyst context-switching.

suggestion.title: Spoofed Trusted Sender + AI-Crafted Authority Pretext
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing abuses trust by impersonating authority figures with AI-generated urgency/pretext. Article implies high success rates, suggesting attackers are leveraging AI-generated social-engineering pretexts effectively.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails spoofing internal trusted senders (C-suite, Finance, HR) originating from external/anomalous addresses. Apply NLP analysis to flag AI-generated urgency language (unusual capitalization, time pressure, authority assertions) misaligned with sender historical tone/style.

suggestion.title: Compromised Internal Account Leveraged for Phishing Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: High-volume, high-trust phishing likely exploits compromised employee accounts to bypass reputation filters. Article volume suggests account abuse as delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing campaigns with account logins exhibiting impossible travel, off-hours access, or anomalous geo-IP for account owner. Flag account for credential reset if it sends >20 phishing-category flagged emails within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: SOC Tier 1 Alert Triage SLA Breach Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload' directly implies alert volume is degrading SOC response time. Pipeline should recommend UC for monitoring response-time SLAs as a proxy for attack success during overload periods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor median time-to-triage and time-to-action for phishing alerts. Alert when Tier 1 SLA (e.g., 30-minute triage) is breached in >10% of alerts during high-volume periods. Correlate SLA breaches with observed phishing click-rates to quantify impact of analyst overload.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass – CVE-2026-50751 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs'. This is the primary attack surface; detections must flag IKEv1 handshake anomalies and successful VPN connections without valid credentials or machine certificates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful VPN authentication events from connections using IKEv1 that lack valid machine certificates or pre-authentication validation. Flag rapid sequential failed authentication attempts followed by successful access as bypass indicators. Alert on legacy Remote Access client connections to gateways configured to accept them without certificate enforcement.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Key Exchange Protocol Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol'. Organizations still accepting IKEv1 should be detected; this is a direct indicator of exploitable infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify VPN gateway configurations and active sessions using IKEv1. Alert on any IKEv1 negotiation success after organizational deprecation date. Correlate IKEv1 usage with absence of machine-certificate validation and legacy client support to identify highest-risk deployments.

suggestion.title: VPN Post-Compromise Activity – Lateral Movement and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' following VPN access. Detection must capture downstream C&C, privilege escalation, and lateral movement within 24-72 hours of VPN auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal VPN user behavior (source IPs, accessed resources, timing). Alert on VPN sessions with anomalous lateral movement patterns: unusual port scanning, RDP/SMB connections to non-standard hosts, credential enumeration tools (mimikatz, bloodhound), or file access patterns inconsistent with role. Prioritize sessions from gateways vulnerable to CVE-2026-50751.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware – Post-VPN Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms Qilin affiliate activity post-VPN compromise. Detection must hunt for Qilin staging and execution indicators (known payloads, C&C infrastructure, file extensions, encryption patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of Qilin-attributed payloads, known C&C domains/IPs (correlate against latest Qilin threat intelligence). Alert on file encryption activity, bulk file modification/deletion, and ransom note creation patterns. Focus detection on systems reachable from compromised VPN gateways within exploitation+dwell-time window.

suggestion.title: Machine Certificate Validation Bypass – IKEv1 MITM (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-50752: 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections'. Detect MITM indicators on VPN tunnels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN tunnels using IKEv1 for certificate validation failures or mismatches. Alert on successful tunnel establishment despite certificate anomalies (self-signed, expired, untrusted CA). Correlate with traffic analysis for injection/modification indicators.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article states mitigation includes 'remove support for the legacy remote access client'. Detect which clients connect and flag legacy variants as indicators of vulnerability exploitation or misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Remote Access client versions/user-agents connecting to VPN gateways. Identify and baseline legacy client connections. Alert on spike in legacy client usage or first-time legacy client connections from new source IPs, especially those without multi-factor authentication or machine-certificate validation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerable Asset Census
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and explicitly names CVE-2026-42271 — pipeline generated zero use cases for identifying unpatched BerriAI LiteLLM instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-42271 against BerriAI LiteLLM instances. Cross-reference asset inventory and network exposure to identify public-facing or internally-accessible LiteLLM deployments unpatched as of federal remediation deadline 2026-06-22. Prioritize low-patch-rate asset clusters.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Command Injection via LiteLLM API Key
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands' — this is the core exploitation mechanic but generated no detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation or command execution spawned from LiteLLM service accounts or application runtime contexts. Flag suspicious child processes (reverse shells, data exfiltration, reconnaissance) that correlate with LiteLLM API authentication logs indicating low-privilege key usage.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Low-Privilege LiteLLM Key Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'low-privilege internal-user keys' can trigger arbitrary command execution — represents privilege escalation from application context to host command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution spawned from low-privilege user or service account context but executing commands with elevated privilege level or scope inconsistent with baseline. Correlate LiteLLM API key usage logs (authentication context) against unexpected process creation events (privilege scope).

suggestion.title: Check Point IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password' — requires detection for IKEv1 sessions completing without credential validation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point gateway logs for IKEv1 Phase 1 completions where pre-shared key validation is absent or marked failed, yet the session advances to Phase 2. Alert on VPN tunnel establishment with null or missing user context.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Session Establishment (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password' — detection must trigger on successful tunnel creation bypassing normal credential exchange
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session creation events where authentication_status is absent, unauthenticated, or marked failed-but-continued. Baseline against known-good IKEv1 credential patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway CVE-2026-50751 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: CISA KEV status means 'observed exploited in the wild' — requires detection for live exploitation attempts against exposed gateways
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IKEv1 handshake packets on standard VPN ports (500/UDP) containing exploitation signatures (malformed payloads, overflow attempts, or vendor-published indicators of compromise). Correlate with vulnerability scanner results showing vulnerable gateway versions.

suggestion.title: Security Gateway Exposure and Patching Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' — pipeline must generate inventory/discovery detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Check Point Security Gateway instances. Cross-reference patch inventory against CVE-2026-50751 fixed versions; flag any system reporting patched but with active IKEv1 anomalies, indicating potential scanner or patch-deployment lag.

suggestion.title: UniFi Auth Bypass via Path Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version...attackers can bypass authentication and reach backend services that should not be publicly accessible.' This is the entry point to the exploit chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi OS HTTP requests for URI encoding mismatches between raw and normalized paths (path traversal sequences, double encoding, special character abuse). Correlate requests that bypass auth validation with subsequent access to protected endpoints. Establish baseline of normal URI patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: UniFi Unauthenticated Access to Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command' and recommends defenders 'monitor requests to ucs/update/latest_package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP requests to /ucs/update/latest_package endpoint. Alert on requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks, $(), command substitution) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Cross-reference against UniFi OS version logs to flag targets running ≤5.0.6.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from UCS Update Service
suggestion.rationale: Article advises 'monitor...suspicious child processes under ucs-update' and notes injected commands execute under the ucs service account, which has passwordless sudo access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by ucs-update service or ucs service account. Baseline legitimate processes (system package management tools) and flag deviations: shells, scripting engines, or reverse-shell patterns. Correlate timing with HTTP requests to package-update endpoint.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Sudo Escalation from Unprivileged Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the affected service account's sudo privileges make privilege escalation trivial' and commands run under 'a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo invocations originating from ucs-update or ucs service account without preceding authentication events. Flag escalations to root from normally unprivileged services. Monitor /var/log/sudo and audit logs for service accounts executing privileged binaries outside their normal operational scope.

suggestion.title: UniFi API Auth Validation Endpoint Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article detection guidance explicitly mentions 'look for requests containing '/api/auth/validate-sso/' and monitor requests to 'ucs/update/latest_package,'' indicating this endpoint is part of the bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ with unusual URI encoding, path traversal patterns, or originating from unexpected source IPs. Baseline normal admin/service access to this endpoint and alert on anomalous patterns. Correlate with subsequent requests to sensitive backend endpoints.

suggestion.title: UniFi Vulnerability Status Verification (CVE-2026-34908/09/10)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Bishop Fox has released a free detection script...by safely sending a specially crafted request that reaches the vulnerable code path without executing any dangerous commands, and then classifying the target as vulnerable, patched, unaffected, or inconclusive.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy vulnerability assessment probing for UniFi OS instances <5.0.8. Flag systems responding to Bishop Fox detection script patterns as vulnerable. Combine with network inventory data to track patch status. Alert on any systems reporting vulnerable status after announcement date (2026-06-08).

suggestion.title: File Inclusion or PHPSpreadsheet Load Call with phar:/// Bypass Pattern in Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability triggered when PHPSpreadsheet's File class is called with a filename parameter matching 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner'. No hunt targets application-level logs (web-server logs, PHP error logs, or application traces) for these specific parse_url() bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs and HTTP access logs for requests to file-upload or spreadsheet-processing endpoints where the filename/path parameter contains the string 'phar:///' with three or more consecutive forward slashes. Correlate with HTTP 500 errors or application warnings related to PHPSpreadsheet parsing.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PHPSpreadsheet Version in Production (Patch Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-45034 is a bypass of the patch for CVE-2026-34084. Pre-exploit detection requires identifying installations running unpatched versions before the phar:// attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset-scanning detection: query Composer/package manager logs, installed dependency manifests, or application version endpoints to identify PHPSpreadsheet versions released before the patch date. Cross-reference against public-facing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Persistence Script Upload Following Phar Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code-execution outcome from phar:// wrapper bypass (leading to shell spawn in UC_6_3), but no persistent web-shell hunt (T1505.003) exists. Attackers would typically upload a web shell to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web-accessible directories (docroot, upload directories) for new PHP/PHTML files created or modified by web-server processes within 5 minutes of a phar:/// request or shell-spawn event. Flag files containing eval(), exec(), passthru(), or system() calls.

suggestion.title: Possible CVE-2026-34084 Fallback (Pre-Patch Bypass Mitigation)
suggestion.rationale: Article references CVE-2026-34084 as the original vulnerability. Some environments may still be vulnerable to the original vector if they patched only partially or rolled back. Separate hunt for the original (non-bypass) wrapper-loading is valuable for defense-in-depth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to PHPSpreadsheet file-load endpoints with scheme-wrapper patterns other than phar:/// (e.g., single or double slash phar://, php://, data://, expect://, zip://) as a fallback detection for systems that may still be vulnerable to CVE-2026-34084 if patches were incomplete.

suggestion.title: Browser process spawning osascript with unescaped URL parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'unescaped URL in Chrome Plugin' leading to injection. Current detections assume osascript already invoked; missing is the browser-to-osascript bridge where URL parameter flows into command. Article describes 'interpolates a…' (truncated) but implies direct parameter substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chrome/Brave/Edge spawning osascript with ProcessCommandLine containing URL-like strings (http://, https://, or URL-encoded characters %xx) mixed with AppleScript keywords ('tell application', 'do shell script'). Correlate process tree: browser → extension runtime → osascript.

suggestion.title: AppleScript/JXA payload in environment variables or temp files from plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'AppleScript/JXA' equivalence; some exploits may write payload to temp file or env var before osascript consumption. Current detections only hunt post-execution artifacts; missing is artifact staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation in /tmp or system temp paths containing 'tell application' or 'do shell script' keywords, created by Chromium process or child, immediately preceding osascript execution.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin process execution anomaly — seturl.js with parent Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Article's vulnerable code path involves chrome_tabs plugin invoking system code; UC_4_1 hunts seturl.js in isolation. Missing is parent-process correlation to confirm browser origin vs. standalone execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: seturl.js execution where InitiatingProcessFileName is Chrome.exe, Chromium, brave.exe, or msedge.exe, or where parent process path includes 'Google/Chrome' or 'brave-browser'. Exclude legitimate extension updates.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — CA enumeration and cross-CA manipulation via /api/v1/cas endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CA-management endpoints in internal/api/cas.go' and 'per-CA ownership is enforced only in the Web layer', indicating API-level CA enumeration and mutation should be detectable as a distinct attack path separate from operator abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for GET bursts to /api/v1/cas endpoints followed by PUT/POST/DELETE to /api/v1/cas/{id}/* endpoints within the same session. High frequency indicates enumeration + mutation chain.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — bearer token usage anomaly: API calls crossing operator context
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'API trusts the bearer token alone for authorisation on most endpoints'. A single token should be scoped to one operator. Detect when the same user/token makes API calls to resources (hosts, networks, operators) across different operator IDs without a legitimate cross-operator role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API calls from the same src/user/token where the extracted operator_id or org_id from request bodies/paths differs from the previous request. Cluster calls within 10s window; alert if ≥3 distinct target operator IDs seen.

suggestion.title: nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — host certificate reenroll loop abuse for persistence
suggestion.rationale: UC_3_2 shows reenroll → enroll, but repeated reenroll cycles within short time windows (indicating re-compromise or re-enrollment of already-compromised hosts) is a persistence indicator missed by the main UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track hosts that hit /api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll more than twice within 24 hours. Three+ reenroll events suggest an attacker repeatedly restaging a compromised host identity.

suggestion.title: Gogs Account Creation Followed by Repository Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' and 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user'—describes a rapid, automated attack sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs audit logs for account creation events immediately followed (within minutes) by repository creation by the same user, particularly on instances with default open-registration settings. Baseline typical account→repo creation intervals; flag non-standard patterns. Query for users who create repos but never commit or interact with code.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Settings Toggle Followed by Merge Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' as a critical part of the exploit chain; the toggle activates the vulnerable Merge() code path that contains the argument injection flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to repository settings enabling 'Rebase before merge' or related merge strategy modifications, especially when followed immediately by merge operations. Flag accounts that enable rebase on repositories they just created. Cross-correlate setting changes with subsequent merge attempts containing unusual characters or escaped sequences.

suggestion.title: Git Merge Operations with Argument Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'argument injection' in the Merge() code path; malicious actors pass crafted arguments to exploit the flaw and execute arbitrary commands. Article states vulnerability 'affects a different code path (Merge()) that was never addressed'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git merge command arguments for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, ||, &&), escape sequences, or suspicious parameter patterns that deviate from normal merge syntax. Alert on merge operations from untrusted or newly-created accounts. Correlate with Gogs process execution logs for unexpected child processes (shells, interpreters).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Private Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'access any repositories (including private ones)'—indicates privilege boundary violation where unprivileged users bypass repository access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs access logs for requests to private repository contents (clones, pulls, file views) by accounts without explicit collaborator or admin permissions on those repos. Flag access patterns where a single account suddenly queries multiple private repos it did not create and is not a declared member of.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from Gogs Service
suggestion.rationale: RCE via argument injection means shell commands execute in Gogs process context; article describes attacker can 'compromise the targeted server' and perform code execution, indicating process spawning activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Gogs service (go executable, git subprocess containers). Flag shell interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe), reverse-shell indicators (nc, socat), or credential-dumping utilities (whoami, id, net.exe) launched from Gogs contexts. Baseline legitimate Gogs subprocesses (git, gpg) and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Version Detection & Vulnerable Instance Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev' are vulnerable; patched in 0.14.3. Shadowserver tracks 2,300+ Internet-exposed instances; Shodan identifies 1,000+ by fingerprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Gogs instances on network/in scope using Shodan fingerprints or banner grabbing (HTTP Server header contains 'Gogs', git endpoint signature). Extract version from /api/v1/version or web UI. Flag any version ≤0.14.2 or 0.15.0-dev as immediately vulnerable. Monitor egress traffic from unpatched instances for signs of post-exploitation (reverse shells, credential exfiltration, lateral-movement tool transfers).

suggestion.title: Fileless .NET Loader Execution via Reflection/Assembly API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fileless .NET loader'—in-memory execution via PowerShell/reflection, not traditional file drop. No detection mapped to this primary attack vector. 'runs [...]' text truncation hides specifics, but fileless execution is the core payload mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect System.Reflection.Assembly.Load/Invoke or equivalent .NET reflection APIs from PowerShell or rundll32.exe without corresponding disk write (Process Create + no File Write correlation). Alert on base64/hex-encoded payloads deobfuscated at runtime, or csc.exe/regsvcs.exe spawning without source .cs file.

suggestion.title: Malspam with Abused Legitimate Redirect Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article's core innovation: 'using Google's own DoubleClick ad-tracking infrastructure to route victims.' Pipeline missed both malspam delivery and abuse of doubleclick.net as trusted redirect vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing doubleclick.net or google-analytics URLs with suspicious query parameters or non-standard User-Agent patterns. Correlate email click events with rapid subsequent connections to IOC domains (xtadts.ddns.net, afxwd.ddns.net, etc.) within 5 minutes. Flag redirect chains where legitimate Google infrastructure terminates at attacker-controlled domain.

suggestion.title: Email Security Bypass via Obfuscated Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'sneak malware past email security tools'—explicit evasion tactic. Article obscures methodology ('runs [...]') but implies encoding, staging, or sandbox-aware delivery. No detection for email-layer evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with .NET-related attachments (renamed .NET executables, DLL files with obfuscated metadata), base64-encoded scripts in body, or multi-stage URL chains (shortener→redirect→IOC). Correlate with low phishing confidence scores from legacy email gateways (false negatives). Alert on emails using 'double-encapsulation' (MimeObfuscation + URL rewriting).

suggestion.title: DDNS-Based C2 Command & Control Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: IOCs xtadts.ddns.net and afxwd.ddns.net are DDNS domains—classic volatile C2. Pipeline categorized these as 'network IOCs' but missed behavioral C2 detection (DNS query patterns, connection frequency, protocol anomalies).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to .ddns.net domains not matching known legitimate DDNS usage. Alert on cascading DNS failures (NXDOMAIN) followed by successful connection on same domain—indicators of C2 failover. Flag connections to DDNS providers on non-standard ports (8080, 8888, 443 for command exfil). Correlate with fileless .NET process execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Registration Patterns in Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: IOCs include randomly-generated subdomains (andrefelipedonascime1778799406970), hacked hosting providers (meusitehostgator.com.br), and DDNS services. Pipeline extracted domains but skipped hosting/registration pattern analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to domains sharing characteristics: <30-day-old registration, WHOIS privacy enabled, hacked/compromised hosting providers, dynamic DNS services, or rapid A-record changes (>3 IPs in 7 days). Correlate with email delivery timestamp to flag infrastructure stood up just before campaign.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Phishing Campaign with Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack.' This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection for anomalous WhatsApp message content (credential requests, urgency, social engineering language) and Meta infrastructure blocks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume WhatsApp/messaging-app phishing patterns: shortened URLs, sender spoofing, requests for account verification/password reset, urgency language. Correlate with Meta threat feeds showing blocked NSO infrastructure. Alert on unusual click-through rates from messaging channels vs. email baseline.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Malware Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group's primary payload is Pegasus spyware. Pipeline must detect post-compromise malware execution. Article's mention of 'new' attack suggests updated delivery or evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NSO Group known IOCs (Pegasus process signatures, file paths, registry keys). Detect unusual child processes spawned from WhatsApp/Telegram, suspicious dynamic library injection into messaging apps, or known NSO C2 beacon patterns. Cross-reference against Citizen Lab/Amnesty International Pegasus indicator lists.

suggestion.title: Meta Account Compromise and Threat Response Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates Meta 'Files Contempt Order,' implying organizational threat response and potential account disruption. Should detect security team escalation, infrastructure changes, and legal/IR activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Meta security operations: mass account disables, security team activity spikes, infrastructure/WAF rule changes, IP reputation downgrades. Correlate with threat-feed updates showing NSO infrastructure blocks. Flag unusual access to legal/threat-intel systems during incident window.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Targeting NSO's High-Value Victim Profile
suggestion.rationale: NSO historically targets journalists, activists, and civil-society leaders. The 'new' variant suggests updated social-engineering or victim profiling tactics. Should detect targeting patterns consistent with NSO profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify messages targeting known high-risk personas (government, NGO, press, activism orgs). Look for OSINT reconnaissance (domain enumeration, email harvesting), message urgency, and impersonation of trusted contacts. Cross-reference recipient profiles against Citizen Lab NSO target lists.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'purpose-built web shell framework' deployed to 'Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers' — this is the primary payload and attack vector, completely missed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS application root directories (wwwroot, inetpub\*) for unexpected .aspx, .ashx, .php file creation or modification. Correlate with w3wp.exe execution, abnormal HTTP status codes, and POST requests to newly created paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptographically Obfuscated Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'cryptographically unique' framework 'designed to evade every detection method' — core evasion technique unaddressed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64/hex-encoded or high-entropy payloads in HTTP request bodies, query strings, and IIS logs. Alert on w3wp.exe spawning processes with obfuscated command lines; monitor for dynamic code evaluation via eval() in IIS logs.

suggestion.title: IIS Server Exploitation or Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets IIS servers as entry point — initial access mechanism (T1190 or existing compromise) undetected
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation patterns in IIS logs: suspicious HTTP verbs (PUT, DELETE, TRACE), long/unusual URI paths, 40x errors followed by 20x responses, or requests to known IIS vulnerability endpoints. Correlate with unexpected file system activity.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article provides C2 IOCs (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com) but no HTTP-level C2 detection — web shells communicate via HTTP/HTTPS, not standard C2 channels
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP from IIS servers to external C2 domains, especially with suspicious headers, absent User-Agent, missing Referer, or repeated beaconing intervals. Correlate IIS access logs showing web shell path execution with network connections.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Spawning Interactive Shells
suggestion.rationale: Web shells execute commands by spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe from w3wp.exe — standard web shell execution pattern
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe creating child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe). Flag execution with suspicious command line arguments, unusual parent-child chains, and time correlation with IIS HTTP log anomalies.

suggestion.title: Discord token harvesting from AppData/process memory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Discord Tokens' as primary target yet no hunt covers Discord credential theft. Article phrase: targets 'Discord Tokens' alongside browser passwords and crypto wallets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system and process memory access to Discord AppData directories (AppData\Roaming\Discord\Cache, Local Storage) and discord.exe process handles by non-Discord processes. Discord tokens are typically Base64-encoded in Local Storage JSON; access by suspcious parent processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe with unusual parents) should trigger.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of multiple cryptocurrency wallet installations
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware targets multiple wallet platforms simultaneously; quick file system discovery of 7+ wallet directories indicates reconnaissance. Article phrase: 'targets 18 Browsers, Crypto Wallets, and Discord Tokens' implies systematic enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential queries to cryptocurrency wallet installation paths (≥5 distinct wallet software directories within 60 seconds) by single process. Suspicious when initiated by non-browser, non-installer processes. Wallet paths: Ethereum\keystore, Bitcoin\wallet.dat, Exodus, Electrum, MetaMask, Phantom, Atomic.

suggestion.title: Telegram-delivered malware installation pattern (IOC correlation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'Discovered through underground channels linked to Telegram' as primary distribution. Correlate Telegram process outbound connections to attacker infrastructure with subsequent file creation matching provided SHA256 IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries from telegram.exe or Telegram client process to article C2 domains, followed within 2 minutes by child process execution or file creation with SHA256 matching any of the 9 provided malware hashes. Indicates malware delivery via Telegram link/file.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Tool execution with RAT-like C2 communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hidden remote access' and ability to 'take full control of an infected machine without [...]' indicating RAT functionality and persistent C2 channel. Current hunts miss post-exploitation remote management phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or anomalous process execution with RAT characteristics (reverse shell patterns, abnormal handles to msagp.dll/wtsapi32.dll for RDP emulation, meterpreter-style encoding). Correlate parent process chain to any of the 9 SHA256 IOCs. Flag outbound C2 to article domains post-execution.

suggestion.title: Outbound exfiltration to attacker C2 domains with stolen credential payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential exfiltration to attacker servers via 'hidden remote access'. Lists 7 C2 domains but no hunt correlates stolen browser/wallet data with network communication to those domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from suspicious process to any article C2 domain (lucidstealer.one, iloveyoulucid.space, ghdfhfjhfg.webhop.me, 0kt.one, storedonutsmp.net, 45.138.16.107, 85.239.155.68) containing Base64-encoded or JSON-structured payloads. Payload inspection should match password/token/wallet data patterns (Base64 'password':', 'token':', 'seed phrase' keywords).

suggestion.title: Phishing emails with cloud credential-theft themes targeting enterprise users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the group uses 'social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials.' This is textbook T1566 spearphishing, yet no email-based phishing hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound emails with cloud-account themes (password reset, verification request, sign-in alert) from external senders to enterprise users. Correlate with sender domain reputation and any URLs pointing to attacker-controlled domains from IOC set.

suggestion.title: Unusual cloud storage account login from attacker-controlled infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials will be used to access cloud storage from the attacker-controlled IPs listed in article IOCs. No hunt for compromised-credential usage was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins to OneDrive/Dropbox/SharePoint accounts from the IOC IPs (185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66) or correlate failed + successful auth from new geolocation post-phishing send.

suggestion.title: Bulk cloud storage data exfiltration post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'listed several initial victims' suggesting stolen data is staged for extortion. No cloud-egress anomaly hunt was generated despite clear exfiltration intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk download/export activity in cloud storage accounts, unusual sharing grants, or downloads to external domains, especially from formerly dormant accounts or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance enumeration of cloud storage content post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Extortion groups systematically map victim environments before exfil to identify high-value data. Article structure implies selective targeting ('already listed several initial victims'), suggesting reconnaissance occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of folders, file searches, or permission-inspection queries in cloud storage immediately following a new login from unfamiliar IP or user agent.

suggestion.title: Cloud storage account modifications and persistence mechanisms post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers stealing high-value data often establish secondary access (add forwarding rules, secondary accounts, backup methods). No persistence-mechanism hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new secondary email accounts added to cloud-storage account recovery options, new app registrations/OAuth grants to third-party services, or unexpected sharing permissions granted to external domains.

suggestion.title: Credential validation against domain infrastructure from IOC set
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three 'passkey'-themed domains (passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com) suggesting credential-harvesting landing pages. No hunt for users accessing these domains was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enterprise user HTTP/DNS traffic to the three passkey-themed IOC domains. Correlate any hits with phishing email sends and subsequent cloud-storage anomalies from same user account.

suggestion.title: Python .pth File Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Users would just have to start Python to trigger the execution of the PTH file' and recommends 'look for Python packages containing executable .pth startup hooks'. This is the core initial-execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .pth files in Python site-packages directories being created or modified, followed by Python interpreter invocations. Correlate file creation by package-install processes with subsequent Python execution chains.

suggestion.title: Bun JavaScript Runtime Download from GitHub
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tries to download the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to run the bundled script' and recommends 'unexpected downloads of the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub'. Distinguishes this attack from standard Python malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python or child processes downloading Bun binaries from GitHub release URLs (github.com/oven-sh/bun). Flag downloads of unfamiliar JavaScript runtimes followed by script execution.

suggestion.title: Process Chain: Python → Bun → _index.js Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'process chains where Python launches Bun to execute _index.js'. Direct attack flow recommendation from the researchers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent-child chains: Python → curl/wget → Bun executable → JavaScript. Monitor for Bun executing scripts from /tmp, current directory, or obfuscated filenames.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using automatically created GitHub repositories to host secrets written via GitHub Actions'. Primary exfiltration channel specific to developer environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid GitHub API calls: repository creation → workflow file commits → push operations. Correlate with environment variable exports or secret refs in .github/workflows YAML files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Anthropic API Endpoint HTTPS Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'pointing to a legitimate but invalid Anthropic API endpoint (api[.]anthropic[.]com/v1/api), which Socket believes was likely used for camouflage'. Unusual C2 disguise exploiting tool legitimacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS POST/PUT requests to api.anthropic.com/v1/api from non-SDK clients or with non-Anthropic User-Agents. Cross-reference with Python/Bun process execution timing.

suggestion.title: Persistence via systemd and LaunchAgent Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Persistence is established through systemd services on Linux and LaunchAgents on macOS, while GitHub workflow and Claude/MCP configuration files are also used'. Multiple persistence vectors requiring distinct detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of systemd unit files in /etc/systemd/system and /usr/lib/systemd/system. On macOS, track .plist file creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/. Flag writes to .github/workflows/ and Claude MCP config directories by non-IDE processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Banking APK Downloaded from GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '56 unique APKs that impersonated mobile apps for banks primarily from Italy and Spain' hosted on a GitHub repository 'since April 10'. Detection should flag APK downloads from GitHub URLs using legitimate banking app names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads of .apk files matching banking app name patterns (e.g., *Carte.apk, *CaixaBank*, *Banca*) from GitHub repositories. Flag GitHub repos created within 90 days of download or with typosquatted names. Correlate with visits to phishing sites impersonating banks.

suggestion.title: NFC Card Data Harvesting via Fake Verification Screen
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware using 'fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's NFC chip' and reads 'card number, type, expiry date, and 4-digit PIN'. Direct credential exfiltration via NFC should generate detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps with NFC read permissions (android.permission.NFC) that trigger multiple NFC EMV command sequences via IsoDep interface within short time windows. Alert when apps request both NFC permissions and credential input capabilities (keyboard overlay, dialog boxes) in the same session.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK Packaging for Static Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states newer samples include 'poisoned/malformed file paths within the ZIP' causing extraction tools to 'wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths and trigger errors'. This is deliberate defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze APK files for malformed ZIP metadata including invalid path structures, non-standard directory ordering, or encoding anomalies. Flag APKs that generate errors during extraction by standard tools but remain executable as indicators of obfuscation intent.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Exfiltration of Payment Card Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel'. WebSocket-based C2 used for stolen financial data is a distinct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSocket connections from banking apps or apps with NFC permissions to external hosts on non-standard ports. Flag WebSocket traffic exfiltrating structured data matching card metadata patterns (16-digit numbers, expiry dates, 4-digit codes).

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Redirect to Malicious APK Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain: 'victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials. Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository'. Site-to-app-download redirect is the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains with homoglyph/typosquatting similarity to legitimate banks (edit distance <3) that redirect users to APK downloads outside official app stores. Correlate phishing domain visits with subsequent APK installations on same device.

suggestion.title: Banking App Installation with Anomalous Signature or NFC+Credential Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article documents APK installation where 'new variants of NFCShare Android malware are being distributed as fake updates for legitimate banking apps'. Signature mismatch + unusual permission combo flags suspicious banking apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag banking app installations where APK signature issuer or hash does not match official publisher records. Alert on banking apps requesting NFC permissions combined with INPUT_METHOD, CLIPBOARD_READ, or record audio permissions, as legitimate apps rarely need all three.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Load Post-Exploit Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploits Now Public' for local-root kernel flaw. Attackers will load malicious modules or trigger kernel code paths; no detection proposed for insmod/modprobe execution or unsigned module loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe execution from unprivileged contexts, kernel module load audit events, or signature validation failures in /lib/modules. Correlate timing with prior suspicious process activity.

suggestion.title: Privilege Elevation Detection via Vulnerable Kernel Version
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Local Root Access' via kernel flaw. Should detect uid/gid elevation anomalies on vulnerable kernel versions matching vuln scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected uid/gid for each process; flag elevation of non-setuid binaries. Correlate elevated-privilege child processes with parent execution from low-privilege accounts on vulnerable kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Kernel Panic / Oops Correlation with Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits commonly trigger crashes, faults, or oops messages. Article describes kernel-level vulnerability; should detect dmesg segfaults, null-pointer dereferences, or stack traces as post-exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest kernel logs for seg-fault/null-ptr/stack-smash signatures. Correlate crash timestamp with preceding suspicious process execution or network inbound on the host.

suggestion.title: Execution of Public Kernel Exploit PoC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploits Now Public'. PoC binaries or shell scripts will match file hashes or behavioral patterns (direct execution, script interpretation, privilege escalation syscalls).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-sig known kernel exploit PoCs once CVE is identified. Detect execution of binaries named *exploit*, kernel-vuln*, or shell scripts downloading/compiling kernel PoCs.

suggestion.title: Runtime Kernel Exploit Compilation (gcc/clang in /tmp)
suggestion.rationale: Public exploits are source; attackers compile in-place on target. Article signals public PoC; should flag compiler execution by unprivileged users, especially in /tmp or download directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on gcc/clang/ld execution by non-root accounts in /tmp, /dev/shm, or $HOME. Correlate with prior wget/curl or web-browser activity and /proc/sys/kernel/* modifications.

suggestion.title: Bulk Password Reset Requests via Account Recovery Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'exploited a flaw in the company's High Touch Support (HTS) tool...obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in.' No detection proposed despite attackers performing resets at scale. Phrase: 'exploited the fact that HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery tool (HTS or equivalent) for elevated password reset request volume from single source IP, for password resets on accounts with mismatched or unverified email domains, or for resets issued without matching the registered account contact. Baseline per user/per IP and alert on 3+ resets in 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Password Reset Bypass of 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled' via password reset. This is a post-compromise detection gap. Phrase: 'password reset links that allowed them to log in...without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful login to account immediately after forced password reset if 2FA is not enforced post-reset, or if login source IP differs from historical norm. Correlate password-reset event to login event within 5 minutes with mismatched geo/device.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Connected Accounts and Linked Services Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gained access to 'other connected accounts and linked services' post-takeover. No detection for lateral movement via account linking suggested. Phrase: 'attackers could've gained access to...other connected accounts and linked services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in to linked/connected accounts (Facebook, WhatsApp, Threads, etc.) using credentials obtained from compromised Instagram account. Alert on logins to linked services from IP addresses previously associated with the HTS abuse or password-reset activity.

suggestion.title: Mass Data Exfiltration from Compromised Social Media Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates sensitive data accessible post-compromise: 'direct messages and communications, social media posts and content (photos, videos, stories), account activity and interaction history.' No detection for bulk data access or download patterns. Phrase: 'the attackers could've gained access to affected Instagram users' contact information...direct messages and communications, account activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume API calls to retrieve DMs, posts, photos, or story history from newly compromised accounts. Alert on accounts accessing significantly more messages/media than baseline within 1-hour post-compromise window, or on exports/downloads of account data shortly after unauthorized login.

suggestion.title: HTS Tool Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific attack vector: unverified email addresses in HTS recovery flow. No detection rule for abuse of the HTS service itself. Phrase: 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts, they obtained password reset links.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTS/account-recovery endpoints for requests where supplied email address does not appear in account records, requests for password resets on non-existent accounts, or requests where email domain/pattern does not match registered account owner domain. Alert on multiple failed verification checks followed by successful reset.

suggestion.title: Mandatory Security Checkpoint Bypass or Delayed Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article states Meta 'enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint.' Detection should flag accounts that bypass or skip re-authentication checkpoints post-compromise. Phrase: 'enrolled all potentially stolen accounts into a mandatory security checkpoint and asked all affected users to reset their passwords again.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to flagged/checkpoint-enrolled accounts that bypass re-authentication steps, skip 2FA enrollment, or resume normal activity without completing mandatory security re-verification. Alert if checkpoint-flagged account is accessed from different geo/device than the initiating takeover IP within 72 hours.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Access From Third-Party Vendor Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers gained access to a database at a third-party vendor containing customer information.' Core collection phase—pipeline omitted detection for abnormal query patterns, bulk exports, or data extraction from vendor databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor database systems for deviation from baseline query patterns: unexpected SELECT volume on customer PII tables, bulk data exports outside business hours, queries from unusual service accounts, or high-volume exfiltration. Alert on compression of database files followed by outbound transfer.

suggestion.title: Compromised Vendor Credentials or Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential compromise as attack vector: 'unauthorized access to a database.' Pipeline failed to surface T1078 (Valid Accounts) or detection scenarios for vendor system account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline vendor system access patterns; alert on anomalous authentication (new IPs, unusual hours, failed attempts followed by success). Monitor for rapid privilege escalation immediately after credential use. Flag lateral movement within vendor network post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Unmonitored Bulk Data Transfer From Vendor Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: discovery on 'April 30, 2026' after 'unauthorized access to a database'—exfiltration predates detection. Pipeline missed outbound data transfer detection from vendor systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound transfers from vendor database systems exceeding baseline volume. Detect archive files (tar, zip) created from database directories. Monitor egress to untrusted IP ranges or cloud accounts. Flag unusual port usage for data exfiltration (non-standard DB ports, HTTP/HTTPS for large payloads).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation at Third-Party Vendor Prior to Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of database with customer PII implies lateral movement or privilege escalation within vendor environment. Article states breach was discovered post-incident; pipeline omitted privilege escalation phase.
