suggestion.rationale: Article states FFmpeg 'powers [...] browsers, streaming platforms, surveillance systems, cloud infrastructure'; no continuous version telemetry or patch-status hunt. Critical for assessing exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg process command-lines and loaded libraries for version strings; cross-reference against CVE-2026-39210 through 39230 patched builds. Alert on unpatched versions in production. Track across media services (browsers, streaming daemons, surveillance stacks).

suggestion.title: Malicious Media File from Untrusted Source — User Interaction & File Source Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires FFmpeg to consume untrusted media; no user-behavior or file-provenance detection. Article implies browser/email delivery vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user downloads of media files (mp4, mkv, mov, avi, flv, webm, etc.) from low-reputation domains or external email attachments with FFmpeg process creation. Flag if browser tab/plugin then spawns FFmpeg on untrusted content.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Media Processing in Isolated Contexts — Surveillance & Streaming Platform Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights FFmpeg in 'surveillance systems' and 'cloud infrastructure' as attack surface; no vertical-specific detection for these high-value targets. Need context-aware monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In surveillance and streaming environments, flag FFmpeg process spawning with unusual network destinations, or processing media from external/unauthenticated sources. Baseline expected stream ingestion patterns per deployment; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Exploitation Attempt (IKEv1 Auth Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' Core attack vector—must detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful VPN session establishment from external sources lacking prior authentication context, especially IKEv1 negotiations. Correlate rapid auth failures followed by success on Check Point gateways accepting legacy Remote Access clients without machine certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Acceptance on VPN Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol.' Enumerate and baseline vulnerable gateway configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access gateways accepting IKEv1 protocol negotiation. Alert when IKEv1 sessions complete without enforcing machine certificate authentication per article mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: VPN Machine Certificate Authentication Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability occurs when gateways 'don't require a machine certificate for connections and accept legacy Remote Access clients.' Configuration drift detection critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point gateways for configuration changes disabling machine certificate authentication or permitting legacy Remote Access client connections. Alert on any IKEv1-enabled gateway without mandatory certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Qilin Ransomware Activity Post-VPN Access
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' Detect ransomware behaviors following successful VPN breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-successful CVE-2026-50751 exploitation, monitor for mass file encryption, credential dumping via mimikatz/lsass, SMB reconnaissance, and large data exfiltration. Cross-correlate VPN access logs with Qilin-attributed behaviors from 400+ known incidents.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client VPN Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable config accepts 'legacy Remote Access clients' via IKEv1. Detection: baseline modern client types, alert on legacy protocol-version patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN sessions from legacy Remote Access client versions or undefined client types on Check Point gateways configured for IKEv1. Correlate with external source IPs and low authentication context.

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Group Infrastructure Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation...400+ victims...since August 2022.' Track actor infrastructure and victim patterns to identify likely breach chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Qilin dark-web leak site for new victim announcements. Cross-reference newly listed organizations with Check Point VPN deployment footprint to identify likely exploitation vector. Track C2 payment portal indicators and negotiation communication channels.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Heap Corruption Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'stems from an out-of-bounds read and write weakness in the Chrome V8 JavaScript engine, which remote attackers can exploit via crafted HTML pages to execute arbitrary code.' No UC exists for V8-specific memory violation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome renderer processes for unexpected V8 exception codes (heap corruption indicators), abnormal memory access patterns during HTML page rendering, and V8 engine crash dumps. Correlate with suspicious HTML downloads or untrusted domains to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass via Out-of-Bounds Memory Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR, making it easier to achieve code execution via another weakness.' No detection UC for ASLR bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful ASLR bypass indicators: repeated failed memory access attempts from Chrome renderer followed by code execution from predicted addresses, entropy analysis anomalies in module load addresses, or exception records showing hits on expected-random address ranges.

suggestion.title: Delivery of Malicious Crafted HTML to Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation vector explicitly described as 'via crafted HTML pages' but pipeline generated no detection UC for web-based malicious payload delivery targeting the browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTML downloads that trigger immediate Chrome V8 crashes or exceptions. Monitor for obfuscated or suspicious HTML content delivered from untrusted/newly-registered domains, correlated with vulnerability disclosure timeline and affected version prevalence.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chrome Instances Post-Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes patch released to versions 149.0.7827.102/103 and 'updates could take days or weeks to reach all Chrome users.' No UC for detecting vulnerable Chrome versions still running.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory detection: flag endpoints running Chrome versions prior to 149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or 149.0.7827.103 (macOS). Escalate if unpatched vulnerable instances are still active 7+ days post-patch release, especially those with active web browsing.

suggestion.title: Chrome Sandbox Escape via Heap Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation enables 'access data beyond the memory buffer via heap corruption' and implicit sandbox boundary violation. No UC for sandbox escape detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome renderer processes attempting to access protected system memory, create handles to system processes, or spawn children with unexpected privilege levels. Alert on any renderer-context process elevation or cross-process memory access outside sandbox whitelist.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Crash Clustering with Suspicious Web Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploitation could trigger 'heap corruption, exposing sensitive information or triggering a crash.' No UC correlates V8 crashes with preceding malicious web activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Chrome V8 exceptions occur within 5 seconds of loading content from suspicious/untrusted domains. Correlate crash memory addresses and exception types with patterns indicative of heap corruption exploitation vs. legitimate crashes.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 Exploitation Attempt (HTTP Payload)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'exploited in the wild' and 'chains to unauthenticated RCE'—there must be an exploitation vector (HTTP endpoint, parameter injection, etc.) that should be detected before execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM instances for HTTP requests containing payload patterns characteristic of CVE-2026-42271 exploitation. Alert on requests to vulnerable endpoints with serialized objects, parameter tampering, or known gadget chains targeting the affected code paths.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Process-Level RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—once exploited, the vulnerability results in code execution on the LiteLLM host. This is a direct execution phase that must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned by LiteLLM application processes (python, java, node—depending on deployment). Alert on process creation with unusual parent-child relationships, suspicious command-line arguments, or execution of binaries from temp/cache directories.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Reverse Shell / C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE typically leads to attacker establishing persistence or command channel. Article headline signals active exploitation, implying post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from LiteLLM hosts for outbound connections to non-whitelisted C2 domains, unknown external IPs, or uncommon ports (reverse shell indicators). Flag DNS queries from the compromised host that differ from baseline application behavior.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Application Log Anomalies Indicating Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of deserialization or injection flaws typically generates error messages, stack traces, or unusual log entries in application logs. These are forensic signals of attack attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse LiteLLM application logs for exceptions, stack traces, or error codes consistent with exploitation. Look for sudden spikes in 400/500 HTTP errors preceded by malformed requests, deserialization failures, or permission escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved on a LiteLLM proxy host, attackers typically pivot to attack downstream systems (LLM backends, secrets stores, internal services). This phase enables broad impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the compromised LiteLLM host for new lateral connections to internal services, API calls to credential stores, or SSH/WinRM connections to other hosts. Baseline the host's network profile and alert on significant deviations in destination IPs, ports, and protocols.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Dependency Injection or Gadget Chain Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: LiteLLM likely depends on serialization libraries or third-party packages. The 'chains to RCE' language suggests a multi-step gadget chain (e.g., Java deserialization, Python pickle, Node.js eval). This is the core exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation of insecure deserialization patterns: monitor for process execution of compiler/interpreter tools (javac, python -c, node -e) spawned by LiteLLM, suspicious file writes to library paths, or runtime bytecode/AST modifications.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states '23 newly discovered malicious PyPI package-version artifacts'—this is the infection vector (T1195.002 supply chain). Pipeline generated zero detection for actual pip install of flagged packages. This is the initial access event. Phrase: 'Shai-Hulud supply chain campaign...23 newly discovered malicious PyPI package-version artifacts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip.exe / python -m pip install execution for flagged package names. Cross-reference against Socket Threat Research intelligence feed of known malicious package-version tuples. Alert with high confidence on install to systems with MCP SDK or development tooling present; medium confidence on isolated systems.

suggestion.title: Python Process Outbound Connection to Identified C2 Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article provides three C2 domains (filev2.getsession.org, getsession.org, git-tanstack.com) and C2 IPv4 (83.142.209.194). No UC for network-phase detection of data exfiltration or callback. This is T1071 (application layer protocol) in command-and-control phase. Phrase: 'IPv4 (defanged): 83.142.209.194...getsession.org...git-tanstack.com'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound DNS or network connections from python.exe, pip.exe, or processes spawned from site-packages to the three identified domains or IP 83.142.209.194. Correlate with recent (within 1 hour) pip install commands on the same host to establish chain of custody.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution from Site-Packages Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as technique but no detection for the execution phase of obfuscated payloads. Malicious packages use setup.py hooks to execute obfuscated code on install or import. Phrase: 'Obfuscated Files or Information'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child process spawning from python.exe or setup.py execution within site-packages directories, especially spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl.exe. Look for temporary script creation (.ps1, .bat, .sh) in %TEMP% immediately following pip install. Baseline legitimate build processes (wheels, setuptools extensions).

suggestion.title: MCP SDK / Development Environment + Malicious Package Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies 'Target MCP Developers' — the threat is actor-targeted at a specific developer persona. No UC correlates MCP environment presence with subsequent suspicious package installations. This is a high-confidence indicator of intentional targeting. Phrase: 'Target MCP Developers'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag hosts where MCP SDK is installed or MCP-related packages are present (mcp Python package, @modelcontextprotocol/* npm, MCP config files in .config or .vscode) that subsequently execute pip install of flagged malicious packages. This behavioral correlation is high-confidence targeting indicator.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Environment via Package Hook
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack targeting developers implies credential exfiltration from .ssh, .aws, .git, environment variables. No T1552 detection suggested despite article's developer targeting. Malicious packages commonly steal API keys and authentication material. Implied but not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python processes spawned post-install for file-read access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.git, .env files, and environment variable enumeration. Correlate with outbound network traffic to article C2 domains. Baseline legitimate tools (git clients, cloud CLIs).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted C2 Domain Registration and Certificate Transparency
suggestion.rationale: Two C2 domains typosquat real services: getsession.org (Session messaging) and git-tanstack.com (TanStack library). No UC for proactive detection of typosquatted-domain registration or WHOIS history. This is a repeatable attacker tactic. Phrases: 'getsession.org' and 'git-tanstack.com'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registration of domains matching pattern: {legitimate-brand}.{com,net,org} or git-{legitimate-brand}.* where brand is known open-source or SaaS product. Alert on new/recent-WHOIS domains with legitimate brand in name. Cross-reference with known malicious package infrastructure feeds.

suggestion.title: Email sender domain spoofing or brand impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers are 'disguising phishing attacks with the branding of platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek.' This is sender-domain forgery or display-name spoofing. Detection: emails claiming to be from OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepSeek but originating from external/free mail domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for inbound email where SenderFromDomain does not match known legitimate OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek domains, yet Subject or Body contains brand language ('Verify your ChatGPT account', 'Claude security alert', etc.). Flag if SenderFromDomain is external (Gmail, Yahoo, free hosters) or previously unseen.

suggestion.title: PowerShell execution from web browser or Outlook process
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates users click links in phishing emails and PowerShell T1059.001 is executed. Standard UC_PHISH_LINK covers this correlation, but a direct hunt for PowerShell spawned from Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Outlook parents within minutes of user activity would catch post-click exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or pwsh.exe spawned as child of browser (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, firefox.exe) or Outlook with command line containing obfuscated/suspicious patterns (encoded commands, registry access, network calls). Correlate to recent UrlClickEvents to the malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Office/Outlook process DNS query or network connection to article IOC domains
suggestion.rationale: Once the phishing payload (Office macro or Outlook folder action) executes, the malware contacts C2 or exfiltration domains. Article lists `pan.ssffaa19.xyz`, `pan.rongtv.xyz`, `dash.awaydouble.org` and others. Office processes initiating connections to these domains would confirm successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Office/Outlook parent processes to the article's IOC domains. Flag any DNS queries from Office to these domains or their subdomains, especially after Office child-process spawning or file download events.

suggestion.title: Failed authentication attempts followed by unusual account/credential activity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes theft of 'login credentials' and 'authentication tokens'. Users entering credentials on phishing pages or malware capturing them would precede atypical login patterns (failed logins from unusual locations, token reuse, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication events (invalid password) from a user's IP followed within 30 min by a successful login from a different IP or unusual location. Also monitor for token-based access (OAuth/SAML assertions) issued shortly after the user received the phishing email, especially if the access location differs from the user's baseline.

suggestion.title: Malware hash match to article's SHA256 IOCs on endpoint or email
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 8 SHA256 hashes, none of which appear in the pipeline output. Detection should match these hashes against files on disk, in-flight attachments, and process memory to identify known payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-based file detection: match article SHA256 values against (1) email attachments for blocked/allowed history, (2) files on endpoints (Downloads, Temp, AppData), (3) process command-line arguments or loaded DLLs. Any hit on these hashes should trigger immediate quarantine and investigation.

suggestion.title: VB script or HTA execution from email client or Office process
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1059.005 (Visual Basic) among observed techniques, likely via Office macro or embedded scripts in attachments. Detection should flag .VBS, .HTA, or VBScript execution spawned by email/Office.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for wscript.exe, cscript.exe, or mshta.exe spawned by Outlook, Word, Excel, or email-related processes. Also detect creation of .VBS or .HTA files in user temp/downloads folders immediately after email arrival, especially if the file is subsequently executed.

suggestion.title: Email-based AI brand spoofing (ChatGPT/Claude impersonation)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states threat actors use 'AI brands as bait.' No UC generated despite clear initial-access vector via spoofed AI product emails/domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with AI brand names (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini) in sender display name or domain that do not originate from legitimate vendor infrastructure. Correlate with known phishing redirection domains.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Schema keywords explicitly flag 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' and 'Credential theft' — core attack pattern. Pipeline failed to generate corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect potential AiTM proxies: authentication events with anomalous IP geolocation shifts, multiple login attempts within seconds from different IPs for same user, or OAuth token generation from IPs never seen in org before.

suggestion.title: Suspicious credential reuse post-phishing
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering + credential theft should trigger detection for reuse of harvested creds. No UC addresses post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing campaign timing with unusual login patterns: successful logins from new devices/locations shortly after high-volume phishing, or logins followed by sensitive API/data access within hours.

suggestion.title: Detect AI-Generated Phishing Emails by Linguistic Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs' establishes AI-crafted phishing as primary vector. Pipeline should detect anomalies in email grammar, sender consistency, unusual word choices, or metadata misalignment characteristic of LLM-generated messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email for linguistic red flags (perfect grammar but odd phrasing, repetitive clause structures, metadata mismatches between Reply-To and From). Cross-check with historical baseline of sender's typical email patterns via NLP scoring.

suggestion.title: Alert Suppression & Tuning for Phishing Campaign Volume
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload'—core SOC operational problem. Pipeline should generate tuning rules to suppress known phishing variants while preserving novel detection, preventing analyst fatigue.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement confidence-based suppression: mark phishing emails matching known campaign IOCs (sender envelope-from, reply-to, URL patterns, subject keywords) with lower priority or batch-notify instead of individual alerts. Maintain rolling list of suppressed indicators, alert on 1-2 character variations (typosquatting).

suggestion.title: Detect Email Forwarding Rules from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Phishing often leads to account compromise. Article implies post-breach impact ('crushing SOCs'); detection should surface persistence via email rules. Pipeline missed T1098.002 / T1078 (Compromised Credentials).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Office 365 audit logs for New-InboxRule, New-TransportRule, or Set-Mailbox forwarding creation within 4 hours of a phishing email being delivered to that mailbox. Flag if forwarding destination is external or newly-created domain.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Bulk Email Sending from Internal Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Compromised accounts send phishing on attacker's behalf. Article implies ongoing threat; detection should trigger on suspicious mail flow volume from users post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-user 7-day baseline of email send counts. Alert if send count exceeds 3-sigma in a 1-hour window, or if recipient list includes >50% external domains, or if 'reply-all' patterns emerge in bulk.

suggestion.title: Monitor Phishing Landing Page Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Phishing URLs deliver users to fake login pages. Pipeline should detect credential harvesting indicators: repeated failed O365 sign-ins followed by successful login from attacker IP/location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate proxy access to known phishing domains with O365 sign-in events. Alert on pattern: (user visits phishing domain) → (failed sign-in attempts to O365 from anomalous IP within 5 min) → (successful sign-in from same attacker IP 10-30 min later).

suggestion.title: Detect Email Gateway Filter Evasion Indicators
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing may employ techniques to bypass email filters. Pipeline should surface defense-evasion tactics: header manipulation, encoding tricks, rare file types, or polymorphic URL generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email headers for spoofed Return-Path, DMARC alignment failures, or unusual encoding (base64-inside-HTML, binary attachments with misleading extensions). Alert on URLs with newly-registered domains, subdomains, or URL shorteners bundled in campaigns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Authentication Bypass on IKEv1 (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs'—core attack vector; exploited in the wild starting May 7.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN authentication logs for successful sessions initiated from unauthenticated sources on IKEv1-configured gateways. Baseline and alert on anomalies: missing or invalid machine certificates, legacy client strings, geographic outliers.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client VPN Connections Without Machine Certificate Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'accept legacy Remote Access clients and do not require a machine certificate for connections' as the exact vulnerable configuration. Configuration audit and behavioral detection both apply.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN connections from deprecated Remote Access client types when machine certificate validation is disabled in gateway config. Cross-reference against change logs for recent removal of certificate requirements.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Protocol Usage in Modern VPN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes IKEv1 is 'deprecated' and vulnerability 'affects only deployments configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol'—any IKEv1 is inherently high-risk given public exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alerts for any IKEv1 Phase 1 negotiation initiation on production VPN gateways. Assume high risk unless explicitly documented legacy client requirement exists.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Qilin Ransomware Behavior Post-VPN Access
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' after VPN breach. Post-access detection is critical for response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24-48 hours of unusual VPN access events, hunt for Qilin indicators: known C2 domains/IPs, ransomware staging patterns (file enumeration, encryption processes), and deployment of secondary payloads. Use threat intelligence feeds for Qilin-specific signatures (~400 victims suggest extensive telemetry availability).

suggestion.title: Certificate Validation Bypass in IKEv1 Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-50752 as 'certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections.' This is a separate attack vector not yet observed in the wild but high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for certificate validation failures or warnings during IKEv1 Phase 1 negotiation on site-to-site tunnels. Flag unexpected peer IP changes paired with certificate mismatches. Check for MITM proxy patterns on VPN traffic.

suggestion.title: VPN Gateway Configuration Change: Disabling Machine Certificate Requirements
suggestion.rationale: Mitigation guidance advises 'set the Machine Certificate Authentication as mandatory,' indicating that removing this requirement enables exploitation. Configuration drift is detectable before exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any firewall policy change that relaxes or removes machine certificate validation requirements on Remote Access VPN gateways. Correlate with suspicious VPN logins within 24-72 hours post-change.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Command Injection - Post-Exploitation Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...to run arbitrary commands on the host.' Detection for unexpected child processes spawned by LiteLLM (shells, system commands, utilities) captures execution phase immediately post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process is LiteLLM or its Python/Node interpreters; child spawns shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) or system utilities (nc, curl, wget). Flag commands with injection markers (;, &&, |, backticks, $()).

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Key Abuse - Authentication Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'holders of low-privilege internal-user keys' can trigger injection. Detect baseline-deviation in API authentication: atypical source IPs, agent strings, or command-like request patterns in prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate usage patterns per internal key. Alert when same key issues requests from new IP, uses system-like prompts containing shell syntax (sh -c, cmd /c, backticks), or rapid sequential calls to same endpoint.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Asset Exposure Hunt - Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context with federal patch deadline 2026-06-22. Detect all LiteLLM deployments across fleet and flag unpatched versions after remediation deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan environment for LiteLLM instances (all ports, services, containers). Match against vendor's vulnerable version range. Post-deadline 2026-06-22, flag any remaining unpatched instances as critical.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Unauthenticated Injection Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: While article specifies 'authenticated user,' command injection flaws often permit auth bypass via crafted payloads. Detect malformed/malicious requests attempting injection before/without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints containing shell metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in URL parameters, headers, or POST body. Flag 4xx auth responses followed immediately by injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary command execution capability enables attacker to spawn cron jobs, systemd timers, scheduled tasks, or reverse shells. Detect persistence mechanisms initiated from compromised LiteLLM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crontab edits, systemd unit creation, or writes to shell initialization files (.bashrc, .zshrc, rc.local) originating from LiteLLM parent process or child shells spawned by it.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: Execution from host provides pivot point for internal reconnaissance and lateral movement. Detect network enumeration or adjacent-system probing initiated from LiteLLM context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM host issuing LDAP queries, DNS queries for internal hosts, or SMB connections to admin shares. Flag port scans (nmap, masscan) spawned from LiteLLM process tree or reverse shells detected on egress.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-50751 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' using vulnerability scan results for this CVE. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Check Point Security Gateway reporting vulnerable to CVE-2026-50751 in vulnerability scanner. Cross-reference asset inventory for public/internet-routable instances. Prioritize by patch due date (2026-06-11).

suggestion.title: IKEv1 VPN Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core attack described as 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange' allowing attacker to 'bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 logs (typically in /var/log/ or dedicated IPS module) for Phase 1 key exchange completions preceded by authentication failures or missing credential payloads. Flag successful session establishment with null/invalid user credentials.

suggestion.title: External IKEv1 Handshake from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: T1190 requires public-facing application. Attack surface is IKEv1 port exposure (UDP 500 Phase 1, UDP 4500 Phase 2 NAT-T); detecting unauthenticated handshake initiation is the earliest signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag IKEv1 Phase 1 exchanges originating from non-whitelisted external IP ranges to Check Point Security Gateway. Look for repeated initiation attempts or multiple simultaneous exchanges per source (brute-force pattern on authentication bypass).

suggestion.title: Check Point Security Gateway Remote Access Session without Pre-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome explicitly stated: attacker can 'establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Successful session creation without antecedent successful authentication is the attacker's objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify VPN sessions in Check Point logs that transitioned from INITIAL_CONTACT / key-exchange to ESTABLISHED without a successful User Authentication phase. Cross-reference IKEv2 xauth or IKEv1 hybrid auth logs for absence of credential submission.

suggestion.title: UniFi OS Authentication Bypass via URI Normalization Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'craft requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization' and recommends 'look for requests containing /api/auth/validate-sso/'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with encoded, obfuscated, or semantically-different URI representations that bypass authentication validation but normalize to protected endpoints. Flag requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ lacking valid authentication tokens or arriving from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Command Injection in UniFi Package Update Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-34910 as 'command injection flaw' against 'ucs/update/latest_package', and explicitly recommends monitoring 'requests to ucs/update/latest_package' and 'suspicious child processes under ucs-update'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to /ucs/update/latest_package endpoint for shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or backtick injection in payload parameters. Correlate with unexpected child processes (bash, sh, system utilities) spawned by the ucs-update service.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Passwordless Sudo by UniFi Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states injected commands 'execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries' and recommends monitoring 'unexpected sudo commands'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any sudo or sudoedit execution from the ucs-update service account or package-update related processes. Alert on sudo invocations without preceding tty allocation, particularly those escalating to root from a non-interactive service context.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Protected Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no credentials, user interaction, or prior access are required' and 'The chain reaches root with no credentials...there is no failed-login trail to look for', requiring detection of endpoint access without auth events
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests reaching protected API endpoints (management console, /ucs/ paths, /api/management) without corresponding successful authentication log entries in the preceding seconds. Look for direct access from external sources bypassing auth enforcement.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exposure via CVE-2026-34909
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-34909 as 'path traversal vulnerability that can expose files on the underlying operating system' as part of the chained exploit
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API requests for path traversal patterns (../, encoded variants like %2e%2e/) targeting UniFi endpoints. Correlate traversal attempts with requests to /api/auth/validate-sso/ or attempts to access system configuration files outside intended directories.

suggestion.title: Raw vs. Normalized URI Mismatch Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article root-cause analysis shows 'authentication component evaluates the raw request URI, while Nginx routes requests based on a normalized version'—this mismatch is the attack vector and should be detectable
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement inspection rules to flag requests where raw URI encoding and path normalization produce significantly different results (case shifts, slash doubling, encoding differences). Alert on auth-exempt paths that normalize into protected routes.

suggestion.title: Malicious spreadsheet file (.xlsx/.ods) with phar:// scheme processed by web-server
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner' — the phar:// URI is embedded WITHIN the spreadsheet file, triggering bypass in PHPSpreadsheet parser. No UC detects the vulnerable file being read by PHP processes. T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) is in advisory but not mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file access: web-server process (php, apache, nginx) opens .xlsx/.ods file from user-writable or upload directory, followed within seconds by child process spawning (shell, curl, python). Escalate if file creation timestamp is recent (< 1 hour before access).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45034 / CVE-2026-34084 asset exposure scan
suggestion.rationale: Article lists two CVEs in 'Indicators of Compromise' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Vulnerability management context: CVE-2026-34084 was patched, but CVE-2026-45034 is a patch bypass. Assets must be rescanned and re-patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scans (Nessus, Qualys) for hosts running PHPSpreadsheet < [patched version]. Correlate with prior CVE-2026-34084 detections to identify hosts where patch was applied but incomplete (likely vulnerable to 45034 bypass).

suggestion.title: Web server spawning reverse-shell or data-exfil tooling post-PHPSpreadsheet processing
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) but no UC hunts for tool download/execution phase. After phar:// RCE, attacker downloads curl/wget/python — this is the bridge between code-execution and command-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web-server process (parent: php/apache/nginx) spawning curl/wget/socat processes with unusual command-line arguments (URLs with suspicious domains, piped shells, base64-encoded payloads). Correlate network events (child process making outbound connection) within same time window.

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet file upload followed by three-slash phar:// HTTP request
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: malicious .xlsx upload → attacker crafts HTTP request with phar:/// URI referencing uploaded file. No UC chains file-upload log with subsequent phar:// request.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST request with file upload (.xlsx MIME type) to same web application within 5 minutes of GET/POST containing phar:// or phar%3A%2F%2F URI. Flag if source IP is the same and upload was from untrusted origin (not internal systems).

suggestion.title: PHP fatal errors or exception logs from phar:// wrapper attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explains that prohibitWrappers check fails when URL has 3+ slashes. Invalid syntax may trigger PHP errors/exceptions in application logs before RCE succeeds — missed by current UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt application error logs (PHP, Apache, nginx) for messages containing 'phar://', 'wrapper', 'stream', or 'parse_url' errors originating from PHPSpreadsheet library within 2 minutes of suspicious web request. High-fidelity signal for failed/successful exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Browser plugin spawning AppleScript with network-origin URLs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'chrome_tabs plugin interpolates a [URL] without proper escaping' into AppleScript. The article explicitly describes the attack vector as URL→AppleScript interpolation, but no detection hunts for the specific pattern of browser plugins (Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari) receiving URLs from network and passing them to osascript/jxa execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for osascript/jxa processes spawned with parent process names matching Chrome, Brave, Edge, or Safari, where the command line contains URL scheme patterns (http://, https://, file://) or encoded URL fragments. Combine with network events showing browser establishing outbound connections immediately before script execution.

suggestion.title: JXA (JavaScript for Automation) code execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection' as the vulnerability mechanism. The existing detections only focus on osascript (AppleScript interpreter), but JXA uses 'jxa' binary or 'osascript -l JavaScript'. Current hunts miss the JXA variant entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for execution of 'jxa' binary or osascript invoked with '-l JavaScript' flag. JXA can perform code injection via similar mechanisms to AppleScript but may evade osascript-specific detections. Alert on jxa or osascript with javascript language flag combined with shell command patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47252 asset exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article lists CVE-2026-47252 in the IoCs section as primary identifier. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Need standard asset exposure detection: identify hosts running Anyquery 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460) or matching vulnerable version signatures, regardless of whether active exploitation is observed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Anyquery plugin versions on macOS endpoints. Flag version 0.4.4 or commits <= 0abd460. Cross-reference with vulnerability feeds for CVE-2026-47252. Combine with browser plugin telemetry to identify hosts with the vulnerable version installed and active.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin network activity preceding command execution
suggestion.rationale: The exploitation chain is: malicious URL → browser receives it → plugin processes it → AppleScript injection → code exec. No detection hunts for the sequential relationship of network inbound (URL delivery) immediately preceding osascript spawning, which is the characteristic behavior of this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser network activity (DNS lookups, HTTP requests) with osascript/jxa process creation within 5-second window. Flag if network event contains URL with special characters (%, $, &, |, ;, backtick) and is followed by suspicious AppleScript execution. This captures the URL-injection pattern.

suggestion.title: Rapid Account-to-Repository Creation by New Gogs Users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance.' and 'Any registered user who creates a repo is automatically its owner.' This is the initial access vector for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user accounts created via open registration (DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false) that provision a repository within <5 minutes, especially with no prior Git commits or commits from other accounts. Baseline normal time-delta between account creation and first repo for legitimate users.

suggestion.title: Gogs Rebase Merge Configuration Enable on Newly Created Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This setting change triggers the RCE condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repositories where 'Rebase before merging' is enabled in Advanced settings immediately after repo creation, especially by newly registered users. Correlate with repository creation in same session to identify self-contained exploit chains.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection in Gogs Merge Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'argument injection vulnerability' and 'affects a different code path (Merge()) that was never addressed.' The exploit path is a malicious merge operation with injected arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs merge operations for shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, $(), backticks) or Go-specific payloads in commit messages, branch names, or merge commit metadata. Alert on child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe) from Gogs service account post-merge or network connections from Gogs process following merge on rebase-enabled repos.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Gogs Instance (Versions ≤0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions: 'affects all Gogs releases up to and including 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev.' Patch 0.14.3 released June 7, 2026. Shadowserver tracks 2,300+ exposed instances; Shodan lists 1,000+.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Gogs API or parse version strings from HTTP headers/responses to identify instances running versions ≤0.14.2 or 0.15.0+dev. Cross-reference with open registration (DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false) and unlimited repo creation (MAX_CREATION_LIMIT=-1) flags to identify fully exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Credential Theft Post-Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers can...steal credentials, move laterally to other systems on the network.' Describes post-exploitation phase after initial RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Following suspected Gogs RCE (argument injection evidence or unexpected child process), monitor for Gogs service user or child processes accessing Git credentials (.git/config, SSH keys in ~/.ssh, .netrc), scanning network (arp, nmap, ping scans), or establishing outbound connections to internal systems on high ports (>10000) or ssh/rdp ports.

suggestion.title: Gogs Configuration Rollback Disabling Mitigations
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends setting DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true, MAX_CREATION_LIMIT=0, and disabling rebase per-repo. Changes reverting these should indicate tampering or misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to app.ini or Gogs config API changing DISABLE_REGISTRATION from true→false, MAX_CREATION_LIMIT from 0→-1, or per-repo rebase from disabled→enabled, especially outside change windows or by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: NSO Pegasus WhatsApp Phishing Link Click
suggestion.rationale: Article describes NSO Group conducting WhatsApp phishing attacks; baseline detection for phishing links shared over WhatsApp messaging platform is foundational for initial-access blocking. Title explicitly states 'WhatsApp Phishing Attack.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users clicking or accessing suspicious shortened URLs or typosquatting domains via WhatsApp mobile or web traffic. Flag first-time contact sharing links to non-whitelisted domains, especially credential-harvesting infrastructure or C2 redirects.

suggestion.title: Outbound NSO Group C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group's Pegasus spyware is mentioned by name in title; detecting callbacks to known or suspected NSO-controlled infrastructure is critical post-compromise detection. Article implies device compromise but no C2 detection baseline provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS/DNS connections to known NSO Group C2 IP blocks and domains (Pegasus infrastructure). Flag characteristic beacon patterns: frequent small data transfers, intermittent connections to non-standard HTTPS ports (e.g., 8443, 9443), or certificate mismatches on infrastructure tied to Israeli operators.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Page Access via Phishing Redirect
suggestion.rationale: WhatsApp phishing campaigns typically redirect victims to fake login portals. Article describes phishing mechanism but no detection for credential-harvesting infrastructure or POST activity was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to credential exfiltration endpoints disguised as WhatsApp login pages. Look for suspicious SSL certificates or domain masquerading, unusual user-agent strings, and rapid password entry/submission on non-WhatsApp-owned IPs.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Deployment via Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat cluster 'targeting Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers using a purpose-built web shell framework'—core attack vector entirely absent from pipeline output. No T1505.004 technique or persistence-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS application pools for abnormal child process spawning (w3wp.exe, aspnet_wp.exe launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Track writes to web root directories (wwwroot, inetpub) by IIS service accounts outside normal deployment windows. Correlate with unusual inbound HTTP requests using uncommon verbs or ASPX upload patterns.

suggestion.title: Cryptographically Obfuscated Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes web shell 'designed to evade every detection method' via cryptographic uniqueness—defense-evasion techniques (T1027, T1140) are completely absent from pipeline output. No detection for high-entropy or base64-encoded payloads in web requests or IIS logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-entropy data in HTTP request bodies or response streams (Shannon entropy > 7.0). Flag IIS logs with repeated XOR, ROT13, or base64-encoded command patterns across multiple requests. Look for cryptographic library imports (System.Security.Cryptography) in dynamically loaded ASPX shells via ETW or Module Load events.

suggestion.title: IIS Remote Code Execution Attack Surface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting 'Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers'—no detection suggested for initial exploitation vectors (T1190). How OP-512 gains initial foothold on IIS is omitted from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS logs for unusual HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, MKCOL, PROPFIND) to suspicious URI patterns. Track failed/successful requests to known IIS RCE endpoints (*.aspx upload handlers, virtual directories). Correlate with subsequent file creation or process execution within 60 seconds of anomalous HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via Web Shell
suggestion.rationale: Article implies command execution through deployed web shell—no T1059.001, T1059.003, or T1018 detection suggested. Pipeline missed execution-phase detections despite web shell being the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or cmd.exe spawned by w3wp.exe (IIS worker process) with suspicious command-line arguments (encoded commands, base64 decoders, registry operations). Monitor for unusual parent-child relationships: IIS → shell → net.exe, whoami.exe, systeminfo.exe (discovery). Correlate timing with abnormal web requests.

suggestion.title: China-linked Threat Infrastructure Registration Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies OP-512 as 'China-linked' threat cluster but pipeline extracts no actor name or geographic/infrastructure correlation. IOC domains (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com) should be correlated with actor infrastructure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference IOC domains and IPs against known Chinese APT registration patterns: whois overlap with historically confirmed OP-512 registrants, ASN geolocation to CN networks, dynamic DNS patterns, domain age/registration cadence. Flag infrastructure clusters matching previous OP-512 campaigns or linked Chinese threat groups.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DNS Resolution to OP-512 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists C2 domains (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com) but no DNS-level detection suggested. Template references C2 phase but lacks hunt for recursive DNS lookups or DNS exfiltration over these domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries from IIS servers or internal hosts to OP-512 C2 domains (ashx.lhlsjcb.com, hcgos.com). Baseline normal DNS behavior; flag high-frequency lookups (botnet-style callbacks) or queries from unexpected source subnets. Correlate with IIS file modification timestamps within 24 hours of first DNS resolution to confirm post-exploitation timing.

suggestion.title: Network Detection: Pink C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides six high-fidelity IOCs in formatted 'Indicators of Compromise' section and explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunts for C2 phase. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic to Pink C2 infrastructure: IPs 185.178.208.153, 172.93.100.252, 96.232.20.66 or domains passkeyadd.com, passkeydeploy.com, deploypasskey.com. Alert on any connection from managed endpoints; block at firewall.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Social Engineering Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector is 'using social engineering tactics to steal cloud storage credentials' but pipeline inferred no initial-access techniques. This is the attack's entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails impersonating cloud storage providers requesting password re-entry or directing to credential-harvesting landing pages. Alert on emails with lookalike cloud domains, urgency language, or requests to verify credentials.

suggestion.title: Cloud Storage Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article's stated objective is 'steal cloud storage credentials' but pipeline generated no credential-access detections. This is the core objective post-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous access to cloud storage accounts: repeated failed logins, successful logins from unusual geographies or immediately after phishing campaigns, or logins from Pink infrastructure IPs. Monitor for token theft via API access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Leak Site
suggestion.rationale: Article notes group 'launched its dedicated data leak site' and 'already listed several initial victims,' indicating data harvesting and exfiltration. No exfiltration detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk downloads, mass file sharing to external accounts, or unusual data-access patterns in cloud storage. Correlate with successful credential compromise and access from Pink-infrastructure IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Distribution via GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states GitHub repository created April 10 hosted 56 unique APKs impersonating banking apps: 'Victims are then urged to update their banking app and are redirected to a GitHub repository hosting a malicious APK file.' Pipeline missed collection/delivery pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub URLs in phishing campaigns, GitHub repository hosting suspicious APK files, or URLs redirecting to GitHub downloads of banking-themed APKs. Look for repos created/modified in April–May 2026 with banking institution names in filenames.

suggestion.title: NFC Payment Card Data Exfiltration via IsoDep/EMV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack: 'After tricking victims with a fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's near-field communication (NFC) chip, NFCShare reads the information using Android's IsoDep interface and EMV commands.' No UC generated for NFC API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android apps requesting NFC permissions paired with suspicious credential-prompt screens or card-scan UI patterns. Monitor for IsoDep interface calls followed by EMV command execution and immediate data exfiltration. Baseline: legitimate banking apps use NFC for authentication, not card-number collection.

suggestion.title: Banking App Impersonation + Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-channel social engineering: 'Recent NFCShare attacks observed starting May 14 begin with the victim visiting a phishing site that impersonates a real bank and asks for banking credentials. Victims are then urged to update their banking app...' and 'SMS messages or phone calls from fake bank representatives may also be used.' No UC for phishing + pretexting coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing landing pages impersonating Italian/Spanish banks (Intesa, Sella, CaixaBank, Nexi, Fideuram, Mooney) with SMS/call logs directing users to GitHub URLs or app update prompts. Baseline geography: victims in Europe, primarily Italy and Spain. Baseline timing: campaign activity from May 14, 2026 onward.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Communication for Payment Card Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' No UC generated for this abnormal C2 channel or for the data types being exfiltrated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket connections from mobile devices to unknown endpoints, especially those carrying payment card metadata (4-digit PIN, card type, expiry). Baseline: legitimate banking apps use TLS, not plain WebSocket. Alert on payment card strings in WebSocket payloads or base64-encoded card data in ws:// traffic.

suggestion.title: Malformed APK Packaging for Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'One interesting aspect of the new version of the malware is the introduction of malformed APK packaging to hinder automated analysis, and potentially also security tools. The APK is still a ZIP archive, but the newer samples include poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP.' This is a defense evasion tactic not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK files with internal ZIP path anomalies (relative paths that resolve as filesystem paths, malformed archive structures, or paths that trigger extraction tool errors). Correlate with failed antivirus/sandbox scans or incomplete code analysis reports. Baseline: well-formed banking APKs have valid ZIP structures.

suggestion.title: NFC Card Scan Social Engineering via Fake Verification UI
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After tricking victims with a fake verification screen to place the cards near the mobile device's near-field communication (NFC) chip, NFCShare reads the information...' and 'malware steals the card number, type, expiry date, and a 4-digit PIN entered by the victim under the pretense of a security step.' This is social engineering targeting NFC card proximity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual NFC chip activation requests paired with credential or card-entry UI prompts in financial apps. Flag apps that request card PIN entry without legitimate authentication context or that trigger NFC scans during unverified 'security verification' screens. Baseline: PIN entry for NFC transactions is extremely rare and should be rare per bank.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Exploitation – Abnormal Privilege Escalation from Unprivileged Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enables local root access'; pipeline generated no detection for privilege escalation. Must detect non-root→root transitions, especially when preceded by unusual process activity or syscall anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a process spawns a child with UID 0 after running as unprivileged user, with no credential-acquisition events (setuid, sudo, su). Correlate with failed syscalls or suspicious ioctl/mmap activity in parent process prior to escalation.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Module Loading or Dynamic Kernel Code Modification
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits frequently load modules or modify kernel memory post-compromise; 'exploits now public' implies attackers will attempt in-the-wild exploitation. No detection UC for kernel module loading or /sys/module modifications generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect insmod, modprobe, or direct writes to /sys/module/ from non-root contexts. Alert on kernel module loads outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate with preceding failed privilege escalation attempts or unusual ioctl syscalls.

suggestion.title: Detection of Vulnerable Kernel Version Execution
suggestion.rationale: 'One-character' flaw indicates a specific, easily-identified vulnerable binary. Pipeline should map kernel version/hash signatures to detect systems running exploitable releases before compromise occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain hash/version signature inventory for vulnerable Linux kernel releases. Alert on execution of /boot/vmlinuz or uname calls on systems matching vulnerable signatures. Baseline by environment and alert on any mismatch.

suggestion.title: Suspicious System Call Sequences Indicative of Kernel Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits trigger recognizable syscall chains (mmap, mprotect, prctl, ioctl, clone with specific flags). No detection for abnormal syscall patterns preceding privilege escalation was generated despite article focus on technical exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes generating rapid sequences of mmap→mprotect or high-volume ioctl calls on /dev/* or /sys/* interfaces. Flag prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0) or CAP_* operations from userland. Escalate if followed by uid/gid change.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Command Execution Following Failed Privilege Escalation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes public exploits; attackers will attempt root-level commands post-compromise. Pipeline generated no impact-phase detection for root command execution following privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning with UID 0 from a parent that previously ran as non-root, especially if parent is a known exploit vector (suid binary, Python, Java, container runtime). Correlate with file system access to /root, /etc/shadow, /boot post-escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Password Reset via Account Recovery Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'obtained password reset links' by exploiting HTS failure to 'verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Core attack vector; no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password reset requests to HTS tool where submitted email does not match registered account contact, or verification step is bypassed. Spike on failed verification attempts followed by successful resets indicates exploitation of validation gap.

suggestion.title: Mass Account Takeover via Shared Account Recovery Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 20,000 Instagram accounts stolen' through single exploited mechanism (HTS). Attack is explicitly at-scale; pipeline generated no volume-based compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained waves of successful password resets followed by logins from new geographies/devices across 50+ accounts within 24h via same recovery pathway. Correlate with known vulnerable authentication mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Post-Takeover Bulk Data Exfiltration from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'could've gained access to...direct messages and communications, photos, videos, stories, account activity.' No detection use case addresses collection/exfiltration phase post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk retrieval of user-generated content (DMs, photos, videos, stories) from recently-reset or anomalously-accessed accounts. Flag where data access velocity and scope exceed baseline after account takeover is detected.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Followed by Unauthorized Recovery Tool Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack sequence: account lockout, then recovery tool invocation for password reset. No detection use case generated for this telltale lockout→recovery→compromise chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequence of account lockout followed within minutes by password reset via support/recovery tools, then login from new IP/device. Distinguish legitimate recovery (user self-service, support-assisted) from attacker-initiated via access patterns and correlation with known compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Email Verification Bypass in Account Recovery Flows
suggestion.rationale: Article: HTS 'didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' Pipeline missed the validation/authentication bypass vector—not just password reset, but broken verification logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery/password reset logs for requests where email verification is skipped, failed verification is overridden, or email-to-account validation logic returns false-positive approval. Baseline normal recovery flow and alert on deviations in auth validation gates.

suggestion.title: Vendor-Provisioned Database Credential Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states breach occurred 'via one of its vendors' with 'unauthorized access to a database.' Pipeline generated no detection use case for monitoring vendor-supplied service accounts for anomalous access patterns, time-of-day deviations, or unexpected geographic sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database logons using vendor-provisioned service accounts occurring outside documented maintenance windows, originating from unexpected geographies or IP ranges, or showing clusters of failed attempts followed by successful access. Cross-reference with vendor communication about expected access patterns and baselines.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer PII Database Query Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach of customer database with 'personal information' exposure. Company warns of 'personal data' involvement but provided no scope. Pipeline failed to generate detection logic for large SELECT queries or bulk export operations against customer PII tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries returning large result sets spanning multiple customer records (names, emails, account identifiers, KYC data), particularly when originating from vendor-accessible accounts or unexpected sources. Flag use of backup and export utilities against production customer tables outside normal administrative maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Vendor Account Privilege Escalation to Production Data
suggestion.rationale: Vendor credentials were leveraged to access 'SoFi Securities (Hong Kong) Limited' customer database beyond expected operational scope. Pipeline did not generate use cases for detecting unauthorized privilege expansion or scope violations by compromised vendor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for permission or role assignments granted to vendor-supplied accounts that expand access to production customer data tables. Flag vendor credentials accessing resources outside their documented operational scope, especially deviations from historical baseline access patterns.

suggestion.title: Vishing Campaign Detection - Targeted Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'vishing' as primary attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface any detection use case for voice-based social engineering. Phrase: 'UNC3753 Used Vishing...in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume unsolicited phone calls to employee groups targeting credentials or access information. Correlate with failed login attempts, password reset requests, or MFA bypass attempts in hours following reported vishing calls. Track callers impersonating IT, vendor support, or executive personnel requesting access details.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Physical Access & Facility Intrusion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'physical intrusions' as attack method but pipeline generated zero detection. Physical access is the initial compromise vector enabling downstream credential and data theft. Phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on after-hours or weekend badge access for users not on approved maintenance/on-call schedule. Flag tailgating events (multiple personnel entering on single badge swipe) and unusual access to secure/data centers. Cross-reference badge timelines with security camera footage for unrecognized personnel or vehicles.

suggestion.title: Post-Intrusion Credential Extraction & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Data theft campaign implies post-intrusion credential harvesting. Pipeline missed detection for credential dumping tools (mimikatz, LSASS access) or network sniffing following physical compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LSASS memory access, credential dumping tools, or network packet sniffing immediately following physical intrusion timelines. Monitor for unusual process launches with SYSTEM privileges correlated to facility access events. Alert on unusual WMI/RPC activity indicative of lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Staging & Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'data theft extortion campaign' requiring data collection and bulk exfil, but pipeline suggested zero detection for compression, archiving, or data movement. Phrase: 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file compression (7zip, WinRAR, tar, zip) in sensitive data directories. Alert on large data transfers to non-corporate IP ranges, foreign countries, or free cloud storage services. Monitor for uploads to paste sites, threat-actor infrastructure, or anonymous file hosting.

suggestion.title: Ransom Demand & Extortion Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'extortion campaign' as objective but pipeline generated zero detection for ransom notes, leak site threats, or threat-actor contact channels. Critical post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search endpoints for ransom/threat note artifacts (README.txt, DECRYPT_ME.html, RESTORE_FILES.txt). Monitor inbound email for extortion demands claiming stolen data possession. Track web traffic to known threat-actor leak sites, paste services, or Tor/I2P infrastructure claiming to host exfiltrated data.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo BRICKSTORM Linux Appliance Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names threat actor VerdantBamboo deploying BRICKSTORM variant on Linux. Pipeline extracted neither. This is the primary incident narrative and should be the anchor detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious binary execution on Linux appliances following network delivery. Look for BRICKSTORM process hashes, filenames, or command-line signatures. Correlate with delivery vectors (phishing, supply-chain compromise) within 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM Binary Cross-Platform Detection (Linux)
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates a BSD variant deployed on Linux—suggests malware family is portable/cross-platform. Pipeline must detect the malware family artifact regardless of OS variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BRICKSTORM variants by file hashing, strings matching known samples, or behavioral artifacts (unusual network egress, process injection attempts). Establish baseline for Linux appliance process behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Linux Appliance Persistence Mechanism (Post-Deployment)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployment but not persistence mechanisms. Typical APT malware establishes persistence via cron jobs, systemd services, or kernel modules. Pipeline should anticipate this attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/cron.d, /etc/crontab, /etc/systemd/system, and kernel module loading post-BRICKSTORM execution. Flag unsigned systemd units or cron entries executing from unusual paths (tmp, /dev/shm, non-standard lib directories).

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM C2 Beaconing (Linux Appliance)
suggestion.rationale: Deployed malware must establish command-and-control. Article does not detail C2 infrastructure; pipeline should generate hypothesis-driven detection for C2 patterns on hardened appliances (unusual outbound, DNS tunneling, HTTP POST to suspicious domains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Linux appliances to unknown or newly-registered domains post-BRICKSTORM execution. Flag DNS exfiltration patterns, suspicious HTTP User-Agents, or encrypted tunnel protocols (DNS-over-HTTPS) from appliance subnets.

suggestion.title: VerdantBamboo Delivery Chain (Phishing / Supply-Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies VerdantBamboo delivered malware but mechanism unstated. Common vectors: phishing, watering hole, supply-chain. Pipeline should generate broad detections for typical initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with malicious attachments or links from threat-intel feeds associated with VerdantBamboo. Monitor for suspicious downloads to Linux appliance users (Office macros, archives, shell scripts). Cross-reference with known VerdantBamboo C2 IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Network-based FFmpeg RCE detection — 183-byte exploit packet signature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'single 183-byte network packet' triggers heap buffer overflow RCE. Pipeline provided zero network detections despite this being the explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network traffic to endpoints running FFmpeg (browsers, media servers, CDN, surveillance) for anomalously-sized packets (160–200 bytes) on media ports (1935 RTMP, 80/443 HLS/DASH/HTTP). Correlate packet spike with immediate destination-host process anomalies or crashes.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg RCE post-exploitation process behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome but pipeline has no detection for code execution indicators post-exploitation. Missing behavioral alerts for shell spawning, unexpected child processes, or outbound connections following media process compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FFmpeg, ffprobe, ffserver, or embedded media processes spawn unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, nc, curl). Flag if parent is a media file, RTMP stream handler, or Chromium renderer. Include parent network context in alert metadata.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg supply-chain compromise or malicious binary distribution
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg embedded in browsers, streaming platforms, cloud infrastructure creates mass distribution surface. Article notes widespread deployment but pipeline has zero supply-chain detection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg binary creation outside trusted package managers (apt, brew, choco, MSI). Detect unsigned or incorrectly-signed FFmpeg binaries. Alert on FFmpeg loads from non-standard paths (temp, AppData, /tmp). Cross-correlate suspicious binary with subsequent process spawning or network activity.

suggestion.title: Detect heap buffer overflow exploitation or crash-before-RCE patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'heap buffer overflow' as specific RCE mechanism. Pipeline abstracted away exploit type; should detect memory corruption indicators, application crashes, or ASLR bypasses preceding code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg and media-processing applications for crashes with heap corruption signatures (Windows: HEAP_CORRUPTION, access violations on freed memory; Linux: segmentation faults, double-free patterns). Flag crash events followed by successful code execution in same or child process within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Detect FFmpeg RCE exploitation attempts via network scanning or fuzzing probes
suggestion.rationale: Once zero-days are public, attackers probe for vulnerable instances. Pipeline provides no reconnaissance or probe-detection for exploitation attempts targeting media endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to media endpoints (RTMP 1935, HLS/DASH on 80/443) for malformed headers, binary payloads where text expected, or rapid sequential requests of varying sizes (scanning pattern). Correlate probe attempts with downstream exploitation attempts or CVE-specific scanner fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE credential access and lateral movement from compromised media services
suggestion.rationale: Article implies RCE but provides no detection for post-exploitation objectives. In widespread deployments, FFmpeg compromise is stepping stone to credential theft or domain escalation, not end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FFmpeg or media-service child processes accessing credential stores (LSASS.exe, /etc/shadow), spawning dumping tools (mimikatz, hashdump), or establishing lateral connections to file shares, registry, or LDAP. Focus on privilege elevation from unprivileged media-service user context to SYSTEM or domain accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect IKEv1 VPN Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-50751)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw...to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection'. Core attack vector; zero detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN logs for IKEv1 key exchange from sources without valid machine certificates. Flag successful authentication immediately following failed certificate validation. Alert if Machine Certificate Verification = False on IKEv1 sessions.

suggestion.title: Detect Legacy Remote Access Client Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires accepting 'legacy Remote Access clients' and Check Point advises to 'remove support for the legacy remote access client'. No detection for deprecated client versions generated.
