suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'exfiltrates it to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) host over a WebSocket channel.' WebSocket is a distinct C2 protocol from HTTP POST that requires specific detection rules for financial data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) from Android devices to C2 endpoints with payloads matching card data patterns: 4-7 consecutive digits for PIN/CVV, 16-digit patterns for PAN, date fields matching MM/YY expiry format. Flag if connection persists >60 seconds with multiple exfil frames.

suggestion.title: Malformed ZIP/APK Structure for Analysis Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'newer samples include poisoned/malformed file paths within that ZIP, causing some extraction tools to wrongly interpret internal relative paths as filesystem paths.' This obfuscation is directly detectable via APK integrity analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APKs with invalid ZIP central directory entries, relative path traversal sequences (../) in internal manifests, mismatched file sizes in headers, or tools that fail to extract certain classes. Correlate with banking app names and GitHub source attribution.

suggestion.title: Multi-Bank APK Variant Clustering from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 56 unique APKs impersonating multiple banks: 'Intesa Carte.apk, Sella Carte.apk, CaixaBank.apk, CaixaBankNfc.apk, CaixaReactivaTarjeta.apk, Nexi Carte.apk, Fideuram Carte.apk, Mooney Carte.apk.' Mass-production of variants is a strong clustering indicator for campaign detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of APKs impersonating different financial institutions sharing identical code sections, C2 endpoints, or signing keys. Use fuzzy hashing or semantic similarity to group variants; correlate with rapid uploads from same source and geographic targeting (Italy, Spain, Germany).

suggestion.title: Linux Local Privilege Escalation via Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access'—privilege escalation is the attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate any kill-chain detection despite clear impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes spawning root shells without sudo/su, unusual kernel module loading, or process parent=kernel with unexpected children. Alert on privilege escalation events following anomalous system calls.

suggestion.title: Public Kernel Exploit Execution Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle 'Exploits Now Public' indicates weaponized code is available. Detection case missing for identifying live exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of publicly-released exploit binaries/scripts; trigger on process execution with suspicious arguments or file staging patterns consistent with exploit delivery (downloads followed by immediate execution).

suggestion.title: CVE Kernel Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have extracted CVE identifier from article context or fallback-tracked it as 'unknown Linux kernel vulnerability'; no generic kernel CVE monitoring rule was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE identifier is confirmed, match against known-vulnerable kernel versions at login time. Alert on exploitation signatures: specific syscall failure patterns, SMAC violations, or post-exploitation behavioral markers (unexpected UID 0 processes).

suggestion.title: Email-Account Mismatch in Password Reset Requests via Support System
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'exploited a flaw in the company's High Touch Support (HTS) tool' because 'HTS didn't verify whether email addresses were associated with the targeted Instagram accounts.' This is the root cause: the system accepted password reset requests for mismatched email-account pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery/password reset endpoints for requests where the email address in the request does not match registered account email. Flag patterns where single or batch requests test multiple email-account combinations. Alert on high-volume password reset requests from the same source IP/user agent in short timeframe, particularly if targeting users not initiating the recovery.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Password Reset Followed by Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 20,000 accounts compromised; 'obtained password reset links that allowed them to log in.' Attack signature is password reset initiation followed rapidly by account access from anomalous location/device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password reset tokens generated for high volumes of users (>50 unique users in 1hr window) followed by successful logins from geographically disparate or VPN-sourced IPs within 15 minutes of reset. Correlate account reset and login logs to identify cases where reset initiator differs from login source.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Token Abuse Bypassing MFA Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'hijack accounts without two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled'—password reset links were used as a backdoor that didn't trigger the normal MFA challenge. This is a defense evasion technique targeting the authentication process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when account access occurs via password-reset flow (detected via auth token or session type field) without subsequent MFA verification, especially for accounts where MFA is normally required. Baseline users' normal authentication path (direct login vs. recovery); flag deviations. Cross-reference successful post-reset logins with account MFA status history to catch cases where MFA was disabled or reset link bypassed it.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access from Recovered Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers could access 'contact information (email, phone)...direct messages and communications...account activity and interaction history.' This is the post-compromise collection phase and should trigger alerts for unusual bulk data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor recently compromised accounts for abnormal data retrieval patterns: bulk DM/message export, contact list enumeration, media/photo downloads, follower/interaction history queries. Establish baseline for each account's typical API call patterns post-login; flag anomalies especially if queries target sensitive PII fields (email, phone, DOB) or communications.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Account Recovery Requests from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploited HTS tool to reset passwords for 20,000 accounts; article dates indicate April 17 as likely attack start. This is a distinguishing pattern: one attacker or coordinated group submitting thousands of password reset requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >100 account recovery/password reset requests originating from single IP, user agent, or API key within 24hrs. Correlate request destination accounts (were they targeted in coordinated fashion?) and timing. Investigate whether request patterns suggest enumeration (cycling through account identifiers) vs. targeted (specific account list).

suggestion.title: Account Lockout to Recovery to Access Chain Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: HTS tool is described as helping 'users regain access after being locked out.' Attack chain likely involved users being locked out, then attackers using HTS to reset. This lockout→recovery→compromise sequence is a distinctive IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user account lockouts (failed login attempts threshold) with subsequent password reset initiations from different source than the user who triggered the lockout. Flag cases where account lockout is followed by recovery request within minutes, especially if reset is initiated from IP/device different from user's baseline, or if user reports not requesting the reset.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Exploitation via Malicious JavaScript Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes CVE-2026-11645 'exploited in the wild'—implying active JavaScript-based payloads trigger V8 engine vulnerabilities. No detection exists for the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome/Chromium processes for abnormal script execution, sudden memory spikes, or child process spawning (especially system executables like cmd.exe). Correlate with unexpected network connections post-crash or post-anomaly.

suggestion.title: Browser Sandbox Escape Detection Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: V8 zero-days enable privilege escalation and sandbox bypass to achieve system execution. Article emphasizes wild exploitation but zero sandbox-escape detections present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Chrome processes spawn system-privileged executables without user interaction. Monitor for file I/O from browser sandboxed processes to restricted system paths.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2026-11645 Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Patch Now', indicating patch status is critical. Pipeline must detect Chrome installations vulnerable to CVE-2026-11645 and flag delayed patch adoption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Chrome versions preceding the CVE-2026-11645 fix version. Flag unpatched systems > 7 days post-patch release, especially those exposed to untrusted networks or public internet.

suggestion.title: Malicious Drive-By Download / Watering Hole Detection
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation requires initial delivery (malicious link, infected website, email attachment). Article references 'exploited in the wild' but zero initial-access detections provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious HTML/iframe injection targeting Chromium-specific APIs, unusual redirects preceding Chrome crashes, or emails with links known to host exploit kits. Correlate web access with subsequent V8-related process anomalies.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) Activity Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Exploited V8 may expose debugging interfaces or enable command injection via CDP. Article lacks detection for post-exploitation C2 or lateral-movement via debugging protocols.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Chrome processes accepting debugging connections on non-standard or localhost ports (9222, 9229 variants). Alert on unexpected network activity from Chrome to internal hosts immediately following exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: V8 Memory Corruption Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: V8 exploits trigger memory safety violations (heap overflow, UAF). Article provides no detection for crash telemetry, memory anomalies, or exploitation fingerprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome crash dumps with heap corruption, buffer overflow, or use-after-free signatures. Correlate crashes with suspicious script execution, unusual parent processes, or network access from crashed process context.

suggestion.title: IKEv1 Protocol Usage in Check Point VPN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol'—IKEv1 usage is the prerequisite condition for CVE-2026-50751 exploitation and should be monitored as high-risk configuration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Remote Access VPN, Mobile Access, and Spark firewall logs for IKEv1 key exchange protocol usage. Deprecated IKEv1 indicates potentially vulnerable configuration exploitable via CVE-2026-50751. Alert on any IKEv1 session establishment, especially from untrusted external networks or from previously unseen client IPs.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Without Machine Certificate Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections' as a vulnerability condition—successful authentications lacking machine certificate validation indicate either vulnerable configuration or active exploitation
log_sources: Check Point SSL VPN authentication logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point VPN logs for successful remote access authentications that bypass or lack machine certificate validation. Alert on connections from legacy Remote Access clients (pre-IKEv2 era) that successfully authenticate without the requisite machine certificate, which enables CVE-2026-50751 exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Legacy Remote Access Client Connection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability applies to systems that 'accept legacy Remote Access clients'—legacy client connections are both the exploitation vector and an anomalous event indicative of CVE-2026-50751 vulnerability or active exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Check Point Spark, Mobile Access, and Remote Access VPN connections from legacy Remote Access clients (non-IKEv2-compliant). These outdated clients are the attack vector for this CVE and should either be blocked or trigger heightened authentication scrutiny including mandatory machine certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN Access Qilin Ransomware Activity Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate' following VPN exploitation—detections should correlate VPN access to downstream ransomware execution and encryption behavior
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful VPN authentications (especially vulnerable configurations: IKEv1, missing machine cert, legacy clients) with subsequent Qilin ransomware indicators: file encryption patterns, ransom note creation, known Qilin process artifacts. Alert if encryption activity or Qilin-associated behavior occurs within 24 hours of new VPN session from external IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated VPN Connection Establishment Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core exploit: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw...to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection'—direct detection of the auth bypass mechanism
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point VPN authentication logs for sessions that establish successfully despite missing or invalid pre-authentication credentials. Flag IKEv1 negotiations that complete phase-1 and phase-2 without valid machine certificate or client authentication, and correlate spike in such events after May 7, 2026 (exploitation timeline start).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Web Interface Access to FortiSandbox with Command-Like Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands through the web interface.' Pipeline missed the primary attack surface: web endpoint access without auth credentials, combined with command-injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox web administrative ports (443, 8080, 9443) originating from external IPs with no valid session token or auth header. Flag payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), &&, ||, backtick, newline) in predictable parameter positions (likely command/script/execute fields). Baseline: ratio of failed-auth:payload-injection attempts per source.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution on FortiSandbox (Process Spawning Post-Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary OS commands.' Detection must track not just the exploit attempt, but successful execution artifacts. Pipeline failed to map execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events on FortiSandbox appliances where parent process is the web server (httpd, nginx, tomcat, or FortiSandbox-specific service) spawning a shell interpreter (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell), especially with UID/GID elevation or execution context inconsistent with normal operation. Key: correlate parent process port listening on web interface port with child command strings containing typical post-exploit payloads (curl, wget, nc, reverse-shell syntax).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Payload Signature Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific CVE flaw. Generic vulnerability scanning alone insufficient; need signature-based detection of exploitation attempts once vendor PoC or IDS rules published.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for parameter payloads exhibiting CVE-2026-25089 exploitation signatures (once vendor advisory includes them or public PoC analysis available). Baseline: anomalous parameter encoding, double-encoding, or command-execution syntax in fields tied to the vulnerability—e.g., 'script', 'command', 'execute', 'shell', 'cmd' parameters.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2/Exfil from Compromised FortiSandbox Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes command execution capability; assumes attacker pivots to C2 or data exfiltration. Pipeline did not anticipate post-exploit lateral or exfil phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiSandbox outbound traffic (vendor updates, threat-feed pulls, legitimate external API calls). Alert on new external IP/domain connections initiated from FortiSandbox processes post-exploitation (correlate timestamp with execution-phase process-creation events). Flag DNS queries from the appliance to non-whitelisted external domains, especially with high entropy or frequency anomalies.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Single Account Accessing Multiple Service Shards
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'accessed every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard' from single compromised account and 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages.' Single account spanning multiple organizational shards (education shard explicitly named) in short window is structurally anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single service account accessing resources across multiple Tchap shards (matrix.agent.*.tchap.gouv.fr) within short time window. Baseline expected cross-shard access by role; alert on accounts exceeding baseline or newly-compromised accounts making any cross-shard access attempts.

suggestion.title: File Download Without Authentication Token
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor explicitly states: 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token' and 'media IDs come from the messages. Once you have a message with a media URL you can pull the file freely.' Direct infrastructure/API abuse of missing authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file download requests to Tchap media endpoints (pattern: /media/<ID>) lacking bearer tokens or valid session cookies. Correlate volume and media ID entropy to detect bulk exfiltration. Baseline: all requests should authenticate; flag unauthenticated retrievals.

suggestion.title: Bulk Message Scraping and Sequential Message Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages' from service. Bulk collection of this magnitude has distinct patterns: sequential message ID enumeration, high-volume pagination, or bulk export API usage across conversation boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential or range-based message ID queries from single account (e.g., iterative offset-based pagination across >600k messages). Flag accounts querying >10k messages per hour. Correlate temporal pattern to account compromise and LDAP credential first-use timestamps.

suggestion.title: LDAP Credential Extraction via Shared PowerShell Script
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director.' Credentials in plaintext scripts represent credential_access TTP and organizational-level exposure vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell scripts for LDAP connection strings (ldap://, LDAP.ServerName), hardcoded DN patterns (CN=, OU=), and cleartext credentials in variable assignments. Alert on scripts shared via file shares, email attachments, or repositories accessible to regional directors. Correlate to LDAP bind events using extracted credential hashes.

suggestion.title: Compromised Account Access to Unencrypted Public Rooms at Scale
suggestion.rationale: DINUM statement: 'public chat rooms are accessible to any user and are not encrypted.' Attacker accessed these public rooms from single account at scale. Spike in unencrypted room enumeration/access by compromised account signals reconnaissance or collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of per-account public room access frequency (typically low; sensitive communication should use encrypted private rooms per policy). Alert on accounts accessing >50 distinct public rooms in 1-hour window or newly-provisioned/compromised accounts joining any public rooms. Correlate to account creation/compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Stolen Directory Credentials Enabling Cross-Shard Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker's LDAP credentials enabled access to 'every file...on any shard' regardless of organizational boundaries, indicating stolen credentials possessed overly broad LDAP scope. This is privilege escalation via stolen service account or admin credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LDAP queries for all-shard or cross-organizational-unit enumeration patterns (wildcards, bulk DN lookups, null base DN searches). Alert on LDAP binds using service/system account credentials followed by immediate cross-shard resource queries or account enumeration (73k+ accounts). Baseline: expected LDAP scope per role; flag broad searches.

suggestion.title: Browser crash telemetry from exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states zero-days 'actively exploited in the wild' but pipeline has no hunt for the exploitation itself. Triggering memory-corruption or RCE vulnerabilities in Chrome causes crashes: 'The post Google Chrome 0-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild — Update Now' indicates active delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormal Chrome process terminations (exit code != 0) on unpatched versions correlated with web browsing to suspicious domains. Stack traces or exception codes pointing to memory corruption (EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, EXCEPTION_INVALID_OPERATION) suggest exploitation vs. legitimate crashes.

suggestion.title: Malware delivery via compromised or attacker-controlled websites
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms exploits are active; attackers must host or inject payloads. Article phrase 'exploited in the wild' implies operational infrastructure, yet no detection hunt for delivery vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unpatched Chrome instances making outbound connections to newly-registered domains or known attacker infrastructure hosting exploit payloads. Correlate DNS queries and HTTP requests for patterns consistent with drive-by-download scenarios targeting the vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation beaconing from compromised hosts
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of a browser RCE typically leads to callback to C2. Article does not detail post-compromise activity, but operational zero-day attacks assume persistence/communication phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from compromised hosts that successfully executed the exploit. Look for patterns: beaconing intervals, connections to rare TLDs, or responses from attacker-controlled IP space after a crash event correlation window.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability stems from 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness in the Chrome V8 JavaScript engine' exploited 'via crafted HTML pages to execute arbitrary code.' No detection for exploitation of this code execution vector was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome (chrome.exe, chromium) processes for abnormal child spawning, unexpected system calls, or memory access patterns following rendering of untrusted HTML content. Correlate with crash dumps containing V8 engine traces or out-of-bounds memory references in heap allocators.

suggestion.title: Chrome Sandbox Escape and Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'execute arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox' and 'access data beyond the memory buffer via heap corruption.' No detection for sandbox escape or post-exploitation execution was offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome processes spawning child processes with elevated privileges or escaping sandbox confinement indicators. Monitor for unusual system interactions (file/registry writes, network calls) originating from Chrome renderer processes, which should normally be restricted.

suggestion.title: ASLR Bypass and Heap Spray Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the zero-day 'could also be exploited to bypass protection mechanisms such as ASLR, making it easier to achieve code execution via another weakness.' No detection for ASLR bypass or ROP gadget/heap spray precursors was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome processes with unusual memory patterns consistent with heap spray (repeated allocation of large JavaScript strings/arrays). Correlate with crashes in memory regions that should be randomized. Flag repeated failures in Chrome startup after applying non-standard command-line flags that might disable ASLR.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chrome Version Running After Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies patched versions (149.0.7827.102, 149.0.7827.103) and notes 'update was available immediately.' Detection for persistence of unpatched vulnerable instances would enable risk quantification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome processes running versions earlier than 149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or 149.0.7827.103 (Mac) after the patch date (June 9, 2026). Correlate with user blocking or deferring updates; flag machines unable to auto-update within 30 days.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption and Out-of-Bounds Memory Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the core weakness as 'out-of-bounds read and write weakness' causing 'heap corruption.' No specific detection for heap memory anomalies or crash patterns indicative of exploitation attempts was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Chrome crashes with error codes or stack traces indicating heap corruption (e.g., heap validation failures, invalid memory dereferences in allocator). Cross-reference crash signatures with public PoCs or vulnerability databases. Monitor for patterns of rapid crash-restart cycles from rendering engine.

suggestion.title: Exploitation via Malicious Web Content Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTML pages' delivered to Chrome users. No detection for identification of attacker-controlled delivery infrastructure or user interaction with malicious content was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users accessing newly registered domains, known phishing infrastructure, or watering-hole sites within the vulnerability window. Correlate Chrome crashes with prior visits to low-reputation or suspicious web hosts. Flag beaconing to attacker C2 infrastructure correlated with time window of known exploits.

suggestion.title: Python setup.py execution with Bun subprocess spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'packages poisoned to auto-run Bun credential stealer'—setup.py hooks or __init__.py files would trigger on package import, spawning the Bun runtime to collect credentials. The pipeline did not generate any detection for supply-chain-injected code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python interpreter spawning Bun runtime (bun.exe / bun binary) with no direct user invocation. Correlate with recent pip install or package update events. Alert if Bun is spawned with credential-stealing indicators (env var enumeration, file globbing for .ssh, .aws, .config paths).

suggestion.title: Credential file access from package installation context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer functionality requires access to credential stores (SSH keys, AWS credentials, browser cookies, shell history). Article states stealer will 'auto-run'—this implies immediate credential harvesting at package import time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes accessing .ssh/, .aws/, .config/, .bash_history, or Chrome/Firefox credential stores during package installation. Establish baseline for normal Python package activity; credential access is rare during setup. Tuning: exclude build tools with known credential-touching behavior.

suggestion.title: Staged exfiltration from poisoned package runtime
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must transmit stolen credentials to attacker infrastructure. Article emphasizes 'auto-run'—the exfiltration should occur immediately or within minutes of package installation, before defender intervention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST or DNS queries initiated by Python or Bun processes to unknown/low-reputation domains within 10 minutes of a pip install event. Focus on outbound to non-CDN, non-corporate IP space. Payload inspection: look for base64-encoded credential dumps, JSON-serialized env vars, or SSH private key material.

suggestion.title: Poisoned package metadata harvesting from PyPI mirrors
suggestion.rationale: 19 packages were poisoned; article does not clarify whether all were new packages or existing packages re-uploaded. Detection should cover both compromised maintainer accounts and wholesale repository injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI package release activity: flag bulk uploads from single account in short timeframe, packages with suspicious version bumps (e.g., jump from 1.0 to 1.0.1 with new binary dependencies), and packages with setup.py or __init__.py that invoke external executables or shell commands at import time.

suggestion.title: Environment variable enumeration by Python interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must discover what credentials exist on the host. Rapid iteration over os.environ, glob.glob, or subprocess calls to enumerate shell config files indicates suspicious setup.py logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes calling subprocess with 'env', 'printenv', 'set', or 'env | grep' commands during package installation. Flag rapid sequential file access to .bashrc, .zshrc, .bash_profile, .ksh_profile within a single package setup transaction.

suggestion.title: Detection of poisoned package installation via package manager logs
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is users installing the 19 affected packages. Article cites 'Hades PyPI attack'—incident response requires tracking which hosts installed any of the 19 packages to scope compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once the 19 package names are published (by incident responders), query all pip install commands and package manager logs for those names within a 30-day window (duration of malicious versions on PyPI). Cross-reference with endpoint telemetry to flag hosts that executed the poisoned packages.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Exploitation Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild' — no detection use case was produced for exploitation attempts despite this being the primary threat vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to LiteLLM API endpoints with payloads matching known CVE-2026-42271 exploitation signatures. Monitor for requests that bypass authentication layers or contain embedded code execution patterns targeting the vulnerable code path.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Command Execution via Compromised LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE' — pipeline missed detection logic for arbitrary command execution by unauthenticated actors against LiteLLM service
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by LiteLLM service/Python interpreter without corresponding user authentication events. Flag shell command execution (bash, cmd.exe, PowerShell) initiated from LiteLLM process with zero interactive logon records.

suggestion.title: API Credential Extraction from Compromised LiteLLM Instance
suggestion.rationale: RCE against LLM proxy layer grants access to stored API keys, model credentials, and downstream authentication tokens — zero detection for credential theft
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads targeting LiteLLM configuration directories (~/.litellm_proxy, /etc/litellm), environment variable dumps, or in-memory credential extraction from running processes post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Backend LLM APIs and Databases
suggestion.rationale: Compromised proxy gains position to pivot to upstream model providers and downstream datastores — missing detection for outbound connections to new destinations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SSH/RDP/HTTP connections from LiteLLM service to IPs not in baseline routing whitelist. Alert on connections to external LLM provider APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) with request rates or patterns deviating from baseline usage.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from LiteLLM Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full RCE impact ('Chains to Unauthenticated RCE') — missing detection for post-exploitation privilege escalation to root/system
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudoers invocation, process injection, or scheduled task creation initiated by LiteLLM service account. Alert on elevation of privilege without corresponding user interaction or service-management authorization.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Timing API Calls for SSD Latency Profiling
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states FROST 'lets websites track what sites and apps you open via SSD timing' — adversary JavaScript measures cache/SSD access latencies via performance.now() and similar browser APIs to infer user's installed applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious patterns of JavaScript calling performance.now(), performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory(), or Resource Timing API repeatedly within a single session to measure latency deltas. Alert on correlation of timing measurements with filesystem probes (checking for app binaries, registry keys) suggesting software enumeration via side-channel.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Installed Applications via SSD Timing Side-Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack method: websites infer running apps by measuring SSD latency differences. This maps to software discovery and process discovery via indirect side-channel inference rather than direct API queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scripts attempting to correlate timing measurements with known application binaries, installed software paths, or active process existence. Look for patterns where load times for resources associated with specific apps (e.g., LinkedIn desktop, Slack, Zoom) are measured and aggregated to infer installation/execution.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin SSD Latency Probing for Site/App Inference
suggestion.rationale: FROST attack described as measuring timing across different contexts — article states attack 'lets websites track what sites and apps you open,' implying timing measurements to detect cached app artifacts or prior page loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Resource Timing API requests for non-existent resources or specially-crafted URLs across multiple origins where only timing delta (hit=fast, miss=slow) provides value. Alert when timing measurements are collected from different sites/apps and aggregated, suggesting inference of user's app installation or browsing history.

suggestion.title: Browser Fingerprinting via Timing Side-Channel Measurement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tracking user's app/site activity via timing inference — this is an extension of browser fingerprinting combining timing channels with application inventory discovery to build a unique profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect coordinated calls to performance measurement APIs combined with probes for user-agent strings, installed plugins, WebGL capabilities, and SSD latency measurements within the same page load. Alert on aggregation of these signals into a fingerprinting beacon sent to attacker-controlled domain.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44963 RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A vulnerability allowing remote code execution (RCE) on the Backup Server by an authenticated domain user' affecting VBR 12.3.2.4465 and earlier — core attack vector requiring active detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VBR service accounts (typically SYSTEM or domain service accounts) for abnormal child process spawning, unsigned binary execution, or network requests to VBR API endpoints (port 9392, 9393). Alert on POST/PUT requests to VBR Backup Server endpoints from low-privilege domain user contexts with unusual payload encoding or size anomalies.

suggestion.title: Backup Server Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'move within breached networks' using backup servers as pivots — detect outbound lateral movement from compromised VBR host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After RCE on backup server, monitor for unusual outbound SMB/RDP/WinRM connections to internal systems from VBR host source IP, elevated authentication chains originating from VBR service account, or network pivots to storage arrays and domain controllers not in baseline communication profile.

suggestion.title: Backup Metadata / Restore Point Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'block restoration efforts by deleting victims' backups' as explicit ransomware objective — mass backup deletion is critical impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion of VBR backup metadata files (.vbk, .vib), removal of restore points within VBR catalog, purging of backup chains by domain users or service accounts, or disabling of VSS writers on backup appliances. Baseline daily deletion patterns and flag anomalous volume spikes.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Domain Account Discovery of Veeam Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'any domain user with low privileges can exploit this vulnerability' — detect reconnaissance phase by non-admin domain users targeting VBR infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain users enumerating Veeam infrastructure (DNS lookups for VBR hostnames, port scans against 9392/9393/10000, LDAP queries for Veeam server groups), failed authentication attempts to VBR, or lateral movement from non-privileged workstations to Veeam subnets outside documented admin baselines.

suggestion.title: Veeam Backup & Replication Version 12.x Inventory and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'all earlier version 12 builds' through 12.3.2.4465 — rapid asset inventory of vulnerable VBR versions is prerequisite for patch prioritization and SOC alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Veeam\Veeam Backup and Replication for ProductVersion string; flag all 12.x versions ≤12.3.2.4465 as vulnerable in CMDB. Correlate process command-line arguments (Veeam.Backup.Shell.exe version enumeration) with host inventory; alert SOC on vulnerable installations without immediate patching plan.

suggestion.title: SHA256 malware hash match — Weedhack samples
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 30 high-fidelity SHA256 hashes; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. These are explicit indicators of the malware install payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file hashes against the 30 Weedhack SHA256 IOCs. Flag any process execution or file write matching these hashes. High confidence: exact hash match on known malware binaries.

suggestion.title: Minecraft launcher or mod-tool executing suspicious child process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploiting their interest in game modifications' — Weedhack is delivered as malicious mods. Detect when javaw.exe, Minecraft.exe, or mod managers spawn unusual child processes (cmd, powershell, curl, certutil).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent-child relationships: legitimate Minecraft processes (javaw.exe, launcher processes) spawning command-line interpreters, script engines, or network utilities indicates malware dropper behavior.

suggestion.title: Credential access following Minecraft/mod installer execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal credentials, drain cryptocurrency wallets, and hijack accounts' — detection gap on credential-theft phase. Alert on LSASS access, credential manager queries, or browser password-store reads by child processes of Minecraft launchers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Child processes spawned from Minecraft/game-modification tools accessing LSASS, querying %APPDATA%\..\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, or reading Discord token storage indicate post-execution credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration to cryptocurrency or account-reset endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'drain cryptocurrency wallets, and hijack accounts' — no detection on command-and-control or exfiltration phase. Pipeline missed technique T1537 (data exfil to cloud) and T1071 (application-layer protocol C2).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound TLS/HTTPS from Minecraft-process children to wallet APIs, account-recovery endpoints, or known crypto-theft infrastructure. Flag any exfil of credential JSON or authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Account login anomalies post-Weedhack infection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijack accounts' — detection gap on lateral movement and impact. Alert on unusual sign-in patterns (new geoips, impossible travel, failed MFA attempts) shortly after Weedhack execution is observed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-hash or process-execution alerts for Weedhack samples with abnormal account login activity (new device, geography, MFA bypass, or account-enumeration failures) within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Mod-distribution site or Discord server C2 callback
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies MaaS targeting 'Minecraft players' via 'game modifications' — no detection for initial-access communication (Discord channels, mod sites, forums). Pipeline missed T1566 (phishing) and T1583 (infrastructure reconnaissance).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTP requests to known Minecraft mod-distribution domains or Discord API endpoints followed by unusual child-process spawns or file-write activity. Discord-based C2 is common for gaming malware.

suggestion.title: LLM Model File Write Followed by Subprocess Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'self-replicating AI worm that operates entirely on local, open-weight models'—requires detection of suspicious model weight files (.bin, .safetensors, .pt) written to disk followed by immediate inference process or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes of model weight files (>100MB, .bin/.safetensors/.pt extension) from temp or user-writable paths, immediately followed (within 30s) by Python/Node/C++ subprocess spawning or LLM inference tool execution (ollama, llama.cpp, transformers). Flag parent process context if non-interactive.

suggestion.title: Self-Referential Model Output Generating New Model Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: worm 'self-replicates.' Requires detection of model inference output triggering creation of new model instances, directories, or downloads without explicit user command.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inference process (python + transformers/ollama) stdout/stderr containing model names or paths with subsequent file writes creating new model directories or downloads. Chain detection: Process A infers → creates model path → Process B spawns inferring that new model → creates another. Loop indicates self-replication.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Network Model File Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Self-replication implies spread across systems. 'Operates entirely on local models' suggests propagation via copying malicious model weights to network shares, UNC paths, or shared storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large binary writes (>500MB) to SMB shares (\\server\share), mapped drives, or cloud-synced directories. Flag when single user copies model files to multiple network destinations in succession, especially if followed by remote host process creation.

suggestion.title: Execution of Model-Generated Shell Commands
suggestion.rationale: Worm must execute system commands to self-replicate and propagate. Article premise requires model output → code interpretation pathway (e.g., prompt injection enabling RCE through model-to-shell translation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python/Node inference processes with immediate child process spawns (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh). Focus on cases where command-line arguments contain strings resembling model output or generated code (unusual randomness, LLM-like phrasing patterns, base64 payloads).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download of Open-Weight Model Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Worm distribution requires staging of malicious model weights. Article specifies 'open-weight models'—expect detection of downloads from HuggingFace, ModelZoo, Ollama registries, or attacker-controlled model mirrors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS downloads of *.bin, *.safetensors, or *.pt files from huggingface.co, github.com, or non-standard domains. Flag if downloads occur outside package manager contexts (pip/conda) or if model size claims don't match file size. Cross-reference against threat intelligence on malicious model checksum blocklists.

suggestion.title: Process-to-Process Model State Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Worm self-replication likely involves copying or serializing trained model state across processes. Detection should flag suspicious inter-process reads of model cache or state files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of model cache directories (/.cache/huggingface/, /.ollama/, PyTorch model dirs) by processes other than the declaring LLM framework. Flag if process A (malicious) reads model state written by Process B (legitimate inference), especially if followed by network exfil or writes to attacker-controlled paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution via binding.gyp Lifecycle Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'binding.gyp Can Do What?' indicates unexpected capabilities; binding.gyp files and package.json gyp lifecycle hooks (preinstall, postinstall) execute arbitrary shell commands during npm install before standard validation occurs, enabling supply-chain payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where node.exe or npm spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash as children during package installation. Flag commands containing references to binding.gyp, node-gyp, or obfuscated script content in preinstall/postinstall attributes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Native Module Build Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp permits native C/C++ module compilation with build-phase script injection; gyp files can download and execute arbitrary binaries disguised as build dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect binding.gyp-triggered processes making external HTTP/HTTPS connections to non-canonical sources, downloading executables, or writing to temp directories before returning to the caller process.

suggestion.title: npm Package install-Phase Privilege Escalation via gyp
suggestion.rationale: Exploring binding.gyp's edge cases likely includes scenarios where gyp build scripts can elevate privileges or escape sandboxes during native module compilation steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install spawning processes with SYSTEM or elevated privileges, or child processes attempting UAC bypass, registry writes to HKLM, or service manipulation during build phases.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Base64-Encoded Command Execution in gyp Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on what binding.gyp 'can do'—likely includes obfuscation techniques; gyp lifecycle scripts often encode payloads to evade endpoint detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell invocations in preinstall/postinstall hooks with base64, hex, or rot13-encoded arguments. Flag commands piping decoded content to interpreters or using eval/exec patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Substitution via binding.gyp Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article title suggests binding.gyp has unexpected capabilities—includes potential for package registry confusion attacks where malicious gyp files override intended dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry queries and file system for binding.gyp files requesting non-standard dependency sources, file:// URIs, or local development packages substituting production dependencies.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Process - Suspicious Child Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited...to Deploy Stealers.' Malicious RAR files trigger extraction spawning stealer payloads. Expected: WinRAR→cmd.exe/powershell.exe/rundll32.exe sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WinRAR.exe or unrar.exe spawning system interpreters or unsigned executables. Legitimate archiving rarely initiates cmd/PowerShell. Baseline internal deployment; alert on process spawn + immediate network activity.

suggestion.title: Stealer - Browser Credential Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Stealers' as deployed payload. Stealer TTPs universally include browser credential harvesting. Detection should monitor process access to Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unsigned/suspicious processes accessing Local/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Edge or Chrome/Default/Login Data. Flag rare accessors; correlate with network exfiltration within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Stealer - Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Stealer payload requires C2 channel for credential exfiltration ('Deploy Stealers'). Detection should identify suspicious processes establishing outbound connections post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor non-standard processes (children of explorer.exe, cmd.exe spawned from archives) initiating HTTPS outbound connections. Flag newly-registered domains, dynamic DNS, non-standard TLDs, or IP ranges geolocated to Russia/CIS.

suggestion.title: RAR Extraction to Temp Directories - Executable Drop
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited...to Deploy Stealers.' Detection should identify WinRAR writing executables to temp locations, signaling malware staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinRAR creating .exe/.dll/.scr/.msi in %temp%, AppData/Local/Temp, or deeply-nested subdirectories. Correlate modification time with extraction event. High-risk: file marked 'Zone.Identifier=3' (internet origin) yet runs unsigned.

suggestion.title: LSASS Access - Credential Dumping Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Stealer payloads commonly harvest LSASS credentials after code execution. Detection should flag unauthorized LSASS memory access from suspicious parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unsigned/low-reputation processes issuing OpenProcess(LSASS, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION|PROCESS_VM_READ). Baseline legitimate EDR/SIEM agents. Alert on sequences: archive extraction → child process → LSASS access → network outbound.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion - Code Integrity Bypass via Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: WinRAR CVE by definition bypasses execution authorization. Detection should identify SmartScreen bypass, code-signing circumvention, or UAC suppression patterns from extracted code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unsigned executables spawned from legitimate application (WinRAR) lacking SmartScreen warning. Monitor Zone.Identifier:3 files running without user prompt. Correlate parent=WinRAR + unsigned child + no signing chain.

suggestion.title: AI Brand Impersonation in Phishing Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes threat actors using AI brands as social engineering lures; keyword 'Credential theft' indicates phishing campaigns impersonating AI vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) to harvest credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with subject lines or body text referencing AI platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) combined with urgency language (verification, account suspension, upgrade required). Flag emails where sender domain mimics AI brand infrastructure or uses lookalike domains with typosquatting patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via AI Brand Clone Portals
suggestion.rationale: Keywords 'Credential theft' + 'AI brands' imply phishing landing pages cloning AI service login pages; article likely discusses malicious redirects or credential-stealing forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous authentication attempts to legitimate AI service domains (api.openai.com, etc.) preceded by clicks from non-corporate email or browser visits to newly-registered domains with AI brand keywords. Flag failed auth attempts followed by successful logins from different IP/geography.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Abuse After AI Brand Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Schema keyword explicitly mentions 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)'; article likely describes how stolen AI service credentials are leveraged for session hijacking or downstream compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful sign-ins to AI platforms from unrecognized ISPs/ASNs immediately following phishing campaigns. Correlate multiple users authenticating to the same AI platform within a short window from the same external IP (AiTM proxy pattern). Monitor for unusual API calls from AI service accounts (automated bulk actions, exfiltration patterns).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised AI Service OAuth/API Tokens
suggestion.rationale: If threat actors compromise AI brand accounts (e.g., OpenAI org admin), they may steal OAuth tokens or API keys to pivot into connected enterprise SaaS (Slack, GitHub, etc. integrations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or reuse of API tokens/OAuth apps within AI service platforms from unusual geolocations or after a phishing event. Monitor for unusual cross-service integrations (e.g., new Slack OAuth grants tied to AI platform accounts) appearing after credential compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Bulk Phishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'—indicates mass-distribution phishing campaign; should alert on >50 emails from same external sender to >10% of headcount within 5 minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spike in external emails to multiple internal recipients sharing suspicious characteristics (same sender, similar subject line templates, lookalike domains). Correlate with sender-domain reputation and prior breach databases.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Linguistic Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names 'AI Phishing'—suggests LLM-generated content; should detect anomalous phrasing, repetitive urgency language, unnatural salutations, placeholder artifacts typical of generative models.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate email corpus for sender domains; flag messages with >3 action-forcing keywords per 100 words (urgent, verify, confirm, click now), grammar inconsistencies, or salutations mismatched to org naming conventions. Escalate to SOC for AI content analysis.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Access
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns universally target credentials; should detect clicks on external URLs hosting forms mimicking legitimate credential providers (Office 365, Okta, Slack, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email clicks (from flagged phishing emails) with HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains. Identify typosquatting variants and homograph attacks. Flag for credential exposure investigation and user notification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Attachment Execution Post-Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Phishing articles typically involve weaponized attachments; should flag file execution from external email downloads within seconds of receipt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery timestamp (T0) with process creation for PowerShell, cmd.exe, VBS, or script engines from user Downloads/Temp within 120 seconds. Prioritize for forensic acquisition and code analysis.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement from Phished Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Successful phishing precedes lateral movement; should detect anomalous account activity (impossible travel, new device, privilege escalation) from accounts that engaged with flagged phishing emails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If user clicked/opened attachment in flagged phishing email at T0, alert on sign-in anomalies within 2–4 hours: new geolocation, impossible travel, non-standard device, unusual time-of-day. Trigger conditional access block and MFA re-auth.

suggestion.title: Sender Domain Reputation & Lookalike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phishing scale demands typosquatting and domain similarity attacks; should detect emails from lookalike or newly-registered domains impersonating trusted senders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare sender domain against org allowlist and DMARC-authenticated domains. Flag emails from recently-registered domains (<30 days), homograph variants (e.g., rn vs m, 0 vs O), and domains with no SPF/DKIM. Quarantine for review.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass via CVE-2026-50751 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploited CVE-2026-50751 to 'bypass authentication on targeted Mobile Access / SSL VPNs, Remote Access VPNs' with 'active exploitation' from May 7 onwards. Direct initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IKEv1 key exchange initiation followed by successful session establishment without valid authentication credentials or machine certificate, especially from unexpected geographies or IPs. Correlate with subsequent lateral movement or data-access events within 4 hours.

suggestion.title: VPN Session Establishment Without Machine Certificate Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects systems 'that do not require a machine certificate for connections'. Mitigation guidance states 'set Machine Certificate Authentication as mandatory', indicating detection opportunity for sessions bypassing this requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Remote Access or Mobile Access VPN sessions that authenticate without presenting or validating a machine certificate, particularly if the session originates from non-standard geolocations or IP reputation is poor.

suggestion.title: Detection and Alerting on IKEv1 Key Exchange in VPN Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly emphasizes 'deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' as prerequisite for exploitation. Configuration audit is foundational to surfacing at-risk deployments before breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit and inventory all Remote Access VPN, Mobile Access, and Spark firewall deployments accepting IKEv1 negotiation. Alert on any new IKEv1-enabled tunnels post-patch release and prioritize for immediate IKEv2 migration or legacy client blocking.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Breach Ransomware Deployment (Qilin)
suggestion.rationale: Article directly links initial breach to ransomware: 'confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate'. VPN compromise enables lateral movement and data encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24–72 hours of anomalous VPN authentication or session events, monitor for file encryption patterns, ransom note creation, mass file access from VPN-connected endpoints to internal shares, and command-and-control domains associated with Qilin.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Vulnerability on Site-to-Site VPN (CVE-2026-50752)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies second vulnerability: 'CVE-2026-50752...affects certificate validation in deprecated IKEv1 key exchange that can be exploited in man-in-the-middle attacks on site-to-site VPN connections'.
log_sources: network packet captures of key exchange
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor site-to-site VPN tunnels using IKEv1 for certificate validation failures or peer-identity mismatches. Alert on IPSec Phase-2 negotiations where presented certificates deviate from expected gateway fingerprints or trusted CA chains.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and threat profile states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'. Detecting publicly accessible LiteLLM instances is the first step to exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for CVE-2026-42271 vulnerable LiteLLM instances exposed on internet-facing ports (typically 8000, 4000, or custom API ports). Correlate vulnerability scanner results with network exposure data; flag instances accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor for version strings matching vulnerable LiteLLM releases in HTTP response headers and API documentation endpoints.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'command injection vulnerability that could allow any authenticated user...to run arbitrary commands on the host'. This is the exploitation phase and must be detectable via API request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to LiteLLM API endpoints (proxy logs, WAF logs) for shell metacharacters and command injection payloads in request bodies (backticks, $(), |, &, ;, >, <, pipe chains). Correlate with successful responses followed immediately by unexpected process spawning on the backend host. Flag requests from low-privilege API keys triggering host-level commands.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Key Used for Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, to run arbitrary commands'. Abnormal command execution by low-privilege credential is a privilege-escalation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of command types and privileges associated with each LiteLLM API key tier. Alert when low-privilege keys issue commands outside their typical scope (e.g., system administration, package installation, credential access). Correlate API key identity with subsequent process creation events on the host using contextual linking (request ID, session ID, or timing proximity).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Host Activity via LiteLLM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'run arbitrary commands on the host'—successful exploitation will spawn unexpected processes. Host-level detection post-compromise is critical given this is KEV (active exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from LiteLLM service parent processes (litellm, python litellm runtime, node litellm if applicable). Flag child processes with high entropy command lines, network connectivity attempts, credential scraping (grep /etc/passwd, cat .ssh), or reverse shells. Correlate temporal proximity to LiteLLM API requests with unusual payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article stresses: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and includes federal due-date 2026-06-22. Compliance-driven detection for unpatched instances is mandatory for regulated environments and aligns with CISA KEV intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for LiteLLM versions < patched build. Flag instances where patch is overdue relative to 2026-06-22 federal deadline. Prioritize systems exposed to internet or hosting sensitive data. Automate remediation workflow or escalate to change management if patching is delayed beyond acceptable grace period.

suggestion.title: Check Point IKEv1 Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'improper authentication vulnerability in IKEv1 key exchange' as the attack surface. Must detect anomalous IKEv1 protocol exchanges or malformed key material consistent with CVE-2026-50751 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IKEv1 MAIN or AGGRESSIVE mode exchanges on Check Point gateways that deviate from RFC 2409 protocol flow (missing authentication payloads, truncated exchanges, reuse of nonces). Flag when IKE SA establishment completes without successful IPsec phase-2 credentials.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass user authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection without a valid user password.' Must detect successful tunnel establishment without credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN authentication logs and tunnel state transitions. Alert when a session reaches authenticated/connected state without a corresponding successful authentication event in auth logs, or when connection time-to-auth is below normal baseline.

suggestion.title: Exposed Check Point Security Gateway Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation of exposed instances. Article states CVE is 'currently being exploited in the wild'—attackers must first locate vulnerable gateways. Asset discovery is the prerequisite phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vuln scanner data for Check Point Security Gateway instances (by banner or product ID) reachable on UDP 500 or VPN management ports. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify systems older than CVE-2026-50751 release date (2026-06-08). Flag any gaps between discovery date and remediation date vs. federal due date 2026-06-11.

suggestion.title: Failed VPN Authentication Spike from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article references attacker bypassing authentication 'without a valid user password.' On systems where exploit fails or is rejected, this manifests as failed auth spikes preceding or concurrent with exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-source-IP baseline for failed VPN authentication attempts. Alert on sudden 5x+ spike or >10 failures in 5 minutes, especially from external/unknown IPs. Correlate with successful connections from same source immediately after failure burst to identify exploitation success.

suggestion.title: URI normalization bypass to protected endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'By crafting requests that appear to target an authentication-exempt endpoint in their raw form but resolve to protected internal routes after normalization, attackers can bypass authentication.' This is the core bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` that contain URI obfuscation techniques (double-encoded slashes, path traversal sequences, case variations) followed by access to normally protected endpoints without prior authentication events. Flag requests that normalize differently in the auth component vs. routing layer.

suggestion.title: Command injection via unauthenticated package-update endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the attackers can target a package-update endpoint with CVE-2026-34910, passing unvalidated user input into a shell command to execute arbitrary commands on the system.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/PUT requests to `ucs/update/latest_package` containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks, command substitution) or command keywords. Correlate with unexpected child processes spawned under the ucs-update service.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via passwordless sudo from service account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'The injected commands execute under a highly privileged service account with passwordless sudo access to several system binaries, making escalation to root trivial.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo command execution from the UniFi service account outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on any sudo invocation targeting sensitive binaries (bash, sh, cat, chmod) or system utilities that could enable persistence or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Suspicious child process spawning from ucs-update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'monitor requests to... suspicious child processes under 'ucs-update.'` Baseline normal children and flag anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected child processes spawned by the ucs-update service. Alert on anomalies, especially network tools (curl, wget, nc, bash), unknown binaries, or processes that themselves spawn additional children.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to protected endpoints with no auth trail
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'The chain reaches root with no credentials and no user interaction, so there is no failed-login trail to look for.' Absence of auth events prior to protected endpoint access is itself anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate HTTP 200/success responses on protected API endpoints against authentication logs. Flag successful requests to protected endpoints that have no preceding authentication event in the session or from the source IP within the previous 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Multiple malformed auth-bypass requests within short window
suggestion.rationale: While Bishop Fox released a safe detection script, actual exploitation attempts will involve repeated requests with URI normalization tricks. Article notes researchers 'did not share the full details or a working proof of concept' but defenders can detect the pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of requests from the same source to `/api/auth/validate-sso/` variations or `ucs/update/latest_package` within 60 seconds using unusual URI patterns (encoded characters, multiple slashes, path traversal attempts). Five or more such requests in 60 seconds warrants escalation.

suggestion.title: PHP stream-wrapper bypass via parse_url() integer-length check evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article core detail: 'parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME)... is_string($scheme) && strlen($scheme) > 1' is bypassed when input is 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' (3+ slashes). Detection should target the specific bypass pattern. Article: 'When the input has the form phar:///path/file.phar/inner with three or more slashes after the scheme'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request parameters containing stream-wrapper URIs with 3+ consecutive forward slashes immediately after the scheme name (phar:///, php:///, data:///, expect:///). Correlate requests to PHP-based web applications with subsequent web-process shell spawning or unexpected file reads.

suggestion.title: PHPSpreadsheet load() called with untrusted file-path parameter containing wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires PHPSpreadsheet's file-loading method to receive attacker-controlled input. Should detect when PHPSpreadsheet processes files via wrapper schemes instead of direct filesystem paths. Article: 'CVE-2026-34084 was patched by the helper File::prohibitWrappers'—this implies load() accepts file paths and lacks input validation pre-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If PHPSpreadsheet is instrumented or logged: flag any File::load() or Spreadsheet->load() call with argument containing phar://, php://, data://, expect://, or other stream-wrapper schemes. Correlate with HTTP parameters to identify external input flow into load().

suggestion.title: Phar archive extraction or code execution within PHP process
suggestion.rationale: Once phar:// bypass succeeds, attacker loads a malicious phar archive. Detection should capture phar mounting, extraction, or execution within PHP/web-server context. Article: 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' syntax suggests archive interior access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process opening/reading .phar files followed immediately by execution of child processes or network connections. Or detect file creation within /tmp/ or cache directories with non-standard ownership immediately after phar:// access.

suggestion.title: Chained: HTTP request with wrapper + web-process shell spawning (exploit evidence)
suggestion.rationale: Full kill-chain: HTTP request with phar:/// → PHP parse_url bypass → RCE → child shell execution. Requires correlation of web logs + process logs. Article implies this is the attack flow but pipeline generated no correlation rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Web datamodel requests containing phar:/// or related wrappers with Endpoint.Processes showing shell (bash/sh/powershell) or wget/curl spawned by php/apache/nginx within 2 seconds of request. High-confidence RCE signal if correlation is strict.

suggestion.title: Expect:// or data:// wrapper usage attempt (alternative bypass vectors)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists expect:// and data:// in the same class of wrappers filtered by the patched check. If phar:/// bypass is successful, attacker may also test other wrappers. Should hunt all variants. Article: 'reject stream wrappers such as phar://, php://, data:// or expect://'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for expect://, data://, or php:// scheme usage in HTTP request parameters to PHP endpoints. Treat as lower-confidence variant of phar:/// but still suspicious in production. Correlate with application errors or exceptions.

suggestion.title: osascript invoked with nested mismatched tell blocks + do shell script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AppleScript breakout pattern' where attacker injects code into osascript causing mismatched tell-block structure that triggers shell escape. Article states vulnerability allows 'Code Injection via Unescaped URL' → osascript execution. Example SPL in article hunts for `tell application` appearing 2+ times in single command, which is the canonical injection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Malicious actor crafts URL containing AppleScript payload with nested tell blocks. Plugin renders URL unescaped into osascript command. Detection: osascript process spawned with ProcessCommandLine containing multiple `tell application` directives (≥2 opens) plus `do shell script`, indicating escape from script context into shell.

suggestion.title: Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari plugin parameter injection — seturl.js activity
suggestion.rationale: Article names `seturl.js` as the vulnerable file in recommended hunts section. No pipeline extraction of this filename IOC. seturl.js likely the URL handler responsible for interpolating unescaped input into AppleScript context. Should hunt for seturl.js process spawn or file modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect seturl.js spawning osascript with suspicious arguments, or file creation/modification of seturl.js outside expected plugin directories. Attacker may inject polyglot URL payloads through browser plugin manager or crafted links.

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin loaded with remote code execution intent — process lineage
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in 'chrome_tabs plugin (and equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari variants)' within Anyquery extension. Root cause is plugin URL handler not escaping input. Should correlate plugin load events with subsequent osascript execution under same user session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process chain: browser (Chrome/Brave/Edge/Safari) → Anyquery plugin context → osascript with injection payload. May appear as browser parent spawning intermediate process (plugin engine) then osascript. User interaction required (clicking link) but attack is one-click.

suggestion.title: JXA script injection — OSAKit/JavaScript bridge with shell escape
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'AppleScript/JXA Code Injection'. CVE affects both AppleScript AND JavaScript for Automation (JXA). JXA variant would use `Application('System Events').execute('shell command')` or ObjC bridge to escape sandbox. Pipeline missed the JXA dimension entirely despite it being in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: JXA injection payloads use `new ($.NSTask)()` or Application('System Events') to spawn shell. Detect osascript with language=JXA (-l JavaScript) combined with shell-escape patterns ($.NSTask, new ObjC proxies, system process invocation).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47252 asset inventory — Anyquery 0.4.4 installed
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected version 0.4.4 (commit 0abd460) of julien040/anyquery repository. Pipeline output shows zero IOCs including zero version/product identifiers. Asset exposure hunt should enumerate any macOS endpoints with Anyquery 0.4.4 or earlier installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt: find macOS endpoints with Anyquery plugin installed (check ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Extensions or equivalent Brave/Edge/Safari paths). Cross-reference version against 0.4.4 threshold. Flag for urgent patching or plugin disablement.

suggestion.title: Gogs Account Creation on Internet-Facing Instance with Default Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account' and 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false).' External account registration on unpatched Gogs is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new user registrations on internet-exposed Gogs instances (ports 3000, 3001 typical) when configuration DISABLE_REGISTRATION is false. Alert on rapid sequential registrations or registration from non-organizational ASNs.

suggestion.title: Repository Creation with Rebase Merge Enabled by Low-Privilege User
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and 'the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction.' Pre-enabled rebase merge on new repos by non-owners is prerequisite for RCE chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repository creation events where rebase-before-merge is enabled in settings by non-admin users, especially within minutes of account creation. Correlate with subsequent commit/merge activities.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Patterns in Gogs Merge Process Execution
