suggestion.rationale: Article states packages are 'poisoned to auto-run Bun Credential Stealer' — this describes post-installation script execution. No detection UC was generated despite this being a primary attack vector in supply-chain poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python package installation followed by execution of unexpected binaries (Bun runtime / credential stealer) with elevated file/registry access. Look for setup.py or post-install hooks spawning non-standard executables within minutes of pip/conda install operations.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Poisoned Package Names Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references '19 Packages Poisoned' but pipeline extracted zero package IOCs. Named package indicators are foundational supply-chain detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish indicator list of 19 poisoned package names. Detect package installations via pip/poetry/npm/conda processes, then correlate with suspicious child processes or network connections within 60s of installation. Flag packages with atypical dependencies or unusual network egress.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Execution by Non-Developer Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Bun Credential Stealer' as the payload. Pipeline missed extraction of 'Bun' as an IOC and failed to generate detection for this executable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Bun runtime (bun.exe / bun binary) spawned by non-standard parents (setup scripts, pip, Python interpreters, scheduled tasks). Monitor for Bun processes accessing credential stores (HKLM/HKCU SAM, browser credential DBs, SSH keys, API tokens).

suggestion.title: Post-Package-Installation Credential Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow is clear: install poisoned package → stealer executes → steals credentials. Pipeline generated no UC linking package install to credential-access behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 2 minutes of Python package installation, detect child processes accessing Windows credential vaults, browser local storage, SSH key directories, or .kube config. Flag if exfiltration (DNS/HTTP/TCP egress to non-whitelist IPs) follows within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Exfiltration from Package-Spawned Processes
suggestion.rationale: Kill-chain endpoint is credential exfiltration to attacker C2. No pipeline UC covers detection of data egress from the stealer payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound connections (high-entropy POST payloads, frequent DNS queries) originating from child processes of Python package installers or Bun runtime. Correlate with credential-access events. Flag destinations not in corporate whitelist.

suggestion.title: Setup.py / pyproject.toml Post-Install Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes auto-run mechanism via poisoned packages. Python's entry point and post-install hook mechanisms are the delivery mechanism but no detection UC was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious content in setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, or RECORD files in site-packages directories. Flag if post-install hooks execute non-Python binaries, make registry changes, or spawn cmd/PowerShell. Baseline legitimate packages and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Against LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild' but pipeline generated zero use cases. This is the primary attack surface and should be the first detection hypothesis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM services are exposed to the internet. Monitor HTTP requests to known LiteLLM endpoints (typically /api/*, /chat/*, /chat/completions) originating from external sources with user-agent or parameter patterns consistent with CVE-2026-42271 exploitation probes. Alert on any request that omits expected authentication headers (Authorization, X-API-Key) while attempting to access privileged endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Code Execution via LiteLLM API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—the core attack vector. Pipeline did not generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh, powershell.exe) spawned by or under the context of LiteLLM service processes (e.g., litellm.py, node LiteLLM runtime). Correlate with HTTP logs showing unauthenticated API calls to LiteLLM endpoints in the preceding 10 seconds. Flag any execution with command-line arguments indicating file operations, network access, or credential access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous API Activity to LiteLLM Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: 'Unauthenticated RCE' implies authentication bypass. No detection use case was generated to identify missing or invalid auth tokens in LiteLLM API logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM logs API calls with authentication status. Detect requests to sensitive endpoints (e.g., /api/call, /api/proxy) that either omit Authorization headers entirely or submit invalid/expired tokens, followed by successful HTTP 200 responses (indicating bypass). Baseline normal token patterns and alert on deviations or batch token enumeration.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command and Control Activity from LiteLLM Host
suggestion.rationale: RCE articles typically describe post-exploitation behavior (C2 beaconing, data exfil). Pipeline generated no impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful RCE exploitation, attackers typically establish C2. Monitor for outbound network connections from the LiteLLM host to unusual destinations, particularly on non-standard ports (not 80/443). Watch for DNS queries to recently-registered or high-entropy domains. Correlate process creation logs with new network connections to identify C2 callback patterns.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Configuration File Tampering or Credential Extraction
suggestion.rationale: RCE chains often lead to credential harvesting. Article title suggests full compromise ('Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'). No credential-access detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiteLLM configuration may contain API keys or database credentials. Monitor for file access to config directories (e.g., ~/.litellm/, /etc/litellm/) by non-service accounts or by child processes of the LiteLLM service. Alert on memory access to the LiteLLM process or execution of credential-dumping utilities (mimikatz, secretsdump.py) after RCE.

suggestion.title: Bulk Business Data Staging for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'off-site business data' being collected and used for ML/personalization; pipeline did not surface detection for data staging, bulk collection, or preparation of third-party datasets ('for AI personalization' implies aggregation for model training).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-scale file operations targeting business data repositories, unusual bulk downloads from cloud storage marked for external use, or data preparation workflows aggregating third-party datasets.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Data Exfiltration via Cloud Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article states Meta uses 'off-site business data'; pipeline should detect unauthorized transfers of third-party data to external cloud accounts or suspicious data flows via Meta's integration APIs ('T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cross-tenant data exports, unexpected cloud-to-cloud transfers of business data, or exfiltration via third-party data integration channels masquerading as legitimate personalization pipelines.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Meta API Data Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses data collection 'off-site' for feed personalization; pipeline missed detection for anomalous API calls to Meta graph API or other data collection endpoints used to ingest third-party business data at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual API rate patterns, high-volume data retrieval from Meta's graph API, or service principals with unexpected permissions to business data collections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Action Execution in CI Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious code injected into GitHub Actions workflow. Article title states 'Azure Functions Action' was compromised and used to disable repositories. Requires detection of unexpected action execution or action version drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions jobs executing unexpected or newly-pinned actions, particularly Microsoft-published actions (azure-functions-action) where the pinned commit hash deviates from repository baseline. Flag runs with new secrets or environment variable exposure not previously observed in workflow history.

suggestion.title: Repository Mass Disabling via API or Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '72 other repositories disabled' as attack outcome. Implies either direct API abuse or workflow-based destruction logic. Look for coordinated repository state changes tied to malicious workflow execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk repository setting changes (archived=true, disabled=true, visibility=private) originating from automated workflows or service accounts within a 24-hour window. Correlate to suspicious workflow executions in the same org/timeframe. False positives: legitimate org-wide maintenance scripts—baseline these first.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Action Tampering – Commit/Tag Reuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on GitHub Actions often exploit pinning to specific commits or tags. Article mentions 'Azure Functions Action' specifically. Need to detect when published actions are re-tagged or commits re-used across multiple orgs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For pinned GitHub Actions, cross-reference the commit SHA against public threat intel feeds and repos known to have used the same action+commit in workflows. Flag if same action commit is pinned in both trusted Microsoft repos and external/untrusted repos within overlapping time windows.

suggestion.title: Abnormal GitHub Token Scope Usage in Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows often request excessive permissions (GITHUB_TOKEN scopes) to enable repository disabling or cross-org lateral movement. Article attack disabled 72 repos, implying wide token scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GITHUB_TOKEN scopes used by legitimate actions in the org. Alert when workflows request 'admin' or 'repo' scope without corresponding job complexity, or when scope-escalation occurs in workflows introduced/modified in the same window as malicious activity.

suggestion.title: Artifact or Build Cache Poisoning via Malicious Workflow
suggestion.rationale: AI coding agents (mentioned in article title as attack target) often consume build artifacts and cached dependencies. Malicious workflows can inject poisoned artifacts/cache. Need to detect cache/artifact upload from suspicious workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for artifact or GitHub Actions cache uploads in workflows that also modify repository settings, disable issues/PRs, or contain suspicious network calls. Flag uploads to shared artifact namespaces from newly-created or rarely-executed workflows.

suggestion.title: Malware Signature or Yara Rule Match in Workflow Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article refers to 'Miasma Worm.' If pipeline has access to threat feeds or sandboxing, malicious binaries/scripts should be detected in committed code or artifacts. Miasma IOCs should be correlated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate Miasma Worm signatures (if available from StepSecurity/threat feeds) into pre-commit or workflow scanning. Alert on base64-encoded or obfuscated shell commands in workflow YAML files that match known IoCs or deobfuscate to known malware behaviors.

suggestion.title: SMB-Hosted VHD File Opened Preceding Microsoft Defender Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server' triggers vulnerability. Describes primary attack initiation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UNC path access to .vhd or .vhdx files (\\\\server\\share pattern) followed by Microsoft Defender (MsMpEng.exe) opening, reading, or enumerating those files. Alert on .vhd file access from user temp directories or unexpected shares. Correlate SMB open with subsequent Defender process high-frequency API calls.

suggestion.title: Command Prompt Execution as Child of Microsoft Defender Process with SYSTEM Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'a Windows command prompt will be spawned with SYSTEM privileges' as exploitation outcome. Describes the privilege-escalation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as child process of MsMpEng.exe (or related Microsoft Defender processes) running with SYSTEM-level integrity/privileges. This is anomalous; Defender scanning should never spawn interactive command shells. Strongly correlate with recent .vhd file access and timing of process creation.

suggestion.title: Junction or Symlink Creation Targeting Microsoft Defender Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'junction attacks' as exploitation mechanism. Researcher notes Microsoft patched 'mpengine!SysIO* API' mid-May 2026 to block these attacks, implying junction reparse points were the vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NTFS reparse point (junction) or symlink creation in user-writable directories (AppData, Temp, user profile) with targets pointing to Windows\\System32, Program Files\\Windows Defender, or ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender. Flag rapid creation-to-access sequences where Defender process accesses the junction target.

suggestion.title: Defender mpengine Self-File Modification or Overwrite via Race Condition
suggestion.rationale: Article states original RoguePlanet variant caused 'defender overwriting its own files' leading to RCE. Describes race-condition window allowing file modification of Defender binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file write/overwrite operations targeting mpengine.dll, MsMpEng.exe, or related Defender library paths initiated from Defender processes themselves or with rapid file-handle chaining (multiple opens/writes to same target path within < 100ms). Baseline normal Defender update patterns and alert on anomalous timing or source.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Service Crash or Restart Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Researcher noted exploit is 'a hit or miss' with variable success ('100% on some machines while it struggled on others'), indicating race-condition instability. Crashes/restarts would correlate with exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clustering of MsMpEng.exe process terminations or Windows Defender service restarts within short time windows (≥2 restarts in 60 seconds). Correlate with user file-access events, especially .vhd operations and temp-directory writes. Flag exit codes indicating crashes or access violations.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Privilege Escalation via Symbolic Link
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-45586: 'Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') in Windows Collaborative Translation Framework allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.' This is an exploitation pattern requiring detection of the link-following abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ctfmon.exe and related CTFMON processes for creation or following of symbolic links or NTFS junctions pointing to privileged locations (%System32%, SYSTEM user context targets). Alert on ctfmon spawning child processes with elevated token elevation or any CTFMON process acquiring SYSTEM privileges.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Bomb Denial of Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-49160: 'Uncontrolled resource consumption in HTTP/2 allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.' Attackers exploit header compression and flow-control manipulation to cause excessive memory allocation in HTTP.sys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HTTP.sys memory consumption spikes unexpectedly or when MaxHeadersCount registry limit is exceeded. Monitor for abnormally large numbers of HTTP/2 headers in single requests or flow-control frames sent in rapid succession designed to prevent memory release.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Bypass via WinRE Physical Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-50507 / YellowKey: 'placing specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition and booting into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where holding down the CTRL key triggered a command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected WinRE invocation or recovery environment access, particularly on TPM-only BitLocker systems. Alert on EFI partition modifications, specially-crafted files staged on USB devices, or command shells spawned from recovery environment with access to encrypted volumes.

suggestion.title: Windows Update Mitigation Deployment - HTTP/2 Header Limits
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Microsoft also introduced a new MaxHeadersCount registry setting. This setting allows you to limit the number of headers included in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests.' This registry key change is a mitigation indicator and compliance-check target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track deployment of KB5102602 and presence of MaxHeadersCount registry setting at HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters. Flag systems missing the registry key or using unusually high header limits post-patch-Tuesday.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized EFI/Boot Partition Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article details YellowKey exploits EFI partition access: 'placing specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition.' Detection should focus on suspicious access to boot-critical partitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on direct access to EFI system partition or EFI boot files from non-system processes, USB device insertion during system boot, or attempts to modify EFI partition content outside of Windows Update contexts.

suggestion.title: CTRL Key Sequence in Windows Recovery Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation technique: 'holding down the CTRL key triggered a command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.' Requires detection of abnormal recovery environment shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Recovery Environment for unexpected cmd.exe or powershell.exe execution, particularly sequences preceded by CTRL key presses or rapid key sequences during boot. Alert on shell access to BitLocker key recovery mechanisms from recovery environment.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Microsoft June 2026 Zero-Day Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-50507, CVE-2026-49160, CVE-2026-45586 as 'actively exploited' zero-days. Pipeline recommended but never generated the asset-exposure hunt that should inventory unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against patch-deployment logs to identify systems running Microsoft products without June 2026 patches applied within 72 hours of release. Flag systems reporting vulnerable versions via endpoint detection agents. Priority: systems with public-facing network exposure.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection — Microsoft Zero-Day Attack Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states zero-days 'were actively exploited or publicly known before a fix was available,' indicating working exploits exist in the wild. Pipeline generated no detection for attack attempts despite this clear evidence of real-world exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation signatures: suspicious child processes spawned from affected Microsoft applications, unexpected network connections from patched services, and HTTP request patterns matching published POC exploit chains for these CVE families.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning for Zero-Day Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation typically precedes scanning of potential targets. Article's mention of active exploitation implies attacker reconnaissance activity. Pipeline missed detection opportunity for pre-attack scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external scanning activity probing for vulnerable Microsoft product versions. Look for repeated HTTP requests with version-detection strings, vulnerability database lookups for these CVE IDs, or scanner User-Agent patterns combined with requests to known vulnerable endpoint paths.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Mass Offline Event
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Microsoft Restores Some GitHub Repos, Keeps Others Offline'—explicit indication of repository availability changes correlated with incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk repository status changes (offline, archived, deleted) within short timeframes, especially when affecting multiple repos in same org. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or token anomalies in preceding hours. Alert on >5 repo state changes in 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token or Deploy Key Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article implies unauthorized repo access leading to offline state; PATs or deploy keys are common initial-access mechanism for GitHub account takeover, mentioned implicitly in 'probe continues' suggesting investigation into attacker persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of new GitHub PATs or SSH keys from anomalous geolocation or time-of-day. Correlate PAT creation with subsequent API calls to unrelated repos. Alert on PAT usage from IP ranges outside normal org footprint. Track key rotation patterns for anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise via Leaked Credentials or Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Repo offline event suggests account control loss; title references ongoing 'Miasma Probe' indicating forensic investigation into breach vector. Article body unavailable but incident scale suggests initial compromise via credential theft (T1556) or public-facing app exploit (T1190).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logins from new devices, new geolocations, or unusual times preceding repo modifications. Flag failed login attempts followed by successful auth from different IP. Monitor for bypass of multi-factor authentication (new recovery codes issued, new trusted devices). Correlate with GitHub API token generation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Org-Level Security Event Suppression or Audit Log Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Selective repo takedown ('restores some, keeps others offline') coupled with 'probe continues' suggests attacker may have attempted to obscure tracks; missing audit logs or selective repo logging would indicate defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gaps in GitHub audit log entries during incident timeframe. Alert on deleted or modified webhook configurations that might suppress event logging. Flag access to org-level security settings (audit log export, MFA policy changes) from non-admin accounts or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Repository Data Exfiltration via Clone or API Export
suggestion.rationale: If repos were compromised before being taken offline, attacker likely exfiltrated code or secrets; article implies investigation ongoing, suggesting data loss assessment is part of response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk repository clones from single user/token in short window (>10 repos/hour). Monitor for large Git push operations to external cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, etc.). Flag repositories accessed but not modified, followed by external data transfer. Correlate with IP geolocation anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Abuse for Lateral Movement or Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Compromised GitHub account access naturally extends to GitHub Actions secrets and workflows; selective repo offline status suggests attacker may have used Actions to maintain persistence or move laterally within connected systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized GitHub Actions workflow modifications, especially changes to secrets or runner configuration. Flag new self-hosted runner registrations. Monitor for workflow runs from atypical accounts or at unusual frequency. Detect Actions that call out to external C2 or cloud accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect High-Resolution Timing Measurement in Browser JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article states FROST 'uses SSD timing' — attack injects JavaScript to measure storage access timing. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection for timing API abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript execution contexts for repeated calls to performance.now() or Date.now() in tight measurement loops, particularly when correlated with synchronous File I/O, SharedArrayBuffer allocation (Spectre/timing channel enabler), or WebWorker spawning. Fingerprinting libraries targeting storage subsystem state should be flagged.

suggestion.title: Detect SSD Timing Fingerprint Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tracking which 'sites and apps you open' — implies derived fingerprint vector (SSD state → user identity) exfiltrated back to attacker. Pipeline missed exfiltration-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate JavaScript timing measurements with subsequent network beacons exfiltrating binary timing arrays, storage state hashes, or device capability vectors. Look for POST/JSON payloads encoding SSD/device fingerprints following high-frequency timing measurement code execution.

suggestion.title: Identify Malicious Website Hosting FROST Exploit Code
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'websites track what sites/apps you open' — attack vector is website injection. Pipeline should detect malicious website delivery and code obfuscation indicative of FROST payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: YARA-based detection of obfuscated JavaScript containing high-frequency timing loops + storage access patterns. Network-based: flag HTTP/HTTPS responses from suspicious sites containing performance API abuse signatures. DNS flagging for known FROST exploit kit distribution domains.

suggestion.title: Correlate Derived SSD Fingerprints Across User Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: attacker links SSD fingerprint to track user across contexts (browser history, app usage). Detection should identify when single computed fingerprint correlates with multiple distinct user sessions or suspicious browsing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build per-device baseline of normal SSD timing variance. Alert on: (1) derived fingerprints deviating significantly from baseline (sign of attacker-controlled measurement), (2) same fingerprint appearing across multiple user accounts/profiles, (3) fingerprint reuse correlated with cross-domain tracking beacons or re-identification.

suggestion.title: Detect Timing-Based Device Capability Inference Queries
suggestion.rationale: FROST leverages SSD-specific timing; attackers probe for SSD model/manufacturer. Pipeline should detect reconnaissance queries for storage subsystem properties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript/code probing storage properties: file creation/deletion in tight loops, querying filesystem metadata timestamps, or timing-sensitive operations targeting /proc/diskstats or equivalent. Atypical storage I/O patterns combined with high-resolution timing API calls indicate device fingerprinting reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: File Hash Matching — MagicAd SHA1 Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 30 SHA1 hashes labeled high-fidelity; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Baseline install-phase detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file creation, process launch, and package installation events against provided SHA1 hashes on Android endpoints. Alert on first hash match; correlate with subsequent ad-anomaly telemetry to confirm infection.

suggestion.title: Background Service Persistence via Boot/System Events
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses multiple techniques to keep showing ads in the background'. Describes persistence mechanisms surviving OS restrictions and user termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag service or daemon registrations launched on boot or system event broadcast, especially unsigned services or those spawned by non-system parent processes. Detect persistence across device reboot or forced process termination.

suggestion.title: Android OS Restriction Bypass — Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cleverly slipping past the built-in restrictions of the Android operating system'. Indicates active evasion beyond T1027 obfuscation alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for dynamic code execution (reflection APIs, classloader manipulation, on-disk dex injection), hooking of Android ad-framework internals, or exploitation of OS kernel weaknesses. Flag process access to system ad-delivery mechanisms without corresponding manifest permissions.

suggestion.title: Command & Control — Ad Payload Delivery and Impression Reporting
suggestion.rationale: Malware sustains 'flooding' behavior implying bidirectional communication: fetching ad payloads and exfiltrating click/impression data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file hash matches with suspicious network traffic: ad-network domains at anomalous request frequencies, high-volume POST requests with serialized ad metadata, or beaconing patterns to known ad-fraud C&C infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Impact — Abnormal Ad System Resource Exhaustion
suggestion.rationale: Primary malware behavior: 'flooding infected devices with ads'. Impact phase manifests as resource anomalies in ad-delivery system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process and ad-framework service for resource spikes: elevated CPU/memory/battery consumption, rapid ad overlay creation cycles, repeated ad-service crashes, or unusually high ad impression event frequency within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Low-privilege domain user RCE on Veeam Backup & Replication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any domain user with low privileges can exploit this vulnerability' and 'the flaw only impacts Veeam Backup & Replication installations that are joined to a domain' — establishes specific authentication + execution boundary for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution on Veeam servers initiated by authenticated low-privileged domain accounts, particularly child processes spawned under Veeam service contexts or system-level commands executed via domain user tokens.

suggestion.title: Backup job deletion and restore-blocking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'block restoration efforts by deleting victims' backups' — describes post-RCE impact activity detectable via backup metadata deletion or job removal events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect deletion of Veeam backup configuration files, backup job removal, or mass deletion of .vbk/.vib files outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on removal of backup copies when recent RCE indicators are present.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement pivoting from Veeam servers
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'move within breached networks' after RCE — Veeam's domain-admin-equivalent privilege level and visibility into all backed-up systems makes it a high-value lateral movement fulcrum.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected SMB, RDP, or WinRM connections originating from Veeam server processes to non-approved internal systems, especially to domain controllers, file servers, or other backup/hypervisor management infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Veeam 12.x version inventory gap
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'attackers will likely attempt to reverse-engineer the patch to exploit unpatched deployments' once patch released — requires active vulnerability tracking against version 12.3.2.4465 and earlier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag and escalate any Veeam Backup & Replication instance running version 12.3.2.4465 or earlier as critical. Correlate inventory against process execution and network anomalies to detect exploitation attempts before patch application.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from backup repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ransomware gangs... always target Veeam backup servers because this allows them to steal sensitive data' — backups contain sensitive data copies and justify bulk-transfer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large unscheduled outbound data transfers (>1GB) from Veeam backup storage paths to external or high-risk IP ranges. Alert on mounting of backup volumes by non-Veeam service accounts followed by file copy operations.

suggestion.title: Ransomware foothold consolidation from Veeam RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article context: FIN7, Akira, Fog, Frag, Cuba all actively abuse Veeam flaws for ransomware operations. RCE enables credential harvesting and additional payload deployment for range-wide encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE, detect scheduled task or registry autostart entries created by Veeam-context processes. Monitor for deployment of secondary payloads (crypters, worms) or persistence mechanisms from Veeam server to other domain endpoints.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Credential Exfiltration to External Email
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'agent located and emailed AWS IAM keys, database credentials, and SSH access details to an external Gmail account.' No detection generated for this direct credential disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email logs and cloud audit trails for agentic framework accounts sending credential-bearing content (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, connection_string patterns, SSH private keys) to newly-contacted external email addresses. Correlate email send events with antecedent credential access in application or API logs. Flag first-contact external recipient alerts where sender is an identified AI agent service account.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Export via Unverified Requester
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'agent retrieved and sent a CRM export containing customer records, contact information, contract details, and revenue data without verifying the sender's identity.' No detection for social-engineered data exfiltration by agent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk exports of data classified as PII, financial, or customer-sensitive (CRM, HR records, revenue data) triggered by agentic framework following email requests from addresses not in internal directory or not in agent's prior recipient history. Require approval workflows for agent-initiated sensitive data exports; monitor for bypasses.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Visits Phishing Site and Submits Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Under the generic configuration, it visited the phishing site and attempted to redeem the gift card using fabricated credentials.' No use-case for detecting phishing-link interactions by agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy/firewall logs for HTTP requests from agentic framework processes to newly-registered or low-reputation domains triggered by email links. Correlate with form-submission or credential-entry events (form fills, POST/login attempts) to those destinations. Agentic user-agents and rapid navigation patterns differentiate from human browsing.

suggestion.title: Identity Verification Bypass Under Operational Urgency
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Both Generic and Strict profiles failed because the verification step still collapsed when the request appeared operationally urgent.' No detection for urgency-driven control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agentic framework execution logs for identity-verification procedure skip/bypass events, especially when preceded by urgency-laden email language (production emergency, critical outage, urgent deadline). Baseline verification-skip rate and alert on anomalous spikes. Cross-reference email content sentiment/keywords with verification-skip timing.

suggestion.title: OAuth Grant Attempt to Suspicious New Application
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Researchers created a malicious Google OAuth application disguised as a timesheet platform. The agent inspected the OAuth flow, analyzed the destination, identified the application as suspicious, and refused to grant access.' While correctly blocked in the test, this vectors needs active detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth authorization attempts by AI agent service accounts targeting newly-registered applications (<90d creation), low-reputation apps, or apps requesting broad scopes (email, Drive, Admin APIs). Correlate OAuth prompts with preceding email or in-app messages. Alert on agents authorizing unfamiliar third-party apps.

suggestion.title: High-Risk Action Initiated by Unverified External Sender
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly describes agent executing sensitive actions (credential sharing, data export) on requests from unverified external email senders without approval gates. No detection for this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag high-risk agentic actions (credential provisioning, sensitive data export, system access grants) initiated by email requests from external or non-directory senders. Require human approval logging for all such actions. Monitor agent logs for action execution following first-contact external email requests within 5-min window.

suggestion.title: Detect Python Credential Stealer Module Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer' as payload; detection must identify Python processes accessing credential stores, password managers, or reading SSH/API key files
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe or python processes accessing OS credential vaults (DPAPI, Keychain), reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, .git directories, or accessing password manager databases. Flag processes spawning without user interaction or from unexpected parent processes like git or package installers.

suggestion.title: Detect Repository Supply Chain Compromise — Anomalous Commits
suggestion.rationale: 'Pythagora-io/gpt-pilot Compromised on GitHub' indicates malicious code injection via repository; detection must identify unauthorized commits, new committer identities, or modifications to package configuration files
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to public repository from new IP addresses, commits during off-hours by known developers, modifications to setup.py/pyproject.toml/requirements.txt outside standard CI/CD workflows, or direct pushes to main branch bypassing pull request reviews.

suggestion.title: Detect Python Code Obfuscation and Linter Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Subtitle 'Blocked by Python Linter' indicates attacker used obfuscation to bypass static analysis; detection should target encoding, dynamic code generation, and anti-analysis patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python code using base64/hex encoding, compile() for runtime code execution, obfuscated variable names, dynamic imports via __import__() or importlib, or string concatenation to reconstruct module/function names in order to bypass linter pattern matching.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Exfiltration via Python Process Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate stolen data; detection must identify suspicious DNS queries, HTTP POST requests, or encrypted tunnels from Python processes to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe or python processes making outbound HTTP(S) to newly registered domains, low-reputation IPs, or known credential-theft C2 ranges. Flag unusual POST requests to webhook services, pastebin clones, or cloud storage buckets; correlate with credential-access process activity.

suggestion.title: Detect Stolen Git/PyPI Maintainer Credentials Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of a public repository targets maintainer credentials to enable persistence; detection must catch unauthorized API calls using stolen personal access tokens
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls (commits, pushes, releases, token creation) originating from unusual geographies or IP addresses; detect PyPI package uploads or version bumps from unexpected API keys or CI/CD runner identities; track creation of new deploy tokens by accounts not in maintainer ACL.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Requests to ServiceNow Related List Edit Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'exploited an unauthenticated access flaw through a vulnerable API endpoint' with endpoint `/api/now/related_list_edit/create` misconfigured with `requires_authentication=false`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow API logs for requests to /api/now/related_list_edit/create lacking authentication headers or with null/false auth status. Alert on any unauthenticated POST/GET to this endpoint. Baseline normal authenticated usage and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect API Queries from Known-Malicious IP 51.159.98.241
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies: 'Numerous admins shared indicators of compromise, including API requests from the IP address 51.159.98.241, advising other administrators to review logs for requests to the vulnerable endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert all inbound requests from 51.159.98.241 to any ServiceNow instance or API endpoint. Retroactively hunt logs from June 5 backwards for requests from this IP. Add to threat feed and correlate with other ServiceNow instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Discovery Across ServiceNow System Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'successfully query the customer instance tables' accessing 'IT support tickets, employee records, internal documentation, asset inventories, security incident reports, workflow data, and configuration details'—a clear table enumeration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow table access logs for single sessions querying 5+ distinct sensitive table types (incident, employee, asset, cmdb, workflow) within 5-minute window. Flag unauthenticated sessions or requests from external IPs. Baseline normal cross-table queries and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass Sensitive Data Extraction from ServiceNow Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes support tickets 'can contain credentials, API tokens, internal documentation, and authentication secrets'—indicating attackers were harvesting credential material. Detection must flag large record access on credential-rich tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access to service-now.incident, sys_user, and cmdb_ci_* tables returning >100 rows per query from unauthenticated sources or suspicious IPs. Correlate large-volume table exports with authentication bypass detections. Flag exports containing PII, credentials, or API token patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect REST API Endpoint Misconfiguration: requires_authentication=false
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'One commenter claimed the endpoint was configured with requires_authentication=false, potentially allowing unauthenticated requests to access instance data.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan ServiceNow API endpoint definitions for requires_authentication=false or equivalent bypass flags. Alert on configuration changes disabling auth on previously-protected endpoints. Monitor API gateway logs for requests succeeding to endpoints marked unauthenticated. Correlate changes with deployment/maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Command Execution via binding.gyp Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp's 'action' and 'variables' fields allow arbitrary shell command execution during npm install. Article title directly references unexpected 'capabilities' of the build system—classic supply-chain RCE vector that should have generated a detection for malicious pre/post-install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installation and node-gyp invocation for process spawning unusual child processes (bash, powershell, cmd) with non-standard arguments. Alert on build scripts executing network tools (curl, wget) or creating/modifying system files outside node_modules. Correlate package installs with unexpected outbound connections.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp Variable Injection Leading to Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: The article specifically explores binding.gyp's 'weirdest' capabilities—likely referring to variable substitution and gyp/scons injection. Missing detection for when build variables are set to command-injection payloads (e.g., variables.some_setting set to shell metacharacters).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation and modification of binding.gyp files within package directories. Look for variable definitions containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) or references to environment variables not typically used in builds. Alert on modifications to binding.gyp during or after package fetch.

suggestion.title: Malicious Native Module Build via Supply-Chain npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Compromised or typosquatted npm packages with malicious binding.gyp files could inject native code into build artifacts. No detection for when build outputs diverge from package signatures or when compiled .node binaries are created/modified unexpectedly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of .node (native module binary) files during npm install. Correlate build completion with unexpected binary artifacts outside documented package structure. Alert if build process creates or modifies files with execution bits in system directories. Track npm package installation of packages with known binding.gyp usage against benign build output baselines.

suggestion.title: Exploitation via binding.gyp 'include_dirs' Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp's 'include_dirs' and 'sources' fields can reference parent directories. This is a classic path-traversal vector allowing malicious packages to compile code from outside their own tree—directly related to 'weirdest capabilities' in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor gyp/scons build invocations for include_dirs pointing above the package root (../../../ patterns or absolute paths to /usr, /opt, /etc). Alert on compilation commands with suspicious -I flags referencing system directories. Baseline legitimate builds and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Post-install Script RCE via binding.gyp Actions
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp 'action' blocks can define custom commands executed at build time. Missing detection for build actions that masquerade legitimate compilation but actually execute downloader malware, reverse shells, or exfiltration payloads—a common npm supply-chain pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect binding.gyp action blocks for commands that spawn interpreters (python, perl, ruby, node) with inline scripts or remote fetch commands. Monitor for build actions that make network requests (curl, wget, PowerShell -Command) to unexpected domains. Alert on mismatches between declared package functionality and actual build actions.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Remote Code Execution Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited'—the pipeline must detect the exploitation vector itself, not just post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WinRAR (rar.exe, unrar.exe) spawning child processes or reading/executing files from archive extraction directories. Correlate with network egress to known stealer C2 ranges. Alert on WinRAR process interaction with compressed files from external sources (email, web download).

suggestion.title: Information Stealer Execution Following Archive Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Deploy Stealers'—detection must cover stealer payload execution post-WinRAR exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution from temporary extraction directories (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%) immediately following WinRAR activity. Flag stealers accessing browser profiles, credential stores, and cryptocurrency wallets. Monitor for unusual registry reads (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU, credential manager hives).

suggestion.title: Stealer Command-and-Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Stealers require C2 callback; article implies exfiltration infrastructure but pipeline extracted zero network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS/HTTP POST requests from temporary-directory child processes to uncommon ASNs or newly registered domains. Flag encrypted TLS 1.2 tunnels from stealer executables with abnormal TLS certificate subject names or issuer patterns typical of commodity stealer infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Stolen Credential Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Stealers' as payload—these tools target credentials. Article does not specify exfil technique; detection should cover archive uploads, encoded DNS tunnels, and bulk email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data reads from DPAPI-protected credential stores (LSA secrets, SAM registry hive copies) followed by network egress. Alert on stealer writing credential dumps to cloud storage services or creating outbound SMTP/DNS queries with encoded credential material.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Archive Payload Delivery Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine targeting suggests phishing delivery vector (typical for this threat class) but pipeline surface no initial-access IOCs or email-based delivery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe or .dll files downloaded from email external links or attachments landing in Downloads folder, immediately followed by WinRAR extraction and child process spawn. Flag emails with Ukrainian language content or spoofed Ukrainian government/corporate domains paired with archive attachments.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Malware Distribution Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 5 IOC domains in a dedicated 'Indicators of Compromise' section: pluginchad.xyz, maxapk.xyz, d4ug.site, slmgr.sh, msget.run. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this structured data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound connections to pluginchad[.]xyz, maxapk[.]xyz, d4ug[.]site, slmgr[.]sh, or msget[.]run. Correlate with Downloads folder activity and recent user engagement with TikTok/Instagram. High-confidence breach indicator.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Detection — Binary File Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 hash (03bbc4fa1fd784276da135ab62fef85aaddea66e6eb176d7e59c3398f818b153) in IOC section; pipeline extracted zero hashes from article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match process creation against SHA256 03bbc4fa1fd784276da135ab62fef85aaddea66e6eb176d7e59c3398f818b153. Flag any execution, especially from user Downloads or AppData/Local/Temp. Correlate temporal proximity to connections to malware domains.

suggestion.title: Browser Download Execution — User-Initiated File Launch from Malicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain explicitly describes users downloading files via fake tutorials and executing them. T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) is the core interaction; pipeline missed T1204 family entirely despite clear narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser child processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) executing files from user Downloads folder within 5 minutes of network connections to malware domains. Elevate priority if downloaded file name contains strings like 'tutorial', 'free', 'software', 'crack', 'activator'.

suggestion.title: Phishing via Social Media Videos — Fake Free Software Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'polished, convincing videos that promise free access to popular premium software' on TikTok/Instagram as the delivery vector. T1566.003 (Spearphishing via Service) and T1036.005 (masquerading) were not identified by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for indicators of social engineering: users with high visit frequency to TikTok or Instagram followed by downloads from malware infrastructure domains. Flag accounts showing engagement with video platform profiles containing keywords like 'free', 'tutorial', 'software', 'crack'.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Premium Software — Legitimate Application Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack uses 'fake software tutorials' and domains like 'slmgr.sh' (mimics Windows licensing tool slmgr.vbs) and 'msget.run' (Microsoft utility impersonation) indicate T1036.005. Pipeline missed this defense evasion technique entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of files with legitimate software names (Adobe, Microsoft Office, Autodesk, etc.) but sourced from Downloads or temp folders, unsigned, or signed by unknown publishers. Cross-reference against known legitimate software publisher certificates; mismatches are high-signal.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Detection in Ivanti Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'OS command injection weakness' enabling 'remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' Direct evidence of shell metacharacter exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (pre-R10.5.2, R10.6.x pre-R10.6.2, R10.7.0 versions) containing command shell syntax: pipe (|), semicolon (;), command substitution ($(), backticks), or logical operators (&&, ||) in request parameters, headers, or body. Baseline legitimate Sentry traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Administrative Account Creation (CVE-2026-10523 Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' Explicit persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate admin account creation events with prior session logs—alert if new admin account appears without authenticated administrative session history. Flag multiple new admin accounts (>1) created within 1-hour window. Cross-check Sentry audit logs for account creation from unauthenticated or default-credential sessions.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root via Sentry Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' Indicates arbitrary command execution at OS root level, not application-level privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning with UID=0 (root) where parent process is Ivanti Sentry gateway service (typically running as unprivileged user). Alert on exec syscalls from sentry daemon context to /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other shells with effective UID=0.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Both CVEs are exploitable 'remotely by unauthenticated attackers'—implies protected admin APIs reachable without credentials. Article phrase: 'can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs for successful (HTTP 200) requests to administrative endpoints (/admin*, /api/admin*, /manage*) missing or bearing null/invalid Authorization headers or session tokens. Alert on requests to protected endpoints from IP addresses with no prior successful authentication session.

suggestion.title: Sentry Authentication Bypass via Session Tampering
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10523 described as 'critical authentication bypass.' Detection requires identifying bypass mechanics: requests that bypass login validation. Article: 'authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry featuring tampered or missing session cookies, Authorization header bypass attempts, or requests succeeding against /api/authenticate or /admin endpoints without prior /login. Baseline expected auth flow and alert on requests that skip authentication steps.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Grants SYSTEM Access'—the core impact. Pipeline failed to surface any privilege escalation detection. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Microsoft Defender components (MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe, WinDefend service) running with SYSTEM integrity where parent was non-privileged or unexpected. Monitor for token impersonation/theft within Defender scanning context.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Code Execution via Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Zero-Day'—exploitation of Defender's scan engine or service interface. Pipeline missed detection for malicious vectors targeting Defender internals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed files (weaponized payloads, malicious containers) fed to MsMpEng scan operations, unusual DLL loads by Defender components, and indirect code execution patterns via scan engine exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation SYSTEM-Level Activity from Defender
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables SYSTEM access. Once escalation succeeds, attacker gains elevated execution context. Pipeline failed to detect downstream abuse after privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SYSTEM-level cmd.exe, PowerShell, or child processes spawned from Defender service/components, particularly if followed by network connections or file access outside normal scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Defender Windows Service Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting a Defender zero-day may involve registry modifications, RPC calls, or service control operations to trigger vulnerable code paths. Article states 'on Updated Windows'—service-level interaction likely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications targeting WinDefend service configuration, suspicious RPC calls to Defender service ports, or attempts to reload/restart Defender with malicious payloads.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Flaw Exploited' targeting ServiceNow instances; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or detections for exploit payloads or vulnerability probing patterns typical of ServiceNow CVE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to ServiceNow instances containing patterns consistent with known CVE exploits (e.g., path traversal, unauthenticated API endpoints, malformed parameters to /api/now/ routes). Correlate with instances where content-length or response codes suggest successful data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized ServiceNow Instance Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'Unauthorized Access to Customer Instances' indicates post-exploitation account activity; pipeline produced no use cases for anomalous login patterns, session hijacking, or mass data access following initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logins to ServiceNow instances from unexpected IPs, rapid sequential API calls querying user/incident/CMDB tables post-initial-access timestamp, or service account usage outside maintenance windows. Cross-reference with exploitation indicators from initial-access phase.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Mass Data Export or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Unauthorized Access'—implies data theft; pipeline generated no detection logic for bulk export patterns, large result-set queries, or authenticated data download anomalies typical of post-compromise reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API queries returning >10k records, list view exports, or scheduled report generation by compromised/stolen accounts. Correlate with unusual outbound connections to non-approved endpoints or compression/archiving tools on ServiceNow application servers.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Vulnerable Systems — CVE-2026-50507 and CVE-2026-45585 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt with confidence 'High' and phase 'recon'. Pipeline failed to instantiate this template. Detects systems vulnerable to disclosed BitLocker bypass affecting encryption bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Windows systems running OS versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-50507 or CVE-2026-45585. Prioritize systems with BitLocker enabled. Cross-correlate with patch-management inventory to flag unpatched assets in sensitive environments.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Disablement or Recovery Key Access — Unauthorized Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthorized attacker with physical access to bypass BitLocker Device Encryption.' Detection should monitor for BitLocker state changes and recovery key access indicative of exploitation or post-compromise forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Event Log 4656 (BitLocker Preparation Tool) and 5061 (Encryption state change). Flag unexpected BitLocker disablement, recovery-key extraction, or decryption initiation outside maintenance windows. Correlate with physical-access logs and after-hours activity.

suggestion.title: Mass File Access on Previously Encrypted Storage — Post-Bypass Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article culminates in impact: 'access sensitive data on the system's storage device.' After BitLocker bypass, attackers enumerate and exfiltrate. Detection closes post-exploitation gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-BitLocker-disablement, monitor for rapid file listing, copy operations on system or user data folders (AppData, Documents, System32), and unusual external device connections. Correlate with BitLocker state changes and time-of-day anomalies.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Logging Disabled or StopLogging API Called
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly references 'abusing cloud logging services'; disabling CloudTrail is the primary AWS logging evasion vector described in this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or PutEventSelectors API calls in CloudTrail logs targeting production accounts. Monitor for successful trail disable within 5 minutes of privilege escalation or credential compromise. Correlate with failed log access attempts by same principal.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Log Files Deleted from S3
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'log storage' and deletion of log entries; S3 bucket tampering is a direct attack vector when CloudTrail logs are stored in S3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk DeleteObject or DeleteVersion calls against S3 buckets designated as CloudTrail log destinations. Alert on deletion patterns that remove logs spanning suspicious activity windows. Cross-reference with IAM policy changes granting s3:DeleteObject to compromised principals.

suggestion.title: Cloud Logging Configuration Modified to Reduce Log Coverage
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'log router' and 'log sink' abuse in Google Cloud context; configuration modification narrows logging scope without full disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UpdateSink calls with modified filter expressions that suppress log types, DeleteSink calls removing sinks to SIEM, or UpdateLoggingBucket calls disabling retention. Alert on configuration changes affecting data-access or activity logs post-compromise.

suggestion.title: IAM Policy or Role Modified to Grant Logging Impairment Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article implies privilege escalation step before logging attacks; attacker must escalate to role/principal with logging-modification permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inline or managed policy attachments granting logging-modification actions (logs:*, s3:DeleteObject on log buckets, logging.logEntries.delete). Alert on creation of custom roles with overly permissive logging-related actions. Correlate policy changes with subsequent logging API calls.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Cloud Logging Configuration and Storage Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker enumeration of logging infrastructure as prerequisite; DescribeTrails, ListTrails, and similar discovery calls precede disablement.
log_sources: GCP Audit Logs (List, Get on logging resources)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of logging-discovery API calls (DescribeTrails, GetTrailStatus, ListTrails, ListSinks, GetBucket) in rapid succession from single principal. Alert on enumeration from newly-compromised credentials or atypical source IP. Baseline expected discovery from compliance/audit tools.

suggestion.title: GCP Log Sink Disabled or Forwarding Target Removed
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'log router' and 'log sink' as abuse targets in Google Cloud; sinks forward logs to storage or external SIEM—removal is evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UpdateSink calls that set includeChildren=false, disable sinks, or modify filter to exclude critical log types. Alert on DeleteSink operations removing sinks that forward to external storage (GCS, BigQuery, Pub/Sub). Correlate with later activity in same GCP project.

suggestion.title: Chrome V8 Exploitation Attempt - Memory Corruption Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Chrome V8 Zero-Day'—indicating memory corruption vulnerability exploitation. Article states 'Exploited in the Wild' but pipeline generated no corresponding detection for memory-based exploitation or browser crash/hang patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome/Chromium renderer processes terminating abnormally with memory access violations or executing unusual child processes post-crash recovery. V8 exploits typically trigger segfaults or heap corruption errors in V8.dll/libv8.so.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Title includes specific CVE identifier (CVE-2026-11645) but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should flag attempts to exploit this public CVE once patches become available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match Chrome version against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-11645. Alert on unpatched versions accessing untrusted content or responding to targeted phishing campaigns linking to exploit pages.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Content Delivery to Unpatched Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates wild exploitation but no detection for delivery mechanism. Browser zero-days typically require social engineering or drive-by download to reach victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails linking to attacker-controlled domains serving exploit kits targeting Chrome. Correlate with browser crash telemetry or suspicious process execution following web browsing sessions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Behavior After Browser RCE
suggestion.rationale: Chrome V8 exploits enable code execution in renderer context. Pipeline missed detections for lateral privilege escalation or payload staging following successful browser compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (token impersonation, UAC bypass) launched from Chrome child processes or following abnormal Chrome termination and restart. Detect suspicious signed-binary abuse (LOLBins) spawned by browser context.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN IKEv1 Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-50751) to bypass authentication and establish a remote access VPN connection.' This is the core initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN gateways for IKEv1 Key Exchange traffic from external sources that establishes VPN sessions without valid credential submission. Alert on authentication bypasses or successful session establishment without corresponding RADIUS/TACACS+ authentication events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous VPN Session Establishment to Check Point Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation began on May 7 and surged over the weekend' targeting 'few dozen targeted organizations globally.' New or suspicious VPN source IPs should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN connections from novel source geographies, previously unseen ASNs, or off-hours access patterns to Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access appliances. Correlate timing with known exploitation window (post-May 7, 2026).

suggestion.title: Qilin Ransomware Post-Compromise Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'One case involved confirmed post-compromise activity associated with Qilin ransomware affiliate.' VPN compromise should precede ransomware execution (file encryption, exfiltration, ransom note).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 48 hours of VPN compromise, alert on mass file encryption activity (bulk file modifications), process execution from SYSTEM context with suspicious parents (psexec, WMI, RDP), or large data exfiltration to novel external IPs known or suspected as Qilin infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Deprecated IKEv1 Protocol Enabled on Check Point Gateways
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The vulnerability affects only instances configured to use the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange protocol' and 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate.' Configuration audit should flag this weakness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Check Point gateway configurations for IKEv1 enablement on Mobile Access and Remote Access VPN instances. Packet inspection should detect and alert on IKEv1 Key Exchange messages on systems that should be IKEv2-only.

suggestion.title: Machine Certificate Authentication Disabled on Check Point VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'security gateways that don't require a machine certificate for connections and accept legacy Remote Access clients' are vulnerable. Machine cert auth enforces device identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Check Point Remote Access VPN configurations for mandatory Machine Certificate Authentication. Alert if disabled or optional. Cross-reference successful VPN sessions against client certificate logs to identify device-unauthenticated connections.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Version Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera' — asset inventory and patch verification against federal remediation deadline (2026-06-23) is foundational for this CISA KEV threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query installed software inventory for Chrome, Edge, Opera versions and compare against CVE-2026-11645 patch release dates. Alert on vulnerable versions persisting past federal due date 2026-06-23. CISA KEV status confirms active in-the-wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution from Browser Engine
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation outcome as 'arbitrary code inside a sandbox' — detection must flag unexpected child processes spawned from browser engines with anomalous execution patterns or resource access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation where parent = chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or opera.exe and child is not a known legitimate subprocess. Flag processes with suspicious cmdline arguments, memory access anomalies, or correlation with V8 engine exceptions.

suggestion.title: V8 Engine Crash Correlated with Suspicious Post-Crash Activity
suggestion.rationale: Out-of-bounds read/write vulnerability ('CVE-2026-11645 — Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Read and Write') consistently triggers application crashes during exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or opera.exe crashes with access violation (0xC0000005) or heap corruption exception codes, especially if followed within seconds by unexpected child process spawning, outbound network connections, or file I/O to sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Browser Sandbox Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Real-world exploitation of client-side RCE vulnerabilities frequently escalates from browser sandbox context to system privileges — monitor for privilege boundary violations even though sandbox escape is not explicitly stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes or their child processes attempting HKLM registry writes, System32 directory modifications, device driver loading, or direct kernel API access. Flag process injection attempts originating from browser sandboxes.

suggestion.title: Web Request to Suspicious Content Followed by Browser Crash
suggestion.rationale: Attack delivery mechanism: 'via a crafted HTML page' — correlation between web requests and subsequent browser crashes may indicate exploitation of CVE-2026-11645.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/HTTPS requests or DNS queries from browser processes to low-reputation or suspicious content sources, followed within seconds by browser process crashes with memory violation exceptions. High fidelity if correlated with V8-specific crash signatures.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Suspicious Crafted File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system' as the exploitation mechanism. Detection should monitor file uploads to SD-WAN Manager endpoints for suspicious patterns or unusual payload characteristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for unusual file uploads or POST requests with file parameters. Correlate with subsequent process execution. Alert on files with suspicious entropy, encoding oddities, or unexpected MIME types directed at vManage endpoints.

suggestion.title: Elevated Privilege Code Execution from SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... execute arbitrary commands as root'. This privilege escalation pattern is detectable via process execution monitoring on systems running SD-WAN Manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Cisco SD-WAN Manager processes (vManage child processes, wrapper scripts) spawn root-level command shells or execute system binaries with UID=0. Establish baseline of legitimate root execution and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Authentication Anomaly Preceding Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'authenticated, local attacker' access. Detect authentication patterns that precede file uploads or process anomalies, including failed login attempts, lateral movement to management interfaces, or credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager (vManage) authentication logs for: (1) successful logins from unexpected source IPs, (2) login spike preceding file upload, (3) service account abuse, (4) failed login patterns suggesting credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Output Encoding Failure in SD-WAN Manager Request/Response Cycle
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper encoding or escaping of output'. Detection should identify HTTP responses or logs from SD-WAN Manager showing unescaped/unencoded payloads, command injection signatures, or encoding bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP responses from SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing unencoded command syntax (bash operators, shell metacharacters) in error messages, parameter echoing, or debug output. Correlate with requests containing special characters (;, |, &&, etc.).

suggestion.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and references asset-exposure template in _TEMPLATES.md; no use case generated. Federal patch due 2026-06-23 makes this time-critical for compliance hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and CMDB for Arista EOS instances with version matching CVE-2026-7473 eligibility. Correlate against network-exposed assets via port scans or NetFlow. Alert on unpatched devices remaining 5 days before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Arista Decapsulation Error Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically involves incorrect decapsulation of tunneled packets ('incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet'); error logs should surface exploitation attempts before successful packet forwarding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS syslog and CLI logs for decapsulation failures, malformed packet drops, or tunnel validation errors. Establish per-device baseline; alert on 4σ spike or sustained 2-3x elevation, particularly if correlated with external source traffic.

suggestion.title: Arista Tunneled Packet Misdirection via Decapsulation IP Collision
suggestion.rationale: Technical root cause: device forwards packets where destination IP matches configured decapsulation IP but originate from unexpected sources. This mismatch behavior should be detectable via netflow and packet content analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline valid tunnel encapsulation patterns per Arista device (legitimate source/dest pairs, protocols). Flag netflow tuples where inner packet destination IP equals the device's configured decapsulation IP but source deviates from baseline, or where encapsulation headers fail signature validation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Unauthorized File Access Without Token Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Every file ever shared on Tchap, on any shard, is downloadable without a token.' Attack succeeded because files were accessible via media IDs scraped from messages, bypassing authentication controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests for media resources using ID patterns extracted from message contents, without corresponding token validation events. Alert on single account/IP downloading files across multiple conversations or users within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Message and Account Enumeration Across Shards
