suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify successful authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager followed by unusual file operations or API calls within seconds. Flag if authentication originates from unexpected source IP or account with no historical pattern of file uploads to the management system.

suggestion.title: Crafted Input File Detection: SD-WAN Manager Encoding/Escaping Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output'—detection should hunt for malformed input that exploits this weakness. Article: 'supplying a crafted file.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager for file uploads or API parameters containing encoding anomalies (double-encoding, Unicode escaping, null bytes, command injection syntax). Correlate with subsequent process execution or configuration changes. Focus on inputs to file-handling functions within vManage.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 Unpatched Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-23'. CISA KEV signals active wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Arista EOS instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-7473. Cross-reference patch version against Arista advisory. Escalate any unpatched externally-routable switch.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Decapsulation Configuration Drift
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability triggers when 'switch incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP'—requires config-change baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authorized decapsulation IP endpoints on Arista EOS fleet. Alert on any add/modify/delete of tunnel decapsulation rules or destination IPs, especially to RFC1918 ranges or previously-unseen external hosts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Tunnel Packet Egress from Arista Switches
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation forwarding 'unexpected tunneled packet'—NetFlow/sFlow can detect egress encapsulation anomalies inconsistent with baseline tunnel usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Arista switch egress flows for tunnel encapsulation headers (GRE, VXLAN, Geneve, IPsec). Flag anomalous egress with unexpected tunnel encapsulation ratios, new source/destination tunnel pairs, or non-production target IPs.

suggestion.title: Cross-VLAN or Cross-Segment Lateral Movement via Tunnel Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Incorrect packet forwarding via tunnel decapsulation is a lateral-movement vector—traffic from untrusted sources arriving as if intra-network requires east-west detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for internal-segment traffic with nested IP headers or anomalous TTL patterns suggesting tunnel decapsulation. Correlate source ASN/GeoIP against known-external profile. Cross-check Arista logs for decapsulation errors or forwarding exceptions on CVE-2026-7473 timeline.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Hardcoded Credential Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker obtained 'hardcoded LDAP credentials allegedly leaked via a PowerShell script shared by a French tax authority regional director.' T1552.007 + T1059.001 directly applicable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell script execution containing password/token literals or LDAP connection strings with embedded credentials. Baseline internal credential-sharing scripts and filter out legitimate admin tooling. Score on regex patterns for 'password', 'ldap://', hardcoded 'cn=' distinguished names in script content.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account and Message Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages and information on over 73,000 accounts.' T1087 (Account Discovery) + T1083 (File Discovery) for batch queries against user/conversation databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Matrix service / messaging platform logs for single account issuing thousands of enumeration queries in short window: list-users, list-rooms, fetch-messages by conversation ID in sequential or pattern-based ranges. Threshold: >1000 account/message queries per user per hour from non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Media File Access via ID Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker states 'Every file ever shared on Tchap...is downloadable without a token' and 'media IDs come from the messages...pull the file freely regardless of which shard hosts it.' Application-layer authorization bypass (T1526 Cloud Service Discovery / Reconnaissance).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET requests to media endpoints (e.g., /media/[ID]) lacking valid authentication token or session cookie. Establish baseline of legitimate media requests per user per hour; flag accounts requesting sequential/enumerated media IDs at rates >10x median. Correlate with non-user-agents (curl, scripting libraries).

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Attacker exfiltrated '13.5GB of documents and media files shared by public servants' following account compromise. Describes T1020 (Automated Exfiltration) or T1030 (Data Transfer Size Limits Evasion) in context of cloud-hosted collaboration service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single user account initiating download/export of large data volumes (>500MB aggregate) within 24-hour window. Flag egress to external IP ranges or high-risk geographies from educational/government shard. Cross-correlate with new login events and deviation from user baseline data access patterns.

suggestion.title: Account Hijacking via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Attacker explicitly states 'I social engineered a valid account on the education shard.' T1078.001 (Valid Accounts) and T1566.002 (Social Engineering) as initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication from new device/geolocation within 1 hour of failed authentication attempts or password reset request. Monitor for MFA bypass or disable event following account unlock. Flag accounts that never previously accessed APIs now suddenly querying bulk data; compare login metadata (device, ASN, user-agent) to 90-day baseline.

suggestion.title: Shard/Tenant Enumeration in Multi-Tenant Architecture
suggestion.rationale: Attacker identified and accessed the 'education shard' (matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr), claiming 'other shards will have more.' Indicates discovery of service topology and potential for lateral movement across organizational boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS lookups or HTTP requests to multiple shard subdomains (matrix.agent.*.tchap.gouv.fr) from single source within short timeframe. Flag patterns suggesting subdomain enumeration (sequential naming, wildcard expansion attempts). Baseline: users should access only their designated shard; cross-shard traffic by a single account is anomalous.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to pheditor.php terminal handler with shell metacharacter patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is triggered by 'injecting shell metacharacters into the dir POST parameter' and that whitelist can be bypassed. Need network-layer detection (WAF/IDS) or application-level logging for POST parameter inspection; endpoint-only detection insufficient.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php containing action=terminal with body parameters including shell metacharacters (;|&$()\`<>) or hex-encoded equivalents. Correlate with subsequent process execution from web server context.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated exploit attempt on pheditor terminal handler
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'any authenticated user' but real-world exploitation likely involves authentication bypass or credential stuffing preceding exploitation. Detect failed authentication attempts followed by successful POST to pheditor.php/action=terminal within minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login/401 responses to pheditor.php within a 5-minute window before successful POST with action=terminal. Anomalous user-agents, rapid requests from single source to pheditor.php, or requests from IPs without prior login history are indicators.

suggestion.title: Whitelist bypass or forbidden command execution in pheditor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions that vulnerability 'bypasses the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist'. Detect attempts to execute commands outside the whitelist or command sequences that should trigger whitelist enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify shell processes spawned from PHP context with command lines matching known blacklist indicators (e.g., /etc/passwd access, network utilities when shell access only should be allowed, etc.). Correlate parent process command line containing 'pheditor.php' and 'action=terminal' with child process command containing dangerous patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation webshell registration in pheditor
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via command injection often results in webshell persistence. Detect file writes to webroot by web server processes, particularly .php files with suspicious entropy or naming patterns typical of webshells (shell.php, cmd.php, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php file creation in web-accessible directories (/var/www, /srv/www, etc.) by php-fpm/apache processes with low entropy filenames, very small sizes (<5KB), or suspicious content patterns (eval, system, exec, passthru, shell_exec).

suggestion.title: Parent-child process anomaly: web server spawning non-standard interpreters via terminal handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via terminal handler. Detect unexpected interpreter spawning (perl, python, ruby) from PHP parent process with command-line structure suggesting dynamic code execution or command substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for php/apache parent with child process (perl/python/ruby) where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains shell syntax operators (&& || ; | < >) or suspicious quoting patterns. Baseline legitimate pheditor usage and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Outbound network activity from PHP-spawned shell processes
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation RCE typically includes command-and-control callbacks, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. Detect network connections originating from shell processes spawned by PHP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated by sh/bash/curl/wget/nc/python processes where parent is php-fpm/apache and command-line includes suspicious parameters (proxy settings, URLs, reverse-shell patterns) or connects to non-standard ports from web context.

suggestion.title: WebSocket-to-HEEx Template Injection Attack Vector
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'WebSocket and interpolates them unsanitized into a HEEx template that is subsequently compiled and evaluated.' Pipeline missed the entry vector entirely—no detection for unauthenticated WebSocket frames feeding attribute values into template compilation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebSocket connections to Phoenix Storybook endpoints (typically /storybook paths) accepting attribute parameters without authentication headers. Baseline legitimate tooling traffic and alert on new source IPs or high-volume parameter injection attempts preceding process execution.

suggestion.title: Elixir Kernel.eval() Post-RCE Execution Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'compiled and evaluated with full Elixir Kernel access' but pipeline missed the execution mechanism—Kernel.eval or Code.compile_string patterns are the actual post-injection execution trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Elixir/BEAM process logs containing Kernel.eval, Code.compile_string, or dynamic template compilation errors immediately following WebSocket writes. Cross-correlate to process spawning or file modifications within 5 seconds post-log-event.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable phoenix_storybook Version Footprint (0.5–1.0 asset exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 1.0 (see UC_16_4 artifact paths) but pipeline provided no inventory-based detection. Missing high-confidence asset exposure for the version range known to be vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for phoenix_storybook package installations or filesystem artefacts matching regex patterns `phoenix_storybook-(0\.[5-9]|1\.0)\.` across dependency manifests (mix.exs, mix.lock), BEAM artifact directories (.beam files), and OTP release directories. Flag as exploitable unless patched to 1.1+.

suggestion.title: BEAM Runtime Persistence After RCE (Long-lived Shell Access Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution' leading to System.cmd spawning but omits detection for sustained shell sessions. Pipeline missed the persistence/dwell-time signature—long-running sh/bash/powershell processes parented by BEAM after the initial RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell processes (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned from BEAM (beam.smp, erl.exe) that remain alive for >60 seconds without legitimate parent process activity. Baseline admin/CI automation contexts; flag unexpected users or off-hours execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Auto-Execution on Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer' — malware executes automatically during package installation, likely via setup.py, __init__.py, or install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning within seconds of pip install completion, originating from site-packages or pip cache directories. Flag execution of credential-harvesting tools (bun, curl, wget, openssl) from Python package context with unexpected parent processes or working directories.

suggestion.title: PyPI Repository Compromise — Malicious Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is supply-chain compromise of public package repository. Title: '19 Packages Poisoned' — need detection of installation of known-malicious package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed Python packages against threat feeds tracking compromised PyPI packages (e.g., Hades campaign packages). Alert on any installation of versions flagged as malicious. Monitor pip install logs for unexpected version downgrades or installation of packages with timing anomalies (rapid re-release, version churn).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Bun Process Post-Package-Install
suggestion.rationale: Malware specifically targets 'Bun Credential Stealer' — executes credential-access operations post-installation. Article phrase: 'Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 'bun' process execution in user context with file-access patterns targeting credential stores (.aws/credentials, .ssh, .kube/config, browser profiles, .bash_history). Flag reads from environment variables containing API keys or tokens. Detect file copies of credential material to /tmp or user-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Attacker C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate harvested credentials to attacker infrastructure. Expected C2 communication post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to non-standard domains immediately following credential-harvesting process execution. Flag DNS queries to subdomains or infrastructure associated with Hades campaign. Detect outbound traffic patterns consistent with credential exfiltration (base64-encoded JSON payloads, high-entropy data blobs).

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Installation or Execution in Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Malware payload is 'Bun Credential Stealer' — may involve Bun runtime installation or execution as part of setup.py, not a native credential-stealing tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of Bun runtime (via curl, npm, or direct download) triggered from Python package installation context. Monitor for suspicious Bun scripts (inline with -c flag or from downloaded .js files). Flag network requests to Bun CDN or package registries from non-standard Python processes.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'; no UC exists to detect initial exploitation. Title phrase: 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM endpoints (typically port 8000 or reverse-proxy frontends) for anomalous HTTP/HTTPS requests targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Flag requests containing serialized Python, template injection payloads, or path traversal patterns. Track 4xx → 5xx response transitions that may indicate CVE trigger.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command Execution via LiteLLM Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE chains from initial flaw; no UC for execution stage. Phrase: 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by LiteLLM Python interpreter (parent: python.exe or litellm service) with suspicious command line: bash -i, powershell -enc, curl/wget to external IP, or execution of /tmp or %TEMP% binaries. Correlate with sudden increase in network egress from LiteLLM process.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Service Privilege Escalation or Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: RCE 'in the wild' exploitation suggests threat actors are achieving impact beyond web-tier code execution; article likely describes lateral movement or persistence. Generic but critical gap if article details privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If LiteLLM runs in container: monitor for privilege escalation techniques (sudo abuse, capability abuse, cgroup escape) or host filesystem access from container. If bare-metal: flag setuid abuse, SeAssignPrimaryToken token-stealing, or kernel exploit markers (dmesg segfaults, SMEP/KPTI bypasses).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection from Compromised Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents.' Attackers compromised popular GitHub Actions used by downstream projects, likely injecting malicious workflow steps or secret-exfiltration logic into the action.yml payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to action.yml or root-level workflow YAMLs in high-star repositories. Alert on commits that inject shell execution (run:, script:), add credential access, or define suspicious `env:` variables. Correlate with bulk downstream workflow failures or secrets access anomalies in dependent projects.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Destruction / Disable Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article reports '72 Other Repositories Disabled'—mass destructive action post-compromise. Single actor/token disabling dozens of public repos is rare legitimate activity and strong indicator of account takeover or automated attack execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single GitHub user or service principal disables/deletes ≥5 public repositories within a 30-minute window. Establish baseline of expected repo lifecycle activity per organization. Correlate deletion burst with authentication anomalies (new IP, impossible travel, MFA bypass).

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Supply-Chain Artifact Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Miasma Worm' distributed via compromised repositories. Attackers replaced legitimate release artifacts (npm packages, Python wheels, Docker images) with malware-laden binaries or added malicious build steps that execute during CI/CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash all released artifacts and alert when binary signatures or cryptographic hashes diverge from source-code-derived checksums. Detect obfuscated code additions in build scripts. Monitor package-repository upload events from compromised accounts, and cross-reference with malware-family YARA rules on decompiled artifacts.

suggestion.title: AI Coding Agent Code Injection via Malicious Prompt or Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'AI Coding Agents' (e.g., GitHub Copilot integrations, LLM-assisted CI/CD). Attackers likely injected prompt-injection payloads or poisoned training data to manipulate agent output, or compromised dependencies used by agent frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent processes for unusual environment-variable access (secrets, tokens), outbound HTTPS to non-standard ports or unrecognized domains, and child-process spawning during code-generation workflows. Alert on agent-generated code that attempts shell execution or network callbacks before human review/approval.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository Lateral Movement via Compromised Organization Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Attack disabled 72+ repositories—suggests attacker gained organization-level API token or service-account credential with broad repository permissions. Look for lateral movement from initial Azure Functions Action compromise to other high-value Microsoft/open-source repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track usage patterns of organization-scoped GitHub tokens or service principals after initial compromise. Alert on API calls to list/modify repositories from unexpected IPs or during non-business hours. Correlate repository access timelines—if Azure Functions Action token used to enumerate/modify unrelated repos within minutes, indicates credential reuse for persistence.

suggestion.title: Downstream Dependency Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: 72 disabled repositories implies broad downstream impact. Detect when projects that declared dependency on the compromised Azure Functions Action (GitHub Actions registry, npm, PyPI) encounter supply-chain poisoning—unusual network behavior, secrets leakage, or build-time code injection in dependent CI/CD pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Map dependency graphs of compromised action/packages. For all downstream consumers, alert when CI/CD job behavior diverges post-update (new network destinations, secret exfiltration, unexpected child processes). Implement transitive-supply-chain monitoring: flag cases where a project's dependency's dependency was compromised.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Race Condition Spawning SYSTEM cmd.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allowing attackers to spawn a command prompt with SYSTEM privileges via a Microsoft Defender race condition vulnerability.' This is the core attack; detectable by cmd.exe parent/privilege combo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned by MpEngineRun.exe or MsMpEng.exe (Defender processes) with IntegrityLevel=System or LogonType indicating SYSTEM context. Flag on abnormal child-process lineage where Defender is parent and shell is child, especially with rapid timing (milliseconds).

suggestion.title: VHD/VHDX File Access Triggering Defender Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploit originally 'required an attacker to coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server' and 'resulted in defender overwriting its own files.' Detectable as suspicious file-type opening followed by Defender self-modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .vhd or .vhdx file access from remote SMB paths (\\<remote-ip>\<share>\*.vhd*) followed within seconds by Defender process (MsMpEng.exe, MpEngineRun.exe) opening/modifying files in its own installation directory (e.g., C:\Program Files\Windows Defender\). High fidelity indicator of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: SMB Symlink/Junction Evaluation Enabling Defender Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'another attack scenario could lead to remote code execution simply by coercing a victim into opening an SMB share if symlink evaluation settings were enabled.' Detectable by registry/policy state and SMB access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to symlink-evaluation policies (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<SMB-service>\...) combined with SMB share mounts containing symlinks/junctions. Pair with Defender execution spikes in the seconds following symlink traversal.

suggestion.title: Defender mpengine SysIO API Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attack surface: 'mpengine!SysIO* API' and notes Microsoft 'silently hardened Defender in mid-May by patching "mpengine!SysIO*" API, which blocked junction attacks.' Detectable by abnormal SysIO call sequences from Defender.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In ETW or kernel trace, alert on rapid sequences of ntCreateFile → ntSetInformationFile (junction reparse) → ntOpenFile within Defender's address space in <100ms windows. Indicates race-condition exploitation attempting to bypass junction hardening.

suggestion.title: Defender Process Abnormal Thread/Timing Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The exploit is a race condition, so it's a hit or miss' — detectable as anomalous Defender thread creation or spawn-timing clustering around specific file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Defender spawning multiple threads in rapid succession (<10ms apart) in response to single file-open event, especially if followed by unexpected child-process creation. Race-condition exploits require tight timing; clustering indicates weaponization attempt.

suggestion.title: Patch-Gap Detection: KB5094126 Absence Enabling RoguePlanet
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ThreatLocker tested 'Windows 11 systems with KB5094126 installed' but RoguePlanet still succeeds. Organizations without this patch are at high risk; absence is an enabler indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all endpoints for absence of KB5094126 (or later cumulative update) on Windows 11. Pair with process execution baseline to identify Defender anomalies on unpatched systems. Flag cmd.exe spawned by Defender on machines missing this patch as high-priority incident.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb Denial of Service Detection (CVE-2026-49160)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'uncontrolled resource consumption in HTTP/2' attack that sends 'very small amounts of data that force servers to allocate disproportionately large amounts of memory' and notes 'dramatically increase memory usage on affected servers.' Researchers manipulate 'flow-control settings, preventing the server from freeing resources.' Clear impact-phase detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 requests for anomalous header-to-payload ratios or header counts exceeding MaxHeadersCount threshold. Alert on sudden memory spikes in HTTP.sys or IIS processes correlating with sustained small-packet HTTP/2 traffic. Baseline normal header density per server and client.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Bypass via WinRE and Physical EFI Attack (CVE-2026-50507 / YellowKey)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes YellowKey: attackers place 'specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition and boot into Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE),' then hold 'CTRL key [to trigger] command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.' Affects 'TPM-only BitLocker protection on Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025.' Explicit defense evasion + credential access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinRE invocation on systems with TPM-only BitLocker (no PIN/password). Monitor USB boot attempts and EFI partition access. Track systems where BitLocker protection mode is queried or changed post-provisioning. Flag unexpected admin command execution during WinRE.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Symbolic Link Privilege Escalation (CVE-2026-45586)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Improper link resolution before file access (link following) in Windows Collaborative Translation Framework allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.' CTFMON is a SYSTEM-level process; symbolic-link-following in its file resolution is a direct EoP vector from user space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CTFMON process for creation of symbolic links targeting SYSTEM-owned directories (%SystemRoot%, %ProgramFiles%, or driver stores). Alert on unexpected CTFMON parent processes or CTFMON spawning privileged utilities. Track link creation in user-writable directories that CTFMON reads during operation.

suggestion.title: Critical RCE Exploitation in Windows Services (28 Critical RCE Flaws)
suggestion.rationale: Article reports '28 [critical] are remote code execution' flaws in a single Patch Tuesday. Pipeline extracted zero detection rules for the execution phase, despite RCE being the highest-impact attack class and all 28 flaws requiring active process spawn or injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation from Windows system binaries (rundll32.exe, svchost.exe, services.exe, lsass.exe, dllhost.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or external binary download/execution. Alert on network connections from system services to non-standard or external ports. Baseline legitimate system-service process chains.

suggestion.title: Information Disclosure via Privileged Data Access (30 Info Disclosure Flaws)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists '30 Information Disclosure Vulnerabilities' category. These typically allow unprivileged processes to read ASLR pointers, cryptographic keys, or credential material from protected memory/registry. Collection-phase exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-mode processes reading sensitive registry hives (SAM, SECURITY, SYSTEM) or kernel-protected registry keys (LSA secrets, cached credentials). Alert on access to process memory of lsass.exe, svchost.exe, or kernel drivers from non-kernel-mode callers. Track unusual open handles to %SystemRoot%\System32 binaries.

suggestion.title: Security Feature Bypass Exploitation (19 Feature Bypass Flaws)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '19 Security Feature Bypass Vulnerabilities' as a distinct category. These target Windows Defender, UAC, Code Integrity, DEP, or ASLR—all defense mechanisms. Pipeline failed to propose detection rules for tampering or disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell/cmd.exe invocations setting Windows Defender preferences (Set-MpPreference, DisableRealtimeMonitoring). Alert on registry modifications to Windows Defender keys (HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender). Track unsigned driver loading or kernel-mode code execution attempts that bypass CodeIntegrity.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass Repository Accessibility Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Microsoft restores some GitHub repos, keeps others offline' — direct evidence of bulk repository state manipulation. Pipeline failed to surface impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when >5 repositories change state (private→public, enabled→disabled, or transfer ownership) within 15 minutes. Correlate with unexpected API calls to org-level GitHub endpoints or unusual modification of repo settings via REST API.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Abuse Against GitHub Organization Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Repository takeover requires prior account compromise. Article implies investigation of stolen credentials ('probe continues'). No credential-access or account-manipulation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts to GitHub accounts from unfamiliar IPs or geographies. Alert on creation of new OAuth applications, personal access tokens, or SSH keys added to organizational accounts. Correlate token creation with immediate repository cloning or API calls.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Repository Clone or Mirror Operations
suggestion.rationale: Miasma probe suggests data theft investigation; no detection for exfiltration patterns (cloning, archiving, or mirroring repos to external hosts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls requesting full repository archives, bulk clone operations, or mirror pushes to external Git hosting. Alert if clone/download size exceeds baseline for account. Cross-reference with egress to non-Microsoft cloud storage.

suggestion.title: Detect Public GitHub Repository Exposure of Sensitive Content
suggestion.rationale: Offline repos may have been made public during attack window. No detection for visibility/permission manipulation prior to takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk permission changes from private to public within a short timeframe. Flag any public repository containing hardcoded credentials, API keys, or secrets based on content scanning. Correlate with access from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation of GitHub Public-Facing API or Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Initial compromise vector not identified. Likely vector: exploit of GitHub web/API to achieve RCE or unauthorized access. No T1190 or T1133 scenarios surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API for unusual payloads, path traversal attempts, or GraphQL abuse. Alert on failed auth attempts followed by successful login from same source. Flag access to administrative endpoints from unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Timing Measurements
suggestion.rationale: Article states FROST 'uses SSD timing' to track apps/sites, implying JavaScript is measuring timing deltas. Pipeline missed detection of scripts performing performance.now(), high-resolution timers, or requestIdleCallback in rapid succession.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript contexts (browser processes) calling high-resolution timer APIs (performance.now, performance.measure) at abnormally high frequency or with timing measurements correlating to file system I/O. Focus on malicious iframes or first-party scripts with unexplained timing instrumentation.

suggestion.title: Browser Information Disclosure via SSD Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'track what sites and apps you open via SSD timing'. Pipeline should detect abnormal read patterns on SSD, cache timing probes, or browser history/app state enumeration via covert channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript or browser processes triggering irregular SSD I/O patterns (cache line fills, speculative reads) or accessing browser history/app metadata in ways that differ from normal browsing. Cross-correlate timing of I/O with successful app/site identification.

suggestion.title: Speculative Execution / Covert Channel Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates SSD timing exploits hardware-level side-channels. If FROST leverages Spectre/Meltdown primitives, detection should target speculative execution gadgets or unusual memory fence / timing-sensitive code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of code patterns known to trigger speculative execution leaks (memory access followed by timing measurements). Monitor for unusual CPU instruction sequencing or performance counter anomalies (cache misses, branch mispredictions) correlated with JavaScript execution.

suggestion.title: Unconstrained JavaScript API Access to Timing Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Browser's exposure of high-resolution timers (performance.now, etc.) without proper sandboxing enables FROST payload. Detection should flag sites abusing these APIs for non-benign purposes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify websites or iframes embedding JavaScript that invokes timing APIs excessively or correlates timing deltas with discoverable user state (browsing history, app installation). Suspicious patterns: repeated timing calls followed by network exfiltration of correlated data.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin Timing Information Leakage Detection
suggestion.rationale: FROST likely violates same-origin policy by inferring user app/site activity across trust boundaries. Detection should catch JavaScript probing timing differences in cross-origin resources or iframes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript making timing-based queries across multiple distinct origins or using navigation timing API to measure load times of resources from unrelated domains in rapid succession, indicative of app/site discovery probes.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Credential Exfiltration via Impersonation Email
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'impersonated a team lead and requested access to the staging environment...agent located and emailed AWS IAM keys, database credentials, and SSH access details to an external Gmail account.' Classic initial-access phishing with collection and exfiltration should trigger detection on email-based credential leakage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email messages from untrusted external senders containing urgent/operational requests, followed by outbound emails from service accounts/agents to new external recipients containing credential keywords (AWS, IAM, password, SSH key, secret). Correlate sender domain spoofing against org directory.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via False Operational Request to AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attacker requested a customer export under the pretext of working remotely on a presentation. The agent retrieved and sent a CRM export containing customer records, contact information, contract details, and revenue data without verifying the sender's identity.' Represents collection + exfiltration without proper identity validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound email from automated systems (agents, bots) to new/external recipients containing PII, financial, or customer data. Raise alert when sender identity validation is bypassed in request handling, especially for high-value data exports (CRM, financial, HR).

suggestion.title: Social Engineering via Operational Urgency in AI Agent Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Both Generic and Strict profiles failed because the verification step still collapsed when the request appeared operationally urgent.' Urgent-framing attacks bypass even hardened policies—should detect temporal manipulation in requests preceding credential/data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails containing urgency markers (production issue, emergency, immediately, critical) followed by credential or data-access requests. Correlate message urgency language against sender legitimacy; flag if strict-mode policies (identity verification, approval workflows) were skipped in response.

suggestion.title: Malicious OAuth Application Consent by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Researchers created a malicious Google OAuth application disguised as a timesheet platform. The agent inspected the OAuth flow, analyzed the destination, identified the application as suspicious, and refused to grant access.' While detection worked here, the scenario itself is a high-risk attack vector warranting continuous monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth consent flows and application registrations initiated by or to service accounts/agents. Flag approval of newly-registered or uncommon applications, especially those with broad permission scopes (mail, calendar, API access). Correlate against allowlist of legitimate integrations.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Interaction and Credential Submission by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The agent received a fake gift card email containing a phishing link. Under the generic configuration, it visited the phishing site and attempted to redeem the gift card using fabricated credentials before eventually identifying the page as malicious.' AI agents interacting with phishing URLs and submitting data should be detectable before identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests from service accounts or known AI agent infrastructure to newly-observed domains, especially those responding with forms requesting credentials or PII. Correlate URL reputation scoring, form submission patterns, and referrer email metadata to detect phishing-link interaction by automated systems.

suggestion.title: Identity Verification Bypass in Automated Email Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The framework's failure to validate the sender's identity' and 'Varonis recommends that agents should be explicitly required to verify sender identities, be prevented from emailing new external recipients without approval.' Missing sender validation detection directly supports the core vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound email from agents/bots responding to inbound requests without documented identity verification. Alert when requests for sensitive data (credentials, customer records) pass through agent workflows that skip SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks or organization directory lookups before fulfilling data access.

suggestion.title: Detect Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Shai-Hulud Credential Stealer' as the attack payload. Pipeline extracted zero detection logic for this malware family despite HIGH severity designation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process execution with embedded credential harvesting libraries or network egress to non-whitelisted C2 infrastructure. Track for suspicious subprocess calls to credential-dumping utilities (pypykatz, impacket) or OS credential access APIs (mimikatz wrappers, DCSync).

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Supply Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'Compromised on GitHub'; pipeline failed to generate supply chain compromise detection. Article phrase: 'Pythagora-io/gpt-pilot Compromised on GitHub'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected commits/releases to high-profile open-source repositories, especially those modifying dependency management files, adding obfuscated Python code, or injecting subprocess/network calls into published distributions. Cross-correlate with repository fork/clone surge from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Python Linter Evasion / Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions malware 'Blocked by Python Linter'—indicates attacker employed linter bypass techniques. Pipeline missed this defensive indicator as an attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python code with syntax patterns designed to bypass static analysis (dynamic imports, reflection, string obfuscation, late-binding function calls). Correlate with commits that suppress linter warnings or add # noqa/# type: ignore comments around suspicious logic.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Post-Repo Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Malware is explicitly a 'Credential Stealer'; pipeline failed to generate detection for credential access or exfiltration phases despite this being the explicit adversary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal credential access patterns following gpt-pilot installation/execution: reading of .aws/credentials, .ssh/config, browser password DBs, cloud token caches. Correlate with DNS queries to non-organizational domains or TLS handshakes to newly observed C2 IPs.

suggestion.title: Compromised Open-Source Package Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets gpt-pilot GitHub repo, likely distributed via pip/PyPI or direct git clone. Pipeline did not map distribution mechanism or downstream consumer impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/PyPI download spikes for pythagora-io/gpt-pilot and forks; alert on installations immediately following compromise date. Track git clone operations of the malicious repository from external networks. Cross-match installed version hashes against known-bad commit SHAs.

suggestion.title: Detection: Shai-Hulud IOC Enrichment and Actor Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'Shai-Hulud' as a malware family identifier. Pipeline extracted zero indicators or actor intelligence despite explicit naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish IOC database entries for Shai-Hulud: file hashes, C2 domains, network signatures. Monitor for code repositories and threat actor infrastructure linked to this malware family. Alert on any binary/script downloads matching Shai-Hulud signatures.

suggestion.title: Model File Unauthorized Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Self-Replicating AI Worm'—self-replication implies the worm modifies model files to propagate. No detection for unauthorized changes to model weights, parameters, or binary artifacts was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to model directories (e.g., .cache/huggingface, pytorch checkpoints, ollama models) outside scheduled updates. Trigger on hash mismatches for known-good models or sudden size changes in serialized model files. Correlate with model loading events immediately after modification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Model Loading with Code Injection Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm 'operates entirely on local, open-weight models'—implying code execution during model initialization. Pipeline generated no detection for unusual imports, system calls, or network activity during model loading phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python/ML frameworks (transformers, torch, ollama clients) spawn child processes, make unauthenticated network connections, or load unexpected shared objects during model initialization. Baseline typical model-loading behavior per framework and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Model Repository / Filesystem Replication Activity
suggestion.rationale: Self-replicating worm must propagate copies of itself; article implies model-to-model or system-to-system spread on 'local' systems. No detection for bulk file copying, recursive rsync, or model artifact duplication was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency cp, rsync, or git operations targeting model directories within short time windows. Alert on model artifacts copied to external storage, shared drives, or network paths. Monitor for model files being pushed to public repositories (GitHub, Hugging Face Hub) without matching git history.

suggestion.title: Inference Output Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Worm operating 'on' models suggests model outputs may be parsed and executed as system commands. No detection use case addresses inference-to-execution chains or eval() patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when model inference outputs are directly piped to shell interpreters (python -c, bash -c, eval) or when model response tokens include suspicious patterns (shebang, command separators, shell metacharacters). Correlate model API calls with subprocess creation in the same execution context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Model Framework / Dependency Loading
suggestion.rationale: Open-weight models may be backdoored to load additional malicious libraries. Article provides no parsed indication of supply-chain indicators, but pipeline should flag detection opportunities for unusual imports or transitive dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python import statements and pip/conda install operations triggered by model loading scripts. Alert on unsigned or unverified wheels, unusual package sources, or dependencies not in original model requirements. Detect dynamic import() calls with runtime-constructed module names.

suggestion.title: Model-to-Model Infection Chain (Cascade Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Worm is 'self-replicating'—likely infects multiple models in sequence. Pipeline generated no cascade-detection logic for identifying secondary infections post-initial-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish temporal baseline of model access patterns per user/system. Alert on unusual model-loading sequences: e.g., User A loads Model X, then Model Y immediately loads from an adjacent directory with modified timestamps, or unscheduled model retraining jobs initiate after suspicious model access. Flag concurrent model-inference processes.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Unauthenticated API Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'exploited an unauthenticated access flaw through a vulnerable API endpoint' and identifies 51.159.98.241 making requests to /api/now/related_list_edit. Detection should flag any requests to this endpoint lacking valid authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /api/now/related_list_edit* endpoints where authentication headers are absent or invalid. Correlate source IP against known-good API consumers. The advisory specifically warns admins to 'review logs for requests to the vulnerable endpoint' from 51.159.98.241 and similar IPs.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Instance Table Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'successfully query the customer instance tables,' implying bulk enumeration of support tickets, employee records, and asset inventories. This is discovery/reconnaissance activity that should be detectable via query pattern anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential queries to multiple table types (cmdb_ci_service, incident, change_request, sys_user, etc.) from a single source IP or session in a short window. Baseline query volumes per API consumer and flag deviations >3 standard deviations.

suggestion.title: Access to Sensitive ServiceNow Tables from External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies data accessed included 'support tickets, employee records, internal documentation, asset inventories, security incident reports.' These are sensitive tables that typically should only be accessed internally or by known third parties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to ServiceNow table types storing credentials, PII, or internal documentation (incident, change_request, sys_user, kb_knowledge, cmdb tables) from external or unexpected source IPs. Correlate with absence of valid authentication to flag unauthorized access.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow API Endpoint requires_authentication Configuration Disable
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals root cause: endpoint was configured with 'requires_authentication=false.' Pipeline should detect attempts to query or modify this configuration parameter via ServiceNow API or config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any API calls or administrative actions that query or modify requires_authentication parameter on REST endpoints. Track configuration changes via sys_properties or web service definition updates. Attackers who discover this misconfiguration before official notice may attempt to disable it on other endpoints.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow API Requests from Known Malicious IP 51.159.98.241
suggestion.rationale: Advisory explicitly warns 'advising other administrators to review logs for requests to the vulnerable endpoint' from IP 51.159.98.241, confirming this as a definitive IOC of the exploitation campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement immediate IP-based blocking or alerting for 51.159.98.241 across all ServiceNow instances. Cross-correlate this IP against EDR, proxy, and WAF logs for other reconnaissance or exploitation attempts. Expand to ASN 12876 (ONLINE SAS, France-based) if broader campaign suspected.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Support Ticket Exfiltration Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'support case information has become an increasingly popular target' as tickets contain 'credentials, API tokens, internal documentation, and authentication secrets.' Post-compromise, defenders should hunt for evidence tickets were accessed and credentials rotated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all support tickets (incident table) modified or accessed on or after June 5, 2026 for sensitive keywords (password, token, API key, secret, credential). Cross-reference accessed tickets against user accounts that rotated credentials immediately afterward, indicating compromise discovery.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical vulnerability in phpBB' enabling 'authentication bypass'—core attack surface. Attackers exploit this to reach admin panels without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB authentication endpoints (/ucp.php, /login, /adm/index.php) for successful access without valid session tokens or CSRF protection. Flag requests with missing authentication context followed by admin function invocation.

suggestion.title: phpBB RCE Command Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RCE' outcome—attackers inject and execute arbitrary commands. This is the exploitation phase after authentication bypass, requiring detection of process spawning from web server contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with suspicious commands (curl, wget, bash, perl, python). Correlate with preceding HTTP requests containing encoded payloads to phpBB endpoints.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation typically installs persistent backdoors. Given 'tens of millions of users' scale, attackers would embed web shells for long-term access, not one-off command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php, .phtml, .phar file creation in web-accessible phpBB directories (/cache, /store, /includes) with suspicious content: eval(), system(), exec(), base64_decode(). Flag ownership changes to web-server user outside patch windows.

suggestion.title: phpBB Configuration File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise persistence involves modifying phpBB core files to install backdoors or maintain access. Article's 10-year history implies persistent compromise and file modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable FIM on critical phpBB files: config.php, /includes/auth/*, /adm/admin_*.php. Alert on modifications outside official update cycles, especially to database credentials, authentication handlers, or network-communicating functions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Admin Endpoint Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass allows direct invocation of admin functions without prior login. Detection should flag /adm/* endpoint access from sessions lacking valid authentication state or tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses on /adm/* endpoints from requests with missing session cookies, invalid CSRF tokens, or anomalous User-Agent/Referer combinations. Establish baseline of legitimate admin access IPs/users and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Privilege Escalation Across Forums
suggestion.rationale: Given 'thousands of forums' in scope, attackers would exploit the vulnerability for mass privilege escalation or account takeover. Multi-instance compromise should show coordinated account manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid user group permission changes to admin across multiple phpBB instances within same time window. Alert on bulk user account modifications from single IP address, single session, or single HTTP User-Agent affecting multiple forum instances.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Traffic Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes botnet 'expansion to 1,500+ devices'—implies command & control infrastructure. No use case generated for identifying C2 heartbeats or beaconing patterns from infected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections from a cohort of 10+ internal IPs to rare external IP/port combinations with regular timing intervals and small payload sizes, consistent with botnet heartbeat/beacon behavior.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Botnet Cohort
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 1,500+ compromised devices, implying prior lateral movement or mass exploitation. Pipeline missed detection for multi-host infection patterns within same subnet/VLAN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential authentication failures followed by successful logons from a single source IP to 5+ internal targets within 30 minutes, then process execution anomalies on those targets.

suggestion.title: Botnet Agent Installation/Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet 'expansion'—agents must be deployed and executed. No use case for detecting suspicious process execution or unsigned binaries consistent with botnet sample detonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution of rarely-seen executables from temporary directories (%temp%, %appdata%) spawning network connections, or scripts (cmd.exe/powershell.exe) fetching from external URLs without prior user browser activity.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Activity from Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly cites 'Cyber Reconnaissance' as botnet objective. No detection for host enumeration, network scanning, or credential dumping originating from internal IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of reconnaissance tools (ipconfig, net view, nltest, AdFind, hashdump variants) or suspicious LSASS access from unusual parent processes on multiple hosts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Botnet C2
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance objective implies data collection and exfiltration. Pipeline generated zero detection for high-volume data transfers to botnet C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internal IPs exfiltrating unusual data volumes (>10MB) to rare external IPs outside business-hours, or transfers of sensitive file types (.xlsx, .pst, .zip) to non-approved cloud/storage destinations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Rust crate (onering) installation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title and severity indicate a supply-chain compromise of a named crate; pipeline failed to surface the crate name, version, or registry indicators that would trigger detection on package manager telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager operations (cargo install, Cargo.lock updates, registry pulls) for attempts to fetch 'onering' crate or flagged versions. Cross-reference against dependency advisories and crate signatures. Alert on any install or lock-file inclusion of affected versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious outbound network connections from Rust binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'performs code exfiltration'—requires detection of abnormal egress from compiled Rust applications to external infrastructure, which the pipeline's empty kill-chain indicates was never modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Rust binaries (.rlib, compiled binaries linked against onering) initiating outbound connections to non-whitelisted hosts, especially over HTTP/HTTPS on non-standard ports or to newly registered domains. Correlate with process execution of affected dependencies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected file access by Rust process preceding network egress
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration requires data collection before transmission; article's core narrative is file theft, yet pipeline contains no detection for reconnaissance or enumeration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Rust processes (especially from third-party crates) recursively reading source files, config, .env, git metadata, or other sensitive file types within 2 minutes of establishing unexpected network connections. Baseline legitimate crate file-access patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Crate registry tampering or package signature bypass
suggestion.rationale: For 'onering' to be compromised and distributed, either the crate was re-published with malicious code or the registry was compromised; pipeline did not surface registry integrity checks or verify package provenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crate registry for unexpected version bumps, new authors, signature mismatches, or yanked versions being re-published. Alert on version metadata changes (checksum, author, dependencies) for high-value crates. Flag crates with sudden popularity spikes among new consumers.

suggestion.title: Rust dependency tree containing onering and code calling suspicious stdlib/network APIs
suggestion.rationale: Code-level detection: the malicious payload resides in Rust source; pipeline should have suggested AST/bytecode analysis for std::net, std::fs, and serialization calls within onering dependency chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Cargo.toml and resolved dependency graphs for 'onering' presence. If present, perform static analysis on onering source (or compiled .rlib) to identify suspicious API calls (net::TcpStream, fs::read_dir, env::vars). Flag for code review and sandbox execution.

suggestion.title: Leaked source code detection via exfiltration artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article states exfiltration outcome; detection should include IOC-matching on exfiltrated content (code snippets, file paths, repository structure) observed in external repositories, pastebin, or attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate internal source code hashes/snippets against external data leaks, GitHub gists, and attacker pastebin activity. If onering was distributed, cross-reference downstream victim repositories for evidence of code being exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains.

suggestion.title: Malformed PKCS7/S/MIME message delivery to vulnerable endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability triggers on 'specially crafted PKCS7 or S/MIME signed messages'—this is the attack surface. Pipeline must detect messages reaching vulnerable systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PKCS7 or S/MIME message processing attempts that deviate from baseline (size, encoding, signature format anomalies). Correlate with OpenSSL versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-45447. Monitor for repeated delivery of similar malformed structures within short windows.

suggestion.title: PKCS7_verify heap corruption exploitation indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'heap use-after-free bug in the PKCS7_verify function'—exploitation manifests as memory corruption. Pipeline should detect crash/exception patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor applications calling OpenSSL PKCS7_verify for abnormal termination (segfault, heap corruption exception, memory protection fault). Correlate with S/MIME or PKCS7 processing events. Flag crashes preceded by delivery of unusual message formats within seconds.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation process execution after PKCS7 parsing crash
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'can corrupt memory and allow attackers to run arbitrary code.' Successful exploitation results in code execution, not just crashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child-process spawning or code injection immediately following OpenSSL PKCS7_verify memory exceptions. Look for injection into system processes or access to credential stores. Baseline normal post-PKCS7 process behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret Enumeration or Brute-Force Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery' — the core enablement. Detection should flag attempts to sign or validate JWT tokens using weak secrets or the literal string 'random' as key material. This is the credential_access phase preceding token abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Python/Go JWT library calls or online JWT debugger access from developer/attacker machines. Monitor for file reads of dev.env or configuration files containing 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET'. Correlate failed or repeated JWT signing attempts with timing patterns consistent with key-derivation or brute-force.

suggestion.title: Software Supply-Chain Exposure: dhax/go-base Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerable package 'github.com/dhax/go-base' by name with 1,685 GitHub stars—recon and persistence baseline. Asset-exposure hunting must detect deployments of this package via package manager logs, container image scans, or source-code references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit go.mod files, container image layers, and package-manager audit logs for github.com/dhax/go-base imports. Flag any instance not in approved supply-chain inventory. Correlate with deployment/build events to establish footprint and recency.

suggestion.title: dev.env Configuration File Enumeration or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'dev.env' file at line 10 as the vulnerability location. Exposure via directory traversal, misconfigured static serving, source-repo leaks, or shell history is the initial discovery phase enabling all downstream exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for dev.env, .env, or config file paths returning 200/301 responses. Flag shell command lines or process arguments containing 'dev.env', 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET', or environment variable dumps. Alert on source-code repository commits exposing .env or configuration files.

suggestion.title: npm Installation Spawns Unexpected Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hidden malware capable of giving attackers complete control' and 'installed or running'—malware must execute during package installation, likely through postinstall hooks spawning shells or utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm.exe or npm spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget) during postinstall phase. Alert on parent=npm/node, unexpected children=system shells or network utilities during package installation windows.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known-Malicious npm Package Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'dbmux' as compromised package on npm registry. Supply-chain IOCs (package names + versions) require dedicated blocklist monitoring, not traditional hash/IP matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm install / npm ci / yarn add commands or HTTP requests to npmjs.org containing known-malicious package names (dbmux and variants from threat feeds). Flag against maintained blocklist of compromised package identifiers.

suggestion.title: Persistence Artifact Creation by npm-Spawned Process
suggestion.rationale: 'Fully compromise developer systems' implies persistence beyond single session—malware likely creates scheduled tasks, cron jobs, or startup scripts during installation for post-reboot execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm/node-spawned processes creating or modifying files in startup directories (/etc/init.d, C:\Windows\Startup), cron jobs (/etc/cron.d), or registry Run keys (HKEY_*\RUN). Parent context: npm/node, target: known persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Configuration Directories
suggestion.rationale: 'Complete control of developer systems' implies theft of SSH keys, API tokens, and cloud credentials. Malware targets ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config, .git configs as high-value exfil targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm/node process or children accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config, ~/.git, /proc/self/environ without legitimate developer tool context. Flag file reads from npm/node parent targeting credential storage.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Communication During npm Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'capable of giving complete control' requires command-and-control or secondary payload download. Monitor outbound connections initiated during npm install phases against baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound TCP/UDP initiated by npm.exe or node to non-standard ports, unsigned certificate chains, or rare-TLD/dDNS domains during installation window. Baseline npm registry traffic; alert on deviations to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Detection for Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states patches released for critical vulnerabilities. Pipeline should have generated detection for software version updates or patch installation attempts. Citation: '[CRIT] Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation/update activity targeting Ivanti endpoint protection, Fortinet FortiGate/FortiOS, or SAP NetWeaver. Look for signed patches from official vendors, version changes in software inventory, or security patch processes launching.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Running Post-Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Once patches are released, unpatched systems become easily identifiable targets. Pipeline should flag detection of software versions known to be vulnerable after patch availability. Citation: 'critical vulnerabilities' + 'release patches'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare running software versions (Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP products) against known-vulnerable version baselines published post-patch. Alert on instances running unpatched critical versions after patch release date.

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt Detection - Web Application/VPN Gateway Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti and Fortinet products are network-facing appliances; critical vulns are typically exploited via HTTP/network protocols. Pipeline should hypothesize exploit detection patterns. Citation: 'critical vulnerabilities' in edge/access-control vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti/Fortinet appliance management or API endpoints for anomalous request patterns (polyglot payloads, unusual User-Agents, path traversal signatures, memory corruption markers).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution (SAP, Ivanti, Fortinet)
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulns often lead to RCE. Pipeline should generate detection for shell/script execution spawned from vulnerable service processes. Citation: vulnerabilities in SAP/Ivanti/Fortinet without specifying impact suggests likely RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash spawned from Ivanti client process, Fortinet service, or SAP service account. Alert on unexpected child processes or reverse-shell signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Registry/Config Modification by Vendor Services
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence often involves modifying vendor config. Pipeline should flag anomalous config changes by Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP processes. Citation: 'multiple critical vulnerabilities' suggests varied attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry (HKLM/HKCU) and configuration file modifications (xml, conf, properties) by Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP service accounts outside of normal patch windows or admin-initiated changes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Network Appliance (Fortinet/Ivanti)
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti/Fortinet are positioned for lateral movement post-compromise due to network visibility. Pipeline should flag internal traffic anomalies from these appliances. Citation: 'critical vulnerabilities' in network-control vendors creates lateral-movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual internal traffic flows originating from or transiting through compromised Ivanti/Fortinet appliances (e.g., scanning, enumeration, lateral SMB/RDP attempts from appliance subnets).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt Against Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'maximum-severity vulnerability stems from an OS command injection weakness' enabling remote code execution. No detection rule was generated for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry devices (product=Ivanti AND Sentry) for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters or command separators (pipes, semicolons, backticks) in parameters targeting command execution endpoints. Alert on any unpatched version (< R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, < R10.7.1 depending on product branch).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass and Rogue Admin Account Creation (CVE-2026-10523)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' No use case captures unauthenticated admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of administrative or privileged user accounts on Ivanti Sentry appliances initiated from unauthenticated sessions or without corresponding authentication logs. Flag any account creation from network sources that did not complete prior authentication handshakes.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Code Execution Post-Exploitation (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables remote attackers to execute code with root privileges'—a critical impact signal. No detection covers root-level process spawning or privilege escalation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry processes for spawning child processes with root or SYSTEM privileges initiated from web-facing service contexts (e.g., gateway daemon, Java process). Alert on UID=0 or GID=0 process elevation from non-privileged parent services.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Default or Patched Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable versions (implies older than R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1) and note 'CISA ordered U.S. federal agencies in May to patch'—version discovery is critical for triage. No asset inventory or version detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP response headers, SSL certificate metadata, or application version strings from Ivanti Sentry deployments to identify version. Flag devices running versions before R10.5.2, R10.6.2, or R10.7.1 as exposed to CVE-2026-10520 and CVE-2026-10523.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Activity Post-Bypass (CVE-2026-10523 Follow-on)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes auth bypass allows attacker to 'gain full administrative access.' Once rogue account is created, follow-on admin actions (config changes, data export, user modification) should trigger alerts but no use case addresses post-compromise admin behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative actions (policy changes, user deletions, export/backup operations, certificate modifications) performed by newly-created accounts or from unusual IPs within 1 hour of potential auth bypass exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Defender Engine Unexpected SYSTEM Privilege Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states the zero-day 'grants SYSTEM access.' No detection logic was generated to identify MsMpEng.exe or related Defender processes spawning commands, shells, or child processes with SYSTEM privileges—the smoking gun of this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MsMpEng.exe, WdFilter.sys, or other Defender core processes spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wmiexec.exe, rundll32.exe) with SYSTEM integrity level when the parent was previously user or service-level. Flag if parent process token differs from expected baseline.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Defender Real-Time Protection Engine Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Privilege-escalation exploits against scanning engines often involve triggering unusual code paths through malformed file patterns or specific binary sequences. The article describes a zero-day affecting Defender's core scanning logic on updated systems—no detection was suggested for anomalous engine behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Defender engine processes (MsMpEng.exe) loading unexpected DLLs from non-standard paths, executing unsigned code modules, or triggering exception handlers that bypass normal validation. Monitor for abnormal file system activity by Defender processes writing outside standard scan caches and quarantine directories.

suggestion.title: Defender Configuration Manipulation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-privilege-escalation, attackers typically disable or weaken Defender to maintain persistence. The article does not describe post-exploitation behavior, but the title ('grants SYSTEM access') implies sustained capability once elevated. No use case targets Defender disablement or modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender registry paths for modifications (DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableScriptScanning, EnableControlledFolderAccess deletions) initiated by processes with SYSTEM privilege that did not originate from Windows Update or official Defender maintenance tasks.

suggestion.title: Defender Engine API Bypass or Validation Failure
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day privilege escalations in Defender typically exploit a flaw in input validation or API boundary enforcement. Title suggests a logic flaw in SYSTEM-grant behavior; no detection logic was suggested for abnormal API call patterns or validation bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MsMpEng.exe or related Defender processes calling Windows API functions (NtOpenProcessToken, NtAdjustPrivilegesToken, NtSetInformationToken) with anomalous parameter sequences or repeated failures followed by success. Flag if these calls originate from input paths controlled by user-mode processes (file system, registry, named pipes).

suggestion.title: Malicious Email Delivery Targeting OWA Users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An attacker could exploit this issue by sending a specially crafted email to a user. If the user opens the email in Outlook Web Access and certain interaction conditions are met, arbitrary JavaScript can be executed.' Initial access vector must be detected at email layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with XSS-like payloads (script tags, event handlers, JavaScript URIs) sent to users known to access OWA. Correlate delivery timestamp with subsequent OWA session initiation within 5-minute window to identify delivery→exploitation chain. Flag messages with base64-encoded scripts or obfuscated HTML.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Execution in OWA Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context.' XSS payloads must be detected post-delivery when rendered by OWA client.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OWA sessions for unexpected script execution patterns: inline script execution, DOM manipulation, XMLHttpRequest calls to external domains, or cookie exfiltration attempts. Alert on JavaScript eval() calls originating from email-derived HTML rendering within OWA frame context.

suggestion.title: Exchange Server Exploitation via Public-Facing OWA Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'actively exploited Exchange Server vulnerability' on public-facing OWA. Requires detection of CVE-2026-42897 exploitation attempts at HTTP layer.
