suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Exchange OWA paths (/owa/, /ecp/) for suspicious patterns: oversized headers, script payloads in URL parameters or message body fields, repeated requests to same endpoint with varying payloads. Correlate with Exchange version fingerprinting to identify unpatched targets (2016, 2019, SE prior to June 2026 patches).

suggestion.title: Post-XSS Payload Behavioral Detection in OWA Session
suggestion.rationale: Article implies successful JavaScript execution leads to attacker capability. Detection must focus on post-exploitation actions taken by injected script.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After XSS execution in OWA, detect exfiltration attempts: injected script connecting to attacker C2, stealing session tokens, retrieving email folders, or forwarding messages to external domains. Alert on anomalous data flows from OWA client IP post-compromise (DNS queries to suspicious domains, outbound HTTPS to unknown IPs with high byte counts).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unpatched Exchange Servers Post-CVE-2026-42897 Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'actively exploited' prior to patch release and CISA mandated 2-week patch deadline. Must detect attacks on systems that failed to patch by deadline (May 29, 2026) or patch date detection evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate patch deployment status with mail flow and OWA access logs. Identify unpatched systems (Exchange 2016, 2019, SE versions before June 2026 update) receiving email traffic post-disclosure date. Detect delivery attempts to known vulnerable servers; escalate if subsequent OWA access occurs, indicating potential breach window exploitation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Attachment or Link Interaction in OWA Session
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires user interaction: 'certain interaction conditions are met' after opening email. Detection gap between delivery and exploitation interaction point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In OWA sessions, detect unusual user interaction patterns post-email delivery: rapid hover/click sequences on email body HTML, scroll/expand actions on suspicious message content, interaction with inline images or links immediately after phishing email receipt. Correlate with browser developer console access or iframe loading attempts within OWA DOM.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts Against Microsoft RCE Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Critical RCE Bugs.' This is the primary post-disclosure attack vector; pipeline failed to generate any execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process creation (PowerShell, cmd.exe) spawned from unusual parents or following SMB/RDP/WinRM network events. Correlate timing with patch announcement date and filter on unpatched system build versions to detect active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation Post-RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Microsoft patch release of 206 flaws likely includes privilege-escalation vectors. Pipeline generated zero privilege-escalation-phase detections despite high probability given vulnerability scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation anomalies (service spawning cmd/PowerShell, 4688 token elevation) with prior RCE indicators. Flag svchost/services parent-child relationships deviating from baseline behavior within 30 minutes of exploitation detection.

suggestion.title: Detect Unpatched System Inventory for Patch Window Risk Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'record 206 flaws' scope. Pipeline must identify systems not applying patches within patch window to drive remediation and isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query SCCM/Intune patch compliance by KB article or CVE within 72 hours post-announcement. Cross-reference unpatched systems with network exposure (internet-facing, external DNS resolution, listening ports 445/3389).

suggestion.title: Detect Vulnerability Scanner Reconnaissance Activity Post-Patch Announcement
suggestion.rationale: Patch announcements trigger immediate automated scanner activity. Article scope (206 flaws) guarantees scanner spike. Pipeline omitted early-warning scanner-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rapid sequential connections to Windows service ports (445, 3389, 5985, 139) from single/clustered IP range within 4 hours of patch announcement. Cross-reference source IPs with known scanner ASNs (Shodan, Censys, ZoomEye).

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Post-RCE Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RCE bugs enable foothold; article severity ('Critical') indicates post-exploitation pivoting likelihood. Pipeline failed to generate lateral-movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE-exploitation detection, monitor for anomalous Kerberos service tickets from RCE-compromised system, SMB/WinRM lateral-movement attempts, LSASS memory access (MiniDump/procdump), and credential-dumping tool execution.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Unauthorized Instance Table Query
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access controls that may enable attackers to execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication.' This is the primary attack vector; detection is completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag queries to backend instance tables (users, credentials, incidents) from unauthenticated sessions or contexts lacking required role permissions. Baseline normal query volume per user and alert on anomalous spikes.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a vulnerability in access controls being exploited for unauthorized access. Exploitation patterns should be directly detectable against the specific flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with malformed parameters, authentication bypass payloads, or API calls circumventing standard ServiceNow security filters.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Sensitive Data Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'query customer instance tables without proper authentication'—threat of data exfiltration is inherent. Large-result-set queries need detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on export/download operations or queries returning unusually large row counts from sensitive instance tables (users, passwords, incidents, change requests).

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Access Control Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'improper access controls.' Detection should identify when RBAC is circumvented or authentication is bypassed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for table access attempts that succeed despite failed authentication, or access from unprivileged contexts to tables requiring elevated roles.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Backend Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers can 'query customer instance tables'—implies discovery phase. Enumeration of schema and available tables should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated information_schema or sys_db_object queries, or systematic attempts to list all available tables in a short window.

suggestion.title: Langflow CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation via Unauthenticated API Access
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Unauthenticated RCE exploit'—this is the primary attack vector (Initial Access). No detection UC was proposed despite this being the entry point for attackers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Langflow application endpoints (patterns: /api/*, /flows/*, /nodes/*) from external/untrusted IP sources. Alert on requests containing exploitation signatures (unusual parameters, executable payloads, or known CVE-2026-5027 POC patterns). Baseline normal API request patterns for your Langflow deployments to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from Langflow Application
suggestion.rationale: RCE by definition requires Execution phase detection. Title explicitly references 'Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE' but zero execution-layer detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned by Langflow application parent processes (python.exe, java.exe, langflow.exe), particularly command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh). High-fidelity signal if spawned from network-accessible Langflow process without corresponding user interaction or legitimate feature activation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Langflow Sensitive Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Unauthenticated' vulnerability. No detection for authentication bypass or unauthorized configuration access was proposed despite this being the core attack premise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow application logs for successful access to privileged endpoints (/api/admin, /api/user, /settings, /config) from requests lacking valid authentication tokens or session identifiers. Correlate successful auth-bypass requests with external/untrusted source IPs and short timeframes to detect exploitation campaigns.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Local Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes CVE-2026-45586 as 'a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM'—this is the core attack vector and warrants behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privilege processes (non-System, non-Admin) invoking CTFMON.EXE with unusual parameters or spawning child processes with elevated token. Monitor for process-token elevation attempts on CTFMON parent/child chains, particularly sudden SYSTEM-level child processes from user-mode CTFMON invocations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal CTFMON Process Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CTFMON as 'a valuable post-exploitation primitive'—threat actors will invoke it abnormally post-breach; baseline expected CTFMON behavior (parent process, command-line args, frequency) to detect abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CTFMON.EXE is a keyboard/language input service with limited legitimate launch contexts. Flag CTFMON spawned by user-mode executables (vs. system services), invoked with command-line arguments, or launched outside scheduled startup times. Correlate with low-privilege process lineage.

suggestion.title: Elevation of Privilege Exploit Success Signals (CVE-2026-45586)
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms the vulnerability allows escalation 'from low privileges to SYSTEM'—post-exploitation, token elevation or access-token events should spike around exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed or successful privilege-elevation events (Windows Event ID 4672 'Special privileges assigned to new logon') immediately following CTFMON process invocation. Alert on unexpected SYSTEM-level process creation within 10s of CTFMON execution from a non-privileged parent.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Registry/File Modifications (Exploit Staging)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation use; while exact exploit vector unspecified, privesc exploits commonly modify registry or drop files. Monitor CTFMON-related resources for anomalous write activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected file writes or registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\CTFMON or %LocalAppData%\CTFMON paths when initiated by processes other than the CTFMON service itself. Correlate with low-privilege process execution.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail / Cloud Logging Service Disabled or Trail Deleted
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Abusing Cloud Logging Services'; primary evasion tactic is disabling audit trails. AWS CloudTrail StopLogging, DeleteTrail, and equivalent GCP/Azure operations are core attack moves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, DeleteLogGroup, or UpdateTrail calls that disable logging. Monitor for log delivery failures or delivery role/bucket removal. Correlate with preceding privilege-escalation events targeting logging service roles.

suggestion.title: Log Router Configuration Modified or Log Sink Deleted
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'log router' and 'log storage' as attack surfaces. Attackers may modify sinks to exclude security events or redirect to attacker-controlled destinations rather than delete.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of log sinks that narrow event filters (e.g., exclude IAM, data access, admin activity), redirect logs to non-standard destinations, or change retention policies to minimize or zero retention.

suggestion.title: IAM Role or Service Account Privilege Escalation for Logging Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must escalate or assume permissions before they can 'abuse' logging services. Privilege escalation to roles with cloudtrail:*, logs:*, or logging.admin permissions is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for assumption of logging-admin roles by non-privileged principals, creation of overly-permissive roles targeting logging services, or policy changes that grant logging modification to unexpected identities.

suggestion.title: Log Group or Bucket Deletion Post-Compromise Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'log storage' abuse. Attackers delete archived logs from S3/GCS buckets to remove evidence of lateral movement and exfiltration after disabling live logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate log group deletions (CloudTrail, GCP Logging) with bulk S3/GCS object deletions from same principal in same session. Alert if preceded by logging-service disable or by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Logging API Calls from Anomalous Identity or Network Source
suggestion.rationale: Compromised accounts used to disable logging often originate from unusual IPs, user-agents, or absent MFA validation—attack pivots differ from day-to-day administrative access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline IP ranges, user agents, and MFA-enrollment status for principals authorized to call logging APIs. Alert on StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or UpdateTrail from out-of-baseline sources or from sessions with disabled MFA.

suggestion.title: Cross-Account or Cross-Tenant AssumeRole to Logging Service Principal
suggestion.rationale: Multi-cloud attack scenarios permit lateral movement across accounts/tenants to disable logging in target environments. Unexpected cross-account or cross-org role assumption targeting logging infrastructure is high-confidence evasion signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AssumeRole calls that target logging-service principals (e.g., CloudTrail service role) from accounts or identities outside the organization, or from unexpected service meshes.

suggestion.title: Detect Chrome V8 Process Exploitation via Memory Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates V8 zero-day exploitation but article body is truncated; typical V8 RCE exploits corrupt memory to achieve code execution. Detection should monitor for abnormal Chrome/V8 process behavior that precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chrome.exe or v8.exe process for abnormal memory access patterns, allocation spikes, or unusual child process spawning immediately following webpage load. Correlate with network beacons.

suggestion.title: Detect Browser-Based Exploitation Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation typically requires malicious webpage or attachment; pipeline missed detection for initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to high-risk domains followed by rapid file writes or temporary process creation from browser context. Correlate suspicious .html, .js, or ad-serving domains with downstream execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly documenting active in-the-wild exploitation. Scanner detection is table-stakes baseline. Article: 'CISA KEV only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all assets running Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Opera) with version below patched baseline. Correlate against patch deployment records. Alert any unpatched instance post due-date 2026-06-23. High-confidence exploitation risk indicator.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Child Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox'—successful exploitation spawns unexpected child processes from browser parents. Article phrase: 'remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chromium.exe, chrome.exe, msedge.exe for anomalous children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe). Flag outbound network calls from browser to non-whitelist IPs. Baseline normal behavior per environment to manage FP rate.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML/JavaScript Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is delivery of crafted HTML. Network and email gateways must detect malicious HTML before browser parsing. Article phrase: 'via a crafted HTML page.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-entropy HTML attachments, HTML from untrusted sources, obfuscated JavaScript (replace/eval/constructor patterns). Correlate delivery to users with known vulnerable browser versions. Monitor for drive-by compromise from compromised web servers.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Patch Compliance Validation
suggestion.rationale: Federal due-date 2026-06-23 is binding compliance deadline. Continuous inventory drives remediation validation and audit readiness. Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily query of installed Chrome, Edge, Opera versions across fleet. Alert on any version below patched baseline post due-date. Cross-validate against patch management records. Generate risk-prioritized remediation lists and audit compliance reports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20245 and classifies it as CISA KEV (active wild exploitation). Federal patch deadline 2026-06-23 makes scanner-based asset discovery the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results matching CVE-2026-20245 against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets. Cross-reference patch management to prioritize unpatched systems, especially those exposed to external networks given CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Suspicious File Upload or Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack vector: 'supplying a crafted file to the affected system.' File upload and file processing operations are the exploitation trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager application logs for unusual file uploads, creates, or modifications, particularly files followed by unexpected process spawning or application errors. Baseline expected file types and paths for normal operations to isolate anomalies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from SD-WAN Manager Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability outcome: 'execute arbitrary commands as root.' Detection must capture process creation and command execution originating from SD-WAN Manager in root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation originating from Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager processes (vManage daemons) running as root. Alert on interactive shells, network utilities, or scripting interpreters spawned from the application context, comparing against operational baselines for the application.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root on SD-WAN Manager Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article describes capability progression from 'authenticated' context to 'root' command execution—a privilege escalation. Escalation events on affected systems signal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts (failed or successful) to root on systems running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Correlate with preceding authentication events, file uploads, or application errors to identify multi-step exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Authentication to SD-WAN Manager Followed by File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, local attacker'—valid session establishment precedes exploitation. Authentication anomalies may serve as early-warning indicators before file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed authentication attempts to SD-WAN Manager or successful logins from unexpected sources, especially from external IP ranges or using service accounts not normally used for interactive access. Correlate successful authentications with subsequent file upload anomalies to detect exploitation chains in progress.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerable Asset Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-7473 'is currently being exploited' per CISA KEV criteria, with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-23. No hunt was generated for identifying vulnerable Arista EOS devices, despite article guidance: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and vulnerability name 'Arista Extensible Operating System Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-7473 matched against Arista EOS product. Correlate with asset inventory to enumerate all Arista EOS instances, versions, and patch status. Prioritize remediation of instances with known-vulnerable versions; establish compliance tracking against 2026-06-23 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Tunnel Decapsulation Failures and Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'switch incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP.' This is the actual exploitation symptom. Pipeline generated zero detection for abnormal decapsulation behavior, the technical signature of successful exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS syslog, packet forwarding tables, and tunnel logs for decapsulation failures or processing errors. Alert on packets with destination IPs matching configured decapsulation endpoints arriving from unexpected source interfaces. Baseline normal tunnel egress and alert on traffic exiting via incorrect tunnel interfaces relative to historical routing.

suggestion.title: Inbound Exploitation Attempts Against Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited.' Pipeline generated no detection for T1190 exploitation attempts. This gap covers active scanning and payload delivery phases preceding the decapsulation bug trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP(S), SSH, and SNMP connections to identified Arista EOS management interfaces originating from external or suspicious networks. Correlate with known Arista EOS exploit signatures (malformed payloads, path traversal patterns, rapid consecutive requests). Alert on management-plane access from non-maintenance IP ranges or geolocations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Behavior Anomalies from Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation leads to 'forwards other unexpected tunneled packet,' creating observable network artifacts: misdirected traffic, leaked inter-VLAN flows, packets on wrong egress interfaces. Pipeline generated zero detection for post-exploitation network impact and packet hijacking behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for expected tunnel destinations and egress interfaces for traffic transiting each Arista EOS device. Alert on: traffic egressing from tunnel interfaces to IPs absent from tunnel configuration, unexpected inter-VLAN traffic, packets appearing on historically-incorrect egress ports. Correlate with T1190 detection attempts to trace attack to impact.

suggestion.title: POST parameter 'dir' containing shell metacharacters in pheditor.php requests
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'injecting shell metacharacters into the \'dir\' POST parameter' as the core exploitation vector. Current UC_27_4 ignores body inspection. This detection targets the actual injection point before code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php where the 'dir' parameter value contains unescaped shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $, parentheses, braces). Prioritize by: successful auth indicator + presence of >2 metacharacters + deviation from expected directory path format.

suggestion.title: Process tree burst: single PHP-FPM parent spawning >N children in <T seconds
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE loop: single malicious POST triggers multiple command invocations. Sequential shell spawning from one php-fpm parent is atypical. Detects exploitation phase even if individual shell spawns are whitelisted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >3 process creations from the same PHP-FPM parent within 5 seconds, where children are (sh|bash|curl|wget|nc|python). Excludes benign multiplex patterns (e.g., apache2 graceful restarts). Baseline per host to account for legitimate tooling variance.

suggestion.title: Outbound network from PHP web server process to unexpected ports/destinations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'full Remote Code Execution with web server privileges.' Post-exploitation behavior (reverse shell, data exfiltration, payload download) would involve outbound TCP/UDP. Not covered by current hunts, which stop at webshell creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections (TCP/UDP) initiated by php-fpm, apache2, httpd, or nginx to non-RFC1918 addresses or non-standard web ports (excluding 80/443/8080). High fidelity if destination resolves to VPS/WHOIS abuse registrar.

suggestion.title: Configuration/execution context modification by authenticated pheditor user
suggestion.rationale: Article notes TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist 'completely bypassed.' Attacker may disable logging, alter OPEN_BASEDIR, or modify php.ini via RCE. Defense-evasion opportunity not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of PHP configuration files (php.ini, .htaccess, .user.ini) or Apache/Nginx config by www-data or web-server processes. Also detect attempts to disable/manipulate logs (e.g., `chmod 000 /var/log/*`, redirect stdout to /dev/null in process arguments).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WebSocket connections to phoenix_storybook /playground endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'accepts user-controlled attribute values over WebSocket' and 'unauthenticated user'—the delivery vector is WebSocket traffic to the playground endpoint. No existing UC detects initial access via this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP(S) connections to paths containing `/playground` or `/storybook` endpoints on known Phoenix apps, specifically unauthenticated requests (no session cookies, missing auth headers). Correlate with BEAM process uptime to confirm the endpoint was accessible during the connection window.

suggestion.title: HEEx template compilation errors and anomalies in Erlang supervisor logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'interpolates them unsanitized into a HEEx template that is subsequently compiled'—compilation failures or abnormal template processing errors would occur in BEAM logs. No UC addresses this in-application signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Erlang compiler errors (ErlangError, CompileError) related to HEEx template parsing in application logs. Flag any compilation failures immediately after WebSocket writes to the playground endpoint, indicating injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Storybook playground endpoint access in non-dev/non-staging deployments
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'phoenix_storybook playground'—this is typically a development/staging artifact. Production deployments should not expose storybook endpoints. No UC checks for presence in non-development environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference deployed Phoenix apps tagged as 'production' with those that respond to requests to `/storybook` or `/playground` routes. Flag misconfigurations where development tooling is inadvertently exposed in production.

suggestion.title: Ingress of Elixir/Erlang exploitation tools or hex package fetches post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) but no UC detects tool staging. Post-exploitation, an attacker would fetch tools via Mix/Hex or direct BEAM wget/curl. No UC targets this behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BEAM processes invoking curl, wget, or python to download files immediately following suspicious shell spawning. Also monitor for unexpected Mix package fetches (new entries in mix.lock on disk) during suspicious time windows correlated with RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Erlang distribution port (4369) abuse post-RCE lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: If the compromised BEAM instance is part of a cluster, attacker can exploit Erlang distributed node protocols. Article does not mention clustering, but this is a known post-exploitation path for BEAM RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected connections on port 4369 (Erlang Port Mapper Daemon) from BEAM processes to internal or external IPs. Combine with detection of new node registrations in epmd or unusual Erlang cookie exchanges.

suggestion.title: Exploit delivery via HEEx attribute injection patterns in request payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'user-controlled attribute values' interpolated into HEEx—the attack vector is a specific payload structure. No UC looks for the injection pattern itself in WebSocket frames or HTTP request bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebSocket or HTTP POST payloads to /playground endpoints containing Elixir/HEEx injection patterns: double curly braces with function calls (e.g., `<%= ... %>`), System.* calls, or Kernel.* invocations. Signature-based detection on common payloads like `<%= System.cmd(...) %>`.

suggestion.title: Suspicious setup.py / pyproject.toml Execution During pip Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages were 'poisoned to auto-run' — implies malicious code in setup.py or pyproject.toml (standard Python packaging mechanisms). No UC exists despite this being the attack execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python interpreter spawning unexpected child processes (shell, curl, wget) immediately after pip install or setup.py execution. Flag script interpreters with command-line args containing credential paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, %APPDATA%) or network exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Repository Anomalies and Malicious Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: '19 packages poisoned' on PyPI. Article emphasizes supply-chain compromise, yet pipeline did not flag package name IOCs or detect installation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/poetry/poetry.lock operations against known malicious package name hashes. Cross-reference installed package versions against PyPI metadata signatures. Alert on installation of packages with unexpected code execution patterns in metadata or post-install scripts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Beaconing and Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Bun Credential Stealer' payload. Should detect credential access (reading .bashrc, .aws/credentials, SSH keys) and subsequent C2 exfiltration, yet no use case captures this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file-system access to common credential stores (.bashrc, .aws, .ssh, .kube, .gnupg) from Python processes or child processes spawned by setup.py. Correlate with suspicious DNS queries or HTTP POST/exfil patterns to unknown destinations.

suggestion.title: Unusual Child Process Launch from Python Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack relies on silent code execution during package installation. Pipeline did not capture detection of unexpected shell/system calls spawned from pip or setup.py contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sh/bash/powershell/cmd spawned as children of python, pip, or setup.py processes. Baseline benign package installs; alert on deviations. Correlate process creation with file modifications to sensitive paths or network activity.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Metadata or Post-Install Script Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack auto-runs on package install—likely via entry_points, console_scripts, or post-install hooks in setup.py/pyproject.toml. No UC addresses detection of obfuscated or suspicious metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package metadata and install scripts for obfuscated code, encoded payloads, or suspicious imports (ctypes, subprocess, socket, requests without apparent use). Flag packages where setup.py contains inline shell execution or base64-decoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Network Beaconing from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies C2 communication post-theft. Article does not explicitly mention C2 domains (truncated), but detection for network activity from Python install processes is essential and missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS/DNS requests originating from Python, pip, or child processes spawned during package installation to non-PyPI/non-standard-repo IPs. Correlate with process creation timestamps and file access to credential stores.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt via LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—this is the core threat narrative. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections despite explicit RCE capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteLLM endpoints for suspicious payloads, parameter-injection patterns, or request signatures matching CVE-2026-42271. Alert on responses indicating code execution (shell output, file operations, process spawning) following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Child Process Execution from LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: RCE capability requires runtime detection of actual code execution. Title claims exploitation in the wild but no process-execution detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned by Python or LiteLLM processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, sh) with arguments suggesting command execution, reverse shells, or credential theft.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Signature-Based IDS Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly tags this CVE as exploited in the wild; IDS/WAF signatures and exploitation patterns should be extracted and operationalized. Zero IOC-based detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fire alerts on network traffic matching known CVE-2026-42271 exploitation signatures, suspicious HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints, or anomalous LiteLLM service behavior post-request.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Repository Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply-chain compromise of GitHub Actions workflows. Phrase: 'Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled' indicates mass workflow/action tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for unexpected modifications to workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml), unusual commit messages in CI/CD pipelines, and out-of-band execution of shell commands or script injection (bash -c, PowerShell -Command) within Actions runners that reference external URLs or unfamiliar artifact sources.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Disablement or Workflow Suspension
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled'—bulk repository actions triggered by compromised automation is a strong impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, bulk repository disablement, archival, or workflow suspension events originating from service principals or automation accounts with no corresponding security incident ticket or change control approval. Correlation: same actor disabling 10+ repos in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Artifact or Dependency Injection in CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks targeting AI coding agents (article context) typically poison build artifacts. Phrase: 'Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents' implies artifact tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized uploads to artifact repositories (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven Central) from CI/CD runners, or modifications to package manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml) in workflows. Also monitor for exfiltration of build secrets or GitHub tokens logged in CI/CD output.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to GitHub Actions Secrets or Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of 72 repositories implies credential theft. Worms typically exfiltrate secrets to propagate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows that decode or echo environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS credentials, or Azure credentials to stdout/logs. Flag workflows that export secrets to external domains or invoke curl/wget to exfiltrate credential-bearing environment variables.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Execution with External C2
suggestion.rationale: Miasma worm suggests persistent, self-propagating compromise. Worms typically establish command-and-control for remote orchestration of repository disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-standard ports or known malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate workflow execution with DNS requests for newly registered domains or IPs hosting Miasma samples. Flag workflows that download and execute unsigned binaries from external sources.

suggestion.title: Self-Replicating Worm Distribution via Forked Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Miasma Worm implies self-replicating behavior across multiple repos. Phrase: '72 Other Repositories' suggests horizontal propagation via fork/clone/cross-repo mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for automated fork, clone, or push operations targeting multiple repositories from single CI/CD context. Alert on workflows that enumerate repository manifests, identify other Actions, and inject code into them. Detect repeated 'git push' or 'gh repo' commands in a single workflow execution spanning more than 5 target repos.

suggestion.title: Remote .vhd/.vhdx File Open from SMB Share
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'coerce a victim to open a .vhd(x) in a remote SMB server' triggering vulnerable code path. This is initial access and no detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file opens of .vhd or .vhdx files from UNC paths (\\\\server\\share). Correlate with Microsoft Defender process activity and alert on non-standard tools or user contexts accessing remote virtual disk images, especially post-phishing.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe Spawned with SYSTEM Integrity Level from Defender Processes
suggestion.rationale: Core success criterion stated: 'spawn a command prompt with SYSTEM privileges.' Pipeline missed the privilege escalation outcome indicator despite explicit mention of cmd.exe with SYSTEM rights.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe with SYSTEM integrity level spawned from MpEngineHost.exe, MsMpEng.exe, or NisSrv.exe parents. Monitor for token elevation anomalies where child process integrity exceeds parent—particularly when Defender process is parent.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Overwrites in Defender System Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation mechanism: 'defender overwriting its own files' via race condition. No file-integrity or file-overwrite detection flagged despite explicit description of Defender binary modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, concurrent writes to System32\\drivers\\etc, System32\\Defender, or other Defender directories. Flag succeeded overwrites preceded by failed writes (timing signature of race-condition exploitation). Alert on modifications to mpengine.dll or MsMpEng.exe with unusual access patterns.

suggestion.title: SMB Junction/Symlink Enumeration with Symlink Evaluation Enabled
suggestion.rationale: Alternate attack path stated: 'coerce a victim into opening an SMB share if symlink evaluation settings were enabled.' Discovery and reconnaissance phase for this vector was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SMB tree-connect requests followed by reparse-point or symlink queries on remote shares. Alert when users with symlink evaluation enabled enumerate network shares paired with searches for system-critical or virtual-disk file patterns (.vhd, .sys, drivers).

suggestion.title: mpengine.dll API Invocation Anomalies (SysIO* Targeting)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Microsoft's mitigation: 'patching mpengine!SysIO* API' in mid-May. Pre-patch or bypass-attempt patterns targeting this specific API surface were not extracted as a detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for injection into Defender processes (MpEngineHost.exe) or direct API hooking of mpengine.dll SysIO functions. Alert on processes attempting to manipulate Defender's file-system or SMB-handling code paths through uncommon API sequences.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM (GreenPlasma)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Improper link resolution before file access in Windows Collaborative Translation Framework allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally' and credits GreenPlasma. No detection generated for a disclosed EoP vector granting SYSTEM access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ctfmon.exe spawning child processes or accessing files outside its normal directories. Detect privilege escalation events where ctfmon is the source process. Flag ctfmon creating cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shells with elevated tokens.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Bomb: Uncontrolled Header Consumption via flow-control Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Uncontrolled resource consumption in HTTP/2 allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service' and notes 'Attackers can also keep the memory tied up by manipulating flow-control settings.' Microsoft introduced MaxHeadersCount registry setting, implying abnormal header counts are the exploitable condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP/2 header counts per server role. Alert on sustained HTTP/2 requests exceeding baseline with concurrent high memory consumption in HTTP.sys. Detect registry writes to MaxHeadersCount as indicator of mitigation deployment or post-exploitation remediation.

suggestion.title: WinRE BitLocker Bypass: Physical Access + CTRL Shell Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'placing specially crafted files on a USB drive or EFI partition and booting into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where holding down the CTRL key triggered a command shell with unrestricted access to encrypted BitLocker-protected drives.' Two CVEs (YellowKey, bitskrieg) exploit this exact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WinRE invocation followed by shell creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Detect reagentc.exe execution with /disable or /enable flags, especially in rapid sequence. Flag BitLocker recovery attempts or encrypted volume access outside normal administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver EoP (CVE-2020-17103 / Mini-Plasma)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Mini-Plasma zero-day vulnerability that gives SYSTEM privileges' via Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver. A driver-based privilege escalation vector was disclosed but no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver (CFFDD) being loaded by unexpected processes. Detect processes accessing Cloud Files registry hives or driver control paths before privilege escalation events. Alert on local system privilege escalation where driver interaction precedes token elevation.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch BitLocker Recovery Failure Pattern (bitskrieg Fix Side Effect)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns the fix 'could cause Windows devices to display an error stating, A required file couldn't be accessed because your BitLocker key wasn't loaded correctly.' This is a post-patch state change detectable and baselining-worthy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline BitLocker errors before/after June 2026 patch. Alert on clusters of BitLocker key loading failures post-patch. Distinguish anomalies from known legitimate recovery (reagentc /disable /enable sequence) to identify exploitation vs. misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Registry Hardening: MaxHeadersCount Set (HTTP.sys Mitigation Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Microsoft also introduced a new MaxHeadersCount registry setting...to limit the number of headers included in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests.' Registry write patterns indicate either proactive hardening or reactive defensive response to HTTP/2 Bomb exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MaxHeadersCount registry key creation/modification with unusual values or privilege context. Correlate with HTTP.sys memory exhaustion or exploit attempts. Track deployment timing as indicator of incident response velocity.

suggestion.title: RDP Heap Overflow Exploitation (CVE-2026-42985)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-42985 is a critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerability due to Heap-based buffer overflow in Remote Desktop Client which allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Clear attack vector for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP protocol connections with oversized payload buffers or heap corruption signatures. Detect anomalous RDP session data sizes exceeding normal bounds, particularly in TLS-wrapped connection data following authentication handshake.

suggestion.title: HTTP.sys Integer Overflow via Specially Crafted Packets (CVE-2026-47291)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to a targeted server utilizing the HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) to process packets.' Network-based RCE vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic for malformed headers triggering integer overflows—Content-Length wrapping, oversized transfer-encoding chunks, or protocol violations in http.sys. Look for 5xx server errors in IIS logs immediately preceding process crashes.

suggestion.title: DHCP Client Buffer Overflow via Oversized Responses (CVE-2026-44815)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An authenticated user could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted network traffic to a server configured for use as a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Server.' Lateral movement and execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DHCP responses for oversized or malformed payload structures. Detect DHCP option fields exceeding RFC 2131 bounds, particularly in custom option payloads from attacker-controlled DHCP servers.

suggestion.title: Office Type Confusion in Outlook Email Preview (CVE-2026-45456, CVE-2026-45458, CVE-2026-47635)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'the email rendering in Outlook (classic) utilizes Microsoft Word functionality, where this vulnerability exists' and 'this vulnerability can be exploited when rendering emails in Outlook (classic).' Clear email-based execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Outlook preview pane interactions with malformed email MIME structures containing type-confusion payloads. Correlate Outlook process crashes (exit code exceptions) with specific email rendering events; flag emails with embedded Word content triggering Win32k type mismatches.

suggestion.title: Windows Kernel TCP/IP Use-After-Free via Crafted Network Traffic (CVE-2026-45657)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted network traffic to a vulnerable Windows system' resulting in 'code with system-level privileges.' Network-based kernel code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed TCP/IP packets triggering kernel exception handlers. Detect unusual TCP sequence/acknowledgment patterns, oversized segment reassembly, or IP fragmentation anomalies that precede system-mode code execution in DeviceProcessEvents.

suggestion.title: Windows Deployment Services Use-After-Free RCE (CVE-2026-42987)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-42987 is a critical Remote Code Execution vulnerability in Windows Deployment Services (WDS)...an unauthorized attacker, exploiting this vulnerability, can execute malicious code over a network.' Network RCE in infrastructure service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WDS service (port 67-68, 69, 514) for out-of-order or repeated file operation requests triggering memory corruption. Alert on WDS process elevation or code injection following network requests from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE in phpBB (T1190 / T1059)
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly references 'authentication-bypass-rce' but pipeline generated zero use cases. Title phrase: '10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums'—the RCE component requires detection of unexpected process spawning from web server processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash process creation initiated by web server process (w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx, php-fpm) without prior authenticated phpBB user session, or execution occurring milliseconds after HTTP requests to sensitive phpBB endpoints (acp.php, login.php).

suggestion.title: phpBB Admin Elevation via Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass (explicit in URL slug) implies attacker gains unauthorized access to admin/mod functions; no detection for privilege escalation post-bypass. Title: 'affecting tens of millions of users' suggests user database and admin account exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB user/group membership tables for creation of new admin/moderator accounts or privilege elevation of existing users immediately following failed login attempts or with no corresponding admin action logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Web Shell in phpBB Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability enables file upload/write; article silent on this but standard post-compromise persistence vector. No use case generated for malicious file creation in phpBB web-accessible paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php, .phtml, .phar file creation/modification in phpBB directories (styles/, store/, cache/) not present in baseline, or uploaded within 60 seconds of authentication failure events on login.php.

suggestion.title: Suspicious phpBB Session/Cookie Forgery
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass mechanism likely exploits session/cookie generation or validation; URL 'authentication-bypass-rce' directly implicates session handling. No detection for forged/elevated session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin/mod-level phpBB operations (ban users, delete posts, grant permissions) originating from IP addresses with no prior successful authentication event in session logs, or with session creation time mismatched to HTTP request timing.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration Post-phpBB Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'tens of millions of users across thousands of forums'—user credentials and forum data are high-value targets. RCE enables undetected database extraction. No exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers (>100MB) from web server processes over unexpected ports/destinations within 5–30 minutes of RCE execution indicators, or mysqldump/pg_dump CLI invocation followed immediately by encoded data streams on port 443.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing to Known JDY Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 1,500+ compromised devices—implies active command-and-control infrastructure. Article likely contains C2 domains or IPs. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from enterprise endpoints to JDY C2 domains or IP blocks referenced in article. Focus on anomalous port usage, non-standard protocols, and persistent beaconing patterns that deviate from authorized traffic.

suggestion.title: JDY Malware Installation via Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet expansion across 1,500+ devices—requires initial infection and payload execution. No execution or initial-access kill-chain phases extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of JDY malware samples (if binary names or hashes provided in article). Monitor for script execution (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) spawning unsigned child processes. Correlate file creation in temp directories with subsequent suspicious process launches.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance from Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states purpose is 'cyber reconnaissance'—yet no discovery or collection kill-chain phases were mapped. Botnet reconnaissance generates detectable process and network signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of reconnaissance binaries (ipconfig, systeminfo, net view, nslookup, arp) on infected endpoints. Monitor for port scanning, ARP table enumeration, and SMB enumeration attempts. Alert on scanning patterns inconsistent with baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence via Autostart Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: 1,500+ sustained infections require durable persistence. Article must describe registry modifications, scheduled tasks, or services—no persistence phases extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry run-key modifications (HKCU/HKLM Run, RunOnce). Detect scheduled task creation with obfuscated commands or binaries in %temp%. Alert on service installation with non-standard service binary paths or descriptions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Remote Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Botnet targeting 1,500+ devices implies multi-stage infection or pivot capability. Article likely documents lateral movement—no such kill-chain phase extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP, WinRM, and SMB connections from infected endpoints to other internal systems. Detect failed authentication attempts followed by successful lateral pivots. Alert on credential reuse across unusual host pairs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Code Commits from Development Devices
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'device is the only constant' suggests code is written across multiple endpoints—should detect commits from unusual locations, out-of-hours, or unrecognized developer devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor version control systems for commits signed with credentials not previously used from that device, or commits outside normal development windows from known high-risk environments (coffee shops, VPNs, guest networks).

suggestion.title: Monitor for Supply-Chain Tool Compromise (Development Environment)
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies development tools/IDEs/package managers are attack surface—should detect compromise of compiler toolchains, package registries, or IDE plugins used across devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or revoked code-signing certificates in build artifacts; unexpected downloads of dev tools from non-canonical sources; integrity hash mismatches on IDE/compiler binaries; unauthorized package installations from typosquatted or compromised registries.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Exposure in Code (Cross-Device)
suggestion.rationale: Multi-device development context increases risk of secrets (API keys, tokens, certs) being committed accidentally across repos from different machines—should detect and quarantine.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all code commits for patterns matching API keys, private keys, AWS credentials, tokens; raise alerts when same credential appears across multiple repositories or committed from multiple devices; correlate with cloud/SaaS access attempts from those credentials.

suggestion.title: Detect Forked/Mirrored Development Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'code is written everywhere' may imply distributed repos—should detect unauthorized forks of internal repositories to external accounts or unauthorized mirrors to attacker-controlled platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected repository forks to external accounts; detect git clones to external storage or non-standard repositories; alert on bulk repository exports or unusual git protocol traffic to non-whitelisted hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect IDE/Editor Plugin Injection and Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: Development across multiple devices/IDEs creates attack surface for malicious extensions—should detect unauthorized plugin installation, plugin source tampering, or plugin-based code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin directories for unsigned or revoked extensions; detect unexpected plugin downloads from non-official markets; alert on plugins modifying build processes, commit hooks, or injecting code during compilation.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Device Compromise via Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: If development is distributed across devices, each device is an attack vector—should detect malware/keyloggers/persistence installed via compromised development tools, build environments, or dependency downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Behavioral detection for unexpected process chains launched by IDEs, compilers, or package managers; network connections from build tools to C2 infrastructure; unsigned binary execution from development tool directories; presence of dev-tool-adjacent backdoors (e.g., malware masquerading as 'npm' or 'gcc').

suggestion.title: Suspicious Rust Crate Installation with Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes malicious Rust crate performs code exfiltration; pipeline missed detection for dependency installation + C2 communication. Phrase: 'onering performs code exfiltration'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Rust/Cargo processes (cargo.exe, rustc.exe) execute immediately before or concurrent with unexpected network connections to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains. Correlate with Cargo.lock changes and unexpected file read operations on source code directories.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Build System Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration during build phase requires detection of data leaving build environment. Article establishes exfiltration as primary payload; pipeline did not surface detection of bulk data transfer from CI/build systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-volume data transfers initiated from build systems or developer machines to external IPs during or immediately after dependency resolution. Baseline normal source-code size + dependencies; alert on multiples of baseline egress in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation Detection (Rust Registry)
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise requires detection at dependency ingestion point. Pipeline did not surface use case for identifying malicious or modified packages from crates.io or other Rust registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo manifest changes and crates.io package queries; alert on installation of packages on threat-intel blocklists or with unusual metadata (newly-created author, recent version bumps, abnormal dependency chains). Cross-reference against supply-chain threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Code Injection via Build-time Dependency Execution
suggestion.rationale: Rust crate execution happens at build/compile time; pipeline missed detection for code execution during dependency compilation. Phrase: 'performs code exfiltration' implies runtime behavior during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for proc_macro or build.rs script execution from Cargo dependencies outside expected system paths. Alert on rustc child processes invoking network utilities (curl, wget, PowerShell) or opening unexpected files during compilation phase.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45447 Exploitation via Malformed PKCS7/S/MIME Messages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'triggered when applications process specially crafted PKCS7 or S/MIME signed messages.' Initial-access detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal PKCS7 or S/MIME message processing: malformed ASN.1 structures, unusual message sizes, repeated failed signature verification attempts, or messages targeting mail servers and TLS libraries. Flag unexpected network traffic patterns to systems known to process S/MIME content.

suggestion.title: Heap Corruption and Process Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'heap use-after-free bug' causing 'memory corruption'—execution-phase detection required to catch in-flight exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process crashes, memory access violations, or unhandled exceptions in OpenSSL-linked processes immediately following PKCS7_verify function invocation. Flag unexpected child processes spawned from crashed or recovering OpenSSL contexts.

suggestion.title: OpenSSL Version Inventory for CVE-2026-45447 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE affecting OpenSSL—asset discovery hunt absent despite this being foundational recon phase work.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all processes executing OpenSSL libraries and extract version information. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-45447 patch timeline to identify unpatched endpoints. Prioritize mail servers, TLS termination points, and S/MIME-capable applications.

suggestion.title: RCE Code Execution Detection Post-Heap-Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Article's RCE impact requires execution-phase detection. Pipeline missed T1059/T1203 implications of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected command execution or script spawning from OpenSSL or S/MIME processing contexts. Monitor for process parent-child anomalies where shell interpreters are launched from library contexts normally incapable of process spawning.

suggestion.title: JWT Cryptographic Validation Against Known Hardcoded Secret
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery.' Direct cryptographic validation—tokens that verify against the string 'random' as the HMAC-SHA256 key—would catch active exploitation.
log_sources: Web access logs with Authorization headers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement JWT signature validation in HTTP access logs. Flag tokens that cryptographically validate against the hardcoded secret 'random'. Correlate against legitimate authentication paths; forged tokens will bypass login/MFA flows.

suggestion.title: go-base Repository Access and Source Code Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the hardcoded secret is 'shipped to all users' in dev.env. Detecting clones, downloads, or reads of github.com/dhax/go-base would identify reconnaissance preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git clone/pull of github.com/dhax/go-base, package manager downloads of 'go-base', or direct HTTP reads of dev.env from GitHub raw content. Pair with subsequent credential enumeration or API reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unmitigated Hardcoded Secret in Active Deployment (Config Override Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Broken Mitigation'—AUTH_JWT_SECRET is configurable via Viper (cmd/serve.go:35) but default 'random' remains active. Detection identifies deployments where the override failed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit running application instances: extract AUTH_JWT_SECRET environment variable. Flag instances where value is 'random', null, or absent. Cross-reference against configuration management to identify deployments where Viper defaults were not overridden.

suggestion.title: Admin API Access via Forged Bearer Token (Missing Authentication Precedent)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1078 (Valid Accounts) and T1550.001. Exploitation pattern: attacker forges token, accesses /api/v1/admin/* without prior login. Detection: successful API call with no preceding authentication event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful API POST/GET to /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, or /api/v1/token/refresh against authentication/login logs for the same user account. Flag cases where API request succeeds (200–299) but no login event exists in the 15 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Cryptomining GPU Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'secretly mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' but no hunt targets resource-hijacking indicators (T1496). Look for sustained elevated GPU utilization, cryptominer process signatures, or memory patterns typical of xmrig/monero miners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes consuming sustained >70% GPU for >5min without user context (e.g., no game/video editor running), or process names matching cryptominer patterns (xmrig, cpuminer, claymore). Cross-reference against installed software to separate legitimate GPU workloads.

suggestion.title: Execution from User Download Folder (Malware Distribution Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'luring them into downloading malware-laced files'—emphasis on user-driven download→execution. Pipeline should hunt process execution originating from Downloads/ AppData/Local/Downloads/ or similar user-writable temp directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when parent process is explorer.exe or file explorer context and child process spawns from ~Downloads, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA%\Local\Temp. Pair with file name deception (e.g., 'VLC-Installer.exe' but hash not known-good).

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Utility Installation (Fake Software Distribution)
suggestion.rationale: Article states '150 fake download sites that closely mimic trusted [utilities].' Detect when a file claiming to be a legitimate utility (WinRAR, 7-Zip, VLC, CCleaner, etc.) is executed but has no valid digital signature or wrong signature issuer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for executables with product names matching popular utilities (7-Zip, WinRAR, VLC, Audacity, etc.) but missing Authenticode signature, signed by unknown or suspicious publisher, or signature timestamp far in the future/past. Cross-reference against catalog of known-good utility publishers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Registration Pattern (gleeze, giize, .icu TLDs)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 10+ domains: 'gleeze.com', 'giize.com', '.icu' TLD variants. These are attacker infrastructure for malware distribution. Detection should flag first-contact to newly-registered or low-reputation domains matching typosquat or homoglyph patterns against known utility vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP requests to domains registered <90 days ago, or domains with permutations of legitimate utility names (e.g., 'download.7-zip-official.com' vs 'direct-downloads.7zip.icu'). Flag suspicious TLDs (.icu, .stream, .download) when combined with utility-name keywords.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Installed with Non-Standard Parent or User Privilege Context
suggestion.rationale: While UC_RMM_TOOLS catches installation, the article's attack chain shows ScreenConnect being dropped by malware, not installed by IT/legitimate deployment. Additional hunt should detect ScreenConnect appearing with suspicious parent processes (cmd, powershell, wget, 7z) or installed by non-admin or suspicious user accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe or installer appears as child of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, msiexec.exe spawned from Temp/Downloads, or when registry/service modifications for ScreenConnect originate from non-SYSTEM, non-LOCAL_SERVICE account. Correlate with file hash IOCs if available.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/Hidden Malware Staging (T1027 Implementation)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 12 SHA256 hashes and emphasizes obfuscation; pipeline caught T1027 at the technique level but generated no detection. Hunt should look for packed/encrypted files (low entropy, signatures matching UPX/Themida/VMProtect), files with abnormal section names, or DLLs with no export table.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executable or DLL is loaded with anomalous headers (entropy >7.8, UPX/packed signatures, corrupted or missing standard sections), or when file is written to disk and immediately accessed by multiple processes before any user interaction. Cross-reference with detonation/sandbox signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation—Threat-Intel-Flagged Package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware-laden npm package 'dbmux' installed on developer systems: 'capable of giving attackers complete control over any developer's system that had it installed or running.' This is the primary Initial Access vector; pipeline generated zero detection for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/update operations where package name or version matches threat-intel feeds (e.g., dbmux). Correlate package installation with child process spawning from node_modules. Monitor for postinstall script execution during suspicious package initialization.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution from npm Postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes malware capability yielding 'complete control'—this implies code execution during or immediately after package installation via postinstall hooks or module init. Pipeline missed Execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or system utilities from npm/node_modules context during package installation. Alert on privilege-escalation attempts or system-level operations (registry modification, service creation) from npm postinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanisms Installed by Malicious npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article's claim of 'complete control' implies persistent backdoor, not ephemeral malware. Pipeline failed to hypothesize persistence techniques (startup items, cron jobs, registry runkeys, shell profile injection) typical of full-system compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions to startup locations (registry HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce, user startup folder, .bashrc/.bash_profile, cron, launchd) coinciding with npm package installation. Alert on scheduled task or service creation by node.js or npm processes.

suggestion.title: Credential and Source-Code Exfiltration from Compromised Developer Workstation
suggestion.rationale: With 'complete control' of developer systems, attackers logically target high-value assets: SSH keys, API credentials, Git tokens, and source repositories. Pipeline missed Impact-phase detection despite this being critical for developer-targeted compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTPS/DNS activity from developer systems post-npm-infection, especially to non-whitelisted IPs or cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, GitHub gists). Alert on unusual data transfers, credential-store access (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain), or .ssh directory enumeration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Developer System Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Developer workstations with full system compromise are staging points for internal infrastructure attacks: Git repositories, CI/CD platforms, artifact registries, and shared development servers. Pipeline ignored this logical attack continuation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections from compromised developer systems to internal Git/CI/CD infrastructure (GitLab, Jenkins, GitHub Enterprise) or shared development servers outside baseline access patterns. Alert on service-account credential usage originating from developer workstations.

suggestion.title: In-memory PowerShell/CLR assembly loading without disk artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace behind'—core evasion tactic. Pipeline generated no detection for unsigned .NET assembly loading, memory-resident shellcode, or WMI event sink persistence. This is the defining characteristic of the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or rundll32 loading unsigned .NET assemblies into memory (via Assembly.Load or reflection), or WMI event sinks created without corresponding .ps1 file on disk. In-memory malware avoids file enumeration but leaves traces in ETW event logs and memory introspection tools.

suggestion.title: Process injection / memory manipulation from script engines
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage malware execution with in-memory payload typically involves process injection (T1055) or hollowing. Pipeline maps T1218 but no UC detects injection patterns (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext calls or suspicious remote handle opens).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell or VBScript spawning svchost.exe, dllhost.exe, or other system processes with no command-line arguments and no corresponding task/scheduled job registry entry. Or detect unsigned code execution in legitimate service processes (signatureless child or remote thread creation).

suggestion.title: Multi-stage malware dropper-to-payload execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage malware' but pipeline generated no UC for detecting the dropper→payload sequence. Typical chain: initial executable launches PowerShell or VBS, which decodes/downloads second stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid (<5 second) parent-child process chains where initial process (powershell, cmd, wscript) spawns a second script engine or LOLBin with suspiciously short lifetime. Correlate with network events (DNS/HTTP) at same time to confirm payload fetch.

suggestion.title: C2 communication from application-layer protocols (post-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1071 'Application Layer Protocol' is listed, implying HTTP/HTTPS or DNS C2 callbacks, but no UC detects beaconing patterns. In-memory malware needs command channel to adversary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual DNS or HTTP traffic from PowerShell (or other script engine child processes) to the extracted IOC domains (guhxmg.com, naiqja.icu, zh-welcome-1xbet.com, etc.) with periodic/regular timing (C2 beacon pattern). Include failed connection attempts to staging domains.

suggestion.title: Credential entry / form submission to tax-themed phishing domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impersonation of 'official Indian government tax authorities'—credential harvesting is the typical end-goal. No UC covers detecting users entering credentials into non-legitimate tax websites or forms.
log_sources: browser process memory or HTTP body inspection (DLP-adjacent)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) navigation to extracted IOC domains (e.g., taxations.indiagov.it.com, taxations.cn-web-okooo.com) followed by form POST requests or password managers being triggered. Cross-reference with known Indian tax domain patterns (indiagov.nic.in) to confirm the impersonation.

suggestion.title: Registry persistence / scheduled task creation without file artifact
suggestion.rationale: In-memory malware often persists via registry run keys, WMI event sinks, or scheduled tasks rather than .exe files on disk. No UC detects this evasion variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entries or scheduled tasks pointing to PowerShell/WMI commands (especially obfuscated or base64-encoded) without corresponding .exe file on disk. Combine with process execution logs to confirm task execution.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection — Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'critical vulnerabilities' from three major vendors; exploitation is the primary attack vector implied by vulnerability disclosure patterns. No use case generated despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests containing known exploit signatures or payloads targeting Ivanti Connect Secure, Fortinet FortiGate, and SAP NetWeaver management interfaces. Flag POST requests with suspicious parameter encoding or known CVE payload patterns to these devices.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Inventory — Patch Applicability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vendors 'releasing patches'; detection should identify systems still running pre-patch versions vulnerable to disclosed CVEs. No inventory use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify installed Ivanti, Fortinet, and SAP software versions against published vulnerability timelines. Flag systems running versions released before the patching date or versions explicitly listed as vulnerable in CVE databases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Patch Behavior Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: If a system running these products exhibits anomalous behavior after the vulnerability window, it may indicate successful pre-patch exploitation. Article implies potential for undetected compromise during vulnerability window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For systems hosting Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP services, correlate unusual outbound connections, process spawning, or DNS queries in the 24-48 hours post-patch deployment with known C2 patterns or data exfiltration signatures.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Bypass via CVE-2026-10523
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10523 is 'a critical authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts.' This is a distinct attack phase preceding RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for unauthenticated requests that successfully create or modify administrative user accounts. Correlate failed authentication attempts followed by new privileged account creation within the same session.
