suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS)' deployed mid-May as temporary control. Should detect exploitation attempts when mitigation is absent or bypassed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when XSS-based OWA exploitation attempts occur on systems where EEMS status cannot be confirmed active, or post-May 15 exploitation events indicate mitigation failure. Correlate with servers lacking June 2026 patches.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Reconnaissance via OWA XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ransomware gangs having exploited 14' prior Exchange vulnerabilities. XSS in OWA could enable credential harvesting or session hijacking for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual credential submission or session token access patterns following OWA XSS exploitation. Monitor for lateral movement indicators (cross-mailbox access, unusual delegation changes) suggesting attacker pivoted via compromised session.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'three zero-days' and 'critical RCE bugs'—explicit exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process spawning from Office applications or Windows services, unexpected command execution, or network connections paired with process creation following known RCE attack patterns.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Microsoft Product Inventory and Exposure Risk
suggestion.rationale: 206 patches released; systems running vulnerable versions before patch deployment are at immediate risk. Title establishes urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Windows, Office, Exchange, and Edge versions against disclosed KB/CVE lists. Prioritize systems with network exposure, interactive user sessions, or email processing capabilities.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Unpatched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: RCE bugs often chain to privilege escalation; article's emphasis on 'critical' suggests elevation-to-SYSTEM possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag UAC bypasses, token theft, or SYSTEM-level process spawning from non-privileged parent (Office, Edge, user-facing service).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Credential Dumping via RCE
suggestion.rationale: If attacker gains code execution via RCE, credential access is immediate next step. No detection use case covers this chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lsass.exe access, registry reads (SAM hive), or in-memory credential tool invocation following unexpected process execution in Office or Windows service context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Unpatched System
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day RCE on internet-facing or frequently-accessed system allows pivot. Article does not mention containment of initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual SMB/RDP/WinRM connections from systems known to run vulnerable Microsoft products, especially targeting admin shares or domain controllers.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft SSH Credential Spray Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes script that 'attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm' with fallback to key-based auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed SSH authentication attempts (>5 in 5 min) to PeopleSoft servers using a small set of usernames (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) from a single source IP. Escalate if followed by successful key-based auth to same account within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft /etc/hosts Enumeration and SSH Lateral Spread
suggestion.rationale: Article describes script that 'parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems and attempts to connect to them over SSH'—discovery followed by lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process reading /etc/hosts (cat, grep, strings) executed from web/app server context, followed within 2 minutes by SSH attempts to multiple distinct internal IPs from same source. Especially suspicious if process UID matches PeopleSoft application user.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Deployment on PeopleSoft Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article provides specific shell script designed to 'create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT' in PeopleSoft web/app directories after SSH breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification matching 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS.*' in PeopleSoft directories (PSP*, PSFT_CFG, web root). Correlate with SSH process execution or shell spawning from PeopleSoft app UID within 5 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Remote Management Tool Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes researcher found 'staging materials, including MeshCentral agents' in exposed attacker directories—indicates persistent C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of meshagent, meshcentral-agent, or msh* binaries on PeopleSoft application/web servers. Monitor for outbound connections to MeshCentral C2 domains. Flag creation of scheduled tasks or service entries for MeshCentral.

suggestion.title: Connections from ShinyHunters Staging Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 7 IOC IPs (142.11.200.186–190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) with TLS cert CN 'azurenetfiles[.]net' used for staging and attack delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on ANY inbound connection from IPs 142.11.200.186–190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24 to PeopleSoft ports (8000, 8080, 9000, 443, 3389). Retroactively hunt logs for successful sessions. Flag TLS certificates with CN matching '*azurenetfiles*'.

suggestion.title: Exposed .bash_history Revealing Attack Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Five of the servers exposed a .bash_history file that gave some insight into the attacks'—indicates web-facing attacker staging directory leaking command history.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET requests for .bash_history, .sh_history, .zsh_history from external IPs to web-facing PeopleSoft directories. Flag 200-responses serving these files (misconfigured web server exposing shell history).

suggestion.title: Detect path traversal in Langflow /api/v2/files uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents vulnerability: 'POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences (../)'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/v2/files for filename parameters containing ../ sequences. Any such request should trigger alert as it represents direct exploitation of CVE-2026-5027. Baseline should be zero occurrences.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated Langflow exploitation attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, no credentials are required to reach the vulnerable endpoint, and a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token'—this is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /api/v2/files from IPs lacking prior authentication context or JWT tokens in session logs. Flag rapid auto-login token generation followed by file upload attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect suspicious file writes from Langflow process
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms impact: 'attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files on vulnerable instances' and 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /api/v2/files requests with subsequent file creation events from Langflow process, especially writes outside application data directory or to system/web-root locations. Flag any write to locations outside expected paths.

suggestion.title: Detect exposed vulnerable Langflow versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies version boundaries: vulnerable <1.9.0 (application) and <0.8.3 (langflow-base package); patched in 1.9.0+, latest 1.10.0 released June 10, 2026. ~7,000 exposed instances identified by Censys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract Langflow version from HTTP headers, API responses, or Git repos. Alert on versions <1.9.0 or any publicly accessible version disclosure. Correlate with network exposure (Shodan/Censys scans).

suggestion.title: Detect rapid token generation from Langflow auto-login
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain requires obtaining session token via auto-login: 'a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token before proceeding with exploitation'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline auto-login token generation rates for Langflow endpoints. Alert on token issuance spikes or tokens immediately followed by POST /api/v2/files requests, indicating automation/scripted exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized ServiceNow Instance Table Query via Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: attackers 'query customer instance tables' and 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication.' The vulnerability itself is the initial_access vector; detection must catch table enumeration without valid auth context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow /api/now/table/* and /api/v2/* endpoints for SELECT queries on sys_* or instance tables where authentication context is missing, bypassed, or tampered (null bearer token, missing session cookie, invalid CSRF). Alert on bulk enumeration (>15 distinct tables in 5min from single source) or access to sensitive tables (sys_user, sys_password, customer data repositories) without valid user context.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Attacker Infrastructure (51.159.98.241)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 51.159.98.241 with 'high-fidelity' rating and explicitly recommends hunt 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' as templated detection in 'c2' phase. Pipeline output contains zero IOCs; this hunt was never materialized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from ServiceNow infrastructure (app servers, API gateways) or internal hosts to 51.159.98.241. Establish baseline of legitimate traffic; flag any sustained connections or data-volume anomalies. Cross-reference with application logs showing table queries during connection windows to confirm data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from ServiceNow Post-Vulnerability Access
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'data exposure across enterprise environments.' Once improper access controls are bypassed, attacker can execute large result-set queries for bulk dumps. Detection must catch collection-phase data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ServiceNow API calls returning unusually large result sets (>5,000 rows per query) from single sources, especially for user tables, password tables, or customer data repositories. Correlate concurrent high-volume queries with network connections to attacker IP 51.159.98.241. Flag API keys or session tokens making queries outside normal usage patterns.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Authentication Bypass or Access Control Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables access 'without proper authentication' and references 'improper access controls.' Detection should catch failed auth attempts immediately preceding successful queries, or successful queries from invalid/missing credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow audit logs for table-query operations where authentication_context is null, invalid, or missing session validation. Flag sequences of failed authentication (401 responses) followed by successful table access (200 response) from same source within <60 seconds. Detect requests with tampered or absent Authorization headers to /api/now/table endpoints.

suggestion.title: Persistent Access via Leaked or Unrevoked ServiceNow Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'unauthorized actors'—if not one-time exploitation, attacker likely obtained valid (but unauthorized) credentials. Improper access controls may allow lower-privilege accounts to query tables above their role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service accounts or admin accounts performing table queries outside normal change windows or from geographically anomalous locations. Alert on API keys created without change ticket correlation or outside maintenance windows. Flag accounts escalating query permissions (querying higher-privilege tables than role permits). Cross-reference accounts used during vulnerability exploitation with account creation/modification audit trail.

suggestion.title: Systemd User Service Installation by Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The monitor runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS.' Malware persists via creation of user-level services that survive token revocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of systemd user services under ~/.config/systemd/user/ or LaunchAgent plists under ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, especially those with unusual executable paths or suspicious parent processes. Correlate timing with credential theft events.

suggestion.title: Dead-Man Switch File Destruction via Revoked GitHub Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'if it's revoked, executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents).' Unique indicator: mass recursive deletion triggered by loss of stolen credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of rm -rf with recursive directory removal targeting user home directories, especially when preceded by failed GitHub API authentication attempts or token revocation events. Scope to unusual execution contexts (systemd services, background daemons).

suggestion.title: Package Registry Trojanization to npm/PyPI/RubyGems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'publishing trojanized versions to infect downstream developers' via npm, PyPI, RubyGems. Malware replicates by injecting malicious code into legitimate packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registry API calls (npm publish, PyPI upload, RubyGems push) from compromised developer accounts, especially for packages with recent legitimate history. Flag uploads following abnormal credential access or GitHub token usage.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Password Managers and Cloud Secret Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores.' Malware exfiltrates all credential types from victim environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to .aws/credentials, .ssh/, Kubernetes config files, password manager DBs (1Password, LastPass vaults), and environment variable enumeration. Look for child processes of package managers or build tools accessing credential storage.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH and AWS Systems Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' Malware uses stolen credentials to propagate across infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH connections using keys from compromised developer machines to unusual targets. Track AWS SSM Session Manager calls with stolen or over-privileged credentials, especially from non-human user agents or outside normal office networks.

suggestion.title: AI Tool Configuration Poisoning (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, Cline, Kiro)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline.' Malware injects backdoors into IDE/AI tool settings to compromise downstream development.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to IDE/AI tool config files (~/.cursor, ~/.claude, .copilot, .cursorrules, etc.) by unexpected processes or with unusual content. Flag additions of environment variables or custom system prompts that reference exfiltration or credential paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Langflow Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Unauthenticated RCE'—the vulnerability requires no auth. Pipeline should flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Langflow without authentication tokens or cookies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints (typically /api/* paths) without standard authentication headers (Authorization, X-API-Key, session cookies). Baseline legitimate Langflow traffic first. Alert on unusual user-agents or request patterns matching public POC payloads for CVE-2026-5027.

suggestion.title: Langflow Process Spawning After RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Remote Code Execution'—implies arbitrary command execution post-compromise. Pipeline missed detection for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process is Langflow runtime (java, python, node depending on implementation). Look for unexpected child processes: shells (cmd.exe, bash), scripting interpreters, file utilities (curl, wget), or network tools spawned shortly after suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is being 'actively exploited' but pipeline extracted no exploitation signatures. Need signature-based detection for known POC/exploit patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create detection rule matching known CVE-2026-5027 exploitation patterns in HTTP request payloads—typically involve specific Langflow API routes, injection vectors, or parameter names. Correlate with high request volume to single target from multiple source IPs (scanning activity) or repeated requests with different payloads from single source (exploitation attempts).

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE implies attacker gains shell access. Article does not detail exfiltration or C2, but pipeline should generate defensive hypothesis for outbound C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from Langflow processes to unusual destinations—non-RFC1918, high-risk countries, dynamic DNS, known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for DNS queries to suspicious domains immediately preceding or during exploitation window. Look for encrypted tunnels (TLS to unexpected ports, raw sockets).

suggestion.title: Langflow Configuration or Code Tampering
suggestion.rationale: RCE attacker can modify workflows, environment variables, or deployment configs. Pipeline missed persistence/impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized file modifications in Langflow directories (workflow files, config files, plugin directories). Alert on creation of new Langflow user accounts or API keys via REST API calls. Track changes to environment variables or secrets managers that Langflow accesses.

suggestion.title: Scanning for Additional Vulnerable Langflow Instances
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation phase often includes lateral reconnaissance. Pipeline should flag credential/asset enumeration against other Langflow instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid HTTP requests (>10/min) to Langflow health check endpoints (e.g., /health, /api/v1/status) from compromised host, indicating scanning for additional vulnerable Langflow deployments in network. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to different internal IPs.

suggestion.title: CTFMON Process Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM' via CTFMON framework. No UC generated for this core privilege escalation behavior despite being the primary and explicitly-described attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CTFMON.exe or related CTF service processes requesting elevated tokens, writing to HKLM or System32, or spawning with privilege level change from low to SYSTEM. Correlate process elevation events with CTFMON execution and DLL load sequences during the exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CTFMON.exe Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CTFMON as 'a valuable post-exploitation primitive for threat actors.' Legitimate CTFMON behavior (parent process identity, command-line arguments, loaded modules) should be baselined to detect when the process is abused in exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CTFMON execution from non-standard parents (other than svchost.exe, explorer.exe, or loginui.exe), with suspicious command-line arguments, loading unexpected DLLs outside System32, or initiating outbound network connections. Alert with high confidence if CTFMON spawns unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45586 Exploitation Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references June 9, 2026 security updates that 'fix' the vulnerability, implying specific code patterns and behavioral artifacts were corrected. No process-level, registry, or file artifacts were extracted despite being high-fidelity exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HKLM registry writes initiated by low-privilege CTFMON process, creation of staging files in Temp/AppData during CTFMON execution, DLL injection or code loading attempts targeting ctfmon.exe, or privilege token request chains. Cross-reference exploit patterns with June 9, 2026 patch diff.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Logging Disabled or Deleted
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names AWS CloudTrail as target; abuse of logging services for defense evasion necessitates disabling trail first. Core attack step missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or PutEventSelectors calls that narrow CloudTrail capture scope or stop recording. Alert on trail deletions followed by privilege escalation or data exfiltration within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Google Cloud Logging Sink Deletion or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article covers Google Cloud logging alongside AWS; log routers and sinks are primary attack surface for blinding logging. No detection for sink configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink and UpdateSink calls. Flag deletions of sinks routing to Cloud Storage, BigQuery, or Pub/Sub, especially sinks that capture admin activity or VPC Flow logs.

suggestion.title: S3 Bucket Logging Disabled or Destination Removed
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include S3 log storage; disabling bucket logging or removing CloudTrail S3 destination is prerequisite for log evasion. Missing fundamental detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PutBucketLogging calls with LoggingEnabled=false or removal of target S3 bucket. Correlate with prior S3 PutObject/DeleteObject activity in same account to detect potential cover tracks.

suggestion.title: CloudWatch Logs Log Group Deleted or Retention Shortened
suggestion.rationale: Cloud logging services article should cover CloudWatch as primary AWS logging aggregation point. Log group deletion removes audit trail. No detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DeleteLogGroup and PutRetentionPolicy calls that reduce retention below baseline (e.g., <7 days) on log groups containing security-relevant data (VPC Flow, Config, GuardDuty). Alert within 15 min of suspicious API activity.

suggestion.title: IAM Policy Modified to Restrict CloudTrail or Logging Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Defense evasion via log access control rather than deletion—article discusses abuse of logging services broadly. Attacker may restrict other principals' ability to read logs rather than delete.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PutUserPolicy or AttachUserPolicy calls that add Deny statements for cloudtrail:*, logs:*, s3:GetObject (log buckets), or monitoring service actions. Cross-reference with prior reconnaissance activity.

suggestion.title: Log Poisoning—Injection of Misleading Entries into CloudTrail or Cloud Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions log poisoning; pipeline should flag detection gaps for injected/forged log entries to mask true activity. Critical evasion technique not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous log sequences: consecutive identical API calls at regular intervals, impossible geographic/source IP transitions within seconds, or out-of-order timestamps. Flag if CloudTrail UserAgent field contains non-standard SDK/CLI signatures.

suggestion.title: Chrome/V8 Exploitation via Memory Safety Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates zero-day exploitation in the wild. V8 vulnerabilities typically manifest as heap corruption, OOB read/write, or use-after-free. Pipeline failed to surface behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chrome processes (chrome.exe, chromium) exhibiting abnormal memory access patterns—specifically heap allocations immediately followed by crashes with fault addresses in V8 memory regions, or Chrome spawning with unusual child processes (sandbox escapes). Correlate with Windows Defender Exploit Guard ASR (Attack Surface Reduction) triggers for code injection into browser processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Chrome/Browser Update or Rollback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Patch Now'—adversary likely exploiting versions prior to patch release. Pipeline missed detection for incomplete updates or downgrade scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome version rollbacks or failed auto-updates via registry changes (HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\ClientState) and file-level modifications to chrome.exe/chrome_elf.dll. Detect stalled or interrupted updates combined with application restart, which might indicate attacker pinning to vulnerable version.

suggestion.title: Malicious Content Delivery via Compromised Web Server or Ad Network
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day 'exploited in the wild' implies attack vector—likely malicious webpage, ad-injection, or watering hole. Pipeline did not reconstruct initial-access delivery chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous DNS resolutions and HTTP requests to known ad-tech CDNs, ad-exchange servers, or typosquatted news/tech sites. Flag unusual referrer patterns in browser logs pointing to drive-by download or redirect chains. Correlate with timing of Chrome crashes on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Sandbox Escape and Process Elevation Post-V8 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Chrome runs processes in sandbox; V8 zero-day often leads to sandbox escape and privilege escalation. Pipeline missed post-exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Chrome child processes (renderer, GPU, utility) attempting to load system DLLs (kernel32.dll, ntdll.dll) from non-standard paths, or Chrome parent spawning SYSTEM-level processes without user consent. Flag abnormal IPC or CreateProcess calls from within Chrome's sandbox namespace.

suggestion.title: V8 Crash Dump and Telemetry Suppression
suggestion.rationale: Exploits may suppress crash reports or delete minidumps to evade detection. Pipeline did not suggest monitoring for telemetry evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deletion or modification of Chrome crash dump directory (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Crash Reports) or disabling of Google Update (GoogleUpdate.exe). Flag SetFileInformationByHandle calls targeting minidump files immediately after Chrome process exit.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payload Delivery via JavaScript Obfuscation or Polyglot Archive
suggestion.rationale: V8 exploits delivered via JavaScript payload. Pipeline missed detection for obfuscated or polymorphic code patterns in Chrome's cached resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect Chrome cache (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cache) for unusually large or deeply nested JavaScript files with high entropy (entropy > 7.5), or WASM binaries with suspicious imports. Correlate file timestamps with V8 crashes.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Chromium Browser Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects Chrome, Edge, and Opera, with federal patch due date 2026-06-23. Pipeline must flag versions below patch cutoff: 'Vendor: Google, Product: Chromium V8' with version inventory cross-reference against known-vulnerable release timelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Chrome, Edge, or Opera instances with version numbers released before June 23, 2026 patch cutoff. Cross-reference Software Inventory against Chromium release notes. Alert on machines with >7-day remediation delay past due date.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Crash Following HTML Content Load
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'out-of-bounds read and write' via 'crafted HTML page.' OOB violations produce process exceptions, segmentation faults, or heap corruption errors detectable in process telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal termination (exit codes 0xC0000374, 0xC0000374 for heap exceptions) of Chrome/Edge/Opera processes within 30 seconds of HTML file download or webpage navigation. Correlate with V8 JavaScript execution context in crash dump if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTML Attachment or Hosted Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly stated: 'remote attacker to execute arbitrary code ... via a crafted HTML page.' Exploit delivery precedes crash/execution. Detect HTML/HTM file transfers to end-users from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .html/.htm attachments in email (especially from external domains) or downloads from non-standard web servers. Enrich with subsequent browser crashes or network callbacks. Prioritize email attachments opened by users in high-security groups.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Child Process from Browser Parent
suggestion.rationale: Impact statement: 'execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox.' Code execution following OOB exploit manifests as unexpected child processes (cmd, powershell, rundll32) spawned from browser parent with suspicious arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child process creation (system tools, encoded PowerShell, registry modifications) spawned from Chrome/Edge/Opera parent process without user interaction or extension context. Cross-correlate with recent HTML delivery to same user within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Verification Against CVE-2026-11645
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due date 2026-06-23. Vulnerability scanners may report false negatives; direct version cross-reference is required: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner compliance reports for CVE-2026-11645 against CMDB browser version inventory. Flag discrepancies where scanner shows compliant but installed version is unpatched. Alert on any unpatched systems 3+ days before 2026-06-23 deadline.

suggestion.title: V8 Memory Access Violation Telemetry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly named 'Out-of-Bounds Read and Write.' Memory safety violations—buffer overruns, heap metadata corruption, access violations—are detectable in Address Sanitizer logs or ETW memory exception events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on memory-related exception codes (0xC0000005 access violation, 0xC0000374 heap corruption) in Chrome/Edge/Opera processes during HTML parsing. If browser telemetry captures memory protections, flag OOB signatures in V8 heap regions.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'supplying a crafted file' — pipeline missed the file-upload/file-modification detection opportunity entirely. Need to monitor upload endpoints and temporary locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager file-upload endpoints from non-standard clients or with unusual Content-Type patterns. Flag file uploads followed immediately by process execution events in the same session.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root via SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Core impact is 'execute arbitrary commands as root' — this is explicit privilege escalation that should trigger T1068 detection. Pipeline omitted escalation angle entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned with root privileges (UID 0) from Cisco SD-WAN Manager or vManage service accounts. Correlate with preceding file modifications or network connections to establish exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Vulnerable Version Presence (CVE-2026-20245)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation — need version enumeration. Article provides no IOCs, but scanner-based version detection is essential given 'currently exploited' status and regulatory patch deadline (2026-06-23).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployment inventory against known-vulnerable versions. Prioritize hosts with internet exposure or lateral-movement risk from compromised network segments.

suggestion.title: Authenticated User Exploitation of Code Injection Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated' access + 'improper encoding/escaping' suggests input validation bypass (likely code injection). Pipeline should have surfaced authentication + exploitation sequence as distinct detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful logins followed within seconds by unusual system calls, shell spawning, or commands containing script interpreters. Flag cases where privilege-level mismatch occurs (authenticated user context → root execution).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Root RCE on SD-WAN Manager enables lateral movement across the network topology it manages. Article implies active exploitation; assume post-compromise persistence hunting is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Cisco SD-WAN Manager process (running as root post-exploitation) to unusual internal or external destinations. Correlate with file transfers, SSH key deployment, or configuration changes on managed SD-WAN appliances.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Configuration/File Tampering (Post-Exploitation Persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Root access post-RCE enables configuration persistence. Article's 'crafted file' mechanism may be followed by configuration modifications; pipeline should suggest monitoring file integrity on the manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to Cisco SD-WAN Manager configuration files, credential storage, or startup scripts. Flag hash changes in /opt/vmanage or equivalent installation directories, especially outside scheduled patch windows.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Tunnel Decapsulation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability occurs when switch 'incorrectly decapsulate and forwards unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP'—this is the core attack pattern requiring protocol-level visibility and anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista EOS devices for unexpected or malformed tunnel decapsulation events. Alert when decapsulation operations are triggered by packets with destination IPs matching the device's configured decapsulation endpoint but originating from unexpected sources, containing truncated/malformed tunnel headers, or showing inconsistent TTL/checksum fields indicating crafted payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerable Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes CISA KEV status (active wild exploitation) and mandatory federal remediation by 2026-06-23. Asset discovery and prioritization is foundational before behavioral hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-7473 against Arista EOS inventory. Prioritize devices processing GRE/VXLAN/IP-in-IP tunnels as exploitation surface. Flag devices exposed to untrusted networks, verify patch status against 2026-06-23 deadline, and correlate with netflow data to identify tunnel-handling traffic volume anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Packet Forwarding Policy Violation on Arista EOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability results in 'incorrectly decapsulate and forwards' — successful exploitation enables abnormal packet forwarding that violates expected routing policies and network topology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect packets forwarded from Arista EOS devices that violate expected routing rules or topology. Alert on forwarding decisions originating from processed tunnel traffic routing to unexpected destinations, or traffic that should have been dropped per configured decapsulation policies.

suggestion.title: Malformed Tunnel Frame Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism requires adversary injection of specially-crafted tunneled frames to trigger the 'incomplete comparison with missing factors' flaw. Article does not specify tunnel type (GRE/VXLAN/etc.) but the vulnerability lies in frame processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network segments connected to Arista EOS devices for tunnel frames with structural anomalies: destination IPs matching known decapsulation endpoints, truncated inner headers, missing or malformed encapsulation fields, TTL inconsistencies. Correlate frame injection patterns with Arista syslog decapsulation error counters.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to pheditor.php terminal handler with shell metacharacters in dir parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'unsanitized dir POST parameter' + 'shell metacharacters bypass TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist.' Delivery-phase detection completely absent despite unambiguous description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php with action=terminal parameter containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, `, $(), &&, ||, <, >) in 'dir' parameter or POST body. High-fidelity if correlated with non-standard User-Agent or atypical source IP geography.

suggestion.title: Web server process spawning shell interpreter with suspicious command-line arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary OS commands' + 'RCE with web server privileges.' UC_33_2 pre-formatted in article (exploit phase) but zero execution-phase hunts generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when php-fpm/apache2/httpd/nginx (running as www-data, apache, nginx, nobody, daemon) spawns sh/bash/dash/curl/wget/nc/python with command-line arguments containing wildcards, output redirects, variable expansion, or network operations—especially without corresponding legitimate web application activity.

suggestion.title: PHP web process creating/modifying .php files in webroot post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistence: 'PHP webserver writing .php file to webroot (Pheditor webshell drop).' UC_33_3 pre-formatted (install phase) but not extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileCreated/FileModified events targeting *.php in /var/www/*, /srv/www/*, /usr/share/nginx/*, /var/html/ initiated by web server processes running as www-data/apache/nginx/daemon. High-confidence if file creation follows HTTP POST access pattern or occurs outside deployment maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: WebSocket frame to untrusted code compilation (phoenix_storybook exploit chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'accepts user-controlled attribute values over WebSocket and interpolates them unsanitized into a HEEx template that is subsequently compiled and evaluated.' No detection monitors the WebSocket→compile→execute chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebSocket frames to phoenix_storybook playground (identified by port 4369 or /storybook URI path) with immediate downstream child processes spawned from BEAM/erl.exe with elapsed time <100ms. Flag as likely exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: HEEx template syntax in BEAM process execution context
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability root cause is template injection: HEEx syntax passed through WebSocket and compiled. No detection for compilation artifacts or template delimiters in spawned process command-lines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BEAM/erl.exe spawning child processes where the parent process command-line or child process command-line contains HEEx delimiters (<%=, <%= @, <>, ~F, ~H) or Elixir code blocks (def , defmodule, require) alongside shell binary paths (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe).

suggestion.title: Elixir Kernel module invocation from phoenix_storybook context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RCE via 'full Elixir Kernel access.' Detecting Kernel.* function calls (Kernel.eval, Kernel.spawn_link, Kernel.require) in the storybook render pipeline would signal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If application logging is available, hunt Elixir supervision tree logs for Kernel module calls originating from playground request handlers (e.g., render stack traces showing Kernel.eval + storybook component path). Absence of app logs: correlate compile.beam + BEAM code-path traversal artifacts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8467 vulnerability scanner payload detection
suggestion.rationale: Public-facing RCE in phoenix_storybook will attract scanner traffic. Article does not describe reconnaissance, but HTTP logs should show probe attempts with template payloads to /storybook or /playground endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to phoenix_storybook playground URIs for requests containing HEEx/Elixir syntax in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers (<%=, defmodule, System.cmd). Correlate 4xx response codes (not found/error) with high request volume per source IP to detect scanner sweeps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution from Python Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states packages 'auto-run'—indicates arbitrary code execution during install. Title: '19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer' establishes execution is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python subprocess spawning unusual interpreters (node, bash, or Bun runtime via `/usr/bin/bun` or `~/.bun/bin/bun`) immediately after `pip install` or during `setup.py` execution. Alert on command-line arguments containing credential paths (.bunrc, .config/bun).

suggestion.title: Access to Bun Credential Manager Config
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Bun Credential Stealer'—attacker targets `~/.bunrc` or Bun config. This is the stated credential exfiltration target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access to `.bunrc`, `.config/bun`, or Bun cache directories from Python interpreter or child processes spawned by pip/setup.py. Include read attempts on Bun's credential store.

suggestion.title: Poisoned Python Package Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 19 compromised PyPI packages. Pipeline missed ingestion of package names as IOCs; detection should flag installation of any package with modified/suspicious setup.py or unusual dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install commands for packages with known-poisoned names or inspect downloaded `.tar.gz`/`.whl` files for setup.py containing shell metacharacters, `os.system()`, or `subprocess` calls in metadata scripts. Cross-reference against PyPI security advisories.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain implies stolen Bun credentials are exfiltrated to attacker C2. Title states 'Credential Stealer'—stolen data must be transmitted. No use case covers post-compromise egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS from Python or Bun process to known malicious domains or high-entropy subdomains shortly after credential file access. Correlate with timing of setup.py execution.

suggestion.title: Bun Runtime Invocation from Python Interpreter Context
suggestion.rationale: Stealer must execute Bun to extract credentials, likely via subprocess from poisoned package init code. Article implies Bun is the target; detection should track cross-runtime execution chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Bun (`bun`, `bun run`, `/usr/bin/bun`) spawned as a child of `python`, `pip`, or processes in site-packages. Inspect command-line for flags targeting config or authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild'—pipeline generated zero detection for a known, active vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteLLM API endpoints for payloads or patterns matching CVE-2026-42271 exploitation signatures. Alert on requests that trigger known vulnerable code paths without proper input validation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Code Execution from LiteLLM Service
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—this is the attack outcome, yet no detection use case exists for RCE activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process creation from LiteLLM service processes (litellm, python instances with litellm in command line) executing shells, interpreters, or system utilities without corresponding authentication or authorization events.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Unauthenticated RCE'—authentication bypass is a prerequisite attack step but pipeline produced no detection for failed-to-allowed auth patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteLLM access logs for successful API calls lacking valid authentication tokens/API keys. Alert on patterns of malformed auth headers, missing credentials, or requests to protected endpoints that return 200 status codes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via Compromised LiteLLM
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability enables arbitrary command execution ('Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'). Pipeline did not suggest detection for post-RCE shell activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell commands (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned from LiteLLM process context with suspicious arguments (reverse shells, data exfil, lateral movement recon).

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Process Anomalies and Behavioral Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates active exploitation of a service ('Exploited in the Wild'). Pipeline omitted behavioral baseline detection for the vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for LiteLLM service process behavior (parent, expected children, network peers). Alert on: unexpected parent process changes, spawning of non-whitelisted child processes, or network connections to non-allowlisted destinations.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Signaling from Compromised LiteLLM Instance
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE implies potential for attacker-controlled post-exploitation activity. Pipeline generated no detection for exfiltration or C2 traffic from the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS and network traffic from LiteLLM processes to non-whitelisted external IPs, unusual ports, or known/newly registered malicious domains. Alert on patterns consistent with C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Auth Bypass + RCE'—authentication bypass is the initial access vector. No use case was generated to detect the bypass attack despite it being central to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB login endpoints for failed auth followed by immediate success from same source IP, logins from geographically impossible locations, or POST requests with malformed parameters (serialized PHP objects, SQL injection payloads in username/password fields) that may bypass validation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RCE' as the exploitation payload; no detection use case addresses process execution from PHP/web server processes, which is how phpBB RCE manifests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by web server daemons (php, apache, nginx) executing shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or system binaries (wget, curl, nc) with suspicious arguments indicating reverse shells, file downloads, or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Webshell Persistence in phpBB Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: phpBB RCE exploits require webshell persistence; article's scope ('tens of millions of users') indicates widespread exploitation yet no detection for malicious file uploads to /uploads, /files, or /cache directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of PHP/JSP/ASP files in phpBB-writable directories with suspicious names (shell.php, admin.php, test.php) or immediate post-authentication file uploads followed by HTTP requests to those new files.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Database Exfiltration Queries
suggestion.rationale: 10-year-old forum vulnerability affecting 'millions' suggests attacker motivation includes user credential theft; no use case monitors for unusual database access patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SELECT queries from phpBB application user querying phpbb_users or phpbb_posts tables with WHERE conditions matching entire rowsets, or DBA-level operations (UNION, INTO) executed outside normal application patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: RCE on forum software is weaponized for lateral movement into the broader network; article's description of 'tens of millions' impact implies multi-stage exploitation chains, yet no discovery/lateral-movement detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution from phpBB-served web content running network scanning tools (nmap, masscan, arp-scan), SMB enumeration (net view, enum), or DNS queries from web server resolving internal infrastructure hostnames.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Signature for phpBB Auth Bypass (CVE-2014-*)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'since 2014' dating and ties vulnerability to named software; no IOCs extracted for CVE identifier, affected versions, or exploitation signatures despite clear metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on requests to known-vulnerable phpBB versions/endpoints using exploit-specific signatures: malformed POST bodies to login endpoints, unauthenticated requests to admin panels, or specific PHP serialization gadget chains documented in phpBB security advisories.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet C2 Beacon Detection - Multi-Host Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active botnet controlling 1,500+ devices; no detection rule for C2 communication generated despite reconnaissance-phase activity requiring live command channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated connection attempts from ≥5 internal hosts to same external IP/domain on uncommon ports (non-80/443) within 24hr window. Exclude known commercial VPN/CDN ranges and patch distribution servers.

suggestion.title: Network Discovery Scanning - JDY Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states purpose is 'cyber reconnaissance'; pipeline failed to generate detection for discovery scanning or port enumeration that precedes attack actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid sequence of failed TCP connection attempts from single source to multiple internal hosts across different subnets within <5min window; correlate with local network enumeration tool execution (ipconfig, arp, nslookup, net.exe).

suggestion.title: Process Injection or Lateral Movement - Reconnaissance Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Botnet distributing across 1,500+ devices implies lateral movement or persistence mechanisms; no use case addresses process tree anomalies typical of botnet implants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process chains where unprivileged service (svchost.exe, winlogon.exe) spawns discovery/networking tools or outbound connections; or suspicious code injection into explorer.exe from non-Microsoft paths.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism - Scheduled Task or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: 1,500-device scale implies persistence across reboots; article does not detail mechanism but pipeline should have hypothesized scheduled task creation or startup registry modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected scheduled task creation (system event ID 106) or registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run from non-admin processes. Exclude known software deployment tools via hash whitelist.

suggestion.title: Compromised Rust Crate Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'onering' as compromised crate; pipeline should flag detection when malicious package versions are installed. Missing from all output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo package manager (cargo build, cargo fetch) for installation of known-malicious crate versions. Baseline legitimate onering usage, alert on version mismatches or unexpected installation contexts (e.g., CI/CD pipeline vs development machine, organization-wide first-time installs).

suggestion.title: Source Code Exfiltration via Malicious Crate Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle 'performs code exfiltration' establishes data theft objective; no detection generated for suspicious file reads or archive creation typical of exfiltration payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After compromised crate execution, detect parent process (rustc, cargo run) spawning archive tools (tar, zip) or curl/wget with source tree targets. Flag unauthorized reads of .rs files outside build artifacts. Correlate with new outbound HTTPS/DNS to non-standard domains (C2 for exfil).

suggestion.title: Unusual Child Processes from Cargo/rustc
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware typically spawns shells or data-staging utilities post-installation; 'code exfiltration' implies active process execution during build. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate rustc/cargo child processes. Alert on spawn of shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe), compression utilities (tar, zip, 7z), or network utilities (curl, wget, powershell -NoProfile) as children of build processes, especially in non-dev contexts or with suspicious arguments (--insecure, piped to /dev/null).

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Diff Anomalies in Version Control
suggestion.rationale: Article describes crate compromise; developers should detect when Cargo.lock or Cargo.toml pins or auto-upgrades to unexpected versions post-compromise announcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo.lock commits for unexpected pinning of malicious crate versions. Flag version downgrades or rapid version churn after package security advisories. Cross-reference git history against supply chain security feeds (RustSec DB, Crates.io yanked notices).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress During Build/Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration requires outbound channel; malware payloads typically beacon during execution. No C2 or network-based detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile normal outbound connections from build processes (crates.io, git repos, mirrors). Alert on connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains during cargo/rustc execution. Correlate with file access to source tree; prioritize TLS handshakes followed by DNS to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Crate Metadata/Post-Install Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states crate performs exfiltration, implying build.rs or proc_macro abuse; pipeline did not suggest detection of automated post-install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Rust crates may execute code via build.rs scripts or proc-macro expansions. Monitor for unexpected process spawns during 'cargo build' with high entropy arguments or outbound DNS queries. Detect file modifications to Cargo.toml or build.rs scripts in git diffs immediately before or during compromise.

suggestion.title: OpenSSL PKCS7_verify Crashes and Memory Faults
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'heap use-after-free bug in the PKCS7_verify function that can corrupt memory.' Process crashes, segmentation faults, and ASAN (AddressSanitizer) signals when OpenSSL processes inbound messages are direct telemetry of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process termination with SEGV/segmentation-fault codes in OpenSSL call stacks, particularly during PKCS7 or S/MIME message parsing. Correlate timing with inbound message receipt (mail, API, file upload). Flag ASAN-instrumented OpenSSL failures.

suggestion.title: Malformed PKCS7/S/MIME Message Structure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'specially crafted PKCS7 or S/MIME signed messages' as the attack vector. Detect non-standard encoding: invalid ASN.1 nesting, oversized certificate chains, malformed signature blocks, or tag-order violations that trigger the use-after-free.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PKCS7/S/MIME messages with atypical structure: oversized payload, nested container anomalies, or cryptographic format errors. Correlate inbound message receipt with OpenSSL error logs or process restarts in mail transport agents and S/MIME validators.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable OpenSSL Version Inventory and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45447 impacts specific OpenSSL versions. Proactive inventory of running OpenSSL libraries and direct identification of vulnerable versions in mail servers, web servers, and VPN appliances enables rapid patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query running processes and loaded DLLs for OpenSSL versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-45447. Cross-reference with network-facing service manifests (mail, web, VPN, API gateways). Generate automated alerts for unpatched endpoints.

suggestion.title: S/MIME Message Processing Anomalies in High-Risk Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'applications process specially crafted' messages. Mail servers, gateways, and cryptographic appliances that process S/MIME show detectable workload anomalies: repeated parsing failures, reprocessing loops, or exhausted memory during signature validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spike in PKCS7 validation errors, memory pressure, or CPU exhaustion in mail transport agents and S/MIME processors during inbound message processing. Correlate with logs from external email sources or compromised internal senders.

suggestion.title: Fake message injection detection via anomalous messages.upsert origin
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload' to 'spoof messages'. No UC targets detection of upsert events where message origin doesn't match established peer relationships or cryptographic verification fails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js/Baileys processes for messages.upsert events where source peer JID doesn't exist in session peer list, message key structure is malformed, or decryption/verification fails. Correlate against known Baileys conversation history to flag spoofed origins.

suggestion.title: App state sync corruption via protocol message anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s...' but pipeline missed detection for unexpected app state mutations, failed validation, or sync recovery attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys session state files for unexpected key additions/deletions, hash mismatches, or corruption markers. Flag instances reporting app state validation failures, forced re-sync cycles, or state rollbacks within minutes of receiving unusual protocol messages.

suggestion.title: Malicious protocolMessage delivery via placeholderResendMessage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'maliciously crafted protocolMessage payload' sent via 'placeholderResendMessage'. Pipeline did not generate detection for unusual protocol message handling or anomalous message resend patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WhatsApp protocol traffic to Baileys-running hosts for unusual placeholderResendMessage frames or protocolMessage payloads exceeding typical size/structure boundaries. Correlate with vulnerable version inventory (<7.0.0-rc12, <6.7.22) to enrich risk context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Node.js/Baileys process receiving suspicious remote protocol frames
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires vulnerable Baileys instance (<7.0.0-rc12 or <6.7.22) to be network-reachable and receive malicious frames. No UC targets behavioral detection of library loading plus anomalous inbound message volume/structure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Node.js processes with Baileys library imports that establish WhatsApp protocol connections with elevated inbound message rates or payload sizes. Correlate module metadata against known vulnerable versions; flag any with abnormal network behavior post-load.

suggestion.title: GPU-intensive process spawned by fake utility installer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states campaign 'mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' and describes payload that 'secretly mine[s] cryptocurrency.' This is the campaign's primary impact (T1496.001/002), yet pipeline generated no detection UC for cryptomining. Gap: article phrase 'mine cryptocurrency using their own GPU' establishes clear impact detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes with mining software signatures (xmrig, ethminer, claymore, cryptonight, stratum worker threads) spawned within 10 minutes of fake utility installation. Monitor for high thread counts matching vCPU count, GPU driver access, and sustained >80% CPU utilization. Cross-correlate with network connections to mining pool infrastructure on non-standard ports (3333, 5555, 8332, 14433) or stratum:// protocol.

suggestion.title: Executable download from counterfeit utility domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '150 fake download sites that closely mimic trusted [utilities]' and users 'lured into downloading malware-laced files.' Initial access is deception/social engineering on fake domains (gleeze.com, giize.com, directdownload.icu). Pipeline generated no UC detecting suspicious downloads or domain reputation checks. Gap: article phrase 'luring them into downloading malware-laced files' and '150 fake download sites' establish initial-access detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web proxy/DNS logs detecting downloads from domains matching typosquatting patterns (free-download.giize.com, direct-download.gleeze.com, directdownload.icu, minemine.gleeze.com) or low-reputation domains with 'download' in hostname. Alert when executable is saved to user-writable temp/Downloads and executed within 5 minutes. Baseline: file downloads from known-malicious domains should auto-fail or trigger endpoint quarantine.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect installed via non-standard installer parent
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect is named as the campaign's persistence/access tool but pipeline RMM detection is generic. Need explicit ScreenConnect persistence UC modeling the attack chain: fake utility installer spawns ScreenConnect installer (not legitimate ConnectWise/IT-managed deployment). Gap: article establishes ScreenConnect as targeted artifact but UC does not model it as persistence mechanism distinct from legitimate RMM deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe installation when parent is suspicious (7z.exe, winrar.exe, nsis-based installer, fake Chrome/Zoom setup) and installation path is non-standard (user AppData, ProgramData, Temp, not Program Files). Alert on registry persistence (Run/RunOnce keys creating ScreenConnect service) without corresponding SCCM/Intune approval context. Monitor for scheduled tasks or WMI event subscriptions triggering ScreenConnect on next logon.

suggestion.title: Malware packer and obfuscation signature in installer artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files) and provides 12 SHA256 hashes but generates no behavioral or signature-based detection UC. Article characterizes payloads as 'malware-laced files' needing detection beyond hash matching. Gap: article phrase 'malware-laced files' and provision of hashes suggest need for unpacking/entropy analysis detection, not just IOC lookups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executables downloaded from fake utility domains with entropy >7.5 (packed/encrypted), unsigned or self-signed cert, invalid digital signatures, or PDB paths referencing mining/RMM toolchains. Cross-reference provided hashes against sandbox/VT detonations for confirmed ScreenConnect+miner execution behavior. Alert on process hollowing, DLL sideloading, or code injection attempts spawned by installer parent.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to mining pool infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Cryptominer must connect to mining pools to function. Article implies persistent C2 via 'secretly mine cryptocurrency' but pipeline provides only generic IOC template for network detection without mining-pool-specific signatures. Gap: article describes ongoing cryptomining but UC does not model mining pool C2 traffic (stratum protocol, mining domains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries and connections to known mining pool domains (nanopool.org, ethermine.org, f2pool.com, antpool.com, poolin.com, stratum.mining.*) or stratum:// protocol traffic on ports 3333, 5555, 8332, 8333, 8222, 14433 from user-context processes. Establish baseline: mining pool connections should trigger alert on first occurrence. Monitor for persistence: recurring connections to same pool infrastructure over hours/days indicates successful installation.

suggestion.title: Non-IT user execution of installer with system-level registry/service modifications
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires non-privileged user to install remote-access and mining tools, both of which typically require elevation. Article does not explicitly describe privilege escalation, but successful installation by non-admin user implies UAC bypass or token impersonation. Gap: if campaign succeeds with non-admin user account, detection should flag elevation attempts or unsigned service installation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-admin user process attempts to create Windows services (sc.exe, reg add HKLM), modify HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE registry hives, or spawn processes with elevation token. Monitor for UAC bypass techniques (DLL hijacking from temp, fodhelper.exe, eventvwr.exe) initiated by fake utility parent. Correlate with ScreenConnect/miner installation within same timeframe to establish attack chain.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Spawns Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'capable of giving attackers complete control over any developer's system'—implies code execution post-installation. No detection for npm hooks spawning shell, curl, or encoded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm or node parent spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, or wget child processes during or immediately after package install. Filter on package.json post-install hooks or malicious package directory markers.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from npm/Node Process
suggestion.rationale: Full system compromise implies exfiltration or C2; 'complete control' suggests remote connection capability absent in legitimate npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm or node process initiating outbound connections to non-package-repo IPs (non-registry.npmjs.org, non-npm-cdn). Flag TLS/HTTP to unknown ASN or high-reputation threat IPs.

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Poisoning — Unexpected Version or Metadata Change
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack; 'malicious package' inserted into registry. No detection for package metadata anomalies or version downgrades in package-lock.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json or package-lock.json for sudden version changes, off-registry sources, or git cloning from suspicious branches. Correlate npm install commands with unexpected file write timestamps in node_modules/dbmux or similar.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation or Credential Dumping Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: 'Fully compromise developer systems' suggests attackers elevate or steal credentials. No hunt for post-install elevation attempts or credential access artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 1 minute post-npm install of suspicious package, monitor for SAM/LSASS access, Mimikatz patterns, SSH key enumeration, .bash_history reads, or sudo/RunAs invocations on developer accounts.

suggestion.title: Memory-resident process injection or injection-free payload execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'runs entirely in memory, leaving almost no trace behind.' Current UCs focus on initial delivery; none detect the in-memory execution phase. Need detection for process injection, code-cave allocation, or direct shellcode execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous memory allocations with RWX permissions, suspicious VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect calls from non-system processes, or rundll32/regsvr32 with in-process shellcode indicators. Memory-resident malware typically avoids disk writes; correlate live-memory forensics with absence of child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Staged payload download chain (PowerShell or VB downloader)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multi-stage malware.' No detection for secondary payload fetches. Pipeline should detect staged HTTP/HTTPS downloads of executables or script files after initial phishing execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PowerShell or VB child process with command-line evidence of DownloadString, DownloadFile, or curl/wget invocation. Correlate to outbound HTTP/HTTPS to non-whitelisted domains with payload MIME types (EXE, DLL, PS1). High fidelity if parent is browser or email client.

suggestion.title: Spoofed government email sender domain detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign impersonates 'official Indian government tax authorities.' Article emphasizes social engineering via false authority. No detection for sender-domain spoofing or lookalike domain abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Email with subject containing 'tax', 'ITR', 'refund', 'government', or 'revenue' from sender domain that is not on official .in, .nic.in, or .gov.in whitelist. Flag SenderFromDomain matching common spoofs: *indiagov*, *itax*, *revenuegovernment*. Cross-reference against WHOIS registration date (newly registered high risk).

suggestion.title: Unusual rundll32 or regsvr32 invocation with .NET/script payload
suggestion.rationale: T1218 (System Binary Proxy Execution) listed but no specific UC. Article's multi-stage fileless approach likely uses rundll32/regsvr32 to load in-memory payloads. Detection should flag non-standard loading patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: rundll32.exe or regsvr32.exe spawned with uncommon file paths, URLs in command line, or suspicious DLL/SCT names. Flag invocations with network URLs (http://, ftp://), base64 strings, or DLL exports that are not standard system exports. Parent process in {browser, email, cmd, powershell}.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Visual Basic child process execution tree
suggestion.rationale: T1059.005 (Visual Basic) listed but no specific detection. VB execution in Office or wscript context should be flagged as potential multi-stage staging or macro exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: wscript.exe or cscript.exe executing .vbs/.vbe files, especially child processes spawned from Office apps or followed by network activity. Flag VB scripts with encoded/obfuscated content (chr(), string concatenation obfuscation) or dynamic command construction.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Critical Vulnerabilities' and vendor patch releases, establishing immediate risk of active exploitation. Pipeline should have generated detection for exploitation patterns matching the implied CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with exploit payloads or suspicious parameters targeting known Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP endpoints. Detect post-exploitation process execution (cmd.exe, PowerShell) spawned from web service accounts or appliance management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Discovery & Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Patch-release articles implicitly reference vulnerable systems still in production. Article mentions multiple vendors, indicating attacker reconnaissance would target version identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag version-disclosure responses from Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP products. Detect scanner probes (Shodan, Censys patterns) or vulnerability scanner signatures against these vendors' management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Appliance or Management Console
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti and Fortinet products are typically placed at network boundaries; successful exploitation grants pivot point for lateral movement into trust boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral connections originating from Ivanti/Fortinet appliance IP ranges post-exploit, credential harvesting from management console logs, or unexpected service account authentication patterns emanating from compromised network boundary devices.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Vulnerability-Based Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'multiple critical' vulnerabilities; patch announcements typically address privilege escalation flaws in management or system libraries. Pipeline missed mapping to privilege_escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with unexpected privilege levels from Ivanti/Fortinet service contexts. Monitor for SYSTEM or root process spawning from normally non-privileged appliance accounts, or suspicious use of built-in escalation mechanisms (sudo, UAC bypass patterns).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authentication bypass that can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers to create rogue administrative accounts and gain full administrative access.' This is both persistence and privilege escalation; must detect unexpected admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry administrative account creation events that occur without prior successful user authentication or service account provisioning request. Flag all rogue admin creations as high-severity incidents.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'an OS command injection weakness' (CVE-2026-10520) enabling 'remote attackers to execute code with root privileges.' Requires detection of command injection syntax in gateway requests and payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry for shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax (backticks, $(...)), pipe operators, semicolons, and known OS command injection payloads. Correlate positive detections with root process spawning from gateway service.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Privilege Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute code with root privileges.' Sentry gateway service should never spawn root-level child processes under normal operation; this is execution phase privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when Ivanti Sentry service spawns child processes with UID=0 or SYSTEM privileges. Alert on first occurrence; normal Sentry operations do not require this escalation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Version Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'patched...with the release of Sentry versions R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1.' Systems on R10.5.x, R10.6.x, or R10.7.x running earlier patch levels (e.g., R10.5.1, R10.6.1, R10.7.0) are vulnerable to max-severity RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Ivanti Sentry deployment inventory for versions with patch level below 2 (R10.5.1 and below, R10.6.1 and below, R10.7.0) and flag for immediate patching. Isolate vulnerable instances from untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Gateway Access Followed by Root Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes authentication bypass (CVE-2026-10523) enabling unauthenticated attackers and RCE as root (CVE-2026-10520). Chaining these events detects the exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated access attempts or failed authentication on Sentry gateway with subsequent privilege escalation or root-level process spawning within 10-minute window. Alert on pattern even if individual events appear routine.

suggestion.title: Unexpected SYSTEM-Level Process Creation from Defender
suggestion.rationale: Article states RoguePlanet 'Grants SYSTEM Access.' Core indicator is when non-system processes gain SYSTEM privileges, likely via Defender vulnerability exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when (a) non-system parent process spawns SYSTEM child; (b) MSSense.exe or Windows Defender processes create children with elevated token; (c) process token elevation occurs without expected UAC/consent prompt events in prior 5-second window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Microsoft Defender Cache/Installation Directory Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability in Defender itself suggests attacker must interact with Defender's file system locations. Article mentions 'RoguePlanet Zero-Day' targeting the product—detect unauthorized writes/executions from Defender dirs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process writing executables or scripts to %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender*, %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows Defender*, or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender* registry paths from non-Microsoft-signed binaries.

suggestion.title: Anomalous MSSense.exe or WinDefend Service Parameter Injection
