suggestion.rationale: To trigger the vulnerability ('Grants SYSTEM Access'), attacker likely must pass malformed parameters to Defender executable or abuse a vulnerable code path. Article body truncated but privilege-escalation ZDs often involve parameter tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MSSense.exe, WinDefend.exe, or SecurityHealthService.exe spawned with unusual command-line arguments, especially paths to temp/user-writable directories, or instances where parent is non-system process and command includes special characters or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Service Restart or Integrity Check Failures
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, defender may restart, fail health checks, or be disabled. Use case detects defensive indicators that ZD was triggered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid WinDefend/MSSense service stop-then-start cycles, failed Defender-integrity checks in event logs, or deletion of Defender quarantine/log files within 2 minutes of Defender process crash.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Vulnerable Defender Code Path
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access on Updated Windows'—a vulnerability that directly elevates privilege. Detection must focus on the exploitation moment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any non-SYSTEM process that acquires SYSTEM token or SID without prior UAC elevation dialog, RunAs call, or service-account context switch—especially if parent is low-privilege user process or runs from temp/Downloads.

suggestion.title: OWA XSS Exploitation via Specially Crafted Email
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary JavaScript can be executed in the browser context' when user opens email in OWA—core exploitation mechanism requiring detection at execution boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe (IIS OWA host process) for spawning of JavaScript interpreters (node.exe, cscript.exe) or inline script execution. Correlate email access logs with unexpected process spawning or script execution events. Alert on Base64-decoded JavaScript payloads appearing in OWA session context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42897 Malicious Email Delivery Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 'sending a specially crafted email to a user'—requires identifying XSS payloads in email transport before user interaction triggers execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Exchange transport logs for emails containing script tags, JavaScript event handlers (onclick, onerror, onload), or HTML-encoded payloads in message bodies. Inspect MIME structure for anomalous content-transfer-encoding or X-headers typical of exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Exchange EEMS Mitigation Service Activation Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'automatic temporary mitigation through the Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service (EEMS)' in mid-May—mitigation activation is sentinel for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when EEMS modifies OWA request filtering rules or injects XSS-blocking headers. Monitor for changes to web.config filtering policies or activation of temporary mitigations. Cross-reference with email access logs to identify exploitation attempts triggering mitigation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Exchange Server Asset Inventory & CVE-2026-42897 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Affects 'Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, and Exchange Server Subscription Edition'—critical for patch compliance and exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Exchange servers for June 2026 cumulative update installation status. Cross-reference against CISA KEV list for active exploitation. Flag any version < 2016 CU23 (June 2026) or < 2019 CU13 (June 2026) as exploitable.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Content Detection in Email Body/Attachments Pre-Delivery
suggestion.rationale: 'specially crafted email'—pattern-match for XSS IOCs including encoded JavaScript, script tags within email sanitization bypass attempts, and embedded event handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with JavaScript keywords (eval, innerHTML, createElement), HTML script tags in message body, or Base64/hex-encoded script content. Monitor for CSS expression exploits or SVG script injection patterns. Raise alert if recipient mailbox is hosted on vulnerable Exchange version.

suggestion.title: Microsoft RCE Exploitation via Patched CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article title claims 'Critical RCE Bugs' but pipeline extracted zero use cases for RCE detection. Any patch article on RCE vulns requires detection for exploitation attempts before patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or network connections attempting to trigger known Microsoft RCE vectors. Look for exploitation payloads matching published PoCs for zero-day RCEs, command execution from unexpected processes, or suspicious Office/Exchange spawning child processes.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Privilege Escalation on Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article references RCE bugs but no UC for privilege escalation post-compromise. Attackers typically chain RCE with UAC bypass or kernel exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious privilege elevation attempts following RCE exploit payloads: registry modifications to HKLM\System, execution of known UAC bypass techniques (fodhelper, eventviewer, compmgmt), or parent-child process chains where unprivileged parent spawns privileged child.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Microsoft RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article synopsis suggests widespread Microsoft product vulnerabilities but no detection UC for attacker movement between systems post-initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump), reconnaissance commands (net view, nltest, dsquery), or lateral movement techniques (PsExec, WMI, RDP) originating from the initially compromised Microsoft product process tree.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Registry/Log Tampering Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE bugs that would trigger security alerts, but pipeline missed UC for attackers disabling logging or AV post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of Windows Defender registry keys (DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableBehaviorMonitoring), deletion of security event logs, or processes terminating Endpoint Detection and Response agents originating from RCE-exploited processes.

suggestion.title: Known Vulnerable Microsoft Binary Execution (Living-off-the-Land)
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day and RCE articles typically describe exploitation via LOLBIN execution; pipeline provided zero UCs for execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of Microsoft legitimate binaries (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, csi.exe, powershell.exe, wmi.exe) spawned from unexpected parents (Office, Exchange, IIS worker) or with suspicious command-line arguments indicative of payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Email/Web Server Compromise via Microsoft Office/Exchange RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article likely covers Office/Exchange vulnerabilities (common zero-day targets) but pipeline extracted zero UCs for compromise of these internet-facing services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Office RCE: monitor for file opening (Word, Excel) triggering child process creation or network connections. For Exchange RCE: flag POST requests to ECP/OWA endpoints from external IPs spawning System.Diagnostics.Process activity; look for w3wp.exe or EdgeTransport.exe child processes executing commands.

suggestion.title: SSH Brute Force Against PeopleSoft Default Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'script attempts to connect to them over SSH using common PeopleSoft and Oracle administrative accounts such as psoft, oracle, and linuxadm.' Defines the primary access vector used in 300+ successful breaches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed SSH authentication attempts against service accounts (psoft, oracle, linuxadm) from external IPs in rapid succession. Escalate if key-based authentication is attempted after password failures, indicating fallback behavior described in the attack script.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ransom Note File Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'script designed to create a ransom note named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT on an internal PeopleSoft server after it is breached.' This is the extortion signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation matching 'README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS*' pattern or similar ransom note variants in PeopleSoft directories (/PS* paths, Tomcat webapps). Correlate with preceding SSH sessions from external IPs or shell script execution.

suggestion.title: Parsing /etc/hosts for PeopleSoft System Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'script parses the /etc/hosts to identify PeopleSoft-related systems.' This is the reconnaissance step enabling lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/hosts file access from unexpected processes (cat, grep, shell expansions) spawned during SSH sessions. Correlate with subsequent network connection attempts to IPs enumerated from /etc/hosts to confirm lateral movement reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: MeshCentral Agent Deployment for Remote Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Researcher discovered 'staging materials, including MeshCentral agents' in exposed attacker directories. Indicates deployment of persistent remote access capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshCentral executable deployment, particularly in /tmp or system temp directories on PeopleSoft hosts. Monitor for network callbacks to C2 infrastructure; cross-reference IP/domain patterns with known ShinyHunters staging infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Inbound Exploitation Attempts from Known ShinyHunters Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 7 IP addresses confirmed by researcher to originate exploitation attempts: 142.11.200.186-190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24. Directly actionable for network defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on any inbound connections FROM these 7 IPs to PeopleSoft servers (ports 8000, 8443, 3306, 22). Cross-reference with TLS certificates CN matching 'azurenetfiles.net' for additional attribution and pivoting on infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Langflow /api/v2/files Path Traversal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'POST /api/v2/files endpoint does not sanitize the filename parameter from the multipart form data, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using path traversal sequences' - core exploit signature never surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /api/v2/files containing parent directory traversal syntax (../, ..\) in the filename parameter of multipart form submissions. Establish baseline of legitimate uploads; flag requests from external sources, unauthenticated callers, or targeting paths outside the application's intended upload directory.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow Session Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'unauthenticated auto-login by default' and 'a single unauthenticated request is sufficient to obtain a valid session token before proceeding with exploitation.' Pipeline failed to flag authentication bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect session token issuance to requests lacking valid credentials. Monitor for unauthenticated POST calls to /api/v2/files returning 200-range status codes. Alert if single source IP rapidly acquires multiple session tokens or requests privileged endpoints with auto-generated tokens.

suggestion.title: Langflow Arbitrary File Write to System Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers writing 'files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem' and honeypots detecting file drops. No file-system correlation detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /api/v2/files requests with file creation events outside the application upload directory. Flag writes to sensitive paths (/etc, /var, /tmp, C:\Windows, C:\Program Files) initiated by the Langflow process or parent web server. Include temporal correlation (file creation within 5 seconds of HTTP request).

suggestion.title: Langflow Exploitation Reconnaissance Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'honeypots have now detected attackers exploiting the vulnerability to drop test files' - pattern suggests probing behavior before payload delivery. No detection for unsuccessful or low-confidence exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bursts of POST requests to /api/v2/files with varying path traversal payloads, responses indicating failed writes (4xx/5xx status codes), or malformed multipart data. Alert if single external IP submits 5+ diverse path sequences within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Langflow Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerable versions <1.9.0 (Langflow) and <0.8.3 (langflow-base), with patch details. Pipeline should flag exposed vulnerable instances for remediation prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint Langflow instances via version disclosure in HTTP headers, /api endpoints, or package manifests. Flag instances running Langflow <1.9.0 or langflow-base <0.8.3 as vulnerable. Cross-reference with external scanning data (Censys detected ~7k exposed instances) to prioritize exposed assets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized ServiceNow Instance Table Query Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized actors to query customer instance tables' and 'execute queries against backend instance tables without proper authentication.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ServiceNow API query logs for table access attempts using invalid/missing authentication tokens or from unauthenticated sessions. Flag rapid queries against configuration/cmdb/instance tables from unexpected source IPs, user agents, or service accounts. Establish per-user baseline query patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Vulnerability Exploitation — Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access controls that may enable attackers to execute queries...without proper authentication.' This is exploitation (T1190); pipeline inferred only T1071.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) requests to ServiceNow API endpoints (/api/now/*, /incident, /cmdb_ci_*) lacking authentication headers or with invalid session tokens. Flag 401→200 or 403→200 status transitions. Alert on IPs with no prior legitimate ServiceNow activity requesting sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: ServiceNow Instance Table Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article implies post-exploitation enumeration of 'customer instance tables' for reconnaissance. Pipeline missing discovery-phase detection for table schema/metadata queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential API calls to sys_* tables or metadata endpoints listing available tables and fields. Flag single-source enumeration of multiple table definitions in short time window. Detect reconnaissance queries from users/service accounts lacking typical discovery roles.

suggestion.title: Recursive Home Directory Deletion After GitHub Token Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'dead-man switch' that 'monitors the token's validity every minute and, if it's revoked, executes a destructive command (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents), recursively deleting files and directories in the user's home and Documents folders.' This is a detectable impact event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rm -rf or recursive delete commands targeting home directory and Documents folder, particularly when executed by systemd user service or LaunchAgent processes within 72 hours of GitHub token revocation or API auth failure events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modifications to AI Coding Tool Configuration Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline.' Persistence via config poisoning is a distinct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to AI tool config directories (.cursor, .copilot, Gemini config paths, Claude plugin manifests) from processes that are not the tool installers or legitimate package managers. Correlate with credential access events on same host.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Abuse for Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware 'requires no command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to operate, as it uses GitHub for that purpose'—abuse of legitimate service for C2 signaling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous GitHub API activity from developer machines: high-frequency metadata queries, unusual repository access patterns, or suspicious commit messages that appear to encode instructions, particularly when originating from machines with known credential harvesting activity.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from CI/CD Config and Cloud Provider Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists: 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores.' File access to these locations is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file access to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure, ~/.kube/config, .circleci config, .github/workflows directories, and password manager vaults. Flag grep, cat, or tar operations on these paths from non-standard user/process contexts.

suggestion.title: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager Lateral Movement from Compromised Developer
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' SSM lateral movement from a developer account is a specific, auditable pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate AWS CloudTrail StartSession calls originating from developer IAM principals with prior credential harvesting on the same machine. Flag SSM sessions to production infrastructure from development accounts as anomalous.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Package Publishing to Open-Source Registries (npm, PyPI, RubyGems)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'abuses them to compromise npm, PyPI, and RubyGems packages.' Trojanized package publication is the mechanism for worm-like self-propagation described in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version publishing from previously dormant maintainer accounts, unusual version bumps outside normal release cadence, or publishes from geographically anomalous IPs. Correlate with GitHub Actions workflow modifications detected via stolen credentials.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Langflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Unpatched Langflow Flaw CVE-2026-5027 Exploited'—pipeline failed to generate any detection for this publicly disclosed, actively exploited vulnerability. CVE ID is the signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Langflow instances for patterns matching CVE-2026-5027 PoC payloads or requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Flag unauthenticated requests triggering backend errors or process spawning. Correlate with subsequent child-process creation from Langflow process.

suggestion.title: RCE Command Execution from Langflow Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Unauthenticated RCE'—the exploitation succeeds in achieving code execution. Pipeline missed detection for the actual execution phase following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, python) spawned from Langflow application process with unusual command-line arguments or network access. Flag unexpected outbound connections from Langflow process to external IPs, especially to C2 domains or data exfiltration targets.

suggestion.title: Langflow Vulnerability Scanning and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'unpatched' vulnerability in active exploitation—implies attackers scan/fingerprint Langflow instances before exploitation. Pipeline missed pre-exploitation reconnaissance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated requests from single source to Langflow endpoints within short time window, requests probing for version info, or known PoC request patterns against CVE-2026-5027. Flag 404s followed by exploitation attempts indicating enumeration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45586 Privilege Escalation Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'allows a local attacker with low privileges to escalate to SYSTEM'—explicit exploitation event. Pipeline assigned T1190 (wrong) but generated zero hunting logic to detect actual CTFMON abuse. This is the kill-chain pivot and should be detection-first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual access patterns to CTFMON binary or its registry/config locations from low-privilege processes, or spawning of elevated child processes immediately after CTFMON interaction. Flag CTFMON execution from non-standard parents (exploitability indicator).

suggestion.title: Low-to-High Privilege Process Elevation via CTFMON
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CTF framework as 'valuable post-exploitation primitive'—meaning CTFMON is the weaponized component. Detection should track process-privilege deltas tied to CTFMON execution, not generic templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal CTFMON process tokens and parents (typically user-space IME processes). Alert on: low-privilege parent spawning CTFMON, CTFMON spawning SYSTEM-context child, or low-privilege process token elevation correlated with CTFMON module load. Window: <200ms post-CTFMON execution.

suggestion.title: Abnormal CTFMON Process Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation use; pipeline noted zero execution-phase detection. CTFMON is a known-benign component—detection must focus on context (unexpected parent, command-line args, launch timing).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CTFMON normally launched by user-session IME or explorer.exe. Alert on: unexpected parents (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, mshta.exe), command-line args (none expected for normal function), or multiple instances from same parent. Correlate with low-privilege process context.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Event Selector Modification for Log Filtering
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Abusing Cloud Logging Services' + keywords 'log poisoning, log router' indicate active log filtering/exclusion attacks; CloudTrail Event Selectors and Data Events exclusions are primary defense-evasion vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PutEventSelectors, UpdateEventSelectors, DeleteEventSelectors, or PutTrailStatus calls that disable S3 data events, Lambda data events, or management events. Monitor for rapid successive calls to reduce logging coverage.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Trail Deletion or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'blinding the watchmen'—disabling observability itself. DeleteTrail, StopLogging, and trail configuration changes are the most direct attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DeleteTrail, StopLogging, CreateTrail with conflicting parameters, or ModifyTrailConfiguration. Flag if performed by non-privileged principals or outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Google Cloud Logging Router Rule Modification or Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Keywords list 'Google Cloud, log router'—equivalent to CloudTrail in GCP. Routing rules control where logs flow; disabling or redirecting them evades detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logging.sinks.create, logging.sinks.delete, logging.sinks.update with destinations changed to /dev/null, deleted sinks, or newly created sinks that exclude sensitive namespaces.

suggestion.title: S3 Server Access Logging Disabled or Redirected
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'S3, log storage'. Disabling S3 bucket logging or changing log destination removes audit trail for data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PutBucketLogging calls that remove logging, change log target bucket, or change log prefix. Alert on DeleteBucketLogging or SetBucketLogging to non-existent/inaccessible targets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized CloudTrail Log File Deletion or Modification
suggestion.rationale: After disabling logging at the source, attackers may delete or overwrite existing logs in S3. Article on 'blinding' implies tampering with stored artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DeleteObject or PutObject on CloudTrail log buckets; monitor for batch deletion jobs or S3 Sync commands targeting log prefixes. Flag if performed by non-admin principals.

suggestion.title: Excessive or Anomalous CloudTrail Lookup Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article likely describes reconnaissance of logging infrastructure. Discovery of which trails exist, their configurations, and what they're logging is a precursor to disabling them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DescribeTrails, ListTrails, GetTrailStatus, GetEventSelectors called repeatedly by single principal in short timeframe. Flag if followed by modifications within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Execution in V8 JIT Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day in Chrome V8 implies exploitation via crafted JavaScript that triggers memory corruption during JIT compilation. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome/Chromium process child spawns with unusual command-line patterns (encoded payloads, suspicious redirects). Detect abnormal memory access patterns preceding process termination. Correlate JavaScript eval/Function execution with process crashes or privilege boundary violations.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Memory Corruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes zero-day exploitation 'in the wild'—implies active memory safety violation. Pipeline generated no detection for exploit-stage anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome processes exhibiting rapid fault/exception cycles, heap exhaustion patterns, or segmentation faults. Cross-reference with injected DLL/module load events. Baseline against benign crash telemetry.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration via Browser Process Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploited in the wild'—implies post-exploitation callback. Pipeline extracted zero command-and-control phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/HTTP connections initiated from chrome.exe to non-standard ports (8080, 8888, 443 with mismatched SNI), known C2 IP ranges, or dynamic-DNS domains. Flag certificate anomalies (self-signed, expired, mismatched CN).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Browser Profile/User Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Browser exploitation often targets stored credentials, session tokens, autofill data. Article mentions patching urgency implying risk to user data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unusual access to Chrome user profile directories (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\), particularly Access to SQLite databases (Cookies, Login Data, Web Data). Detect credential manager or password-extraction utilities running in same session as Chrome crash events.

suggestion.title: Exploit Delivery via Watering-Hole or Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day delivery mechanism not captured. Typical browser exploits arrive via compromised legitimate site or phishing. Pipeline reconstructed zero initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sudden traffic to low-reputation or newly-registered domains with subsequent crash/exploitation telemetry from Chrome. Flag users clicking suspicious shortened URLs or emails with unusual headers immediately preceding browser exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-11645 Vulnerable Chromium Browser Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-11645 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and directs reader to standard asset-exposure hunts. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for unpatched Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Chromium instances. Flag any system reporting no patch status or missing from inventory. Correlate with federal patch-due deadline (2026-06-23) for executive reporting.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Sandbox Escape — Arbitrary Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via crafted HTML page.' This execution phase (sandbox escape) is distinct from initial access and requires process-level anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes from browser executables (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, opera.exe), abnormal memory allocation in browser process space, or browser crash dumps indicating out-of-bounds memory access. Correlate spikes with publication dates (2026-06-09 forward).

suggestion.title: Crafted HTML Delivery — V8 Exploitation Vector
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTML page' as the attack vector. This delivery phase warrants detection separate from the vulnerability assessment, particularly if staged via email or watering-hole.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious HTML files or obfuscated JavaScript delivered via email attachment, email link, or web download. Correlate with browser version of target and known Chromium V8 exploit kits. Flag if followed by browser crash or unexpected process spawn.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detect: CVE-2026-20245 (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and federal patch due date 2026-06-23. Unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances must be flagged immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan results identifying Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager or vManage instances with CVE-2026-20245. Prioritize internet-reachable or management-network-accessible instances. Correlate with asset inventory to identify patching gaps and timeline to federal due date.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Delivery to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker must supply 'a crafted file to the affected system.' Detect unauthorized or suspicious file creation/modification in SD-WAN Manager directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/modification in Cisco SD-WAN Manager application directories, configuration paths, and temp folders. Alert on files with suspicious extensions, encoding artifacts, or escape sequences. Correlate with authenticated user activity and network uploads to detect malicious file delivery.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution by Cisco SD-WAN Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes arbitrary command execution 'as root' triggered by crafted file. Detect child process spawning from Cisco SD-WAN Manager with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vmanage process) spawns child processes with UID 0 or EUID 0. Monitor for unexpected command interpreters (bash, sh, python) invoked from the SD-WAN service account. Baseline normal root operations and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Encoding Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'improper encoding or escaping of output' leads to privilege escalation. Detect exploitation of encoding/escaping weaknesses in input handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager input logs for escape sequences, encoding artifacts (hex, octal, Unicode), or path traversal sequences in file parameters. Correlate with successful privilege transitions (uid 0). Alert on repeated encoding patterns or error log entries indicating parsing failures.

suggestion.title: Authentication Abuse to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, local attacker'—detect lateral movement and credential abuse targeting the management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager for authentication volume spikes, credential reuse from unusual sources, or service account compromise. Alert on failed login attempts followed by successful authentication from the same source. Correlate with network access logs to detect lateral movement into management interfaces.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-7473 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE is actively exploited (CISA KEV status) and explicitly recommends substitute the CVE in scanner hunts. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; vulnerability detection is the primary detection mechanism for privilege enforcement and scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Arista EOS devices reporting vulnerable status for CVE-2026-7473 in vulnerability scanners, device inventory, or patch-management systems. Identify exposed Arista switches failing vulnerability checks or missing security patches deployed after 2026-06-23 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Arista EOS Device Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application); exploitation requires externally-facing Arista EOS switches. Pipeline provided no asset-exposure use case despite article explicitly referencing template guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate and tag all Arista EOS switches accessible from untrusted networks (WAN, internet-facing). Identify switches with SSH/HTTPS/management ports (22, 80, 443) reachable from external IP ranges. Correlate against patch inventory to flag unpatched assets post-2026-06-23.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Tunneled Packet Decapsulation and Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Article core technical detail: 'switch incorrectly decapsulate and forwards other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP.' Pipeline generated zero use case for this attack behavior despite it being the vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista switches for unexpected tunneled packet forwarding: capture or netflow data showing packets with encapsulated headers (GRE, VXLAN, IP-in-IP) being decapsulated and re-forwarded to IPs matching configured decapsulation targets but originating from unexpected sources. Alert on decapsulation errors or forwarding of non-matching tunnel types.

suggestion.title: Arista Configuration Change - Decapsulation Rules
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability manifests through decapsulation configuration. Detection should include baseline configuration audits, especially post-exploitation when attacker may alter tunnel handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track configuration changes on Arista EOS devices, particularly decapsulation rules, tunnel protocol handlers, and IP decapsulation settings. Alert on unauthorized modifications to decapsulation targets or enablement of decapsulation features. Correlate config drift with patch deployment timeline.

suggestion.title: WebSocket HEEx Template Injection to /phoenix_storybook Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'playground accepts user-controlled attribute values over WebSocket and interpolates them unsanitized into a HEEx template.' This is the initial-access/exploitation event, yet no detection for abnormal /phoenix_storybook endpoint traffic or malicious HEEx syntax was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/WebSocket traffic to /phoenix_storybook playground endpoints for HEEx template syntax markers (e.g., '<%', 'EEx.eval_string', embedded Elixir code patterns) in request parameters. Alert on unsanitized attribute values containing interpolation operators or function calls that suggest template injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unsafe HEEx Compilation and Kernel.eval() Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states template is 'compiled and evaluated with full Elixir Kernel access.' Detection of Kernel module evaluation or compile-time errors from malicious templates during RCE attempt is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture BEAM/Elixir runtime logs for failed or unexpected HEEx compilation events, Kernel.eval() calls with non-standard arguments, or exception stack traces indicating code injection in the /phoenix_storybook context. Baseline normal storybook compilation patterns and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: BEAM Runtime Code Execution Post-HEEx Injection (System.cmd() Spawned Processes)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have generated UC_35_2 but did not. Article describes unauthenticated RCE; once achieved, attacker would likely spawn OS shells or tools via System.cmd(). Parent process matching BEAM interpreters spawning shell/LOLBin children is foundational post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation where parent is BEAM runtime (beam.smp, beam.smp.exe, erl.exe, werl.exe, erlsrv.exe, erl_child_setup). Alert when children include sh, bash, dash, zsh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, python, perl, or LOLBins (rundll32.exe, certutil.exe, curl, wget, nc, bitsadmin). Confidence high; most phoenix_storybook apps do not spawn shells.

suggestion.title: First-Time BEAM Outbound Public Network Connections (Post-RCE C2/Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have generated UC_35_3 but did not. After achieving RCE, attacker would establish command-and-control or exfiltration channels. Baseline-deviation approach (first-time public connections from BEAM) is medium-confidence but high-value indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish 30-day baseline of typical BEAM runtime network destinations (package mirrors, localhost, internal repos). Alert on new public IP/domain connections from beam.smp, beam.smp.exe, erl.exe, or werl.exe processes where RemoteIPType=Public and destination not in baseline. Suppress internal/corporate proxies and known CDNs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable phoenix_storybook Artifact Inventory (Versions 0.5–1.0)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have generated UC_35_4 but did not. Article identifies vulnerable library versions; file-path and binary name patterns (extra_assigns_helpers.beam, component_renderer.beam) enable asset discovery and triage prioritization critical for vulnerability management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query deployed Phoenix applications for presence of phoenix_storybook library versions 0.5 through 1.0 (match folder path regex: phoenix_storybook-0\.[5-9]|1\.0). Cross-correlate with running beam.smp processes and reachable network endpoints to identify exposed instances. High confidence asset inventory; directly remediable.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Request to LiteLLM Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE' explicitly establishes the vulnerability does not require authentication. This is the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteLLM proxy endpoints (/v1/*, /litellm/*) arriving without valid authorization headers (missing Bearer token, API key, or x-api-key). Baseline should show near-zero unauthenticated requests to production LiteLLM services; spike or 200-OK response to unauthenticated request indicates exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from LiteLLM Process
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—RCE is the execution phase. Legitimate LiteLLM should not spawn child shells or interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any child process creation under LiteLLM parent processes (litellm_server, python -m litellm). Alert on /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget spawned by litellm. Legitimate operations use model API calls only; shell execution is exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-42271 Vulnerable LiteLLM Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly names CVE-2026-42271; identification of affected versions is a foundational threat-intelligence IOC missing from the pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all LiteLLM installations via package managers (pip list | grep litellm), running processes (ps aux | grep litellm), or package metadata. Flag any external-facing instance running a version within the CVE-2026-42271 affected range as critical remediation target. Cross-correlate with network exposure (public IP, DNS records).

suggestion.title: Abnormal HTTP Response Size from LiteLLM Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Chains to Unauthenticated RCE'—the attacker must exfiltrate command output. RCE output typically leaves via HTTP response body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline response sizes for LiteLLM endpoints (typical model responses: <20KB). Alert on responses >100KB or containing shell metacharacters ($, *, >, |, &&, ;) combined with command output patterns (#, $, root@). Correlate spike in large responses with preceding unauthenticated requests to same endpoint.
